items: This is creation. And Jesus was there. "Let Us make them in Our image," as man was spoken into creation on the 6th day and given dominion over all He created. John 1 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not. And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth. Colossians 1 For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist. And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence. For it pleased the Father that in him should all fulness dwell; And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven. Ephesians 1 According as He hath chosen us in Him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved. Revelation 1 I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty. Hebrews 13 Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever. Amen Now, note the order of things. This is how all of creation was made. And the creation of days, separated from night, morning and evening, was created by God who is outside of time. The fullness of the Godhead exists when nothing else did, including time, and through Him was created light, substance, life, and mankind. Everything after its own kind, with the seed contained therein propagating that life over time. This is a literal story of creation, as it occurred roughly 6,200 years ago. Not because of fossils found in weird places, or the problems with carbon dating, or the position of the stars in the firmament unchanging, or the complexity and variance of life. But because God said this is how it happened. In His inspired and preserved word, The God who cannot lie tells us these things and that they are so. Evolution, which is the worship of time, or Kronos as the creator, is literally the worship of the created, as we see in Genesis, because God created time. And so we know it's false. Biblical inerrancy, and the fundamentalist belief that it is the inspired and preserved word of God, has yet to fail, even as science falsely so-called makes claims to the contrary, God's hand is revealed continually making the wise into fools. This is why God's word is continually under attack. This is why doubt is continually sown. Because, if many have doubts about any aspect of God's word, then many will not believe the report. The Gospel, and will perish as sinners. And while you don't have to necessarily believe in the literal biblical creation in order to believe that Jesus is the son of God who died for our sins and was resurrected again, and whom through which we are given Grace by God unto eternal life, it is difficult to then express that Faith to others while doubting much of His word. Or thinking it allegory, or some sort of parable. The gospels give account back to Adam. The genealogies are there to mark time. And the generations from Noah back to Adam, from Abraham back to Noah, from Israel to Christ... These are there for a purpose. And while there are some seeking to take away from God's word by casting doubt not just on the creation story but on every biblical text that draws upon it, all scripture that refers to it in describing Jesus Christ to us, there are people that seek to add to his word as well. It is easy to read into it things that are not there, and this too is an error. So as we go forth through Genesis understand that it is not only the faith of this author, but my firm opinion that the Bible is literally true, and the truths revealed from Genesis 1 through the end in Revelation 22, is the story of Jesus Christ. God revealing His Son to us that we may believe and have eternal life. It is God's word, His testimony, the testaments that He has given us to His promise for us. And from start to finish, Alpha to Omega it is one gospel, the good news of salvation through Christ Jesus.

Amen. The stage is set. God and man and woman. The garden. The one law, told directly from God to Adam. Before Eve was made from him. Free from sin, naked and unashamed. There are 66 chapters in Isaiah just like there are 66 books in the Bible. There are 39 books in OT, 27 in the NT. 39 of Isaiah's chapters deal with the concurrent events of those days (and glimpses of far future in end days), while 40 to 66 deal with the Messiah and his first and second coming. Some have gone far enough to say each chapter may correspond to their respective books in the Bible thematically, so in a way the books of Isaiah also prophetically matches the books of the Bible before it was completed.

Romans 5:12-17 Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned: (for until the law sin was in the world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law. Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come. But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many. And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification. For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ. And so, sin entered the world by the disobedience of one man, who knowingly violated the one command of God. Adam, given the perfect situation, abundance of food, dominion, a perfect help meet for a wife, climate so perfect they could be naked, and the purity and innocence to not be ashamed of it. He knew God, could talk with Him and know he was loved by His creator more than anything else in creation. Paradise on earth with none of the cares of this world that we use as excuse and snares to trap us. And had this been given without choice, without free will, the ability to choose, it would have been a prison. A cosmic dollhouse. But God, as He made us in His image, made us with the capacity for will. Conscious of our own independent thought. Not simply a biped humanoid with a beard, the shell of the flesh, but like unto Him in that we can think, reason and have an independent soul. And thus, our own will. That is what makes us like unto God, made in his image. God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit all have will to choose, the Bible tells us, and the Son and the Spirit do the will of the Father, by choice, as Jesus wept in prayer in the garden of Gethsemane, committing Himself to the Father's will, not Jesus' own. And so, Adam was given a choice. A law. A commandment to obey, with consequence if he chose not to. In a garden, man made a choice to sin and disobey the will of God the Father, and in a garden, the Man, Christ Jesus chose to obey unto death. For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ. Sin couldn't enter the world without choice. Sin couldn't be taken from the world without choice. A free gift cannot be received by force, or it is no longer free. It must be accepted by choice. And so, God's first interaction with man was to provide him a choice. In the first few chapters of the first book of God's word, given to us by Him to know Him. And the choice of fallen man to believe that sure testimony, or not. To be like Eve, who was told of the command by Adam, and instead of believing God's word, was deceived. And so, knowing that we have free will, knowing for certain that God has given us choice, and that ability to believe or disobey is ours, not His, we reject the damnable heresy of Calvinism, for it would deny Adam his choice to sin and make the suffering and sacrifice of Christ for that sin into some kind of sick joke. Now, what was the command of God? Genesis 2:16-17; And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die. And we note this was given Adam, before Eve was. And told to Eve by Adam. Which is how God's word is given each of us. Spoken of the LORD God, by faith passed down to others, by faith received and believed. And it is that faith in the received word of God that Satan, more subtle than any beast, preys on, when as the serpent he comes to tempt Eve; And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden? "Ye, hath God said?" This is Satan's oldest trick. Casting doubt upon God's word to get us to sin. This is the reason for false Bible versions. This is the way of false prophets. Making us doubt that God's word is pure and right. "Many of the earliest manuscripts leave this passage out...this verse is not found in earlier manuscripts...the Greek here could actually mean this instead. Do you even know Hebrew?" Footnotes. Margin notes. "Study Bibles." "You need a seminary graduate with a doctorate in Divinity to understand the Bible!" "God of the OT is angry, but Jesus is love!" "That was written to people of that time, not to us!" Fill in your own example of "Yea, hath God said..?" here. And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die. And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die: For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil. The serpent misquotes and questions, Eve knows the truth of the word and corrects him. Then Satan incredulously casts more doubt. And this doubt, we see work in Eve, sparking the curiosity and wonder and reason, gifts of God that make us like unto Him, but now, under our will and doubts sown by Satan, used to choose sin. And so she saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, and so curious and doubting, covetous of the wisdom of God, Eve was beguiled into sin, and ate of the tree. And Adam? Eve gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat. There's no subtlety, no casting of doubt. No tricks of the serpent. His wife sinned and he readily joined in immediately. Of his own free will. Many such cases. Misery loves company and the sin of those around us, like the little leaven that leavens the whole lump, it spreads. And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons. So, having sinned and felt the conviction in their hearts, they knew they were naked before God, and ashamed. Having the knowledge of good and evil, just as the serpent said, using that seed of truth to say it would make them like God. This is another favorite deception of the devil, to make us covetous of God, and the false promises that we can become God and usurp His station and take His power for ourselves. And the first instinct Adam and Eve had, when faced with this feeling of shame, was to attempt to cover it up with their own works. In aprons they made. And like our own works, the fig leaves were insufficient to make them righteous. And seeing that the LORD God was in the garden, they hid from Him, showing that they knew in their hearts their work wasn't enough. God calls to them, and calls them out for their transgression of the law, (for sin is the transgression of the law), and questions them, if they ate of that tree He forbid. And Adam, like many of us when caught up in sin, blames another, and in fact, blames God. The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat. It's her fault. And you gave me her, so it's really your fault, God! How often do we rationalize our sins this way? How laughable it is when Adam does it. It's cringe, embarrassing, to see him, who given everything and free will, still has the audacity to blame the God who created him for his own choices. "Oh if I had this advantage" and "If things were different and I didn't have this pressure on me..." "If this person didn't give me the opportunity, the temptation, oh Lord! The person you brought in to my life, I might add!" And Eve answers no better; The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat. Her own covetousness playing no part in her excuse. How many times in our lives have we, like Adam, blamed the cruel fates and fallen nature of others, and the God who made us for our willful and intentional sin? Or blame the devil for tricking us into doubting God's word, beguiled. It's as pathetic and stupid as when Adam and Eve do it here. And how many of us seeking our own righteousness, poorly sow together fig leaves of our own works, seeking to erase the transgressions ourselves. Hiding from God? So having sinned and fallen, God the Father who loves man, offers the first promise of Christ, while laying out the consequences of bringing sin into the world. To the devil, that old serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. I plan on expounding on the seed of the woman/seed of the devil, Revelation 12 and how this promise is fulfilled in Jesus in another post. But note that the seed who bruises Satan's head, and whom Satan bruises the heel, is Christ. To Eve, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee. Women know pain and complications of childbirth in ways few creatures in creation can. And their season of fertility, more frequent, and their conceptions, multiplied. And by their nature, they shall desire their husbands will. This last part deserves its own post as well. Both the meaning and implications of this desire, and how man's failure subverts and damages relationships, twisting this God given inclination in woman. (I would also note modern Bible versions change this verse to have opposite meaning, and how that undermines everything). And to man, through Adam, we are punished; Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return. The consequences of sin is death. We return to the ground whereof we were made, after a lifetime of labor to feed ourselves and survive. With the very things of nature we had dominion over, turned against us. Struggle. Death. The wages of sin. But here, in Genesis 3, at the very beginning of mankind as a fallen creature, loved by God, He covers our sins. Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them. Shedding of blood for the remission of sin. Covered by the righteousness of the lamb, slain before the foundation of the world. God gives them this gift, freely. Of His own handiwork, not ours. And so we are now, still naked. Still in sin. Our nature, made manifest in Adam, to choose struggle and death over obedience. Unable to cover our shame by our own works, and needing instead the gift of God, the blood of Christ, covered in the spotless coat of the lamb, slain without blemish. Given the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ as a gift from a loving and merciful God. This is the Gospel. This is the same faith, as received by Adam, and passed on to his descendents, who call upon the name of the Lord to be saved, and becoming sons of God. But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name. Revelation 12 And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars: 2 And she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered. 3 And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads. 4 And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born. 5 And she brought forth a man child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron: and her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne. 6 And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days. 7 And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels, 8 And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven. 9 And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him. 10 And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night. 11 And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death. 12 Therefore rejoice, ye heavens, and ye that dwell in them. Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea! for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time. 13 And when the dragon saw that he was cast unto the earth, he persecuted the woman which brought forth the man child. 14 And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness, into her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent. 15 And the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman, that he might cause her to be carried away of the flood. 16 And the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed up the flood which the dragon cast out of his mouth. 17 And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ. Hebrews 11:4 By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh. Now fallen, cast out from Eden, Adam and Eve, the mother of man are fruitful and multiply. And her first born, a man from God is Cain, a tiller of the earth. Working the fields. We know from Genesis 3 the burden God placed on fallen man. Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return. Cain, under this burden grew herbs and vegetables, fruit of the land. With sweat of his brow. Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord. And God respected not his sacrifice. And Abel, a keeper of sheep, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering. The firstling lamb. The sacrifice of blood for atonement. The Bible says Abel by faith brought the sacrifice that was acceptable unto the Lord. But Cain brought his works and was rejected. But God, long suffering and who the Bible says would not that any man perish, gives His word to Cain, to repent towards the faith, in the blood of the lamb for remission of sin, as He had given Adam and Eve, that Abel gained God's pleasure by. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him. Unable to get past his own pride and accept God's promise, His word, Cain allowed his wrath in, and in covetousness slew innocent Abel, and the very earth cries out to the Lord that his blood had been spilled. This is a Biblical doctrine that's often overlooked. The spilling of innocent blood actually causes the earth itself to cry out to God. We see several times throughout scripture God warns man against it; That innocent blood be not shed in thy land, which the LORD thy God giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee. Deuteronomy 19:10 For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. Romans 8:22 The blood of their sons and their daughters, Whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan; And the land was polluted with the blood. Psalm 106:38 One of the things that curses a land and brings judgement on a people is innocent blood shed. It pollutes the land, and the earth travails and groans, crying out to the Lord. And so undone, Cain is cursed. When we reject God's word, His gift of salvation in the blood of Christ, the lamb slain at the foundation of the world, when we count on our works and want credit from God for our own righteousness, we invite sin into our heart, and when we reject God's word finally, are rejected of Him. Marked as Cain. So, now cursed and reprobate by God, rejected having spilled innocent blood of his brother, God takes from Cain the source of his pride, unable to work the field. Afraid that this first few generations of man will slay him in vengeance for what he's done, God places a mark upon Cain and promises man who takes their own vengeance to be avenged by God sevenfold. Vengeance is the Lord's. (God will command that the blood of the guilty be upon themselves and that His justice be done by His people to cleanse their land, but that's not of this time) And we are told of Cain's establishment of a city, and generations from his marriage and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son. (Different Enoch, you're thinking of this Enoch's nephew) And from this, we surmise that Adam and Eve had been fruitful, and the land of men had grown sufficiently in the process of time, that Cain could take a wife. We will see in the next chapter that all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died. Eve likely as long lived. Their offspring, multiplied. And Cain's great-great-great grandson, Lamech was a murderer who, in pride boasted to his wives that if Cain be avenged sevenfold, he would be all the more. We see Tubalcain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron, Jubal the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle. Many read into this more than we can know, and ascribe to the idea that this curse of Cain continues in his bloodlines, but scripture doesn't back that up. What the accounting of Cain's generations seems to be is that they're just people. With skills and trades, taking wives and having children and populating the world. Sinning, as all men sin. Even being wicked as Lamech. In the epistle of Jude, he writes of the common salvation, that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ....Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain... The way of Cain is the way of works, self-righteousness, wrath, giving way to sin, and stubbornness and stiff-necked willful refusal to accept the gift of common salvation, denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. Jude is warning against reprobates, who teach damnable heresy of works, and turning liberty into lasciviousness, using Cain as an example, the first reprobate. The first works-based heretic. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. Acts 2:21 And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call. The promise of eternal life in the Lord, who is our salvation. This is the faith which all man has been saved by, in Christ Jesus, since the world began. And as Enos' generation came to be, and the faith given the father's by God's word handed down, men began to call upon the name of the Lord for salvation. Jesus the same yesterday, today and forever. For my autistic brothers in Christ, this is 1,558 years from Adam to Shem. The chronogenealogies of Genesis 5 are given to provide times and understanding of the human nature of man, and to provide the direct lineage from Adam to Noah and his sons. Long-lived though they may have been, they lived, had children and died. They populated the earth. They all sinned whether sons of God or sons of man, whether they called upon the name of the Lord or rejected His salvation. But they lived and these were the span of years from creation to Noah and his sons. Biblical authority and fundamentalism should rest on rightly dividing the word of God, and taking what's given literally as literal, and what's parable, a picture or a symbol as figurative. These ages are given literally. It is odd how those who take the figurative literally, such as the Nicodemuses who gets caught up in misunderstood false doctrine taken from parables, almost invariably take the literal as symbolic, and most reject the specific accounting of years from creation to flood, to Christ. And so, taking the Bible literal where it's given to us literally, and going from Genesis 5 to Genesis 11:32, we get to Shem's descendant Terah, father of Abraham. Adding all of the provided years gives us a time span of about 2,008 years from Adam to Abraham. And from Matthew 1, we are given the generations from Abraham to Jesus Christ. So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations. The total of these generations isn't as precise but adds up to roughly 2,000 years to the first coming of the Messiah. As far as the Bible goes, we have recorded the rough years from creation to Christ, given, inspired and preserved by God. The time from Christ to now, the anno domini so to speak, well, that could be roughly 2022 years. It may not be. Missing time, garbled calendars, i's for 1's...I can't say. The calendar is not the preserved word of God. (I lean towards some centuries being faked and it being less time from Christ to now, but it's all speculation) But taking the given ~2020 years that is commonly accepted, this places the earth at just slightly more than 6,000 years old. Give or take a century or two. I have never seen anything convincing that suggests otherwise, through all the science so-called, and theories and theologies of man. In fact, given time, the wisdom of man invariably fails and is changed to fit new secular theories, unfalsifiable as they are. But God's word is the rock of our salvation, that we as believers build our faith and our lives upon. Unchanged and unchangeable. And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him. Hebrews 11:5 By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God. Jude 1:14-15 And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him. I've read that, when we look at these early patriarchs, we can see the pattern for salvation. Adam knows God, his creator, and knows his sin. Abel brings the blood of atonement, given in faith for redemption. Seth and Enos, that with the mouth, confession is made, calling upon the name of the Lord. And with Enoch, we have the testimony that he walked with God, that he lived separated, pleasing God. That each of us goes through these steps when we come to Christ and live for Him. An illustration given by God in His word, through the lives of these men. But what of Enoch? The seventh from Adam (not to be confused with Cain's son, 3rd from Adam), Enoch was a prophet. A preacher, who gave witness in the Spirit to Christ's victory on the day of the Lord. We know that by faith, he was transformed, translated that he should not see death. But this is the promise to all saved by faith in Jesus. John 8:51 Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death. So what then? What does scripture mean by saying he was "translated?" That he was not found? Does it mean bodily ascension? Literally taken by God, not just his bodily death? In John 3, Jesus says "no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven," referring to Himself. What then are we to take from this? Is there a hidden meaning to the story of Enoch? Can we dwell in ancient texts and Jewish fables searching for his fate? Certainly. Lots of rabbi holes to go down with his story. But what we can know from scripture is that Enoch walked with God, prophesying of Christ, and was pleasing to God. And draw inspiration to live in accordance to that ourselves, seeking to be similarly pleasing to God. In faith. In the Spirit. Not knowing death. And that's really all that matters. Hebrews 11:6 But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. Enoch had faith in God, he pleased God, he walked with God. He had eternal life. Simple as.

Here we arrive at the story of Noah, the flood and the destruction of man. Again, as we studied yesterday, only a short while, epochally speaking, after creation. And as I pointed out in yesterday's study, the story of the patriarchs from Adam to Noah is the pattern of salvation given to us by God. Here, Noah by faith builds the Ark, obeying God, and is saved from destruction, the earth cleansed of it's wickedness in a global baptism, itself a picture of the death, burial and resurrection of Christ. We see in Noah, a just man, perfect in his generations, who walked with God in the same way as Enoch, that Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord. Man has always been saved by grace through faith. The Bible says in Hebrews 11; By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith. But what of man? As the Bible says, man began to multiply on the earth, and daughters were born unto them. The sons of God took the daughters of man, being fair, attractive to the men, and the Lord surmised that man, being flesh would not always strive with Him, and to limit the wickedness of man, God began to shorten man's natural life. There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown. The Bible says there were giants in the earth in those days. And that after that, the sons of God came unto the daughters of man and bare children who were mighty men of renown. Note these are men. Of great stature, no doubt. Same as we see in Goliath, his people, and even occasionally today. The genetic potential of man being what it is, divinely made. And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. This is God's judgment of man. He is telling us it was the wickedness of man that repented Him of our creation. God repents, changes His mind given the outcome, and He seeks to destroy them and the earth for it too has become corrupt with the blood of the violence of men. But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord. This is the prologue to the generations of Noah. Now, having seen that the earth was corrupt and mankind hopelessly wicked, being flesh, being sinful and fallen since the garden, God seeks to destroy His creation, but for the sake of one just man, Noah, offers grace and gives a path to salvation. God looked upon the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth. And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth. As I wrote in a previous study on Genesis 4 and the murder of Abel, the concept that the earth itself becomes corrupt by our sin, by the spilling of innocent blood is established Biblical doctrine. Nations fall due to this very thing, and here we see all the earth has been made corrupt by man. God gives Noah a plan of salvation, instruction on the preparation of the ark, for him, his wife and his 3 sons and their wives. The size and type and purpose of the ark; to hold 2 of every living thing, male and female, for the salvation of the world. A covenant made to preserve them. And Noah did all that God commanded of him. The story of the flood as a judgment upon mankind is clear throughout that it is man's own wickedness that God is punishing. That within 8 generations, mankind had fallen so utterly that it had corrupted the earth itself. That only Noah had stayed faithful, God's Spirit striving with him, but not so that of man. It is humanity that has fallen. It is man that is corrupt and wicked of heart. The same as it was in the beginning as it is today. This is an important biblical doctrine to understand. Many false doctrines place evil as something that is 'other,' foreign, introduced by bloodlines or genetics or ancestry. That salvation is only for a certain people, elect by nothing other than genes. But we see in Genesis 6 that it is man's own wickedness that destroys us. That our flesh is what brings us to sin. That by faith in God, man can find grace and salvation. This is extremely important and is a tangential doctrine to the concept of free will and individual soul liberty/damnation. If man is irredeemable by genetics, then it is by a false calvinist god. If man, is saved by an inalienable quality bestowed by a creator, then he hasn't free will. If man is judged by other's sin, he hasn't the individual soul liberty to be saved by faith in Christ, being condemned by another's actions. Since the time of Adam in the garden, blaming his sin on Eve and God for creating her, man seeks to find an excuse to justify themselves before the Lord in His judgment. To push it off on the devil for offering temptation. To place it on the sins of another. But God knows our heart, and says the thoughts of man's heart was only evil continually. There is none righteous, no not one. And this understanding is the basis for the faith in God for salvation. The knowledge that to walk with God, to strive with His Spirit requires His grace and His promise of salvation. Not of ourselves, but as a gift of God. That we are wicked and sinful creatures, deserving death and Hell, and in need of saving. By placing the blame on external forces, even upon the demonic lineage of quasi-human chimeras, for example, we say "maybe it's not our fault God. After all, maybe it's not our fault." But God hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth. He made nations and habitations and divisions of people, but we are all one blood, given to the same temptation of the flesh, sinful nature, with free will and the need for salvation. And so, who are the sons of God? The Bible says as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name. Believers. Those that call upon the name of the Lord. For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope, Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. Those born again into the promise, adopted sons, heirs to the Kingdom of the Lord. Adopted now, as in the days of Seth and Enos and Enoch and even Noah; That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world. Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God! Take comfort in this knowledge, joy in the incomprehensible love God has shown us, that we may be adopted joint heirs with His only begotten Son, Christ Jesus. Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is. We know that all who believe are the sons of God. That we appear before God in Heaven to present ourselves before the Lord. When God laid Jesus as the cornerstone of our salvation, the angels sang and all the sons of God shouted for joy. And in Christ Jesus God has made His covenant with man, that He will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty. But what of angels, the creations of God who serve divine purpose? The hosts of heaven? Are they sons of God? The Bible definitively says no; For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son? And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire. ...For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak.But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands. And so we see that angels, while higher created beings than man, are in no way the sons of God, for they are below man in our dominion as sons of God. They aren't heirs to the promise. They are not partakers with Christ, they but serve God and His heirs, or rebel and tempt and accuse. Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation? And all angels are spirit, not flesh, and not made in the image and likeness of God. Jesus, describing their limitations as He spoke of our glorified bodies in the resurrection; For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven. The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage: But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection. And so, mindful of what the Bible says (and does not say), we can draw doctrine that counters the claim of half-human hybrids made of spiritual things copulating with daughters of men. Angels are servants of God, ministers to us that are saved in Christ. That we are His children, His sons. What love He has for us! Amen. One more application of the story of Noah, we should be mindful of the approaching judgement. Matthew 24:37-39 But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. We, like Noah, who are obedient to the Gospel, following God's instructions to our salvation, knowledgeable of the end times we are in, should be ever mindful that just as in the days of Noah, things continue as ever. Man is just as caught up in the things of this world, but we are mindful to keep watch of the skies for His return in glory

The Bible says that God's judgment came upon the wicked and the scoffers, and the corrupt earth tainted with the blood of violence and sin, and just Noah was saved, with his sons and their wives, along with the animals of the earth. That all flesh died otherwise in a global flood, waters pouring in from the skies like through open windows, up from the deep like a fountain, and covered the earth for 150 days. This is true. There are archeologies and secular histories that all confirm a global flood, relegated to 'myth' status but wondered about by natural men, seeking to confirm the story by natural means. We could go into the fossils of sealife found on top of Everest, or deposits of salt in high plateaus. The deluge changing the face of the earth in grand canyons and fiords and river beds. The common DNA, traced to the time of Noah. Etc. But the Bible says it's true, and that's enough. Scoffers laugh at the idea of Biblical Fundamentalism, and some believers take it personally and are embarrassed by the word of God, even as the science of man comes around to confirming the accounts of scripture. We shouldn't be moved but rather, those scoffers should be embarrassed by themselves and their own foolish hearts. The Bible tells us how we should act when facing them, and puts their fate in perspective for us; 1 Peter 3 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ. For it is better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing. For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water. The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ. Jesus was triumphantly shown in Hell before those that didn't believe, preaching His glory, leaving captivity captive. Noah and his family were given physical salvation as the scoffers and unbelievers who mocked God were swallowed up in the flood. 2 Peter 2 For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment; And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly; And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;) The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished: We are called to have the faith of Noah, who, having the grace of God extended to him, and faith in the Christ to come, believed God's promise of salvation. Building the ark, diligently and meekly, obeying the Lord. Like Lot, vexed by the filthy, sinful fallen man around him. Yet Noah stayed true, and God delivered him and destroyed the wicked, just as He will in the great day of the Lord. And so like Noah, by faith in God's word, we should stand ready, with an answer for our hope, meekly and with fear, standfast in the truth knowing God rewards those who diligently seek Him, and, despite all long suffering, delivers His wrath on the wicked. Amen.

While the earth remaineth... Noah and his ark of survivors ride out the flood, and the deluge abates, as God closes up the windows of heaven and the fountains of the deep. Noah's 601st birthday is marked while waiting to get God's blessing to disembark. The raven and the doves, sent by Noah, and the olive branch the dove returns with are taught in every Sunday school, that God offered an olive branch of peace to mankind. Reads a bit more into it than is there, but maybe. Nothing is incidental accidental or coincidental in scripture. The times given are details that mark this account as historical rather than symbolic or allegory. God rarely gives precise measures of time or place unless it is to create a hard record of events in scripture. So we know the days and the weeks and the months of the flood and the aftermath. The final resting place for the Ark, in Turkey. Mt Ararat. So many On Search Of's and History channel specials, claiming to have found the ark, but we know everything we need to from scripture.

God blesses Noah and his sons, gives commandments and a covenant with all living things in the earth. Blessings, commandments and promises. This is the pattern of things with God when those who are faithful and saved by His grace walk with God. God here tells Noah and his sons to be fruitful and multiply, birthing all nations of man. To that end, he reminds them that all animals are meat to eat, with no restrictions. Of the clean and unclean animals they may eat, but only the clean for sacrifice to God, being they represent Christ Jesus. As we saw in Chapter 7, Noah had seven pair, male and female of every clean beast, that he could give sacrifice in thanksgiving to God for saving his family in chapter 8. But there is no restriction on what they can eat, provided they drain the blood, the life thereof. Of that they should not eat. This was replaced for a time for Israel with strict dietary laws against eating unclean beasts under Mosaic law, which along with the priestly and carnal ordinances were done away with in Christ. God institutes the death penalty and capital punishment for the shedding of blood. Before the flood, from Cain on, the requirement for blood didn't exist, and evil propagated. Here, God established a new understanding for man; that we were to enforce His law, blood for blood for in the image of God made he man. God commands again that man be fruitful and multiply. Replenish the earth, bringing forth life abundantly. God promises all life that He would never destroy the earth and all living things again by flood. He gives the rainbow as His reminder, a token of the covenant between Him and the earth. And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth. And so the Bible tells us of Shem, and Ham, and Japheth (and that Ham is the father of Canaan). That of these three were the whole earth overspread. The next chapter of Genesis will go into detail of the generations and nations of them, but for the next part of chapter 9, we need to know Ham's offspring Canaan. Noah, retired from ark building, becomes a husbandman, a grower of grapes. The Bible says he drank his own wine and became drunk, and that Ham saw his nakedness as he was passed out in his tent, and that he called his brothers to see. There is a lot of speculation as to what this means. Most agree that Ham did something unspeakable to Noah in his condition. The Bible doesn't say that and, generally, God's word isn't shy about naming the acts done by the wicked. The implication comes from Noah's reaction and punishment, which is severe. Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done unto him. And he said, Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren. He curses Canaan to be servants of Shem and of Japheth. The nations that spring from each son. He blesses Shem with the blessing of the Lord God, as the oldest. This is the blessing of Christ through his seed. And he blesses Japheth with abundance, to be enlarged greatly. And curses Ham's son Canaan to be their servants. There is a lot of speculative theology based off this curse. Eustice Mullins book, the Curse of Canaan is worth reading, even if his sourcing and Biblical scholarship is lacking in some points, and some of his conclusions aren't supported in scripture. He does give a good overview of concepts people have drawn from this story. It's a secular take on a spiritual matter, so take it with the appropriate grains of salt. Noah lives 350 years following the flood, a total of 950, but he is the last of the antediluvian long-lived men. There are, of course, deeper things of God, His promises and blessings, the salvation of Christ mirroring the salvation of the ark. Spiritual applications from the story of the flood and its immediate aftermath, but the predominantly secular focus on hidden meaning, esoteric knowledge, the hyperfocus on race and genealogies of man, conspiracies and Jewish fables have all but flooded out those truths in the minds of man. Even saved Christians get sucked in to endless strivings about the meaning of some of what's revealed to us in God's word. We add to it our own preconceived or preprogrammed ideas. Or get caught up in things like the Jewish highjacking to impose their wicked schemes on us. What's important to Bible believing Christians is to draw spiritual application from scripture, to understand the things of God which He revealed to us from the beginning. Mercy, judgement, grace and salvation. The fallen nature of man and the prevalence of sin while we are in the flesh. The righteousness of the living God. Today, as we give thanks to God for our salvation and the blessings He bestows, the same way Noah gave thanks after leaving the ark, we should try to keep in mind the spiritual, looking forward to that better country, and the feast of Christ Jesus, knowing that man's relationship with God has always been, from the beginning. Amen

And so we have the division of man into races and nations. 70 different ethnic tribes, descended from the 3 sons of Noah. God commanded them to be fruitful and replenish the earth. Much has been made of this account, and conclusions drawn from the curse of Canaan through Ham, the Ashkenaz being of Japheth not Shem, etc. I won't lie, when the Bible gets into lists of names I glaze over. Genealogies tell me that scripture is a historical account of man. That God sets the nations and their borders and habitations thereof. That God judges nations of men on earth, blessing them, cursing them and at times erasing them. That when the nations unite under a one world government of men, they challenge God. And so God scatters them. But I know for many of my more spergy frens, these lists and maps fascinate. The speculation of men like Josephus and later historians to trace the migration and evolution of the 70 original nations to today are very popular. Have at it.

All of Genesis, as important as the stories of Adam, Cain, Noah, the flood and Babel are, was prologue to this. The story of Abram and Sarai. Abraham and Sarah. Up to this point, mankind who called upon the name of the Lord had the promise of His blessing and protection, of God being their savior, but not the specific promise of the man Christ Jesus. Born of man. Seed of Abraham. Here we see that the LORD appears unto Abram and makes him promises. - I will make of thee a great nation - I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing - I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: - and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed. These are direct blessings and promises to Abram, himself. This is found no where in Scripture. This is God's promise to protect him and his wife, as God has called Abraham to go to a different land, to Canaan, and there He would establish his legacy. And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and the souls that they had gotten in Haran; and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan. There, God appeared again to him, and gave this more specific promise; Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the Lord, who appeared unto him. And Abram called upon the name of the Lord. He was saved by faith through grace. Note the timing of when that was. It comes up later in scripture. This promise was made to a 75yr old, childless Abram in a place where the Canaanite was then in the land. His altar built between the Mediterranean and Jordan, between Galilee and Jerusalem. The LORD appearing to Abraham is considered by many to be an Old Testament appearance of Jesus. A theophany. As the Bible says at no time has man seen the Father, many consider the appearance of God unto man in the OT a representation of Christ, who was from the beginning with God and is God. Chapter 13 of Genesis brings Abram and Sarai and his nephew Lot back to the land of Canaan, back to where Abram called upon the name of the Lord, near Bethel, which is on the West bank of the Jordan, in the area of Jerusalem and Bethlehem. There, scripture reminds us, he had built an altar. Because of the greatness of his herds and Lot's, and growing contentions between each other's herdsmen, he gives Lot a choice of grazing land, and Lot chooses the area around the plains of the Jordan, just above what's called the Dead Sea today. Given the choice, and seeing there was much water and vegetation, even as the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt. And so enticed, he pitches his tent there to the east, towards Sodom. There's many times in life we are given a choice like this, and choosing from ease or greed or comfort, we pitch our tents towards Sodom, towards wickedness and sin. There's a spiritual application there. Abram, meanwhile, settles down to Hebron and the plains of Mamre. And God gives Abram two more promises, all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever, and I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth, too numerous to count. The Bible says in Galatians 3:16 Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ. Christ is the answer to the promises, kept by God. Jesus is the seed through whom all nations are blessed. It is in Jesus that the promised land is given forever, to those who believe and call upon the name of the Lord. It is in this seed that Abram can be said to have fathered a people too numerous to count, saved sons of God. Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar unto the Lord. The Oak of Abraham, located in modern day Hebron, along the plains of Mamre, on the West Bank, is said to be thousands of years old. Traditions of men claim when it dies, it would signify the birth of the antichrist. It died in 1996. Thinking about the times in my life where rather than do what needed to be done to end strife, or to get through problems with myself or others, I instead pitched my tent towards Sodom. Trusting in a perceived gain over doing what was right. Choosing selfishly, rather than in grace. And often lured by the promise of worldly and carnal gains, ignoring the sin of those around me, (and so ignoring my own), I did what Lot did when given a choice. And much like just Lot who separated himself from righteous Abram, dwelled among the men of Sodom, throwing my lot (👀) in with men who were wicked and sinners before the Lord exceedingly. This temptation to choose the easy path leads to backsliding and often, to destruction. To years and talents and influence wasted that could have been in service to God and being a blessing to my people. And if I didn't make it clear, pay attention to the order of events here. It is after Lot chooses to pitch his tent towards Sodom that God appears to Abram and gives him additional blessings, reinforcing His promise. This is how it usually works.

Genesis 20 tells a familiar story, Abraham and Sarah lying about being brother and sister while sojourning in another nation. We were just reading a similar account in Genesis 12, where they went to Egypt to flee a famine, acting out of fear, and compounding his sin, Abraham lied to Pharaoh about being married to fair Sarah. Here, they sojourn in Gerar, a nearby kingdom and their ruler, Abimelech sent and took Sarah, believing she was not married to Abraham. We learn that this tactic, lying, wasn't a one-off, or even a two-off. Abraham actually tells Sarah: This is thy kindness which thou shalt shew unto me; at every place whither we shall come, say of me, He is my brother. Righteous Abraham. Father to us all who believe on Christ Jesus. Who with perfect faith believed God would spare or raise Isaac, whom he was prepared to sacrifice on an altar by faith. Great Abraham. And he struggled with sin and faith, repeatedly. He lies, the Bible says, because she is fair (even elderly in years), and he believes that these nations he's sojourning in are godless heathens who would kill him as husband to take his wife. He leaves the land God gave him out of fear. In Genesis 12, fear of famine. And he concocts a lie about Sarah out of fear. And, at least twice, it bites him in the butt and God has to bail him out. This should be a great lesson for us, especially those of us who aren't as righteous as Abraham. If he, a mighty man of faith, called "a friend of God," struggled with sin and fear. Who is embarrassingly caught in the same lie more than once, recorded forever in the preserved word of God, then we can know the same is true of us. We all have sin in our lives that we struggle with. It is different for each person, and at various times in our life. Some old sins we conquer with the help of God's word and the Spirit within, while others we may pick up a long the way. For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. We shouldn't be puffed up in our righteousness, hypocritically fruit inspecting other believing Christians to compare our own righteousness against theirs. Because we all sin and our righteousness is as filthy rags, the Bible says. But by grace are we saved, and the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ covers us all. This doesn't mean to not judge, but to judge while understanding our own failings. Showing mercy and grace as God has shown us. If Abraham struggled with fear and dishonesty, at certain times and situations, understand that we too likewise struggle. But we can also see that God saves us regardless of our fear or lack of faith. He chastises those he loves and scourges every son. He often will expose us to embarrassment and humiliation in exposing our sin. But it is to our benefit, as it is here for Abraham. Now, when Abraham is outed by Abimelech, whom God visited in a dream to reveal the truth of Abraham's lie, Abimelech is wroth with anger, because he had taken Sarah in the integrity of my heart and innocency of my hands. He was actually a God-fearing king, of a righteous nation. He believed God would have killed him had He not kept the king from knowing Sarah, and committing adultery. He was righteously angry at Abraham for putting himself and his nation at risk. When confronted, Abraham says essentially, well, I was telling a half-truth, we are married but she's my half sister. Daughter of his father Terah and a different mother. Now this is held dogmatically by many, that Abraham and Sarah were half-siblings, sharing the same father. But this is the only instance where this appears in scripture, and it's Abraham caught in one lie by an angry king, told under duress. We cannot assume she is Terah's daughter just because Abraham says it. Unless God or someone in the Spirit speaking for God says it, we have to look at context to see if what they're saying is true, or the truth from their perspective, or possibly a lie or rationalization. But, Abraham does make the claim. It is possible that he's telling the truth, but it's not enough to draw a definitive conclusion. Oh, and I did what I just warned against in believing everything a human says in the Bible as truth, Abimelech and his Nation were not righteous, as in saved believers, just because he said so. Their nation is listed as being near Sodom and Gomorrah and clearly if you're kidnapping women passing through your land and making them your wife, forcing yourself upon them, you're not doing right by God. But it's clear that Abimelech was God fearing. That he understood the real God, His laws, and knew the curses that would come upon him for committing adultery in that manner. Had to think about that for a minute. Again it's important to compare scripture to see if something is so.
