And so Moses became a prophet of God. Jehovah. I AM THAT I AM. The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. The living God. Moses was neither Egyptian nor suffering as a Hebrew, living as a shepherd. Doubtful that his brethren would believe him, given they questioned him; Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? And yet it was him who the Lord chose to confound Pharaoh and free His people from bondage. A picture of Christ. God's promise is that not only would they become free, but spoil Egypt as they left. Taking the treasure of the Egyptians and the land of the Canaanites, overflowing with milk and honey. And so Moses entered into this covenant with God. Note that like the patriarchs before him, when Moses is called by God his reply is "here am I." The difference between here am I and here I am is that of being called as a servant and appearing before the Lord ready to do His will, vs giving your location, your current circumstance, where you've ended up. It's this distinction we should keep in mind when God calls us to His service. When God's will is to be done. That we answer "Here am I." Thinking of the retelling of his story in Acts, where Moses had set out as an adult to visit the Hebrews in their affliction, and ended up murdering the Egyptian taskmaster and being rejected as a judge by his people, and then in chapter 3 being called by God to do just that, and you can see how when Moses sought to put himself in that position, by his own will, he failed. Up to this event, we were given Moses' life story, which like most biography in the Bible, is short and spans decades in a few verses, giving us only what God believes we need to get the picture, and gain understanding. We saw Moses being raised in both worlds, a prince of Egypt and as a Hebrew. And how when he reached his prime, Moses went forth to see his brethren in their affliction. To be as a judge, or deliverer to his people under his terms. And he immediately murders a taskmaster, badly hides the body in sand, his sin covered by dust. The people mock him for it, Pharaoh orders him killed, and Moses flees to the land of Midian for decades. When God calls to him, and gives Moses this task of bringing the Israelites out of bondage, and God gives this covenant and promise to Moses; Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain. But Moses immediately begins to question God. Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt? Who shall I say called me? What name for you shall I give? He didn't want to return to his greatest failure. He did not want to do God's will. Where Moses had failed on his own, he doesn't have the faith in God's promise that where he failed, God won't. That God uses the weak to confound the strong. That lo, I am with you to the end of the world. And so, chapter 4 has even more objections to his calling. More excuses to not serve God and do His will. Moses says no one will believe him. God answers and says, what do you have in your hand? Moses answers his rod. A shepherds crook. The simple tool that he gathers his flock with. Moses' excuse that none will follow him, that he's not equipped for the task, is answered by God; that the Lord will use whatever it is you have on hand, He provides the rest that He receives the glory. Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, what ye shall drink...What ye shall say... So God shows Moses that his staff will turn to a serpent at his command so that the people who doubt will believe He sent him. (except hard-hearted Pharaoh) And the Lord said furthermore unto him, Put now thine hand into thy bosom. And God shows him that Moses' hand will turn leprous and be healed. And God promises the reluctant Moses; And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe thee, neither hearken to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign. But wait, there's more! God tells Moses that he will have the power to turn the water to blood when it is cast on dry land. God has given Moses assurance of His word, the name by which the people may call upon, the power to do wonders and signs. And Moses says, yeah, but I'm not really an elegant speaker. He has another excuse. Not only an excuse, but a lie. Acts 7:22 says of Moses; And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds. So his claim to not be able to lead due to his being "slow of tongue" is just another excuse not to do the will of God. But to this, God already has an answer: Who hath made man's mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I the Lord? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say. Just as Jesus instructs His disciples to not take heed for what they shall say, that the Holy Ghost will put His words in their mouths, so too promises God to Moses. And stubborn Moses says; O my Lord, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send. He tells God to send someone else. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Moses. We are all called to do the will of the Father. To believe the gospel of Jesus Christ, first and foremost. But then to follow His commandments that we may be well in this life. That we may be vessels by which His will is done. To go out and give the good news to others, being a light that draws those seeking truth to the right paths. To give the gospel to every creature. To lead those in bondage of sin out of spiritual Egypt and to the promised land, the kingdom of Heaven. And for many of us, for much of our lives, we are like Moses. We have every excuse in the book not to go. We fear no one will believe us. That we don't have the skills. That we don't have the ability to say the right things. That we aren't capable. But God has already told us in His word, from the red letters in our Bible, "Take no thought...lo, I am with you until the end of the world." We are promised that we will know what to say, the Holy Spirit bringing all things to remembrance. That some may be hard hearted, but that's ok. Those who hear His voice and know Him will believe. That we have the tools already with us to serve Him. That we have been shaped upon God's potter's wheel to be what vessels He needs us to be to serve His purpose. We just need to stop making excuses and go forth to do His will. Imagine having the anger of the Lord kindled against you because you're full of excuses? And so, in His righteous anger God has had enough of Moses' excuses and says, look I will have your brother Aaron speak for you. I will tell you what to say, and he will be your spokesman. He tells Moses he shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do signs. He is done listening to the excuses, He has an answer for every one of them. And Moses concedes, and submits to God's will. He also tells Moses as an afterthought that all those seeking him for the murder he committed are dead. It's safe to return. And the Lord said unto Moses, When thou goest to return into Egypt, see that thou do all those wonders before Pharaoh, which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go. And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn: And I say unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me: and if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn. Simple as. And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the Lord met him, and sought to kill him. That escalated quickly! Moses sought to return to Egypt to lead the people out of captivity with the word of God that they may believe and signs and wonders that they may know, but his own son he had not brought into the covenant of Abraham. Zipporah cuts the foreskin off their son and casts it at Moses' feet. Angry that she had to tend to this bloody business, maybe even angry that she was being uprooted to go with him back to Egypt. Maybe their son wasn't circumcised because she opposed it, and backslidden Moses went along to avoid this kind of confrontation with his wife. That's the application I take from it, the final excuse many of us have against doing God's will for us is the anger and confrontation we will have with loved ones. The division of family Jesus warned about in the gospels. But it is clear Zipporah isn't happy about any of it. We may be similarly hindered in our Christian walk by loved ones and relatives who aren't where we are spiritually. Who may be unsaved or have the cares of the world in their hearts. Who put the carnality of life before serving God. And at some point, God will seek our lives for being castaway, for putting their objections over God's will. For our being half in and half out. Lukewarm. Finally, the Lord sends Aaron to meet Moses in the wilderness on the way to Egypt, and they are reconciled and begin the work of the Lord. And the people believed: and when they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped. Because faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Amen

Matthew 5:10-12 Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you. Moses and Aaron go before the Pharaoh, and speak the words God had gave them; allow the Israelites a 3 day release from their labors that they may assemble to worship Him. (3 days without labor, works, just as we see during Christ's death, burial and resurrection). And as God said, Pharaoh's heart was hardened and he not only said no, but added to the people's labors, making them gather their own straw for brick, while keeping the same expectations for output. And the taskmasters over them tell the people that it is due to Moses and Aaron's plea that they be allowed free to go and worship God. And the people turn to criticize Moses, who in turn goes before the Lord and asks why God has not instantly freed them, and instead made their situation worse. As we have already seen, Moses is not the most stalwart man of faith, and the people, as we will continually see, are stiff-necked and impatient with the Lord. But we are called to be faithful and long suffering. To understand that God's timing is perfect and ours is lacking. To take joy in being persecuted for His name. This is an important factor that needs to be reinforced, especially today. God didn't lead with freeing the nation of Israel from the Egyptians. He didn't begin with plagues and curses. He led with "let my people worship." From that point on, everything that happens to the Egyptians is due to their reaction to this plea. The persecution of His people will be for His name's sake. This has to be every Christians starting point. Regardless of how harshly we are treated, make it be for God's sake. For Jesus' name. Not because we are riotous. Not because we will render evil for evil. But because our oppressors despise the Lord. When we are delivered from this persecution, it will be by God's hand in His time, by His wrath. Vengeance is His that all glory may go to Him. And if we must suffer, rejoice. Psalms 20:7 Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God. Psalm 144:5-15 Bow thy heavens, O Lord, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke. Cast forth lightning, and scatter them: shoot out thine arrows, and destroy them. Send thine hand from above; rid me, and deliver me out of great waters, from the hand of strange children; Whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood. I will sing a new song unto thee, O God: upon a psaltery and an instrument of ten strings will I sing praises unto thee. It is he that giveth salvation unto kings: who delivereth David his servant from the hurtful sword. Rid me, and deliver me from the hand of strange children, whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood: That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace: That our garners may be full, affording all manner of store: that our sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets: That our oxen may be strong to labour; that there be no breaking in, nor going out; that there be no complaining in our streets. Happy is that people, that is in such a case: yea, happy is that people, whose God is the Lord. And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose. And the officers of the children of Israel did see that they were in evil case, after it was said, Ye shall not minish ought from your bricks of your daily task. And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh: And they said unto them, The Lord look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us. The elders of Israel, its failed human leaders, take to task Moses and Aaron who, having done what God told them to do, even saying what God told them to say. Remember in Exodus 4: And Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel: And Aaron spake all the words which the Lord had spoken unto Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people. And the people believed: and when they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped. God had told Moses that Pharaoh would not allow them to go to worship Him. Moses told Aaron all of what God told him, and Aaron spake all the words. They knew it wasn't going to be as easy. But at the first sign of tribulation, the elders come against Moses and Aaron for preaching and doing God's word. And they say "you have made our savour abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh." These leaders are more concerned with how they look to the world than to God. But look what Paul writes in 2 Corinthians 2:15-17: For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish: To the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things? For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ. To the world, we stink like death, because we remind them that they are perishing, but our obedience to God in Christ is a sweet savour unto the Lord. We shouldn't worry about what the world thinks of us, even if it means persecution. We need to remember that all things, not some things, not a few things, not only good things, but ALL things work together for good to them that love God.

Picking up from the end of chapter 5, where Moses, feeling defeated by the rejection of the elders after Pharaoh's abuse, turns to God and asks; Wherefore hast thou so evil entreated this people? why is it that thou hast sent me? For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done evil to this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all. And the LORD answers him, saying I am Jehovah. The same who appeared unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. God Almighty. And the Lord recounts His covenant He made with them regarding the promised land. He reminds Moses that He has heard His people's groaning from bondage, and in it remembering His covenant, seeks to free them. He reiterates the deal He made with the patriarchs, and says; I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with a stretched out arm, and with great judgments: And I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God: and ye shall know that I am the Lord your God, which bringeth you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians. And I will bring you in unto the land, concerning the which I did swear to give it to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it you for an heritage: I am the Lord. This covenant is offered by God through Moses to the children of Israel, and they reject it for their anguished spirit. But God persists that Moses go unto Pharaoh, and tell him to Let My people go. Rejected and dejected, Moses asks how will Pharaoh hear me when the Israelites won't even believe? Basically asking who am I that they should listen? And God answers to Moses and Aaron, with their Levite genealogy and the genealogies of the heads of the houses of Ruben and Simeon, from who they are from and or married to. These are that Aaron and Moses, to whom the Lord gave charge to bring the children of Israel out of Egypt. That they are who the Lord told to go to Pharaoh and speak all that Moses was told to say. Basically God answers Moses doubt with a statement of facts, which should be sufficient for Moses. That this is the will of God and he is chosen to do this. "Because I said so." He has chosen Moses of these generations to be the means of salvation to the people. And Moses said before the Lord, Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh hearken unto me? The Lord answers Moses in the next chapter with a foreshadowing of Jesus Christ.

If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God. God tells Moses he will be like a god unto Pharaoh, and Aaron his prophet, to be the salvation of His people, freeing them from their burdens and delivering them to the promised land. This picture of Christ Jesus our Lord and deliverer, John the Baptist His prophet, bringing salvation to the faithful, free from the burdens of sin and death, given to the promised land, the Kingdom of Heaven. It is a beautiful foreshadowing, done for our edification and as an example that we may know the mind of God. 1 Corinthians 10 Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; 2 And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea; 3 And did all eat the same spiritual meat; 4 And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ. 5 But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness. 6 Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted. 7 Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play. 8 Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand. 9 Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents. 10 Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer. 11 Now all these things happened unto them for examples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come. 2 Timothy 3:16-17 All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works. The events of the Old Testament are all pictures of those of the New, that we may be thoroughly furnished unto all good works. Just as all of creation exists as a parable, that we may understand the truth of God, without excuse. Understanding this, and knowing that Moses is a picture of Jesus, the physical deliverance from Egypt by God's mercy, the like picture as a believers spiritual salvation from sin. We are able to draw parallel with the crossing of the Red Sea to baptism, the promised land to Heaven. These foreshadowings are there to edify and guide us. An example. And so too is Pharaoh. In him we witness the Reprobate Doctrine played out. We see how there are those who, haven been given the chance to know God and be healed, refuse. Who prefer a lie to the truth. Who after attempts to be reached are rejected, and signs and conviction by the Holy Spirit are ignored, God is through with them. They are given up and given over. For this cause they are given strong delusion. For this cause their conscience is seared. They harden their hearts to God's attempts to extend His mercy and grace to them, and in turn God hardens their hearts that they cannot believe. They are done, being twice-dead. Sons of Belial. Just as the Israelites will harden their hearts in the wilderness and forget the God that freed them, and so we're denied the promised land. God decides when. He knows the beginning to the end, and knows who will reject him utterly, and STILL sends His prophets to preach, and the wrath of nature to show them, and still they refuse, and so He cuts them off. The rejection of this Biblical truth has set at odds modern Christians with the judgment of God. Thinking themselves wise, they became fools. They accept wolves among the sheep. Men crept in unawares. Who have the appearance of righteousness but inwards are open graves, full of death. Acts 20:29-31 For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock. Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them. Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears. Paul spent 3 years warning the Christians at Ephesus, with tears, against the reprobate wolves who would come in behind him, and who would spare not the flock, yet modern Christians don't hear a peep from most pastors about this very topic, and, if anything, those pastors invite in every wolf in an effort to please the world. John 12:40 He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; That they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, And be converted, And I should heal them. 2 Thessalonians 2:11-12 And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness. Romans 1 18 For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; 19 Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. 20 For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: 21 Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. 22 Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, 23 And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. 24 Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: 25 Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. 26 For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: 27 And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. 28 And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Hebrews 3 8 Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness: 9 When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years. 10 Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways. 11 So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.) 12 Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. 13 But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. 14 For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end; 15 While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.

2 Timothy 3:6-9 For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts, Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as their's also was. Revelation 22:18 For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book Deuteronomy 28:58-68 If thou wilt not observe to do all the words of this law that are written in this book, that thou mayest fear this glorious and fearful name, The Lord Thy God; Then the Lord will make thy plagues wonderful, and the plagues of thy seed, even great plagues, and of long continuance, and sore sicknesses, and of long continuance. Moreover he will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt, which thou wast afraid of; and they shall cleave unto thee. Also every sickness, and every plague, which is not written in the book of this law, them will the Lord bring upon thee, until thou be destroyed. And ye shall be left few in number, whereas ye were as the stars of heaven for multitude; because thou wouldest not obey the voice of the Lord thy God. And it shall come to pass, that as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you; so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you, and to bring you to nought; and ye shall be plucked from off the land whither thou goest to possess it. And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone. And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind: And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life: In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning! for the fear of thine heart wherewith thou shalt fear, and for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see. And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you. Hebrews 10:31 It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. The story of the deliverance of the Israelites from Egypt continues, and the plagues of God increase against Pharaoh and the Egyptians. And still Pharaoh hardens his heart against the truth of the Lord, given to Moses and prophesied by Aaron. Keeping in mind that this history is a parable of salvation and the spiritual state of man, we have seen the word of God given to man, through His chosen redeemer. A promise of deliverance from bondage and towards the promised land, a paradise of milk and honey, which is given to all who believe. But there are those who refuse to believe. Who harden their hearts, even as the Spirit of the Lord convicts and rebukes them. Even as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, the court magicians to Pharaoh, who manage to stage copycat wonders through their sorcery. Tricks. Slight of hand given them by the Devil that Pharaoh would have doubt, refusing to believe Moses. Even they eventually give up, unable to duplicate the wonders of God. It is fitting that Paul mentions these sorcerers in the context of reprobates concerning the faith. Those who creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins. Ever learning. Never coming to the truth. Like false prophets, these wizards have the appearance of Godliness, His power, sufficient to fool those who aren't saved, who lack discernment. Enough to get others to harden their hearts to the truth of the knowledge of God. Paul warns Timothy against such people for a reason. God gives us the example of Pharaoh for a reason. As much as the story of Exodus is a picture of salvation in Christ, it covers the entire gambit of human reaction to this gift of grace given us by God. The believers who praise God when they hear Moses and Aaron tell them of His promise to free them from bondage. The scoffers in the secular leadership of the people. The mixed multitudes, many who aren't of the chosen people, but go along with them. The Reprobate, like Pharaoh. The unsaved Egyptians who remain behind, in sin. It's all there. We should heed the warnings and obey the Gospel and understand the nature of man. Be wise as serpents and harmless as lambs. Watch for ravenous wolves who spare not the flock, and bring whole houses to ruin. Because, if we don't get the full picture, we run the risk of our children falling to the wolves. Turning from the Lord. Hardening their hearts and having the plagues of the book, God's wrath kindled, and turned on them.

For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. I wrote this in response to Calvinists objecting to the reprobate doctrine, but it serves as a good guide to how Pharaoh is given as an example of a reprobate, even as the children of Israel are given as those saved by faith in Christ, Egypt as sin, sin as bondage, etc... It is all given to show us the doctrine of salvation.

John 12:37-40 But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him: That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed? Therefore they could not believe, because that Esaias said again, He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them. 1 Thessalonians 2:14-16 For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judaea are in Christ Jesus: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Jews: Who both killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God, and are contrary to all men: Forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they might be saved, to fill up their sins alway: for the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost. The plagues against Egypt continue. We see Pharaoh's heart has been hardened. He cannot believe God's word, even to his own destruction and the destruction of his people. And even as Moses is a picture of Christ, and the physical salvation of the Israelites from bonds in Egypt are a picture of spiritual salvation from sin and the bonds of the law, Pharaoh is a picture of a reprobate, and the Jews who deny Christ. Just as Pharaoh refused to allow the children of Israel to go and worship God as He commanded, the Jews persecute Christians, forbidding the Gospel to be preached that they may be saved. In a like manner, those who call themselves Jews have had their hearts hardened, and also have had the curse of God's wrath upon them, to the uttermost, even when it brings about their destruction.

This is it, the final plague is given to Moses that the wonders of God may be multiplied in Egypt. The Lord will send the angel of death to take the firstborn of every house, even the beasts. God says "ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel." The picture of sin, Egypt, is become death. The picture of Israel, of being God's people, is life and freedom from the burden of sin. We see in this that reprobation is real, and final. God has taken Pharaoh's hardened heart and made it so he cannot believe the word of God. But Moses found favor in the eyes of the people and those Israelites were given favor in the Egyptians eyes that they should spoil Egypt by taking with them their treasure. Just as the meek, the humble, the believers in Christ will inherit the earth in the millennium, spoiling all nations. Amen.

Just a few weeks ago, we did a studyon Exodus 12 and Luke 22, the ordinance of Passover the Lord's supper which replaced it. The foreshadowing of the feast, the burnt offering, the blood of the lamb without blemish. I recommend checking it out. Everything in the Old Testament, but especially the Passover and Exodus of the people from Egypt, point directly to Christ. Unbelief is sin and death. But faith brings salvation from the bonds of sin and the promise of a better country. I find it interesting that in spoiling Egypt, where the people gave the Israelites their gold and treasure, would ultimately become grievous sin in the wilderness, melted down to form the image of the calf the Hebrews worshipped while Moses was on Mt Sinai with God. Is that a picture of the blessings we have as saved Christians, which by not staying with the word of the Lord, not walking in the new man with the remembrance of the bondage God freed us from in Christ, that we risk turning to sin; into idols? How often we forget our deserved fate. How often we forget what should have happened to us based on our choices, and spared the worst of the consequences by God in His mercy through Christ Jesus. I don't know a saved Christian, no matter how backslidden and carnal, who when pressed won't admit that God saved them physically from the most grave of consequences they rightly deserved. Moving things in our life in such a way that we were delivered from the fruit of our sin, as we gained faith. But many forget when it's not present in their mind. Many take their blessings for granted and turn their comfort into an excuse to sin. There are people who have relatively easy lives and yet never come to peace with their life and the choices they made. And so they are miserable. We who are saved are blessed, that we can come to terms with it and understand what a blessing things actually are when you consider how bad it could be given the choices we've made. The humility and perspective we gain by understanding just how pitiful our position was that we trusted in God and called upon the name of the Lord, should allow us to see the bondage He freed us from and appreciate the wilderness He's led us through on our way to the promised land. God spares us by saving us from ourselves. His hand is constantly upon us. Like the Hebrews. His light, guiding us in the darkness. His bread, His word, come down from Heaven to feed and nourish us like manna. And like the Hebrews, we often complain at the hardships we must endure to get ourselves back to the place God has intended for us had we not sojourned in Egypt. Had we not chased after sin. We forget where we were. We forget how we escaped. We forget how the blood of the lamb upon our hearts, as it was upon the doorposts, spared us from destruction. We melt down the treasure God provided, and, as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play. We require an ordinance. A memorial. That our children's children can ask, why do we observe this? That we never forget or grow comfortable in our own conceits. To walk with God, feeding the new man, because the old man remains, calling us back to Egypt. To sin. We join with an assembly of believers, all who have been set at liberty from the same bondage, spared the same fate. We break bread and give thanks, in memory of Jesus and His sacrifice for us. We share the cup, of His blood spilled out for us. We need to be reminded that we not take our salvation for granted. A lot of new Christians, and many not-so-new, will become frustrated and despair that when they got saved, and began "turning their life around," that they still had to endure the pain and hard work of getting up out of the hole their old man had dug for them with their sin. But that hole was a grave. And in it was death. And God has given us the rope to climb out of it, and the light above to guide us from the darkness. That while the worst consequences are mitigated, and miraculous opportunities to escape are granted them, there is still a process of shedding sin in their life. There is still lost opportunity and easier paths lost to them by their choices. There's still a price to pay in this world. People sometimes can only see the walls of the hole they are in, and the light above seems small and distant. And the climb difficult, to where they take occasion to despise the rope they've been given. And they backslide. Sometimes God shakes the rope to draw their attention and get them back focused on the light. As we will see with the children of Israel, that sometimes we see falling back into sin, going back to servitude in Egypt, as easier than getting right with God. And God will remind us the foolishness of this. Harshly. My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of his correction: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth Acts 3:22-23 For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you. And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people. Hebrews 11:23-29 By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment. By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward. By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible. Through faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of blood, lest he that destroyed the firstborn should touch them. By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were drowned. John 5:46-47 For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?

And so commanded God to all of Israel. To commemorate the day He freed them from bondage and brought them out to the land He promised their fathers, and gave ordinances regarding the feast of unleavened bread, the removal of all yeast and leavening from the home for 7 days, and the consecration of the firstborn males, in remembrance of the slaying of the firstborn of Egypt and as a picture of the Christ to come. Leaven represents sin in the Bible. Egypt, bondage to sin. This is done in remembrance of God, just as the Lord's supper took the place of Passover, and Jesus took the place of the lamb without blemish. And so going forward, Israelites were to offer sacrifice of the first born, and in place of their first born, to sacrifice them. Jews today claim the bar mitzvah, the purchase of sanctification by use of silver shekels, is the equivalent of the blood sacrifice required by God, because they don't worship Him or follow the Old Testament at all. They worship moloch, and follow the traditions of men. The idea of parents instilling in their firstborn male the knowledge of Him, and what He has done for Israel is important. God needed them to retain knowledge of Him and His Promises in mind throughout generations, that in the days of Jesus, a remnant may be saved. God, with a fiery pillar by night and a pillar of smoke as a cloud, by day, took the Israelites and the mixed multitudes our, towards the Red Sea, that they not pass through the land of the Philistines, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt. We see this in newly saved Christians lives, all the time. There is an effort by God to guide us away from the worst tribulation in the beginning, that our faith grows, so we don't immediately turn back to sin. To bondage of the law. We know from the parable of the sower that even this period of the newness of the joy of salvation isn't enough for many. That the joy and relief can give way to the cares of the world. Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away. And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them. Not everyone who is saved is fertile ground. Many fall away or become offended by and by. That is why the Apostles were so intent on edification. On walking in the new man. Even David, the apple of God's eye, felt this: Psalm 51:12-14 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee. Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness. But by keeping in memory the strong arm of the Lord that has lifted us out of bondage by His own works, by the atonement and sanctification given us by Christ's blood, His death burial and resurrection, we will not repent towards Egypt, but press on to the promised land.

Is not this the word that we did tell thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness. Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord. Psalms 46:10 Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth. Psalm 28:7 The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him. 1 Corinthians 10:1-4 Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea; And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ. Psalm 27 The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the Lord is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid? 2 When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes, came upon me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell. 3 Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident. 4 One thing have I desired of the Lord, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to enquire in his temple. 5 For in the time of trouble he shall hide me in his pavilion: in the secret of his tabernacle shall he hide me; he shall set me up upon a rock. 6 And now shall mine head be lifted up above mine enemies round about me: therefore will I offer in his tabernacle sacrifices of joy; I will sing, yea, I will sing praises unto the Lord. 7 Hear, O Lord, when I cry with my voice: have mercy also upon me, and answer me. 8 When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, Thy face, Lord, will I seek. 9 Hide not thy face far from me; put not thy servant away in anger: thou hast been my help; leave me not, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation. 10 When my father and my mother forsake me, then the Lord will take me up. 11 Teach me thy way, O Lord, and lead me in a plain path, because of mine enemies. 12 Deliver me not over unto the will of mine enemies: for false witnesses are risen up against me, and such as breathe out cruelty. 13 I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living. 14 Wait on the Lord: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the Lord Read the scriptures and be still, knowing the salvation of the Lord is true, that He will be your strength and shield and take Vengeance on your enemies, while He carries you to the promised land. Don't repent at troubles. Don't turn back to Egypt. Don't lament your tribulations, but give glory to God for His strength will carry you out from them. Be not afraid. This is the faith, the peace that passes all understanding.

Revelation 15:3 And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways, thou King of saints. Now, the song of Moses in Revelation is more likely the song he wrote in Deuteronomy 31, but given the Lord God overcoming and delivering the saved to the promised land, and destroying the enemies of His people, it may be this is it. It is a song we could learn now, as it is applicable to our own lives and the eternal life we possess. We see near the end, after the triumphant singing and dancing unto the Lord, that the Israelites first begin to complain. And God makes a covenant with them as a nation, through Moses. If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the Lord that healeth thee. All of God's covenants with the Hebrew are if/then. All come with responsibility of the people to hold to what God asks. This is the covenants with nations. With the people on this earth. God judges us as individuals spiritually by faith, but God judges nations on earth by their works. This invitation to nations is still around today. It is how a godly nation that turns from its wicked ways becomes spared the evil God will do unto it. If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

John 6 26 Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled. 27 Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed. 28 Then said they unto him, What shall we do, that we might work the works of God? 29 Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent. 30 They said therefore unto him, What sign shewest thou then, that we may see, and believe thee? what dost thou work? 31 Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat. 32 Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven. 33 For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world. 34 Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread. 35 And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. 36 But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not. 37 All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out. 38 For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. 39 And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. 40 And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day. In Exodus 16 we find the recently freed Isralites, a month now out from bondage in Egypt, shown signs and wonders of God by Moses, murmuring that they were better off in chains. Having run low on supplies, their flesh in need afflicted their spirit. But God hears their murmurs, and tells Moses and Aaron that he will send them bread to eat in the morning, and the flesh of quails at night. God sets the rules of His heavenly bread that each person takes the measure allotted, and uses it that day, and all would be filled. If they tried to store it up for the next day, it would rot, except for that manna gathered on the day before the sabbath, which would feed them both days. And like the entire story of Exodus, we have a picture of salvation in Christ. Jesus, who is the bread of life. Jesus, who is the sabbath. Our rest. Jesus who was sent by God the Father that all who believe on Him shall never hunger. Jesus is the rock from which the water springs as well, as we will soon see. And those that believe on Him shall never thirst. In John 6, Jesus is preaching to the crowd that had followed Him to Capernaum, He had just fed the multitudes with a few loaves and fishes, that thousands were full and there was more to spare. Like in the wilderness of Sin, He fed them whether they followed God's laws or not, to prove them, that they may know He was of God. But Jesus first chastises the multitude, saying they didn't come to Him for spiritual reasons, but because their belly was full. And just as the children of Israel in the wilderness murmured against Moses, against God, here too the Bible says they murmured against Christ; The Jews then murmured at him, because he said, I am the bread which came down from heaven. And Jesus, being God, hears their murmurs and knows their hearts, and says; Murmur not among yourselves. No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day. It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me. Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he which is of God, he hath seen the Father. Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me hath everlasting life. I am that bread of life. Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead. This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die. I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world. He is giving a spiritual lesson using the allegory of bread from Heaven, the manna in the wilderness, and applying it to His own body, which in death would take on the sins of the world that whoever believes on Him shall have eternal life. But the unbelieving Jews, unable to understand Jesus take what He says literally and scoff; The Jews therefore strove among themselves, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat? And knowing their hardened hearts and dull hearing, Jesus doubles down on His parable; Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you. Whoso eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day. For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed. He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, dwelleth in me, and I in him. As the living Father hath sent me, and I live by the Father: so he that eateth me, even he shall live by me; This is that bread which came down from heaven: not as your fathers did eat manna, and are dead: he that eateth of this bread shall live for ever. Get the context; Jesus had just preached a basic parable of salvation in Him, using the manna and His miracle the day before, as a picture of the spiritual application of belief and eternal life, and they couldn't understand it. Like Nicodemus, they couldn't receive spiritual things. Like all unsaved people who take this literally, they either invent a cannibal cult doctrine, or are offended by His dark sayings. But we see, Jesus would always expound on His parables to His disciples, so that we were not left to interpret doctrine from unclear symbolism. Many therefore of his disciples, when they had heard this, said, This is an hard saying; who can hear it? When Jesus knew in himself that his disciples murmured at it, he said unto them, Doth this offend you? What and if ye shall see the Son of man ascend up where he was before? It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life. He explains that the words He speaks are spirit, and understanding them is life. That it is a parable, a picture of the salvation He is offering, one that mirrors the story in Exodus 16. But some remained offended, hung up on the literal. But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him. And he said, Therefore said I unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it were given unto him of my Father. From that time many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him. Then said Jesus unto the twelve, Will ye also go away? Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God. So we see that Peter understood the lesson. Peter was saved by faith, speaks the truth of what Jesus was conveying; that Jesus has the words of eternal life. Not the literal flesh and blood to consume to obtain it, but the words that by faith grant the believer eternal life, because Jesus is the Christ, the son of the living God. This teaching is an excellent way to separate the believer from those who aren't. Jesus uses it to divide, to alienate and offend those who don't understand the spiritual application because they are there to have their bellies filled, or to see wonders, not because they seek salvation. This still applies today. People who take any sort of literal view of actually eating the body and drinking the blood of Jesus to gain salvation are not saved and have not come to the knowledge of the truth. They are not called according to God's will, because they aren't seeking to know or understand it. Don't get that twisted, though. This isn't an appeal to Calvinism. Again, John 6 is a stumbling block for the unbelieving who use the "called" to teach their limited atonement damnable heresy. For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day. But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not. But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him. Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil? He spake of Judas Iscariot the son of Simon: for he it was that should betray him, being one of the twelve. Just to further illustrate the heresy of Calvinism, Jesus repeatedly says that those His Father gave Him have believed on Jesus, they are given to Him by faith, that they did the will of the Father. To believe His Son. But that some didn't believe, including out of the twelve Jesus had chosen. It is not by being chosen that we believe. We believe and become chosen.

And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ. Short chapter. Pretty straightforward. But note, as the Israelites left Sin, they were beset with tribulation and attacked by Amalek. As saved Christians we too will see more people attack us, more tribulation, as we leave sin. As we straighten up our former lives. As we seek to grow in God and walk after the Spirit, people will attack us. Even family and friends. And, like Moses raising the rod, we will be winning when we are trusting in God. But we may grow weary. Our arms may fall, and trouble may seem to be getting the better of us. But surrounding ourselves with fellow believers, the brethren who will help hold up our arms, and the rock that is Jesus Christ, to rest on, we will be victorious. But we have this written in memorial and preached to our ears, that we will know God is at war with Amalek from generation to generation. Jehovahnissi, because the Lord will have war with them, the unbelieving who seek to destroy His people.

Luke 10:1 After these things the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come. Acts 6 And in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration. 2 Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them, and said, It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables. 3 Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business. 4 But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word. 5 And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch: 6 Whom they set before the apostles: and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them. 7 And the word of God increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith. So we see that Jethro, his father in-law catches up to Moses in the wilderness, along with Zipporah his wife, and Moses' sons. Moses seems very happy to see his father in-law. No real reaction to seeing his wife, who in her last appearance threw her son's bloody foreskin at Moses and cursed him out. Jethro is an interesting character. The scriptures give us just a hint of who he is and it is enough to make you genuinely curious, was he a Gentile believer of God? Did his priesthood entail general worship of the LORD? Outside of Abraham's covenant to be sure, given the opposition to circumcision Moses faced from Jethro's daughter. But was he a priest after the order of Melchizedek? The priest-king of Salem who Abraham paid tithes to, and who may have been an Old Testament appearance of Jesus? Were there other people who worshipped the one true God, but by and by fell away, as the Hebrews were given His attention? Israel was to act as a light unto the world, to bring other nations to the knowledge of the truth. In this they failed, mostly. But not entirely. We know there were other people who believed, outside the Israelites. Regardless of anything else, Jethro seems genuinely enthusiastic about praising God for the victory over the Egyptians and that He delivered the children of Israel from bondage. He says "Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods." Did he get saved in this moment? We can't really say. It could just be a case of head knowledge, of every knee bowing and tongue confessing. We don't know. We do know from extra biblical sources that Jethro is claimed patriarch of the Druze. "Druze are ethnically Arab and Arabic speaking. Their monotheistic religion incorporates many beliefs from Islam, Judaism and Christianity, and is also influenced by Greek philosophy and Hinduism. Druze have not proselytized since the 11th century, and the religion remains closed to outsiders." It is by all accounts a satanic cult that teaches mysticism, gnosticism and reincarnation. They believe Jethro or a reincarnation of him, was their founder and teach weird doctrines and damn about a million adherents today. But regardless of all that, and regardless of the marriage troubles Moses may have had, Jethro in his visit gives good advice to his son-in-law Moses. Moses has 600,000 men, plus women and children in the mixed multitudes encamped with him. 12 tribes of Israel, come out of Egypt, and as their leader, he must sit in judgment. Jethro observes the long lines and the grind of dealing with them all that Moses faces and offers good advice. The thing that thou doest is not good. Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone. Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God: And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do. Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee. If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go to their place in peace. God blesses this arrangement, and Moses takes to it and does as Jethro advised. We see other times, in other places throughout the Bible that God approves of delegation of authority. He wants the people to know His ways and laws and the ordinances of remembrance, that in what they do they know the next right choice to make. We are to know the word of God that we can know ourselves what His will is. Without needing someone micromanaging and interpreting scripture, to constantly make decisions for us on normal matters. God then sets up captains over people, to judge matters for their people. By 10s, 100s and 1,000s. And a leader who answers to God, for the tougher matters of judgment. Thus will it be in the Millennium. Those who showed judgment and did great things for the Lord will be given much in the Kingdom. Those good and faithful servants will be made rulers, as Jesus described in the parable of the servants. We see the wisdom in this arrangement. The way it maximizes the ability to serve God and edify people. And this exists today through God's word; the priesthood of believers, the husband/father of the home, the local pastor, his helpers the deacons or elders, all answering to Jesus. It is the form of Christian nationalism that we should seek. It is also worth mentioning that God can use unsaved people, people who are wrong on doctrine but in position of authority, to do His will. Jethro as Moses' father-in-law was to be honored. His advice, considered and heeded. We sometimes see brothers and sisters in Christ struggle with that, where their parents are unsaved, sometimes wicked. Occasionally reprobate. And how does one honor them and honor God? The same question comes up with husbands with wives who won't submit to Christ or to their husbands, godly wives with unsaved husbands who treat them poorly, and other hierarchical conflicts, such as submitting to government when it is wicked. God's word is clear and consistent. That we are to as much as possible live peaceably with all men. To submit to the higher authority with meekness and faith, always keeping God as the head, that we don't cater to evil ourselves or join in another man's sin. People hate to hear that. They want to rebel constantly and be in open defiance of the order of things in this world. Only refusing to budge on the clear fundamental teachings of God, but also giving honor to whom honor is due, and paying tribute to whom tribute is due, and trusting God in all. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose. People are afraid to live by faith. Fear is the opposite of faith. It kills faith. It undermines and leads people to sin, rather than trusting in God to deliver us. Like the Israelites in the wilderness, people forget what God has already done for us, and so we are easily led to sin, fear and wrath. But if we walk in the Spirit, continuing in prayer and studying the word to be approved by God, faith grows, and with that faith, judgment and discernment which all work together to keep us from being afraid and reactionary. And the just shall live by faith. This ties in to this sermon I posted yesterday. The judges of God who delivered their people, who were meek normal men, God-fearing, who when the opportunity was brought before them, trusted the Lord and did great things for His people. This is the way forward for Christians.

IF ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine. This is the foundation of the covenant at Sinai, the promise made to the children of Israel by God, that IF they kept it, they would be a peculiar people, special to God. God judges nations on earth by their works. He judges people as individuals by their faith. His promises to nations are conditional. They are if/then. To us as individual souls, the only condition to be His is faith in Christ. The if/then covenant with Israel, that they broke themselves repeatedly, despite God's longsuffering and mercy, despite being given chance after chance to get right, they broke entirely with the Crucifixion, the rejection of His Son Jesus. But it is in Jesus that are made partakers of the new and better covenant. The better testament. And the old one is done away with. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. And where was the fault of the first? In the Israelites. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people: And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more. In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away. This is the bookend to the Sinai covenant, fulfilled: I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. And this should be the final nail in the coffin for the Dispensationalist Zionist heresy that God is still on the hook for the first covenant. No, He has replaced the physical nation with a new one. Israel was to be a peculiar people, but failed. Now His peculiar people are those saved in Christ. But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.

And from the mountain God made His covenant with the children of Israel, these 10 commandments. And the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished. This covenant has ended with Christ. The law of death replaced with the law of liberty. The moral components remain, covered by the two great commandments reiterated by Jesus in the new testament; Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
