Hebrews 10 For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect. 2 For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins. 3 But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year. 4 For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. 5 Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: 6 In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure. 7 Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God. 8 Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; 9 Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. 10 By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. 11 And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: 12 But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; 13 From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. 14 For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified. 15 Whereof the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before, 16 This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; 17 And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more. 18 Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin. 19 Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, 20 By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh; 21 And having an high priest over the house of God; 22 Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. 23 Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) 24 And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: 25 Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching. 26 For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, 27 But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries. 28 He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: 29 Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace? 30 For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people. 31 It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. 32 But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions; 33 Partly, whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, whilst ye became companions of them that were so used. 34 For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance. 35 Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward. 36 For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise. 37 For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry. 38 Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him. 39 But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul. If by the law we learn that all have fallen short and are in need of salvation, then by the carnal ordinances of the law we see the futility and eventual corruption of a priestly class administering materialist rites and sacraments. In other words, this was all given that both the faithful of the Old Testament had symbols of Christ that they may understand the hearing of the word and by it have faith, over centuries and generations, but also to serve to us that come to faith after Christ the vanity of trusting in such things. That even with the perfect expression of faith in the offerings for sin and the rest, it doesn't work. Only faith and the grace of God through the blood of Jesus can give remission of sin. Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law. Psalm 51 For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise. Hosea 6:6 For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. These things were put in place by God not because He desired them, but because man does. Man needs to see it. To touch it, smell it, experience it in the flesh. They had not the indwelling of the Holy Spirit as we do in the New Testament. So it served a like purpose, and it appeals to natural men and even some overly sensual believers to this day. I think this is the appeal for many of those looking for some form of spirituality and religion, but not having the truth of it found in the Gospel. The Retvrn types, who hearing chanting and smelling incense and seeing frescos and images of humans cast as idols, lit by candlelight, and seeing priests in robes and ephods, say they "feel God" when it is just carnal and appeals to their flesh. Same with fog machine, good time disco churches. It scratches the itch that we all have, but they worship what they know not.

Exodus chapter 30 continues laying out the physical tabernacle and carnal ordinances and diverse washings for Aaron and the priesthood, the incense altar and the holy oils and perfumes for anointing, as well as curses on those who fail to keep God's instructions regarding them, or who profanes the holy things. We see that it is gold that makes the altar precious, and myrrh and frankincense for the anointing oil and holy perfume; a picture of the gifts given Christ by the three wise men and His holy being. But God takes a slight detour from the ordinances of Aaron and his sons, to an offering given among the people. That when the people are numbered, an offering of half a shekel be given for every, on top of tithes, as an atonement offering. A ransom for their souls. Everybody paying the same price. No more no less, rich or poor. That it may be a memorial unto the children of Israel before the Lord. This requirement being a memorial, through the generations to come across the centuries, pointing to the coming of Jesus Christ in the flesh to be the actual ransom for all. A picture of the price paid for the atonement of our souls. For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's. Amen Mark 10:45 For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many. 1 Timothy 2:5-6 For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time. Job 33:23-25 If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom. His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth Hosea 13:14 I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction: repentance shall be hid from mine eyes.

Mark 2:28 Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath. Matthew 11:28-30 Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light. Chapter 31 provides an additional teaching on the sabbath, God instructs Moses to tell the people they are not to work on the last day of the week, least they be cut off and put to death. That the sabbath is a day of rest to memorialize His perpetual covenant, that it is by faith in the Lord that sanctifies us. It is a fitting picture of Christ, in whom we are called to rest on His perfect work for salvation. That salvation is by faith alone, not of works. And if you reach the end and are trusting in your works rather than the sabbath God provided, you're perishing. You will be cast out and put to death, which is Hell. People struggling with the idea that our works do not save us don't understand how the Sabbath is a memorial for the covenant of Christ. That we are free of the yoke of the law in regards to righteousness, because by the blood of Christ God will not impute sin to those that are saved when we are called to the Kingdom. They miss the point of the 3 sabbaths in a row between Passover and Easter Sunday, the first day of the week. That no works of the law shall save us. Jesus did it all. 7th Day Adventists and others under the yoke of the law keep the old testament sabbath, the last day of the week, in order to be saved. It is judaized nonsense. Christians celebrate and gather on the first day of the week, the Lord's day, in remembrance of His resurrection and the establishment of the new testament. As a memorial throughout our generations that we may know He is the Lord that sanctifies us. Galatians 5:1 Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage. The instructions regarding Bezaleel and Aholiab, and their craftsmanship in building all things as God revealed to them, through the talents He has blessed them with, is a wonderful reminder that as all knowledge comes of God and the Lord makes wise the simple, that any can be called to service of God via the talents and understanding He blessed us with. We are all made to conform to the image of His will, if we live for Him. Isaiah 64:8 But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand. Romans 9 20 Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? 21 Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour? 22 What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: 23 And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, 24 Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles? 25 As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved. 26 And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God. 27 Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved: 28 For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth. 29 And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha. 30 What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. 31 But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness. 32 Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone; 33 As it is written, Behold, I lay in Sion a stumblingstone and rock of offence: and whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

The Children of Israel were always a stiff-necked people, prone to mischief. Even after their being freed from bondage in Egypt, brought out by the hand of God, through the baptism of the sea, fed with heavenly meats and given the spiritual waters of Christ, knowing the will of God and His conditional testament agreed to at Sinai, a covenant signed with blood, still many at first chance, rebelled, followed molten gods crafted with hands indulging in wickedness before the Lord. And of them were smote 3,000 by the sons of Levi at the order of Moses, and the Lord's promise to plague those in sin for the idol they made. God sought to destroy them utterly and from Moses make a new nation to carry the promise and blessing of the seed, that is Christ Jesus. To make of him a new Abraham. But the Lord repented of the evil He sought to do, and allowed Moses to execute judgment, rather than wipe out all of Israel. Now Moses with the tablets carved by God's own hand returned from the mountain, and seeing the sin of Israel, he smashed God's laws to the ground, the people not worthy of such a gift. In his wrath, Moses did sin himself, and we will see his punishment is in carving these things himself in tablets of stone he must cut for himself. But, again we see the parallels to spiritual salvation, and the application of these things that serve as our examples. That many when led up out of bondage to sin and to the wilderness that is our earthly life, fall away having believed in vain. Never truly having faith. Turning immediately to other gods and to sin. Others, like Aaron, who have faith and accepted God's grace, backslide and go with the crowd, falling into sin. Still others like the sons of Levi, stand back, a loyal remnant of God. Like the parable of the sower, there are some seeds sown that never take root, others that have shallow roots but are taken away by the cares of the world. And some falls on fertile ground and with deep roots produces much fruit. It is easy to look at the Israelites, throughout the Old Testament, as a uniquely wicked and ungrateful people, who don't love the Lord, their deliverer, as they should. But we shouldn't get too cocky in our own conceits. Because none of us live up to what we should. All of us fall short and with a stiff neck of our own will, stand in defiance of the Lord who bought us, putting our own will before His. Christians today who sit down to eat and drink and rise up to play. We should consider the fate of those 3,000. God will scourge every son He receives. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the Living God.

2 Corinthians 3 2 Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men: 3 Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart. 4 And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward: 5 Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God; 6 Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life. 7 But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away: 8 How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious? 9 For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory. 10 For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth. 11 For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious. 12 Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech: 13 And not as Moses, which put a veil over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished: 14 But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. 15 But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. 16 Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away. 17 Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. 18 But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord. Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost. And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent. Exodus chapter 34 finds Moses in need to hew the rocks into tablets to replace those he broke in his anger at the golden calf and the sin of the children of Israel. The first God hewn, now must be made by Moses that God could give to him the covenant as a record, written in stone. Only Moses was allowed on Sinai, not even the beasts of the field were allowed to graze the foothills nearby. The Lord came in a cloud and the figure of Christ Jesus (IMO) appeared before him, as the glory of the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed "The Lord, The Lord God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation. This is who God is. We who are saved seek to know Him and throughout scripture we are given many names and descriptions that allow us to understand the holy God. Here is the quality of God that is judgment. He is merciful and longsuffering. He forgives. But He does not clear the guilty, and he visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third or fourth generation. That is not to say they are punished for the sins of the father, but rather their inequities being judgment upon their people for generations. God is about to declare a genocide of the people in the way towards the promised land. The wickedness they have done in His sight. The groves and high places, molten gods and altars. God tells Moses that they are to destroy these people that their wickedness doesn't infect the children of Israel, through practice, through marriage, or in any way including eating meat sacrificed to idols. We learn a name for God and it is Jealous. He is a jealous God. Jealousy is not envy or covetousness. It is fiercely protecting that which one owns. God is saying in this covenant He owns them, they are His people. And if they go whoring after strange gods because they were snared by covenant to make peace with the people He has judged be destroyed, He will have vengeance upon the children of Israel. To further defend what is His from whoredoms, going after strange gods, the Lord further emphasizes the ordinances for feasts He has put in place as a memorial for what He has done for the people of Israel, and as a picture of the Messiah to come, Christ Jesus. The feast of unleavened bread that begins immediately after Passover, which is the sabbaths of Christ when He is 3 days and 3 nights in Hell for our sins. And because His only begotten Son is a sacrifice for us, and because the firstborn sons of the children of Israel were spared in passover, even if their cattle, they belong to God and must be atoned through a substitutionary sacrifice. All a picture of Christ. The sabbath, again a picture of Christ. The feast of weeks, which leads to the Pentecost. The firstfruits of the harvest. Then the feast of the harvest at years end. All a picture of the time to come, and a memorial for the children of Israel that they may know Jesus. Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven; neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left unto the morning. The unleavened bread and unfermented wine of the Lord's supper. Taking Jesus down from the cross before sunset on Passover. The first of the firstfruits are God's under this Mosaic law. All a picture of Christ. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk. What does this mean? Why do Jews forbid the mixing of dairy with meat entirely from this passage? The act of seething, a form of boiling meat, in this case in milk, was a way of cooking, even basting in butter that which is roasted. It's a wonderful way to enjoy the food that God has blessed us with, but even the idea of using the actual mother's milk to cook her kid seems cruel. But why prohibit it? The logic of man says that the traditions of the people they were to drive out included this form of cruel sacrifice to their pagan gods. That may be. It could also be symbolism of Christ and a prohibition of the cooking method that they keep it a burnt offering. But what it does not do is ban dairy with meat generally. The "kosher" practices are just more of the vain traditions of the judaizers. And these dietary laws are done away with for Christians in the New Testament anyway. But it is an interesting verse to chew upon, no pun intended. And so we see, after 40 days upon the mount with the Lord, Moses having fasted and prayed and recording all God commanded, he returns to the people and his face shown in the reflected glory of God, so much so that the sinful people couldn't stand to look upon Moses. We know that here the veil was placed upon them that they may not look upon the glory of the Lord, but in Christ Jesus we may boldly go before God, the veil torn in twain. Removed that we may see Him in His word. We see in Moses that his spending time with the Lord changed him, and the glory of God shone through him. We who are saved Christians who walk in the Spirit, reading His word, praying ceaselessly, spreading the Gospel to others, feeding the new man, we are similarly changed. We have the same glory, magnified and reflected in us, shining as a light unto the world. And sinful man can't bear to look at us. They get angry. Resentful. They call for a veil to cover our faith. And sadly, many Christians today hide our light behind a bushel. But Jesus said to let our light shine. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

Psalm 54:6 I will freely sacrifice unto thee: I will praise thy name, O Lord; for it is good.

1 Corinthians 6:15-20 Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ? shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid. The first several chapters of Leviticus, which lays out the Levitical priesthood and its ordinances and practices, deal with the subject of sacrifice for atonement and oblations, gifts given to the Lord of meats, which in Biblical terms is foodstuffs, not just flesh of an animal. As we see in chapter 1, this is the holocaust or burnt offering of the lamb without blemish. The blood carrying the atonement. The sweet savour of the fire roasted fats and meats being pleasing to the Lord. And this is a picture of Christ. Just as are the meat offerings in chapter 2. Everything in the Old Testament does. Here we see the gift offering of fine flour, anointing oil and frankincense. The bread, representing Jesus, made without leaven, leaven representing sin. Note that it was both raw ingredients baked by Aaron and his sons. Or finished cakes and wafers. Cooked or baked. And the priests eat thereof what is left over. The frankincense consumed completely, all anointed with oil, as befitting a King. And the priest shall take from the meat offering a memorial thereof, and shall burn it upon the altar: it is an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord. Showing the Israelites the truth of their savior in these ordinances. As a memorial to Him that was to come. All burnt upon the fire. But the oblations of the firstfruits shall not be burnt in the altar. And all the meat offerings of the first fruits are to be salted generously. To season it completely as it is the salt of the covenant with God. This represents the saved, the firstfruits of the harvest. The salt, the holy Spirit. Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. Salt is a seasoning, increasing the savour of the food, enhancing it. But it is also a preservative, keeping food fresh, longer. In this way, the Spirit acts in the believer. It isn't burned in the fire, just as believers are spared Hell. God makes a provision for the corn given in a meat offering to be as the flour or unleavened bread, anointed with oil and frankincense, to be burned as the other flours, as a cornmeal, that there be no confusion. And that includes admitting our faults, confessing our trespasses with each other, and seeking prayer to help us overcome the flesh. This is natural, normal and good. The very act of a sincere confession to God is often enough to bring us out of the delusional rationalizing we do to cover our sins. And to tell others of our sin, knowing that it could be humiliating but for their love and grace, and their own humility in being an admitted sinner, is freeing. Knowing others are praying for your growth. These things provide a bulwark against sin. If your heart isn't deceiving you, it becomes more humiliating to stay in a sin than it is to fear being exposed. True confession is a wonderful tool given by God that we may become separated unto the Gospel and better vessels fitted to His purpose. False confession, anything that seeks to be given excuse or justification for our sin that we may remain in it, or that we can work it off in some way of penance, is wicked as Hell and leads people further and further into sin.

2 Corinthians 5 14 For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that if one died for all, then were all dead: 15 And that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again. 16 Wherefore henceforth know we no man after the flesh: yea, though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now henceforth know we him no more. 17 Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new. 18 And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation; 19 To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation. 20 Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God. 21 For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. Numbers 21:9 And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived. John 3 14 And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: 15 That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life. 16 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. 17 For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. 18 He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God. As we continue through the ordinances for the Levitical priesthood and sacrifices, we are also given more insight into the law, building on the fundamental of loving thy neighbor. The sin of robbery by guile or by violence, by any dishonest means, was punished by restitution plus 5%, and a trespass offering. That's it. Now as we saw yesterday, this required a confession of the wrong in order to share in the sacrifice for atonement, and obviously to restore the person who suffered loss. God says this is just. Man says we must create an entire criminal justice system with prisons and punishment, cops and robbers. As we saw in Exodus 21, 22, there are more provisions for theft, and include instructions for those impenitent to or destitute to be given to servitude to repay. If they are caught breaking in and killed by the owner, there is no blood guilt. If there is harm done. Eye for an eye. Tooth for a tooth. Stripe for stripe. God's law is perfect. It may not be able to save us, sinners as we all are. But for a nation to live by His perfect judgments, if they were to be followed, it would be a much better country. In our founding, much of the original laws came from the Old Testament. They are right and just. 1 Timothy 1:8-11 But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, for whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; according to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust. Continuing the instructions for burnt offerings for trespassing and sin, we do see that the Levitical priesthood were to eat of their portion of the sacrifice. The breads and meats. Because the tribe of Levi had no land given unto them in promise, they were to be given of these sacrifices. 1 Timothy 5:18 For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.

Exodus 29 19 And thou shalt take the other ram; and Aaron and his sons shall put their hands upon the head of the ram. 20 Then shalt thou kill the ram, and take of his blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about. 21 And thou shalt take of the blood that is upon the altar, and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it upon Aaron, and upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon the garments of his sons with him: and he shall be hallowed, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons' garments with him. 22 Also thou shalt take of the ram the fat and the rump, and the fat that covereth the inwards, and the caul above the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the right shoulder; for it is a ram of consecration: 23 And one loaf of bread, and one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer out of the basket of the unleavened bread that is before the Lord: 24 And thou shalt put all in the hands of Aaron, and in the hands of his sons; and shalt wave them for a wave offering before the Lord. 25 And thou shalt receive them of their hands, and burn them upon the altar for a burnt offering, for a sweet savour before the Lord: it is an offering made by fire unto the Lord. 26 And thou shalt take the breast of the ram of Aaron's consecration, and wave it for a wave offering before the Lord: and it shall be thy part. 27 And thou shalt sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up, of the ram of the consecration, even of that which is for Aaron, and of that which is for his sons: 28 And it shall be Aaron's and his sons' by a statute for ever from the children of Israel: for it is an heave offering: and it shall be an heave offering from the children of Israel of the sacrifice of their peace offerings, even their heave offering unto the Lord. The heave and wave offerings were a form of free will offering given in peace to God, in thanksgiving, and in supplication or to a vow, with the understanding that a portion went to feed the Levite priests. Heave and wave, the motions done with the portion that was given the priests. Literally lifting up or waving above their heads, signifying that portion that was theirs. Some interpretations hold that the wave offerings signify the resurrection of Christ, while the heave as either His being lifted up on the cross or, more commonly His assent into Heaven on Pentecost. I don't know, or really have a strong opinion on it. It is sufficient to know that Christ is the propitiation, the sacrifice, by which we make peace with God and Whom we give thanks through. Blessing all we do in Jesus' name. I generally avoid commentaries when doing a study, seeking to allow the Bible to explain itself. They have a purpose, my own thoughts recorded here are a commentary, but reliance on them often keeps us from allowing the Spirit to give us the knowledge and wisdom, directly from the word. But, for these Levitical ceremonial laws and ordinances, sometimes I lean on them. I try to make sense of it myself from scripture first, then go to them to see what others may have to offer. In his commentary on Exodus 29:27, Clarke wrote this regarding the heave and wave offerings: “As the wave-offering was agitated to and fro, and the heave-offering up and down, some have conceived that this twofold action represented the figure of the cross, on which the great Peace-offering between God and man was offered in the personal sacrifice of our blessed Redeemer.” For this idea, Clarke cited the work of Charles Houbigant, a French Bible scholar of the 18th century. Seems as likely as my own interpretation. Your mileage may vary. I thank God for His Son, Jesus, that we aren't held under the ceremony and ritual sacrifices of the Mosaic law. That in Him we have peace with God and are able to boldly to before Him in thanksgiving and supplication. Romans 5:1-2 Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.

Moses, as an agent of the Lord needed no such consecration to consecrate, or none we are told, except the word of God. Dressing Aaron in the vestments of his office, Moses gives him the ephod or ceremonial vest, the mitred headdress, and other articles commanded of the Lord, that we saw made in Exodus. With the baptismal washings, anointing with oil and blood, representing the holy Spirit and the sacrifice of Christ, and the burnt offerings and wave offering, Aaron and his sons are shut in 7 days in the Tabernacle for purification that they may be consecrated and separated unto their service. Ceremonially clean. The priesthood of Aaron being a picture of the salvation and anointing of the believer into the priesthood of Christ, after the order of Melchizedek. 1 Peter 2:9-10 But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy. 2 Corinthians 1:21 Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God 1 John 2:20, 27 But ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things...But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him. Hebrews 7 For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him; 2 To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace; 3 Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually. 4 Now consider how great this man was, unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils. 5 And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham: 6 But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises. 7 And without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better. 8 And here men that die receive tithes; but there he receiveth them, of whom it is witnessed that he liveth. 9 And as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham. 10 For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him. 11 If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron? The ephod, a breastplate of righteousness, had upon it the Urim and the Thummim, the lots of judgment given the high priest. Just as we spiritually have the word of God in our hearts, having been anointed into the holy priesthood, giving us the judgment of God in matters of righteousness, the carnal priests of Levi had a manner of seeking after the judgment of God. When the judges and kings of Israel sought to know God's judgment of them or their plans, they would seek the lots to be cast by the high priest or prophets. Guilty or innocent, "cursed or faultless," the Urim and the Thummim would determine the matter when the wisdom of man fell short. Later interpretation by apostate churches and cults like the Mormons, place the carnal application of these lots as the literal, and miss the spiritual application found in faith through Christ. But he told not his father. 2 And Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which is in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men; 3 And Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the Lord's priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone. 4 And between the passages, by which Jonathan sought to go over unto the Philistines' garrison, there was a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh. 5 The forefront of the one was situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah. 6 And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the Lord will work for us: for there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few. 7 And his armourbearer said unto him, Do all that is in thine heart: turn thee; behold, I am with thee according to thy heart. 8 Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto these men, and we will discover ourselves unto them. 9 If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them. 10 But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up: for the Lord hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign unto us. 11 And both of them discovered themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves. 12 And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armourbearer, Come up after me: for the Lord hath delivered them into the hand of Israel. 13 And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armourbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him. 14 And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armourbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were an half acre of land, which a yoke of oxen might plow. 15 And there was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling. 16 And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another. 17 Then said Saul unto the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there. 18 And Saul said unto Ahiah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel. 19 And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the noise that was in the host of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thine hand. 20 And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture. 21 Moreover the Hebrews that were with the Philistines before that time, which went up with them into the camp from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan. 22 Likewise all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle. 23 So the Lord saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over unto Bethaven. 24 And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted any food. 25 And all they of the land came to a wood; and there was honey upon the ground. 26 And when the people were come into the wood, behold, the honey dropped; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath. 27 But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened. 28 Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food this day. And the people were faint. 29 Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey. 30 How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines? 31 And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint. 32 And the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground: and the people did eat them with the blood. 33 Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the Lord, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day. 34 And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the Lord in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there. 35 And Saul built an altar unto the Lord: the same was the first altar that he built unto the Lord. 36 And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatsoever seemeth good unto thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God. 37 And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day. 38 And Saul said, Draw ye near hither, all the chief of the people: and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day. 39 For, as the Lord liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him. 40 Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee. 41 Therefore Saul said unto the Lord God of Israel, Give a perfect lot. And Saul and Jonathan were taken: but the people escaped. 42 And Saul said, Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken. 43 Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die. 44 And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan. 45 And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not. 46 Then Saul went up from following the Philistines: and the Philistines went to their own place.

Amen. Moses did as God commanded, in the ways he was instructed, and the glory of God was revealed to all before them. In our recent study on Romans, we saw how God has revealed Himself to us. Through His word. Through His mercy and grace towards we who believe. Through the power of the Gospel given by believers to others that they may believe. By His wrath revealed from heaven against all who hold the truth in unrighteousness. Here we see an instance of God's word being believed and followed, revealing His glory to the whole nation of Israel in the wilderness. But we can experience this on a personal scale, in the life of others when we live out the Gospel, being a blessing to them, in love. Don't miss out on this revelation. Be a vessel that allows the glory of God to be present in your neighbors' lives. God's glory is revealed in our atonement by the blood and obedience of Christ. His mercy and grace are given witness. And so too here, as Moses consecrated Aaron and his sons into the holy priesthood, we see it witnessed, that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Exodus 33:17-20 And the Lord said unto Moses, I will do this thing also that thou hast spoken: for thou hast found grace in my sight, and I know thee by name. And he said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory. And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before thee; and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy. Ephesians 2:4-10 But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;) And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus: That in the ages to come he might shew the exceeding riches of his grace in his kindness toward us through Christ Jesus. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them. Hebrews 1:3 Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high; Just as we see God's glory revealed in wrath against the unrighteous, it is truly revealed in our salvation from that wrath, the good news of His free gift. In His grace and love. This is why salvation is so simple that a child can understand it. This is why it is without works, that no man can boast of having deserved it. That all the glory be given God. This is why we who believe on Him that is faithful and true may know we have eternal life. That we are sealed unto redemption by His Spirit. That He testifies within us. That we may have that blessed assurance. Eternally adopted sons and daughters of God. To show His glory. And all those who seek to establish their own righteousness, who deny the eternal gift, who make grace into some sort of rewards system in a game, rather than the gift of God given in the blood of His only begotten Son, seek to rob God of His glory. It is blasphemy.

Over the course of 9 chapters we have seen the detailed instructions from the Lord to Moses, telling the Levitical priesthood of Aaron and his eldest two sons with great specificity, what they were to do regarding purification and sacrifice, where and how and when, and to what portion was God's, the blood, the burnt offering, the wave and the heave offerings, all of it. And despite these clear and explicit teachings of the word of God, the first thing the newly anointed sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, do is add their own works to it. They light incense with a "strange fire," that is not the fire the Lord provided within the Tabernacle, but fire they made themselves. Their intentions seem to be good; they offered this strange fire before the Lord. They were seeking to praise Him, perhaps. Glorifying God with their own invention of religious expression, which the Lord commanded them not. And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord. Aaron, chosen to be the first high priest of the Levitical priesthood, honored by his sons being chosen with him, to lead the congregation and perform the propitiations and oblations, to instruct the people in the ways of salvation through Christ by their adherence to the commands of God, in sanctification, showing the judgment of God that all the people may glorify Him. And he watches his sons burn to death, seeking their own righteousness. The error of Cain is a natural impulse for man. To add our own works or to place new and strange ways of worship upon the things of God that His word instructs, is something we see throughout the Bible. And we see God's judgement upon those who seek their own sanctification, their own means of being holy. Who add to His word. Who brings their own works to the table of the Lord. And yet, it continues. Just as Judaizers and those teaching strange doctrines of men were creeping in unawares to the early New Testament churches. Just as heretics and apostates twisted the word of God, bringing another gospel, so too did Nadab and Abihu. Those who claim that the "church fathers" were correct when they deviated from scripture and that there were hidden traditions, passed down from apostles, are the same as those who Jude wrote about in his epistle; Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. They bring strange fire before the Lord. After having kin remove the remains, Moses calls Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and instructs them to do as the Lord commanded, to eat the sin offering, cooked by the same fire that killed their brothers, that came from the Lord. To eat it beside the altar, because this is a holy thing, designed to teach the congregation of the separation of holy from unholy. From clean and unclean. But later, Moses sees their portion of the offering burnt without the camp. Likely in fear of divine retribution, Moses seeks out the sons to rebuke them, but Aaron says it was his own fault. That he couldn't bear to do it given the events of the day and the loss of his eldest two sons. Aaron admits the error, but appeals to the fact that it wouldn't have been done in the spirit of God's command had he gone along and ate it, and that it wouldn't have been acceptable given his state. This excuse is acceptable to Moses. It is important to make this distinction, that while we must obey God's commands and seek to diligently follow what His word tells us is right, there are times where our heart isn't in it. Our spirit is low. And unlike those who seek to add their own works to the glory of God, kindling His wrath, the Lord is understanding of our own weakness and longsuffering in His mercy. Aaron held his peace. He had accepted the judgment of God. But he was still grieved. He was on God's program but it was too bitter that day. Aaron resumed his duties following this, but it was too much to bear at the time. God is merciful and loves us. He is understanding that sometimes the truth of His word is bitter to us, in the flesh. His judgments may seem harsh to us at the time, and we may need a little time to come to acceptance. We must not use that occasion to curse God or to backslide. But He is patient. Note that Moses instructs the priests should remain sober. And that if they drink alcohol and enter into the Tabernacle, they will die. Do not drink wine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sons with thee, when ye go into the tabernacle of the congregation, lest ye die: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations... This instruction coming on the heels of the devastating loss of two sons, may have been directed at Aaron in his grief, but it's a standing command from the Lord for those who are called His priests. We who are saved are of the royal priesthood. We are a Tabernacle of the Spirit of God. Just as Proverbs 31 states; It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; Nor for princes strong drink: Lest they drink, and forget the law, And pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted. We who are saved are joint heirs to the kingdom. We are princes. As priests and princes, we should abstain from intoxicants. We are called to be sober. To refrain from the appearance of evil. To be holy because He is holy. It is incredibly difficult to read these scriptures and come to the conclusion that it's ok to drink booze. And it is gravely heretical to claim, as the Romans do, that the priests they appoint should drink alcohol as part of their false sacrifice at the altar they claim is holy. Blasphemously calling it the blood of Christ.

Hebrews 9:6-10 Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God. The dietary laws of the Levitical priesthood were part of a series of ordinances and rites of cleanliness that served as a way to make a difference between the unclean and the clean. To provide this distinction as a lesson to the people, the law being a schoolmaster, that they may better understand the holiness of God. Ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy. As Peter writes in his first epistle, declaring the priesthood of the believer, Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy. It is an example. A means of separation that the Lord instituted with Moses and Aaron to demonstrate this concept. A living parable. But as Christ Jesus says, it's not what goes into our mouth that is unclean, but the spirit by which it is received, and what proceeds out of our own mouth. And we know that out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. The Israelites were given a chance to commune in assembly with God. To see their faith in His salvation be practiced before them with the ceremonial washings and sacrifices. To witness the spiritual through the physical, that they may come to understand God, and in it, Christ. Now the time of reformation had come, the death and resurrection of Christ, and these carnal ordinances and diverse washings and sacrifices and oblations were done away with. Hebrews 7:11-12 If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron? For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law. And as Peter has revealed to him by God, that the "unclean," the people who were not a people, the Gentiles, were now to be folded into the promise of the kingdom, of the "clean." What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common. And so now, graft in, we are called to be holy for He is holy. Not by the food we eat. Not by the things that enter into the mouth, by what's in our hearts and what we profess. There are some false religions that impose carnal ordinances of abstaining from types of meats to be "holy," what the Bible calls "doctrines of devils." This applies not only to the Catholic practices of not eating meat on Fridays, which we see is totally foolish and unbiblical, but more and more in Judaized Evangelical circles, the imposition of Levitical dietary laws. But we who are saved in Christ know that nothing is unclean if it is eaten in thanksgiving, blessed by God. This provides a simple test for the believer to see if they are involved in a cult or false religion. Any implementation of the Old Testament ordinances done away with in the reformation that is Christ, should be a giant red flag.

Leviticus 11-15 deal with the purity laws, the idea of physical uncleanness in the eyes of God, both in a ceremonial aspect and a public health aspect. We see here that the Levitical priesthood were also the physician, and God has given them the diagnostics and treatment. Historians consider the Hebrews to have been the first people to use physical isolation to treat these outbreaks, and the distinction in diagnosis to determine type and severity, also a first. The fool never learns right from wrong from experience. They do the same foolishness over and over again and expect it to work out differently "this time." The average person learns right and wrong from their own experience, imperfectly. The wise learn what's right and wrong not only from their own, but by others'experiences. The righteous learns what's right and wrong from God's word, and believe Him when He says something is so. The wicked know what is right from wrong and do it anyway. Knowing the judgment of God, yet they don't care. The hypocrite knows what's right from wrong and does it to hold it against others who fall short, and to hold themselves up as better than the rest, while failing to maintain it themselves. You will notice as you read the Bible that each character is a rich, deep and complex person, shown with their foibles and failures, sin and falling short. The contrast between retched man and Christ is as deliberate, as much as the clean and the unclean from the Levitical laws we are currently studying. None are good, save God. None are righteous, no not one. But then we see Jesus, who is righteous, and who is good. Being God.

I have covered the symbolism and importance of the law of leprosy, and the atonement offered at the cleansing of one who is cured in another post here. It is fascinating to me that an incurable disease is given a process by God for ritual cleansing in the case of a leper who is cured. There were cases in the OT of leprosy being "cured." In Numbers 12, after Aaron and Miriam gainsay Moses for marrying an Ethiopian, God curses Miriam with leprosy for 7 days. The other instance is in 2 Kings 5, where a captain of the Syrian guard, Naaman contracts the disease, and the Syrian King sends him to the king of Israel asking him to heal his servant. And it came to pass, when the king of Israel had read the letter, that he rent his clothes, and said, Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man doth send unto me to recover a man of his leprosy? wherefore consider, I pray you, and see how he seeketh a quarrel against me. As we see, it was as if he had asked him to raise the dead. An impossible task and the king worried that it was a provocation for war with Syria. But the prophet Elisha heard of it and said; And it was so, when Elisha the man of God had heard that the king of Israel had rent his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel. It's a wonderful story of faith and shows the power of God, highly recommend reading it. But we can see that the idea that one could be healed from leprosy would have been something that the Israelites would have thought impossible save by God. And yet an entire chapter is devoted to this unlikely thing, filled with imagery of the sacrifice of Christ. A picture of Jesus saving sinners from death. And the purpose of the practical application, as we see Elisha say, is to let people know there is a prophet of God among them. Jesus heals the leper and sends him to the temple to perform this ritual, as a testimony unto the priests, that the Son of God was here. As I wrote about it in the study of Luke 5; "The bird in the earthen vessel, the clay that man is made from, as a substitutionary sacrifice, its blood upon wood, like the wood of the cross. On the scarlet, as the garments of Christ were so stained. On the hyssop, like the sprig dipped in vinegar, given to Jesus on the cross. And this blood of atonement then cleanses the man, and the living bird, like the risen Christ ascends to the heavens." Jesus Christ is in an earthen vessel, made manifest in the flesh. There is running water, the baptismal washing that came with the carnal ordinances, the law of the clean and unclean. Everything points to Jesus. We don't figure out what's right and wrong from circumstances, we aren't called to be superstitious. God doesn't instruct us to place our faith in rituals or washings, ordinances and observations. He calls us to serve others and to study His word. There are blessings and judgments and promises and curses, God's wrath revealed against the workers of iniquity, His mercy revealed by those who believe on Jesus and are saved. Matthew 5:44-45 But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust. The Bible tells us that sometimes circumstances happen for no other reason that God willed it. That we may not know His purpose and it isn't our place to question Him. "Under the order of the Presbyterian Church in the USA, the General Assembly was not authorized to accept or dismiss the complaint. It should have demitted the complaint to the presbytery and could have done so with instructions that the presbytery hold a heresy trial. The result of the trial could then be appealed to the Synod of New York and from there to the General Assembly. However, the 1910 General Assembly, acting outside its scope of authority, dismissed the complaint against the three men and at the same time instructed its Committee on Bills and Overtures to prepare a statement for governing future ordinations. The committee reported, and the General Assembly passed the Doctrinal Deliverance of 1910, which declared that five doctrines were "necessary and essential" to the Christian faith: -The inspiration of the Bible by the Holy Spirit and the inerrancy of Scripture as a result of this. -The virgin birth of Christ. -The belief that Christ's death was an atonement for sin. -The bodily resurrection of Christ. -The historical reality of Christ's miracles. Leviticus 20 begins laying out specific punishments for the violations of the civil laws given to Moses and Aaron by God, especially the paganism and the sexual immorality listed in the previous chapters. The sins of those whose lands the children of Israel were entering into, and the land the Lord freed them from, Egypt. And as God frequently has stated in giving this law, the purpose was to separate the people unto God and away from the error, whoredoms and abominations of the other nations. To be holy because He is holy. The law of God is perfect. His judgments are righteous. A just nation seeking after the Lord, who have the fear of God, would implement these strictures and punishments, that their nation not be judged, and the land that the Lord has granted them the habitations thereof wouldn't spew them out. And so, as a practical matter, these things given by God, not to be confused with the ordinances and sacrifices that were done away with in the reformation of Christ, but rather are His law by which He judges nations. They are in full effect, even today. And His wrath is clearly upon those nations that don't follow His precepts. And so, practically, physically, these laws give us insight to the perfect will of God for a people. We start with a continuation of the following after false gods from chapter 19, where if a man offers his seed, that is his children, to Moloch, the false god of the Canaanites, he shall be cut off. Not allowed to defile the house of the Lord. Stoned to death, God's face turned from him. Reprobation. He is rejected and it is up to the people to do as God commanded and not to ignore his presence among them. This rejection is both physical and spiritual, (I want to focus on the literal application as we go through the list of sins and punishment, tying in the spiritual application afterwards.) Next he warns against those who go after mediums; those who have "familiar spirits," and after wizards, they too shall be cut off, the mediums and wizards stoned to death. Note these things are closely aligned with the false gods, because they are not only satanic but mean the person has no respect for the Lord, no fear of the living God, and has no faith in Him that saves, but rather seeks another god of their own invention. Reprobate concerning the faith, and physically cut off from the nation seeking to be holy. Sanctified. Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy: for I am the Lord your God. And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am the Lord which sanctify you. Again, separation by keeping God's statutes, that He may sanctify us. Something that Israel failed to do, and were cut off for when, after the longsuffering of God was over, Jesus had come in the flesh. We know the law is made to be a schoolmaster to bring Israel to repentance of faith in the Christ to come. That the failing of the law to achieve righteousness wasn't God's fault, but man's. Because when a man dishonored his father and mother, cursing them, the people didn't put him to death. Because when a man committed adultery with his neighbor's wife, they weren't put to death. When a man committed incest, uncovering the nakedness of his own family's women, committing abominations, the people do not put him to death. When sodomites were found amongst them, men laying with men, abominations to the Lord, the people suffered them to live rather than stoning them to death, their blood being upon them. Bestiality, incest, the abomination of sex in the blood of menstruation...all these things that God warns nations about eventually are left unchecked by a wicked and perverse generation. The people didn't follow His statutes. Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all my judgments, and do them: that the land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out. And ye shall not walk in the manners of the nation, which I cast out before you: for they committed all these things, and therefore I abhorred them. God's wrath abides on a nation that fails to sanctify themselves through his statutes and judgments. As the nations driven out before the Israelites were condemned. As Israel itself would be. And as nations even to this day find out as the land spews them out for their abominations. This is the practical application of the law, and the spiritual application for those of us at liberty from sin in Christ, we see the pattern of what is right in God's eyes, that we may be sanctified by Him through the Spirit. Because of the weakness of the flesh and the failing of sinful man, we need a savior. We need Christ, and through the grace of God, we are given Jesus to do what we couldn't. That by faith in Him we have remission of sin and peace with God. And in that peace, paid for entirely by the blood of Jesus, we can then be sanctified by the Spirit. We are to standfast in the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free. Not being entangled again with the yoke of bondage. Our unrighteousness done away with by the grace of God to His glory. His mercy being a revelation from Heaven through we who are saved that others may see and come to the knowledge of the truth, and repent towards God. Believing on Christ, to be set at liberty as well. Despite some, who have crept in privily to spy out liberty, and who slanderously report that we say "let us do evil..." The liberty we have from sin, the blessing that God will not impute sin to us, is to allow us to then walk in the spirit and not fulfill the lusts of the flesh. To strive for the mark that God calls us towards, that we may be conformed to His use, that His will be done. That we be sanctified. That we be holy because He is holy. And in that sanctification, we can bring others to Christ, being a light unto the world as Israel was to be to other nations. This is why, if we take an honest look at those who preach salvation by grace through faith, without works, without depending on our own selves to turn from sin, or change our lives, or "make Jesus our Lord," but by acknowledging the truth of God, we see so many who are living for God today. We see those set free in Christ turning from sin, walking in the Spirit, doing great things for the Lord. Not sanctification to gain justification, but sanctification to become vessels fit for His use. That we may be blameless before men. That we may be justified before men, who may say, as in James 2, show me your faith by your works. That we may lead others to the truth. And so, you see independent fundamental Baptist churches that are soul winning, studying to be approved, comparing that which they received with scripture to see if it is so. Engaged in the edification of the local church and reaching out to the poor, the brokenhearted, that they may find peace with God. Fundamentalist Baptists are often the most separated, actually allowing the Spirit to work effectually in them to remove thorns from their hearts, and to feed the new man, starving the flesh. This is not to say all Baptists or even a majority of Baptist churches are perfect. This is not to say that just by being Baptist, you become justified or holier than anyone else, or that only a Baptist Church can achieve this. But the fruit of the more stedfast Baptist churches is undeniably a more separated people doing great works for the Lord. Now the salvation of the children of Israel from Egypt, that are freed from the yoke of bondage, came in faith on the promise of God. That by the blood of the Passover offering they are spared death. That by the waters they passed through, baptized into a new people and brought to a land promised them of God. Flowing with milk and honey, a land taken by those who failed to fear and serve the living God, but set about to establish their own righteousness. And then sanctified by the Lord to His purpose. This historical and physical story is a picture of the spiritual, and the individual salvation of us who believe and are adopted by God as His people. And so we should notice the order of things; salvation is front loaded and found only by faith. For the salvation of Israel from bondage and death came by faith alone, by the blood. The Israelites in Egypt were not told to change their ways first. To become holy first. To repent of their sins and throw themselves before God crying for mercy because of how wicked they were. God decided in His grace to offer them mercy if they believed Moses and Aaron, and trusted in the blood of the lamb. And so all Israel was saved. Then they were baptized together. Then they were given God's law. Then they were told to sanctify themselves, for their own good and to better serve God's will. Those who place the giving of the law before the acceptance of faith are in error. Those telling others they must turn from their sins first before they can believe are entangling them in bondage. Placing the yoke upon those who should be set free. This same pattern is seen in Abraham. Abraham was given the word of God by His promises, and in faith alone was given those blessings. Romans 4 What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? 2 For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. 3 For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. 4 Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. 5 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. 6 Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, 7 Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. 8 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. 9 Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. 10 How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all, 17 (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were. 18 Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations, according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be. 19 And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah's womb: 20 He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God; 21 And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform. 22 And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness. 23 Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him;
