It is literally about sedition and setting yourself up as better than or worthier than the man of God that He has placed over you in His hierarchy. That even if you disagree with their own life choices and resent them for whatever reason, you still must respect God's choice, giving honor to those who should be honored. Tribute to those due tribute. 1 Samuel 15:23 For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king. The reason behind their rebellion is incidental. They used a flaw in Moses to seek to undermine him. That's the essence of the story. If that's who God puts in place of power, given the spirit of leadership over the people, then that's who God chose. Render honor to them, and fear the Lord. It doesn't change the fact that there are several prohibitions and warnings against taking outlandish women as wives. That taking a stranger for a wife leads to children who fall away from the faith of their fathers and chase idols. It is a punishment on a nation to be bred out of existence, and it begins by the acceptance of mixed marriage. It was especially true in the idea that Israel was a means of getting from Abraham to David to Christ Jesus. And it remains true in a spiritual sense today, and being unequally yoked, and the judgment against nations being ethnically erased still exists, and will unto the day of redemption. God sets the boundaries and habitations thereof. The nations will rejoice in that day. And we will be one people in the resurrection. Until then, it isn't prudent to be accepting culturally of miscegenation. We have to be very careful in letting the Bible tell us what's being discussed, to understand the context and not wrestle something else out of it. And it angers a lot of people who have settled into one side or another on a secondary or tertiary doctrine, and seek justification from scripture for it, to make dogmatic statements. I have noticed that so many of these dogmas, and the binaries that form from them, are carnal and incidental to the larger point being made. And so people miss the forest for the trees. When I have applied this form of exegesis to pet theories in scripture, even when I agree with the theory in whole or in part, people get angry. "Both sides" foam at the mouth over this. Labels of heresy and compromise abound. But in my view the Bible is very clear on doctrine and things that have to be forced out of the text aren't worthy of being dogmatic. Simple as. The Bible is not for our eisegesis to win fights online. Especially about carnal things. It is for the winning of souls.

Deuteronomy 1 19 And when we departed from Horeb, we went through all that great and terrible wilderness, which ye saw by the way of the mountain of the Amorites, as the Lord our God commanded us; and we came to Kadeshbarnea. 20 And I said unto you, Ye are come unto the mountain of the Amorites, which the Lord our God doth give unto us. 21 Behold, the Lord thy God hath set the land before thee: go up and possess it, as the Lord God of thy fathers hath said unto thee; fear not, neither be discouraged. 22 And ye came near unto me every one of you, and said, We will send men before us, and they shall search us out the land, and bring us word again by what way we must go up, and into what cities we shall come. 23 And the saying pleased me well: and I took twelve men of you, one of a tribe: 24 And they turned and went up into the mountain, and came unto the valley of Eshcol, and searched it out. 25 And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it down unto us, and brought us word again, and said, It is a good land which the Lord our God doth give us. 26 Notwithstanding ye would not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of the Lord your God: 27 And ye murmured in your tents, and said, Because the Lord hated us, he hath brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us. 28 Whither shall we go up? our brethren have discouraged our heart, saying, The people is greater and taller than we; the cities are great and walled up to heaven; and moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakims there. 29 Then I said unto you, Dread not, neither be afraid of them. 30 The Lord your God which goeth before you, he shall fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes; 31 And in the wilderness, where thou hast seen how that the Lord thy God bare thee, as a man doth bear his son, in all the way that ye went, until ye came into this place. 32 Yet in this thing ye did not believe the Lord your God, 33 Who went in the way before you, to search you out a place to pitch your tents in, in fire by night, to shew you by what way ye should go, and in a cloud by day. 34 And the Lord heard the voice of your words, and was wroth, and sware, saying, 35 Surely there shall not one of these men of this evil generation see that good land, which I sware to give unto your fathers. 36 Save Caleb the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it, and to him will I give the land that he hath trodden upon, and to his children, because he hath wholly followed the Lord. 37 Also the Lord was angry with me for your sakes, saying, Thou also shalt not go in thither. 38 But Joshua the son of Nun, which standeth before thee, he shall go in thither: encourage him: for he shall cause Israel to inherit it. Numbers 13 presents the turning point in the children of Israel under Moses. They had been camped at Mt Sinai, Horeb in the south of the Arabian Peninsula for over a year. There God had communed with Moses, the Law given, the Tabernacle built. The camps made, and their order given. The sanctification of the people performed. So now was their time to enter into the promised land. We read in the account in Numbers that God authorized the sending of 12 spies, one of each tribe, into the land to report back what the Israelites would be encountering there. But we see in Deuteronomy 1 that the initial idea to send someone wasn't God's, but the people's. Though God promised them He would scatter and destroy the inhabitants before them, and promised that the land was full of richness, a land of milk and honey. And God said to Moses go in to possess it, yet the people said "We will send men before us and bring us word." Moses agreed and God allowed it and told Moses the makeup of the spies, authorizing them to go into Canaan. The Bible tells us that among the 12 men chosen were Oshea the son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, who is also known as Joshua, a key figure, as well as bold Caleb, son of Jephunneh of the tribe of Judah. Moses instructs them to simply go and report back; of the people there be few or many, strong or weak, walled cities or tents. And the nature of the land, if it be fat or lean. And to return with examples of the fruit of the land, as it was Spring and the first fruits of the vine would be ripe. And so the men spied out the land and returned after 40 days with the famous grapes of Eshcol, a cluster so large two men had to carry it. Reporting to Moses and Aaron and the assembly of the people, they confirm what God had promised, a land flowing with milk and honey. Then the men reported of the people who dwelt in the land and it dismayed the children of Israel. Nevertheless the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there. The Amalekites dwell in the land of the south: and the Hittites, and the Jebusites, and the Amorites, dwell in the mountains: and the Canaanites dwell by the sea, and by the coast of Jordan. Caleb, apparently seeing the fear come on the people immediately tried to calm them down before Moses, saying Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it. Caleb showed faith in God's promise. But the other men answered in doubt and fear. We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we. And they brought up an evil report of the land which they had searched unto the children of Israel, saying, The land, through which we have gone to search it, is a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it are men of a great stature. And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight. Their fear spread to all the people, and the faith in the God who had led them from Egypt and promised to deliver them, faded. And God's anger was kindled. Yet in this thing ye did not believe the Lord your God...And the Lord heard the voice of your words, and was wroth, and sware, saying, Surely there shall not one of these men of this evil generation see that good land, which I sware to give unto your fathers. The exceptions to this curse were Caleb and Joshua. The lack of faith and questioning the word of God led to having the Israelites shut out for a generation. Left to wander 40 years in the wilderness. There are lessons in these stories that are for our benefit as Christians. Here we see how doubt can lead to disputations, and even when assurances of the bold in faith come, many people cling to fear and would rather believe a bad report than trust in the Lord and His word. For this cause, many who seek salvation turn away. Probably the biggest stumbling block people get caught on is the idea of eternal security. That once we are saved, we are always saved. That our faith in Christ is unto redemption. Not only that He exists. Not only that He is the Son of God. Not only that He lived, died for us and was raised again from the dead, but that the earnest of our redemption is given us, the Spirit that indwells and quickens us, sealing us, and that in no way shall we be cast out. That we may know we have eternal life. And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand. I and my Father are one. This is the promise made by Jesus. That we are given the Kingdom of Heaven by faith in Him. The promised land. Speaking in the spirit of Caleb, Paul boldly testifies; For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. Yet, those seeking the truth may need our testimony. They may need us to spy out the land and confirm to them from scripture exactly what God said that they may believe. To boldly proclaim His Gospel. But there will be many, including those who claim to be of God, who give a bad report. Who tell people that their problems are insurmountable. That their sins are like giants and they are as grasshoppers. That to enter the promised land would be death. And so fear and doubt spread and keep people from accepting the truth. From trusting in the Lord to deliver them. This is the spirit of fear and doubt that uses the lie that eternal security doesn't exist. That you can lose your salvation. That because you are small and weak, you won't make it. You won't "persevere to the end." That you must "Repent-of-your-sins!" That if you fail to produce "fruit" by the judgment of men that you cannot make it to Heaven. But we see here, God was providing the fruit, in a size and abundance that they could not even imagine. Joshua and Caleb showed them the fruit that comes from trusting in the Lord. And yet they saw their fears as bigger than their God. We should be reminded by these Old Testament stories that God was going to deliver all of the children of Israel to the promised land, that He would do all the work. Going out before them. They merely had to trust in Him and He would do the rest. The picture of individual salvation is the same. Never let others tell you you need to do works of your own to be saved, that it isn't a free gift paid for by Jesus, that grace isn't grace. Never make your sins or tribulations and problems to be a cause not to trust God. Never let your shame or fear keep you from turning towards Him. When you do, you will see your faith grow. You will witness miracles. You will be led of God to places you can't imagine, and be given the opportunity to do great things for the Lord. To harvest fruit more abundantly. To have your faith quiet other people's fears. To counter those who give a bad report with the peace that passes all understanding. Be bold in Christ. Go read yesterday's study on Numbers 13, especially the Bible passages. Too many seemed to have skipped past and it's sad because what I wrote about them has far more views than the word of God. I promise you, you'll get more from reading scripture than my retarded takes on it. Mark 6:7-13 And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits; and commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse: but be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats. And he said unto them, In what place soever ye enter into an house, there abide till ye depart from that place. And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city. And they went out, and preached that men should repent. And they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them. I was rereading Numbers 13 and it occurred to me the like picture of sending out the 12 spies to the 12 Apostles. And be ye of good courage, and bring of the fruit of the land. Now the time was the time of the firstripe grapes. The pairs of Apostles sent out to spy out the land and to return with fruits of the Spring harvest. The first ripe grapes. In the area of Judea, in what are subtropical zones, the grapes set their first fruit in April and May. The Bible compares Christ's first coming as being pictured in the Spring feasts. The fruit being those that repented unto the truth. Like the grapes of Eshcol, so were the lost sheep of Israel, gathered by the Apostles, and later the 72 disciples, and of course those who came to believe on Pentecost. And the message to the soul winners to be of good courage remains true in this time of gleaning, before the fall harvest, bringing in the sheaves at Christ's return. The agricultural symbolism of the parables and pictures in the Bible provide us a greater understanding to the spiritual things of God. The nature of the seasons and the sowing and planting and harvesting, existing as a means to teach us His ways. All creation exists to reveal God unto us. Amen

We are in Numbers 14, and the narrative really begins to heat up. The 12 spies went out for 40 days into the promised land. And despite their returning with massive fruit, the grapes of Eshcol, and Caleb's faithful cheer that they will easily take the land from those living there, a land flowing with milk and honey, the evil report of the ten spies who feared the Canaanites more than the Lord had turned the Israelites to rebellion. God HATES rebellion and He abhors those who sow discord among the brethren. Proverbs 6:16-19 These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren. Even today, in our churches, there are those that give a bad report, who sow discord among the brethren. Who seek to spread fear and doubt rather than edifying one another. Gossips. Backbiters. Naysayers. Those who call others back to spiritual Egypt. Who lead others to sin. God hates this. And like the 10 bad spies, He will destroy them. Maybe not by plague in front of the congregation, but He will surely let them know His judgment. We should reject and rebuke those who sow discord. Who, like Aaron and Miriam, question the man of God to bring the people to sedition. Who act like gainsaying Korah (who we meet soon). Fear is contagious. Sin is like yeast, and a little leavens the whole lump. We are called to a different spirit, like Caleb. To only fear the Lord. To accept His paths and judgments as true by faith. Without seeing the promised land, and yet to know unquestionably that it's there. Falling in to fear and doubt, rejecting faith, doomed this generation to fall in the wilderness. It nearly led to their utter destruction, but for Moses' plea and appeal to the Lord. Even as we who are saved have an advocate in Christ, we won't be utterly destroyed but God will judge our fear and rebellion, our sowing discord, and He will judge us in this life. Don't be a burden or a stumbling block for others in church. Be a blessing. Seek to build. Be like Caleb. I will smite them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of thee a greater nation and mightier than they. ... How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me. Say unto them, As truly as I live, saith the Lord, as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward which have murmured against me. Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun. But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised. But as for you, your carcases, they shall fall in this wilderness. This story is also a picture of the casting out of the unbelieving Jews in Christ's time and the early church. Of their being cut off and denied the Kingdom. Dispensationalists cannot see that the so-called Jews are like this generation, that despised the land promised to them. And only a believing remnant, like Caleb and Joshua, would be allowed to enter therein. After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years, and ye shall know my breach of promise. Jesus was crucified in 30AD by the reckoning of the Passover and 3 sabbaths in a row before His resurrection. 40yrs later was 70AD and the Romans destroying Jerusalem, the Temple and killing and scattering the remaining Jews. The passing of a generation, left to die in the wilderness, never to enter into the Kingdom, the promised land. The breach of God's promise made known to that wicked and gainsaying generation. Amen

Luke 22:14-20 And when the hour was come, he sat down, and the twelve apostles with him. And he said unto them, With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer: For I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God. And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and said, Take this, and divide it among yourselves: For I say unto you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God shall come. And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me. Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you. 1 Corinthians 11:24-26 And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me. After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, this cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me. For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord's death till he come. Galatians 3:28 There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. Numbers 15 veers back to the clarification of the law, in this chapter, the ordinances of sacrifice, the meat offerings which includes the lambs or goats, which contain the blood of the testament between God and the Israelites, but also the flour and oil, which is made bread and wine, the juice of the vine. Just as Jesus is the lamb slain for our sins, and His body broken like bread for our transgressions, and the cup offered as the blood of the new and better testament between God and man. Ordinances are a memorial. They themselves have no power, and aren't the thing itself, but a picture of that thing, so too are the sacrifices given Moses a picture of Christ to come. Given us, as the Lord's supper, in remembrance of the risen Christ Jesus. That whenever it is done, we memorialize His work and the promise of God, until Jesus returns. And we see that the stranger among the Israelites would be given the same ordinance, for the same memorial, of the same faith. There is no Jew or Greek. God is not a respecter of persons. The salvation offered by faith was always available to whosoever will. To those that call upon the name of the Lord. Before there was Abraham. Before the circumcision. Before Jacob birthed Israel. Before the giving of the law at Sinai. The promise of salvation was given to all who called upon the name of the Lord, and they were made sons of God. Israel was meant to be a beacon, to draw all men to repentance that they could participate in the supper table of the Lamb. But in their failing, God lifted up Jesus that all men be called that some might be saved. Amen.

Jude 3 Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. 4 For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. 5 I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not. 6 And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. 7 Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire. 8 Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities. 9 Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee. 10 But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves. 11 Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. 12 These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots; 13 Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever. Leviticus 10:1-2 And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not. And there went out fire from the LORD, and devoured them, and they died before the LORD. I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.... The Lord killed 14, 700 by plague, the households of Korah the Levite (Core in the NT), Dathan and Abiram's households, swallowed up by the earth. And the 250 men offering strange fire before the Tabernacle, burnt up by fire from Heaven. All for the sin of rebellion against the man of God. And ultimately for determining their way as being correct, despite what God had said. They sought to take over priestly duties that weren't theirs, to speak out against the man of God. Moses and Aaron, the high priest. And even after God's judgment came down on the 250, The Israelites themselves rose up and were smitten with a plague. God would have wiped them all out there. And as Jude tells us, It was for for unbelief. Because ultimately it's a lack of faith in the things of God that destroyed them. We see here too that despite the claims of dispensationalists, there was no hesitation by God to cut off those in the congregation of the children of Israel from not only their promises but casting them into hell. Moses, Who has the power to bind and loose, condemns these men that their sin be not forgiven. So when they die they were going to hell. They were made reprobate by their lack of faith. Apostates. Clouds without water twice dead. And they were plucked up by the roots and cast into the fire. Oh, one more thing regarding Numbers 16 and the rebellion of Koreh and the 250 priests and their plan to usurp the order established by the word of God. This could be considered the first ecumenical council, like those of the Catholic Church. And like those councils of men, who added to or distorted the doctrines of faith given in scripture - heresies like "baptismal regeneration," infant baptism, the allowance of images and idols, Mariology and the worship of saints...These heresies fly in the face of clear Biblical fundamentalism, and instead lean on the gainsaying of Core. The ideas and traditions of men. It is impossible to not see how God views these wicked men and their false doctrines of devils.

Hebrews 9:3-4 And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all; which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant... Isaiah 11:1-4 And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord; And shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord: and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears: But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth: with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked. The budding of Aaron's rod, a dead branch, brought to life, as an image of the chosen High Priest of the people is a clear and obvious picture of Christ Jesus. A rod out of the stem of Jesse, a Branch that grew out of his roots. Who was dead and was risen, and, like the almonds that Aaron's rod brought forth, Jesus gave forth fruit for all time, those that believe on His holy name. Aaron's rod is added to the Ark with the manna and the tablets, in the Tabernacle of testimony. They literally were carrying God's word made manifest, in the heart of their camp. The testimony that His word was true. This method of quelling rebellion amongst the children of Israel, allowing the will of God to be made clear by way of miracle, seems to us perfectly decisive. Aaron would be the high priest. The Levites would serve the Tabernacle. A gift to the Lord, given to bear the iniquity of the people. And to redeem them. As the next chapter tells us; And ye shall keep the charge of the sanctuary, and the charge of the altar: that there be no wrath any more upon the children of Israel. And Moses did as the Lord commanded him. But did the anointing of Aaron and his sons and the Levites cease the murmurings of the children of Israel? And the children of Israel spake unto Moses, saying, Behold, we die, we perish, we all perish. Whosoever cometh any thing near unto the tabernacle of the Lord shall die: shall we be consumed with dying? They acknowledged that they would perish if they came near the Tabernacle. That there would be only the Levitical priesthood as God commands, but their fear of dying makes them seem bitter. Their understanding that they shall all perish without accepting the rod that God had chosen to bear their iniquity, who would redeem them, coupled with fear, carries with it a resentment that mirrors that of people today, reacting to the truth of Christ Jesus as our high priest. A resentment that in many hearts leads to rebellion and reprobation. God's word doesn't just provide us the model of faith and sanctification that we see in men like Moses, or Caleb. Or as we will see in Joshua. Scripture seems to show us more glimpses of unbelief in stiff-necked and gainsaying people. And the destruction they suffer as a result of their pride. But we are those who hear God's word, see the budding of the rod and know His will, and delight in it. Or we should if we walk in the Spirit, reading His word. That we gain understanding and acceptance of it. Amen

Here in Numbers 18, following the budding of Aaron's rod in the previous chapter, we have God's covenant with the Levites and Aaron and his sons, and their portion. The Levitical priesthood is given to them the service of the Tabernacle, and the iniquity of the people to be cleansed in offerings as an ordinance of the faith. And Aaron and his sons to take their iniquity and those of the Levites, and make offerings unto the Lord. The Lord gives them the gift of service and in exchange they will live off their portion of the meats given to the Lord, the tithes taken, which the priests offer up a tenth themselves. And they are set to redeem the firstborn with the shekels commanded of God after the deaths of the firstborn of Egypt, at Passover. These Levitical laws are given as a picture of Christ to come and the service of the Lord that Christians today are called to. To offer redemption and forgiveness to the people. It is funny that of all the talk of covenants by dispensationalists, they never bring this one up. As so-called Jews have no priesthood. No offerings. No cleansing of the iniquity and trespass and sin of the people. No redemption of the first born. No heave offering. No sacrifice for their atonement. The admonishments against allowing non-Levites into the Tabernacle, and even against Levites entering behind the veil which was for Aaron and his sons, that those who offended would surely die, is again showing there is only one way to please God, by following His word. It echoes the commandment given Adam in the garden. It is repeated in Christ's preaching that He is the only way to the Father. Our High Priest. The lack of an inheritance in the land, among the children of Israel, other than service, is a like picture of the separation we as Christians should have with this world. We look towards a better country. A heavenly Kingdom. We are a holy nation. A peculiar people. A royal priesthood. The cares of this world are not ours. But the service of the Lord, and the blessings that come from it are our portion. As the increase of the threshing floor. As the increase of the winepress. Amen

The law of the water of separation is given by the Lord. That those that become unclean by contact with a dead person could be purified, and the things of the tent where in the person died, and their sin be covered, a purification ritual. The law requires a red heifer, without blemish, be brought without the camp and slain and burned. In the fire was required cedar, hyssop and scarlet. This is a holocaust, a burnt offering, that is an explicit picture of Christ. The cedar wood of the cross, the hyssop dipped in vinegar, the scarlet of His blood. The ash mixed with water to be used on the 3rd day for purification, that on the 7th day the unclean may be clean. The parallel with Jesus 3 days and nights, and our redemption at his eventual return. Note, this is not a "prophecy of a red heifer," which has been in the news lately. Where they claim that "Israel" needs a red heifer to build the third temple, a "prophecy" some American cow farmer invented in the 1990s. Whatever prophecy this ritual foresaw was filled in Christ. The burnt offering for our sin, and the water of life given us to purify ourselves. Also, I wanted to circle back to Numbers 18:19, and the "covenant of salt," made by God with Aaron; All the heave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer unto the Lord, have I given thee, and thy sons and thy daughters with thee, by a statute for ever: it is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord unto thee and to thy seed with thee. The same phrase is used in 2 Chronicles 13:5, given to David; Ought ye not to know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt? Thus the covenant of salt is bestowed on a priesthood and kingdom. Both fulfilled in Christ Jesus who is our High Priest and our King. Salt is a preservative, a thing that keeps decay away, protecting it. Just as we who believe are the salt of the earth; Matthew 5:13 Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. The preservation of the world is given us, just as the preservation of God's priesthood and kingdom are kept forever in Christ. And when that salt is taken out of the world, it will be destroyed.

Exodus 17:6 Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel. Numbers 20 begins like most stories about the children of Israel, complaining and carrying on with a lack of faith or fear of the Lord. They have witnessed triumphant miracles, seen the hand of the Lord strike down their enemies by the sea they passed through. Been guided through the desert by a pillar of flame. Had their bellies filled with bread made from manna of heaven. And have had water come from out from a rock to drink. They have seen punishment of the Lord, His wrath revealed from Heaven, taking out thousands of their people. By fire. Plague. Venom. The earth swallowing up those that rebelled against the Lord. His mercy and His wrath, the same revelations which Paul writes about in Romans, that no man has an excuse to not know and fear the Lord. And yet they complain. And so here, having been condemned for a generation to wander the wilderness for their unbelief in the promise of God to deliver them into the promised land, and fresh off of the rebellion that had the Lord had slain so many by plague, they once again complained to Moses. "Wherefore have ye made us to come up out of Egypt?" Lacking faith that God would provide. Moses and Aaron go to the Lord in prayer with their problem. The correct thing to do, of course. And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water, and thou shalt bring forth to them water out of the rock: so thou shalt give the congregation and their beasts drink. Similar to the event that happened earlier in Exodus, the people murmuring in complaint, and God had Moses strike the rock and brought forth water. So the people knew it was possible and Moses knew to follow the word of the Lord. And yet, in his anger or frustration, Moses disobeyed the word of God, and instead of speaking to the rock, he struck it with his rod. Not once, as at Meribah in Exodus, but twice. Speaking to the rock is a picture of calling upon Christ for salvation; If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water. God wishes to be sanctified by the people from this miracle. (Not that He needs man to make him holy, in this use it means to acknowledge that He is holy.) And because Moses disobeyed His word, God keeps Him and Aaron from ever stepping foot in the land He had promised them. But the water came forth and the people and their cattle drank, and they sanctified the Lord anyway, despite that great cost. Now the people wandering came to the boundaries of Edom, their brothers after the flesh, and not wishing to battle, Moses sent word that they would pass along the king's highway, and not take of the fields of vineyards. Only asking for safe passage through in the name of the God their mutual fathers knew. And the Edomites denied them passage, and threatened to come put them to the sword. And again, Moses entreated them to allow them passage, even offering to pay for any incidental water their cattle may drink. And again Edom said no, coming down to war against the Israelites. A contentious relationship that would ultimately see Edom destroyed and her people scattered, as they'd no longer followed the Lord. And so to avoid war, Moses turned his people back into the wilderness. You can see comparing this story to the incident in Exodus 17, where Moses sent Joshua against the Amalek shortly after bringing forth the water from the rock, and they were victorious against their oppressors. Obedience to the word of God, and they received the water and later victory against their enemies by the power of the Lord. And here, in disobedience, slinking away in fear. In the Christian life, we may go through phases like this. Where despite being delivered for so much early in our salvation, and despite seeing the blessings that come from obeying God, we may backslide. Become disillusioned. No longer listen to what His says, and do our own thing. Striking the rock, twice even. And when it comes time for battles against the world, turning in fear, unsure without faith. It can be difficult to get back on track. To turn to God in humility and ask forgiveness. But if we do, He is merciful to forgive and forget. He wants to do things for His children that we may sanctify His holy name. Finally, we are told of the death of Aaron and the Lord passing the mantle of High Priest to his son, Eleazar. Moses' sister Miriam passes earlier in the chapter, but to little notice. Aaron however is given 30 days of honor in mourning by all Israel. Worth noticing.

And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread. Chapter 21 of Numbers begins with a military victory, God delivering their enemies into their hands, and it ends with military victories. And yet in the midst of it, we see this familiar complaint of the Israelites. "If God be real, why bad stuff happen?" They are spoiled by their own lack of faith and gratitude. They begin during their journey having spies captured in the land of Arad king of the Canaanites, and so the people bowing a vow to the Lord that they will utterly destroy the cities of their foes, if He delivers them into their hands. And the Lord hears them and does just that, and they destroy the cities of the Canaanites. But this faith in Him is short lived. As they sought a way around Edom to avoid their borders, they become discouraged again. And complain again. They say they have no water, despite being given water multiple times. They say they have no bread, despite even admitting it is the "light bread" of Manna that they are sick of. And so the Lord sends fiery serpents among them to torment and slay the people of Israel. You would think they'd have learned this lesson, but people can be stubborn. Have short memories of what God has done for them. Don't appreciate blessings and come to despise the spiritual bread. A like picture of the word come down from Heaven. Daily reading of scripture is for the NT Christian the same as gathering the Manna, to grind into bread. They have backslidden and we tend to as well when we neglect that daily bread. And so, His wrath revealed against them, they come to Moses to beg forgiveness. And the Lord tells him to make a brazen snake, that the people may look upon it lifted up, and live. A picture of Christ; John 3:14-16 And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. After this short story, we are given an account of the victory against the Amorites, through the power of the Lord delivering them. And the king of Bashan, who went against them and perished. And the children of Israel took their cities and killed everyone of the people. Thus Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorites. There appears reference of a book of the wars of the Israelites, and it is mentioned in Exodus and may be referred to in some of the prophets. Tales or songs sung of the victories the children of Israel had in this time. But that it's lost to us means it ultimately wasn't important to us. There are similar mentions in Kings and Chronicles to other accounts recorded. But we get the gist from the canonical books. There is an itch some have where they desperately want to know these things, and seek out extrabiblical sources and are prone to believing Jewish fables offered as truth. It is a fine line to walk and discernment is a must. But for most seeking truth outside of the Bible, it becomes a trap and a snare. Just look at the weight some give to apocrypha. And to clear forgeries like the "Gospel" of Andrew and the "Book of Enoch." People get derailed, even saved Christians, by studying things that had they been important, would have been inspired and preserved by God in His word. Until someone has read the Bible multiple times, I really suggest staying away from histories and extrabiblical accounts and sources. Build up the knowledge of the Lord and the Spirit will provide discernment. 2 Kings 18 Now it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign. 2 Twenty and five years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name also was Abi, the daughter of Zachariah. 3 And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father did. 4 He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan. 5 He trusted in the Lord God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor any that were before him. 6 For he clave to the Lord, and departed not from following him, but kept his commandments, which the Lord commanded Moses. Just to add this postscript to the study on Numbers 2, this chapter and the story of the brazen serpent, is often cited by Catholics and Orthodox to justify their wicked pagan Idolatry. To a man, those who have brought it up to me don't know or ever heard of "Nehushtan." Nehushtan means a thing of bronze, and it was not meant to be prayed to, to be bowed before or served. It wasn't meant to have incense burned to it, or candles lit in devotion. It has a singular purpose and it was to serve as a picture of Christ, who was lifted up on the cross, and became sin that we may look to Him and live. Hezekiah, who did what was right in the sight of the Lord destroyed idols and temples and high places of the false gods, and he brake apart the brazen serpent. It was being worshipped in the same way crucifixes are in these apostate churches today. A picture for our benefit to understand the concept of salvation and eternal life in Christ, whose literal purpose was simply to heal Israelites bitten by the fiery snakes God had sent among them. The physical application and spiritual are given us. And it is not a license to Idolatry.

Deuteronomy 23:3-6 An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever: Because they met you not with bread and with water in the way, when ye came forth out of Egypt; and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam; but the Lord thy God turned the curse into a blessing unto thee, because the Lord thy God loved thee.Thou shalt not seek their peace nor their prosperity all thy days for ever. Joshua 13 15 And Moses gave unto the tribe of the children of Reuben inheritance according to their families. 16 And their coast was from Aroer, that is on the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain by Medeba; 17 Heshbon, and all her cities that are in the plain; Dibon, and Bamothbaal, and Bethbaalmeon, 18 And Jahaza, and Kedemoth, and Mephaath, 19 And Kirjathaim, and Sibmah, and Zarethshahar in the mount of the valley, 20 And Bethpeor, and Ashdothpisgah, and Bethjeshimoth, 21 And all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, which reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses smote with the princes of Midian, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, which were dukes of Sihon, dwelling in the country. 22 Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them. 23 And the border of the children of Reuben was Jordan, and the border thereof. This was the inheritance of the children of Reuben after their families, the cities and the villages thereof. Micah 6:5 O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim unto Gilgal; that ye may know the righteousness of the LORD. Revelation 2:14 But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication. Jude 1:11 Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. 2 Peter 2:15 Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness. The presentation of the story of Balaam in Numbers 22-24 shows the glory and truth of the Lord will be spoken, even if through a priest of Baal, offering sacrifices on high places, including the altars on the mount of Peor. Balaam knew to fear the Lord, and knew not to go against God because it would end poorly for him. And when God knew he would go, He allowed it, that He could show Balaam his folly from the mouth of an ass. And by the Spirit of the Lord, Balaam was unable to curse Israel. Despite the burnt offerings to Baal. Despite the bribes and threats of the king. Like the donkey, the Lord put words in the mouth of a false prophet, that we may know the righteousness of the Lord. Balaam, under God's word, gives a wonderful prophecy to Christ Jesus; How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river's side, as the trees of lign aloes which the Lord hath planted, and as cedar trees beside the waters. He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters, and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted. God brought him forth out of Egypt; he hath as it were the strength of an unicorn: he shall eat up the nations his enemies, and shall break their bones, and pierce them through with his arrows. He couched, he lay down as a lion, and as a great lion: who shall stir him up? Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee. I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth. And Edom shall be a possession, Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies; and Israel shall do valiantly. Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion, and shall destroy him that remaineth of the city. Balak the king was angry at Balaam, but as Balaam had told them; If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the commandment of the Lord, to do either good or bad of mine own mind; but what the Lord saith, that will I speak? Balaam knew he had no control over what the Lord would put in his mouth to say. He tried to warn the princess who came for him. He reminds the king of Moab. And in the remaining appearances of the prophet of Baal, we see his true nature revealed and his fate, slain at the hands of Israel.

The aftermath of the story of Balaam, a priest of Baal, who was called up by the king of Moab to curse the Israelites, especially after sacrifices made to Baal on the mountain of Peor. We see that having failed, because the word of God was made to come out of Balaam and bless the people, that the Israelites fell to whoredoms with the woman of Moab. Not only in the sense of fornication, but worshiping their false god at the very altar of Peor used by Balaam. This is the matter of Peor. One of the men brought a Midianite woman to his tent, in the sight of Moses and the assembly. And God sent a plaque again among the Israelites. But as the children gathered to God at the Tabernacle, the son of Eleazar, grandson of Aaron, Phinehas, took a spear and killed the man and the Midianite. And the Lord stops the plague for his zeal. 24,000 had died. The Lord confirms the covenant of peace with Aaron and the Levites, in Phinehas, and instructs Moses to vex the Midianites and to smite them for they vexed the people with their wiles. They used their women to lead Israel after Baal. To eat the sacrifices and vow before their altars. This will be a common theme. Outlandish women bringing the men of Israel to whoredoms, the worship of their false gods. We see a pattern forming. That as God blessed Israel, freeing them from bondage, making covenants with them, giving them the perfect law, feeding them in the wilderness, bringing forth water from the rock, defeating their enemies, driving them out before them, even unbeknownst to them preventing Balaam from cursing them from afar, that despite all that the Lord does for them, they either fall into complaint and lack of gratitude, or into sexual sin and chasing after false gods. And they are struck down by the Lord in His wrath. And still they complain. And still they go whoring. And though their number is great, the matter of Peor is one in a string of plagues and pestilence, fiery serpents and fire from heaven, that have consumed thousands and thousands of the children of Israel. A winnowing has taken place. God is sorting out the chaff. Just as He told Moses, the generation that would die in the wilderness.

After the latest plague that befell Israel, the Lord tells Moses to again count the tribes and get the number of them there are. And again, by camp and tribe Moses counts the men, over 20. Fighting age. And receives their number. I will note that what was 12 tribes has become many nations already. The sons of the sons, their own people. Clans forming, as they would inherit the land of their fathers, given in the promise. It is a subtle thing but it seems important that they are listed this way at this time. And after the polling, and the count is made, that among them numbered was not a man left alive who were counted before in the wilderness of Sinai, way back at the beginning of Numbers, except for Caleb and Joshua. Just as God said. They would all die in the wilderness.

Chapter 27 of Numbers covers two cases of inheritance, one by the law and one by election. When the daughters of Zelophehad come to ask that their father's portion fall on them, as he had no sons, Moses seeks the council of the Lord. The establishment of the law of inheritance, the idea that each family have its place, and the generational wealth of the land God gave them to possess being passed down by the law, is set as a statute of judgement, a precedent set by the Lord. Of course this idea always was, that the eldest inherits by law. But, as we see played out with Ishmael and Isaac, Esau and Jacob, even with Israel and Joseph, giving the second youngest of 12 the double portion usually reserved for the eldest, that some are elect, or chosen, to receive that inheritance over the one legally entitled to it. We see that as Moses is commanded by God to climb one last mountain, Abarim, to see the promised land, his thoughts are with who shall inherit his role as leader of the people. And it doesn't fall on his own sons, Gershom and Eliezer, who by law it could be expected, but to Joshua, the son of Nun. God chooses to elect Joshua in place of the children after the law. Galatians 4 Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; 2 But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father. 3 Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world: 4 But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, 5 To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. 6 And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. 7 Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. 8 Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods. 9 But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage? 10 Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years. 11 I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain. 12 Brethren, I beseech you, be as I am; for I am as ye are: ye have not injured me at all. 13 Ye know how through infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you at the first. 14 And my temptation which was in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus. 15 Where is then the blessedness ye spake of? for I bear you record, that, if it had been possible, ye would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me. 16 Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth? 17 They zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them. 18 But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you. 19 My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you, 20 I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you. 21 Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law? 22 For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman. 23 But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise. 24 Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which gendereth to bondage, which is Agar. 25 For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children. 26 But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all. 27 For it is written, Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband. 28 Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise. 29 But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit, even so it is now. 30 Nevertheless what saith the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman. 31 So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free. Romans 4 12 And the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised. 13 For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. 14 For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: 15 Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression. 16 Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all, 17 (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were. Romans 8 14 For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. 15 For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. 16 The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: 17 And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. Romans 9 6 Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: 7 Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. 8 That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. 9 For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son. 10 And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac; 11 (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;) 12 It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. 13 As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. 14 What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid. 15 For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. 16 So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy. The idea that there is a legal inheritance, for earthly matters and yet an inheritance and blessing of election for spiritual things of God, is found continuously in scripture, starting with Cain the elder, and Abel the younger. And it all pictures the adoption of the Gentiles in the seed of Abraham, who is Christ Jesus over Abraham's children after the flesh. The first children of God, circumcised of the flesh, rejected, reprobate, for the adoption of children of God, circumcised of the heart. The entire Bible teaches this. What is derisively called "replacement theology," is simply the understanding that the eldest may receive the inheritance of earthly things, but the Kingdom of Heaven is only inherited by faith. Just as the daughters of Manasseh were given the land promised their father in the absence of brothers by law, and Joshua was given leadership of the children of Israel by the election of faith.

31 Ye shall offer them beside the continual burnt offering, and his meat offering, (they shall be unto you without blemish) and their drink offerings. As the book of Numbers begins to wind down, and Moses nears the end of his life, the Lord reiterates His ordinances and feasts. There is a new high priest. The men of the first generation having all died in the wilderness except Caleb and Joshua. The Lord lays out the requirements for the continual burnt sacrifices and sabbath sacrifices and the offerings made for sin. Each has its specific requirements, varying by the day or type. The offerings of lambs or kids or bullocks. The flour and oil to be given. And the drink offerings poured out. All a picture of Jesus. All a continuous savor to the Lord. As the children of Israel reach the promised land, they are called to remember these ordinances for all time, that their faith in the Lord not be forgotten, and His favor given them. Verse 7 contains a description of the drink offering. And the drink offering thereof shall be the fourth part of an hin for the one lamb: in the holy place shalt thou cause the strong wine to be poured unto the Lord for a drink offering. This is a verse that could be used to defend the consumption of alcohol, or the blasphemy of using fermented wine at the Lord's supper, although it rarely is. But the prohibition against the priests consumption of strong wine; Leviticus 10:8-9 And the Lord spake unto Aaron, saying, Do not drink wine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sons with thee, when ye go into the tabernacle of the congregation, lest ye die: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations: ...and the numerous places in scripture that teach against it present a problem for those seeking to use this verse to justify it. But what then? First, we see the drink offering is to be poured out with the burnt offering, which is a continual fire. Alcoholic strong drink would feed the fire, where new wine would quench it. Also, where fermented juices store easily, there is the idea that in the wilderness it would be easiest to obtain and have on hand for the purpose of a twice daily sacrifice. Ellicott's Commentary states: (7) Shalt thou cause the strong wine to be poured . . . --Better, pour out the drink offering of strong drink. The word shecar, which is here rendered "strong wine," denotes any kind of intoxicating drink, whether made from grapes, honey, or grain; but it is more frequently used to denote a drink which is not made from grapes, as, e.g., in Leviticus 10:9, where the command is given to Aaron and his sons not to drink "wine nor strong drink" (shecar) when they went into the tent of meeting. In the parallel passage in Exodus, the drink offering was to consist of "the fourth part of an hin of wine" (Numbers 29:40). (Comp. Numbers 15:5.) In Exodus 30:9 it is forbidden to pour any drink offering upon the altar of incense, from which passage it has been inferred that the drink offerings were poured upon the altar of burnt sacrifice. The indication that strong wine is liquor from other sources than grapes, which has weak fermentation. Matthew Henry commentary says; The daily sacrifice is called a continual burnt-offering; when we are bid to pray always, at least every morning and evening we should offer up solemn prayers and praises to God. Nothing is added here but that the wine poured out in the drink-offering is to be strong wine, to teach us to serve God with the best we have. It was a figure of the blood of Christ, the memorial of which is still left to the church in wine; and of the blood of the martyrs, which was poured out as a drink-offering on the sacrifice and service of our faith, Php 2:17. I only note these to show that this passage is unique in what it commands, and the reason unclear other than to suppose it is a libation for God, and His will it be offered.
