Here in Numbers 29 and 30, we have the Lord again reestablishing commandments and ordinances of the law. We will have a second giving of the law when we go through the book of Deuteronomy as well. God repeats each thing as important, for the edification of the children of Israel, and to our own edifying as Christians in our life and as judges in the Millennium to come. The fall feasts, as we have covered elsewhere, signifying the second coming of Christ. The feast of trumpets, as in Revelation. The law of vows, especially concerning fathers and husbands, over their women, reflecting the order of hierarchy given by the Lord. It makes what is often done flippantly and in vain today, seem far more grave and serious. But as Jesus said, better to not vow at all. We are nearing the end of Numbers, God willing by the end of this week. These recaps are necessary as constant reminders that the Israelites were not left to rely on tradition, but on the word of God given them. Generational reestablishing of the Law by the word of God marks the time in the wilderness. The books of Moses kept to be read by the priests and the sacrifices made continually that they may not forget what they are a picture of.

Another straight narrative in Numbers 31, a telling of the slaughter of the Midianites, who had tried to curse the Israelites through Balaam, and who had managed through whoredoms to bring many to worship Baal. We see the deaths of their kings and of Balaam, their priest. The spoil taken, which included male children and adult women, whom Moses insists be put to the sword, least they lead men astray again and another plague is sent by God in judgment. The spoils then left are divided up, each man of war his own, and the people their own, and to the Levites a share, and to God, His. Further the men of war offer of their own share a portion to honor God, as a memorial. We see that the law of the unclean being purified by the manner laid out in Numbers 19 is applied here. Each man who had slain or touched a body, their captives and the spoil, all things that could not be purified by fire were taken without the camp for 7 days, with the washings done on the 3rd day. When you consider all the pestilence that had been brought against them in the wilderness, adherence to this practice makes sense, pleasing God and also isolating any contaminated person or item. The things that could be purified by fire were passed through the fire. Gold and silver and other metals. It reminds me of 1 Corinthians 3:12-15; Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire. The spoil, the treasure, that we store up in Heaven that is given of the works we build upon the foundation that is Christ. And the crowns we earn which are thrown at the feet of Christ, as the men of war who give of their share a tribute to God; Revelation 4:10-11 The four and twenty elders fall down before him that sat on the throne, and worship him that liveth for ever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying, Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created.

Genesis 49:3-4 Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, The excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power: Unstable as water, thou shalt not excel; Because thou wentest up to thy father's bed; Then defiledst thou it: he went up to my couch. 49:18-19 I have waited for thy salvation, O LORD. Gad, a troop shall overcome him: but he shall overcome at the last. Genesis 48:13-18 And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right hand, and brought them near unto him. And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim's head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh's head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the firstborn. And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day, The Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth. And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he held up his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head unto Manasseh's head. And Joseph said unto his father, Not so, my father: for this is the firstborn; put thy right hand upon his head. And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it: he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations. And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set Ephraim before Manasseh. Here in Numbers 32, we find the tribes of Ruben, Gad and Manasseh, entreating Moses that they be allowed to set their tribes homelands east of the Jordan, rather than cross over into Canaan. They had much cattle, especially after the spoil of the nations God had driven out before them, and those He had them put down by the edge of the sword. This land was good for cattle, they argued. A familiar theme of those choosing the easier path in this world; Genesis 13:8-11 And Abram said unto Lot, Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren. Is not the whole land before thee? separate thyself, I pray thee, from me: if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if thou depart to the right hand, then I will go to the left. And Lot lifted up his eyes, and beheld all the plain of Jordan, that it was well watered every where, before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, even as the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt, as thou comest unto Zoar. Then Lot chose him all the plain of Jordan; and Lot journeyed east: and they separated themselves the one from the other. Settling for the land, east of the Jordan because of having much cattle and the land being good for the herds, ended poorly for just Lot. For the sons of Ruben, the first born who was denied his inheritance by law, and told his people should not excel, perhaps the idea of the bird in the hand appealed to them more than their lesser status and inheritance would be in the promised land. Gad as well, of Jacob and his first wife Zipporah, were not favored among the tribes, but were warriors. They sought the frontier surrounded by enemies of Israel. Manasseh, also the eldest of Joseph, like Ruben to Israel. Like Edom to Jacob, who was destined to be great, but Ephraim the younger was the elect, given the greater blessing. These tribes sought to receive what they felt was good enough, rather than seek that which the Lord had allotted them. And Moses, afraid of a repeat of the 12 spies and the sowing of fear among the people by their bad report, which cursed the children of Israel with 40yr wandering in the wilderness, tells them no, least their not crossing over brings a similar fear to the people, and kindles God's wrath. But they agree to lead their armies of fighting men, armed for war, over with the rest of the tribes and fight for them, and Moses accepts the offer. And Moses said unto them, If ye will do this thing, if ye will go armed before the Lord to war, And will go all of you armed over Jordan before the Lord, until he hath driven out his enemies from before him, And the land be subdued before the Lord: then afterward ye shall return, and be guiltless before the Lord, and before Israel; and this land shall be your possession before the Lord. But if ye will not do so, behold, ye have sinned against the Lord: and be sure your sin will find you out. Commanding Joshua and Eleazar the priest that this would be acceptable terms unto the Lord.

The retelling of all the movements of the camp of Israel. The places they'd been for 40 years. Wandering in the wilderness as God moved them. It is often said they wandered aimlessly. That they were lost and unable to find the promised land. But their every movement was by the Spirit of God. The pillar of smoke and fire. Following the Lord. As they prepared to enter the land of Canaan, the Lord instructs them to drive the inhabitants out before them, and to destroy all their images and idols. To tear down their altars in the high places. And God warns Israel if they fail to do this, all that remain will be a vexation to their people. And He warns again about the conditional nature of their covenant (which dispensationalists deny). He says He will do unto them as He thought to do unto the Canaanites. Destroy them. Drive them from the land. To be cut off.

Basically. I will say that while the gift of the promised land was given as an inheritance to those children of Israel, by tribe and by lot, this inheritance was always not only conditional, but by the election of grace, given of God. God elected that they would receive this land, by covenant of their keeping Him as their God, which they failed to do, the fault being with the people. The Bible is a book of winnowing, narrowing down and casting off. Of God choosing to bless the lesser. The younger. Not by law or entitlement, but by His purpose and need. Inheritance, but with caveats to His purpose. A continuous replacement. If the study of Numbers has taught us anything, God has no problem casting off into the fire any branches He wishes. Reprobation in the Wilderness meant not only being damned, but destroyed in the most painful awful ways. Plague and fire and being swallowed up by the ground itself.

In Numbers 35, God gives the law of sanctuary cities and the judgments against murderers and the allowance for cases of manslaughter. Read through it and you really can appreciate how perfect God's law is. With the granting of the land to the tribes of Israel, given by lot, the Levites who have no inheritance are to be given land within the tribes, cites and suburbs for living among them. To minister and serve. And on top of that, given cities to serve as refuge for those that accidentally slay a man, that someone seeking revenge not slay them in return. All to minimize the blood shed in the land, which cannot be cleansed. Multiple times in Numbers, the laws for cleansing those who were exposed to death or bloodshed. But the land itself cries out over bloodshed, as we saw in the murder of Abel; Genesis 4:8-10 And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's keeper? And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground. It was this curse of Canaan, made by Noah when Ham had uncovered his father's nakedness, and so by the time of Exodus, the Canaanites land was polluted by the blood shed and offerings to idols. God's judgment upon them that they be dispossessed and slain to give the land to Israel. But it was polluted again, even by the wickedness of the Israelites who turned to whoredoms and killed their own children to idols as the people there before them; Psalm 106:37-40 Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils, And shed innocent blood, Even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, Whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: And the land was polluted with blood. Thus were they defiled with their own works, And went a whoring with their own inventions. Therefore was the wrath of the LORD kindled against his people, Insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance. And so the idea of having a city of refuge, where the innocent of murder could flee and live, so long as they were found to have done it by accident, until the death of the high priest. That the revenger catching them outside the city was innocent of the blood. And that the murderer be put down upon the testimony of witnesses, their own blood being upon them. It's an elegant system that prevents the people from falling into tribal warfare, especially given the Levitical priests being among all the tribes. Artist's rendition of the Levitical walled cities and suburbs

The final chapter of Numbers, and one last bit of housekeeping for Moses and the law, revisiting the command of God that land inheritance in a family that has no sons should go to the daughters. The worry being that their daughters marry of another tribe and this dilutes the inheritance when those sons take possession of the land. Moses gives the command of the Lord that the inheritance remains in the tribe, so as the daughter must marry those of her father's family. Recall that at jubilee, there is a right of return, that any land sold or let to outsiders is returned to the family that had owned it, keeping the boundaries and habitations thereof as given by God. Now daughters could marry outside the tribe, but not carry with them rights to property inherited. The Lord had need that the tribes remain separated as much as possible, leading to the birth of Christ. And with that commandment, we come to the end of the study of Numbers. Difficult in some places, wonderful picture of Jesus in others, and wisdom and doctrine throughout, well worth the effort. Psalm 106 Praise ye the Lord. O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever. 2 Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord? who can shew forth all his praise? 3 Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times. 4 Remember me, O Lord, with the favour that thou bearest unto thy people: O visit me with thy salvation; 5 That I may see the good of thy chosen, that I may rejoice in the gladness of thy nation, that I may glory with thine inheritance. 6 We have sinned with our fathers, we have committed iniquity, we have done wickedly. 7 Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt; they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies; but provoked him at the sea, even at the Red sea. 8 Nevertheless he saved them for his name's sake, that he might make his mighty power to be known. 9 He rebuked the Red sea also, and it was dried up: so he led them through the depths, as through the wilderness. 10 And he saved them from the hand of him that hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy. 11 And the waters covered their enemies: there was not one of them left. 12 Then believed they his words; they sang his praise. 13 They soon forgat his works; they waited not for his counsel: 14 But lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert. 15 And he gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul. 16 They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord. 17 The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan and covered the company of Abiram. 18 And a fire was kindled in their company; the flame burned up the wicked. 19 They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the molten image. 20 Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass. 21 They forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt; 22 Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea. 23 Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them. 24 Yea, they despised the pleasant land, they believed not his word: 25 But murmured in their tents, and hearkened not unto the voice of the Lord. 26 Therefore he lifted up his hand against them, to overthrow them in the wilderness: 27 To overthrow their seed also among the nations, and to scatter them in the lands. 28 They joined themselves also unto Baalpeor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead. 29 Thus they provoked him to anger with their inventions: and the plague brake in upon them. 30 Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed. 31 And that was counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations for evermore. 32 They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes: 33 Because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips. 34 They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them: 35 But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works. 36 And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them. 37 Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils, 38 And shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: and the land was polluted with blood. 39 Thus were they defiled with their own works, and went a whoring with their own inventions. 40 Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance. 41 And he gave them into the hand of the heathen; and they that hated them ruled over them. 42 Their enemies also oppressed them, and they were brought into subjection under their hand. 43 Many times did he deliver them; but they provoked him with their counsel, and were brought low for their iniquity. 44 Nevertheless he regarded their affliction, when he heard their cry: 45 And he remembered for them his covenant, and repented according to the multitude of his mercies. 46 He made them also to be pitied of all those that carried them captives. 47 Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the heathen, to give thanks unto thy holy name, and to triumph in thy praise. 48 Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting: and let all the people say, Amen. Praise ye the Lord. Psalm 106 is a sort of reader's digest version of Exodus and Numbers, and the prophecy of the coming of His holy name, in Christ Jesus. A prayer in triumph and praise. Amen

Beginning Deuteronomy, which means 'second law,' Moses retelling of the events that led the Israelites to the verge of the promised land, and the restatement of the law of God. The events retold in this chapter are familiar to us, having just finished Numbers. But there is still doctrine to be found. Deuteronomy 1 has the clearest proof text on the idea that there is an age of accountability. That children do not carry some original sin, as some insist falsely, but are innocent without the law. Moreover your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, and your children, which in that day had no knowledge between good and evil, they shall go in thither, and unto them will I give it, and they shall possess it. This isn't a set age, but a spiritual condition. For some, the realization between good and evil comes younger, some older. Some developmentally disabled, it may never come at all. This idea is reflected in Paul's writing, in Romans 7:9 For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died. The concept of infants being born with sin is a wicked one, but required by the apostate false churches that teach baby "baptism" in order to make a lifetime claim on a soul, to exert power and control over the masses. The heresy of baptismal regeneration leads to it, and for mothers especially, the idea that their baby could pass and end up in hell or "limbo" was too much to bear. And silly women carried away by false doctrine, like Eve, lead their men to stray. And so, heretical practices take root, and damnable ones at that. Matthew 18:2-4 And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them, and said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven. We need to humble ourselves as children to receive the grace of salvation. Knowing we are helpless in obtaining our own righteousness and totally reliant on the Father. 2 Samuel 12:15-23 And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah's wife bare unto David, and it was very sick. David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth. And the elders of his house arose, and went to him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them. And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead? But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead. Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the LORD, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat. Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread. And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live? But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me. David took comfort in this fact when his infant son by Bathsheba was taken from him. David knew he would see him again, in Heaven. This comfort is given to all who lose a child, especially in infancy, but those who push the false doctrine of baby baptism steal it from parents, giving them fear in its place. Cruel and evil. Making God a monster.

Here in Deuteronomy 2, Moses continues his retelling of the time in the wilderness, the 40 years recounted in part in the Book of Numbers. There are some perspective changes and details added that broaden the underlying history, and containing details that flesh out the story. A few things that stand out to me in this reading; the promises of land to Lot and Edom, and the nature of the giants that were in many of these lands. Modern "Jews" and their Zionist pets will make quite a big deal about the conditional covenant made in the wilderness to deliver the land to Israel, which had been promised to Abraham and his seed, which is Christ. A promise repeated to Issac and Jacob. They claim ownership as the nation of Israel (by deception, but none the less) based off this idea that they are the inheritors. But the promises to Lot and Esau were to the nations they spawned, by the blessings of God, and yet those nations were destroyed in time, and the land taken as spoil, after the wickedness of the people. The same as Israel. The same as the remnant in Judah. God judges nations on this earth and their bounds and habitations are His to give and take away. As for the giants, the men who were of such stature they frightened the spies sent to scout the promised land, whose reports caused fear and doubt among the children of Israel, leading to the banishment of that generation of men, precipitating the 40 years of wandering, we learn that there were such giants in the other lands, too. Anakims, Emims, Horims, Zamzummims... Mighty people who occupied land God had promised, and who were destroyed by God in fulfilling those promises. 1 Corinthians 1:27-28 But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence. And Romans 9:22-24 What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: and that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles? What if the men of renown, towering as Goliath, nearly 10' tall, existed for the single reason of showing God's might in delivering those He chose, the weak, against the mighty? What if some vessels were fitted for destruction to make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy? 1 Corinthians 4:10 We are fools for Christ's sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak, but ye are strong; ye are honourable, but we are despised. 2 Corinthians 12:9-10 And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong. Isaiah 40:31 But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint. Philippians 4:13 I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. Deuteronomy 31:6 Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee. Isaiah 41:10 Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness. Deuteronomy 20:4 For the LORD your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you. Numbers 13:30 And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it. The faith of Caleb in the face of what seemed overwhelming odds, saved him while the fear of the other spies condemned them. You cannot be delivered by God from tribulation, without tribulation. You cannot make manifest the glory of God without first being weak. Faith is acting on belief rather than doubt, trusting on hope rather than fear. From salvation, knowing first we are sinners deserving death and Hell, but trusting Christ to redeem us, and so calling upon the name of the Lord to save us, to allowing God to deliver us from evil by faith, rather than taking charge ourselves in fear and our own destruction, faith that He strengthens us, that even giants will be destroyed before us, is the means of obtaining the promised hope. Hebrews 11:1 Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. We believe something unseen to be true, and despite doubts we act on that faith by the unseen evidence we trust in our hearts, that we may receive that which we hope for. And God rewards us for it, building our faith. As long as we walk in that Spirit of truth, faith continues to build, and the hopes we have are obtained. None of that can happen without tribulation. Troubles. Seemingly impossible odds. 2 Timothy 3:12-13 Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution. But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived. John 16:33 These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world. 1 Peter 5:10 But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you. James 1:12 Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him Romans 8:18 For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. I dunno about any of you that might be reading this, but I needed that reminder of the blessed hope we have by faith in the promises of God.

O Lord God, thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness, and thy mighty hand: for what God is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy works, and according to thy might? I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon. There are things in this life, blessings from the Lord that we earnestly and humbly seek, the beginnings of which we are shown, and yet will never see the fruit of while we live. But we are comforted by the Spirit, that we are given the discernment and ability to see as God does. The longview, from the top of the mountain, the future spreading out before us waiting to be fulfilled. Raising children, winning souls, serving others. These all bear fruit that we cannot see while we live, because of the nature of time and our physical corruption. But God gives us a glimpse, if we walk in the Spirit, growing in faith, our hope. Jeremiah 17:7 Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, and whose hope the LORD is. 2 Peter 3:8 But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. Romans 10:11 For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. We look forward to a better country, a Heavenly Kingdom. Faith in the hope of our redemption. Amen. The patience we gain as we wait for that blessed day should also satisfy us as we wait for those things in this life we have entrusted to the Lord. As it did Moses. And like Moses, we can look forward to God delivering on promises and blessings in this life. The delayed gratification of our salvation and redemption should lead us to see things as God sees them, and strengthen us. The glimpses from the mountaintop are a blessing from the Lord for faithful service. Psalm 37 Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity. 2 For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb. 3 Trust in the Lord, and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed. 4 Delight thyself also in the Lord: and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart. 5 Commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass. 6 And he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday. 7 Rest in the Lord, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass. 8 Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil. 9 For evildoers shall be cut off: but those that wait upon the Lord, they shall inherit the earth. 10 For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: yea, thou shalt diligently consider his place, and it shall not be. 11 But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace. 12 The wicked plotteth against the just, and gnasheth upon him with his teeth. 13 The Lord shall laugh at him: for he seeth that his day is coming. 14 The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, and to slay such as be of upright conversation. 15 Their sword shall enter into their own heart, and their bows shall be broken. 16 A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked. 17 For the arms of the wicked shall be broken: but the Lord upholdeth the righteous. 18 The Lord knoweth the days of the upright: and their inheritance shall be for ever. 19 They shall not be ashamed in the evil time: and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied. 20 But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the Lord shall be as the fat of lambs: they shall consume; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread. 26 He is ever merciful, and lendeth; and his seed is blessed. 27 Depart from evil, and do good; and dwell for evermore. 28 For the Lord loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints; they are preserved for ever: but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off. 29 The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever. 30 The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom, and his tongue talketh of judgment. 31 The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide. 32 The wicked watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him. 33 The Lord will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when he is judged. 34 Wait on the Lord, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land: when the wicked are cut off, thou shalt see it. 35 I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree. 36 Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found. 37 Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace. 38 But the transgressors shall be destroyed together: the end of the wicked shall be cut off. 39 But the salvation of the righteous is of the Lord: he is their strength in the time of trouble. 40 And the Lord shall help them, and deliver them: he shall deliver them from the wicked, and save them, because they trust in him. Just as the wicked pass away, and their devices come to naught, we can know that there is a reward for the righteous. And it is through the wrath of God against the unrighteous and His mercy towards us who believe, that we can see the future, not as a dream or a vision, but in the hope we have in Christ, established by His word. 2 Corinthians 4:14-18 Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you. For all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God. For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day. For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory; While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal. Romans 4:16-22 Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all, (As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations,) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were. Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations, according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be. And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah's womb: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God; And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform. And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness. All this to say that the faith of Christ that we have in Him to deliver us from judgement, unto eternal life should give us hope also in the things promised in this life. As Abraham believed in the promise of being the father to many nations, and to the Deliverer, things which he would never see while alive in this world. Even as he believed that God would give him a son. And as Abraham believed God, who calleth those things which be not as though they were. And it was imputed to him for righteousness. I dunno how clear I am being. Just saying God is faithful and we should have hope in His promises in this life considering the hope we have in the next. Deuteronomy 1:41-45 Then ye answered and said unto me, We have sinned against the LORD, we will go up and fight, according to all that the LORD our God commanded us. And when ye had girded on every man his weapons of war, ye were ready to go up into the hill. And the LORD said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies. So I spake unto you; and ye would not hear, but rebelled against the commandment of the LORD, and went presumptuously up into the hill. And the Amorites, which dwelt in that mountain, came out against you, and chased you, as bees do, and destroyed you in Seir, even unto Hormah. And ye returned and wept before the LORD; but the LORD would not hearken to your voice, nor give ear unto you. Nearly 40 years later: Numbers 21:21-35 And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying, Let me pass through thy land: we will not turn into the fields, or into the vineyards; we will not drink of the waters of the well: but we will go along by the king's high way, until we be past thy borders. And Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and went out against Israel into the wilderness: and he came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel. And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from Arnon unto Jabbok, even unto the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong. And Israel took all these cities: and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all the villages thereof. When the men of Israel had been fearful, and lacked faith, the Lord told them they would die in the wilderness and not see the promised land. And rather than accept the chastisement and live in hope for their children, they tried to defeat the Amorites themselves, only to be driven out, attacked as if by bees. When their children went to war, 38 years later, on God's schedule, with His blessing, they easily defeated the children of Ammon. It is entirely about faith, patience and meekness, trusting God to deliver. Not forcing the issue. Not taking matters into our own hands. Accepting that the Lord may deny us something now, that we have something better later. Not living in fear but in faith. Having the longview. Seeing things as God does.

There's a lot of doctrine in this, the 4th chapter of Deuteronomy, and a lot to digest. Moses speaking to the assembly of Israel, after successfully destroying two of the Canaanite kings and their kingdoms on the east side of the Jordan, about to enter the promised land. Recounting the events leading up to this moment and retelling the law as given by God to their fathers, 40 years earlier. Starting immediately with the understanding that they have the statutes and judgments of God, given them that they may live. The reminder that the commandments of God are given for our benefit, that it be well with us. That by following His precepts we prolong our lives. The Lord God has blessed us with this knowledge and understanding. Many professing Christians today minimize the civil laws of God, acting as if they were for that time and place, or dismissing them with the carnal ordinances and sacrifices done away with in Christ. But they do so to their own destruction. As Paul writes in Ephesians 6:2-3; Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth. This is the first commandment with promise, but hardly the last. We will see similar promises of God that following His law is to our own benefit throughout Deuteronomy. Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you. Relevant to us today, the diminishing of God's word continues to be Satan's main line of attack. "Yea, hath God said..?" Revelation 22:19 And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book. The recording of the law begins and ends with the same admonition. Yet so many today will cling to false versions of God's word that remove and add to it, seeking to diminish from it, that man might fail to keep God's commands. Moses continues, reminding the people of the destruction of those that chased after the error of Balaam, worshiping idols on the altars of Baalpeor. Moses tells them again that they have the advantage of God's preserved word, His laws, and that it is not only good for them to follow, that they may possess the land by walking in these commandments, but that they are to be an example to other nations who did not receive the oracles of God. That Israel would serve as a light unto the world, bringing them the truth of the Lord, to His glory. Saying Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people. For what nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them, as the Lord our God is in all things that we call upon him for? And what nation is there so great, that hath statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day? This blessing is given with a warning to keep these commands and teach them to their children and grandchildren, that they continue in the land. Gather me the people together, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children. Moses in the Spirit, recounts when they assembled and heard the voice of the Lord God in Horeb, and witnessed His power there in the giving of the law. And he uses this to reinforce the second commandment, as the reminder of the destruction at Baalpeor reminded them of the first. How the people were destroyed for seeking another god to put before them. Now Moses warns against serving idols, graven images, bowing before them. He reminds them that "the Lord spake unto you out of the midst of the fire: ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude; only ye heard a voice." There is no image or idol or any physical representation of God that appeared unto them. Just glory and might and power, and His word, like thunder. Take ye therefore good heed unto yourselves; for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day that the Lord spake unto you in Horeb out of the midst of the fire: Lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image, the similitude of any figure, the likeness of male or female, The likeness of any beast that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged fowl that flieth in the air, The likeness of any thing that creepeth on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the waters beneath the earth. The command against idols and graven images in worship is clear; and God considers is an abomination. He knows the wicked hearts of men would turn to giving His glory to the created rather than to the Creator. The vanity of men over the power of the Living God. He even warns against the worship of nature; lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them. There is no physical or carnal worship in the religion of God. Not of idols made by superstitious man. Not in the physical creation we can observe. Because we must come to Him in faith, for without faith it is impossible to please Him. The Bible says faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen, so by the very definition, a physical representation of the living God or anything in creation be it man or woman or beast or celestial body, is anathema. Idolatry is wicked. There is no excuse given for "veneration," or honoring saints, or to be used as "focus for prayer" or any other thing. Catholicism hates this commandment of God so much that they remove the prohibition against Idolatry from the list of the 10 Commandments, relegating it to a watered down subsection of the 1st, and splitting up the command against covetousness to maintain their deceitful decade. Flee idols. Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of the Lord your God, which he made with you, and make you a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, which the Lord thy God hath forbidden thee. For the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When thou shalt beget children, and children's children, and ye shall have remained long in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, and shall do evil in the sight of the Lord thy God, to provoke him to anger: I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed. And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell. This prohibition against Idolatry was not only to Israel. The nations being driven out before them had fallen to Idolatry, forgotten the Lord God that brought them out of Noah and his sons. They committed abominations. They behaved as Romans 1:18-25 describes; reprobate. For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. Moses tells them that they will suffer the same judgment as a nation if they turn to idols. That they will be destroyed, made desolate, driven from their homeland, scattered. This is God's judgment on all nations that turn from Him to serve idols, and even more so those nations claiming to be called His. This same judgment that destroyed the Canaanites, ultimately destroyed the Israelites, who were rejected of God. Reprobate silver. Given up and given over to their vain imaginations. And this same judgment exists today. Roman Catholicism and Orthodoxy especially, have turned entire nations to idolatry, and in doing so, brought the judgment of God upon them. This is why Europe was overrun with Muslims in the past, and why it is happening again today. And in other Christian nations that have allowed altars to idols to flourish are seeing the same judgment, especially America. More than Sodomites, more than antichrist Jews, people claiming to be Christian yet bowing and praying to idols, worshiping the created more than the Creator, are the reason for our current state. We are overrun with the fruits of a Reprobate mind; sodomy and abominations. We are being ethnically cleansed. Our children barren and filled with all unrighteousness. And it first starts with idolatry. This is the primary lesson of the Reprobate Doctrine. But with this judgement against nations, God in His mercy offers a promise; But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul. When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice; (For the Lord thy God is a merciful God;) he will not forsake thee, neither destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers which he sware unto them. This is repeatedly offered throughout scripture, a way to turn back the judgment against nations, to get right with the Lord. 2 Chronicles 7:14 If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. This extended not just to the Israelites, but was given even to the Gentiles of Nineveh; Jonah 3:3-10 So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of the Lord. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey. And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown. So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes. And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands. Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not? And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not. God judges nations on this earth, just as He judges individuals in Heaven. And if we, like so many times in the history of the judges and kings recounted in scripture, destroy the altars and high places, smash the idols, remove the sodomites from our land, and turn from those evil ways towards the Living God, the Lord will repent of the evil He would do, and heal our land. Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that the Lord he is God in heaven above, and upon the earth beneath: there is none else. Thou shalt keep therefore his statutes, and his commandments, which I command thee this day, that it may go well with thee, and with thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days upon the earth, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, for ever. Amen The remaining parts of the chapter are fairly straightforward establishing sanctuary cities on the east side of the Jordan in the lands given to the Reubenites, Gadites and Manasseh, which decided they'd be happy with the fertile plains for their cattle, just short of the promised land. These cities established for those that accidentally kill someone else, that they could flee to and be given refuge, as dictated in Leviticus. There are a few more chapters before we get into the meat of the retelling of the law. As we go through however, Note that there is a consistent voice in scripture. Whether it is Moses, the prophets, the apostles... Christ Himself, all of it has a consistent and clear voice. Reading Deuteronomy 4 and then going to read Galatians for this study, I was struck so hard by how consistent the word of God is. All given by the same Spirit. Not a collection of the works of men, but the word of an eternal and living God.

Moses continues the second telling of the law, and so Deuteronomy 5 contains a second recitation of the 10 Commandments, reminding the people of the covenant made with them at Mt Horeb, also known as Sinai. This covenant came from the living God directly to the people, speaking to them from a fire that covered the mountain with His glory, saying: I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage. Thou shalt have none other gods before me. This first command holds true to us today, having been delivered out of bondage by the grace of God through faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. Set at liberty from the bondage of the law, and being servants to sin. Thou shalt not make thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the waters beneath the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself unto them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me... There is no amount of cope and vain imagining that can excuse the use of idols and icons in the false churches of the Roman cult. None. The second commandment of God couldn't be clearer. "We don't worship them!" Bowing before, kneeling, praying to and serving these idols, is worship. Lighting candles, incense, decking them with flowers and crowns, holding vigils to them and feasts...these are all blasphemy. And God warns that he will visit evil on the people who do this to the 4th generation, because this inequity comes from hatred of God. But we who love Him and keep these commands are blessed by His mercy. Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain. Profaning His holy name, using it as a curse or to make a false vow, all take His name in vain. But worse are those who claim to be from God, using the name of the Lord to bring a false gospel or to justify evil. Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee. Six days thou shalt labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, nor thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thine ox, nor thine ass, nor any of thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates; that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thou. The Sabbath has always been a picture of Christ, and the rest we have in Jesus. And the prohibition against working on that day was to illustrate that we contribute nothing to our salvation except to honor His sacrifice by trusting on Him to justify us before God. It is a gift of God, not of works, least any man should boast. Again, there are no equivocations or rationalizations that can possibly justify those who add their works to God's plan of salvation, given us in Christ. They damn themselves just as assuredly as the man who gathered wood in the wilderness on the Sabbath. Salvation by grace through faith without works has been the Gospel from the beginning. And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the Lord thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day. The spiritual application of this understanding, that Jesus is the Sabbath, that our works contribute nothing to our salvation should be coupled with remembering that we were servants to sin. That we were in bondage in Egypt. That before God brought us out from the ministry of death and into eternal life by His mighty hand, we were as slaves, just as the Hebrews were. And the extension of the Sabbath to those who are our sons and daughters, our employees, and even to strangers, is to show the same mercy given us who were once servants, that they may come to know the truth in Christ. Never forget that we were servants in Egypt, and only are free by the grace of the Lord. Have charitable love for the unsaved that they may be lifted out of bondage as well. Honour thy father and thy mother, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee; that thy days may be prolonged, and that it may go well with thee, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee. Again, as Paul later writes, the first commandment with promise, that by honoring our parents we honor Him. And our days will be prolonged in this life. It is a blessing to serve them as children, respect them as adults, and care for them in their old age. Even if they aren't saved. Even if they aren't the best. Because you are serving God, not them. And the blessings are His, not theirs. Thou shalt not kill. Neither shalt thou commit adultery. Neither shalt thou steal. Neither shalt thou bear false witness against thy neighbour. Neither shalt thou desire thy neighbour's wife, neither shalt thou covet thy neighbour's house, his field, or his manservant, or his maidservant, his ox, or his ass, or any thing that is thy neighbour's The 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th commandments as God gave them, are simple to understand, and as eternally relevant as the first five. There are some professing Christians today who claim the civil laws of God and His commandments given Moses, are no longer in force. They point to the ceremonial laws and carnal ordinances of the Levitical priesthood that were done away with in Christ, and apply it to things like sodomy and adultery. Saying that these things are allowed in the New Testament. That the death penalty has been done away with. That God now loves abominations. "If the dietary laws aren't in effect, if you can eat pork and shrimp, then there's nothing wrong with being a Sodomite!" Of course, these same people would not claim that murder, cheating on a spouse, stealing, perjuring or coveting the things of others are now ok. They simply want to call evil good and good evil. They want to pick and choose, and not knowing scripture or hoping those they seek to mislead don't, they make these ridiculous claims. But we know better. Ye shall observe to do therefore as the Lord your God hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left. Ye shall walk in all the ways which the Lord your God hath commanded you, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days in the land which ye shall possess.

This is the purpose of the law, and those that claim to be Christ's and yet eschew Biblical separation, who claim their liberty means they no longer need the law, or that the law of for the OT, or who hold to vain tradition and the commandments of men, and yet do not value God's word, and despise His commands, or cry "LEGALIST!" do not understand it or value it. They do not fear God or trust in Him when He promises us that His ways are just and good, and that we who hold to them will prosper and a nation that seeks His precepts will prosper. Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us. But in Christ, we establish the law. 1 Corinthians 6:12-20 All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any. Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats: but God shall destroy both it and them. Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body. And God hath both raised up the Lord, and will also raise up us by his own power. Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ? shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid. What? know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh. But he that is joined unto the Lord is one spirit. Flee fornication. Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body. What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's The most important aspect of the knowledge and keeping of God's law is separation unto the gospel. To be blameless and justified before men, that by our conversation, our behavior, they may be drawn to the light of the Lord, magnified in our obedience, as imperfect as it might be. And so; 2 Timothy 2:15 Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.

Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up. This reminder, that we are to teach our children diligently of the law of God, is a commandment. We are to learn His law, and practice it to prolong our days, that it be well with us. That we be blameless and with meekness and longsuffering, we may win others to the Lord, but most importantly that we may instruct our children in His ways, that they carry on this legacy. Proverbs 22:6 Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it. Ephesians 6:4 And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. This is a solemn responsibility, and one we often neglect. Even godly Christian parents can become lax in their duty to diligently instruct their children, believing that sharing the gospel with them and bringing them to church is sufficient. Maybe by not living the example, and bringing them to wrath. Or by not disciplining them when they need it. Proverbs 23:13-14 Withhold not correction from the child: For if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.Thou shalt beat him with the rod, And shalt deliver his soul from hell. Proverbs 22:15 Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; But the rod of correction shall drive it far from him. This principle is important, because the rod of correction teaches them that chastisement comes from love, and they get a picture of God the Father through you. Hebrews 12:6-8 For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons. As important as this is, demonstrating to them the precepts of God's word, and serving as an example of that grace and mercy He showed us, while we were yet sinners, is even more important. And when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments, which the Lord our God hath commanded you? Then thou shalt say unto thy son, We were Pharaoh's bondmen in Egypt; and the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand. Remember we were servants in Egypt. We were bondsmen to the law, slaves to sin. But by His mighty hand, God lifted us up and freed us by His Son. We remember this and remind our children, least we forget, and our sons turn to other gods and forsake the law. And the Lord commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as it is at this day. We should also remember that obedience to the civil laws of God are for our benefit. For our good always. That it be well with us. That it prolongs our days and that we are preserved alive. Not for salvation. Not for our own righteousness. The law is a schoolmaster, teaching us our need for salvation in Christ. Galatians 3:24-27 Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Because; It shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us. If we observed to do all these commandments, it would be our righteousness. We would have to glory. Romans 4:1-12 What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, And whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also: and the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised. But knowing that it is impossible in our flesh to observe all these things, we understand that it is God's glory that His mercy is revealed. James 2:10 For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all. Romans 3:10-12 As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one. As Paul writes a few verses later, There is no fear of God before their eyes. But as Moses writes here in Deuteronomy 6, under the same Spirit as Paul, we are to learn the law of God and keep it in our hearts, in our minds, That thou mightest fear the Lord thy God. And in that fear, that respect and love of the Lord, we may know we have His mercy towards us: Romans 3:23-26 For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. The Lord also reminds the Israelites that they are being given a gift that they did not work for. Cities they did not build. Wells they did not dig. Vineyards they did not plant. And it shall be, when the Lord thy God shall have brought thee into the land which he sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give thee great and goodly cities, which thou buildedst not, And houses full of all good things, which thou filledst not, and wells digged, which thou diggedst not, vineyards and olive trees, which thou plantedst not; when thou shalt have eaten and be full; Then beware lest thou forget the Lord, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage. This pertains to us, and the promise made to Abraham that was fulfilled in Christ Jesus. That it is to an inheritance uncorruptible, a heavenly Kingdom that contains many mansions. A land flowing with living waters and fruit of the tree of life. We would do well to remember this, with humility and fear of the Lord. That we were bondmen, set free. That He delivered us and gave us an inheritance in a land we buildest not. Matthew 5:17-20 Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled. Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven. For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven. Psalm 19:7-11 The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul: The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple. The statutes of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart: The commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes. The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring for ever: The judgments of the LORD are true and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: Sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb. Moreover by them is thy servant warned: And in keeping of them there is great reward. Psalm 119:137-160 Righteous art thou, O LORD, And upright are thy judgments. Thy testimonies that thou hast commanded are righteous and very faithful. My zeal hath consumed me, Because mine enemies have forgotten thy words. Thy word is very pure: Therefore thy servant loveth it. I am small and despised: Yet do not I forget thy precepts. Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, And thy law is the truth. Trouble and anguish have taken hold on me: Yet thy commandments are my delights. The righteousness of thy testimonies is everlasting: Give me understanding, and I shall live. I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O LORD: I will keep thy statutes. I cried unto thee; save me, and I shall keep thy testimonies. I prevented the dawning of the morning, and cried: I hoped in thy word. Mine eyes prevent the night watches, That I might meditate in thy word. Hear my voice according unto thy lovingkindness: O LORD, quicken me according to thy judgment. They draw nigh that follow after mischief: They are far from thy law. Thou art near, O LORD; And all thy commandments are truth. Concerning thy testimonies, I have known of old That thou hast founded them for ever. Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: For I do not forget thy law. Plead my cause, and deliver me: Quicken me according to thy word. Salvation is far from the wicked: For they seek not thy statutes. Great are thy tender mercies, O LORD: Quicken me according to thy judgments. Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; Yet do I not decline from thy testimonies. I beheld the transgressors, and was grieved; Because they kept not thy word. Consider how I love thy precepts: Quicken me, O LORD, according to thy lovingkindness. Thy word is true from the beginning: And every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever. Galatians 3:24-27 Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Romans 3:30-31 Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith. Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law. 1 John 3:4-6 Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law. And ye know that he was manifested to take away our sins; and in him is no sin. Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not: whosoever sinneth hath not seen him, neither known him. 1 Timothy 1:8-11 But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, for whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; according to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.

The Lord is instructing the Israelites before their entry into the promised land, through the Spirit-filled preaching of Moses. Commanding that they destroy the 7 wicked nations of Canaan utterly, despite their being mightier and larger, but by His power, God promises they would overcome. He warns against intermarrying with them. That by taking the daughters of the heathen, it would be their undoing as they'd lead their sons away from serving the living God. The same prohibition against being unequally yoked that Christians should honor, and for the same reason. He commands them to tear down their altars and destroy their idols. Cut down their groves and burn their graven images with fire. God's love is upon them, being the weakest that in their triumph, He would receive the glory and the people would know He is the Lord God. Just as they spoiled Egypt because of His mighty hand, they will make desolate the lands they are to inhabit. He warns continuously through this of their failure to heed His commands and to destroy their idols and to not take them as wives, that if they become like the heathen, He will visit them with sudden destruction. Just as God repays those who hate Him; And repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them: he will not be slack to him that hateth him, he will repay him to his face. Those who God destroys know that the vengeance is His. Even those that deny Him. Even reprobates who seek not to retain God in their knowledge. In the end they all know, because His wrath reveals Him to them. They know the cause of their destruction is a just and holy God. The Lord gives the promises and blessings that will follow them as a people if they harken to His word. That they will be fruitful, their land giving increase, their flocks growing, blessed of all people. That there would be none barren in the land. Declining birthrates, to extinction level, is a curse of God on the ungodly. Nations in decline die off. Or are destroyed as the Canaanites were. God promises to take away sicknesses, and lay them on their enemies. And encourages them in their hope for victory, knowing the awesome power He had already displayed for them, from Egypt to this day.

We are here in Deuteronomy 8, and we again see that God is again repeating the same themes regarding His commandments and statutes and judgments. Seeking to get His word to be plainly understood by a vain and stiff-necked people, be they Israelites or we today. That the purpose of His law is that it be good with us, that we may live and multiply and thrive in the boundaries and habitations He has set for our people. That when we receive the blessings that come, we remember it is from the Lord. That while we were weak, He brought us out of captivity. Freeing us from bondage in Egypt, the chains of sin. Testing us and proving us through the wilderness, that we may be humbled. To hunger. To thirst. So that He may give us the bread of life. That we may drink of the living waters. That we may know that we do not live by bread alone but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord. He has provided for us in tribulations, that we may know we have eternal life in a better country. In a land promised us in Christ. An everlasting Kingdom. By keeping His statutes, we are reminded of the grace and longsuffering of God towards us, that it be well with us. That we live long on the earth, and be blessed. That we never forget what He has done for us. That we don't glory in ourselves, and become unthankful. That we don't seek after other gods or become vain in our imaginations. Over and over He has repeated this to the children of Israel, that we may have understanding now. And so it is written; And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Lord doth man live. As it is written; Thou shalt also consider in thine heart, that, as a man chasteneth his son, so the Lord thy God chasteneth thee. As it is written; Where there was no water; who brought thee forth water out of the rock of flint...Who fed thee in the wilderness with manna, which thy fathers knew not I love New Testament references to Old Testament scripture, showing us the spiritual things of God. For the stubbornly Dispensational, we have yet another condition placed in what they claim is an unconditional promise to the tribes of Israel; And it shall be, if thou do at all forget the Lord thy God, and walk after other gods, and serve them, and worship them, I testify against you this day that ye shall surely perish. As the nations which the Lord destroyeth before your face, so shall ye perish; because ye would not be obedient unto the voice of the Lord your God. The unbelieving Jews of the 1st century would not be obedient unto the voice of the Lord. They surely perished. Destroyed before the face of God. This is the promise without repentance that the Lord made. This is the covenant made with the fathers in the wilderness, where their clothes did not wax old, lo those forty years. Hebrews 8:7-13 For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people: And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest. For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more. In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.

Romans 5 Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.
