God is very clear that He will exact the price for your vow. So don't make one you cannot keep. There is no sin in refusing to vow in His name. And as Christ tells us, being honest in all your dealings is a much better policy. Let your yea be yea and your no, no. When thou comest into thy neighbour's vineyard, then thou mayest eat grapes thy fill at thine own pleasure; but thou shalt not put any in thy vessel. When thou comest into the standing corn of thy neighbour, then thou mayest pluck the ears with thine hand; but thou shalt not move a sickle unto thy neighbour's standing corn. Fairly straightforward. Don't gather that which you have not planted. But, as neighbors we are to allow the gleaning, even of passersby. God gives the increase, it is a blessing to share. Just don't take advantage.

We are here in Deuteronomy 24, which opens with mention of the divorce allowed by Moses due to the hardness of the hearts of the children of Israel; Matthew 19:8 He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so. It comes up in the context of remarrying the ex after she had remarried, whether her second marriage ends in divorce or death. The Lord says it's an abomination that causes the land to sin, a cause of the end of a nation in judgment. There is a spiritual application in that God, having put away the former betrothed for fornication, that is Israel after the flesh, has instead been promised to the faithful in Christ, in the law of grace. To turn back to the beggarly elements of the Old Testament and the law, which is the ministry of death, would be an abomination. When a man is married, he is free from service to war for one year. It is fitting and right. Unconditional drafts were and have been the norm. But God's law is perfect and just. Taking a pledge is the giving of something as collateral towards a loan or vow, and the taking of a man's millstone, that they cannot grind flour is taking his life. It is a prohibition against taking advantage of the person by taking their means to live. The Spirit of this law could apply to other items, like their tools for their trade. Pawn brokers, a very Jewish profession, is well known for violating this precept and others in this chapter. Next is the death penalty for kidnapping and slavery among the brethren. In a just society, any man that kidnaps another person is capable of anything. It is wicked. They deserve capital punishment. God again commands to follow the rules laid out in Leviticus 14:1-9, referring to the case of Miriam as an example. If you let a neighbor borrow something, you aren't supposed to go into their home to retrieve it. Allow them to return it. The implications of barging back into their home to get whatever it may be shows an insult to the person's character, and undoes the kindness. And if someone poor offers you a pledge and it needs to be repaid them. Don't wait a day, but rather return it that they may be relieved not worrying about if they're getting it back. Especially as they are poor and have little and can't afford it. It's just common courtesy and love for another. Don't oppress your servants, regardless of who they are. God is not a respecter of persons and neither should we be, and we should remember we were bondsmen in Egypt. If you hire someone, pay them in the manner agreed upon. Do not make them wait for their wage. It is evil. Fathers and children should not be put to death for the others crime, only their own sin. Don't take a pledge from the needy, take advantage of the stranger, or foreigner, or the orphan or the widow. Give them their need, or righteous judgment, to the best of your ability without any expectation of repayment. Love them because you were once a bondman in Egypt, and God has redeemed us. Have the same mercy. Another reminder to allow gleaning of your crops after harvest. Not to go back over and over to get every last morsel. Leave what was missed for the poor. That they may work that they may eat. Thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt: therefore I command thee to do this thing. This humility and loving of your neighbor and even the stranger, the poor and the fatherless and the widow, should come from the knowledge that but for the grace of God we should be in their position.

Judge rightly. If the judgment is that a man be beaten for his transgressions, God commands not to give more than 40 lashes, least it be cruel, and the punishment meted out in the presence of the judge. In 2 Corinthians 14:23-24, Paul is preaching against false prophets and those slandering him as one, he begins to remind the Corinthians of what he had paid for the gospel; Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft. Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one. Forty stripes save one, 39 lashes counted by measure that they not exceed 40. Careful to the letter of the law, but not the spirit because they did not judge rightly. Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he tredeth out the corn. Another verse, used by Paul to justify the support of those ministering the Gospel and pastoring churches, again to the church in Corinth; 1 Corinthians 9:8-14 Say I these things as a man? or saith not the law the same also? For it is written in the law of Moses, Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn. Doth God take care for oxen? Or saith he it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope; and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope. If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great thing if we shall reap your carnal things? If others be partakers of this power over you, are not we rather? Nevertheless we have not used this power; but suffer all things, lest we should hinder the gospel of Christ. Do ye not know that they which minister about holy things live of the things of the temple? and they which wait at the altar are partakers with the altar? Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel. Next, we see again the law that if a brother dies without siring a child, their brother is to take her as a wife and impregnate her that the name of his brother not be lost in Israel. That he have a first born to carry on the inheritance. Here, we see what's to happen if the living brother refuses, he is subject to humiliation by the widow who spits in his face and loose his shoe from his foot. Becoming The house of him that hath his shoe loosed, known throughout Israel for his dereliction. It reminds me of John the Baptist, who would later say of Jesus; John 1:27 He it is, who coming after me is preferred before me, whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose. Customs of servants versus the humiliation of the unfaithful brother, so not the same obviously. But it's a strange custom and meaning. Next we see that if a woman grab a man by the stones in a fight, she's gonna have to lose that hand. No pity or mercy. Women should keep themselves from a fight between men, even if her husband is being beaten.

Deuteronomy 26 contains the ordinances of the year of tithing, in the place God shall choose to place His name, where the children of Israel are to bring their first fruits in an offer before the priest, thanking God in remembrance for His taking the people out of bondage in Egypt, and with a high hand, in strength and power, brought them to the land flowing with milk and honey. The first fruits being His, and blessed and given to share with the people, especially the poor, the stranger sojourning in the land, the widow and the fatherless. And to vow to keep His commandments and praise and honor His name, as His peculiar people. The picture of the spiritual things to come, for all saved believers in the kingdom of Heaven. Picturing the practice of our religion, the expression of our faith here on Earth. And understanding the blessings He has given us that we are to share with the world. The prayer given by the Lord in this chapter contains reminders that the people that Jacob, who is Israel, are of the Syrians. (his mother Rebecca, an Aramean, which is Syria. Aramaic language Jesus and the apostles spoke coming from this area and people) Jacob who fled Canaan during the famine to Egypt, and there the people grew into a great nation of the 12 tribes, and fell into bondage. A reminder of our own beginnings, as a disparate people, brought into the world and to sin and bondage of the law. Made into the Israel of God by faith, set free by His render mercies. Not of ourselves, but a gift of God. We who called out His name for salvation and were brought out from captivity by His mighty hand. Amen. To Him we owe everything. And that it be well with us, we should continue in His commandments with our whole heart and soul. Amen
Let all God's children say "Amen!" Amen

Deuteronomy 28:1-14 details the blessings of a people who call themselves by the name of the Lord and who keep His commandments. A nation blessed with the abundance and wealth provided by God. This is where most Dispensationalists end their reading of the chapter. They say this is the promise to the Jews today. That God never set conditions on His covenant with them through Moses. Let's see about that. But in every temptation, the Lord is merciful to provide a way out. He tells us precisely what must happen to reverse these curses and restore the blessings again. 2 Chronicles 7:14 If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. This is the way we are given. It still holds true today. It doesn't fall on the wicked to repent of their sins, but for Christians to return to the fundamentals. To humble ourselves, hold to the old paths, the old time religion of our fathers. To separate ourselves from the world, while living in the world as a beacon, shining forth. Bringing others to Christ that they may be healed and in doing so, heal the land.

Even all nations shall say, Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land? what meaneth the heat of this great anger? This warning, given at the establishment of the covenant at Moab, unto the children of Israel as they enter the promised land, shows the conditional nature of the Law by Moses, which are not the same as the promises made to Abraham, Jacob and David. As we read in Hebrews 8, the law of Moses was for until the time of reformation in Christ. Fulfilled in Jesus with the blood of a better testament. Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens; A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man. For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer. For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount. But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. And so the destruction of Israel was just and with the desolation of Judah God's righteousness revealed. Just as He said to them through Moses.

Romans 10:6-11 But the righteousness which is of faith speaketh on this wise, Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:) or, Who shall descend into the deep? (that is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.) But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; that if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. Following the blessings promised and the cursings threatened by the Lord against the people of Israel in the Mosaic covenant, God makes clear it is their choice. A free will gesture, to either choose life or choose death. And because of the fault of the people, the law became a ministration of death. He says to them that they have the oracles of God before them. They don't need someone to go up into Heaven and return with them, they are right there. They do not need someone to go over the sea, or descend to its depths as Paul rephrases it, the Law is before them. Their love of God and faith of the heart determines if they are willing to seek life or choose death. The word is very nigh unto them, even in their mouth. Even in their hearts. That the righteousness of the law may prove the need for the righteousness of faith and the grace and mercy of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth. For Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them. Corinthians 3:7-18 But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away: how shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious? For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory. For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth. For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious. Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech: and not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished: but their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ. But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart. Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away. Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord. For the Dispensationalists, the Lord who cannot lie and Who keeps His promises forever, as they are fond to remind us, had this to say; But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. "Aha, but if they turn again to the Lord they shall be graft in!" Yes. Individual jews who choose life, seek the Lord and find Him in Christ will be forgiven and be made heirs to the promise. But that choice is theirs to make, as individuals, choosing between death and life in Christ Jesus. Calvinists and Zionists share the same twisted theology; that God will force individuals to believe, just as He keeps them from obedience to the Gospel. But here in Deuteronomy 30 (and throughout scripture) God makes it clear that we all have a choice. That it isn't by who we are, but what our heart believes. That it is by choosing to love the Lord, and in doing so, living by faith. Choose life. I wanted to note that the order of things is to love God and then we keep his commandments, that it be well with us and that we live long and prosper, so to speak. But it makes people then go "see? You have to keep the law too!" or "See? If you believe you will follow the law automatically!" But that's not what it says, especially in the NT. Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord. We have the Spirit of the Lord so we are at liberty. We aren't judged by the law. But even so, in liberty, and beholding the glory of God towards us, by walking in that Spirit, we see our own selves transformed by His glory. We are changed by it if we choose to be. And that change is in ourselves, observed by us in our own spiritual reflection, from glory to glory. We feel God working in us, and as we feel it, His Spirit works in us even more. People overcomplicate these things and want to make hard and fast rules of how this works and how it can be observed in others, usually for the express purpose of lording over those who we feel aren't walking the Christian walk the way we do, being holier than thou. Hypocrites.

The life of Moses, to whom the law was given, nears its end, and Joshua, a picture of Christ, is given power to lead the children of Israel into the promised land. Like John, a voice crying out in the wilderness, Moses cleared the way, making the paths straight for the one who would come to bring deliverance. The book of the law is written, and placed in the Ark that is in the heart of the camp. Done to bear witness of the sins and iniquity of the people. Like the law written in the hearts of man, a conscience, pricked of the Spirit to lay bare our transgressions. To let us know when we have gone astray. As a testimony of the Lord against them who were given the oracles of God. To remind them of their need for His salvation. An ordinance is given, that in the jubilee year, at the fall feast of Tabernacles, the feast of tents, the people shall gather and hear the reading of the Law. The story of God and His people. His Commandments and His love for them that believe on His name. How he rescued them from bondage and delivered on the promises He made. Every 7 years the people will be reminded. And yet He knows their hearts. And so the Lord teaches Moses a new song. One to teach the children of Israel that they may know that God knows, they will break the covenant. This song and its need are all the evidence we need to understand that the fault of the covenant made in the wilderness was always the people. The law itself pure and perfect. The people forsake the God who delivered them, and chase after other gods. God promises to forsake them in turn, for all the evils that they wrought. Moses, delivering this all to the people before the congregation, reiterates his own knowledge that they will turn aside. That they will utterly corrupt themselves. Once again, proving dispensationalism to be unbiblical heresy.

The Song of Moses is a prophecy of Christ and the end times. The Rock of our salvation. Who hath purchased us, bought with a price. Publishing the name of the Lord, Jesus. God will move the children of Jacob to jealousy with those who are not a people. Provoking them to anger with a foolish nation. (For the preaching of the cross is foolishness to them) But vengeance is His. The Lord will judge His people. Their calamity will come with haste. The days of Vengeance. Rendering vengeance for the blood of His servants, those martyred in His name. Utterly destroying them with fire. Amen

Similar to the blessings of his sons by Jacob in Genesis 49 Deuteronomy 33 contains both blessings for the tribes of Israel, and end times Bible prophecy. The return of Christ and His saints, as Enoch the 7th from Adam prophesied; Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, Moses does as well. The blessings for each son and each tribe contain a mix of short term and long term prophecy. Some of which is fulfilled in the taking of Canaan, some in the kingdom periods, and some to come during the millennium, IMO. Where the saints rule and reign with Christ, including OT saints of the 12 tribes, in the resurrection. But we see through a glass darkly. It's a study for another day. For now it is sufficient to see that we are the Israel of God. O people saved by the Lord, the shield of thy help, and who is the sword of thy excellency! Amen! People who don't believe they have eternal security in Christ are not saved, because they do not believe the record. That all who believe have eternal life. John 3:15-17 that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

Even so, come, Lord Jesus. There's a certain symmetry to reading the last of Deuteronomy and the book of the Revelation of Christ Jesus. The entrance into the promised land. That far off country we look forward to as believers, even here in the wilderness. I am blessed to have them coincide over the past few days, knowing the Song of Moses will be sung by the choir of Heaven. Knowing God is true, and delivers all who trust in Him. I thank God for all who came along on this study with me. It has been a blessing for me, and I pray the Spirit spoke to others as we went. Even so, come Lord Jesus.

Beginning the Book of Joshua, the narrative of the capture of Canaan by the Israelites, the land given them by God for their rest, led by a deliverer named Joshua, a Hebrew variation of the name Jesus. A picture of the Christ to come. We read the Lord speaking to Joshua as He had Moses, and reaffirming the promises made in His word, upon which Joshua trusted. By faith the people would possess the land for an inheritance, which God had sworn unto their fathers. The Lord's promise is the same to those of us who believe; I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee. The captains of the tribes give their loyalty to Joshua, to lead them in Moses' place. And God reminds Joshua of the promise made in the covenant with Moses, that if they obey His commandments, and follow His law, turning neither to the right nor the left, that they shall prosper. That by meditating day and night upon His word, and letting His law depart not from their mouth, they will have good success. This promise is to us as well. That if we love His word and keep it in our hearts, His law upon our lips, meditating on it day and night, we will prosper and have success in this life. Like the Israelites, we are saved by faith, delivered by His mighty hand into the promised land, but we are also blessed in this world by keeping His commandments. That it be well with us. This is the hope of God, the good news of His Gospel. The same faith that saves us today, and the same obedience that blessed those who keep His law. So be not afraid. Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest. Amen

And so we are here in Joshua chapter 2, and the newly anointed leader of the Hebrews is about to lead the people over the Jordan and into the promised land. His first act is to send 2 spies to spy out the walled city of Jericho. This is similar to an earlier appearance of Joshua, in Numbers 13, where Moses sent 12 spies into the land, and 10 spies were bad and 2 were good. Joshua and Caleb were the good men, who had faith in God to deliver the land to them. The 10 cast doubt and fear. Not wishing a repeat, apparently, Joshua sends only 2, and these men make their way into Jericho by way of the home of the harlot, Rahab. There she lodges them and hides the spies when the king of Jericho sends out men to find them. The harlot hides the men upon her roof and sends the kings men on a fruitless search back towards Jordan. She tells the Hebrew spies that she has done this because the whole land knows that the Lord God is with them, and are friegtened of them, considering the miracles of the Red Sea and the defeat of the other Canaanite kings. She has faith that the same Lord God will bring them victory in Jericho. The spies thank her, and she asks that they swear her family will be protected in their eventual siege of the city. The spies grant her an oath. That if she places the scarlet thread she had let them down on in her window, that all within her household will be saved. Her faith in God to deliver the Israelites, and her faith in the promise of the spies, will lead to her salvation, as we will see in a few chapters. And the same faith serves as a picture of Christ. The scarlet thread, like the blood on the door frames on the first Passover. The same scarlet thread of the blood of Christ that runs throughout the Bible. And Rahab is part of that bloodline of Christ Jesus, as we see during the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew; Matthew 1:5-6 And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse; And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias The Greek spelling of 'Rachab,' is Rahab. She birthed Boaz of Judah, who eventually begets David, in the human lineage of Christ. A scarlet thread. And she is saved by her faith, we know. Despite being a harlot. Despite her sinful life. She is redeemed, and honored with a mention in the Hall of Faith found in Hebrews 11, in the company of great Old Testament believers; Hebrews 11:31 By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace. She is also used by James, alongside Abraham, in his examples of those whose actions demonstrated to others the faith she had in her heart; James 2:25 Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way? Given as an example of faith by God, to show us that He may use anyone for His purpose, and redeem anyone who holds the faith. Notice the spies, upon hearing her declaration of faith in the Lord, never told her to repent of harlotry. Never placed a condition of her being contrite and sorry for her sin before agreeing to save her from the sword. Just her trust in that scarlet thread, that by the word of God she and her family would be delivered. Repenters and other works-based false prophets would judge her in unrighteousness, despite her profession of faith. And while she clearly cleaned up her life, was married and produced godly children, as part of the human lineage of Jesus, it was her faith that saved her. Amen

Here in Joshua 3, we see Joshua commanding the priests and people, with God's word. The Lord tells him, This day will I begin to magnify thee in the sight of Israel, that they may know that, as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee. Now, prior to these events, Joshua was a man of renown among the children of Israel. Moses chose him to lead the fighting men of Israel for their first battle after the exodus from Egypt, against the Amalekites in Rephidim. Joshua went with Moses to the Mount where Moses received the 10 commandments from God, and was with him when they returned to the reveling of the golden calf. And of course Joshua was one of the 12 spies sent to scout Canaan. He had a name for himself. He secured the Tabernacle of meeting, during Moses speaking with God; Exodus 33:11 And the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle. All this, and anointed by Moses upon his death to lead them, but it was this day that the Lord began to magnify him before the children of Israel. For it was this day that, by the command of God, the people crossed the Jordan as the Lord parted the waters, holding back the flow of the river in the late rains of the harvest, at its peak levels. Held back in a heap of water while the Levites with the Ark stood on dry ground and the people passed over, clean. It was a miracle of God, whose word Joshua carried to the people, and his obedience and faith that magnified him before the people. Not his own work. Not his previous deeds. Not his station. But his faith and obedience to the living God.

Psalm 1:1-3 Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. As a picture of Jesus, and as an example of the way we are to live in faith, Joshua shows obedience to God, delighting in His word, prospering by His judgments. Joshua is magnified and respected, feared by the children of Israel as they feared Moses, knowing the Lord was with him. Joshua hears the word, obeys it, and not only is a hearer and doer, but he tells others what God says, repeating almost verbatim the instructions for the memorial of the 12 stones at Gilgal, marking their passage over the Jordan. And the people harken to those words and obey. And they prosper. Entering the promised land at last, with an army of men assembling on the plains of Jericho, knowing the Lord is with them.

The children of Israel have entered the promised land, by the mighty hand of God. And the kings of Canaan are in terror of Him. The parting of the Jordan signifying that the Lord was with them. And God tells Joshua to prepare knives for the circumcision of the men of the camp, who were raised in the wilderness and had not been circumcised during that time. Notice they were given entry to the promised land by faith, without circumcision. It was only after, in Gilgal that the Lord commanded it. And after the men died in the wilderness because of unbelief. And as they ate the Passover in Gilgal, the manna stopped falling from Heaven. The corn of the land was theirs. The land flowing with milk and honey. Just as God had promised. Now a really interesting part of the book of Joshua begins, the appearance of Jesus before him. The captain of the Lord's hosts. The place He appears, holy ground as was the burning bush for Moses, and the same command given, for Joshua to remove his shoes in the presence of God. His presence signifying that the Lord and His armies were with Israel, as the siege of Jericho begins.

The Lord, the captain of the Hosts, Jesus Christ Himself IMO, appeared before Joshua and He commanded the new leader of Israel in the manner that God would deliver the city of Jericho to them. And Joshua, carefully explained the plan to the people, and they believed, following all the Lord's words given to Joshua. Circling the city with the Ark. Blowing the horns. Giving a shout on the 7th time on the 7th day. And a miracle occurred, the walls came tumbling down. Joshua not only conveyed the word of God, but cautioned the people to be silent, least they feel the need to shout at another time, and in doing so disobey the word of God. He sought to obey with such care, because he didn't want even the appearance of a lack of faith in the plan or disobedience to the command. The lesson of obedience to the word of God, even when it seems foolish or silly to us, is one we must take to heart as Christians. And while God hates it when we add our own works or deeds to His plan for us, He appreciates diligence in our honoring His command. To take the spirit of His word and apply it to how we live our Christian life. This is a key point of separation. Taking not just the letter of the commandments and statutes God has provided us, but honoring the Spirit of it and not leaving ourselves open to temptation. Some professing Christians call this "legalism." But Joshua wasn't being legalistic in his telling the people to remain silent in their performance of God's command until the final day and appointed time. He was safeguarding them against temptation. 1 Corinthians 6:12-20 All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any. Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats: but God shall destroy both it and them. Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body. And God hath both raised up the Lord, and will also raise up us by his own power. Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ? shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid. What? know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh. But he that is joined unto the Lord is one spirit. Flee fornication. Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body. What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's. We are at liberty in Christ. God will not impute sin against our ledgers in His judgment. We are covered by the imputed righteousness of Jesus. But not all things edify. Not all things are convenient. Not all things bring a good report of the gospel to those outside the faith. Not all things serve to keep us from backsliding into sin. So Christians who hold that commandments like sobriety, abstaining from strong drink and drugs, that it doesn't just apply to wine. Dressing modestly or in gender appropriate clothing means women wear dresses that cover their thigh. Men should have short hair. These are examples of being extra careful in applying the spirit of the commandments of God. And it is for our own edifying and to not give a bad report of the faith. To be a good witness. To avoid our own temptation. Separation should be in a like manner to Joshua's command to remain silent until called upon to shout. Talmudic Jews today, like the Pharisees, seek loopholes and workarounds, trying to skirt the letter of the law by ignoring the spirit of them. Some Christians do the same to their own destruction. When in doubt, honor the command in a way that keeps the spirit of what God wills for us. The destruction of Jericho is also a picture of the end times, the 7 trumpets and the walls breaking down before the armies of God, the unbelieving perishing and the believers, like Rahab and her household, being spirited away and protected from the wrath by their faith. The scarlet thread of the blood of Christ, echoing back to the valley of Jericho like the trumpets and the shout that signals Christ's return. Amen

Here in Joshua 7, we see the sin of Achan, of the tribe of Judah, that he disobeyed the word of God regarding the sacking of Jericho, as we saw last chapter; And the city shall be accursed, even it, and all that are therein, to the Lord: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent. And ye, in any wise keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed, when ye take of the accursed thing, and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it. But all the silver, and gold, and vessels of brass and iron, are consecrated unto the Lord: they shall come into the treasury of the Lord. Joshua learns of the trespass when an easy victory for the children of Israel against the Amorites, turns into an embarrassing defeat. Rending his clothes in torment, the Lord chastises him and reveals that there has been sin that has turned Him against the Israelites. He gives Joshua instruction to find out who has taken the accursed things of Jericho into the camp. By tribe, family and house, Joshua inquired, and finally Achan confesses; When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it. The items, Achan, his children and possessions, are all led without the camp. They are stoned and it all burned in the valley of Achor, or "troubles," and a cairn of stones was heaped upon the remnants as a reminder to the children of Israel. A memorial to what happens when one brings sin among them. The spiritual application of this story, like much of the accounts of Israel from Egypt though the promised land, can be applied to our lives as saved Christians. Sometimes, even as we are delivered by God from our enemies, or having received blessings by our obedience and reward, our hearts turn to covetousness. We are given a temptation to sin. The devil loves to bring a test before us when God is in the process of rewarding our faith in Him. When we are the most comfortable. Many times in the Christian life, you will find that you've made it through something by walking in the Spirit and trusting in God, only to stumble at the finish line because the relief turns to complacency. Satan looks for ways to accuse us and what better time than victory? The lesson of Achan can be a valuable one, to not depart from the path God laid out for us, even in victory, because it can undo all the good God has done in our life, and lead to our destruction. The devil hides temptations even in the smallest victories of our lives. How much more the temptation when the odds seem overwhelmingly against you, and yet you persevere in the Lord. Beware of the sin of Achan. Don't let the devil snatch defeat from victory.

Joshua 8 tells of the taking of Ai, the plan of God to have a force lay in wait as an ambush, drawing the men of the city out to pursue the Israelites who feigned a retreat. Using their previous defeat at the hands of Ai, due to the abomination spoiled from Jericho by Achan, as a means to trick the Canaanite horde. But unlike Jericho, the Lord grants Joshua and the children of Israel the spoil of the city. There is a time and a place God will allow blessings, and other times where the blessing is withheld, and it isn't for us to question when or to take opportunity ourselves. But to patiently do what the Lord tells us, that it be well with us. Joshua commemorates the taking of Jericho and Ai with an assembly of the people and the reading of the law given by God to Moses, and the instructions Moses gave to the people, as we read in Deuteronomy 27; And Moses with the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying, Keep all the commandments which I command you this day. And it shall be on the day when ye shall pass over Jordan unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, that thou shalt set thee up great stones, and plaister them with plaister: And thou shalt write upon them all the words of this law, when thou art passed over, that thou mayest go in unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, a land that floweth with milk and honey; as the Lord God of thy fathers hath promised thee. Therefore it shall be when ye be gone over Jordan, that ye shall set up these stones, which I command you this day, in mount Ebal, and thou shalt plaister them with plaister. And there shalt thou build an altar unto the Lord thy God, an altar of stones: thou shalt not lift up any iron tool upon them. Thou shalt build the altar of the Lord thy God of whole stones: and thou shalt offer burnt offerings thereon unto the Lord thy God: And thou shalt offer peace offerings, and shalt eat there, and rejoice before the Lord thy God. And thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly. And Moses and the priests the Levites spake unto all Israel, saying, Take heed, and hearken, O Israel; this day thou art become the people of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt therefore obey the voice of the Lord thy God, and do his commandments and his statutes, which I command thee this day. And Moses charged the people the same day, saying, These shall stand upon mount Gerizim to bless the people, when ye are come over Jordan; Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Joseph, and Benjamin: And these shall stand upon mount Ebal to curse; Reuben, Gad, and Asher, and Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali. Obedient Joshua personally carves the law into the rock. The blessings and the curses are given again, and the sacrifices made as instructed. Joshua even takes down the hanged king of Ai at sunset as God's law stated, least it be a curse on the land.

Continuing the narrative of the taking of Canaan by Joshua and the Israelites, we see that the kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites have begun to ally against the invasion of the Hebrews, led by the Lord God that performed miracles in Egypt and destroyed the kings beyond Jordan. And the people of Gibeon, seeing the power of God at work in Jericho and Ai, decide a different strategy; they offer a truce by deception. Wearing old and tattered clothing and supplies, they pretend they are from a far land, afraid of the Lord God, and get Joshua to swear an oath that they would not be harmed. But Joshua discovered their city is just 3 days away, neighbors to the camp at Gilgal. In punishment for the deception, Joshua commands they agree to be servants of Israel in perpetuity. Bondsmen, hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of God. Serving the congregation and the altar for the Levites. The Ark finding a home there for a while in the time of the Kings. King Saul, in his zeal, will attempt to wipe them out during his reign. And for this betrayal of the oath, David his successor will deliver up the sons of Saul to the city of Gibeon for execution. The oath was a serious one, and by acquiescing to Joshua's compromise, the curse of Canaan given against Ham for his abomination against Noah, is fulfilled. Genesis 9:18-27: And the sons of Noah, that went forth of the ark, were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth: and Ham is the father of Canaan. These are the three sons of Noah: and of them was the whole earth overspread. And Noah began to be an husbandman, and he planted a vineyard: And he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent. And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without. And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father's nakedness. And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done unto him. And he said, Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren. And he said, Blessed be the Lord God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant. God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.

Joshua 10 is one of the greatest battles of the history of man, where Joshua and the Israelites, the Lord fighting for them, fought the battle of the 5 Kings at Gibeon, where more men were slaughtered by the hailstones rained on them by God than the edge of the sword. Joshua commanded the sun and moon to stand still so that they could destroy the enemies of God in the light. And the Lord granted it. The Bible says this miracle was told of in the Book of Jasher, what seems to be a lost book of the history of the Hebrews, called the "book of the righteous." Many forgeries have been produced, and Jewish fables surround this mention, but we have the inspired preserved word of God in Joshua to tell us of His glory that day. As the armies of Israel pursued the 5 Kings, the sought refuge in a cave. Joshua has stones rolled in front of the entrance, to deal with them later. The nature of this battle, the miracles, the wrath of God, kings hiding in mountains to escape, is a picture of the end times. The Day of the Lord. Where instead of standing still, the Sun and Moon darken. The stars fall from the heavens. And the kings and mighty men of the earth are cut down by the coming of Christ Jesus, with ten thousands of His saints. With the kings trapped, Joshua leads his armies against the nearby city of Makkedah, killing its king and all the people. Following this, he executes the 5 Kings, hanging them all from trees, cursed (for he that is hanged is accursed of God). He proceeds to then raid and slaughter city after city, killing king after king, until all these kingdoms were taken in one campaign, because the Lord God of Israel fought for Israel. And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the Lord hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the Lord fought for Israel. The glory and power of the Lord to execute His fierce wrath and deliver enemies, is the promise for the second coming of Christ as well. It is the prayers of the saints, asking for His wrath to be poured out. That every knee bow and tongue confess, He is Lord. That our enemies be made to know He loved us. As wicked and awful the world may seem, we as Christians have this sure hope of being delivered. That the Lord will repay. So stand fast in the faith of Christ. Unafraid. Amen John 3:17-18 For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God. Titus 3:10-11 A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself. Those who choose not to believe the truth given by the grace of God through His word, condemn themselves. They oppose the truth and in doing so oppose themselves. Many times Calvinists will point to verses that they believe teach that salvation is by the whim of God, man unable to choose to believe. But God makes clear those who choose not to believe are responsible for their own condemnation. Something to keep in mind. Acts 18:6 And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles. Another great verse that shows the error of Calvinism from the viewpoint of the unbelieving. They oppose themselves. Their own blood is upon them, because they chose not to believe Paul's preaching of the gospel. If this were by the election of God, predetermined beforehand, they wouldn't be opposing themselves. Their blood wouldn't be upon their own heads.

A map for the visually minded. The epic conquest of Canaan by Israel through the power of God, led of Joshua, is an amazing story. One you'd think would be fit for a Hollywood blockbuster. The taking of the kingdoms, the slaying of kings. The burning of the cities and spoiling of the people to whom God had appointed destruction. Hardening the hearts of those who had committed abominations in the land, that they fed into their own destruction. For it was of the Lord to harden their hearts, that they should come against Israel in battle, that he might destroy them utterly, and that they might have no favour, but that he might destroy them, as the Lord commanded Moses. This is reprobation. The hardening of men's hearts that they may be destroyed of God. But Joshua did all that the Lord had commanded Moses. He was obedient and faithful, and the land was delivered unto them. Amen John 1:42 And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone. We can see how modern translations fail in this simple verse, which when understood gives the important context to Matthew 16:13-18. Cephas/Petra/Peter mean stone and as we see so often, the Bible defines itself. By eliminating this self-referential definition, it allows false doctrine to be established in those ignorant to the word.

Through the obedience of Moses and his successor Joshua, the Lord delivered unto the children of Israel the land promised of Abraham, Moses defeating 2 kings, Joshua 31 kings. Make of that what you will. But the defeat of the 33 Kings in Canaan and beyond the Jordan to the East shows us the power of God when we walk in the paths He has chosen for us. When we are trusting in Him to deliver us and we are obedient to His will for our lives.

Joshua 13 maps for us visual types. With the majority of the warfare over. And the Lord having delivered the Israelites the land, and Joshua, who was with Moses from the beginning of the exodus, is getting old, God commands the land be apportioned, beginning east of the Jordan in the area Moses had promised Gad, Manasseh and Ruben. And of the Levites, a place in each so their priestly inheritance may be practiced in the sacrifices they maintained. We see potential for trouble in that there are still strangers of the Canaanites among them. The seeds planted that will cause problems down the line. Joshua 13 maps for us visual types. With the majority of the warfare over. And the Lord having delivered the Israelites the land, and Joshua, who was with Moses from the beginning of the exodus, is getting old, God commands the land be apportioned, beginning east of the Jordan in the area Moses had promised Gad, Manasseh and Ruben. And of the Levites, a place in each so their priestly inheritance may be practiced in the sacrifices they maintained. We see potential for trouble in that there are still strangers of the Canaanites among them. The seeds planted that will cause problems down the line.

Caleb, the other spy who went out with Joshua, who never wavered in his faith in the living God, is given his reward. The mount called Hebron, where the giants called Anakims were. 2 Samuel 5 Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh. 2 Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and the Lord said to thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel. 3 So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a league with them in Hebron before the Lord: and they anointed David king over Israel. 4 David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years. 5 In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah. 6 And the king and his men went to Jerusalem unto the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land: which spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither: thinking, David cannot come in hither. 7 Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David. 8 And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind that are hated of David's soul, he shall be chief and captain. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house. 9 So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David. And David built round about from Millo and inward. 10 And David went on, and grew great, and the Lord God of hosts was with him. 1 Chronicles 11 Then all Israel gathered themselves to David unto Hebron, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh. 2 And moreover in time past, even when Saul was king, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and the Lord thy God said unto thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be ruler over my people Israel. 3 Therefore came all the elders of Israel to the king to Hebron; and David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord; and they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word of the Lord by Samuel. 4 And David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, which is Jebus; where the Jebusites were, the inhabitants of the land. 5 And the inhabitants of Jebus said to David, Thou shalt not come hither. Nevertheless David took the castle of Zion, which is the city of David. 6 And David said, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain. So Joab the son of Zeruiah went first up, and was chief. 7 And David dwelt in the castle; therefore they called it the city of David. 8 And he built the city round about, even from Millo round about: and Joab repaired the rest of the city. 9 So David waxed greater and greater: for the Lord of hosts was with him. The Jebusites and other remnants of the Canaanites that the children of Israel did not deal with, and allowed to live, ate as a canker, acting as a constant sore. And led the people to abominations. Ezra 9:1 Now when these things were done, the princes came to me, saying, The people of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations, even of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites. A little leaven leavens the whole lump. God promises to remove the sin and temptation in our hearts. No temptation being too great for us to bear, He provides deliverance in every test. And yet we allow these temptations to remain among us. Never fully removing them from our lives. And for many, the results are being backslidden and lessening out ability to do great things for the Lord. Even here in Jerusalem, the heart of the city where God made known His name, the Israelites had allowed the Jebusites to fester. They were never fully driven out and destroyed. We all have sin in our lives. Things we know we ought not do, that remains not because God isn't faithful to deliver us, but because we are lazy and weak. In such a rush to claim our spot in the promised land, and enter into peace, we fail to stay vigilant.

As we see, the inheritance by lot of the promised land, divided unto the various tribes, shows that we are all given by God and chance the things we need, but some require work to maximize the potential. And so we shouldn't complain about what we have vs what we feel we deserve. Like those who didn't drive out all the Canaanites, or take the lumber, or face the armies for fear, we often leave so much on the table. God provides to us abundantly and we squander so much of it, while complaining. We should be grateful for what we have and make the most of every opportunity and gift God has given us.

Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations. O my soul, come not thou into their secret; unto their assembly, mine honour, be not thou united: for in their anger they slew a man, and in their selfwill they digged down a wall. Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel. In Genesis 49, as Jacob blesses each son, the children of Israel, he places Levi and Simeon together. Note that for their wrath their nations are cursed. Levi to be scattered throughout Israel, as the Levitical priesthood was, having no inheritance of their own, and dividing Simeon into Judah, where they eventually fade away. There are some accounts of Simeon left to come. But minor mentions. Their numbers dwindled by half between the census in the wilderness, from the beginning of the 40 years to the end. In Judah they remained, until a mention in 1 Chronicles 4; These mentioned by their names were princes in their families: and the house of their fathers increased greatly. And they went to the entrance of Gedor, even unto the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks. And they found fat pasture and good, and the land was wide, and quiet, and peaceable; for they of Ham had dwelt there of old. And these written by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and smote their tents, and the habitations that were found there, and destroyed them utterly unto this day, and dwelt in their rooms: because there was pasture there for their flocks. And some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi. And they smote the rest of the Amalekites that were escaped, and dwelt there unto this day. This is prior to the Babylonian captivity, and it is assumed they being within Judah, were carried away captive, and by the return, lost as an individual tribe. Of course, 12,000 saved believers from Simeon will be among the 144,000 in the wrath, according to Revelation 7:7. Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; and he shall be for an haven of ships; and his border shall be unto Zidon. The territory allotted Zebulun was at the southern end of the Sea of Galilee, with its eastern border, the western border being the Mediterranean, the south bordered by the Tribe of Issachar, and the north by Asher on the western side and Naphtali on the east. It isn't quite near Zidon/Sidon which is by Tyre, in the northern part of Asher, but it is entirely possible that by their central location along the river Kishon, between two seas, that as a seafaring people had made ports along the coast of the Mediterranean. Their tribe has very little mention, other than again to say they'd be part of the north kingdom of Israel, and scattered away by Assyria during their conquest of the kingdom (and their part of the 144K). But their territory is where Christ Jesus was raised, as a Galilean in Samaria. Not as a Jew in Judea. I will attempt to deal with the remaining tribes given in this chapter, before moving on. They may have to wait until tomorrow, but for the most part, their stories are similar and their dates the same. Other than the remnants of saints among their people, each falls to Idolatry and the same abominations of the people who God drove out before them, and so were scattered or bred out of existence, some returning to Christ during His ministry. Most never retaining any of the blessings of God having been unfaithful.

and do that which hath proceeded out of your mouth. 25 And the children of Gad and the children of Reuben spake unto Moses, saying, Thy servants will do as my lord commandeth. 26 Our little ones, our wives, our flocks, and all our cattle, shall be there in the cities of Gilead: 27 But thy servants will pass over, every man armed for war, before the Lord to battle, as my lord saith. 28 So concerning them Moses commanded Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the chief fathers of the tribes of the children of Israel: 29 And Moses said unto them, If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, every man armed to battle, before the Lord, and the land shall be subdued before you; then ye shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession: 30 But if they will not pass over with you armed, they shall have possessions among you in the land of Canaan. 31 And the children of Gad and the children of Reuben answered, saying, As the Lord hath said unto thy servants, so will we do. 32 We will pass over armed before the Lord into the land of Canaan, that the possession of our inheritance on this side Jordan may be our's. 33 And Moses gave unto them, even to the children of Gad, and to the children of Reuben, and unto half the tribe of Manasseh the son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land, with the cities thereof in the coasts, even the cities of the country round about. Genesis 49:19 Gad, a troop shall overcome him: but he shall overcome at the last. Deuteronomy 33:20-21 And of Gad he said, Blessed be he that enlargeth Gad: he dwelleth as a lion, and teareth the arm with the crown of the head. Deuteronomy 33:6 Let Reuben live, and not die; and let not his men be few. Matthew 5 33 Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: 34 But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: 35 Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. 36 Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. 37 But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. James 5:12 But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation. Matthew 7:7-8 Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened. 1 John 5:11-15 And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life. These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God. And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him. Here in Joshua 22, the first half of the chapter, we find the children of Israel victorious in the promised land, delivered to them by the power of God, who had driven out the kingdoms and left them cities and fields and vineyards, a land flowing with milk and honey. But not all the tribes of Jacob wished to settle there. Before they'd crossed over into the land west of the Jordan, the tribes of Gad, Ruben and half the tribe of Manasseh had petitioned the Lord through Moses that they may have the land to the east of the river, which was good for cattle, being they had much and were ranchers. Just as Lot saw the plains of Jordan, and saw it was good for herding his flocks, there in the east, and separated himself from Abraham, pitching his tent towards Sodom. This was the same land. And Moses became indignant at their request, because he felt they were abandoning the brethren to do their own thing, just as the battle was about to be truly met. That it would discourage the remaining Israelites from crossing into the promised land, just as their fathers who spied out the land had 40 years earlier, causing God to curse them to wander in the wilderness. But, they said not so, while they would build cities for their children and pens for their cattle, the Gadites and Reubenites and half tribe of Manasseh vowed that their men of war would go before the people across the Jordan and fight with them until Canaan was theirs, and they had peace. So, here in Joshua, having kept their word and fought with their brethren, they are given permission to enter into rest in the lands Moses had given them. And Joshua warns them to follow in the commandments of God and then blesses them further, as they departed; Return with much riches unto your tents, and with very much cattle, with silver, and with gold, and with brass, and with iron, and with very much raiment: divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren. These men had let their yea mean yea, their promise kept. They believed God and kept His will, but asked in return to have that which they sought on the east of the Jordan, and the Lord gave it to them. We know the Lord is faithful, and keeps His word. We know the Father answers our prayers and fulfils our needs, and allows us that which is in our hearts as long as it doesn't conflict with His larger plans. If we ask, it shall be given. We may have confidence as believers that if we ask anything according to His will, that our petitions that we desire will be granted. And blessings given for our obedience to His will. The lesson for believers today is that our promises and blessings are related. Our willingness to do as He commands of us grants us not only reward for our obedience, but He will accommodate that which we seek in this life, so long as it is according to His will. God is flexible, and a good Father; Luke 11:11-13 If a son shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone? or if he ask a fish, will he for a fish give him a serpent? Or if he shall ask an egg, will he offer him a scorpion? If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him? These men risked their lives for their brothers, they obeyed the will of God. They let their actions speak to their vow, and we're not only given that which they sought for themselves and their families, but were blessed on top of it all for their faith and obedience. Following this example, being willing and able to do the will of God, as His sons, adopted by our faith in Christ, allows us to enter boldly before the throne, and ask Him and receive. Hebrews 4:16 Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need. In my own life, I know with certainty that when I first seek the things of God, when I turn to His word, and pray for His will to be done, to be used as He sees fit, that I am blessed beyond measure and the things I seek are given unto me. This isn't a prosperity gospel. It is the promise of God. Seeking His will first will find you asking for ways to please Him, to be a blessing to others, rather than riches. Asking for patience or understanding and wisdom. Asking to be able to lead others to Christ. The material blessings will follow, usually just enough to satisfy your needs. Just enough to keep you from trouble, in my case. But the spiritual blessings of helping others to the truth or even just being in the right place at the right time to affect someone positively, they are endless and wonderful. And you receive a good name, as these men did. Amen. Numbers 25 And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. 2 And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods. 3 And Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel. 4 And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel. 5 And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baalpeor. 6 And, behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. 7 And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand; 8 And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel. 9 And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand. Psalms 119:104 Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way. Proverbs 18:13 He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him. In the second part of Joshua 22, we see that time has passed and the men of war from Gad, Ruben and half tribe of Manasseh have returned east, across the Jordan to their inheritance. Their land bordering Ammonites and Moabites, the places the children of Israel had come through to reach the promised land. And word makes it back to Shiloh, at the Tabernacle of the Lord that the Israelites across the Jordan had set up an altar for themselves. The Israelites fear the worst. That these men who had helped liberate the land for their brethren had turned from the Lord and began worshiping the gods of the people who had been driven out and slain. We see again Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron, who had ended the plague of God sent against the Israelites for joining the fornication and worship of Baal at Mt. Peor in Moab by slaying with a javelin a man of Israel and a Midianite woman flagrantly fornicating within the camp. A plague which slew 23,000 in one day, 24,000 over all; 1 Corinthians 10:8 Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand. Phinehas journeys out with the princes of Israel to inquire about the altar. Confronting the Gadites, Reubenites and men of Manasseh, he asks if they've rebelled against God. He reminds them of the matter of Baal-Peor, and of Achan, who had kept the cursed thing from Jericho to his own destruction ans his family's as well as the defeat of the armies of Israel, and the deaths of untold numbers of men in that defeat. He begs them, that if the land they possessed was too wicked for them, that they not resist the call to worship false gods, to bring their people back over the Jordan to be with the other tribes. To get right with God. But the tribes east of the Jordan explain that it is nothing like this. That their intentions were pure. They say may God judge their hearts, and punish them if they're lying, but that they simply set it up as a witness to their fellowship with the God of Israel and their brethren. To serve as a reminder for their children, that even though a river separate them, they are of Israel. They named it Ed which means 'witness.' This answer satisfied everyone, and so there was a happy ending all around. But the story has applications that we can learn from, as does the entire Bible. But here we see the tendency of distance and absence from among one another often leads to misunderstanding. We can see it in our own experiences, where a sibling moves away to the city, or a brother from church takes a job in another state, or even coworkers who don't share an office or a site, but question the ethic of those working remotely...distance and absence stir up questions, and an innocent act by one can spark a potential conflict between the two. Godly parents worry about whether their children who leave the nest are living godly themselves. For example we see Job offering sacrifices for his children, just in case they weren't; Job 1:5 And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually. It is a natural feeling to have, but it can also lead to paranoia and rash action. Phinehas, who in his zeal for the Lord acted decisively in Moab, taking a spear and ending the judgment against his people with the deaths of the fornicator and the whore, shows discernment, judgment and mercy here, at Ed. Rather than impulsively allowing his hatred of every false way lead to violence, he asks of them the altars purpose. And rather than accuse, he reminds them of why he has concerns. That not only would this be bad for them if they'd fallen away to Baal, but that God's judgment is upon nations, and all of Israel could suffer. Phinehas asks them to return cross the Jordan if it meant repenting of their possible sin, a chance to get right. And, most importantly, he listens to their answer, not deciding the matter before hearing them out. This is a pattern we can all learn from. Especially in situations where we don't know the intent of the heart. The same right judgment he showed in Peor, he shows here. And of course there's an innocent explanation. And the explanation made by men of the 2.5 tribes who had just demonstrated their honor by keeping their word in settling Canaan is accepted. And all of Israel rejoiced at the news. Crisis averted. Now, the other application is that we should hate every false way, and there is no harm in asking someone professing to be Christian to explain their apparent behavior or statements that seem contrary to the Gospel. As we see online especially, there are many who hold damnable heresies and doctrines of devils, claiming to be of Christ. There is no profit in blind ecumenicalism, and accepting everyone calling themselves Christian regardless of their beliefs. But we should trust someone who claims to be a believer, giving them the benefit of the doubt unless there is a sign that concerns us. And then, remembering Phinehas, inquire what they meant, meekly and with care. It could simply be a misunderstanding or a different way of phrasing something, perfectly innocent. Yes, if they announce their beliefs in a false gospel or a different god, or some vain traditions and dead works, we should confront them with scripture and rebuke them. But there are times brothers as set at variance, when the truth is there are only surface differences caused by distance and absence of fellowship. Thankfully, God's word has a shortcut to finding out if we share a common foundation; asking "What must one do to be saved?" Paul repeatedly uses the gospel as a way of assurance of common mindedness with the churches he writes to. That we all share the same foundational belief. As Jesus says of testing the spirit of a teacher, we shall know them by their fruits, by the beliefs of their followers. If they are saved by the gospel or if they believe some false way. We need to meekly and humbly seek to know, before either grabbing a javelin or declaring peace, and always ready to provide a way out should they prove to be going the way of Balaam, and heading to the destruction of Baal-Peor. By giving them the true gospel in love. Amen

As we near the end of Joshua's life, the leader of Israel in the promised land, we see his repeating the instruction and admonition of the Lord given as promise, from Joshua 1; Now after the death of Moses the servant of the Lord it came to pass, that the Lord spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister, saying, 2 Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Israel. 3 Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you, as I said unto Moses. 4 From the wilderness and this Lebanon even unto the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and unto the great sea toward the going down of the sun, shall be your coast. 5 There shall not any man be able to stand before thee all the days of thy life: as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee: I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee. 6 Be strong and of a good courage: for unto this people shalt thou divide for an inheritance the land, which I sware unto their fathers to give them. 7 Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper withersoever thou goest. 8 This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success. 9 Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest. This promise is the inheritance they now possess. As a parable of salvation, the entrance into the promised land, with some battles, backslides, attacks by the world, and deliverance by the Lord, Joshua serves to remind us that to live a peaceful and profitable life in Christ requires our having the strength and courage to obey the commandments of God. To follow where He leads. That it be well with us. To not cling to the old ways. To separate ourselves from the things of this world. To walk neither to the right nor left, but on the path God has laid out for us. To cleave ourselves to the Lord of our deliverance. And when we are old and waxen of age, we may say to our children and grandchildren that this is the living God who delivered us, gave us prosperity and that His was are right and proper. So that they don't turn back to other gods, to disobedience. That they may inherit the same promised land of salvation, by our example. Amen Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper withersoever thou goest. This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success. Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest. This is the true purpose of God's commandments. This is how the law is relevant to those saved by the law of liberty, by grace through faith in Christ Jesus. Yes the law is a schoolmaster that brings us to understand we need salvation. Yes the law of for the lawless, that they may be punished according to the will and perfect judgement of God. But it's real purpose is for a righteous people to know the will of God for their lives, and in keeping it as best they can, have a prosperous and successful life in service to our God. Those that make this obedience to the law their gospel, and seek to work their own righteousness as a means of achieving or maintaining their salvation, miss the point and whatever gain they receive is offset by their constant doubts and fears. Not having faith, they please not God. Their filthy rags of their own righteousness give them nothing but hopelessness. This isn't a prosperity gospel. There is no promise of riches and earthly wealth. But true success in our walk with Christ. Being taken care of, all we need, that we may store up riches in heaven. That we may be saved and all our house. That we may win souls and edify the brethren. Amen Structurally, we should note that like the second to last chapter of Genesis, chapter 39, we find the blessings of Jacob on his children. In the second to last chapter, Deuteronomy 33 is Moses' blessings of the tribes. Here in the second to last chapter of Joshua, it is a blessing and a warning given to all of Israel.
