And all they of Israel were a thousand thousand and an hundred thousand men that drew sword: and Judah was four hundred threescore and ten thousand men that drew sword. But Levi and Benjamin counted he not among them: for the king's word was abominable to Joab. And God was displeased with this thing; therefore he smote Israel.

1 Kings begins with a other son in rebellion against an elderly, dying David, this time Adonijah the son of Haggith, who begins to behave as Absalom and takes advantage of David being bedridden to declare himself King of Israel. We see Joab, who was left out of David's praise of his mighty men, has joined in the sedition, along with Abiathar the priest. But the mighty men, and Nathan the prophet and Zadok the priest and others remained loyal to David and the kingdom. They tell Bathsheba to go inform the King of this treachery, for her life and the life of Solomon, the promised heir. So while the upstart and his coconspirators feast outside the city, David commands that Solomon be anointed king, and Zadok and Nathan do as he commands, and all Jerusalem praises King Solomon. Adonijah and the others at the feast gear the commotion and Jonathan son of Abiathar comes to tell them of the news. The men scattered and Adonijah fears, gripping the horns of the altar he had set up for the feast, where the beasts were slain. His guests abandoned him, he fears for his life, but Solomon promises his half-brother peace if he shows himself worthy. So he sends for Adonijah, who comes and bowed before King Solomon is spared and allowed to go to his house. The image of David giving the kingdom to Solomon, putting all beneath his feat, David's anointed riding on a donkey, while the child in rebellion clings to the altar, is to me an echo of The Father putting all in subjection under the Son, Christ Jesus. And the betrayal of the Jews pictured in Adonijah and the altar. The mercy of Solomon to him, as the mercy of Christ that all men may bow before Him and proclaim that He is Lord. This allegory plays out more, as we shall see in the next chapter.

We finally come to the death of King David, and before he passes on he has words for his son, Solomon. He reminds Solomon to walk in the ways of the Lord that it be well with him and his kingdom. A walk with God that David mostly kept, despite a few times of his own lusts getting the better of him. David has unfinished business with Joab and Shimei, and leaves it to Solomon in his wisdom to do that which is right. Having Joab executed for the blood on his head, for the murders of righteous men, having participated in the attempted sedition of Adonijah. And Shimei, the Benjamite who cursed David and coaxed a reprieve from the King when David returned from exile during the Absalom coup. Shimei, Solomon judges to remain in Jerusalem for the rest of his life, and when Shimei leaves to retrieve two runaway servants, Solomon has him put to death. A fitting end for those that despised the anointed of the Lord. Now Adonijah, who had been spared after he bent the knee to Solomon comes to the King's mother, Bathsheba, with a request. He asks for Abishag a Shunammite to be his wife. In 1 Kings 1 we are told that the sick and dying David took young and fair Abishag to lay with him for warmth. And although they never consummated their relationship, she was as a concubine to the King. Adonijah asks Bathsheba saying that because of her relationship with Solomon, the king couldn't refuse her. Perhaps flattered, Bathsheba does as he asks and approaches the king, and is even given honor of sitting at his right hand, and she asks this thing for the half-brother of Solomon. Solomon, in his wisdom, recognizes what this entails, for an elder son to take for wife the concubine of the former king, solidifying Adonijah's false claim to the throne. Solomon correctly ignores his mother's petition and orders the upstart's death. Roman Catholicism will sometimes point to a truncated version of this story to paint a picture of Mary as "queen" and mediatrix between man and Christ Jesus. They will include the flattery of Adonijah, saying "for he will not say thee nay" anything Mary asks of Him. As if this were some sort of cheat code to get around the will of God by appealing to the mother of Christ. They will say that Solomon's response to his mother is the same response of Jesus to Mary, "Ask on, my mother: for I will not say thee nay." They will ignore that Solomon not only said nay, but had Adonijah killed for his attempt to make an end run around the anointed of the Lord. There is one mediator between God and man. The man Christ Jesus. Joab, knowing he was to be executed for the blood he had shed and his betrayal of the king, flees to the tabernacle, and grabs hold of the altar and refuses to budge, thinking that this will save him. But Solomon knows that the blood Joab shed remained on David's kingdom, and by extension his own, and must be repaid to get right with God. Again, like Adonijah who had done the same thing in the previous chapter, Joab's desperation to escape the just punishment for his sin by clinging to the altar, rather than to the mercy of the King, is an image of the unbelieving Jews clinging to their dead works and vain traditions, rather than repentance towards Christ.

In 1 Kings 3 we see Solomon settling in as King of Israel, making peace with the Pharaoh of Egypt through marriage to his daughter, while building his palace and the Temple of the Lord in Jerusalem. We are told that the people sacrificed in high places because there was no house of the Lord for central worship as had been when the Ark and the Tabernacle were in one location, together. David had brought the Ark to Jerusalem, while Zadok the priest was in charge over the Tabernacle in Gibeon, apparently a high place, according to the account in 2 Chronicles 1. And while we have association with Baal worship in high places, and the existence of them was no God's plan for a central place of worship, in this strange in-between time, it wouldn't be outrageous for Solomon, who loved the Lord and kept David's statutes, to sacrifice at Gibeon to the Lord God of Israel. And Solomon does, and offers a thousand burnt offerings upon the altar of the Tabernacle out of love for God. And God graciously speaks to Solomon by dream, and tells the new king to ask what God shall give him. Solomon says Thou hast shewed unto thy servant David my father great mercy, according as he walked before thee in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with thee; and thou hast kept for him this great kindness, that thou hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day. Solomon wisely begins his petition by recognizing how God blessed his father, David. The great mercy the living God showed him, and the great kindness of giving David an heir to sit upon the throne. As the father of saved children, I can tell you this kindness is awesome, and the mercy of God that we may know our children are co-heirs with Christ to the Kingdom is one of the greatest gifts God can bestow on a parent. Solomon continues, wisely recognizing his youth and inexperience as he takes the throne given to him as God's anointed, king over a great number of people. And so Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge God's people, strong discernment between good and bad. This pleased the Lord, and because Solomon did not ask foolishly or selfishly, God says Behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart. The wisest man to ever live. The question then arises, was this gift given to Solomon at this moment, where his eyes opened and he gained this wisdom supernaturally? Or, given his upbringing by David, and his love for the Lord and his desire to walk in the ways of his father and the word of God, had Solomon been shaped by God from birth to be such a King? When Solomon is given an opportunity to ask of God anything, and he was wise enough to give glory to God first and ask for right judgment to rule wisely, was he already displaying that wisdom that had been given him by the Lord? Because Solomon asked rightly, God says He will not only bless him with wisdom, but riches and honor, elevating him above all kings during his reign. God also repeats His promise, one that stands for Christians today; And if thou wilt walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as thy father David did walk, then I will lengthen thy days. Psalm 37:28-38 For the Lord loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints; they are preserved for ever: but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off. The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever. The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom, and his tongue talketh of judgment. The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide. The wicked watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him. The Lord will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when he is judged. Wait on the Lord, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land: when the wicked are cut off, thou shalt see it. I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree. Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found. Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace. But the transgressors shall be destroyed together: the end of the wicked shall be cut off. And so, we are told the famous story of an example of the wisdom of Solomon; the cutting of the baby in half. This is such an extraordinary tale, that even secular and worldly traditions of wisdom recognize it and teach it throughout the world. Two harlots, and both give birth to sons within days of each other. And the one accidentally kills her own baby, smothering it in its sleep. She steals the other woman's son in the night and gives to her the dead child. They come before the King to judge and he discerned the matter by presenting a horrific choice; cutting the infant that each woman be given half. The woman who objects and says rather let the other woman keep it, is clearly the real mother, while the one who agrees to "split the baby" is revealed to be the imposter. This wisdom established the understanding throughout Israel that God had blessed their King. and gained Solomon the people's respect. Fame that would soon spread to the rest of the world.

The wisdom given to Solomon was and is the greatest wisdom possessed of man, before or since. And we have been blessed by God to have much of this wisdom providentially preserved in God's word. Although Solomon is said to have composed 3,000 proverbs, only 800 bearing his name appear in the book of Proverbs. But these are the inspired word of God and given for our admonition and instruction. We have the book of Ecclesiastes, which is the wisdom of the prophet of God, Solomon set out to test the truth in all things of this world, only to find vanity, except in the Lord. True philosophy from the Spirit. We have only one song of the 1,005 the King composed, the Song of Songs, and its deep meaning. We have the cream of the wisdom given to Solomon by God, at our fingertips. Able to study and know it. What a blessing. But of the thousands of proverbs and hundreds of songs and all his deep knowledge of flora and fauna and things of this earth and this life, we have no record. Only that which pertaineth to God. There is wisdom there, too.

Matthew 16:15-18 He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God. And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. 1 Corinthians 3:9-11 For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Isaiah 2:2-4 And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD's house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more. As we read through 1 Kings and the story of King Solomon, there are parallels with the second coming of Christ Jesus, and the millennial reign. Just as David's kingdom was at times a picture of Jesus. Here we see a false king try to usurp the throne in Adonijah, just as the Antichrist will in the Great Tribulation. Joab as the Jews who betrayed the Lord and help establish the beast system for the Antichrist. Abiathar, the high priest who is like the beast's prophet. And when Solomon deals with them, and they are killed or cast out, and he established his reign in peace, with kings like Hiram of Tyre giving him praise, and ruling with wisdom and right judgment. And Solomon builds the house of God where He has placed His name, just as Jesus builds His temple of the saints, His church in which the saved are pillars, and He is the foundation. It is an interesting foreshadowing. Like most OT pictures of the end times, it isn't perfect but a reflection through a glass darkly. But the parallel is there.

And so Solomon, in his 4th year as King of Israel, began construction of the temple of the Lord, in the place where He placed His name. In the midst of Jerusalem. The King's Valley. Where the High Priest, and King of Salem, Melchizedek took tithes and offerings from Abraham. Where Abraham took Issac to be sacrificed by faith. Mount Moriah. Where David placed the Ark. Where Christ Jesus was crucified. Where He shall rule and reign with a rod of Iron. Deuteronomy 16:6 But at the place which the LORD thy God shall choose to place his name in, there thou shalt sacrifice the passover at even, at the going down of the sun, at the season that thou camest forth out of Egypt. Deuteronomy 14:23 And thou shalt eat before the LORD thy God, in the place which he shall choose to place his name there, the tithe of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the firstlings of thy herds and of thy flocks; that thou mayest learn to fear the LORD thy God always. 1 Kings 6:11-13 And the word of the Lord came to Solomon, saying, Concerning this house which thou art in building, if thou wilt walk in my statutes, and execute my judgments, and keep all my commandments to walk in them; then will I perform my word with thee, which I spake unto David thy father: And I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will not forsake my people Israel. Galatians 6:14-18 But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature. And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God. From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus. Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. Revelation 21 And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea. 2 And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. 3 And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. 4 And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away. 5 And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. And he said unto me, Write: for these words are true and faithful. 6 And he said unto me, It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely. 7 He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son. 8 But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death. 9 And there came unto me one of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues, and talked with me, saying, Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb's wife. 10 And he carried me away in the spirit to a great and high mountain, and shewed me that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, 11 Having the glory of God: and her light was like unto a stone most precious, even like a jasper stone, clear as crystal; 12 And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: 13 On the east three gates; on the north three gates; on the south three gates; and on the west three gates. 14 And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. 15 And he that talked with me had a golden reed to measure the city, and the gates thereof, and the wall thereof. 16 And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal. 17 And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel. 18 And the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass. 19 And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald; 20 The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolyte; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst. 21 And the twelve gates were twelve pearls: every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass. 22 And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it. 23 And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof. 24 And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it. 25 And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there. 26 And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. 27 And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb's book of life. This is the promise of Jesus, Who is the Alpha and Omega. Who is our High Priest, the King of Salem, King of Kings. That He will live with us in the place He chose to place His name, and to be our God, we who are saved of every nation, our names written in the Book of Life, the Israel of God. And in the new Jerusalem, there is no temple, for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it. Amen. But then, in the reign of Solomon, there was a temple built, that God had a house in the place where He chose to place His name. The design is given, and with the cedars of Lebanon, cut and measured before being brought in, and stone cut without that no sound of hammer or axe nor any tool of iron was heard in the house while it was building. And the stone, covered in wood. And the wood overlaid with gold. The decorative carvings of flowers and ornamental knobs, were made, and cherubs, including two massive golden cherubims over the mercy seat of the Ark, called the Oracles here, were made to reflect the throne of God in Heaven. Some idolatrous cults will claim the authority to make images of man to be worshipped in their temples from this, but the holy of holies was not seen by the people, only the High Priest, once a year, and no worship or serving of these things ever took place. They never were used in any form of ceremony or prayer. They were purely decorative, and taken from the Ark, itself patterned from the vision of Heaven given Moses of His throne. And so, in 7 years of building, Solomon's temple for the Lord was complete.

Solomon built the House of God in 7 years, his own palace in 13. His zeal was towards the Lord. Matthew 6:33 But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. By seeking first the things of God, Solomon had the peace and blessings to them see to his own. The same promise to all believers, that in building up the temple of Christ, of which every believer is a pillar, we will be blessed in our lives. Mark 10:28-30 Then Peter began to say unto him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee. And Jesus answered and said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel's, But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life. Not a "prosperity gospel," so much as a promise to be rewarded in our relationships with others, and the opening of their homes to those who do the work of the Lord. Fishers of men. Persecution and all, but we shall overcome. Revelation 3:12 Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name. The pillars Hiram made for the Temple, named Jachin—He will establish; and Boaz—in Him is strength, pictures of that Heavenly temple in which we are pillars of Christ's church. The great sea, held up by oxen, an enormous bath filled with much water for the ritual washing of the priests and cleansing of the sacrifices. It was massive, holding hundreds of gallons of water based on the dimensions. Given Israel's penchant for worshiping oxen and cattle, some question the purpose of including them in the decorations adorning the Temple. I have read that the purpose was to place the beasts of burden under subjection to the purposes of man in worship of the Most High, to keep the children of Israel from holding them in any higher esteem. And for the washings and purification, ten smaller lavers were made, set up on wheels. Portable, and able to be filled and rolled out. King Solomon made all the vessels that pertained to the house of the Lord, the altar and the table and candlesticks, lamps and tongs, bowls, sniffers, basons and spoons. Everything fitted for the purpose of the Lord, pure gold. The purity and value given to the vessels and implements are like our new man, redeemed. In the resurrection, perfected to do the work of the Lord. No more earthen pots made of clay, but golden.

2 Chronicles 8:1-2 And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, wherein Solomon had built the house of the Lord, and his own house, That the cities which Huram had restored to Solomon, Solomon built them, and caused the children of Israel to dwell there. Continuing in 1 Kings, and the reign of Solomon, we see that after 20 years, and much building and growth of his wealth and power, Solomon has completed the temple, and his palace and fortified Jerusalem and built up cities throughout Israel. He has been blessed by God, given tribute by many, gifts such as the city given by Pharaoh to his daughter, Solomon's queen. And through extensive trade and the loans and goodwill of the Phoenician King, Hiram (Huram in Chronicles), Solomon has made Israel a great nation. But first he began with the Lord. And so, 20 years after the first visitation of the Lord, God again appears unto Solomon, pleased with his faith and devotion. And He reiterated the covenant made with David, and to say Jerusalem is the place He has put His name, forever. That God's heart and eyes shall be upon it in perpetuity. The Lord says; And if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded thee, and wilt keep my statutes and my judgments: Then I will establish the throne of thy kingdom upon Israel for ever, as I promised to David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man upon the throne of Israel. This covenant, that there shall be a king forever over Israel from David's lineage, is fulfilled in Christ Jesus. This is a personal covenant, not made to Jews or to the nation of the 12 tribes, or any modern state, but to David, and confirmed to Solomon, and kept in Jesus. But the conditions of keeping the blessings that had so enriched Solomon and blessed the Temple he had built for the Lord, which He had hallowed for His name, were clear. That He would cut off the people if they or their children strayed, and the Temple cast out from His sight. Becoming a byword and an astonishment. While Jesus rules over all things, forever the King of Salem, the blessings of that promise aren't without condition. We who are saved and become co-heirs with Jesus Christ, have the same understanding. That we, in this life are blessed by that promised King, and given eternal life and made sons of God, but we do not have a license to sin and disobedience is met with punishment and chastisements from our Father. Many a great Christian has fallen to this, backslidden and ruined in this life. Lacking proper fear of the Lord. Because they forsook the Lord their God, who brought forth their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have taken hold upon other gods, and have worshipped them, and served them: therefore hath the Lord brought upon them all this evil. Never forget the Lord that led you from spiritual Egypt. From the bondage of the law, to make you His people. To whom much is given, much is expected. We read that Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee. And that these cities, near the border of Hiram's nation of Tyre, which is Lebanon, pleased him not. In 2 Chronicles 8, we are told he returned these to Solomon and Solomon built them up and filled them with Hebrews. The area was filled with remnants of Canaanites who had not been purged from the land. They are called Cabul by the Phoenician King, which according to the context, means unpleasing or not desired. This area in the Northwest of Galilee is where the Decapolis, the ten cities mentioned in the Gospels is located. An important part of Christ's early ministry. Where the fame of His works went out throughout Syria and Galilee and down to Judea and beyond the Jordan River. I don't know if it was meant as a gift to the king of Tyre or surety on loans given to Solomon for the vast wealth provided to build the Temple and his palace and all the improvements and cities built up in this time, but it seems odd that Solomon would, in his wisdom, give a gift that would insult his friend and benefactor. Maybe it was the landlocked nature of the cities. Maybe it was that they were inhabited by Canaanites. All we really know is Solomon eventually built them up himself and filled them with men of Israel. He also built ships for trade on the Red Sea, sending them out to places like Ophir, which is believed to be on the Indian subcontinent, famous for gold and other precious materials. The cities mentioned in the proceeding verses are along a trade road through southern Palestine, in the wilderness that the Israelites had wandered. A road connecting the port of Eziongeber to Jerusalem, and likely continuing through to Solomon's allies in Egypt and Tyre. We are told how he built up his armies by making the men of Israel soldiers of war, and multiplying horses and chariots. And by subjugation of the Canaanite tribes as bondsmen. The wealth and power of Israel reached its peak in this time. And Solomon went to the Temple and made sacrifices to God three times a year, and burnt incense to the Lord.

Solomon's fame and the judgement and wisdom of the Lord that was given unto him, went out into all the world. And the richness and wealth of this mighty nation compounded. Israel under King Solomon had trade by ships from Tharshish of Spain, to the Indian subcontinent in Ophir. He had tribute from Egypt and all the Kings of Syria and of the Hittites. He had the King of Phoenicia, Hiram commanding his navy of merchants, and the gold, silver, precious stones and finest wood of the world all came through Jerusalem. And the Queen of Sheba came down to sit at his feet and to be instructed of all she asked, bringing gifts of great riches to hear the wisdom the Lord had given the King. And the precious items that came to King Solomon were used to build his house and God's Temple and the blessings of his riches came upon all the people. This is a beautiful picture of the millennium reign of Christ. Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred threescore and six talents of gold... Here is wisdom. Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man; and his number is Six hundred threescore and six. The number 666, in 1 Kings 10 of wealth of Solomon, and in Revelation 13, the number of the beast. There is a lot of speculation as to the significance of this number and how it will present itself in the "Mark," during the Great Tribulation. I don't have any particular insight to those theories. But I do wonder if it is an allegory of the beast trying to imitate the glory of the global empire of trade and merchants found in Solomon's kingdom, which itself is a picture of Christ's millennial Kingdom. But that's just my own speculation.

Now King Solomon had done all these things for the Lord, and built Him a house in Jerusalem, and God had blessed him with great wisdom and 40 years of peace and great prosperity. But despite being the wisest of all men, Solomon's comfort led to his lusting after strange women, and in his sin he gave these wives altars and high places to worship false gods and commit abominations. The Lord had not just blessed Solomon, but appeared to him, twice! And reaffirmed the covenant with David to Solomon, that if he walked in the statutes and judgments of God, it would be well unto him. But even the wisdom of Solomon couldn't keep him from being led to sin by his own flesh. Ecclesiastes, the book of wisdom written in the Spirit by Solomon shows that the King understood the vanity of the flesh, and his Proverbs shows he understood that chasing after women led princes to sin and perverted their judgement. And yet... The spirit is willing but the flesh is weak. And for his sin, though Solomon was saved and believed on the Lord and it was counted for righteousness, he was punished by God in this world. The kingdom he spent so much time and effort and wealth in building, would be taken away from his son. And enemies long thought vanquished would return to plague all of Israel. God says to Solomon; Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father's sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son. Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake which I have chosen. As we see in this chapter, the Lord begins to put into motion various threats for the kingdom, and sends the prophet Ahijah to Jeroboam, to give to him the northern kingdom of Israel, divided from Judah. Saying; I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand, and will give it unto thee, even ten tribes. And unto his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a light alway before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there. And I will take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desireth, and shalt be king over Israel. Notice that it is not the Judeans whom God is concerned with, or a covenant with the people. The Jews, as they will come to be called. The covenant the Lord made is with David, and His concern is with keeping Jerusalem because that is where God chose to place His name; Christ Jesus. Dispensationalists falsely claim that it is the Jewish people who God chose. But it was always a winnowing, and of Judah He chose David. The city of Jerusalem was chosen before there even was a tribe of Judah. Before Abram was Abraham. God had a purpose and a plan and it was that the Son be made flesh and dwell among us and be put to death in the same place Abraham willingly offered Isaac by faith. Genesis 22:7-8 And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering? And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together. The seed of Abraham, that would bless the whole world, was Jesus. The son of David, the King that would rule forever, is Christ. God preserved the one tribe not because of their own righteousness; Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in mine eyes, and to keep my statutes and my judgments. They failed to hold up their end of the covenant made with their fathers in the wilderness, that had they kept the commandments of the Lord, they would be His people, and He would be their God. Hebrews 8:7-9 For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. Reject Dispensationalism

With King Solomon dead, his son Rehoboam goes up to Shechem, the place Abraham talked to God when he entered Canaan, where Joseph was buried, and where Israel had dwelt. And there he went to be anointed king. But Jeroboam, son of Nebat, to whom the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite spoke the word of God, that he should be king over the 10 tribes in Israel, came with the men of Israel to challenge the heir of David. Ahijah had told Jeroboam, a mighty man who was put in charge over the children of Joseph, (Manassas and Ephraim) by Solomon, that God had ordained that the kingdom be rent as a garment. And gave the covenant that God would bless him as king over Israel, excluding Judah; if thou wilt hearken unto all that I command thee, and wilt walk in my ways, and do that is right in my sight, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with thee, and build thee a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel unto thee. Solomon hearing this, sought to have Jeroboam killed, and so he had fled to Egypt. Returning from that exile he led the men to confront Rehoboam, saying that his father Solomon had made the men of Israel to carry a heavy yoke. To perform grievous service for the King. In 1 Samuel 8, when the people went to Samuel demanding a king, the Lord spoke through Samuel warning the people that a king would take their sons for chariots and horsemen and manservants, and their daughters to be cooks, and their vineyards for himself and their income by tax. Solomon had indeed done all this. Was it unfair, given they demanded a king over Israel and were warned? Maybe. Though Solomon also brought them great wealth, and rest in the land, and made Israel great among nations. Obviously, Jeroboam had ulterior motives as well, seeking the approval of Israel that he may be king, and making Rehoboam look weak; Either relent and pledge to lighten the yoke, deny their claims and look uncaring to the people, or to react angrily and rash. This difficult situation was one the Lord had caused, that He might perform His saying which the Lord spoke by Ahijah. Ironically, this was one that the wisdom of Solomon would perhaps have been able to navigate. But lacking that wisdom, Rehoboam asks for 3 days and he sought counsel from his father's elder advisors and from his own young men in his court. The elder gave moderate advice; speak good words and promise to serve them, and the people will be yours. The younger gave harsh advice, that as King he would increase the burden. That his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins against them. There is debate among Christians as to which advice was right, and if the men of Israel had a valid complaint. Should we heed the hoary head of experience, or the brash and young? But really, the scripture tells us the Lord had made this a no win situation to begin with. Rehoboam was going to lose the 10 northern tribes regardless of what he did. He could have shamed his own father by conceding their complaints, and been shown to be weak as Saul, seeking after the approval of the masses. The advice of the elders wasn't much better than that of the young men that he chose to follow. And so he answered them roughly and Jeroboam speaks for Israel and says they will have nothing making them loyal to Judah and the throne of David. They depart, every man for their tents and leave the Kingdom divided. Rent as a garment, never to be united again. And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was come again, that they sent and called him unto the congregation, and made him king over all Israel: there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only. Once this occurs, Rehoboam assembles his men, including the remnant of Benjamin that remained inside the territory of Judah, and sought to go out to war against Israel. But the Lord speaks through the prophet Shemaiah, saying not to do this thing, and slay brothers. That the divided kingdom had come from Him. And so they stand down. Meanwhile, in the North, Jeroboam realizes that with the Temple in Jerusalem, and the pilgrimages the men were required to take under the ordinances of God, three times a year, plus all the sacrifices and services of the Levites there, that eventually he would lose the hearts of the people and they would turn towards Rehoboam because of the Lord. And so, forsaking the word of God given him by Ahijah the Shilonite, the King sets up altars to golden calves, one in Bethel, and the other in Dan. In the South and one in the far north. He set up high places and created his own feasts and made requirements for worship at the same time as those given by the Lord. And further, he made priests of the lowest of people, not of the Levites. Generally in scripture what is being described are reprobates. Sodomites and the worst manner of people. Sons of Belial. Creating his own false religion, claiming to be worshiping the "god that took them out of Egypt," while worshiping the golden calf, idolatry. Setting up his own feast days. Using an unqualified priesthood made up of the lowest people, all for political power...This is a picture of the apostate Roman Catholic Church. It will eventually lead to the utter destruction of Israel.

2 Kings 22 Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty and one years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath. 2 And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in all the way of David his father, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left.... 2 Kings 23:1-27 And the king sent, and they gathered unto him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem. 2 And the king went up into the house of the Lord, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the people, both small and great: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the Lord. 3 And the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord, and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant. 4 And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the door, to bring forth out of the temple of the Lord all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven: and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto Bethel. 5 And he put down the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places round about Jerusalem; them also that burned incense unto Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the host of heaven. 6 And he brought out the grove from the house of the Lord, without Jerusalem, unto the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped it small to powder, and cast the powder thereof upon the graves of the children of the people. 7 And he brake down the houses of the sodomites, that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove. 8 And he brought all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba, and brake down the high places of the gates that were in the entering in of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which were on a man's left hand at the gate of the city. 9 Nevertheless the priests of the high places came not up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, but they did eat of the unleavened bread among their brethren. 10 And he defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech. 11 And he took away the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the entering in of the house of the Lord, by the chamber of Nathanmelech the chamberlain, which was in the suburbs, and burned the chariots of the sun with fire. 12 And the altars that were on the top of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, did the king beat down, and brake them down from thence, and cast the dust of them into the brook Kidron. 13 And the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mount of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had builded for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Zidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon, did the king defile. 14 And he brake in pieces the images, and cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of men. 15 Moreover the altar that was at Bethel, and the high place which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, had made, both that altar and the high place he brake down, and burned the high place, and stamped it small to powder, and burned the grove. 16 And as Josiah turned himself, he spied the sepulchres that were there in the mount, and sent, and took the bones out of the sepulchres, and burned them upon the altar, and polluted it, according to the word of the Lord which the man of God proclaimed, who proclaimed these words. 17 Then he said, What title is that that I see? And the men of the city told him, It is the sepulchre of the man of God, which came from Judah, and proclaimed these things that thou hast done against the altar of Bethel. 18 And he said, Let him alone; let no man move his bones. So they let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet that came out of Samaria. 19 And all the houses also of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, Josiah took away, and did to them according to all the acts that he had done in Bethel. 20 And he slew all the priests of the high places that were there upon the altars, and burned men's bones upon them, and returned to Jerusalem. 21 And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the passover unto the Lord your God, as it is written in the book of this covenant. 22 Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah; 23 But in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, wherein this passover was holden to the Lord in Jerusalem. 24 Moreover the workers with familiar spirits, and the wizards, and the images, and the idols, and all the abominations that were spied in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, did Josiah put away, that he might perform the words of the law which were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the Lord. 25 And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to the Lord with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him. 26 Notwithstanding the Lord turned not from the fierceness of his great wrath, wherewith his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal. 27 And the Lord said, I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and will cast off this city Jerusalem which I have chosen, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there. Now the years of the reign of Jeroboam in the Northern Kingdom of Israel were 928–907 BC. King Josiah of Judah reigned for 31 years in 640–609 BC. So the prophet of the Lord came up from Judah to Bethel to preach against Jeroboam roughly 300 years before the prophecy was fulfilled. Jeroboam was burning incense upon the altar he had set up in Bethel, for Israel to worship the false god the King had established to keep them from the Temple in Jerusalem, Judea. One of the two golden calves Jeroboam had set up. Burning incense and candles and making offerings of food and drink to false gods is considered serving them in the Bible. Make no mistake that the Catholic rationalizations about their "venerating" idols and not worshiping them. God's word is clear it is serving them in any way, and sacrifices made to them are an abomination to the Lord. The nameless prophet sent by God to Bethel cried against the altar in the word of the Lord, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the Lord; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men's bones shall be burnt upon thee. And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This is the sign which the Lord hath spoken; Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out. The king thrust out his hand to order his men to seize the prophet, and his hand withered. Astonished, he begs the prophet to restore him, and the Lord does. The altar itself splits in two, and the ashes of the animals sacrificed there spill upon the ground, just as the man of God had prophesied. King Jeroboam offers the prophet a reward, and to come with him to his palace to eat, but the prophet declines saying that the word of God that came upon him said not to eat bread or drink water in Israel, not until he had returned to Judah and not to return the same way in which he had come. Now there was an old prophet in Bethel, and his sons tell him of the miraculous things that transpired and the sign proving the prophet from Judea was truly of the Lord. And the old prophet wished to meet him and perhaps to gain something from him, just by being near someone used so mightily by God. So he sets out on his ass and finds the young prophet by the way and invited him to come to his home and eat. When the young prophet tells the old that he may not because the Lord had spoken thusly to him, the old prophet lied. He claimed that God had given him His word to come and bring him to his home to eat. The younger man believes him, and despite knowing the word of the Lord firsthand, goes with the older man. This is a picture of something all too common in Christianity today. A young believer, with the word of God at his fingertips, yet trusting the word of an older man, and believing their lies. Often, we seek understanding or hear something pleasing from a false teacher, and rather than searching the scriptures to see if it was so, we allow ourselves to be taken along for a ride. At the old man's house, they eat and drink. And the Spirit of the Lord comes upon the old prophet, perhaps for the first time; And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the Lord, and hast not kept the commandment which the Lord thy God commanded thee, But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which the Lord did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers. The young prophet sets out on an ass given by the old prophet, and doesn't go far before a lion sets up on him, killing him. And the ass he rode up on and the lion itself stood by his corpse in the road. Men seeing this reported back to Bethel, and the old prophet hearing this is distraught. He goes and takes his body and has it buried in his own grave. And when he was dying, he ordered his bones to be buried with the younger man's in the sepulchre. 300 or so years later, Israel was already destroyed and scattered, the land now called Samaria. And King Josiah sits on the throne of Judah. He was a good king and upon finding and reading and believing the law of God, he sets up on making things right in the land. And so the prophecy is fulfilled, that the false priests, base men of the lesser sort, sons of Belial, and digs up the bones of the sepulchres that were buried there, and burned them upon the altar, polluting it. Josiah fulfils all of the prophecy, and buys a little time for Judah, which was to be punished by the Lord for the wickedness of Josiah's grandfather, King Manasseh. A story for another day. But the bones of the prophet and the old prophet buried with him, Josiah leaves undisturbed. Today's study on 1 Kings 13 is a banger, one of the best chapters in 1 Kings.

Here in 1 Kings 14, we are given the end to the first Kings of the divided kingdom. Jeroboam, King of Israel, to whom the 10 tribes were given by the Lord and Rehoboam, son of Solomon, who ruled in Jerusalem over Judah. Jeroboam's son is ill, and so the king recalling the prophet Ahijah, sends his wife in disguise to Shiloh in hopes of finding out what would become of their son. The Lord tells the old, blinded prophet her identity and he preaches to her the end of Jeroboam's house and of all Israel, because of the sin Jeroboam had brought to Israel with the golden calves and the false worship and priesthood he set up in God's name. The son, he says, will die as she returns to him and all Israel will mourn. The child will be buried in a grave, properly, because there is found some good thing toward the Lord God of Israel. I take this as another proof text for the age of innocence, that God doesn't hold children who haven't yet come to the knowledge of sin guilty for the sin of their fathers. But for whatever reason, the prophecy is not kind for Jeroboam and his line. They will die in the streets and in the fields and be eaten of dogs and of carrion birds. And all Israel will be destroyed and scattered, because the Lord will give all Israel up, cast out. Give them over to reprobation. Being rejected of the Lord. The mother returns and her son dies as told of the Lord, and all Israel mourns. Jeroboam eventually does and is replaced by his son Nadab. The rest of his story is told in Chronicles, God willing we will get there soon. Rehoboam, King over Judah, son of Solomon, reigned in Jerusalem 17 years, and under his leadership Judah too did evil in the sight of the Lord, provoking God to jealousy with their sins. They also built up altars, groves and high places to worship strange gods. And they allowed sodomites in the land to commit the abominations of those nations the Lord had driven out to give the promised land to the children of Israel. It is important to note that whenever people fall away from worshiping the true God and take up false gods and worship of idols, even under the guise of worshiping Him, it provokes the Lord. But allowing sodomites to exist and commit their filthy abominations is even more wicked and God punishes nations engaged in this behavior. Judah was being protected for His name's sake, the coming of Christ and for the sake of that promise to David that was fulfilled in Jesus. But the Lord was wroth with the people and their king. America is currently coasting on the blessings bestowed on our forefathers for their right worship of God, and the liberty found in Christ. And rapidly headed to judgment for idolatry and false religion, and the sodomites in the land. The Lord took away the treasures in the Temple set by Solomon. All the gold, even the shields set in place by Rehoboam's father. The King sets a cheap imitation of the shields, made instead of brass. A humiliation. Again, the rest of the story of Rehoboam is found in Chronicles.

King Asa removed the groves and altars and idols and drove the sodomites from the land. Amen. We see the cycle of good leaders followed by bad in Judah and worse and good being established. God preserves Judah for David's sake and because of Jerusalem, where Christ will be crucified. Not for the people's sake. Not because of any covenant made with their fathers in the wilderness. Israel however keeps spiralling, waxing worse and worse. And their ally Syria is bought off by Asa, and turned against Israel. Eventually the Assyrian Empire will destroy the northern kingdom, because God has no reason to regard them as a nation. Pray for a King like Asa, leadership that prolongs our days and brings God's favor on our land. Especially this Independence Day weekend.

Joshua 6:26 And Joshua adjured them at that time, saying, Cursed be the man before the Lord, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it. 1 Kings continues, and shows that during the reign of Asa the good in Judah, the Northern Kingdom of Israel continues its slide into sin and heathen abominations, each king more wicked than the last. Baasha is preached against by Jesu, being cursed to the same fate as Jeroboam, his posterity cut off, and while his son Elah takes the throne, his rule is short lived. His captain, Zimri executes a coup, killing Selah and every male descendent of Baasha, fulfilling the prophecy against him. But even as the Lord uses Zimri to do His will, he punishes Zimri for his sin of rebellion. Omri, the captain of the host on battle against the Philistines is made king by the people, and he goes against Zimri and destroys him and the capitol, the palace burning down on the would-be king, as punishment from God for his sin. It is interesting that God allows evil men to do the evil in their hearts in order to use them to His own purpose. The Lord gives us free will, and yet knowing beginning from the end makes all under His will. Omri faces a civil war upon his succession, from Tibni the son of Ginath. He defeats Tibni, and those of Israel that followed him are slain. Omri builds the city of Samaria, which will serve as the capital of the kingdom, and become the name of the territory once God destroys Israel. Of course Omri is worse than the previous wicked kings, and like Jeroboam causes all Israel to sin with false gods. And he dies and Ahab his son reigned in his stead. Ahab takes for a wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him. Israel becomes as the Canaanites that were driven out before them. Ahab builds altars and groves to Baal, not even pretending that they worshiped the true God in their idolatry as Jeroboam had. This progression is very similar to the way false religion such as Catholicism rises up, and then is used by the beast to bring the people to worship him in the end times. Then we are told that Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, just as Joshua had prophesied at the destruction of Jericho centuries earlier. Hiel sacrifices his own sons, killing them to rebuild the ancient city. An abomination before the Lord.

In 1 Kings 17 we are introduced to the great prophet of the Northern Kingdom, Elijah the Tishbite. Elijah is a key figure in scripture, having been prophesied as coming in the day of the Lord, a voice crying out in the wilderness, fulfilled by John the Baptist. He appeared with Moses at the transfiguration of Christ Jesus. Some believe he is one of the two witnesses to come after the Tribulation and the Rapture, during the pouring out of the wrath of God. The witnesses having the power to shut up the heavens from rain, as we see Elijah do in the name of the Lord in this chapter. Prophesying the word of God to King Ahab, declaring a drought upon the land for their wickedness, God sends His prophet to hide beyond Jordan. At the brook of Cherith, the Lord feeds him by ravens, quenched by the brook as long as it flows. When even the brook is dried up, the Lord sends him down to Zidon, and to a widow and her son. Arriving there, he sees the widow and asks for water and bread. The widow confesses that she had just enough grain and oil to make a final meal for her and her son. Elijah tells her that by the word of the Lord God of Israel that the barrel of meal and cruse of oil will not run out until the end of the drought. And this miracle plays out just as he had said. And so during the wrath of God upon the wicked, so are we kept alive by His grace. The word of God is like the meal and oil, the bread that never spoils or wastes. Never depleted. The promise of life by faith, that we will always be provided for. That we have eternal life in His word. And even as her son becomes ill and died, Elijah calls upon the name of the Lord and he is risen again. The pictures of the word of the living God, being provided for, tended by ravens as they were angels, made alive again by the Lord. The living God. The wrath upon the wicked. The reward for the faithful. This is one of my favorite chapters in the Old Testament.

The great story of Elijah vs the prophets of Baalim, even the prophets of the groves who ate at Queen Jezebel's table. God sends Elijah back to the Northern Kingdom of Israel after 3 and a half years of drought and famine. Luke 4:25 But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land Ahab, having been searching for Elijah this whole time to get the prophet to undo the curse Israel was under is off searching again for Elijah, and with him his chief steward Obadiah. They separate, and Elijah comes upon Obadiah who knows him well. Obadiah is a saved believer in the Lord, yet he works for the wicked king and queen. Elijah tells Obadiah to fetch Ahab and tell him he's returned, and Obadiah fears for his life. He has been, this entire time, hiding his faith, just as he has his the prophets of the Lord in caves to keep them from Jezebel. Rather than standing up to evil, preaching against Baal and sin, to bring Israel back to the Lord, they've been shut up in caves and Obadiah's paranoia at the possibility of Elijah ghosting him shows the level of fear of man, and not the fear of the Lord he claims to have. This is similar to the way many Christians today hide their faith and fear tribulation and persecution more than they fear God. God may have used those hundred prophets to bring about revival. But they hid rather than face death. Matthew 10:28 And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. But Elijah assures Obadiah he will speak to the king that day, and when they return Ahab accuses Elijah of being responsible for the famine. Elijah corrects the wicked king, that it is he and his father's sin that brought it about. And Elijah challenged Ahab to being all Israel together and the prophets of Baal, and meet him at Mt Carmel. There Elijah challenged the people of Israel; How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. Then, as now, people generally are unwilling to commit to faith. They go along to get along and put off the choice of salvation or damnation if they can, usually to their own destruction. The purpose of the word of the Lord is to bring people the choice and force them to decide; do they want to accept the truth? Eternal life in Christ Jesus, admitting they are sinners deserving death and taking the gracious gift of God? Or do they want to reject God and be given up, and given over. Twice-dead. There are saved people in the world. There are slightly fewer reprobates (although that number seems to be growing). There is a vast majority of those who are caught between, often and in indecision. Soul-winning, giving the gospel to the unbelievers forces them to make this choice. And many receive it gladly. But others, it's the final straw before they decide they do not wish to retain God in their knowledge. And it's too late, reprobate. Elijah is putting this same decision in the hands of the people. And as a sign, Elijah calls for two pyres to be set up, two altars, with bullocks upon each as sacrifice. He challenges the 450 priests of Baal to call down fire from their god, to burn up the sacrifice. And these priests called and called and danced and prayed and from morning until noon cried out 'O Baal, hear us!' But there was, of course, no answer. And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked. And so until evening they intensified their futile and vain efforts, even cutting themselves as the demonic and pagan do, and of course no answer came and no fire was called down from their dead gods. And Elijah repaired the altar to the Lord that had been torn down, and took 12 stones for each tribe, representing the tribes of Jacob to whom the Lord had come. And he made a trench about the altar and had them fill it with water and soak the wood and upon the sacrifice. Four times he had them drench the area. And Elijah said; Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel, and that I am thy servant, and that I have done all these things at thy word. And fire fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice, the wood and stones and dust, and evaporated the water in the trench. And the people who had gathered bowed falling on their faces and said "The Lord, He is the God!" This is a picture of the end times, and the fire from heaven and the sure return of Christ, when every knee shall bow and tongue confess that He is the living God. And while the people were in a fervor from this mighty sign, Elijah tells them to take and kill all the prophets of Baal, and they do, at the broom Kishon. Elijah, having proved his point in an epic fashion by the mighty hand of the Lord, turned to King Ahab and says; Get thee up, eat and drink; for there is a sound of abundance of rain. Elijah then takes himself, and goes up Mt Carmel, and waits. Sending a servant 7 times to go look towards the sea. And it came to pass on the 7th time there raised a cloud from the sea. At that, Elijah sends a message to Ahab to hurry and get home that the rain not stop him. And a great rain fell as the king returned to Jezreel. Elijah running to the entrance by the hand of the Lord, beating the King and his chariots as the rains came down. Epic story of faith and the power of God. The people witnessed a great miracle, and see the skies open up. They even slew the prophets of Baal. But as we will see, this zeal didn't extend to a revival at all. And Elijah will have more challenges before him.

And so, Elijah the prophet of Israel, fresh from being used by God unto mighty works, flees from the wrath of Jezebel, wife of King Ahab. Elijah shut up the heavens from rain, causing three and a half years of famine by the word of the Lord. He was fed by ravens, and by meal and oil that never ran out or spoiled. He called upon the Lord and saw the widow's son raised from the dead. By faith, Elijah returned to Israel and confronted the king and the 450 prophets of Baal, and by the word of the Lord called down fire from Heaven to show the children of Israel the power of the living God. They slew the prophets of Baal. And by the word of the Lord, rains came and returned to the land. During the challenge to the prophets of Baal, Elijah claimed to them that he alone still followed the Lord and against the 450. He met Obadiah, who kept his faith secret for fear of the king and hid prophets of God in a cave, an act of cowardice compared to mighty Elijah. And yet, Elijah fled. And went beyond Judah, to Horeb. Mount Sinai, where God appeared before Moses with the Law, and lived in a cave. The triumph that should have led to revival brought depression and fear in the prophet. He wished to end his life. He says: I have been very jealous for the Lord God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away. Again, saying he was alone in his zeal for the Lord as he had boasted to the priests of Baalim. But the Lord corrects him here; Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him. In our Christian life, even after seeing the power of God on us and having great triumphs of faith, it isn't unusual to feel a sense of letdown afterwards. To have doubts. To feel alone. But the Lord works in more than us. And we are never alone. There is always a righteous remnant, and despair isn't an option even in the face of tribulation. God has use for us yet. And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. The Lord tells Elijah to stand out before Him. And a mighty wind passes, and an earthquake and a great fire; but the Lord is not in these things. Instead, God is the still small voice, speaking to us. Asking, What doest thou here? We find the still small voice speaking to us the word of God, asking what are we doing? He has plans for us. For Elijah it is to go forth and anoint his successor, and a King over Israel and a King over Syria. Great tasks for the glory of the Lord. His purpose for us may not be as bold and as great. But if we search for Him by faith, and listen to that small still voice, who is to say what He calls us to do isn't going to have impact that results in great things for the cause of Christ?

Now we are here in 1 Kings 20, and if you remember in 1 Kings 19 the Lord had told Elijah to go forth and anoint his successor as prophet over Israel, Elisha which he had done, and to go anoint Hazael to be king over Syria, and to anoint Jehu to be king over Israel. We see in chapter 20 that Benhadad was currently King over Syria, and he was besieging the capital Samaria. Ahab conceded to him, and had agreed to pay a ransom of his wives, children, gold and silver. But Benhadad decided in Ahab's weakness to press for more, to take whatever his men wanted as spoil. Ahab consults with his leadership and sends word that he will not agree. Benhadad sets his men in array against the city, and goes and gets drunk with his princes. Meanwhile, a prophet of the Lord comes to Ahab and the word of the Lord is that He will deliver the multitude of Syrians into Ahab's hands that day, to show him that He is the Lord. And so Ahab does as he is told, and sends out his small band of princes and their men. Benhadad, drunk and overconfident allows the men to approach. And the young men, by the power of God slay the Syrians and pursued them even unto Damascus. The prophet tells Ahab that Benhadad will return with his armies in a year. For the king of Syria's advisors tell him that the God of Israel is just a god of the high places, not the valley, and so send his armies to the plains and defeat Israel. God in His wrath tells Ahab again to go out against the multitudes and He will deliver them that they may know He is the Lord, and once again the inferior forces of Israel destroy the Syrians in battle. Finding Benhadad, the king begs for mercy and Ahab grants it, angering the Lord. A prophet with the burden of the Lord tells another man to hit him. The man refuses and the Lord sends a lion to devour him. A second man (wisely😂) agrees. The prophet, battered dusts himself up and lay in the way for the king. Ahab comes along and he tells the king a story, that he was sworn to keep a man, who escaped. And now the prophet claimed, he owed his life for it. Ahab judges that it be so, and the prophet reveals himself to say this was actually Ahab's situation, for the Lord demanded Benhadad's destruction. But for a ransom and an appeal, Ahab had spared him. This God would take his life, and Israel for Syria. The Lord makes plans and sees them through, while a man compromises.

Leviticus 25:13-16 In the year of this jubile ye shall return every man unto his possession. And if thou sell ought unto thy neighbour, or buyest ought of thy neighbour's hand, ye shall not oppress one another: According to the number of years after the jubile thou shalt buy of thy neighbour, and according unto the number of years of the fruits he shall sell unto thee: According to the multitude of years thou shalt increase the price thereof, and according to the fewness of years thou shalt diminish the price of it: for according to the number of the years of the fruits doth he sell unto thee. Now Naboth had a vineyard, and Ahab sought to possess it. But Naboth's land was the possession of his inheritance. According to God's law, while he may have chosen to lease it to the king until the jubilee, it wasn't right for him to sell it. Ahab was despondent at being denied the thing he covered, and his wicked wife Jezebel came up with a scheme to please him. She called for a feast in Ahab's name, with Naboth as an honored guest. Then she sent two sons of Belial, reprobates, in to bear false witness against the Jezreelite. The people, believing the lewd men of the baser sort, took and stoned poor Naboth to death. And the word of the Lord came upon Elijah, and the prophet went up to Ahab, who saw him as his enemy, always bringing bad tidings from the Lord. Elijah tells the king that because of his sin, and the murder of an innocent man for his covetousness, that his lineage will be cut off, as Jeroboam and Baasha before him. All those men, them that pisseth against the wall, will be slain and the place where Naboth was stoned, the dogs will lick up Ahab and his kin's blood. Jezebel killed by the wall of Jezreel, and eaten by dogs.

Jehoshaphat, King of Judah was a weak but godly king, walking in the ways of Asa. But Ahab of Israel was wicked all of his days, walking in the way of Jeroboam. When Ahab was at peace with Judah and Jehoshaphat came together with him, Ahab's thoughts turned to war. Ahab had peace with Syria and its king that Ahab compromised with, in defiance of God's will. But he saw opportunity in his alliance with Judah and asked Jehoshaphat if he would come with him in war against the Syrians to reclaim disputed land. Out of kinship, Jehoshaphat agrees, but wants to first seek counsel from a prophet of the Lord. Ahab sends for his prophets of Baal, even 400 of them, who all speak encouraging words and flattery. What Ahab wants to hear. A godly ruler seeks the word of God. A wicked ruler seeks to have their pride and ego stroked. Jehoshaphat asks if there isn't at least a prophet of the Lord to ask, and Ahab begrudgingly sends for Micaiah, whom the king says is his enemy, because he preached against Ahab and didn't hold back from delivering the word of God. Many leaders today surround themselves with yes men. With pastors and religious leaders who all too willingly will provide a wicked ruler with encouragement and support and claim God is with them. Using flattery and deceit, they convince these evil leaders, and themselves, that God is blessing them. But Micaiah comes, and while he at first just parrots the false prophets, Ahab knows the game and asks for him to speak truth. And the truth is that Israel will be scattered without a shepherd, because Ahab will die in battle. Further, Micaiah says that an angel of the Lord came as a lying spirit to put falsehoods in the mouths of the prophets of Baal, to feed the delusions of Ahab. To lead him to destruction. Ahab has Micaiah jailed until his return (a return the prophet stakes his veracity on not happening). And the kings set off to battle. But Ahab disguised himself, hoping to escape being the target of the Syrians. Jehoshaphat goes out to battle in his robes, unashamed. There's symbolism there, the godly king unafraid in battle to proclaim the truth of God and place his faith in Him. But an arrow finds Ahab anyway, and always the king and the words of the prophet are fulfilled, every Israelite returning to their homes, leaderless. I feel very strongly that the lessons of Ahab and the other kings of Israel, who get worse and worse as they go headlong to their ultimate destruction, are being played out this week. I think we are witness to a very similar tale. I think God sends warning to these wicked kings, the time and again. Maybe by word of a prophet. Maybe by the near miss of death. And most, being wicked and prideful, seek rather the comforting words of false prophets guided by lying spirits, feeding their strong delusions.

Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that thou sendest to enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron? We see a King of Israel, Ahaziah son of Ahab, wounded and dying, sending his servants to inquire of Baalzebub, the false god of Ekron, to see what his fate would be. Imagine, an injured leader of a group of people called after His name, going after false gods, to seek their counsel and blessing. But the angel of the Lord comes to Elijah, and tells him to meet the servants of the king and to tell them that because of this evil of going after strange gods, he will surely die. Hearing this ill omen of the word of God angers the king, and he sends out a band of 50 and their captains tell Elijah to come with them, oh man of God. Elijah says, If I be a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty, and fire rains down consuming them. And again, another band comes for him, and again Elijah calls down fire from Heaven and kills them all. The third time, the captain of the men falls to his knees, begging the prophet to not kill them. And the angel of the Lord tells Elijah to go with them, no harm would come to him. And so King Ahaziah dies as the word of the Lord said, and with no heir. The line of Ahab cut off. The name of his successor, Jehoram is confusing because both Jehoram of Israel and Jehoram of Judah are in the same passage, and both reigned at the same time.

The passing of the mantel of Elijah to Elisha. Elijah being taken by a whirlwind, and the chariots of fire that are the Lord's. A double-measure of the Spirit upon the younger prophet, who was anointed by Elijah under God's instruction. I believe the two prophets of Revelation will be Moses and Elijah. The same as appeared with Jesus at His transfiguration upon the mount. Who can call down plagues and cause drought, and fire comes from their mouths to consume any who seek to harm them. Some believe Enoch will be there in place of Moses, because his death was as Elijah's, not sleeping with his fathers, but taken up to heaven. Regardless, we should strive to have half the Spirit of these men of God. To have the faith that parts waters and calls down fire and can heal waters and curse unruly and wicked children.

And so Jehoram, son of Ahab reigned over Israel and he put away the idols of Baal that his father and Jezebel worshipped, but he kept the false religion established by Jeroboam. It isn't enough to rid yourself of false gods. It isn't enough to turn from the idols of this world and the blasphemous images and wicked things that are obviously against God. Jehoram did the right thing but he kept the false religion that claimed to be of the God of Israel. Just as the golden calf of Aaron was said to be the same god that carried them out of Egypt, Jeroboam made like images and said they represented the same gods. Aaron called the children of Israel to a feast for the Lord in front of the calf, where they worshiped and offered sacrifices. Jeroboam created feasts to the Lord and idols to be worshipped in His name and sacrifices made by the priesthood he'd created to serve him. They mixed paganism with the Lord and it was an abomination to God. The word tells us how He wants it to be and by doing this, these leaders caused the people of God to sin. And both Aaron and Jeroboam did it for political reasons. To maintain power and control over a stiff-necked and rebellious people. The false apostate church of Roman Catholicism is the same. They created their own idols, feast days, religious practices, rites and sacraments, instituted their own priesthood, sacrifice to idols they tell their followers represent God.
