He destroys that altar and the image where the prophet of old had come and preached against the first king of divided Israel, foretelling of this day, which we covered here. He destroys the houses of the sodomites, kills the evil priests and tears down the places where children were sacrificed by passing them through the fire. And at each place, the king not only grinds them to dust, but scatters their ashes and desecrated the places with the ashes of dead men's bones. When we read the list of places, and see that not only evil kings, but "good kings," such as Solomon, had put up these abominations. That the worship of false gods had permeated nearly everything, including the temple and the gates of the city. A little leaven had leavened the whole lump. But Josiah purges it with fire. Notwithstanding the Lord turned not from the fierceness of his great wrath, wherewith his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal. And the Lord said, I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and will cast off this city Jerusalem which I have chosen, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there. The revival and zeal for the Lord shown by King Josiah led God to grant his reign a measure of peace and delayed their judgement against them. But it did not prevent God's wrath from being poured out eventually. And Josiah knew by the prophecy given to him that the judgment was inevitable. But he still did that which was right and was tearful and full of regret for the evil done in the land by his fathers and the people. Contrast that with when Hezekiah said unto Isaiah, who had given the same warning; Good is the word of the Lord which thou hast spoken. And he said, Is it not good, if peace and truth be in my days? Hezekiah, a good king as well who did fear the Lord, accepted the judgment and was glad it wasn't in his day, but did not utterly purge the land as Josiah did. He was relieved that the wrath was held back, and that his children would suffer the consequences rather than him. This mentality is common among what is called the "baby boomer" generation, many of whom recognizing that the consequences for their sin would lead to judgment, took comfort in the fact that they wouldn't be here to see it. And it is no wonder that the false doctrine of a pre-tribulation rapture was so appealing to them. They rested in the delusion that while the nation may be going to Hell in a hand basket, and that judgment was coming, that they didn't need to worry. They would be spared any trouble when it "got really bad." They didn't make any effort to turn back to the Lord with zeal and lead a revival in hopes of turning back God's wrath or buying more time. They said Is it not good, if peace and truth be in my days? Then you see another generation come, who like Josiah, look to the word of God and understand that the sodomites and the idols and the failure to walk in the statutes of the Lord is the cause of the judgment, and as righteous as God's indignation against us is, we still have a duty to follow His commandments, even if it means facing great tribulation. To lament the wickedness done and to preach and act against it. And to proclaim the word of God and His righteousness to the world. In season or out of season. It is a different attitude, and one that the old guard of Christians often resent and look down upon, because it convicts them for their inaction, or leads them to special pleading, saying "I tried ...it's not my fault." I would rather have the spirit of Josiah rending his clothes and seeking after the Lord than of Hezekiah's acquiescence and pride in his earthly wealth. The nature of revival, of proclaiming the truth of God to all men, to soul-winning and contending for the faith, and challenging false ways and compromise, is that it forces people to choose. We often talk of God's constant winnowing, the separation of the wheat from the chaff, which is shown throughout the Bible, but the truth is, God is constantly giving men a choice. He is offering us the truth and life, and placing the choice on our hearts. Deuteronomy 30:15-20 See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it. But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them. I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them. Joshua 24:15 And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. Forcing people to make this choice is the purpose of revival. It is the fruit of preaching the word and going out to win souls. It forces people to choose. Some will hear the word and be converted unto eternal life. But many will reject Christ and decide to harden their hearts and hold the truth in unrighteousness. The revival led by King Josiah was short-lived. When he died in battle, his sons were made king, first Jehoahaz, who was then carried away to Egypt, and then Eliakim aka Jehoiakim. Both did evil in the sight of the Lord. In our study of Jeremiah, we covered these kings and the wickedness of Judah in their day, when Babylon came and made Jerusalem a desolation, fulfilling the word of God. They did evil in the sight of the Lord and willfully and knowingly turned to the sins of their fathers and the abominations that they did. The Lord giving Judah one last chance to know the truth, to have it read to them by Josiah, and acted upon by his hand, meant that while many believed unto righteousness, most chose death. So that when God's wrath came upon them, they were without excuse. Soul-winning is what we are called to do, but the more we do it, the more the gospel is proclaimed to every creature, and gone out to all the world, the more people will become reprobate. Even our own families. At some point, the fullness of the Gentiles will come in. Everyone who will be saved will be, and the rest will choose to worship the beast and take his mark, and condemn themselves. Our job is to go work the harvest. To force the issue. To make people decide if they choose life or death. Luke 12:51-53 Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three. The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. This idea of division is confusing for some, but it is something that I think saved Christians understand by the Spirit, even if they don't intellectually. We all have had loved ones, family, friends, who we have shared the gospel with and given the good news to, but we hesitate to push the issue. To bring them to make a decision. To force them to either accept or reject the truth that's saved us. The grace that we stand on. Sometimes, it's embarrassment at our own sins being evident to those who know us best. Fear of being exposed as a hypocrite. But often, it is the understanding that pushing the issue may push them away. That in trying to save them, we could lose them. And that nagging feeling that if we do, we lose them forever and that they will condemn themselves. Christians are often so afraid that our loved ones will perish and be damned, but at the same time are scared we could be the cause of it. We love them more than the truth of Christ and our indecision and fear of making them choose comes from that. And the spiritual discernment to know it may be their final decision, reprobating themselves. Matthew 10:37 He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

2 Chronicles 7:14 if my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. We see throughout the Old Testament that the people of Israel, given every advantage by the blessings of God, His protection, the law, the ordinances, the faith in the Christ to come delivered by the Spirit unto the prophets, and yet they continually turn to Idolatry, building altars and groves, burning incense to the hosts of heaven, bowing down before strange gods, passing their children through the fire; killing them as a sacrifice to Baal, and tolerating the houses of the sodomites which do the abominations of the nations God has driven out of the promised land. And God's wrath was kindled against the people. And He swore destruction of the northern kingdom of Israel and Judah. But good kings came occasionally, and did what was right in the sight of the Lord, and when they did, they bought their people reprieve, as God repented for a time of the evil He was to do. The Bible is clear in these accounts that not only did they tear down altars and kill the priests worshipping idols and burning incense to false gods (ahem RCC), but the sodomites were killed and removed from the land. As we enter into June, it is important that we who call ourselves by His name, Christians, stand firmly opposed to the sodomites and all those who defy the judgment of God. Like Josiah, who when he read the book of the law found in the Temple, rent his clothes and called for revival, being moved by the word of God, we must do the same. In season or out of season. Even if we are persecuted and attacked for it. We must call our evil when it is presented to us and have no fellowship with the sons of Belial. If there are open queers in your political organizations or in your communities, spreading their filth, stand up and speak against it, in the name of Jesus Christ. Cast them out where you are able. Especially if they have crept in to your church, especially if they claim to be "reformed." And if these places cast their lot with the sodomites, and put you out instead, rejoice. Go willingly. Better to be like Micah, the prophet, who spoke God's truth, even to kings, as all other prophets spoke flattering lies to get along.

As 2 Kings begins to wrap up, with the captivity of Judah into Babylon, which we covered extensively during the study on Jeremiah, we see that God's wrath will not be delayed forever. Even as we read through the fall of the Northern Kingdom of Israel, you might wonder at how long God gave them to come around before utterly destroying them. But to Judah, it really only took the kingdom of Manasseh before the wrath came. And even then, Judah would ultimately be spared for Christ's sake, and captivity ending after 70 years. In a like manner, the unsaved are often given chance after chance, and seemingly get away with their sins, but are condemned in death to Hell for eternity, while the saved, to whom much is given, are chastened by the Lord, but kept as sons for His sake, by His grace. We really see this in the final chapter, tomorrow

The final chapter, 2 Kings 25 brings us up to the beginning of the captivity of Judah into Babylon, which we also covered in the study of the major prophet of this time, Jeremiah. The city of Jerusalem is besieged for a little more than 2 years, and starved the people. And the King sought to flee, and was captured and his sons slain in his sight and then his eyes plucked out. And all Jerusalem was destroyed, the temple looted and destroyed. The walls burned. Absolute desolation came upon them. But the poor of the land were left to be vinedressers and husbandmen. This has echos of the end times. The period of great tribulation. The abomination of desolation in Jerusalem. The destruction of the temple. The king and the rich men taken away into captivity into Babylon. The poor left to tend the vineyard for the king, to bring in the harvest. And halfway through the 70yr captivity, Jehoiachin, now king of Israel, was lifted up, caught up with the King, and taken out of prison. And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon; And changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life. And his allowance was a continual allowance given him of the king, a daily rate for every day, all the days of his life. An image of the saved being raptured out of great tribulation, halfway through the 7 year period, and given new garments of white and made to sit at the table of Christ, having a continual allowance of the king all the days of our eternal life. The constant echos of the end times found in the Old Testament, especially regarding the children of Israel as a nation, vs the spiritual Israel of that new nation made of believers, the Israel of God, is an awesome thing. Histories given over thousands of years, by multiple prophets and scribes, writing it down in the Spirit, having no clear understanding of what was to come, seeing through a glass darkly, and yet we who are here at the end of the world can look and see and understand. What an amazing gift the word of God is. Chronicles, a sort of retelling of Samuel and Kings, is chronologically next, but I think I will detour to some of the minor prophets first. And then maybe swing back around to Daniel. Don't hold me to it. God willing, we will get to where we need to be. Amen

The generations and roles of the Levites ends this section of Chronicles. We made it. You can study out the names of many of the men and women mentioned in the first 9 chapters of first Chronicles. There are some insights there. Especially with some of the details given and seeing their relationship to others in scripture. We see in this chapter that the purpose of all this was to establish the residence and inheritance of those carried away to Babylon for 70 years. To trace that lineage and find place for the men of Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh, in the land of Judah. It is here, in the southern kingdom of Judea, where they will come to be called Jews. And Jew did not only refer to the tribe of Judah, but all the residents - including those of other nations, not of Israel. Now having established this, and the Levites and their roles, the genealogy ends with a retelling of the lineage of Saul; And in Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon, Jehiel, whose wife's name was Maachah... This to establish the narrative that begins in the following chapter, with Saul's end as king of Israel, and the beginning of David's reign.

Finally past the genealogy of the first 9 chapters, Chronicles turns to a recounting of the history found in 1 & 2 Samuel and Kings. Specifically here in chapter 10, parallel with 1 Samuel 31. The reign of David and the covenant made with him is the primary focus of 1st Chronicles, and the temple and the importance of Jerusalem as the place God chose to put His name. Written for those returning to Judea, post-captivity, it places more emphasis on the promises of God and David's obedience and less on the personal failings of the king. While many of these stories are word for word, and familiar, there are some differences, and I will try to cover them here. 2 Samuel 1:23-27 Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions. Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with other delights, who put on ornaments of gold upon your apparel. How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, thou wast slain in thine high places. I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women. How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished! The psalm lamenting their deaths, written by David for Saul, his persecutor, and his best friend and brother in the spirit, Jonathan, Saul's son.

Here in 1 Chronicles 11, we find a very similar list of mighty men of David and their feats, as found in 2 Samuel 23 One difference that really stands out is that these honors are given by David in 2 Samuel 23 at the end of the King's life, where this account is by the narrator and given at the beginning of David's reign. Hopefully, man of the names are familiar to you. Especially Joab and Uriah the Hittite. The tale of David's longing for water from a well at Bethlehem while engaged in a battle afar off, and the three men who fought through the Philistines to fetch him that drink, is epic. And his refusal to take it for himself, but poured it out for the Lord, not wishing to have his men risk blood for vanity, shows the heart of the king, and why he was the apple of God's eye. It is good to inspire that kind of loyalty in people, but not to take advantage of it for petty things. We also see that while these men are honorable, there were those set apart, and others that did not attain the same status in the kingdom. This chapter reminds me of the Apostles, constantly competing for position and favor and honor in the Kingdom of Heaven. Luke 9:46-48 Then there arose a reasoning among them, which of them should be greatest. And Jesus, perceiving the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by him, And said unto them, Whosoever shall receive this child in my name receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same shall be great. Luke 22:24-30 And there was also a strife among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest. And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors. But ye shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve. For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am among you as he that serveth. Ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations. And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel. Mark 10:35-45 And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come unto him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall desire. And he said unto them, What would ye that I should do for you? They said unto him, Grant unto us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glory. But Jesus said unto them, Ye know not what ye ask: can ye drink of the cup that I drink of? and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? And they said unto him, We can. And Jesus said unto them, Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of; and with the baptism that I am baptized withal shall ye be baptized: but to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give; but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared. And when the ten heard it, they began to be much displeased with James and John. But Jesus called them to him, and saith unto them, Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them. But so shall it not be among you: but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: and whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all. For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many. The Apostles and chief disciples of Jesus were as the mighty men of David. And we are called honor as well. We can do great things for the Lord, even strive with one another to out do each other. We can run the gauntlet of Philistines to bring water for our Lord, but first we should seek to serve. First we should seek to be a good judge for the children, the fatherless, the widows. A servant to our brethren. And we should be cautious in what we strive for, as the sons of Thunder, James and John sought. The baptism of pain and persecution may be the price for glory. The cup of tribulation and suffering for His name. But even so, we should reach for the prize set before us; 1 Corinthians 9:24-27 Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain. And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible. I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air: but I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway. Philippians 3:13-14 Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. Hebrews 12:1-2 Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.

Here in 1 Chronicles 12 we get a better understanding of the men of Israel who came to David in exile, in Ziklag. Men who were captains over their own tribes, and with thousands riding with them. Men of war and valor, pledged to David. Even of Benjamin, who were Saul's people. David, meeting the Benjaminites come to him, says: If ye be come peaceably unto me to help me, mine heart shall be knit unto you: but if ye be come to betray me to mine enemies, seeing there is no wrong in mine hands, the God of our fathers look thereon, and rebuke it. Loyalty and love if they are friends, but to God goes the vengeance If they were enemies. This is an attitude we should all have as Christians, when dealing with brothers and sisters in Christ. But the Spirit comes upon their chief and they reply they are on his side. The men gathered to support David were a great host, like the host of God. With his anointing, David has united all Israel in joy. Just as we will gather joyfully as the host of God under Christ, the Anointed of God, when the saints gather to Him on His return, Jesus the King of Kings.

Here is a truncated version of events that we covered in 2 Samuel 6. David has been anointed King, and he decides to bring the ark of God to Jerusalem, that they may worship in one place, the city upon which God has placed His name. Poor Uzzah had little faith, and it cost him his life. Obededom received the ark into his home and was blessed. David's desire to set the tabernacle is delayed. Solomon will of course build the temple. This story is recounted here, again for those coming back from the 70 years of captivity in Babylon, tasked with rebuilding the temple. The Ark of the Covenant was not present in the Second Temple. It has been missing since the Babylonian invasion destroyed the First Temple. Presumed destroyed, but many hold out hope it exists somewhere on Earth. But the law is in our hearts, not tablets of stone. We are the branch that budded, like Aaron's rod. Dead but bringing forth life and fruit. The Mercy Seat in Heaven, sprinkled with the blood of the Lamb. Our High Priest, Jesus Christ. We don't need a physical ark.

And again, a retelling of events, this from 2 Samuel 5. We can see that while Chronicles is often word for word, it also can be more concise, and far less judgemental against David, and Solomon. Stating things like David taking more wives as just a fact, and the generations added to. But we see more directly the relationship David has with God. In the Christian life, we are not just our sin and failings. In some ways, we only are the things we do for God and reflections of His glory. Because the sin of our flesh and the trespasses we may do are not imputed against us. God remembers them no more. The flesh is nailed to the cross. If God sees our sin as far from us as far as east is from west, we should strive to be as gracious and merciful to our brethren. Forgiving and avoiding the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. Colossians 1:9-15 For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God; Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness; Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son: In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins Be thankful that God has already done so much for us that have been justified in Christ, while we were yet sinners. God has already made us partakers of the inheritance of the saints, delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son, and so, we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins. As in verse 20-21; having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven. And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled We are now reconciled, having made peace with the Father through the blood of the Son. This is the good news, the glory of the Gospel of God. All of these promises have been fulfilled already, the moment you believed and received the baptism of the Spirit, quickening your spirit and sealing you into redemption. As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him. Amen. Let us give glory to the Lord Jesus for this, and to God the Father for having the grace and mercy towards us that all these things have been predestined for those who place their trust in Christ. Knowing this peace and forgiveness and reconciliation, knowing this grace and mercy, let us extend it to our brothers, and to others that they know of our conversion, and hear the gospel on which we stand by faith. Amen

Psalm 134:1-3 Behold, bless ye the LORD, All ye servants of the LORD, Which by night stand in the house of the LORD. Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, And bless the LORD. The LORD that made heaven and earth Bless thee out of Zion. Numbers 4:15 And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the vessels of the sanctuary, as the camp is to set forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. These things are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation. Poor Uzzah. If only he had been a Levite of the line Kohath. David builds the tabernacle in his city, and his houses and settles the ark of the Lord in Jerusalem. Leading the congregation with music and singing. Glad to be going to the house of the Lord. But Saul's daughter, Michal, David's first wife, looks upon him and despises him. The hatred of Michal towards David is personal, obviously their turbulent history and his taking her father's place act as kindling for it. But the spark seems to be seeing David gladly worshipping the Lord. Joining in the assembly. Getting right and doing things for God. In a like manner, we may often experience this reaction as saved believers, where a family member or someone close to us resents our relationship with Jesus and our going to church, reading the Bible, cleaning up our life. Bringing the word of God, the holy Spirit, the love of Christ, into our lives can make worldly people despise us. Jesus came to bring division. Luke 14:26-27 If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple. A man may come to Jesus, and despise not his wife or family, and so, not be a disciple. A believer can be saved and yet be caught up in the cares of this world, being influenced by others who pull him away from living for Christ. Matthew 13:22 He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful. If you seek to be more than just be saved, a good husband and father, wife and mother, but instead wish to do great things for the Lord, don't neglect Jesus' warning. And as Paul wrote, in his opinion; 1 Corinthians 7: It is good for a man not to touch a woman. Nevertheless, to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband. Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband. But I speak this by permission, and not of commandment. For I would that all men were even as I myself. But every man hath his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that.I say therefore to the unmarried and widows, it is good for them if they abide even as I. Marriage is honorable. Family is a blessing. But be aware that your commitment to Christ can put you at enmity with your loved ones. Division; Luke 12:53: The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. This may be frustrating or discouraging, but like David, it shouldn't prevent us from doing all we can for Christ, Who has done everything for us. 1 Corinthians 7:10-17 And unto the married I command, yet not I, but the Lord, Let not the wife depart from her husband: But and if she depart, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband: and let not the husband put away his wife. But to the rest speak I, not the Lord: If any brother hath a wife that believeth not, and she be pleased to dwell with him, let him not put her away. And the woman which hath an husband that believeth not, and if he be pleased to dwell with her, let her not leave him. For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy. But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace. For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife? But as God hath distributed to every man, as the Lord hath called every one, so let him walk. And so ordain I in all churches. Sometimes you see people justify separation and divorce over these differences. But we should not. An unbelieving spouse isn't sufficient grounds to initiate a divorce; 1 Peter 3:1-2 Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.

Psalm 105:1-15 O give thanks unto the Lord; call upon his name: make known his deeds among the people. Sing unto him, sing psalms unto him: talk ye of all his wondrous works. Glory ye in his holy name: let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord. Seek the Lord, and his strength: seek his face evermore. Remember his marvellous works that he hath done; his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth; O ye seed of Abraham his servant, ye children of Jacob his chosen. He is the Lord our God: his judgments are in all the earth. He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations. Which covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath unto Isaac; And confirmed the same unto Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant: Saying, Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance: When they were but a few men in number; yea, very few, and strangers in it. When they went from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people; He suffered no man to do them wrong: yea, he reproved kings for their sakes; Saying, Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm. We see the focus of the chapter is the Psalm of thanksgiving David wrote in honor of the ark being returned to the tabernacle, and the sacrifices and offerings restored. In this psalm, which is also captured in Psalm 105, themes of return and deliverance from foreign oppression, which would be inspiring especially to those coming back out of Babylonian captivity. There is also the messianic message of Christ and judgment against the nations. We can also see a larger purpose to the list of genealogies that opened 1st Chronicles. We have been introduced to many of these names already. And their pedigree is established. We also see the nature of singing in worship. That God wants us to sing songs of praise and thanksgiving, continuously. As it is in heaven, as it was in the Tabernacle and the temple. As it is in our hearts today as Christians. Ephesians 5:18-20 And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit; Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ

1 Chronicles 17 finds David at his peak as King of Israel. He has power, a capital, great palaces and all from the anointing of the Lord. He sits with Nathan the prophet, and inquires about building a temple for God that He may no longer be in tents. And just as in the same story found in 2 Samuel 7, God speaking through Nathan tells David that he shall not build the temple, but makes instead a covenant with David that his son will, and that the son of David will rule forever. This is a clear picture of Christ. The intended audience for the chapter were men of Israel returning from the captivity of Judah by Babylon, and God's mention of redeeming their fathers from Egypt was particularly fitting for them, as was the reassurance that the kingdom was blessed by God through David's son. That a Temple of God would be built. A house, just as the exiled were returned to rebuild. But the same covenant is clearly speaking of Jesus, the house He shall build, the redemption He would pay for. That Jesus would be as a son to the Father. And rule and reign forever. It is a beautiful passage, and you gain understanding of why when in the gospels people call Jesus the "son of David" there is a messianic meaning behind it. Luke 18:38-42 And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me. And they which went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried so much the more, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me. And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought unto him: and when he was come near, he asked him, saying, What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight. And Jesus said unto him, Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee. Matthew 1:1 The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham. Romans 1:1-4 Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God, (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,) Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead

1 Chronicles 18 is a retelling of 2 Samuel 8, (the alleged KJV discrepancy of horses and horse men is addressed here)..and we see David's kingdom growing and prospering under his rule. We find Edom becoming the servants of Israel, just as Issac told Esau who is Edom; Genesis 27:38-40 And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept. And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck. Edom eventually rebelled against Judah, in 2 Kings 8:20-22, fulfilling the second part of the prophecy; In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves. So Joram went over to Zair, and all the chariots with him: and he rose by night, and smote the Edomites which compassed him about, and the captains of the chariots: and the people fled into their tents. Yet Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. Then Libnah revolted at the same time.

Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the Lord do that which seemeth him good. Be of good courage, and let us behave ourselves valiantly for our people, and for the cities of our God: and let the Lord do that which is good in his sight. This encouraging message of faith given by Joab before what could have been a haplessly outnumbered battle, with his forces split and surrounded, should be a mantra for Christians, especially Christian men. Too often today, professing Christian men come off as afraid, behave with no honor or duty to their people, and do not trust in the Lord to do what He sees as right. We see it daily, especially among the "conservatives," and even the more right-wing. Men, who seeing the odds and thinking that it's "so over," that the "West has fallen," either cower in fear, retreat from the world to hide, or take up blindly reactionary causes to "do something!" and force outcomes without any faith in the Lord to provide victory. But the Bible tells us again and again to have no fear. In the life of David we see that he behaved like a man, valiantly. Having the morality of God to guide him and following His word. Trusting in the Lord to deliver him and his people. And in his leadership, King David's faith and attitude trickled down to his captains, and from them to their men. And eventually to all Israel, rising up to put an end to the threats facing them, when God delivered victory against their enemies. That's the secret to winning. To win souls and obey God, live righteously and trust in Him when the battle comes.

Here is a condensed version of the events found in 2 Samuel 11 and 12, and the telling of David's wars, the slaughter of the Ammonites and the slaying of giants. We know, having read the earlier telling, that David had sinned with Bathsheba during this time, and murdered Uriah her husband by sending him out to war. That David tarrying in the city when it was the season of kings going to war, led to his temptation. But Chronicles doesn't much cover the failings of sin, but the glory of victory with God. In a like manner, we see how as a Christian, we have two tales of our lives. The one, details our sin and the other remembers it no more. Because we crucified our sinful flesh to the cross when we believed, and our new man, the quickened spirit within us, is incapable of sin. When we are redeemed on the day of the Lord, God remembers our sin no more. Blessed is the man to whom God will not impute sin. Amen Will note here the "controversy" of 1 Chronicles 20 and 2 Samuel 21, and who slew Goliath, is mentioned in our previous study.

This is a story of David we covered back during the study on 2 Samuel 24 The difference between the versions is slight, but the added detail gives us perspective. In 2 Samuel 24, we are told; And again the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah. Here, in 1 Chronicles 21 we get more understanding; And Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel. Just like Job, often God uses Satan to tempt us that we may be chastened, corrected and brought to repentance or, sadly, fail and condemn ourselves further. 1 Corinthians 5:4-5 In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when ye are gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, To deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus. We see this in the case of the fornication going on in the church at Corinth, where a man among them is chambering with his father's widow. Not only fornication, but an abomination. Paul tells them to church discipline him, that he be given over to Satan for destruction of the flesh, even if his spirit is saved. God allows Satan to destroy us in the flesh. The hope in church discipline is that the person gets right. Sees their error and comes back. But if not, at least in death they are free from the sin and present with the Lord. Note this teaches OSAS. Please follow the link to the previous study where I break down the sin of numbering the people in a way other than how God intended. I would add that in addition to God using Satan, He uses David as the King to bring this upon the people. God uses good rulers and bad rulers, the powers that be, the government, to enact judgment on the people for their sin, collectively. God judges nations on this earth. Romans 13:1-5 Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake. Many Christians today hate this doctrine, and seek to riot in the daytime, to rebel against the government that is doing the Lord's bidding. That because a government is clearly satanic, we have a responsibility to violently react. But the Bible teaches that we as believers have a responsibility to seek God's mercy and to come to Him asking for forgiveness. To do the things of God and turn unto Him. To get right. It isn't for us to kick against the pricks. That can be a hard lesson to swallow. Fear and pride can fight against the Spirit, but in the end, cannot prevail. Better to trust in God and pray and offer thanksgiving and supplication. Win souls. Edify the brethren. Raise godly children. Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not? If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

Again, we are reminded that Chronicles is written for the returning Jews out of captivity, freed to rebuild the temple. And so the focus is on the lineages of the people and the history of building the first temple. David, near death, has chosen Solomon as heir, and God has made it known that he will build the house of the Lord in the place He had chosen to put His name. We also see a foreshadowing of Christ, in that David would have a son who should rule in peace and be as a Son to the Lord, establishing His house, forever amen.

Again, more encouragement for the returning Jews, mainly Levites, who would build the second temple, and numbering and genealogy that hundreds of years later, they would know their parentage and patronage. As for us, we gain encouragement knowing, as David said, The Lord God of Israel hath given rest unto his people, that they may dwell in Jerusalem for ever. New Jerusalem is ours. We will dwell in peace forever. Repentance Moment: Matthew 3:1-12 In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey. Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire. Repent ye; for the Kingdom of heaven is at hand. Repent means to change your mind, to accept new information as true and have a change of heart, a conversion. Here, John the Baptist is saying "Reconsider what you know and believe me." He is not saying "get your life together and stop sinning, the Kingdom of Heaven is here." They were baptized in the water confessing their sins, because they believed him, and were saved. While false gospels that add works to salvation may disagree, Bible believing Christians who know water baptism is an answer for a good conscience before God, and not the cause of it, should be able to understand this context. John further chastened the religious leaders of the Jews, who came down to see him and his work, making the paths straight for the Lord. He asks them who has warned them to flee the wrath to come? Where are their followers come to be baptized before the coming of Christ? Where is their fruit meet for repentance? If they had preached the coming of Christ, they would have followers ready to accept the truth that the Christ was come. But this generation of vipers did not. They were trusting in being seed of Abraham. The water baptism of repentance, the sign of believers, was a prelude for the baptism of the Spirit in Christ. A baptism of fire. Amen

Here in 1 Chronicles 24, we have the division of service in the house of the Lord, cast by lot among the Levites in the presence of the king, again establishing roles and responsibilities by lineage for the returning Levites from Babylon, rebuilding the temple. We start once again with the line of Aaron. One of the most understated verses in the Bible; But Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and had no children... Leviticus 10:1-3 And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the Lord, which he commanded them not. And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord. Then Moses said unto Aaron, This is it that the Lord spake, saying, I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified. And Aaron held his peace. It is funny how that's glossed over, but it fits the theme of the book. As with King David, Chronicles is not interested in rehashing the sins of the people, but in documenting who is who and their origins and roles. We see the sons of Aaron, the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech are favored, and the line for the priest in David's and Solomon's reign ran through Zadok, whose own children would eventually be the Sadducees in Jesus' time. Even today, modern Jews, so-called, supposedly trace the sons of Aaron patrilineally. While all other Jews keep a matrilineal line due to adultery and fornication. Today, the Cohen's and like named are considered direct descendants of Aaron. Jews even pay them shekels for indulgences in the Talmudic tradition, a perversion of the poll tax of the OT.

Psalm 150:3-6 Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: Praise him with the psaltery and harp. Praise him with the timbrel and dance: Praise him with stringed instruments and organs. Praise him upon the loud cymbals: Praise him upon the high sounding cymbals. Let every thing that hath breath Praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD. Music in worship is an unambiguous command. Praise Him. And not just at the assembly: Ephesians 5:19-20 Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ; Here in 1 Chronicles 25, they draw lots for those who are to make the music in the temple, and again by name and lineage for the purpose of the returning exiles from Babylon. People who recognized their forefathers and kept the same roles. Generational trades, family businesses, are a blessing. Not every child may want to go into the same line, but historically, even in the recent past, this was the way. Children followed after their parents, and sons joined their father in learning the skill or trade of their ancestors. It was a better time.

Matthew 25:14-23 For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods. And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey. Then he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents. And likewise he that had received two, he also gained other two. But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord's money. After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them. And so he that had received five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents: behold, I have gained beside them five talents more. His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord. He also that had received two talents came and said, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me two talents: behold, I have gained two other talents beside them. His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord. 2 Timothy 2:12 If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us: Revelation 20:4-6 And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection. Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years. Much like the division of priests and rulers in the kingdom of David, so too will be the Kingdom of Heaven. And in the millennial reign, we who are saved will be appointed to duties, roles and responsibilities, and even being judge over matters pertaining to God and affairs of the King. Dedicate your time to taking the talents God has given you, and gaining others to Christ. Strive to be one who on that day, hears the voice of our Savior say, "Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over what's been given you. I will make you ruler over many things." We shall judge even angels. And there shall be thrones, cities and wards, areas of responsibility, and gates and roads where a good and faithful servant shall have responsibility, and less fruitful will serve in other capacities to the administration of Christ's Kingdom. These are the crowns we strive for. This is why we humble ourselves and serve those in need. This is where the least among us, meek and lowly, become first in the Kingdom of God.

We see further divisions and delegation of the roles in the kingdom of Israel, and the way David, under God's influence structured it is likely very similar to the millennial Kingdom. Note that each tribe has a force of 24,000 that served one month a year in a duty rotation, had captains over them, and the thousands and the hundreds. Each area had a governor. There were men over the various state needs, farms and vineyards and cattle. There were men chosen as advisors, a companion, a general of the armed forces....a role for every man and those under them. And of these men, we have a record for our instruction and admonition, and to their glory having mention in the Bible by name. We also are given another reason God's wrath was kindled at the unlawful numbering of the tribes begun by David and halted by plague. But David took not the number of them from twenty years old and under: because the Lord had said he would increase Israel like to the stars of the heavens. Joab the son of Zeruiah began to number, but he finished not, because there fell wrath for it against Israel; neither was the number put in the account of the chronicles of king David. If the Lord promises something as a blessing, counting it for your own purpose or to "trust but verify" is either a sign of taking it for granted in a selfish way, or an insulting lack of faith. Or both. We know it displeased God to the point where we know, whatever the number has been, it was down 70,000 Israelites in the end.

As we near the end of 1 Chronicles, we see the account of David, having assembled the people, all of whom he'd assigned roles and drawn lots for responsibilities, to give them the plan for the resting place for the ark, and a footstool upon the earth for the Lord. That his son Solomon had been chosen of God to do this thing, to build the temple, and the details and design which were given David by the Spirit. Again, the audience of the author are the Jews returning from captivity centuries later, who would rebuild the temple, that it serve as a picture of the risen Christ. That it be there, in Jerusalem when Jesus came, to serve its purpose of sacrifice and ceremony until that reformation came; the resurrection of the Christ. I recently was giving the gospel to someone who said, "I understand God loves us, and that His Son, Jesus was born and died and rose again for us, but I struggle with the question; Why?" Not as in why did God do this, which we know is because He so loved us. But why in this manner? I think one of the reasons is that man by our nature we know sin requires a sacrifice for atonement. Of course every animal sacrificed from Adam and Eve and God showing them the way, through righteous Abel, to Noah disembarking from the ark, to Abraham with Melchizedek, to Moses and Arron and the Levitical priests, were pictures given by God of the actual sacrifice to come. The Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. And they who trusted in the Christ to come were saved by that faith. But without some means of understanding, it was difficult for them to form faith. Thus the process laid out in the law. But for the other nations called, after the crucifixion and resurrection, the one sacrifice made for all time, for all sin, by Jesus' blood, man needed to understand it clearly. And so we place trust in His word. Faith being the evidence of things not seen, which comes from hearing His word. There needed to be witnesses. It had to happen here, in this world that others would believe, sight unseen. As Jesus says to Thomas, blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed. Without the prophets and scriptures promising Christ, the sacrifice of Christ, and without the witnesses to the resurrection testifying of Christ, I think man would not believe God wanted to forgive them. Without the gospel preached, a witness, exactly as it stands: 1 Corinthians 15:1-8 Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand; By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain. For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles. And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time. Be strong and of good courage, and do it: fear not, nor be dismayed: for the Lord God, even my God, will be with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee, until thou hast finished all the work for the service of the house of the Lord. This is a promise to all believers, in Christ. We are the temple of God, where the Spirit dwells. He will not fail us or forsake us as we do the work for the service of the house of the Lord. When someone is backslidden and in sin, they will seek to get others to join them. Misery loves company. If someone reminds them of their sins, or makes them feel badly for them, even passively, let alone rebuking them, they will find whatever fault they can with that person. Any sin they may have done, real, exaggerated or imaginary, and use that shortcoming to justify their own sin. Tu quoque; Latin for thou too: a retort by one charged with a crime accusing an opponent who has brought the charges of a similar crime. As if a railing accusation of hypocrisy absolves themselves of what they are doing. When you see this, with no sincere attempt to acknowledge and rectify their bad behavior, everything they say should be treated as a lie or an attempt to gain sympathy and moral high ground.

Here in 1 Chronicles 29, the final chapter, we come to the transition of power between King David and his son Solomon. David has, in obedience to the Lord, organized the Kingdom, set up the leaders of men and the chain of command in the various roles and responsibilities. He has given Solomon the plans for the house of God, the pattern given by the Spirit, and laid up treasure and provisions to see it built. And the people all willingly gave treasure to build up the house of the Lord and to do His work. Free will offerings. David calls them to prayer and to bless the Lord God of Israel, to give Him all glory and honor. David's prayer reminds us that whatever we give to the service of God is His to begin with. Tithing, the practice of giving the first of the flock, the tenth of the wealth and harvest, etc...these are commands in the Old Testament, that we honor today in the New. But the free will offerings here are a reminder that all we have cometh of Thine hand, and is all Thine own. Not just 10%, pretax income, itemized and listed on our taxes. All of it. Everything we have is His because it is by His grace we have it at all. For all things come of God. And when we give, it is of God's own. When we approach giving towards the church, or to help the brethren, or missions and church plants and soul winning trips...whatever it may be, give cheerfully, willingly. Because riches and honor come from God. It is His power to make us great, and blessed by whatever riches He provides. We can't take it with us; there are none abiding. So give joyfully, knowing it's not yours but the Lord's. And rejoice in it, praising Him in thanksgiving, that you have abundance wherewithal to give.

Proverbs 9:10 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding. Solomon begins with fear of the Lord. He asks for wisdom to rule well, and receives it. He seeks understanding and has respect for that which is holy. He then gathers riches and multiplies horses unto himself, trading with Egypt. Deuteronomy 17:16 But he shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt, to the end that he should multiply horses: forasmuch as the LORD hath said unto you, Ye shall henceforth return no more that way. Solomon is a complicated person. Filled with seeming contradiction. The wisest king, ruling well. God provides him unprecedented peace and prosperity for the people under his rule. And yet Solomon compromises, allows his wives to multiply and to lead him from that which is holy. His son sees a divided kingdom and the people suffer due to his mistakes. A lot of wisdom to be found in his story. Again, we see the focus in Chronicles is on the means and manner of the temple, and given to be instruction to those returning from Babylon. But the insights we receive in a slightly different telling add complexity and depth to the tale, as we will continue to see in 2 Chronicles.

In 1 Kings 3 we see Solomon settling in as King of Israel, making peace with the Pharaoh of Egypt through marriage to his daughter, while building his palace and the Temple of the Lord in Jerusalem. We are told that the people sacrificed in high places because there was no house of the Lord for central worship as had been when the Ark and the Tabernacle were in one location, together. David had brought the Ark to Jerusalem, while Zadok the priest was in charge over the Tabernacle in Gibeon, apparently a high place, according to the account in 2 Chronicles 1. And while we have association with Baal worship in high places, and the existence of them was no God's plan for a central place of worship, in this strange in-between time, it wouldn't be outrageous for Solomon, who loved the Lord and kept David's statutes, to sacrifice at Gibeon to the Lord God of Israel. And Solomon does, and offers a thousand burnt offerings upon the altar of the Tabernacle out of love for God. And God graciously speaks to Solomon by dream, and tells the new king to ask what God shall give him. Solomon says Thou hast shewed unto thy servant David my father great mercy, according as he walked before thee in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with thee; and thou hast kept for him this great kindness, that thou hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day. Solomon wisely begins his petition by recognizing how God blessed his father, David. The great mercy the living God showed him, and the great kindness of giving David an heir to sit upon the throne. As the father of saved children, I can tell you this kindness is awesome, and the mercy of God that we may know our children are co-heirs with Christ to the Kingdom is one of the greatest gifts God can bestow on a parent. Solomon continues, wisely recognizing his youth and inexperience as he takes the throne given to him as God's anointed, king over a great number of people. And so Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge God's people, strong discernment between good and bad. This pleased the Lord, and because Solomon did not ask foolishly or selfishly, God says Behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart. The wisest man to ever live. The question then arises, was this gift given to Solomon at this moment, where his eyes opened and he gained this wisdom supernaturally? Or, given his upbringing by David, and his love for the Lord and his desire to walk in the ways of his father and the word of God, had Solomon been shaped by God from birth to be such a King? When Solomon is given an opportunity to ask of God anything, and he was wise enough to give glory to God first and ask for right judgment to rule wisely, was he already displaying that wisdom that had been given him by the Lord? Because Solomon asked rightly, God says He will not only bless him with wisdom, but riches and honor, elevating him above all kings during his reign. God also repeats His promise, one that stands for Christians today; And if thou wilt walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as thy father David did walk, then I will lengthen thy days. Psalm 37:28-38 For the Lord loveth judgment, and forsaketh not his saints; they are preserved for ever: but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off. The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever. The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom, and his tongue talketh of judgment. The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide. The wicked watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him. The Lord will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when he is judged. Wait on the Lord, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land: when the wicked are cut off, thou shalt see it. I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree. Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found. Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace. But the transgressors shall be destroyed together: the end of the wicked shall be cut off. And so, we are told the famous story of an example of the wisdom of Solomon; the cutting of the baby in half. This is such an extraordinary tale, that even secular and worldly traditions of wisdom recognize it and teach it throughout the world. Two harlots, and both give birth to sons within days of each other. And the one accidentally kills her own baby, smothering it in its sleep. She steals the other woman's son in the night and gives to her the dead child. They come before the King to judge and he discerned the matter by presenting a horrific choice; cutting the infant that each woman be given half. The woman who objects and says rather let the other woman keep it, is clearly the real mother, while the one who agrees to "split the baby" is revealed to be the imposter. This wisdom established the understanding throughout Israel that God had blessed their King. and gained Solomon the people's respect. Fame that would soon spread to the rest of the world.

A son that honors his father, even after their death, will build upon their legacy and have honor of those who loved their father. A son who rebels and attempts to tear down what their father has built will be distrusted and scored by those that love the father, and they will come to naught. Now Solomon takes all of his father's plans, and the inspiration of God and sets about building the house of the Lord in the place that God chose. He secures the things needed, humble at the very thought of being chosen to do this task. And again this is written to instruct those returning from Babylon and the rebuilding of the House of the Lord. Calling on them to approach it with this humility. Just as we are, as Christians, given the ability to build up and edify the church of Christ. Through salvation and spreading the gospel. We have the tools. We have the past relationships that allow us to build upon the foundation which is Christ and all that has been laid upon it before us. And just as the strangers in the land are called to be servants, doing the work to build the temple, so too are Christians. We are strangers in the land yet given this task as servants to God. It's a picture of the salvation coming to the Gentiles.

The construction begins, noting specific measurements and qualities of the decorative features and layout. Some idolaters justify their bowing and serving images of men by pointing to the decorative and illustrative placement of Cherubim and pomegranates in the Temple design. No Israelites bowed to these things, representative of the pattern in Heaven. They didn't offer prayers or sacrifice to them. They served no purpose other than to make the house of the Lord reflect His temple in Heaven. The location of the Temple mount, Moriah, where the Lord appeared to David, and where the sacrifices to the Lord took place by the threshing floor of Ornan, was also where Abraham brought Isaac to be sacrificed; Genesis 22:1-2 And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am. And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of. There, in a picture of Christ, where Issac, Abraham's only begotten son, carried the wood up the mountain to be offered, with hyssop and crimson. And God the Father provided a substitutionary offering, a ram in a thicket of thorns. The same Jerusalem where Jesus was brought before the high priest, near Golgotha where He gave His life. Likely the same place Melchizedek the King of Salem offered Abraham's sacrifice. Where Christ will return to rule and reign. The place God chose to place His holy name. "According to the first-century Romano-Jewish scholar Josephus' book Antiquities of the Jews, Jachin (Hebrew יָכִין yakin "He/it will establish") stood on the right on the portico of Solomon's Temple, while Boaz (Hebrew בֹּעַז boʿaz "In him/it [is] strength") stood on the left, and the two were made by a Canaanite craftsman named Hiram." The pillars stood outside the entrance, free standing. One to the North the other the South, in the East-facing entrance. East to catch the rising sun. Where He will establish, where He is strength. A reminder of the testimony of Christ. The faith of redemption that all man has been saved by since Adam. The twin pillars are a picture of the promise and strength of the Christ to come. It is unknown if these pillars made it into the design of the 2nd Temple, but their inclusion here in Chronicles, written for the admonition and instruction of those returning from Babylon makes it likely in my opinion. We know from Jeremiah that they were destroyed and broken down at the beginning of the captivity, and the desolation of Jerusalem.
Solomon makes the things of the Temple, with great specificity for those returning from Babylon.

The Temple built, the covenant of God at its heart, and the sacrifices were made and the priests ministering in a picture of the one sacrifice and one priest, Christ Jesus. And the joyful noise of Psalms and hymns and instruments were made unto the Lord, Who receives all praise. And the Spirit of the Lord fills the place, filling the house of God. This is like unto us, each one of us who has accepted the gospel, and the staves removed, meaning no longer would the ark be taken from place to place, but there in the place God placed His name, a reminder that once we are saved we are always saved. Amen. Psalm 69:30-31 I will praise the name of God with a song, and will magnify him with thanksgiving. This also shall please the Lord better than an ox or bullock that hath horns and hoofs. Reading 2 Chronicles 5 and the dedication of the Temple as a picture of this salvation process in us isn't perfect, naturally. But a parable is never exact. And all of creation is a parable to the glory of God, in the end, yet nothing compares or approaches the majesty of God. So, reading the order of things, we see the sacrifices and offerings were not when the cloud of God's Majesty came, (just as He did in the Tabernacle at Moses's dedication in Exodus 40:34-37). It was when the praise and worship of the Lord was made. Ephesians 5:19-20 Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ If you want to feel the power of God in your life, if you want to have His presence come upon you, start with this. The sacrifice was made already. The promise of Christ is God's to fulfill. Now we should praise Him in all things, and we will know we are His by His presence. The Spirit testifying within us that we are children of God. Even the prayer Jesus teaches us as a model for our prayer life begins by recognizing that our Father is hallowed, holy. Set apart from all others. And that His will is our will, that it be done. The Psalms filled with such praise. If you wish to have a more fulfilling and productive Christian walk, keep that song in your heart and throughout the day, joyfully praising all things. Giving honor to our holy God.

Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the Temple is dripping with doctrine. Of the glory of God and the promises of salvation, the covenants with David, and with Israel. The King begins recounting that God's glory is hid by the thick darkness, the cloud that protects the people from being consumed by His majesty, but Solomon has built this house for a dwelling place. Blessing the Lord God of Israel, loyal and true, keeping the promises made to David by His word. That He has chosen Jerusalem to place His name, and in David, a King to rule. The promise of Christ Jesus. Solomon, on his knees, kneeling upon a brazen scaffold, hands outstretched to the heavens before the congregation, says O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like thee in the heaven, nor in the earth; which keepest covenant, and shewest mercy unto thy servants, that walk before thee with all their hearts. We who are the Israel of God, believers, are His servants. We receive these same blessings of our faithful God. His kept promises and mercy adding to our faith, and our faith leading to our obedience in Him. Solomon acknowledges that the Lord God of Israel cannot be contained by a dwelling place, not of a temple made by hands, but prays instead that God's eyes be on this house he's built, that He in His grace grant prayers and supplication made within the Temple. To the people of Israel and to the stranger who comes to worship. That all nations be blessed in Him. He prays for forgiveness for future generations, who may by sin be chastened by the Lord, that if they turn again to Him, that the Lord forgive them and bring them again into the land. Or to heal the land from pestilence and blight. He prays that God favors their armies when they set out to do His will, to return them from captivity when they repent, and that His mercies extend to the people who pray towards the land, the city, the Temple, the house which has been built for His holy name. Of course this is relevant to us, who as saved believers are the temple of God. He has placed His name in us, and His great mercies and blessings extend towards us, in the name of Jesus. The land we turn towards is that better country, the Kingdom of Heaven. Our King, the king of kings, the Son of David upon His throne forever. If we sin, for there is no man that sinneth not, He will forgive. We are His priests, clothed with salvation. His promise, His Word, the ark of strength in our hearts. Let us rejoice in goodness. Amen

Here in 2 Chronicles 7, we see the dedication of the Temple complete, with a 7 day feast and the sacrifices made, and the people worshiping in the presence of the glory of the Lord. The fire of the Lord come down from heaven to consume the burnt offerings. The priests committed to their service, making the offerings, even the musicians as David had instructed, with Solomon as King, presiding over all. And the people praised God, saying He is good; for His mercy endureth forever. Jesus Christ is the mercy of God which endureth forever. The grace of the Father made manifest in the Son, Who is the consuming fire come down from Heaven. And the judgment of God upon the nations of people who call themselves by His name, one of the most quoted verses of scripture, comes in 2 Chronicles 7:14 If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. This is the only answer to the sin in the land. God's mercy. This is how we as a nation are restored today, just as this promise inspired revival in the returning Jews out of Babylon. The Lord's mercy endureth forever. Amen.

Seeking first the things of God, Solomon has great success and peace in the land, and all Israel prospers. Others do their labor. Foreign kings provide their goods, entire cities are built for stores, and merchants go afar to bring back gold and treasure. Peace is in the land. It all starts by starting with God.

2 Chronicles 9 tells a digest form of the reign of King Solomon, describing the heights of his kingdom. Famed for wisdom, brought riches by other kings and queens, the boundaries of Israel expanded to their largest, and held in peace. It tells of 666 talents of gold brought to Solomon per year. And tribute made by kings seeking his presence and to hear his wisdom, as the Queen of Sheba had. The vessels of silver and gold, and horses and spices, year after year. The great ivory throne that he has built, as his judgment seat. The ships of Tarshish brining treasure from far lands. We have read in 1 Kings the story of Solomon, good and bad. His wives by which he sinned. His son, doomed to rule a divided kingdom. But here, we are given the description of a king and a kingdom that are a picture of the millennial Kingdom of the Lord Christ Jesus. As the author says, the rest of the acts of Solomon are found elsewhere. In long lost books that the inspired book of Chronicles is drawn from. In Kings.
