David teaches us the same lessons in Psalms. The wisdom of God is most valuable, because in that knowledge we may find eternal life. David expresses confidence in his salvation. He is not afraid when the time comes to be given the wages of his sin, the iniquity of his heels, the death that awaits us all, the consequences of our own making. Why should we fear in the days of evil, that comes our own making? He knows his redemption is a gift of God. But the man trusting his riches has no hope at all in that day. They cannot redeem themselves or their brothers, and cannot pay the ransom due God for their sins. Again, this idea that man's riches are worthless in the judgment, that they do nothing for the dead, is repeated by Solomon; Proverbs 11:4 Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death. Proverbs 27:24 For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation? Their way is folly. The wise man dies like the fool, like the brute, and all their wealth is left for others. But the precious redemption of the soul, that one lives forever and shall not see corruption, that is of God, through faith in the Lord Christ Jesus. 1 Timothy 2:5–6 For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time. David laments the fact that worldly prosperity deceives the wealthy, their own riches fooling them into a false sense of security. This is the larger context of the preaching of Christ; Matthew 19:23–26 Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. When his disciples heard it, they were exceedingly amazed, saying, Who then can be saved? But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible. The only hope of man, rich or poor, is God. Only in Him is salvation possible. Proverbs 15:16 Better is little with the fear of the Lord than great treasure and trouble therewith. The blessings of this life are not a hope for the next. The praise of men is vanity before the Throne of an almighty and holy God. Agur's prayer in Proverbs directly addresses this wisdom; Proverbs 30:8-9 Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain. Better to be satisfied with what the Lord has given us, and trust and fear Him, than to allow wealth to take us from fearing the Lord, or poverty that brings bitterness to our soul. Psalm 49 perfectly encapsulates these wise sayings, showing that David's hope is not in riches, but in the salvation of the Lord. But God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave: for he shall receive me. Selah. So, no matter the station you have been born to, or the prosperity you've been blessed with, fear God and follow His ways, seeking His wisdom and be blessed by His redemption. Learn from his dark sayings and parables, before it is too late. Man that is in honour, and understandeth not, is like the beasts that perish. The call by David to hear and understand his "dark sayings and parables," brings to mind the way Jesus taught in His ministry. Matthew 13:34–35 All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them: That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world. Jesus revealed to His disciples that parables act as a spiritual filter. To the humble seeker of wisdom, they provide deeper understanding; to the spiritually blind, they remain obscure "dark sayings." Matthew 13:10–13 And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables? He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given. For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath. Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand. The unfolding revelation to man throughout scripture was never meant to keep wisdom hidden. Especially, not forever. Unlike the religions of man, with their esoteric knowledge, vague and shallow sayings fed in dribs and drabs, with no clarity ever given, God's word opens itself up, and Jesus ultimately shows what all these "dark sayings" and prophetic parables actually mean. John 16:25 These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs: but the time cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall shew you plainly of the Father. During His earthly ministry, even Jesus' most faithful disciples required His explanation of the parables He spoke in, to the crowds and Pharisees. Mark 4:33–34 And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it. But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples. But the full revelation of scripture came in the days following His resurrection, when all things were finally made known. To the men He met on the way, in Luke 24, Jesus, beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself. And to the gathering of the disciples, He did the same; Luke 24:44–45 And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures. He explicitly references the three divisions of the Old Testament, (the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms, like Psalm 49) and grants them the spiritually supernatural ability to finally see past the "dark sayings" to understand the plain truth of the Gospel. These things are revealed to us by the Spirit, Who teaches us all things. We are able to see the entire picture, fully revealed in Christ, and the understanding imparted by the Apostles in the Epistles for added clarity and depth. Only the future Revelation of Christ Jesus is still through a glass darkly, (although the gist is pretty clear on timing and events). We see that the Old Testament scriptures aren't an empty recitation of genealogy, geography and events. They aren't the vain contemplations of man. They are the words of eternal life, and all these were written to point the way to Jesus, and provide us with understanding. 1 Corinthians 10:11 Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come. Not only does God's word exist to show us His ways, but ultimately it is the tool He has given us to fulfill the Great Commission, leading others to the truth. Luke 24:46–48 And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. And ye are witnesses of these things. We are witnesses of these things. We have the testimony of God, revealed. We are given the wisdom and power of His word to teach repentance towards God and remission of sins by His Son, in Jesus' name. Not in dark sayings and parables, although they help reveal the truth, but by the power of our witness that all is revealed in Christ. Amen.

Psalm 50, is a song written directly from the voice of God to His people, His own perspective directly to man. It is instruction in doctrine and prophecy, by His word. In the first person. He spoke these things through a psalmist other than David. The superscript titles this as "A Psalm of Asaph," making it the very first of the 12 "Asaphite Psalms" in the Bible. Asaph was a prominent Levite, appointed by King David as the chief musician and worship leader before the Ark of the Covenant when it was brought to Jerusalem. More than just a song director, the Bible credits him as a prophet. A seer. 2 Chronicles 29:30 Moreover Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the LORD with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped. While prophesying may refer to preaching the word of God, seer is the specific term for a visionary who is given glimpses of the future by God, prophetic understanding of things that are not but will be. He begins his song by introducing its Author. The mighty God. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, it is God breathed, and spoken. But this will be the word of God, as a message of judgment for His people. It establishes first the primacy of God, the Creator. By His Word the earth and the heavens were made. John 1:1–4 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men. It is important when we see credit for creation to God in the Bible, to remember that this includes Jesus. 1 Corinthians 8:6 But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him. We have a New Testament understanding when we reflect on the Old Testament revelations. The nature of the Godhead is revealed in the creation. And it is relevant to this Psalm. Out of Zion, the place God chose to put His name, God hath shined. His presence in the Tabernacle and the eventual Temple, God with His people through their worship, is an echo to the true coming of the Lord in the flesh, and His return on His day to judge the nations, upon that holy mountain. Our God shall come, and shall not keep silence: a fire shall devour before him, and it shall be very tempestuous round about him. The Second Coming, the return of Christ, is the day we all look forward to with gladness. He will come with power, a consuming fire proceeding from Him, and the sword of His word from His mouth shall slay the wicked. 2 Thessalonians 1:7–9 And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power The future judgment of the world was a key part of the Israelites understanding, though through a glass darkly. However, having the full revelation of the complete Bible, we see clearly what they only glimpsed in faith. He comes as a judge, the Son calling up to Heaven, and down to Earth, with a shout, with trumpet, the call to judgment of His people, before His wrath is poured out on the world. Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice. And the heavens shall declare his righteousness: for God is judge himself. Selah. The gathering of the elect, those sanctified by the Spirit in Christ, is not a "new doctrine," as some would claim. The Rapture, or the gathering of the elect being caught up together to meet the Lord in the air, was a key part of prophecy for the Lord's people. The covenant was made by sacrifice; the blood of the covenant made by Moses and the people with God was sealed with blood that represented the blood of Christ, and the promise of a better covenant with God by sacrifice, the sacrifice of the Son. Hebrews 9:19–23 For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission. It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these. The heavens declare the righteousness of Christ Jesus, and His righteousness is upon all His people. God is the judge Himself. The Atonement, Himself. The mediator, Himself. The saints are secure in His righteousness. But God speaks to Israel in judgment. Beginning with His people. Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee: I am God, even thy God. The future prophecy versus the current call. The continuous sacrifices made before God to give the physical nation of Israel the honor of being His people, keep His hand from reproving them harshly. They maintained the Levitical ordinances which He based promises on. The sacrifices that needed to be done constantly to maintain ritual cleanliness and keep His presence among them had been done. He isn't asking for more sacrifice. No additional bulls or goats to shed their blood. Again, we have a better sacrifice, once and for all, a covenant made by the blood of Jesus, the burnt offering for our sin. Hebrews 9:11–14 But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? But, in the old covenant, the blood of bulls and goats were used, continually, signifying the Sacrifice to come, and this the Levites did. God is telling His people at this time He isn't asking for more, and in fact it is not the blood of bulls and goats, and their burnt offering that He seeks. Every beast is His. The cattle upon a thousand hills. If He were hungry, and in need of the savour of the fat and the sustenance of meats, He has His pick and fill. He doesn't need them. Their sacrifices are a picture and a necessity for the covenant, but they do not please Him in and of themselves. Hosea 6:6 For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. Sentiment repeated by Christ; Matthew 12:7 But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. Here, in Psalm 50, God makes it clear that the offering is thanksgiving. They are vows to be paid to maintain their part in the covenant as His nation. Tithes and first fruits as acts of faith. It is not, as other gods, a meal for Him to consume, but a thanksgiving offered to show gratitude for all that He has supplied them, and to keep themselves unspotted, and be His people. God desires mercy towards others. Right judgment, defending the weak and hating the workers of iniquity. Matthew 23:23 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. These aren't the repetitive acts done by priests, but matters of the heart which God judges, and that He seeks from us. Having established His ways, God continues in v15 to give the Gospel message. The good news to all men in all ages; the dispensation of grace: And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me. Calling upon the name of the Lord for salvation, that we may glorify Him to all men. The promise of salvation and the heart of the great commission, coupled with the truth that we magnify His light, when we are in Him, that man may see our works of righteousness, mercy and thanksgiving, and glorify God. Matthew 5:16 Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. This is our purpose as believers. To give the judgment of God and an example of His mercy, praising His name in thanksgiving, all as an outlet to be seen by man, that He may be glorified. Now, having been summoned to His judgment, and having stipulated His position, God begins the indictment against His people, giving the matters of His suit, which He Himself will judge. God, in showing that He has no need for the blood of bulls and goats, fowls or anything else, begins by laying the charge of formalism against His covenant people. The religious practices are being maintained, the bare minimum of service to keep the covenant. The Lord isn't accusing them of failing this aspect, but in the weightier matters, as Jesus accused the Pharisees. God established promises and practices to maintain them as His people, but they are failing to declare His statutes, or to proclaim His law. The entire point of Israel was to be a light to all men. Not to selfishly reap the benefits while doing nothing to teach all nations as an example. Deuteronomy 4:5–6 Behold, I have taught you statutes and judgments, even as the LORD my God commanded me, that ye should do so in the land whither ye go to possess it. Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people. They had squandered their blessings by not fulfilling this role. Matthew 15:8 This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. God is directly accusing the wicked among His people of missing the entire point, a charge Jesus will use to indict the religious leaders of the Jews. Matthew 23:27–28 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness. Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity. As an application for Christians today, the indictment is the same leaven of the Pharisees; hypocrisy. Hebrews 10:8 Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law. Just as the Pharisees had the OT sacrifices, we have the once and for all sacrifice of Christ, and total remission of sins. Hebrews 10:17–18 And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more. Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin. Just as He says to His people That he isn't seeking to add more sacrifice to those that they are already, God isn't asking us for additional acts of atonement. He remembers our sins no more. There is no more sacrifice to be had. Hebrews 10:26–27 For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries. Just like Israel in Psalm 50, we are covered by the blood. We are his people. But are we bound by the formalism and outward appearance of being clean, while failing to maintain the good work that God has saved us for? That gives Him glory? Or are we looking over our shoulder, expecting a similar charge to be made by God against us as He is making here? If we're not declaring his righteousness and glory in Thanksgiving, and showing mercy and judgment to others, loving our neighbor, how are we taking his covenant in our mouths? How are we telling the world that we are Christians when we aren't acting like it? Who does it benefit? James 2:14–17 What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him? If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone. This isn't legalism. This isn't God saying that to be his we have to do works to be saved, or to be His. We are not justified before God by our works, but before men. But God does have works for us to do. Ephesians 2:10 For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them. The indictment against His people is that while we have availed ourselves of his covenant and promises, we have squandered and wasted the talents of silver He is given us. Matthew 25:14–30 For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods. And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey. Then he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents. And likewise he that had received two, he also gained other two. But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money. After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them. And so he that had received five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents: behold, I have gained beside them five talents more. His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord. He also that had received two talents came and said, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me two talents: behold, I have gained two other talents beside them. His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord. Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, there thou hast that is thine. His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed: Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury. Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents. For unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath. And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. To whom much is given much is expected. There are professing Christians in this world who have never accepted the gift that God has extended to us. They've taken the offer and buried it and done nothing with it. They didn't take it in as their own and nurture it and use it to increase God's kingdom. Again this isn't a works-based salvation. If the unprofitable servant had taken his one talent of silver and kept it in his care, he'd still have been saved. But rather he buried it, and went through the motions. God goes out of his way in his indictment against Israel in Psalm 50 to stipulate that His people who are righteous are protected under his care. His problem is with the false professors of His name who think that the formalism of their worship is sufficient to spare them from His wrath. God's accusations against them are sharp. They can tend with thieves and are partakers with adulterers. Both the literal engagement with the worldly, and the spiritual, of general ecumenicalism. They speak evil things, and lie. They not only don't love their neighbors, but they lie against their own brothers. And God, God who is longsuffering and merciful and wood that all men come to repentance, gave them space and time to reconsider their ways. Instead they considered themselves holy, like God is Holy. They thought that in their religious practices, and keeping the letter of the law that they could ignore the purpose of the law and its spirit. It's the same indictment here as in Matthew 23. And it could be said Of so many supposed Christians today. It's interesting to me that Hebrews 10 bookends the idea of being no more need for sacrifice for those in Christ, and there being no more sacrifice for willful sin, around the command to attend church. Hebrews 10:23–25 Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching. We are commanded to not forsake the assembly. And the purpose of that is to love one another. Edifying each other. Building each other up. So much more as the day approaches. But today, there are those who see church as a check box for their righteousness. Proving that they are holy as God is holy simply by their attendance. And in so many acts that they do, they wash the outside of the vessel, while inside they are whited tombs filled with dead men's bones. Those people to whom religion is a series of rituals and obligations that only benefit themselves, who see sacraments as their sacrifice rather than the blood of Christ. Christians in name only who go through the motions and never once consider God. They forget God and he will tear them to pieces. They bury their talent out of fear, while never truly fearing God. But God, ever gracious ends on a positive note. Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God. Our purpose of being his people is to praise his name that he be glorified among men. We are the salt of the earth. We are what is preserving the world against judgment. And so he's encouraging us to continue in that praise and thanksgiving and glorifying God among men. Because it is possible for salt to lose its savor. For lukewarm Christians to have the candle of their church put out. To be of no further use of God so he calls you home if you're saved and if you're not, casting you into outer darkness. Matthew 5:13 Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. God's case against Israel is God's case against all who call themselves by His name and fail to live to proclaim His glory. Let us then stay salty, maintain our savor, do all things with Mercy and judgment forgiving those who trespass against us, considering the plight of the poor and the widow and the fatherless. Exhorting one another. So that at the coming of Christ, when He brings fiery judgment upon the world, We will be found acceptable. Where He will say that we are good and faithful servants. Amen

Psalm 51 is the clearest and most sober cry of contrition and supplication for forgiveness by a believer, in the face of a judgment by the Almighty God, that we have in Scripture. It is David at his lowest. "A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba." We know the story. David doesn't go off to war as kings were expected to. He stays at his place and sees Bathsheba, the wife of his soldier, Uriah the Hittite, bathing on her nearby roof. Filled with lust, he has her. And as a consequence of that adultery, David conspired to have Uriah killed in battle, and wed his pregnant widow. Nathan confronts the King, and the Lord curses David for his sin; 2 Samuel 12:7–10 And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul; And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon. Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife. The judgment of God was given, the child should die. 2 Samuel 12:14–15 Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die. And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick. David fasts and prays and stays by the child's side, but in the end the illness takes the boy. 2 Samuel 12:18–19 And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead? But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead. David, devastated, cleans himself and goes into the house of the Lord to worship. It is in this context that this Psalm was written. Rather than a root of bitterness against the judgement of God, as many are tempted to take on in the face of such fierce judgement, David concedes and comes to the Lord, asking for mercy. As he has so often in Psalms, he begins in worship, praising God for His lovingkindness and mercy. Reminding himself, and the Lord of His great qualities, and appeals to the ultimate judge to blot out his transgressions. This is a formula of prayer that we should commit to our prayer life. Under better circumstances and joyous events, or in grave repentance and regret for whatever sins we have committed, the Lord should be approached in humility and meekness of spirit. Hallowing His holy name. The request is to forgive the confessed transgressions, knowing He is merciful and faithful to forgive His children. 1 John 1:9 If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. This same promise applies to believers, today. The sure knowledge that our heavenly Father is faithful to forgive us, even the sins of the level of David. To wash us throughly, to cleanse us. To blot the iniquity from our record, and heal us, and our relationship with God. But note, it is if we confess our sins. David acknowledged his transgressions. We cannot lie to God and we should not lie to ourselves. We cannot hide from our sin when we've faced judgment, and our conscience keeps the sin ever before us in guilt. The joy and benefit of the forgiveness of God comes in relief from that burden, and removing the fear of chastening, that comes from a contrite heart seeking His mercy. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight...that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest. David confesses that it is the transgression towards God that out him in judgment, and so he admits to God that not only has he sinned against Him, but that David acknowledges his understanding that God's judgments are right and deserved. Again, it is very common to see people in sin, when facing the judgment of God for it, to grow to resent Him and despise His judgements. To make excuses for their acts, to deny their intent, to place what has resulted from their wicked ways on the shoulders of a God whom they reject as judge. These people are destroyed with their bitterness, wracked with guilt, have a broken relationship with the God that bought them, and are often called home early, the result of their being incapable of being honest and appealing to His mercy. But David shows us the better way. David continues his confession; Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me. He uses hyperbolic language to say that he is a sinner, born of a sinner, in his appeal for mercy. There is much made of this passage, and all manner of doctrines that have been spun out of it. The primary being "original sin" as the idea that babies are born guilty, and condemned. But the very account being mentioned show that David did not believe any such thing. 2 Samuel 12:21–23 Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread. And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live? But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me. David, who knew he was redeemed by God, saved by faith, under the grace of the Lord, states plainly that he will go to be with his dead child in the end. That Heaven is their home. While Psalms are dripping with doctrine, we should still always compare scripture with scripture, and gain understanding by the totality of the Bible, rather than out of context proof texts. Continuing in Psalm 51, having established the context and getting the contention on the false doctrine of original sin guilt that comes from a shallow reading of the text, we see the purpose of the Psalm is the honest confession of a righteous man. David is not placing the blame of what he has done on anyone else, and accepts full responsibility for whatever God judges against him. His fear of the Lord has led him to Godly repentance and reconciliation. Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom. This is the meekness and honesty about our sin that God seeks, that in it, we can actually learn from Him and grow. We discussed in the previous Psalm 50 study that God doesn't seek the sacrifices and burnt offerings, but a meek and contrite heart. He is pleased as a Father when we come to Him for restitution and forgiveness. His mercy and grace are limitless, all He asks for is honesty in our heart. For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering. David confesses, and calls upon the Lord to purge him with hyssop, the sponge like plant that was used to apply the blood on the posts during the first passover, the same that was present when the Lord was crucified and they gave Him gall to drink. The washing of forgiveness by the blood of Christ is ours, that we become white as snow. Isaiah 1:18 Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool. David pleads to be made to hear joy and gladness, to be cheered by the power of God's word to heal the brokenness he feels from the Father's chastening. He asks God to hide His face from David's sins. To see them and remember them no more. To blot out his iniquity. We know as saved Christians that this promise of God, to forgive our sins past, present and future, that He will remember them no more and place them as far from us as east is from west, is our blessed hope in the redemption that is found in Christ. We take comfort in this truth when we are faithful to confess to Him; 1 John 1:7–10 But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us. This promise shows not only the faithfulness of God to forgive, but also that our sin in the flesh is not held against our ledger in Heaven. It is not imputed against those that are in Christ. 1 John 3:9 Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God. John is not contradicting himself by saying if we say we have no sin, we are liars and simultaneously saying we cannot sin, being born of God. He is describing the same feelings from the failure of the flesh David writes about here. When we sin, it is not the new man, created in Christ, but the flesh. Romans 7:15–17 For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I. If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good. Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me. Our flesh sins. If we deny that we are liars. But by being born again in Christ, we do not sin. The difference is that the flesh, which we can mortify to sin, and restrain from our lusts, is dead. Nailed to the cross with Christ. Galatians 5:24–25 And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit. Our spirit is quickened and covered by the imputed righteousness of Christ Jesus. It is His righteousness that covers our transgressions and the Spirit that seals us unto redemption. So David, in his sorrow and remorse reminds God of this truth, and by doing so, reminds himself. Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy Spirit from me. Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation and uphold me with thy free spirit. David is not writing that he is afraid to lose his salvation, but seeking the confidence in it again that has been marred by his transgressions and the fear from the chastening he has received. He is seeking to renew his relationship with God through his confession and appeals to mercy. And the purpose? Is it to selfish ends of not wanting to feel guilty and to get back on the blessings side of God? No. Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee. It is the mercy God shows us as His children that leads us to share His praise to others, that the lost see His light upon us and they glorify Him in Heaven. It is not only the wrath that leaves the world without excuse, but the peace that passes understanding we are given by getting right with the Lord. When He delivers us from our guilt, forgiving our sin, restoring our relationship as sons, we cannot help but sing aloud of His righteousness. The sinner who trusts Christ is celebrated in Heaven by all the hosts of God... Luke 15:7 I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance. ...How much more the prodigal son who returns to his Father? Luke 15:18–20 I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. The Father runs to meet his returning son, showering him with love. Before any confession of guilt or offer of penance or anything other than turning back towards God, the Father goes to him in comparison and restitution of their relationship. God wants to forgive us more than we want to be forgiven. And we rejoice in His grace, that we may shew forth His praise. Again, God doesn't want sacrifice. He doesn't want our works of penance and vows to change. He takes no delight in the ritual formulas of burnt offerings, and performative acts of contrition. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise. It is the healing of a loving relationship that He wants for us. Even at our lowest, we should remember this, and turn to Him again. It is then, in reconciliation and peace with God, through Christ Jesus our Lord, that the works we do and the praise we sing will please Him. Then will our religion match our hearts, in healing and in service to the mighty God. Amen

Psalm 52 is told to us as a Psalm written when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said unto him, David is come to the house of Ahimelech. The situation is described in 1 Samuel 21, David has fled Saul, who is determined to kill him. Consumed with pride and evil spirits, the king seeks the life of a man considered a hero among Israel. David seeks food and weapons at the Tabernacle in Nob, from the unsuspecting priest, Ahimelech. Ahimelech unwittingly provides David with the shew bread, and Goliath’s sword as David claims he is on a secret mission for the King. 1 Samuel 21:2 And David said unto Ahimelech the priest, The king hath commanded me a business, and hath said unto me, Let no man know any thing of the business whereabout I send thee, and what I have commanded thee: and I have appointed my servants to such and such a place. (An act that Jesus uses to justify His Apostles plucking corn to eat on the Sabbath. Matthew 12:3-4 Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him; How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?) But the priest isn’t the only person there to see David. 1 Samuel 21:7 Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD; and his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul. Now, Doeg is not a man of war. He is a herdsman. He oversees the other shepherds and wranglers for the King. But he took the opportunity of seeing David there in Nob, on the run, to curry favor with Saul. The story continues, showing David’s flight, ending up in Judah at the advice of the prophet Gad, bringing his parents to the King of Moab for protection, and gathering with him loyal men as he went. 1 Samuel 22:2 And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men. (This is a lovely picture of Jesus and salvation, the distressed and debtors gathering unto him.) Saul hears tell of these activities; 1 Samuel 22:6–7 When Saul heard that David was discovered, and the men that were with him, (now Saul abode in Gibeah under a tree in Ramah, having his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him;) Then Saul said unto his servants that stood about him, Hear now, ye Benjamites; will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make you all captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds; As Saul assembles his armies, Doeg enters the picture; 1 Samuel 22:9–10 Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub. And he enquired of the LORD for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine. We should note that much time has passed since David’s flight to Nob, and Saul has an idea of where David and his men have hidden, in the forest of Hareth, in Judah. But Doeg brings his knowledge to the King as he is already readying for war. It feels even more opportunistic and craven in light of that passage of time and the context. Doeg’s word causes Saul to summon the priest and his kin; 1 Samuel 22:11–13 Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests that were in Nob: and they came all of them to the king. And Saul said, Hear now, thou son of Ahitub. And he answered, Here I am, my lord. And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast enquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day? The hapless Ahimelech then pleads ignorance and asks that Saul understand that he had no way of knowing David fled the King. 1 Samuel 22:15–16 Did I then begin to enquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more. And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house. Saul refuses clemency. In his murderous rage he orders the death of the priest and entire lineage. 1 Samuel 22:17 And the king said unto the footmen that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of the LORD: because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the LORD. Even Saul’s loyal men hesitate and refuse the order of their King, out of fear of the Lord and harming His anointed priests. In the state the King was in, in the context of his twisted, murderous vengeance, the footmen feared God more. But not Doeg the Edomite. 1 Samuel 22:18–19 And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod. And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword. Does the shepherd, Doeg the herdsman, who brought out of date intelligence to Saul’s attention, jeopardizing the priest, that led to this situation, took full advantage of the license given him by Saul, and wickedly carried out the command. First slaying 85 priests, and then murdering every man, woman, and child, beast and all, found in the Levite city of Nob. One of the sons of Ahimelech escapes to see David, telling him of the wicked act done at the hands of Doeg; 1 Samuel 22:20–23 And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David. And Abiathar shewed David that Saul had slain the LORD’s priests. And David said unto Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father’s house. Abide thou with me, fear not: for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard. David’s guilt at not taking care of Doeg when he had the opportunity, and the resulting deaths, has him offer Abiathar refuge with him and his troop of men. David will have Abiathar act in his office, with the ephod, to consult with the Lord several times. Asking Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? will Saul come down, as thy servant hath heard? And later, enquiring of the Lord, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? Seeking the wisdom of God to direct his paths in times of uncertainty. David, in exile, is given the oracles of God through the Levite and ephod, as a King would. Saul, in his rage had cut himself off from this avenue of prophecy. As the sole survivor of the high priestly line of Eli, Abiathar brings the official religious authority of Israel to David’s camp, signaling that God has abandoned Saul. By using the Urim and Thummim in the ephod, Abiathar provides divine reconnaissance that saves David from Saul’s traps and ensures the defeat of the Amalekites. Abiathar serves as David’s high priest throughout his exile and reign, eventually helping bring the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem. During Absalom’s rebellion, Abiathar remains behind in Jerusalem to act as a secret agent, feeding David crucial intelligence through his son Jonathan to help win back the throne. The evil of Saul and the bloodthirst of Doeg, became good for David, who loved God and was called according to His purpose. But Doeg became a byword. Psalm 52 mockingly called Doeg a "mighty man," for slaying men of God, dressed only in linen, and helpless women and children, even babies. Doeg did what was unthinkable to the actual mighty men of Saul, after causing the entire situation by his obsequious talebearing. Immortalized in his wickedness by the psalmist, David. Psalm 52:1–3 Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God endureth continually. Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully. Thou lovest evil more than good; and lying rather than to speak righteousness. Selah. We can imagine Doeg’s fate, the Bible doesn’t speak specifically of what became of him afterwards, but Psalm 52 gives us some idea of his ultimate fate before God. Psalm 52:5–7 God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah. The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him: Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength; but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness. But by his evil, good came. David trusted in the mercy of the Lord, and was strengthened by Doeg’s actions, and was able to sing of the praises of the Lord because of it.

In Psalm 52, the psalmist presents the polar opposite of the contrite heart of Psalm 51, the mischief-making man who doesn't avail himself to the longsuffering mercy of God. The wicked and their deceitful tongue, inventing lies, telling slander against God and God's people, boasting of their blessings, not thankful but vain in their imagination, loving evil more than good, these are the men who continually reject the call to fear the Lord. Those of us who are saved can become incredulous at the prideful stance of the wicked, who reject the fear of God and lean on their own strength. We can often grow confounded and even depressed over the ways of the wicked. Like just Lot, living in Sodom, being afflicted by the wickedness around him 2 Peter 2:8 (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;) The Bible is not afraid to call these people out, directly and to their face. They are boastful, mockingly called "mighty men," liars, evil, haters of righteousness, lovers of slanderous and wicked words, lovers of mischief, having deceitful tongues. We should not fear to identify exactly the perverted in our midst when they reject and mock the gospel of God and the word we preach. Nor should we tiptoe around the heart of the matter; Their immanent destruction and the torment in the fire of Hell that awaits them. Jude 1:22–23 And of some have compassion, making a difference: And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh. Those who do not see the wrath of God revealed from Heaven upon others as a reason to repent and believe, and won't see the mercy and hear the praise of the meek, feeling the compassionate love of believers magnify God's grace, need hard preaching to let them know exactly what they've chosen, in hopes that they might be saved. That their love of devouring words will lead to God likewise destroying them forever. Literally, being devoured by flame and worm in outer darkness, forever. Eternal suffering at the hands of a just and mighty God. God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah. If "selah" is meant to be a pause, a moment to reflect on what was just sung or said, is there anywhere more fitting than in that moment, having heard that sobering truth? God will destroy you. He will take your life and root you out of the land of the living, to place you in a place of eternal destruction. And the righteous shall see their end and fear God, and laugh at the calamity they brought about on themselves. The end their mischief brought about, turned back upon them. Proverbs 26:27 Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him. The ironic nature of the bitter end experienced by the boastful sinner is often evident and clear to those that fear God. The humor of the Lord is appreciated by His children. We laugh at their calamity. When the wicked are made a parable or a byword among the people, it should give other men pause. The wrath revealed from Heaven should give instruction to the simple to turn towards God. It shows the righteous in Christ God's power and promise. Proverbs 1:7 The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction. The warning is ignored by the fool. And God will not be mocked. Proverbs 1:25–30 But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh; When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the LORD: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof. These men that did not trust in God, but made their own puny strength and their worldly, perishing riches their stronghold, will be brought low. By their evil deeds they seek to maintain power and control, and by the same they will be brought low by our God, Who is a consuming fire. But we are His. We have humbled ourselves to rely on His holy name. To be meek servants, poor in spirit, that we may receive His grace, and the abundance of life in His love. I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: and I will wait on thy name; for it is good before thy saints. They waited for Jesus, we look back to His cross and the glory of His resurrection. We shall praise His name among the people. We shall look at His mercy and wrath, and know He is our salvation. We will praise Him forever, as His saints. Amen

Luke 1:41-55 And it came to pass, that, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost: And she spake out with a loud voice, and said, Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For, lo, as soon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in mine ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy. And blessed is she that believed: for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord. And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord, And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name. And his mercy is on them that fear him from generation to generation. He hath shewed strength with his arm; he hath scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts. He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree. He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away. He hath helped his servant Israel, in remembrance of his mercy; As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever. God's promise to those that believe, to be blessed and the performance of all that He has given us by His word, is shown in His grace and mercy through the birth of Christ. Our God and Saviour. Just as Mary was blessed, and received the grace of God to save her, and was not ashamed. Just as Elizabeth and Zacharias were. So too are we blessed among men for the promise of God. Let our soul magnify the Lord. Amen

Who is God? Our creator. Our savior. Our comforter. By whom all things are made. Who spake all things into existence and breathed life into His creation, giving it light and form and substance, and He called it Good. He is the Father, and the Son and the Spirit and these three are one. God the Father has always been. Jesus has always been, and been with God and is God. His Spirit, the holy Ghost, has been upon man doing the Father's will, bringing all knowledge and wisdom, and coming as a Spirit, to indwell with man, as He indwelled the Tabernacle and the Temple, entering those who are saved, sealing us unto the day of redemption. These are the basic doctrines of God that we as Christians accept, given us by scripture that He spake unto the fathers by the prophets, by Christ in His ministry, testified by the Apostles through epistle and gifts of the Holy Ghost, and in these latter times by His complete and inspired word. But what are the attributes of God? Who is He? We often hear this; 1 John 4:8 He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love. And God is love. Hebrews 13:8 Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever. God is eternal, including the Lord Christ Jesus who has always been the Son, and always been the promise of God. John 1:1-5 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not. We are created in Their image. Genesis 1:26-27 And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. God's Spirit, He breathed life into us that were made, giving us individual souls. Genesis 2:7 And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul. And man fell, being flesh and having free will, when temptation came into the world. And so man needed a redeemer. And a promise was given that man may reconcile with God. Revelation 13:8 And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. Psalm 8:4-6 What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour. Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all things under his feet: For this is the promise of God, who is love and faithful above all. John 3:16 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. 2 Peter 3:9 The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance. The same faith of repentance towards God given all men, from the beginning. Genesis 4:26 And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD. And this promise shone like a light throughout the ages, the light of the Lord magnified by those who trusted in Him to be their salvation. 1 John 1:5 This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all. And because God is love, and in Him there is no darkness at all, God is Holy. Separate. Pure. He cannot stand the sight of iniquity. And man's heart is wicked and loves darkness more than light. Jeremiah 17:9 The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it? And this iniquity stirs the longsuffering God to wrath, and He scourges every son. Psalms 30:5 For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning. Numbers 14:18 The Lord is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression, and by no means clearing the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation. So what then? God is love. God is light. His word is true. He is Holy. He seeks reconciliation with all man, because God so loved the world. Because He is not slack concerning His promises. Because He is slow to wrath. Because He is quick to mercy. Because God is grace unto man. Isaiah 40:28 Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding. And in Him comes every blessing and gift, for all men. Even those that fail to believe His word. The rain falls on the just and the unjust alike. Ecclesiastes 9:11 I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all. James 1:17 Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning. But God promises to those who love Him, blessings. Romans 8:28 And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose. And those who obey His commands, rewards. 1 Corinthians 3:12-15 Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire. For we are His vessels, fitted to His purpose, that we in the Spirit may conform to do His will. Galatians 5:22 But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith... We, given the traits of the Spirit, magnifying the love found in God, whom we in His grace show forth His light to the world. Matthew 15:14-16 Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid. Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. And that light is to be a guide to bring others to the path of righteousness. A path God's word has given us to follow, with a promise of security, a foundation of stone, that we may always be able to trust to hold us up, to deliver us from tribulations. Psalms 18:30 As for God, his way is perfect: the word of the LORD is tried: he is a buckler to all those that trust in him. And to that end, we are sent the Holy Spirit. John 14:26 But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you. And this is promised to those who have accepted the free gift of salvation paid for by Christ Jesus. John 14:6 Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me. And so, knowing these things of God. The Father, Son and holy Spirit, longsuffering and true. Unchanging and eternal. Who is love. Who has provided us with life, all things in creation, knowledge and wisdom, comfort and reconciliation with Him, a calling and a purpose to do His will, rewards for our labor and strength in temptation, we are told not to fear. Isaiah 41:10 Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.

Dispensationalism in light of the Book of Romans. The events of the past week have seen an increase in the false claim that modern Jews occupying the Levant are the Israel of God, not saved believers. To defend this heretical garbage, those supporting this claim will use a handful of scripture, but they especially rely on Romans 11:26; And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob Stripped of context, this appears to support their false teaching, but luckily for us, we have the entirety of Romans to demonstrate why this interpretation is wrong, and frankly dishonest. For the next few days I am going to go over the building blocks for the arguments made by Paul in Romans to refute that reading of 11:26, once and for all. Starting today in Romans 1; Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God, (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,) Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ In Romans, the often abused epistle to the believers in Rome, Paul makes several arguments, and in the Spirit, these arguments build upon each other, each underpinning the next. Here in the opening greeting, Paul stipulated several important and fundamental points as a foundation of everything that follows. Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ, separated unto the Gospel of God. This is important. It isn't separation from; it isn't separation from the world, from sin, from his previous beliefs prior to salvation. It is towards something, with a purpose. And that something is not only the Gospel of Jesus in the sense we generally think of, the 4 books that tells us His life, teachings, death and resurrection, but Paul places the entire canon of scripture up to that point, the Old Testament as we refer to it, as the good news of God, because to Him all prophets gave witness. As Christ says; John 5:46-47 For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words? This is important to establish. Jesus being the fulfilment of the prophets and the oracles of God sets the context for everything that follows. Paul is going to give the final word on the Dispensation of Grace, and how it relates to both Jew and Gentiles. And this dispensation has been in effect from the beginning. It is of God, given in sundry times and diverse places to the fathers by the prophets, moved by the Spirit. The only new revelation is that it is Jesus who is called upon, the mystery of salvation that always existed, revealed in these last times, that all who call upon the name of the Lord are saved. The promise of God in Christ, His good news that He's been telling the patriarchs and the Hebrews in general, from the beginning, that Jews always had access to. They should know and have recognized who Jesus was. Paul then gives a concise rendition of that Gospel by which he and the Romans he is writing to (and we today), know we are saved: -Jesus was made flesh through the seed of David -Declared the Son of God with power. Many signs miracles and wonders. Raising the dead and healing the sick. Preaching the word with authority, etc, According to the Spirit of Holiness -And by the resurrection from the dead -By whom we received grace, apostleship, called of Jesus Christ. God became flesh and dwelt among us, was killed and raised from the dead as God promised, and all who answered the call are given the grace of God, the gift of eternal life. Called to follow Him and spread this good news to all nations. Establishing this foundation that is Christ, the common faith shared between the Apostle and the assembly of believers in Rome, who have never met, but share this singular set of beliefs. Just as we who are saved today have believed. All who believe those truths are given eternal life. No works, no turning from sin, no other conditions making us worthy of the grace. And not by being a certain ethnicity or people. It is all excluded because it is in Christ we are saved. That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me. That is the mutual faith, this recital of facts, the creed of the Gospel of Christ Jesus. Let us have comfort in that as we continue along. If you have added to this common faith, or taken from it, everything else that follows will offend you. Because the natural man receiveth not spiritual things. But, we who are saved and in agreement should be able to rightly divide the word of God as we move forward, comforted in this truth. I should also make clear here at the beginning that I am only going to rely on clear scripture, being guided by the layout of Paul's thesis in Romans. I am not going to get too far into the weeds of endless genealogies and Jewish fables, of who the modern state calling itself Israel are. While I have opinions and there are many brothers with strong ideas one way or another, we don't need to get into it to provide understanding of the Jews in light of the Bible. So forgive me if I don't bring up these tertiary ideas, and take some others that are likely wrong at face value for the exercise. Thanks 🙏🏻

The book of Proverbs is given to man, a gift of God with a very specific purpose. To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding; To receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, and judgment, and equity; To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion. Much of the book of wisdom is by Solomon, who God gave an abundance of wisdom and knowledge and understanding, who as King displayed this wisdom in ruling, making Israel great again. But in his personal life, not so much. It is astounding how we, as men, can hear God's word, know His word, study it, hear it preached, and yet still lean on our own understanding, rather than in all our ways acknowledging Him that He may direct our paths. A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels: To understand a proverb, and the interpretation; the words of the wise, and their dark sayings.The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction. God's word should lead us to fear Him. To respect His holiness, power, mercy and justice. His wrath and His judgments. This is what makes a man wise, our fearful respect for the Lord, and being doers of the word, increases our knowledge and faith. Solomon writes, My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother, these truths are from God, and it is every parent's responsibility to teach them to our children, that they be an ornament of grace upon their head, and chains about their necks. It is the greatest inheritance we can give our children. It is also a command: Raising them in the fear and knowledge of God, to bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. Continuing Proverbs 1, we see a warning against joining in another man's sin. Not being led to robbery and violence by greed. That ultimately, it ends in their own blood and death. Crime doesn't pay. Next, Solomon tells us of Wisdom, as a woman, though this is more the feminine of the word than a gendered being, and Wisdom is much like the Spirit of God, today. The original Hebrew word for wisdom, hokhmah, is a feminine noun, and Solomon will compare the virtuous woman of Wisdom to the harlot, the "strange woman," the folly of fools later in the book. But the literary device aside, like the male Spirit of God, He reproves and reproaches, and calls men to truth. Like God has done through the inspired word of the prophets, crying out, how long, ye simple ones? Scorners and fools reproofed. Wisdom is "poured out" in spirit. Calling us to repentance. God's words, the wisdom itself, made known unto us. As God promises to write the law in our inward parts. This echos so many passages, especially when Jesus rebukes the Jews; Matthew 23:37 O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Isaiah 65:2 I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts Those thoughts are foolishness. They set at naught His counsel. This crooked generation refused to accept His Wisdom, and so, He will laugh at their calamity. He will mock the. When their fear cometh. What a sobering thing to be mocked of the Lord. To get to the place where you've been given up and given over. When you are destroyed in His presence, cast into eternal torment, and God will laugh, because He gave you ample warning. The wrath of God being revealed from Heaven, that you had no excuse. But they didn't wish to retain God in their knowledge. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord But those who fear the Lord, and receive wisdom from Him, have a better promise; But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from fear of evil

Proverbs 2 continues the instruction on Wisdom, and The importance of accepting her as the truth of God. That Spirit of truth that we as Christians are given, so long as we receive it, walking in the Spirit, walking in God's word. We go to church to hear the word preached (faith cometh by hearing), as we incline our ear unto wisdom. Not being, as many are described in scripture, dull of hearing. We should rather be ready to hear and to keep it in our hearts, as doers of the word. We should seek the wisdom of God as it were silver, a treasure. More valuable than riches is the wisdom of God's commandments. Matthew 7:24 Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock A wise man cries for knowledge, and lifts up their voice for understanding. Asking God for His wisdom, like Solomon did. Ask and it shall be given you. Seek it and ye shall find. And with knowledge, understanding, and in doing what God says, we grow in faith. Hebrews 11:6 But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. The Lord giveth wisdom. Out of His mouth: Matthew 4:4 But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God. If wisdom proceeds out of the mouth of God, and we live by every word of God, and all scripture is given, inspired by God, written by holy men of God who spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost, we need to have a Bible that conveys all of them. That we may be perfect, complete and throughly furnished having everything we need. In English, this is found only in the authorized version of the King James Bible, the perfect and preserved word of God. Continuing Proverbs 2 we see the the Lord giveth wisdom, and the paths of judgment preserves the way of His saints. The paths analogy is used throughout Proverbs, and the way, is the doctrines of Christ. Early Christians were said to be followers of the way. We hear about keeping the old paths. God's word is a light unto out feet, and He directs our paths when we acknowledge Him. This understanding is very much the beginning of wisdom. Knowing where you've been and where you're going, seeing down the road. Knowing there's an end. Knowing the journey can lead you from the straight path, to the left or right. It is this understanding that gives us our first discernment, to see "If I continue this way, danger" knowing there are consequences "down the road." We see God's ways are not our own, but in His knowledge we get righteous judgement, to see every good path. The way. And that discretion preserves us, keeping us safe. Delivering us from the evil man, the froward who walk in paths of darkness. Or laying in wait on uncertain, or crooked ways. This discretion delivers us from the strange woman, the counterpoint of Wisdom. The strange woman forsakes the good paths, the ways of her youth, the covenant of God. Her paths lead to death. Wisdom's, to life. We are called to learn God's ways to avoid that snare. To walk the way of good men. To keep the paths or righteousness. And the promise of God is that, by keeping to Wisdom and her paths, we will be upright and true. His saints, sanctified in His Son. That we will dwell in the land. But the curse of those who don't keep the way, who choose the strange woman, and her paths of death; being cut off from the earth, and rooted our of it. Jude 1:12 These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots... Cast into the blackness of darkness forever.

Continuing in Proverbs 3, building on the understanding given already; that fear of God brings knowledge, His word brings discernment, and the Wisdom of God is the fruit of following His ways over our own. Following the way, walking His paths, being doers of the word and not hearers only, is Wisdom. But following other paths is like going in unto a strange woman, whose ways lead to death. But what are the advantages of knowing and keeping God's ways? Obeying His commandments? For length of days, and long life, and peace, they shall add to thee. God's commandments have promises. And it just makes sense that since the wages of sin is death, righteousness is life. Mercy and truth are the most precious of God's commandments. His mercy towards us shows the value of mercy to others. Truth guides us to judge righteous judgment. Jews today literally bind the words of the law to their arms, and in boxes on their forehead.
