They take the promise of finding favor of God and men for "binding" literally, and omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith. Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths. This is the key verse of Proverbs. The foundational understanding. Remember it, sing it, say it. And in everything acknowledge God first. Be not wise in your own eyes, don't lean on your understanding. Don't think to blaze your own trails and beat down your own paths. There is nothing new under the Sun and God's ways are the best ways. The old paths, tried and true. And following them brings health. And honoring the Lord by giving of your substance, your riches, the first portion of your increase, will bring prosperity. Note this isn't a prosperity gospel, but show that gratitude for the blessings He provides, and acknowledging Him first, will see our blessing compound. He rewards gratitude and hates murmuring. My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of his correction: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth. Gaining wisdom and understanding comes also from His chastening when we don't keep to His paths, when we stray to our own understanding. Like a mule that may wander off the path is whipped, so too are we chastened. And we should be thankful. Hebrews 12:7-8 ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons. Be happy in chastening. Delight in His law. Gain understanding, covet Wisdom the way men covet riches, because it is more precious than silver, gold or rubies or any of the merchandise of the world. Wealth cannot extend your life and give you health, not like the Lord can. And love of money is the root of all evil, and for covetousness sake come wars. But pursuing Wisdom brings life. Length of days is in her right hand; and in her left hand riches and honour. Her paths lead to peace. Wisdom is a tree of life! So by faith we step out on the paths, and keep the commandments, understanding the promises of God. The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth. Creation is by His knowledge and understanding. And knowing all things were created by His Word, through Christ Jesus, we see that Jesus IS the way, the truth, the light that is described throughout Proverbs. He is Wisdom. He is the tree of life. We are followers of the Way. We follow Jesus. And so we keep His word, we study His ways, we keep wisdom and discretion, with the promo that He gives us life to our soul and lays grace upon our necks. Safety in our walk, and sure steps along His paths. Though we walk through the valley of the shadow of death, we have no fear. We lay down to sleep, and sleep the sweet sleep of those resting under the Good Shepherd. In the arms of Jesus. The Lord is our confidence. Verse 27-32 can be summed up; Love thy neighbor. Give to him his due, good when it is in your power, loan to him freely when you can. Don't devise evil against him. Our neighbors dwell against us, locally. Jesus answers the question, "Who is our neighbor?" with the parable of the good Samaritan, leaning on this very wisdom. Our neighbors are those in our proximity who need help, and it is in our power to provide it. Love thy neighbor. Strive not with a man without cause. In the NT, Paul writes; Romans 12:8 If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. Love our enemies, certainly, but don't go out of your way to make one. Especially if they've done no harm to you. Don't be like the froward and oppressors, they are an abomination to the Lord. FRO'WARD, a. L. versus: turned or looking from. - Perverse, that is, turning from, with aversion or reluctance; not willing to yield or comply with what is required; unyielding; ungovernable; refractory; disobedient; peevish; as a froward child. Implacable, unmerciful, disobedient. It is as much an abomination to unreasonable and unyielding as being a sodomite, to the Lord. The Lord's curse will be on the house of the wicked. Vengeance is His. But the Lord blesses the household of the just. Those who work righteous judgement and show mercy. Peacemakers. The meek and lowly. This is wisdom. And as the meek inherit the earth and peacemakers are blessed, the wise shall inherit glory. While fools inherit shame.

Solomon continues giving the reader what is essentially a preface for the Book of Proverbs, that runs through chapter 9. The understanding of Wisdom vs folly, the good woman to be sought vs the strange woman, who leads to ruin. While there are plenty of wise sayings given in the first 9 chapters, including here in Proverbs 4, the thrust of Solomon's instruction is to emphasize this choice, and to encourage the pursuit of God's will, His paths, knowledge, discernment and Wisdom. He recalls his father David's instruction, stressing this idea. Keep my commandments, and live. Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth. Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee. Wisdom is the principal thing... She brings honor, promoting the wise, and more importantly, leads to a crown of glory through the ornament of grace. The pursuit of Godly wisdom is inextricably linked to accepting the truth of God in His gospel. The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, but the end of it is grace and glory. Note the urgency of David in instructing his son, reflecting in Solomon's own words to his sons, and by the Spirit, to we who are sons of God. This should be every parent's priority, too. Imparting this same understanding, that in wisdom is life, and that if you prioritize knowledge of God, you will not stumble, He will direct your paths, you have life in Him. Coupled with the warning to not follow after the wicked, the froward, the evil. Those who are only satisfied by mischief and by causing others to stumble. Taking pleasure in harming others. In violence. In offense. This is literally true, referring in previous chapters to those who rush to spoil and bloodshed. But it is also true of those who, rather than instruct children to go down the paths of Wisdom, instead mislead and bring children to offense. Luke 17:2 It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones. And so, like David to Solomon, the king urges his children to not let these sayings depart from them. To keep them. To not turn to the left or the right. To keep our heart with all diligence. To ponder the path of our feet. In all our ways acknowledging God, that He may direct us where to go. To keep on the Way. To remove our foot from evil.

Proverbs 5 continues the introduction section of the book of wisdom, and the near pleading of the father, Solomon, to his son, but in the Spirit, God the Father pleading with His children, to pay attention and listen to what He is teaching us. His instruction on chasing Wisdom, as knowledge and discretion, and warning of chasing after the strange woman of folly. But Solomon being the pen used by the Penman, the analogy given in this chapter of adultery serves as both a metaphor and practical application of chasing after women who aren't yours. Something the king with a thousand wives and concubines knows all about. So we can apply both literal and figurative and receive wisdom from both. The strange woman speaks sweet sayings, and is seductive in her ways, but her end is bitter and sharp. Deadly. God's paths are straight and knowable, a path of life, but her ways are moveable, ultimately unknowable. The Way is laid out and the light of that path is His word. The path of death shifts and moves and is full of snares and stumbling stones. Where you could think you know where you are and what lies ahead, and suddenly you're turned around and lost. In an adulterous relationship, this is also true. What may start in lust and be seen as temporary, often leads somewhere else, and far away. As they say: Sin will take you further than you want to go, keep you longer than you want to stay, and cost you more than you want to pay. Don't go looking for the strange woman. Don't seek out the folly of other men's understanding. It can cost you your honor, and take away years of your life to the service of the cruel, your wealth and labors to the stranger. Again, literally in the case of chasing after strange women, foreign women. Unsaved women. Women who are not your wife. In 1 Kings 11 we read, king Solomon loved many strange women...he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart. For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father. The wisest man in history, who wrote these warnings to his sons and to us, fell prey to the very thing he counseled against. Solomon may have written this in repentance and regret. He may have been in the midst of it. It could be before he succumbed to the temptation. But it is often true that the preacher preaches what he needs to hear, more than the audience. Verse 11 ties the literal back to the spiritual, and death and hell that awaits those who didn't fear God and seek after His Wisdom. The regret the fool will have as his flesh and body are consumed in never ending torment. How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof; And have not obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me! The shame in the midst of the assembly of being almost in all evil, when the books are opened in judgment...If physical death from a lifetime of bad choices and sin is heartbreaking, the regret in Hell for those that didn't harken to the gospel must be overwhelming. Solomon then compares fidelity to the wife of your youth, your first love, as with Lady Wisdom, to a fountain, to a well. To the cistern you dug. The waters are yours and you need not look for another source. Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth. Don't stray from your wife. Don't stray from the instruction of your fathers. Be ravished always with her love. Be satisfied in her. Our sins are before the Lord, He knows all our ways. A man's iniquities are the bonds he is caught in, the cords he is held with. Going after folly and rejecting instruction leads to a man's own sin binding him unto death.

Here in Proverbs 6, the instructions to his son continues, as we begin the meat of the advice Solomon, in the Spirit, gives. The wise sayings and understanding that come from the Lord though the king. Starting with financial advice. If you act as surety for a friend, pay it. If you make a deal and agree to it, make good on it, but if you can, don't act as another man's guarantee on a loan, and if you have, don't even sleep until you can humble yourself to get out of the trap, and deliver yourself. Don't be lazy. Don't be a sluggard. Consider the enterprising ant. Napping and laziness leads to poverty and want. Stay from the naughty, the froward. They wink, they are shifty and steal. They are constantly plotting mischief and love to get people wound up and set against one another. Don't be like them. Their destruction is sure. The 7 things God hates; proud looks, lying, hands that shed innocent blood, hearts that devise wickedness, feet swift to mischief, a false witness and sowing discord among the brethren. This is what a naughty or froward man is. These are traits of being froward. Take heed not to be proud, not to lie and bare false witness against others, plotting evil schemes to sow discord, to commit violence, to do these things, especially for your own profit is to be an abomination before the Lord. Many do it to just take pleasure in the chaos they create. My son, keep thy father's commandment, and forsake not the law of thy mother: Bind them continually upon thine heart, and tie them about thy neck. This appeal to listen to the good and Godly word, given by your parents, the instruction in righteousness, and to keep them in your heart, and allegories like it are found frequently in Proverbs. It is a source cited by Jews to defend their practice of "phylacteries." Matthew 23:4-5 For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers. But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments, Pharisees and scribes exaggerated religious symbols, specifically phylacteries (small leather boxes with scripture inside them, worn on the forehead and straps with scripture worn on their shoulders and wrapped in their arm, called tefillin) and garment tassels (tzitzit) to appear more pious and draw attention to themselves, rather than truly living God's law. They made the command literal, rather than in the spirit of how it was given. They lose sight of the words and living them, not being doers of the law. Being led by the law, on God's paths, going His way, is the meaning behind it. That when you sleep, when you wake, His word talks with you. This is so true. When we wake in the night, if we walk in the Spirit and stay in the word, our idle thoughts become more focused on Him, and prayer and pondering His word. When we don't it is easy to have the cares of this world and fear and sin knocking at the door. The commandment is a lamp, a light to your feet. Reproofs of instruction are the way of life. The way, the path, the road God wants us to walk on, that we may live. Solomon again applies this wisdom and the strait path of God's way, to being tempted by strange women. Still an analogy of foolishness, but also the very real danger of sin. Keep God's word, the law of your mother handed down to you, near in your thoughts and heart, to keep thee from the evil woman, her flattering tongue, beguiling the young man. Lust not after her beauty in thine heart... Matthew 5:27-28 Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery: But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. Jesus' words are the words of God. He is not doing away with the law, He isn't really adding to it, but clarifying the word and wisdom He gave to Solomon by the Holy Spirit. Giving further understanding. Because, the way of the harlot is tempting. Her lips and eyes, a trap. Men are ruined by these lusts. The adulteress hunts for the precious life, to take wealth and honor from the foolish man. Today, how many married men are taken in by pornography, Only Fans whores, and internet cat fishing schemes? Lust of the eyes is a powerful thing. Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned? The horrible sin of coveting your neighbors wife, going in to her, laying with her, it's an evil thing before God. And it is so easily avoided. Drink from your own cistern. Delight in the wife of thy youth. Don't look upon the strange woman with lust. God says that a thief is less condemnable because he can pay back what he stole. An adulterer can only give his life to be satisfied by the jealous husband.

Again, Solomon appeals to his son to take heed to wisdom, to bind it in his heart. To keep the commandments he's given him that he may live. The law as the apple of his eye. Making wisdom and understanding your sister and kinswoman that they keep you from the strange woman, which is death. To illustrate, he gives a parable of a young man, void of understanding, who encounters a woman dressed as a harlot, who subtly entices him to bed. He says such a woman is loud and stubborn and exists on every corner, just as folly and temptations are around every bend in the way. She catches him, kisses him and saying she's holy, having made her offerings and confirming her vows, she beguiles him. Sheep's clothing for a ravenous wolf. She appeals with flattery, she sought him special, seeking to find only him, while she is a snare to any who cross her path. She appeals with the lust of the flesh. With enticing sensual carnality. Perfumed bed, preciously adorned to spend the night in passion. To take the fire to his bosom. To spark that desire in his heart. She says the Goodman of the house is not home, and gone for a long journey...making it illicit and adultery. There likely is no "goodman" as a harlot keeps no husband. But there is an allegory here for sin and the temptation that judgment of God is afar off. The Goodman which is Christ, not here. Similar to the warning of complacency Jesus gives us; Matthew 24:44-51 Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh. Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season? Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing. Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods. But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; And shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of, And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. There is an allure to this idea, that we may justify sin by the distance of judgment. By the illusion of safety given by distance and time. But all who are fooled by this are found out. And so; With her much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him. Temptations often come through flattery and fair speech, the things we make rationalizations with, like weaving a net for a snare. And the fool falls headlong into it. Until they get trapped. The dart in the liver. The knife taking their life. Like a bird in a net. This parable, taken literally, has played out innumerable times. We may all know simple young men who have fallen for it. But allegorically, it is true of folly, of rejecting wisdom for sin. For rejecting God's path of life to go our own way. For she hath cast down many wounded: yea, many strong men have been slain by her. Her house is the way to hell, going down to the chambers of death.

Proverbs 8 (& 9), are an Ode to Wisdom, the Word and Spirit of God, with Him in the beginning , through Whom all creation was made. Wisdom cries out from all creation, from the top of the mountains, in the high places and in the paths. The Lord's way is wisdom. In the coming and going of the city. At its gates and doors. Like God calls to all men, as Jesus lifted up, wisdom calls out to all. To the simple and fools. To those who love wisdom and seek her excellent things, her right things. To those that seek truth. John 14:6 Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me. Matthew 7:7 Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you John 8:32 And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free The words of wisdom are the word of God, and there is nothing perverse or froward in them. Holy and plain to those that listen. More precious than any treasures, wisdom is better than gold. With wisdom dwells prudence; Wisdom applied to practice. Discernment and action according to knowledge. The wise hate evil; pride and arrogance, froward mouths they hate. By wisdom kings and princes rule. I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me. The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom. Psalm 63:1 O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is The Lord's wisdom is from everlasting, His word. Before all creation, He is. Eternally with Him, as one brought up together. John 1:1-2 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. Blessed is the man who finds wisdom. They receive life and favor of the Lord. They live in His grace. But woe to those that hate wisdom. All they that hate me love death. No surviving canonical list from the first three centuries includes the deuterocanonicals as part of the closed Old Testament canon. The earliest inclusions appear in 4th-century sources. Here is a popular poem used to teach the books of the Bible. Concerning the Genuine Books of Divinely Inspired Scripture But let not extraneous books seduce your mind, For many malignant writings have been disseminated. Accept, O friend, this my approved number. The historical books are twelve in all: First, Genesis; then Exodus; Leviticus next; Numbers; Deuteronomy; then Joshua the son of Nun; Judges, and Ruth the Moabitess with it; The four books of the Kings; and two of Chronicles; Then Esdras, first and second [Ezra-Nehemiah]. Then Job the sufferer, Psalms of David the singer, The Proverbs of Solomon, Ecclesiastes, And the Song of Songs, the bridal chamber of the bride. The twelve [minor] prophets as one book, then Isaiah, Jeremiah with Lamentations, Ezekiel, Daniel. Now count also the books of the New Mystery: Matthew indeed wrote for the Hebrews the wonderful works of Christ, Mark for Italy, Luke for Greece, John, the great preacher, for all, walking in heaven.[Gospel of John and Revelation of Christ] Then the Acts of the wise apostles, And fourteen Epistles of Paul, And seven catholic epistles, of which James is one, Two of Peter, three of John again, And the last is the work of Jude the kinsman of Christ. This is the sure canon of the divinely inspired Scriptures. Anything beyond these is not genuine. - Gregory of Nazianzus (c. 329–390)

Proverbs 9 concludes the preface of Proverbs, the instruction of Solomon to his son on Lady Wisdom and the strange woman of folly. Wisdom's table is set for the feast, her house ready, her wine mingled (the restoration of the preserved fruit of the vine mixed with water, spiced with myrrh, sweetened with honey), her maids sent to call all who would enter in to come. Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him, Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled. The unadulterated truth of God's word is that wine. The bread which has come down from heaven is Jesus. John 6:32-36 Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world. Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread. And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not. Her maidens calling out to the feast of Wisdom as the parable of the wedding feast: Luke 14:16-23 Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many: and sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready. And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused. And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused. And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come. So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind. And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room. And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled. Just as both the simple and the wise are compelled to turn hither to Wisdom's feast, so too the gospel is for both good and bad; So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests. Matthew 22:10 So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests. Jesus crying out in the streets, telling all to come to Him; John 7:37-38 In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. Forsake the foolish and live! Whosoever will, let him come. Revelation 22:17 And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely. The invitation of God to wisdom, to knowledge and understanding, is the invitation to life; as a wedding feast laid out by the host. Where the wise enters into the meal already prepared. The wine mingled. The wedding clothes, laid out, white and pure. To eat that bread of life and drink that living water, never to hunger or thirst again. Solomon then gives this instruction; Forsake the foolish, and live. He says to not reprove a scorner, to not rebuke the wicked. This is echoed in the way Christ gave to His disciples when sending them out to the lost sheep of Israel; Mathew 10:14 And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet. As Paul instructs Titus; Titus 3:10 A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject These men oppose themselves. Peter writes that we should not argue with scoffers; Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing. 1 Peter 3:16 Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ. When we are out in the hedges and highways, compelling all to come to the wisdom of God, by His gospel, we aren't there to argue. To debate. We are not supposed to waste our time with scoffers and mockers and scorners of the truth. We are supposed to shake the dust and move on. But, if we give instruction to the wise, they will be wiser. Those seeking the truth will hear us. They will understand that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the holy is understanding. And by His wisdom, our days are lengthened, our life increased. It is on every man to bear this. To the wise, for themselves and to life; for the scorner, to themselves unto death. This is individual soul liberty. We carry our own guilt and are responsible. But by faith we enter into His grace. In contrast to the feast of wisdom and the prudence of going forth to invite all, the strange woman sits at the door of her house, and calls to those who cross her path. She calls to the simple, that so often turn in to her. And, to the wise, she tempts them. Rather than with the sumptuous feast of wisdom, she offers the lure of covetousness. Of the appeal to the evil of the heart. Stolen waters are sweet, and secret bread pleasant. The heart that desires that which isn't theirs can guide even the wise to folly and sin. As the Lord said to Cain, if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. Sin becomes a master unto you. Those that enter in to folly, to sin, wise and fools, enter into death, for her guests are in the depths of Hell.

This is why it's important not to get into arguments with people whose entire premise is false. Who aren't arguing in good faith. They aren't looking for an honest debate they just want to justify being scornful or railing against you. It's one thing to rebuke or reprove and move on. But it's another to get dragged down into the mire with them. It's okay to walk away. To leave a chat or to block someone. That doesn't mean that you're admitting defeat as they would like to believe. It means you're not giving that which is holy to dogs.

Proverbs 10 begins the more familiar listing of wise sayings, made in the Spirit by Solomon, his proverbs. But the lesson contrasting the righteous listening to instruction, being industrious, refraining from speaking evil and being wise, with the fool who is lazy, full of iniquity and violence, with a froward mouth, continues to be the primary theme carried over from the introduction in chapters 1-9. Verse 1 contains an eternal truth that any parent could attest to. Establishing early the wisdom to found is accurate and true. A wise son is the pride of a dad, while the foolish son is the heaviness and sorrow of his mother. From this base, the sayings stack up, precept upon precept, truth on truth. Building a foundation of wisdom that, sadly is lacking in the world today, because most, even many Christians, don't harken to the word of God. They do not fear Him, and so do not have His wisdom to rely on. They do not acknowledge Him in all their ways, and so He isn't there to direct their paths. There are also proverbs given that have become ingrained in the secular lexicon (even if they don't acknowledge it). Such as the first half of verse 2; Gain made by wicked deeds profit nothing. In other words, crime doesn't pay. But the wise counter to this truth is that the way of the righteous delivers one from death. We are told the truth of the Lord that He will provide for His own, the righteous won't famish, while He destroys the substance of the wicked. Not a prosperity gospel, but the understanding that when you walk in the Spirit, working in righteousness, the Lord will take care of your basic needs. Luke 12:27-31 Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith? And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind. For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things. But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you. This is a promise of Christ Jesus Himself, with the caveat that the poor often are that way by being slackers, not diligent in their works. 2 Thessalonians 3:10 For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat. God blesses those that prepare, gathering in the summer against the winter is wise. Sleeping through the harvest is a shame. Being forward thinking and considering the end of something, understanding consequences, cause and effect, is wisdom. Shortsighted sin leads to shame. Of course, the harvest analogy is not just applicable to agrarian cultures, or to earthly financial goals, but also the sharing of the gospel of Christ's Kingdom is frequently likened to the harvest. John 4:35 Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest. Go soul-winning! The workers are few and the harvest is plenty. He that winneth souls is wise. Psalm 126:6 He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him. But the sluggard who buries his talent of silver, to mix metaphors, he will be ashamed. He will not have sheaves of glory to rejoice in. Being a just man, fair and merciful, extending grace to others, brings blessings and glory. The Lord will esteem the name of the just but the fool will die unknown, they will fall. Walk upright, consider what you say. Don't be a prattling fool or a subtle and froward man, or a man of violence and offense, stirring up strifes and hatred. Knowing love covereth all sins. 1 Peter 4:8 And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins. Wisdom is for the lips of the man with understanding, the rod is for the back of those without it. The wise lay up knowledge against the future, keeping instruction, but the fool is always near destruction and refuses to be corrected. The chapter is rich with promises for the righteous, including the desires of those walking the path of the Lord being granted, while the wicked do without and live in want and fear. Mark 11:24 Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them. Psalm 37:4-5 Delight thyself also in the Lord: and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart. Commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass. The consistent promise of God for those that trust in Him is repeatedly given throughout the Bible. But seek the treasure in Heaven, not riches on this earth. Opportunity to serve God, to win souls, to help the poor and heartbroken. To judge the fatherless. Ask for this treasure and you will be blessed beyond measure. The fear of the Lord prolongs your days. Brings knowledge and understanding. Provides for your needs and will grant you your desires. A wise man watches what He says, giving wisdom and speaking truth. The mouth of the wicked is perverse. The way of the Lord is strength to the upright: but destruction shall be to the workers of iniquity. The righteous shall never be removed: but the wicked shall not inhabit the earth. Amen

The main themes presented in chapter 11 see the ways of the righteous compared to the transgressor, in matters of finance, fortune and benefit, and spiritual gain. The delight of the Lord in our keeping of integrity and honesty in our dealings. Just measures, not cheating others, being upright in our dealings. God places an emphasis on our doing well for others when we could, in secret, selfishly gain at their expense. Doing good when no one is watching, while the froward man's perverse ways destroy them. He warns that pride leads to shame and humility shows wisdom. How often have we seen pride lead to an almost immediate fall? In our own lives alone! Embarrassed and ashamed when we are puffed up. But walking in humility, we receive glory from God and others. Solomon's wisdom shows a repeated contrast between the righteous being delivered and the wicked destroyed. That the generosity of the righteous builds up more wealth, the liberal soul made fat. Not only in this life, but the next. Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death, reminds us that at the judgment, all the wealth in the world will do nothing to spare the wicked from wrath. Only the righteousness that is in Christ can. We are not appointed to wrath, by His mercy and imputed righteousness. The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead. And so we should put the Kingdom first in our hearts; Matthew 6:19-21 Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. A warning that those that hoard and withhold being generous, or not selling their excess, will lead to poverty and worse in the day of judgement. God loves a cheerful giver and sees fair and just enterprise as good. But hoarding and coveting, helps no one. Luke 12:16-21 And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits? And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods. And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided? So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God. In the judgment, the hope of the wicked perishes, they shall not go unpunished. Their expectation is wrath. While the just and righteous shall be delivered. The righteous, those who are fair, just, walking upright, speaking truth, walking in the way of the Lord, not only benefit themselves, but their community. Their city rejoices in them. They bring prosperity to their people. They are a blessing. The wicked, however, curse their neighbors and overthrow their city. Being void of wisdom and unable to give counsel, despising their neighbors, bring destruction. They reveal secrets and are quick to mischief, and people suffer for their evil. He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it: and he that hateth suretiship is sure. In Proverbs 6, we saw Solomon warning against surety, for a friend or a stranger, and here we see a similar warning. The seeming contradiction, that one who disfavors backing another's debts is seen by God as more sure than one who gives their pledge for a stranger. That they will regret it. The only surety we can count on is God's. In scripture the Holy Spirit is described as the "earnest" or seal guaranteeing a believer's eternal inheritance and salvation. The surety of our eternal life. Ephesians 1:12-14 That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ. In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory. Because our surety is covered by the finished work of Christ, and sealed by the ernest payment of the Spirit, we can count on it. But for the stranger, we shall smart for it. Finally, we are also given instruction in character. That gracious women are honorable, but women without discretion are not. That strong men retain their riches and merciful men do themselves good. The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness shall be a sure reward. How do we scatter righteousness? Winning souls. The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise. The spiritual application to being one who scattereth, sowing righteousness, winning souls and bearing fruit, not hoarding our corn but blessing others...is again agrarian language as a parable for spreading the gospel. The greatest wisdom and counsel one can share. A blessing to those that receive it, and laying up treasure in Heaven for those that freely give it. And this is the promise of God for our efforts; Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.

Proverbs 12 opens with another reminder that loving instruction and knowledge is precious, and the way of righteousness, while hating correction and wisdom is brutish and wicked. And verse two reiterates that a good man - the just, wise, fearful of God who seeks after knowledge and walks in His ways, obtains favor from the Lord, but the wicked are condemned. Proverbs 9:10 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding. Hebrews 11:6 But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. Romans 10:17 So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Romans 5:1-2 Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God. Ephesians 2:8 For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God... We see how a man is made good, by the fear of God and hearing of His word, by faith seeking Him and truth, and by faith we have access to His grace, we obtain the favor of the Lord, receiving His gift of salvation. The consistent gospel message of Proverbs cannot be overlooked. Wickedness cannot establish a man, but the root of Righteousness, that is Christ Jesus, shall not be moved. He is the "root of Jesse" and a "branch of righteousness" (Isaiah 11, Jeremiah 23:5-6), established as the foundational righteousness for all believers. Through faith, believers are grafted into this root, allowing them to bear the fruit of righteousness, by the precious seed of His word. Romans 11:16-18 For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Dispensationalists will claim the root is Israel, but it has always been Christ. Just as Catholics will claim Peter, "a stone," is the rock, which actually is the profession that Jesus is Christ. Because no other foundation can be laid; 1 Corinthians 3:11 For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. All wisdom leads to Christ. Matthew 7:24-25 Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock. Much of the chapter gives a contrast of the righteous and the wicked. The fruit of righteousness produces a stable, life-giving outcome: right and just thoughts, words that deliver and bring deliverance, enduring houses and legacies that stand firm, wisdom that earns commendation, compassionate regard even for beasts, roots that yield true fruit, escape from trouble, satisfaction from good speech and diligent hands, truth that establishes forever, joy for those who counsel peace, protection from evil, delight in the sight of God, excellence over neighbors, and ultimately leading to eternal life without death. While the fruit of the wicked proves destructive and fleeting: deceitful counsels, words that lie in wait for blood and ensnare through transgression, overthrow and utter disappearance, perverse hearts deserving despise, cruel even in pretended mercy, desire only for evil nets, snaring by their own lips, momentary lying tongues, hearts filled with imagined evil and mischief, abomination through lying lips, seductive ways that lead others astray, and a path ending in no lasting good and death. We see that even in how we treat animals, livestock, pets, our heart is revealed. And the sad truth that even as we excel over our neighbors by our seeking first the ways of God, many would rather choose to chase lies and false promises of the wicked. The diligent and the hard worker will bear rule, have precious substance, while the slothful is ruled over and eats rotten raw meat. That a man hated but established is better than a braggart with nothing to show for it. That a virtuous woman is desired above a shameful woman. These lessons of life and how to live it are a blessing of the grace and mercy of the Lord. His words are the rock which we can build upon, knowing it shall never move.

Proverbs 13 opens and closes with very similar sayings, bookended thoughts that go well together. A wise son heareth his father's instruction...He that spareth his rod hateth his son. A scorner heareth not rebuke...He that loveth his son chasteneth him betimes. These concepts all go together. A scorner is that way because his father didn't love him enough to scourge him. A wise son listens because his father cared enough to apply the rod. In the same manner, the Lord often applies His wisdom by the rod, and humility and understanding of consequences comes with each stroke. Hebrews 12:4-8 Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin. And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons. God is a loving Father. When we have forgotten the instruction of our parents, when we wander from His paths and neglect His word, we are rebuked of Him. If we aren't, we should wonder are we sons or bastards. Are we wise sons or scorners? I know from experience that the Lord chasteneth betimes, that is early and as needed. And we should endure it with joy, knowing He is our Father, and take heed to His instructions, as wise children. Similarly, verse 2 mirrors verse 25, and you can see why those that applied the numbering for our benefit saw it fitting to cap chapter 12 here. A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth: but the soul of the transgressors shall eat violence... The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked shall want. God ties our physical and spiritual fullness and satisfaction to our words; the righteous man speaking goodly words has what they need, but the wicked transgressors receive only violence and destruction, and are ever wanting. He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life, but he that openeth wide his lips? Destruction. It is a bitter end to the wicked. As the chapter goes on we see the end of their ways is always sure; hunger, shame, overthrown in violence. Their lamp put out. Proud, contentious. The wealth of vanity diminished. A hard way ending in nothing but death. Their folly revealed to all. Subject to mischief, given poverty and shame. Destroyed by their choice of foolish companions. Pursued by evil, their wealth taken to repay the just for the wicked's trespasses. Their savings a ransom for themselves. They end up destroyed for want of judgement. They didn't listen to the instruction of their father. They didn't take to the reproof from God. Now the wise son, who takes instruction and reproof, who learns from the word and the scourging, his end is sweet. A good father who loves him enough to instruct and chasten. A God who does the same. This results in prudence and discretion, diligence in labors, rejecting the way of the sluggards. Hatred of lying, keeping in the upright way, watching their tongue, what proceeds from their lips. Matthew 15:11, 17-20 Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man...Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught? But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies: These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man. The light of the righteous man does shine and those that receive it rejoice, the wisdom of good counsel, rewards all who harken to it. Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed: but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded. This gospel theme continues to be hammered in Proverbs, and the spiritual application of this wisdom is undeniable, but the practical meaning cannot be ignored. God tells us over and over of the reward of obedience to His commandments. The long life, the blessings and the abundance of wealth all come to those who are wise and fear the Lord, and His commands. His promises are sure: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death. This good understanding brings favor. God's grace, making our way easier. The sinners life is hard. Diligence is rewarded, but this wise trait is often coupled with the wisdom of delaying gratification. Putting off their desires, knowing a greater reward awaits. Knowing to scatter the seed, in anticipation of a later harvest. Building up stores to the winter, but being generous with what you have, not being too short sighted to miss how that benefits you in the long run. How to wait patiently on the Lord. The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul...Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life. Hard work pays off. Quick riches fade but he that gathers by labor gains increase. Low time preference is the behavioral tendency to delay immediate gratification in favor of future, long-term rewards. It reflects a patient, disciplined, and forward-thinking mindset that values hard work, prudence, acquiring knowledge and understanding, and it is a sign of wisdom. The foolish are sluggards, they have high time preference and are easily tempted into sin. They covet, they seek mischief and violence, they gain their wealth by vanity, only to loose it. When they do store up against the future, they allow their greed to keep them from using it wisely, and it corrupts and rots, it's turned over to the just to recompense for evil, and is stolen or lost - destroyed for want of judgement. This lesson of wisdom and folly being the vision of long term rewards vs immediate gratification creates a seeming contradiction in Proverbs 13:7: There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches. How can a man make himself rich and have nothing, or poor and have everything? By faith in Christ Jesus. Matthew 5:3 Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Mark 8:36-37 For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul? Matthew 19:24 And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. God is not opposed to earthly riches, to financial gain for His children. Proverbs is filled with calls to diligence and wisdom, that it be well with us and promises of substance and wealth if we do well. Job and Abraham and Solomon were incredibly wealthy in their day. It isn't the wealth we gain but what we do with it. Being poor of spirit, that we humble ourselves before the Lord. Being filled with gratitude and delayed satisfaction, liberal and generous with what we have, putting other's profit above our own. Being financially poor is not always a sign of wickedness. But the ways of the wicked lead to poverty and shame. The poor heareth not rebuke. But the poor man may be wise and rich in Christ. The rich man may be so by wisdom, but it is harder for one with riches to do what's right. It isn't the wealth but the spirit of a man. It isn't their gain but what they do with it. It isn't the riches but where your treasure is. This is not a contradiction, but discernment and Wisdom. Wealth isn't the point, but the willingness to follow the word of God, and to be satisfied with what He provides. Philippians 4:11-13 Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. Amen! This is so important for parents to understand. Don't spare the rod!

"We're not talking about them leaving a certain congregation or a certain church. What we're talking about is them leaving the faith, leaving the faith in general. We're talking about people who they leave and now all of a sudden they're joining another religion. Okay. So if somebody leaves our church and goes and joins the Mormon church, we would, I believe all agree based on this scripture and other scriptures, we would say that person was never saved in the first place, period. Because if they'd been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us. You know, Jesus talked about how his sheep, they hear his voice, they know the shepherd, a stranger will they not follow, a stranger will they flee from for they know not the voice of strangers. And of course the LDS church, that's the voice of strangers. That's not the voice of the shepherd. That's not biblical Christianity. You know, once you're saved, you have the Holy Spirit living inside of you to guide you into all truth. You're not going to sit there and just join a false religion. I'm a Hindu now. I'm a Buddhist now. We would say, Hey, you were never saved in the first place. If somebody said, I'm an atheist now, I'd say you were never saved in the first place. If somebody said, you know, Oh, well, I'm Roman Catholic now. I'm Eastern Orthodox now. We had, look, we had a family that came to our church for almost a year and then left and joined the Russian Orthodox church. I have zero doubt in my mind that those people were not saved because no saved, born again Christian is going to go join the Russian Orthodox church, which is way, way out there from biblical Christianity, super pagan and not even close to being the gospel of Jesus Christ. Salvation by faith, not even close, way, way off the mark. I would look at that situation and say, they went out from us, but they were not all of us for if they had been of us, they would no doubt. How much doubt is there? No doubt that they would have continued with us. And again, we're not talking about physically continuing with us. We're talking about spiritually."

Continuing in Proverbs 14, we are given several wise sayings, often repeating the points to really drive them home. Archetypes of wisdom contrasted with the folly of fools and warnings against liars. The wise builder, embodied especially in the "wise woman" of verse 1 who "buildeth her house," representing constructive, diligent wisdom that strengthens family, home, and community, where the foolish woman destroys her home, as plucking a hen. Bit by bit. Again, we are told the upright fear the Lord. This healthy respect for God is the source and substance of wisdom. But those on the crooked ways of the perverse hat the Lord. They have been made to know the truth, by the wrath of God revealed from Heaven against the ungodly, but they hate Him and truth. Romans 1:28 And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient God will give the wicked what they desire, and by rejecting them utterly, give them over to their perverse ways to their own destruction. The fool speaks out because of pride, but the wise keeps their lips quiet when insulted. This is a hard one for many, including myself. Hard to remain quiet when being falsely accused and raised on or our pride is attacked. But Jesus showed us the way; Matthew 27:11-14 And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest. And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. Then said Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee? And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly. Humility in the face of accusations is often the most potent defense. Counterintuitive but like much of God's wisdom, it goes against man's understanding. Where no oxen are, the crib is clean: but much increase is by the strength of the ox. There are tradeoffs in life, and we are better for it. Sometimes, to get things done you have to be willing to shovel the dung. Another example of delaying gratification to your betterment. Faithful witnesses do not lie, but a false witness will. It seems obvious, and repeated in verse 25: A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies. When given the opportunity, we should remember the deliverance we received, and speak truth to deliver others. This is pleasing to God and foundational in the 10 Commandments. Thou shall not bear false witness. A scorner seeketh wisdom and findeth it not... reminds me of the false teacher, a reprobate who Paul describes in 2 Timothy 3:7 Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. How can they, without the fear of God? How can they when they scoff at truth and hold it in unrighteousness? When they hate God rather than fear Him? So we should reject the foolish man when you perceive he does not have knowledge. Again, flee a false prophet or someone claiming to know who just spouts nonsense. They ultimately will lie and speak falsehoods and defend their pride. They make a mock of sin, joking about evil ways. Flee these people. Don't take company with them, and don't try to sift any knowledge from them. They may be right about something, but in the end it isn't worth the rest that comes with it. The heart knoweth his own bitterness; and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy. No one but you and God can know the heartache or the joy you feel in your heart. Truly know it. And you can't know another's, even when you empathize or rejoice with them. It's an important thing to keep in mind when others deal with you, or you're dealing with others. Have grace because of this limitation, and thank God for it, too. If our heart were open to men, it could be embarrassing and shameful. Thank God we don't actually wear our hearts on our sleeve. Again, in verse 11 we see the wise builder's tabernacle flourishes when the wicked's will be overthrown. Not the structure, tent of building but the nature of the home. The family. There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death. God's ways are not our ways. Our heart is deceitful and wicked. The things we think are right or the things of God we see as counterintuitive, often lacks perspective. Longview. Or are based on lies we tell ourselves to justify our sin. Prideful and graceless. Even the things we may laugh at, the Bible says, our heart remains sorrowful. Even in mirth is heaviness. Who can know man's heart? And so, The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man shall be satisfied from himself. When we fall into sin, leaving the good path of the Lord, backsliding from whatever progress we have made, not walking in the Spirit but our own desires, we are filled with our own judgement. A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones. We should be mindful of our heart, to keep it sound. To limit what we give into when we heed it. To know the spirit where what we desire comes from. Remember the poor. Do not despise them, as we are poor in spirit and God gave to us abundantly. As Jesus said; Matthew 25:35-40 For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. And the promises of God to repay, that when we give to the poor we lend to the Lord. Psalms 41:1 Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble. And again, in verse 32 we see the gospel in Proverbs, the righteous has hope in our death. That blessed hope of eternal life in Christ Jesus. This is wisdom, to hear and believe the truth of God's mercy and grace, by the imputed righteousness of Christ. Because righteousness exalteth a nation and sin is a reproach to any people, we should strive to win souls, instruct wisdom, have standards, that our nation would be blessed by our righteousness in Christ. Not Christian nationalism but a nation of Christians.

Proverbs 15 begins by again establishing the truth that things we say, and the manner we say it, is a key instruction for holy living. A soft answer, given in kindness and grace can calm a situation. The tongue of the wise uses knowledge and disperses it. A wholesome tongue, speaking pure words is a tree of life. Both spiritually, by the gospel, but also metaphorically by lifting up others' spirit. Plans and purposes rely on wise counsel, and many counselors make them established. How we use our mouth, the words we choose, the knowledge we impart, the instruction we give, all is ultimately judged by God. Matthew 12:36 But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. Because of this, the grievous words that engender strife, stir up anger, or the mouth that pours out foolishness, all is ultimately vanity, and the man who hasn't humbled himself to the Lord, and received justification through Christ will surely be ashamed at the judgment. Imagine every foolish or wicked thing you've ever said in anger, read aloud by the holy God for all to hear. Every perverse word that causes others' spirit to fall. Every ignorant thing that led others astray. Every contention and strife stirred up by our unwise words, lack of discretion and wisdom, all revealed from the Great White Throne. I thank God for His great salvation, that spares me from such utter humiliation. This alone should convict man to repentance towards the gospel. We see that even the thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to God, but pure words are pleasing to Him. A soft answer and pure words, instruction and knowledge, these please the Lord, and they are good to our soul, and are a blessing to the people in our life. A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it! How good it is to hear the joy of a brother when we are feeling down! The comfort in our mourning, being told exactly the thing we needed to hear, with all due wisdom and counsel, this is a gift to all, one we should spread ourselves. The words we say, the things that our tongue forms and passes our lips, is a window to our heart. Matthew 12:34 O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. The heart of the fool prevents their lips from speaking wisdom. The heart one without understanding seeks foolishness to fill it, rather than understanding. The righteous' heart studies that they may give good answer to those seeking wisdom, but the wicked heart causes evil things to pour out the mouth of the fool. Every thought and word is known by God. The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good. The Lord is omnipotent and omniscient, ever present and knowing all things. Not only the words we speak, but the heart we keep. Hell and destruction are before the Lord: how much more then the hearts of the children of men? If the dead and hell are tormented in the presence of the Lamb, before God night and day, how much more our hearts are known by Him? Psalm 44:21 Shall not God search this out? for he knoweth the secrets of the heart. The heart rejoices in the light of the eyes, a message of good report. Being the bearer of glad tidings, the reproof of life, the gospel...all this serves to brighten the heart of many, if they are inclined to wisdom and seek truth. Of course the fool rejects reproof and correction, to their shame. The constant reminder from God to heed the wisdom of your father, to incline your ear to instruction, to prudently regard reproof continues to be hammered home. Following after the way of righteousness is wise, but those that have forsaken the way of God despise correction and hate reproof. Scorners hate being reproved of their ignorance. They won't seek after the wise. They feed on foolishness, are destitute of wisdom, their plans come to naught for lack of counsel, those greedy of gain and their pride brings destruction to their house. The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the upright is his delight. The Lord is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous. Having God on your side, accepting your prayers, working in your life is a treasure beyond measure. The wicked and their public display of piety, their self-righteous works and so-called fasts, the "sacrifices" they make, be it the Old Testament animal offerings, or the vows made today to "cut out sweets," or to "drink less" or whatever, are an abomination to the Lord. The fear of the Lord is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility. The wicked may have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. They lack the humility that comes before wisdom. Romans 10:3 For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. The humility of submitting to His righteousness, the fear of the Lord, that we may gain understanding, being willing to receive reproof and correction, to seek after knowledge and study to be approved before God, that we may have a ready answer to all for our hope, this is the wisdom and the way we must seek. The way of life is above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath. The promises of God towards His children are unfailing. That in our house will be much treasure, but not necessarily riches and wealth of this world. So rejoice! Our days with a merry heart are a continual feast. Better is little with fear of the Lord than great treasure and trouble therewith, Solomon writes. Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith. The slothful fool's way is made harder, like a hedge of thorns to get through. The wicked and greedy see their own destruction and live in constant fear and trouble. Choose the path of life. The way of God, by humbling yourself to His wisdom and hearing the instruction of your father, and bring that light to others. Be a wise son: A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish man despiseth his mother.

Proverbs 16 can be divided into thematic sections, the first of which is dealing with the relationship between the Lord and man, and His work and judgment. The second, the understanding of kings and man. Third, against pride and for meek wisdom. Fourth, the ungodly, froward, violent and naughty men vs the righteous. Like chapter 15, Proverbs 16 is also bookended by similar passages. Here, on the power of God to determine outcomes. The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the Lord. As Jesus says; Mark 13:11 But when they shall lead you, and deliver you up, take no thought beforehand what ye shall speak, neither do ye premeditate: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye: for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Ghost. If from the abundance of the heart man speaketh, the heart inclined to the Lord will give us the words that are spoken. The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord. Just as what to say is influenced by the Spirit, the lots of chance are cast to the Lord. Throughout the Old Testament, lots - or marked sticks, bones or stones, similar to dice in purpose but not design - were used to determine divine will for priestly duties, such as assigning temple service, burning incense, and wood offerings, as described in 1 Chronicles 24:3-5, 19, Luke 1:9, and Nehemiah 10:34. They were used to divide the promised land (Joshua 14:2, Numbers 26:55). The Levitical ordinances required holy lots, called the Urim and the Thummim, as part of the ephod, or official vestiture. The right to use these items was strictly reserved for the Levitical High Priest (Deuteronomy 33:8). They functioned similarly to lots, often providing a "yes" or "no" answer to a specific inquiry. For example, in 1 Samuel 14:41, King Saul asks for the "Thummim" to determine if guilt lay with him or the people. Ultimately, it left matters to seeming chance, but God's will was the end of the matter once the lots were cast. The sovereignty of God is found in such things, as giving us the words to speak from His wisdom, or settling a matter by accepting God's will, when the choice isn't clear. Not in micromanaging every outcome, but giving us the heart to understand and the serenity to accept what comes. Following the opening verse, we get a quick succession of proverbs that highlight the way of the Lord, and insight to His understanding. The Lord judges the ways of a man by the spirit behind what we do. Men may justify every deed and word, but it is the intent and heart behind them that God cares about. A man can do good for bad reasons, he can do evil with good intentions. We do things in ignorance, we do things willfully, and so God judges righteous judgement, as only He can. And so, to ensure we are walking in His ways, we are encouraged to commit our works to the Lord and our thoughts will be established. The spirit behind our deeds will be His, rather than our vain rationalizations. The Lord has made all creation, everything that is, is His. Even the wicked who do evil serve a purpose for the Lord. Consider Assyria; Isaiah 10:1-6 Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed; To turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless! And what will ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory? Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation. I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets. The destruction of the northern kingdom of Israel by the heathen empire was done by the wicked. Assyria is described as the rod of God's anger. Again the sovereignty and judgment of the Lord results in all things being for His purpose. Not determinism, but utility of the ultimate authority, towards His ends. The proud of heart are an abomination to the Lord, even when they join forces against Him. I think of the armies Satan deceives into attacking Jesus and the camp of the saints at the end of the Millennial Kingdom, appealing to their pride. They unite for the battle of Gog and Magog, and are instantly destroyed, punished for their pride. Revelation 20:7-9 And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog, and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them. As we have been instructed over and over again, fear of the Lord brings understanding and wisdom, wisdom brings mercy and love of truth, and these in practice purge iniquity and injustice from men. By heeding the wisdom of the Lord, by seeking and walking in His paths, by acknowledging Him in all our ways, we please the Lord and rather than the destruction of the prideful and the visiting of evil, He will even make our enemies be at peace with us. In Genesis 26:28-29, Isaac prospered and lived righteously, causing his chief enemy, King Abimelech, to come to him seeking a covenant of peace, acknowledging that God was with him. This is most evident in the cycle of Judges. Judges 2:14-19 And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies. Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them: and they were greatly distressed. Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them. And yet they would not hearken unto their judges, but they went a whoring after other gods, and bowed themselves unto them: they turned quickly out of the way which their fathers walked in, obeying the commandments of the Lord; but they did not so. And when the Lord raised them up judges, then the Lord was with the judge, and delivered them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge: for it repented the Lord because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them. And it came to pass, when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way. Over and over again, the wicked were prepared to be used by God to punish Israel, and when Israel was delivered by God's judges, they would walk in His ways and have peace. While a man's heart may deviseith his way, the Lord directs his steps. One way or another. Carrot or stick. Blessing or rod. Like the chance of the lots or by the rod of His wrath, man will know the Lord. Continuing in Proverbs 16, we reach the proverbs of kings and the understanding that God behind their authority, in a similar way that He uses the wicked as a rod of His wrath or the chance of lots fall to His will (regardless of the roll of them, I believe. The power isn't in the roll, but in accepting His will in your heart). The rule of God over government is a doctrine fully spelled out by Paul in Romans; Romans 13:1-5 Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake. But this isn't to say rulers are always correct and righteous, that there is a divine right of kings to do as they will. But their main function is to punish those that reject God's appointment, and His use of the anointed rulers to His purpose, whether good or evil. The judgment of the king is a divine sentence. What they say, goes. Even as David refused to harm Saul, despite the evil Saul sought to do to him. Just as the weights and balances used in trade are the Lord's. That's why, as we've previously read, an unjust weight is an abomination to Him. And so a king that commits wickedness is like an unjust weight, the ruler's iniquity is an abomination as well. The Lord will repay. The righteous lips delight a king, and a wise man can pacify even a king's wrath. They hold the lives of men in their hands, and should they choose, they can easily take it. But the love of wisdom and true words, well spoken by the righteous man can pacify the ruler. Finding favor with the king, is life and brings forth abundance as the spring rains. In this context, we see the wisdom of vs 16: How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! and to get understanding rather to be chosen than silver! When the wisdom and soft word of the righteous can curry favor and the mercy and blessings of the king, it is worth more than gold. So we stick to the way of the Lord. Departing from evil. In the meekness and humility found in the fear of the Lord. Humble in spirit, rather than with the proud, even in their spoil. Because pride comes before destruction, and the spirit that God judges haughty will be brought low. Matthew 5:3-5 Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted. Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth. The wise, those that trust the Lord in all things, regardless of the situation or persecution or poverty or even being lifted up by kings, will find good, and will be happy. They shall be called prudent and be teachers of men, respected for their sweet sayings and soft words. A wellspring of life. The wise teaches his mouth to obey, and adds learning to his words. James 3:7-9 For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed of mankind: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison. Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God. Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be. Seek to tame your tongue, and add learning and knowledge, that when you speak, it is a blessing to all. That is wisdom. Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones. The chapter begins to wrap up with one of the most cited Proverbs. There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death. Man is able to rationalize any transgression, any trespass against others, every petty sin and idle thought. But man's ways are not God's. Isaiah 55:8-9 For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts. This is why God tells us to acknowledge Him in all our ways, that we may walk His paths. To study and gain knowledge, that we can know His thoughts. Because His way is life and ours death and there's no good end to the wicked. Ungodly men dig up evil, and the words they say are destructive. They sow strife and with a froward mouth, cause friends to fight. The violent man tempts his neighbor, and entices them from God's way. The unrighteous devises perverse things to say, bringing evil to pass. This is contrasted with the righteous elder, his gray head a crown of glory. Being slow to anger is the real might of a man. A man with in control of himself, will be able to rule others. But either way, it is to God's purpose.
