For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error. While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage. And again; Jude 1:12 These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots It is amazing how often the worldly application of the wisdom of God is applicable to spiritual things.

Proverbs 25 introduces a section (chapters 25–29) of Solomon’s proverbs that were compiled by King Hezekiah's officials, approximately 250–270 years after Solomon's reign. Hezekiah, the son of the wicked king, Ahaz, began a revival and reformation, tearing down altars and idols. In the first month of his reign, Hezekiah opened and repaired the doors of the House of the Lord. He commanded the Levites to "sanctify" themselves and carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place. He restored the observance of Passover. He brought order to the Levites, and proclaimed tithes and offerings from the people. And in his zeal, the young king commanded scribes to write these sayings of Solomon, that they be preserved and observed. They begin with the honor of kings to search out the hidden things of God. 1 Corinthians 2:10 But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God. As I have previously stated, my opinion is that the wisdom for princes and kings is for the saved, as co-heirs with Christ. Even the least in the Kingdom of Heaven is a prince, who will judge with Him in the millennium. We will judge angels. The study of the word is like unto princes under tutors, until the day of adoption. The resurrection where we come into our power as glorified sons of God. Galatians 4 Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father. The context here is the law bringing man to understand the need for a savior, but the application mirrors the process of a prince coming into his own by instruction, until the determined time of the King. As Paul writes in Romans 8:23 ...even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. The day of redemption, the resurrection, is the day of our adoption; the time of the giving of the inheritance, to rule and reign with Jesus. The Greek word Paul uses for 'adoption,' huiothesia, carries a heavier legal meaning than our modern idea of adoption. In that context, it wasn't about bringing an outsider into a family; it was the formal ceremony, the "placing as a son," where an heir reached the age of maturity, the father publicly recognized them as a legal adult, granting them the full authority, a signet ring, and power to manage the estate, or the lands appointed them. We become sons of God when we are born again, but notice the adoption is at the resurrection. At the day of redemption. So, when we see proverbs about kings or princes, about judgement and mercy, who to be influenced by, who to seek counsel from...it is all instructions from THE King, God our Father, to His children, who will inherit the Kingdom. Continuing in the chapter; if the deeper things of God are the glory of kings to search out, then the heart of the king is as high as Heaven and as deep as the earth; unsearchable to the common man. The Spirit that brings those who seek it, understanding, being absent in the natural man (who receiveth not the spiritual things of God) cannot fathom the heart of the king. This process, walking in the Spirit, seeking wisdom and the richness of God's judgment, produces a refinement; the fire of God removes the dross, the impurities in a man, and we come forth a finer vessel, pure silver, fit for holy use. While we have the legal inheritance to rule, as sons and co-heirs with Christ, we gain the character needed to rule, to judge righteous judgment, by this refinement. Our God is a consuming fire and all that burns away is dross. We are meant to be fitted as vessels of honor, and so the instructions for Godly living, His wisdom given by inspiration to Solomon, here written by order of Hezekiah, is designed to act as a refining fire. To see things the way God sees things. To walk His path, to be in the way of righteousness, following after Christ Jesus.

Proverbs 26 continues the collection of Solomon's sayings, prepared for King Hezekiah, the 12th generation descendant of the wisest man ever to live. These sayings return to the more rapid fire style of earlier chapters, and focus heavily on the warnings against fools, liars, sluggards and talebearers. In order, vs 1 compares the honor given a fool to unseasonable weather. Snow in summer, rain at harvest. It should bother us as Christians when the foolish and froward get honor and praise by this world. We should see it as unseemly. It happens all too often, and vexes the heart. Curses without cause shall not come, curse not at all. It's vanity, generally speaking. The cause rarely rises to the level of the curse, and if it did, God will repay. Better to bless, and give it up to the Lord. The rod on the fools back serves the same purpose as a bridle, to direct the stubborn fool and keep him in line. Corporal punishment for foolish and malignant behavior is a good thing, and better at correction than jail, onerous fines and probation. Stripes serve a purpose, and it's cruelty that our society has abandoned this corrective in the name of progress. Vs 4-5 bring a seeming contradiction; Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him. Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit. The understanding here is that when a fool is arguing foolishness, debating their false premises, bickering back and forth makes you as much a fool, no matter how correct you are. But to not answer a fool in his folly leaves him wise in his own conceit. The instruction then is to rebuke, not argue. To correct with authority (from scripture especially), and, as we've discussed, shake the dust. A Titus 3:10 situation. To be "wise in your own conceits" is to be dug in or convinced of your false or nonsensical beliefs. It could be some weird doctrine that they've heard and taken to heart, repeating it as fact. It could be the conclusion of their own ignorance applying twisted logic. It could be lies and rationalizations they use to deceive themselves. It often is an identity they've adopted and the presuppositions and shibboleths that come with it, something we see in people taken in by special boy theology. They are constantly looking to provoke arguments and to get people into endless debates, that go no where. Verse 12 explains precisely why; Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him. Whatever the conceit may be, the fools are entrenched in them. And so, after the first and second admonition reject. You've better hope convincing a fool of the truth than changing their mind. Using a fool as a messenger is foolish. It will undermine and damage what you sought to accomplish. Just as the lame struggle to walk, the fool will misuse parables to their own purposes, drawing wrong conclusions and clouding understanding, rather than gaining wisdom. While God uses parables throughout the Bible, Jesus teaching almost exclusively in parable to the hard-hearted Jews, so many have been used to create false doctrine. Proper application of parables should lay primarily on any explanation given in the text, (Jesus would often expound to the Apostles their meaning) but for those without clear teaching, the context should then be drawn by comparing scripture with scripture. No doctrine should stand alone on a parable. The most obvious example is the false doctrine of "Abraham's bosom,' taken from Luke 16's tale of the rich man and Lazarus. Jesus is using their example to convey a message of urgency to the Jews, to repent and believe the gospel before its too late. To say that the prophets and Moses gave witness to His day, harken to them and believe. That those who don't are Hell-bound, no matter how rich they are. That those with dull ears and blind eyes will not believe, even if one were to raise from the dead. But that the faithful, even the afflicted and poor in this world, who call upon the name of the Lord, are carried by angels into Heaven, honored and seated with Abraham, the father of faith. To be comforted forever. The eisegesis and natural man logic required to turn this simple (and I believe, true) story into a doctrine that says that there is a place in Hell that's actually a compartment containing paradise, called "Abraham's bosom," and that that's where Old Testament saints went, is absurd. The embrace of Abraham is specifically to show how even the lowly beggar, covered in sores, whose life was misery and rejection, someone lower than the dogs without the rich man's gate, rejected by the respecters of persons Jesus is addressing, is given an honor that Jews would be envious of. To sit down with Abraham, in the paradise that is God's heavenly kingdom. As vs 9 says; As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouths of fools. The binding of a stone in a sling, trapping it there in its pocket, makes the weapon useless, and so it is equally vain to give honor to a fool. Sometimes, we try and build up a foolish person by encouraging them when they do right. Unfortunately, this generally puffs them up, and enables their wrongdoing by making them feel justified. The correction of a fool often fails, as we've seen in other passages, how less then their praise? God, the Creator of all things, Who is blessed forever, amen, rewards the fool, and transgressors. They get what is coming to them, and His rebuke and reproach is far greater than anything we do. As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly. Peter quotes this proverb, and applies it to the false teachers, crept in. The apostates who hear the gospel preached and know the holy commandment to believe, yet fall away back to the rudiments of the world, their later end worse than before. 2 Peter 2:22 But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire. The apostasy leads to reprobation. As Hebrews 6 explains, those that have tasted of the truth, and the power of the Spirit, yet reject it, holding the truth in unrighteousness, become hardened. Unable to come to the knowledge of the truth. So they return to their unrighteousness as a dog to their vomit. Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him. The fool, wise in their own conceit, is the "special boy." Convinced that they know something to be true, despite clear scripture and common reason, context and consistent application across the text, they are immovable from their opinions. Their opinions are their own self-identity. They can no more consider they're wrong than deny their own name, because it would destroy the things that make up the very concept of who they are. The more esoteric or counter to the plain reading, the better, because it allows them to feel superior to those that "just don't understand" their doctrine. They have carefully curated proof texts, and circular arguments and unfalsifiable theories. Again, this is why we shake the dust, and are told to reject them. The sluggard and slothful are next, and their ways mocked again. Their lame excuses to avoid work, their excessive sleeping habits, their self-destructive laziness. They're convinced that their rationalizations and justifications for refusing work cannot be reasoned or debated with. They simply don't care. It cannot be that the fault lies with them, and so it must be you being unreasonable. If you've ever had to deal with a sluggard, you know this tendency and how fruitless attempts to shame, cajole or rebuke them are. They only respond to starvation, and many even then cannot bring themselves to work. The last section of Proverbs 26 deals with strife, and those that cause it with their lying tongue. He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears. Getting involved in other people's fights, whether it's taking up a cause between two parties in your church, between neighbors, or total strangers, is a foolish thing to do. The warning here leans into the uncontrollable danger, likening it to a dog turning and rending you. But it also applies to chatroom drama and Facebook fights. It happens online all the time, where the physical stakes are low, and the busybody tendencies are not inhibited by potential violence. Stay out of contentions that don't involve you. If we are to bless our own enemies and turn the other cheek, then what business is it of ours to join in another's vengeance? And, while it is blessed to be a peacemaker, it isn't arrived at by stepping in between brawlers or meddling in their strife. Better to counsel with soft words to the parties separately, than join in as a third member of an ongoing fight. You really don't want to be the reason two warring factions unite out of spite to go after you for your meddling. This should be applied in context to ruling a kingdom as well. When Jehosaphat, King of the Southern Kingdom of Judah joined the wicked Ahab of Israel in his war with Syria, we see in 2 Chronicles 19; Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord. A godly nation should not join the enemies of Christ in war against their enemies. And Christians shouldn't cheer when their leaders yoke with unbelieving countries to make war. If two nations of those who hate God choose to go to war, you can pray for God's will to be done, or that His judgement brings peace. You can be indifferent to the outcome, and leave it to God. But don't meddle in their strife, even by egging it on. Next, we see that it is like a mad man randomly firing arrows, flaming arrows and sowing death to be a neighbor who lies to his neighbor for sport. To be "funny." To rile up a reaction through lies. The spirit behind it is the same. Seeking mischief to stir up strife is wicked as Hell. Finally, vs 20-22 and vs 23-28 deal with stirring up strife by being a talebearer and a liar. Strife caused by that little member, the tongue, that has such great power. James 3:5-6 Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth! And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell. Talebearing and spreading rumors acts as kindling, as coals, keeping a fire going or sparking new fires. Gossiping to stir contention, to bring about trouble where there is none, causing wounds of the heart, is like a potsherd covered with silver dross. A shard of a broken pot, with the impurities and refined waste of silver. Worthless and wicked. Haters will lie and build up deceit within them. Paul warns Timothy of this kind of man; 1 Timothy 6:4-5 He is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings, Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself. Evil surmising is the act of harboring unproven, malicious suspicions, assuming the worst motives about others without evidence. It is a destructive, divisive attitude that often produces pride, strife, and envy. They take innocent actions of someone and inventing malicious intent, spreading rumors to others to poison them against the hater's target of ire. Someone filled with hate can typically be characterized as having an unhealthy obsession with accusations that ruin fellowship, and sow discord among the brethren. Vs 25 specifically links discord and the other 6 things God hates, the 7 abominations from Proverbs 6:16-19, to these hate filled liars, flatterers, and talebearing deceivers; These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren. Don't be one, obviously, but also don't fall victim to one by listening to their talebearing. Their evil will be exposed and shown the whole congregation. The pit they dig to trap others will trap them. The stone they roll to crush their targets will return unto them. Their lying tongue and flattering mouth works ruin.

The record of Solomon's wisdom, as recorded by King Hezekiah's scribes, continues in Proverbs 27. The litany of sayings found here offers some new insights, retelling of others and repetition of yet more, all for our edification. The chapter begins with the understanding that we should not assume what the future brings. We are prisoners of the moment, and our breath is in God's hands. Tomorrow isn't promised. We primarily use this Biblical understanding to stress the urgency of the gospel when preaching to the lost. That getting your account settled on the way cannot wait. Because, as the Bible says in 2 Corinthians 6:2 ...I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation. If you haven't trusted on Christ as your only means of salvation, given by the grace of the Father, now is the time. If you have received that precious gift, get to work doing the will of God and winning souls. Romans 13:11 ...now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed But even in general terms, boasting about what you will do tomorrow is an empty promise when you don't know what lies in store. James 4:14-15 Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away. For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that. God willing, it shall come to pass, but better to deal with today, redeem the time and accomplish what may be done now, than seek glory for what you've yet to do. And even then, boast not at all; Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips. It is in the nature of finite man to boast on the morrow while we procrastinate difficult things. To justify our not doing anything now, because of how wonderful our plans are for then. Getting lazy. Saying "If it's God's will" as an excuse. But what then? Should we not plan for the things that may come? To just wait on the Lord for all things? Not at all. Verse 12; A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished. Some, rather than foolishly passing on, or boasting on what they may do, get so caught up in worry for tomorrow that they are paralyzed today. Jesus teaches us to avoid that as well; Matthew 6:34 Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof. We should recognize that the future exists, and the evil thereof, and plan accordingly. Being diligent in the works of today, is being prudent for tomorrow. Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured. This is the correct balance, to see the future as an opportunity that's built in the work of the present, guarding against evil, while knowing the harvest will come. The reward is waiting. The honor and glory will come. Whether serving God and the spiritual works as a laborer for Christ, or just in your daily life in taking care of those things God has put before us. Achieve balance, seek Him first, be prudent and plan, without worry, don't out off till tomorrow what can be done today. Do not seek your own glory and honor, or boast about what you plan to do, but work diligently knowing you will earn the praise of others, even God, Amen. Following along in chapter 27:13, we are again reminded to avoid guaranteeing the debt of someone unknown or unreliable, to take their coat or a pledge as collateral. This of course, is always wise, or to swear not at all for a stranger. Verse 14, don't be an annoying neighbor. Even a good thing, such as blessing a friend, is counted a curse when done at an inappropriate or inopportune time. A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike. Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself. It is clear that Solomon had issue with contentious women, and the Spirit confirms this plight. As annoying as a continuous dropping or rain, impossible to hide. Like holding back the wind or a handful of oil, her nagging and arguing is impossible to contain. Don't be that woman. Don't be that henpecked husband. Next, an often quoted verse, Iron sharpeneth iron. We in the Christian life should cultivate other Christians as friends. And as friends, we can help hone one another, as sharpening a blade, to improve each other. Hebrews 10:23-24 Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works A friend can sharpen the countenance of his friend, then to, as the reflection of your face in water revealed your appearance, so too is your heart revealed when you deal man to man. In other words, our friends can be a mirror into our own heart. When we have the opportunity to see ourselves as we are, don't ignore it or forget it. It's a means to improve. To sharpen our iron. The way we see ourselves without reflection, is often tainted and false. Built up by our own rationalizing and self-deception. But our heart is made known to us by our interactions with others. It is also reflected back at us in reading Scripture. James 1:23-25 For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was. But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed. We should relish the opportunity to see ourselves as we really are, unashamed because we are walking God's path. Being a doer or the word, not a hearer only. That when we see our heart, man to man we are not ashamed. And that others look at us and see the love of Christ. Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him. This saying carries another reminder that fools are locked in to their foolishness, that they are wise in their own conceit and even stripes won't make them listen. Not even grinding them in a mortar and pestle could remove their foolishness. Finally, as in earlier parts of the chapter, is the lesson in the diligence of now, the favoring of low time preference and having a long view. Tend your flocks. Look well to thy herds. Manage the resources and wealth you have, and don't be wasteful or careless. Riches are not forever. The crown does not endure to every generation. These things can be squandered and lost by poor management, slothfulness and foolishness. God provides the tender grass and herbs of the mountain. The food for your flock. The means of your substance. The ability to make a living depends on His grace and generosity, and our diligence. Keeping this in mind, He promises that we shall have what is sufficient to care for our family. If we take care of our worldly wealth, and manage and work it, taking advantage of all the Lord provides, how much more the treasure we store up in Heaven? The Lord provides us His word to feed the flock, as the grass and herb. We all have opportunities to serve Him and reach the lost, to tend to the flocks He has given us. It may a mother over her child. It may be as a teacher to young men. It may be as a Pastor over a church. But our diligence to know the state of them, and look well over our herd, will benefit ourselves and our family in the long run.

Proverbs 28 continues the sayings of Solomon, recorded by the order of his 10th-generation grandson, King Hezekiah. And it begins with an often used saying; The wicked flee when no man pursueth... The guilty fear the wrath they know they deserve. Constantly looking over their shoulder, and quick to defend themselves where no accusations have been made. Paranoia strikes the thief and the murderer, the habitual criminal lives in constant worry of being found out to the point they will expose themselves when there is no threat. Parents are familiar with this behavior in guilty children. God is used to this in His children as well. but the righteous are bold as a lion. This boldness comes from having a clean conscience towards God by the blood of Christ; Hebrews 10:16-22 This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more. Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin. Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh; And having an high priest over the house of God; Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. For God treats us as His children, by faith in Christ, that when we sin, we have forgiveness. Hebrews 4:16 Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need. We don't need to keep a guilty conscience, in constant anxiety. We have the boldness of Christ's righteousness and the promise of a merciful Father The righteous don't despise the chastening of the Lord, or faint when we are rebuked of Him; Hebrews 12:6-8 For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons. But the unbelieving allow the fear of their guilt and unrighteousness overcome them, and their love of sin betray and snare them, they flee the throne of God to hide from His vengeance. Especially those that have heard His word and the instruction of righteousness, and have rejected it. Hebrews 10:26-27 For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries. For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged. There is no political solution for a spiritual problem. The iniquity and sin in a country results in many princes, that is more and more oppression and rules and rulers. It could also mean instability and high turnover. Frequent coups. Parties switching off power every few years. Revolution after revolution. A sinful people get the leadership they deserve. While a wise king, filled with the fear of the Lord and the understanding and knowledge that follow, his rule shall be established and stand, and is the joy of a righteous people. Reminder that God has given the responsibility of preserving our nation to Christians. 2 Chronicles 7:14 If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. Revival begins in the heart of believers, in the pews of their local church, in the highways and hedges, at the doorstep of the lost. Not at a ballot box, not on cable news, or a podcast or YouTube comments section. It doesn't begin in a Telegram chat, or social media post, or at a rally for a politician. Christians are the salt of the earth, preserving their land, prolonging the state of a land. Matthew 5:13 Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. What follows, from verse 3 though 28, is a litany of sayings that contrast the wicked, the rich without understanding, the haters of the law, the violent and bloody man, with the faithful, upright, keepers of the law. The prince of understanding, the righteous man, these see their fortunes and their reputation in increase, while their counterparts are undone by their sin. We see that a poor man who helps oppress the poor is a threat to all, and also self-destructive. That those who forsake the law will praise the wicked, but this that keep the law will contend with them. Those law-haters out there, that make grace an opportunity to justify their sin, will inevitably go after the praise of the wicked. We see it all the time. It begins with excusing themselves from God's precepts, and extends to then justifying sodomites and degenerates. Female led churches with rainbow flags, glorifying rioting and rebellion, and teaching abominations. Because evil men understand not judgment, they are perverse and so oppose any mention of what God says, to chase after their own lusts. "God wouldn't want the death penalty!" or "A loving God wouldn't send anyone to Hell!" Those that seek the Lord and in all our ways acknowledge Him, understand the need for love being without dissimulation. Why we must abhor that which is evil. We are reminded again it is better to be poor and walking in God's ways, than to be rich and wicked. A wise son keeps the law and is a joy to his parents, but the riotous and rebellious son is a shame to his father. Romans 13:13-14 Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying. But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof. As Christians, we are to give honor, tribute and custom to whom it is due. To obey the higher authority and the powers that be. Not seek cause for lawlessness and giving the wicked praise because they cause the righteous to go astray unto evil. Verse 8 cautions against usury and unjust gain, linking the two. Much is made about what the Bible means by usury. Some suggest that a little interest for a loan is fine, that it's just prohibited to charge high or "predatory" interest rates. But, in the King James Bible, usury is defined as any interest, profit, or premium charged on a loan, not just excessive or illegal interest as understood in modern terms. When servitude could be the result of not keeping the terms of the agreement, compounding interest on top of the principle could be the difference between slavery or liberty. Seeking to profit off another's need is unjust gain. Redemption is the freeing of the burden of debt, paying what's owed and liberating oneself or another from owing something. The gospel language of Christ setting us at liberty from the wages of sin through the gift of eternal life, where the Spirit acts as the surety for the promise of God, that He will not impute our sins against us, but rather apply the payment of Jesus' blood, is all quite deliberate. So the idea of adding burdens to the needy that make their ability to pay someone back fairly is an abomination to the Lord. He is gracious and expects us to be gracious as well. God's law instituted a "Sabbath year." Every seven years, a "release" was mandated, where creditors were required to cancel debts owed by their fellow Israelites. Deuteronomy 15:1-2 At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release. And this is the manner of the release: Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the Lord's release. Servitude could often be a means of survival for the poor, and a blessing. Having a way to work off that which is owed, without interest was a fair system, and limiting the debt to what could be repaid in 7 years not only kept this process from exploiting the poor, but made lenders more cautious in issuing loans. But some have an evil heart, and their love of money tempts them. And so the Lord warns; Deuteronomy 15:9 Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto the Lord against thee, and it be sin unto thee. Not all debt was for money. Some servitude was to obtain favor or other gain. In Genesis 29, Laban tricks Jacob into a total of 14 years of labor for the honor of marriage to Rachel, Laban's younger daughter. After Jacob serves seven years, Laban switches his daughters on the wedding night, sending his older daughter, Leah, to the bridal bed instead of Rachel. Laban justifies this deceit by claiming it is custom for the younger to marry after the older, but he sought to keep Jacob bound to service, exploiting his love for Rachel. In addition to the 7 year release, God commands a jubilee every 50 years; Leviticus 25:10-13 And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family. A jubile shall that fiftieth year be unto you: ye shall not sow, neither reap that which groweth of itself in it, nor gather the grapes in it of thy vine undressed. For it is the jubile; it shall be holy unto you: ye shall eat the increase thereof out of the field. In the year of this jubile ye shall return every man unto his possession. The purpose here was to restore families to their land, and set free the captive, that generational poverty could be prevented. Stopping a lending class of rich men from exerting permanent control over the poor. If lending to a poor neighbor, one was forbidden from charging usury at all; Exodus 22:25 If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer, neither shalt thou lay upon him usury. This even extended to making a profit on food sold to the poor; Leviticus 25:35-37 And if thy brother be waxen poor, and fallen in decay with thee; then thou shalt relieve him: yea, though he be a stranger, or a sojourner; that he may live with thee. Take thou no usury of him, or increase: but fear thy God; that thy brother may live with thee. Thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor lend him thy victuals for increase. Land owners were expected to allow gleaning of their fields, that after a harvest, the poor should go through the fields and bring in anything left behind by the laborers. Alms and feasts of charity are expected of the Lord's people. Forgiveness of debts. A cheerful giver, providing for those in need is praised. Proverbs 11:25-27 The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself. He that withholdeth corn, the people shall curse him: but blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it. As Proverbs 28:8 promises; He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor. The gain you may make is temporary. The Lord will make certain your wealth is distributed to the righteous, in the end. Because God is so just to forgive us, we should love one another enough to be like Him. Luke 7:41-42 There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty. And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most? So, we should not seek unjust gain, and further, we should relieve those in our debt, as God has forgiven us. Matthew 6:9-13 After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen. Nehemiah 5 And there was a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brethren the Jews. 2 For there were that said, We, our sons, and our daughters, are many: therefore we take up corn for them, that we may eat, and live. 3 Some also there were that said, We have mortgaged our lands, vineyards, and houses, that we might buy corn, because of the dearth. 4 There were also that said, We have borrowed money for the king's tribute, and that upon our lands and vineyards. 5 Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children as their children: and, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought unto bondage already: neither is it in our power to redeem them; for other men have our lands and vineyards. 6 And I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words. 7 Then I consulted with myself, and I rebuked the nobles, and the rulers, and said unto them, Ye exact usury, every one of his brother. And I set a great assembly against them. 8 And I said unto them, We after our ability have redeemed our brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen; and will ye even sell your brethren? or shall they be sold unto us? Then held they their peace, and found nothing to answer. 9 Also I said, It is not good that ye do: ought ye not to walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the heathen our enemies? 10 I likewise, and my brethren, and my servants, might exact of them money and corn: I pray you, let us leave off this usury. 11 Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money, and of the corn, the wine, and the oil, that ye exact of them. 12 Then said they, We will restore them, and will require nothing of them; so will we do as thou sayest. Then I called the priests, and took an oath of them, that they should do according to this promise. 13 Also I shook my lap, and said, So God shake out every man from his house, and from his labour, that performeth not this promise, even thus be he shaken out, and emptied. And all the congregation said, Amen, and praised the Lord. And the people did according to this promise. 14 Moreover from the time that I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even unto the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that is, twelve years, I and my brethren have not eaten the bread of the governor. 15 But the former governors that had been before me were chargeable unto the people, and had taken of them bread and wine, beside forty shekels of silver; yea, even their servants bare rule over the people: but so did not I, because of the fear of God. 16 Yea, also I continued in the work of this wall, neither bought we any land: and all my servants were gathered thither unto the work. 17 Moreover there were at my table an hundred and fifty of the Jews and rulers, beside those that came unto us from among the heathen that are about us. 18 Now that which was prepared for me daily was one ox and six choice sheep; also fowls were prepared for me, and once in ten days store of all sorts of wine: yet for all this required not I the bread of the governor, because the bondage was heavy upon this people. 19 Think upon me, my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people. The covenant God made with the Israelites, that by the works of the law they may know Him, and they would be His people, and He would be their God, put the people in bondage. Because by the same law comes the works of death. For Christ to then set them that believe at liberty, by the grace of the Father to not hold us to that covenant, but by the blood of Christ being a new and better testament, built on better promises, that we have been reconciled despite our sin. Despite our own transgression of the law. That God commendeth His love towards us that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. This is that forgiveness of debt. This is that grace and mercy that He has for us, and commands us to give towards others. Proverbs 28 continues. Verse 9; He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination. The law-haters out there, who allow the reality of grace and reconciliation in Christ to then turn their ear from the hearing of the law, should consider this saying. Their prayers are an abomination to God. To take our liberty and use it as a cover for sin, is wicked. Rather it is a cause to cleanse ourselves, as much as possible, and to not lead those weak in the faith to stumble. 1 Corinthians 10:23-24 All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not. Let no man seek his own, but every man another's wealth. We should be a model of the law, that it convicts the unsaved, and serves to edify our brethren, weak in the faith, to do better. Not as a stumbling block or a snare, but as an example. Not being offended at the hearing of the law, but affirming it, that it may bring others to Christ. That our prayers are acceptable to the Lord. You might not be perfect, and we all fall short, but preaching against sin, especially the sin you still do, shouldn't offend you. It should convict. It should elicit an even hardier "Amen!" It's no wonder that verse 10 follows; Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession. Romans 14 warns of causing a brother to sin by your liberty. Romans 14:14-16;21 I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean. But if thy brother be grieved with thy meat, now walkest thou not charitably. Destroy not him with thy meat, for whom Christ died. Let not then your good be evil spoken of... It is good neither to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor any thing whereby thy brother stumbleth, or is offended, or is made weak. If matters of conscience are left to us to determine, yet we should defer to abstain for the edification of those weak in faith, how much more so the clear things of the law which are sin? So, those who take liberty to be libertine, and who teach that the redundant term "free grace" means "God isn't mad at your sin," to then allow fornication, drunkenness and the like, misleading others, will themselves fall victim to their sin. God will repay. And those that deliberately bring offense, who corrupt and pervert others into sin, they will fall themselves into the pit they've dug for others. They will be snared by their own trap. Better to have standards, to teach the whole counsel of God. To love the law and delight in it, even at liberty by grace. To put the profit of others before your own lusts and desires. To not give others cause to blaspheme the Lord. For the upright shall have good things in possession. They shall be blessed. Picking up the chapter study at Proverbs 28:10; The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out. We all know the story of the rich young man and Jesus, where he claimed to Christ himself that he had observed all commandments from his youth, and Jesus told him to sell all his things for the poor, and he went away unsaved. Matthew 19:24 And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. Earlier Proverbs told us some of the reasons this is true. Their riches are their strong tower. They place their trust in things. But, like the rich young man, they are also wise in their own conceits. He thought he had it all figured out. Those that are well off financially often see themselves, their own wisdom and discernment, as the cause for their success., and their wealth as evidence of their righteousness. A feedback loop that keeps them from even questioning the truth. The rich young man sought to be validated by the "good master," and it didn't occur to him that there is none good but God, that the man Christ Jesus sitting there in front of him was the Lord. Out soul-winning, you encounter far more pushback to the gospel among the wealthy. Even in a more modest neighborhood, if you find a home with a pool, motorsport vehicles, a boat, sports car, or some other sign of wealth, you're likely to great a scoffer at the door. But the poor? So many are seeking to know the truth. They have nothing else to cling to. Their lives are in turmoil and their futures uncertain and they just seek to know why, and what they can do to know God. This is why the current welfare system is so cruel. It provides sustenance and comfort. It artificially created the same condition in them as the wealthy. They become wise in their own conceits. Sadly, this is all too common these days. There are few that are searching out wisdom. There aren't many in America where poverty hits hard enough to make a person stop counting on things and their own entitled arrogance, and be humbled. Praise God for fields of white, ready to be harvested in some areas. Moving on: When the righteous men rejoice, there is great glory. When God has blessed His people with leaders who openly praise His name, we have the opportunity for glory. But when the wicked men rise, the righteous are hidden. Tying this again to soul-winning, evangelizing to the lost, praising God's name in the open, or even reading the Bible and speaking His word confidently, is easy in modern America, today. We have the freedom to openly glorify God. Our leaders, even if they are wolves and deceivers, pay lip service to the Lord and believers are able to openly proclaim Christ without fear. Yet so many men are hidden, still. It's a shame that many churches do not have any soul-winning. That many Christians hide who they are, and what Jesus has done for them. That so few read the Bible here, while there are countries where reading scripture can be a prison sentence. That confessing Christ can end in death. Maybe it is a parallel to the rich young man. That by our comfort and safety we grow complacent. Maybe revival requires tribulation. Maybe the embarrassment of riches we have in the freedom we've been granted by God has caused too many Christians to have their heart hardened for the lost. Vs 13; He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy. We know that in Christ our sins are forgiven, past, present and future. But we are also to faithfully confess our sins to the Father, Who is faithful again to forgive. Covering sin leads to the chastening of the Lord. Humbling ourselves to admit our failings will have mercy. Keeping the theme going, you can see how those Christians who don't go to church, don't read their Bible, don't spread the gospel, would rather hide their sin than acknowledge and forsake them. If they confess, they're conceding to God that they know better, and if they agree that His way is the way forward, then they cannot continue on in theirs. They become paralyzed by their own guilty conscience and love of their sin. "If I go to church, I am admitting I should, and so now I am on the hook to keep going." Same with Bible reading, prayer, or evangelizing. We read in vs 9 that if you hate hearing the law because you want to continue doing the things God says you shouldn't, even your prayers shall be abominations. How much worse are our prayers when we have the liberty to go to church, to get plugged in, to hear hard preaching, to learn God's word, to hear the law and confess our sins and be forgiven, and have the freedom to joyfully tell others the riches of God, and yet we ignore it all? Is it any wonder we end up with a wicked ruler will rise up over a spiritually poor people? To take away the things and riches we take for granted? To provoke God's people to turn again to Him and do what's right, that He may heal the land? V 14-15 seem to be separate points, yet in this larger context they reveal a greater truth; Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief. As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people. Don't harden your hearts. Humble yourself. Confess your sins, including those that come from omissions. To know to do good and to do it not. Return to the first love. Obey the Great Commission. We have been given the ministry of reconciliation, and the opportunity to be servants to the Lord. Don't squander it. Redeem the time. Repent, ask forgiveness and turn to the paths of the Lord. Continuing the series on Proverbs chapter 28; The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor: but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days. This saying ties together two seemingly disparate concepts, but as advice to a young prince of the kingdom, they tie together. Lack of understanding leads to covetousness. Not having knowledge and the wisdom to execute it, leads to a desire for things. As we've already discussed, regarding the rich young man and Jesus, want for understanding and desire for "things" go hand in hand. Longing for riches, seeking what's not yours, fills the hole that's left. Vs 17 warns to let the bloody man go to where his violence shall take him. To his own violent end. Vs 18-28 are another set of contrasting sayings, between the good man and wicked, but focusing on a particular type of behavior that is driven by seeking gain without the work it takes to earn it. And warnings against being corrupt enough to be taken in by vain men. Those who walk upright, honest in their dealings shall be saved. Not necessarily in the gospel sense, although that may apply, but in the "sudden destruction" that comes upon the wicked. The man perverse in his ways will see their life fall apart quickly. A corrupt and crooked politician, suddenly exposed as a degenerate and a whoremonger, for example. It is as inevitable as the bloody man's race to the pit. The prudent man, who tilleth his land, who tends to the fields now that they may harvest later, will have plenty. But those that follow after vain persons shall have poverty. The vain hope in flatterers, seducers and false teachers, perverse political leaders, will take those that follow them, by covetousness and sloth, itchy ears and lusts. But there is no profit in the energy expended on vain pursuit. A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent...To have respect if persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress...He that hastens to be rich hath an evil eye, and consdereth not that poverty shall come upon him. The theme of covetousness and following after vain persons really hits hard in v20-22. The faithful man will abound with blessings, but those looking to get rich quick choose to corrupt themselves in their greed. The "Prosperity Gospel" scam artists take as much advantage of this tendency in man as the street corner swindler. The old secular saying, "you can't con an honest man" is simply resting this biblical truth. Having respect of persons, favoring one over others because of their wealth, their position, their power, is wrong, not only because it leads to treating the poor and powerless as less than yourself, but instills a form of covetousness in your heart that makes it easier for these false teachers, crept in unawares, to make merchandise of you. This tendency towards greedy covetousness and seeking to gain favor with those you favor for appearance and empty promises, will lead you to sell out for a piece of bread. For a small fraction of what you could have earned honestly with prudent diligence. He that hasteneth to be rich, is being guided by their evil eye, not by the ways of the Lord. 1 John 2:16 For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. This can strike anyone, at any age or station. Presidents and kings can be taken out by the same lusts peddled by vain men, as the poorest man. They delude themselves that their end won't be poverty, but as we've seen, the perverse in his ways shall fall all at once. And great is that fall. Better to be the upright man who rebukes those being taken in by the flattering tongue of a con man. Better to till your field for a future harvest. Better to do the work of the Lord for rewards in Heaven. Put your trust in the Lord, and you shall be made fat. Humble yourself before God, and don't let walking in your ways, pride in your heart that the flattering tongue can appeal to, the coveting of riches, the desire for clout and fame, ruin you, and cause divisions and strife from your pride. Walk wisely, not as a fool. Don't be a respecter of persons, don't value things over people. Don't worry about giving freely to the poor, you are leading to the Lord and He will repay. Don't turn a blind eye to the suffering that you can help alleviate. To know to do good and do it not is a sin. A curse. Follow after God. The wicked will perish and He will deliver us from tribulation. Bless us for our diligence and charity. Reward us for not seeking after riches, but seeking understanding. And when the wicked perish, the righteous increase. Their ill gotten gain will be gathered for him that pity the poor. God will see to it. Proverbs 28:24 Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer. The last verse in this study of Proverbs 28 deals with a child who steals from their parents, excusing it as "no transgression," saying it is not a sin, the same is the companion of a destroyer. Exodus 20:12 Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee. As the fifth of the Ten Commandments, it emphasizes filial respect, obedience, and care, including financial support. It is notable as the first commandment with a direct promise of blessing; Ephesians 6:1-3 Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth. While honor generally means respect or value, it frequently denotes a "heavy" weight or value, which in the KJV context translates to tangible actions like financial offerings. We see this use of the word in the payment of elders in the church; 1 Timothy 5:17 Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine The financial aspect of 'honor' is clear; Romans 13:7 Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour. By including it in the list of taxes and tributes we are called to obey, we see the idea is supporting those above us, in positions to be honored, including parents. And also, the Lord; Proverbs 3:9 Honour the Lord with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase Masking tithes and offerings unto the Lord, paying honor to whomever honor is due is a command. And it absolutely extends to children taking care of their parents. 1 Timothy 5:3-4 Honour widows that are widows indeed. But if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God. Matthew 15:1-9 Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread. But he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition. Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. Here Jesus reinforces the concept of honoring your father and mother, referencing the honor due them, and placing the command against cursing your parents as the direct counterpoint to the 5th Commandment. Leviticus 20:9 For every one that curseth his father or his mother shall be surely put to death: he hath cursed his father or his mother; his blood shall be upon him. The promise of a long life upon the earth for those that honor their parents, versus the death that those who fail to, who rob their parents, deserve. The doctrine of the Pharisees held that a son who pledged his wealth to the temple, while yet holding on to it for his own use, could declare it as a gift, and exempt the person from their duty to their father and mother. Mark 7:11 But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free. This commandment of men made God's law to no effect. Creating a holier than thou excuse. The curse of God upon a people who dishonor their parents, leading them to destruction, Is something that we have seen in modern times. The baby boomer generation was the first to abandon the care and support of their parents to the state. To nursing homes. To their health insurance and Medicare. Food stamps. They also abandoned care of their children to schools and day cares. They broke the generational cycle God had put into place and we have all suffered for it. They took the inheritance of their parents and squandered it while bragging that they're spending their grandchildren's inheritance on frivolous things. It's fitting that many have broken relationships with their now dead parents, and their children and grandchildren. And sadly, they spend their final days alone in the same nursing homes they consigned their own parents to. God put in place a system of family, of fathers in a hierarchy, wives in respectful submission to their husband, children under both, and honor due to the elders, to the widow indeed. A multi-generational family where children are arrows in the quiver of the father. Where each generation provides something to the unit, and stability to society. But those that have broken this tradition the same is a companion of the destroyer. They've brought only suffering and death. As always, Jesus is our example. Philippians 2:5-8 Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Being obedient unto death, honoring the Father. The good Son. John 6:38 For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. John 14:31 But that the world may know that I love the Father; and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do... John 15:10 If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love. Jesus provided the example of a lifelong commitment to honoring the Father. Of doing His will. Of obeying His Commandments. A lesson in obedience that we are called to emulate. Hebrews 5:8 Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered. As children of God by faith, as heirs, we owe the same honor and respect and obedience to the Lord. Even obedience unto death. Which is why martyrs are honored in heaven. Receiving greater reward and crowns. Loving God with your whole whole and soul, having fear of the Lord, begins with fearing your parents. That is why there are so many Proverbs revolving around being a good son. Why so many call upon parents to raise their children properly. Obedient children are a reflection of Christ and good parents are a reflection of the Lord. God, our Father. The ordered society that comes from it is a blessing. The obedience that it be well with us, that we live long upon the Earth. And to better know Him. Amen

Proverbs 29, the last of the sayings of Solomon transcribed by order of Hezekiah, begins with the reality of reprobation in those that stiffen their necks to reproof. The Bible often shows examples of heart hardened people, like Pharaoh and the Pharisees, coming to destruction without remedy, despite the reproof of the Lord. Romans 1:18-19 For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. Plagues, curses from Heaven, the reproof of Christ among them, all revealing the iniquity and unrighteousness of men, who refused to acknowledge the truth set before them. And their foolish hearts darkened. There became no more remedy for them, no repentance towards the truth of God. And so they are destroyed. Vs 2 echos similar sayings, that the rule of the righteous brings joy to the people, but the wicked kings bring mourning. Vs 3 brings another reminder to honor your father. A wise son will pay tribute to him, but the whoremongers spend what should rightfully be the family's wealth. Verse 4-8 show some of the ways that a wicked man lays snares for kings and neighbors. With gifts and flattering words, seeking favor. Or by the transgression of an evil man, there lies a snare of sin for others. Vengeance, wrath, or even common cause for filthy lucre's sake, others can be caught up in it when the wicked sin. But the righteous song and rejoice, happily trusting God. Avoiding those pitfalls. The righteous consider the poor, and turn away wrath. But the wicked don't care. Their scorn for the afflicted and bring others to transgression. Vs 10 The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul. The bloodthirsty, the violent man, the scorners and scoffers and fools, they all hate the upright man, the righteous in Christ. Their deeds are wicked, and the good man magnifies the light within him. John 3:20 For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. Jesus warns us of this truth; John 15:18-19 If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you. They hate His children because they hate Him. They hate the light that exposes their evil. They hate reproof and become stiff necked. They hold the truth in unrighteousness. Continuing in Proverbs 29:11 A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards. Keeping your tongue, holding back your opinions and thoughts, is a measure of wisdom. Discerned speech, as we have seen repeated in Proverbs, is valuable. Blabbing every idle thought that comes into your head is vain. Rulers who believe lies, he will be surrounded by wicked servants. This could have dual meaning. Either, due to his own delusion and desire to be told lies, only the wicked prosper in his court. Or, if he is acting on lies, the servants carrying out his will are made wicked. Both are true. Vs 13 is another reminder that we all, rich or poor, good or wicked, are given life by the same Lord. Another way of expressing the opposite end of life found in Ecclesiastes; Ecclesiastes 2:14 The wise man's eyes are in his head, but the fool walks in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all. Ecclesiastes 9:2 All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath. If all men are alive, their eyes lightened by the Lord, and all men die, having the same end, then all the things we gather, the vows we make, the wood, hay and stubble we accumulate, all is vanity. We should have no respect of persons and we should all seek that which is eternal, in Christ. This is the way. The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever. There is truth in the saying, that a good king or ruler will judge the poor fairly and righteously, and prosper. But only one King has faithfully judged all men, who are all poor in His sight, and His throne is established forever. Christ Jesus. Vs 15 is another admonition to not spare the rod of correction for a child. Feral children, left to their own foolishness, undisciplined, will bring their mother to shame. Vs 17 is a companion to 15, Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul. Sandwiched in between these sayings, vs 16 says; When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall. The fastest way of multiplying the wicked is to raise a generation without fear of their parents or fear for the Lord. They lack wisdom, fear of the Lord is its foundation. They shame their parents. They indulge themselves and think not of others. The city is made bloody and lacks defenses against the stranger. But vs 16 also is prophetic. 2 Timothy 3:1-7 This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away. For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts, Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. The wicked will be multiplied, but the righteous shall see their fall. In the end times, we who have overcome in Christ will see the wrath of God poured out on them. Where there is no vision, no righteousness of a king that follows the law, where there is no understanding of the ways of the Lord, the promises of God though His commandments, no prophecy and appreciation for the end times promise and eternal rewards, the people will perish. Finishing up Proverbs 29. V19 A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer. A master verbally correcting a servant has to weigh the fact that they may understand, but cannot answer for themselves due to fear. Don't be hasty with your words. Again, the discernment and temperance to withhold your words, rather than rushing to speak is wisdom. Those entrusted to our stewardship young, become as sons. More familiar sayings. Angry men stir up strife. Pride brings man low. Honor upholds the humble. Many of the repeated sayings remind me of those things my parents often said. "I told you a million times!" Repetition brings understanding. God wants us to internalize these things. My Father often said "Control yourself, or someone else will and you won't like it much." My mom, "you are your friends." These often said sayings stuck. And I passed them down with a few of my own. Don't keep company with a thief or you'll regret it. V25 The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe. Is yet another gospel message. We have security in the Lord when we trust in Him alone. So don't be afraid. Seek the favor of the Lord, from Whom all judgment comes, the rest will fall into place. V27 An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked. The children of disobedience are in conflict with the children of God, and vice versa. Don't be surprised when they hate you for His sake.

Proverbs 30 introduces the "sayings of Agur," who, some argue, is not Solomon, but possibly the sayings of a Gentile wiseman, under the influence of the Spirit. However, Jewish tradition views this as a pseudonym for King Solomon, describing him as one who "gathered" or collected wisdom. Jakeh, means pious and faithfully religious. It may be a title, rather than a name. The passage is addressed to Ithiel and Ucal, possibly students or symbolic names meaning "God with me" and "I am strong," respectively. These wise sayings were included in the scripture that Hezekiah's scribes compiled at the righteous King's request. The humble self-deprecation of the introduction in v2-3 ironically demonstrates this man's wisdom. Admission that as a brutish, or generally stupid man, with no training or knowledge, before dropping insightful and prophetic oracles, is a key to wisdom. Humility and willingness to grasp that even the smartest man doesn't know all the ways of God, is itself wise. Immediately, we are given an understanding of God and prophetic mention of Jesus, that also serves as a reminder of the limitations man has in understanding God. Asking rhetorically, Who it is that has done these things? What is His name? We know it is the Lord. What is His Son's name? We know it is Jesus. But the glass darkly that they saw through pointed only at the Son, not the name. Further revelation has given us the only name under Heaven by which a man may be saved. Regardless of the identity of the human author, the Spirit is showing us that even in the day of Solomon, and the Kings of Judah, God's Christ was known and believed on. v5-6 give the inspired case for Biblical fundamentalism. Every word of God is pure. 2 Peter 1:19-21 We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts: Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. And if every word of God is pure, we need an "every word" Bible. We are blessed that we have one, in the Authorized version, in English. Preserved by God unto all generations. God is a shield unto them that out their trust in Him is the promise of the gospel. The same yesterday, today and forever. And the curse against changing His word, adding to it, bringing false gospels, remains consistent; Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar. Be it Satan, in the beginning, asking Eve "Yea, hath God said" in Genesis 3:1, or modern churches claiming Christ while adding to and perverting the word to deceive. The wrath of God against those that corrupt His pure word. Deuteronomy 4:2 Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you. Revelation 22:18-19 For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book. The sure knowledge that we can trust the word of God is a foundation which we can build a strong fortress upon. Matthew 7:24-25 Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock. Continuing Proverbs 30 and the sayings attributed to Agur the son of Jakeh. Vs 7-9 is a form of prayer to the Lord to grant Agur favor in this lifetime; That God removes from him vanity and lies and to give neither poverty or riches, yet have sufficient food to eat. Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain. This should be the attitude we strive for. To take away the worthless and useless things in our life that take us away from fully serving God. That we deal honestly, not only with others but ourselves and therefore with God. Hiding nothing. Rationalizing or excusing nothing. Not heeding delusion that covers sin. Being satisfied with what God has blessed you with. Being content to have sufficient food to eat. Living simply unto the Lord. As many Proverbs before this have shown, the rich place their trust in their possessions. Themselves. They deny God and say "Who is the Lord?" Make no mistake, that even the temporary and sudden wealth an average or lower middle-class person may receive, a windfall or an unexpected inheritance or bonus, is often sufficient to knock them off the pathway of God. To make them forget the blessings and the Blesser. How much worse to have the wealth always about you, where you want for nothing and grow complacent towards God? And be thankful that you're not poor, and left to steal to eat. To curse God for your station and take His name in vain. Sometimes, in our Christian walk, we are tempted. Covetousness turns to greed. How often do we pray, not with thanksgiving for what we have, but desiring "just a little more, God, please?" That He would increase our wealth so we can afford some luxury or extravagance that we've convinced ourselves that we deserve. "Everyone else has one!" Coveting. "If we only had a little more!" Greed. Philippians 4:12 I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. Paul writes the end goal that Agur sought. To know how to be both rich and poor, everywhere in all things, to know whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. Why? I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me. The vanity of riches and the lies that rationalize sin away, are traps we should call upon the Lord to save us from. Contentment and gratitude go a long way to remove these things far from us. An example of this in my life, a small thing that maybe others can relate to; After grocery shopping, putting away the perishables in the fridge, and there being no room for the plenty, and cursing how nothing more fits, and finding old leftovers and nearly empty bottles of sauces, angrily throwing them away to make room for more...Or the pantry too full. Cans or boxes falling out because the shelf is packed, and cursing to yourself, "Dang it!" Imagine having so much plenty that this is a problem, and then asking God separately, "Lord, could you please increase my salary?" Or worse, many keep subscriptions to worldly streaming services, eat out multiple times a week, blow their money on a video game or some fancy brand clothing, or on bad and sinful habits like drinking, smoking or gambling...AND then asking God to give you more! We all do it to some degree, and you don't have to be on the extreme ends of rich or poor to have vanity and lies in our life. To forget the Lord, and deny Him. To justify sin and use His name in vain. Gratitude for the grace of God should be sufficient for us. Agur's prayer should be our own. Like Paul we need to work on being content, and doing the work of the Lord, allowing Him to bless us and provide what we need, keeping the vanity and lies away from us, leading us not into temptation. Delivering us from evil, even the evil of our own heart. Continuing Proverbs 30:10 Accuse not a servant unto his master, lest he curse thee, and thou be found guilty. The practical application of this is to guard against accusing the master through his proxy, his servant, especially false or exaggerated claims, that expose hypocrisy and deficiency in your own life. An accusation against another man's servant is an accusation against the master's stewardship. If the servant did wrong, dealt dishonestly, was slothful, the implication is that the master can't oversee his own, or is lax in some way. Spiritually, Paul uses this proverb to warn against brothers in Christ accusing one another for their failings in their Christian walk. Romans 14:4 Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand. We are answerable to God. If one is falling down in some area, weak in the faith, God will correct them. Accusing them accuses Him, and opens yourself up to being called out and chastened for your own deficiency before God. It isn't an excuse to enable, and standards and church discipline still exist. Fellowship can still be broken. But encouraging speech, edifying one another with fear and admonition of the Lord, is what we should use. Not accusations of being less holy than thou. Meekness and humility, with the grace to understand you're not perfect either, is the key. As Christ taught; Matthew 7:3-5 And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye. So, we must be cautious that we aren't projecting, that we who also serve the Lord aren't falling down in our own way. To not be a hypocrite, least He curse us and we be found guilty. v11-14 contains an indictment of a group of people, a crooked and perverse generation; There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.
