But Christians should take comfort and rejoice that we have a more sure word of prophecy; 2 Peter 1:19 We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts

Isaiah 14 continues the prophecy against the Babylonian empire, and addresses the Assyrians and Philistines at the end. It is a companion to the oracles given by Jeremiah, particularly chapters 28-31, where the prophet confronts a false prophet named Hananiah who predicts a quick restoration of Judah from Babylonian exile, directly contradicting Jeremiah's message of impending judgment; Jeremiah is proven right when Hananiah dies shortly after making his false prophecy. Chapters 29-31 then shift to a vision of God's future restoration of Israel, how the day of Jacob's trouble will end, and Babylon be destroyed. And a king of David's line, Zerubbabel, would rule the returning remnant. Here, Isaiah preaches the same future timeframe, and events. After the destruction of Babylon by the Medes, when the mercy of God will be upon those returning from captivity, still centuries away from Isaiah, will see them set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob. Foreshadowing the formation of Judea, with not only Judah, Benjamin and Levi, but Edomites, Chaldeans and others, the establishment of what would be called Jews. This burden of the Lord came upon Isaiah the year Ahaz died, ~716BC. Jeremiah preached during the pre-captivity era of 626-580BC. Amazing consistency and prophecy of God. The dual fulfillment with end times, where Satan, similarly will fall, and will be destroyed. How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations! For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High. Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit. We can know Satan's end will be as sure as Babylon. For he is the spirit of Babylon, even till this day. And that one world government that is endtimes Babylon will be destroyed, and cast into Hell, just as its predecessor was. Amen!

The judgment of the other kingdoms is preached, and the burden of knowing Moab's destruction is given to Isaiah. The kingdom disappeared a few decades after the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Jerusalem in 586BC, wiped off the map just as Isaiah describes more than a century earlier. The Moabite patriarch was Lot, the nephew of Abraham and the father of Moab and Ammon by his two daughters. The people lived in the land south east of the Jordan, and were enemies to Israel. It was Moab that led Israel to sin by the advice of Balaam. Introducing Idolatry through fornication with Moabite women. God erased the nation from the earth. Isaiah 17:14 And behold at eveningtide trouble; and before the morning he is not. This is the portion of them that spoil us, and the lot of them that rob us. ... Psalm 103:8 The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy. Psalm 94:3 Lord, how long shall the wicked, how long shall the wicked triumph? Isaiah 18 opens with nations far from Israel, but still close enough to be trading partners, wondering at the desolation caused by Assyria, sending messengers to find out what's going on. God says to wait upon the Lord's judgment. That He will raise the banner and sound the trumpet. But meanwhile, He takes His rest, and considers His judgement, the Lord's wrath building like the heat of the sun upon the grass, like the clouds made of dew that gatherer there. He promises, when the time is right, like fruit in its season, and the time to prune comes, he will cut off their branches, and winter shall come on them. Job, the 18th book of the Bible; Job 38:25-28 Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder; To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man; To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth? Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew? Job 15:32-33 It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green. Here in Isaiah 19, we find the prophet burdened with the word of the Lord against Egypt, the neighboring kingdom that many in Judah turned to for help when facing the threat of Assyrians and Babylonians. But the Lord says they will see drought and famine. Civil war and unrest. That they would turn to their idols and false religion and other vain things, and still be brought down low. There is a promise of a future where the Lord of hosts, the LORD would rule over them, and where Israel and even Assyria shall be at peace with them. The Lord shall be known in Egypt. The parallel to Isaiah 19 is the 19th book of the Bible, Psalms, with its repeated use of calling out to the Lord and being delivered to salvation. It also works with the Hebrew ordering, and Jonah. Jonah 1:14-16 Wherefore they cried unto the LORD, and said, We beseech thee, O LORD, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man’s life.. So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging. Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice unto the LORD, and made vows. Jonah 2:1-2 Then Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish’s belly, And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice. And of course the people of Nineveh, crying to the Lord for salvation.

In the year that Sargon of Akkad, King of Assyria, sent his general Tartan to take Philistine city of Ashdod, the word of the Lord came upon Isaiah. And the Lord instructed Isaiah to go about naked and barefoot, for 3 years. This as a sign to how the Assyrian empire would take Egypt and Ethiopia captive, leading their people away the same. The pride and glory of these nations would be brought low by the vessel God chose, Assyria. Just as Samaria and Assyria would be brought low by Babylon, and Judah led away into captivity. Isaiah, with great humility, obeyed the Lord. Naked, without shoes, for years to preach a point of God. How many of us have the opportunity to share God's truth with others, and being embarrassed hold back? Or say nothing? Fully clothed, even clothed in the righteousness of Christ Jesus, we still shy away from preaching His word. Let us be as bold and meek as Isaiah. Praise God and win souls, warning them of the coming destruction that every man faces without Jesus.

Here in Isaiah 21, the prophet has multiple visions of the various nations that are in the region, just as the previous chapters. It begins with another foretelling of the destruction of Babylon, by the Persians and Medes. Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media...Elam referring to the Persians, Media of Medes, and their preferred method of chariots, asses and camels. This prophecy is again taking place at a time where the greatness of the Babylonian empire had yet to occur, let alone her end at the hands of Cyrus and the Medo-Persian Empire. But its prophesied destruction served as a hope to those of Judah during the eventual 70yr captivity. That the corn of the Lord's threshing floor, those saved by faith having been separated from the chaff by the threshing, by tribulation, will know when this happens, when the treachery and spoils come against Babylon by Cyrus, their time of captivity would be near its end. In much the same way, we see the similarities to Revelation 18:1-2; And after these things I saw another angel come down from heaven, having great power; and the earth was lightened with his glory.And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird. Here in Isaiah, it is the watchman of his vision; And he answered and said, Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods he hath broken unto the ground. For those in the 1,260 days of the wrath, the fall of Babylon is a sign that the wrath of God is nearing its end, and the battle of Armageddon drawing nigh. The Millennial Reign set to begin. Verses 11-17 are prophetic visions of the fate of the nations of Ishmael's sons. The Arab kingdoms, and their fall. These seem to me to be fulfilled in short order after Isaiah's prophecy, and again, seem to be a sign to those to come later of God's word being trustworthy and true. That since these short-term predictions came true, you can trust on the longer-term predictions. The same watchman appears to deliver the message, out of Mt Seir, of the Edomites, which geographically gives a view of these southern nations.

The valley of vision, the place of preaching, the location of the law. Jerusalem in the valley of Zion. The burden of the word of God against Jerusalem comes upon the prophet. They've gone up to their rooftops, not in prayer, or to shout the truth. In his vision, Isaiah sees them in fear over their troubles. The men are not slain with swords, but famine. Thirst. Disease. The rules fled, only to be captured. And the prophet Isaiah weeps for his people. Elam and Kir, Persians and Assyrians, arrayed against Jerusalem. The valley filled with chariots. The walls with breaches. The men are preparing for siege. None are turning to the Lord or considering the ways of their fathers, in trusting in God. This prophecy is both fulfilled in Isaiah's time, Eliakim being made chief over the house of the King. The Assyrians and their hosts laying siege to the city. 2 Kings 18 tells the story. Rabshakeh the Assyrian taunting the city. And Isaiah preaching to King Hezekiah to fear not. His prayers were answered by the Lord, Who sent away the army by spreading doubt, and a rumor, and the fled. But there would be a day where they would be made desolate and cut off. It was inevitable because the Lord had spoken it. And in that day did the Lord God of hosts call to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth: And behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep, eating flesh, and drinking wine: let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die. The Lord brings His people to a place for repentance, and for mourning their lack of faith and wicked ways that He defend them and repent of the evil He would do unto them. But the people didn't harken, and remained as they were, feasting and drinking in the face of death. Jesus describes the man who has laid up stores here on earth, prepared as the men of Jerusalem, but it was for naught: Luke 12:19-21 And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided? So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God. Or as Paul wrote, coming from the other direction; why suffer for God and righteous if there is no hope of the resurrection 1 Corinthians 15:29-36 Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead? And why stand we in jeopardy every hour? I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily. If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; for to morrow we die. Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. Awake to righteousness, and sin not; for some have not the knowledge of God: I speak this to your shame. But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come? Thou fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die That because we are not as others, having no hope we may embrace the separation and discipleship of God in Christ, rather than being as men, most miserable, who say "eat, drink and be merry, for tomorrow we die."

The burden of Tyre. The main Phoenician trading city, in the coast of the Mediterranean. There are many geographic locations mentioned here that are no longer named as such: Tyre - Coastal Lebanon Zidon - Coastal Lebanon Tarshish - Spain or Portugal Chittim - Cyprus Egypt - Egypt Chaldeans - Southern Iraq Assyria - Northern Iraq/Southeastern Turkey Sihor - Nile River or Eastern Egypt The prophecy given by Isaiah against this mighty merchant nation being brought low, reminds me again of the fall of the city representing Babylon in Revelation 18:2-3, 11; And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird. For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication, and the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth are waxed rich through the abundance of her delicacies....And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more. Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not, till the Assyrian founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness: they set up the towers thereof, they raised up the palaces thereof; and he brought it to ruin. Howl, ye ships of Tarshish: for your strength is laid waste. And it shall come to pass in that day, that Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king: after the end of seventy years shall Tyre sing as an harlot. Isaiah prophesied the rise of Babylon, of the Chaldeans, and that it was the might of Assyria that would lead to its glory. Further, the prophet says during its 70 years of glory, coinciding with the 70 year captivity of Judah, that Tyre no longer be remembered. But that at the end of the captivity, the remaining Jews would value her trade, despite Tyre now being a harlot...committing fornication with all the kingdoms of the earth. Similar language to the city destroyed in Revelation, that had the spirit of Babylon upon it.

Revelation 4:10-11 The four and twenty elders fall down before him that sat on the throne, and worship him that liveth for ever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying, Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created. The end of all things. The earth decaying away. Barren. The great leaders gone, with the devil, leader of the host of one third the angels, cast into the pit. And the name of the Lord God of Israel, Jesus Christ, ruling and reigning from Zion as the ancients, the elders of Heaven, sing the glory of His name. Amen

Revelation 21:4-6 And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away. And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. 1 Corinthians 15:54-55 So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory. O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? Here is the promise of God in Christ. Here is the hope we trust in. That the Lord, Who takes mercy on the poor, the downtrodden, the weak in their times of trouble, Who is a shelter and a fortress and a shield, has victory over death and Hell. Has overcome this world. Is greater than the earthly gods, princes and principalities. That all nations shall bow and confess He is God. And He shall wipe away our tears. His enemies brought low. His children raised up. A perpetual feast in His presence, and no more pain. All things made new in Christ. Some use Isaiah 25:6 to justify drinking alcohol. Wines of the lees, that is juice of the grape left with the dregs, seed and skins, unfiltered, to develop a deeper taste and sparkling, indicates to them wines of today that are left in their lees; champagne, moscato and others. These style wines are lower in alcohol, generally, and consumed for their taste more than their ability to get someone drunk, but they do contain alcohol. But does every wine that is left in their lees for flavor, ferment? The Hebrew word shemer refers to the dregs or lees, and it generally is used in a negative context, comparing nations to unfiltered wine. Jeremiah 48:11-12 Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed. Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will send unto him wanderers, that shall cause him to wander, and shall empty his vessels, and break their bottles. The lack of tribulation, of wars and captivity, of the nation of Moab, God says, means they are like unrefined wine, left in their lees. Settled with the dregs. This is a negative quality. Compare this to Isaiah 25:6, which says we will drink wines on the lees well refined. The refining, the filtering, is the difference. Alcoholic wine, left in its lees, was filtered before drinking. But wines filtered from their lees before fermentation, and frequently filtered or refined, was significantly weaker and the alcohol content negligible. Plutarch, who lived between 46 and 120 A.D. said, "Wine is rendered feeble in strength when it is frequently filtered. The strength or spirit thus being excluded, the wine neither inflames the brain nor infests the mind and passions, and is much more pleasant to drink." Pliny the Elder (23-79AD) wrote, "The most useful wine was all its force or strength broken by the filter." This process, a well refined wine left in its lees, produced a weak, good tasting juice. Pleasant to drink, a drink of kings. Just as the fat and marrow of meat was desirable, highly refined, despirited wine was as well. The Lord of hosts will make unto all people a feast. Amen.

Isaiah 26 is a psalm of the resurrection of believers and the glory of Him that raised us, the Lord God, Jehovah. In Whom we trusted. He will ordain peace for us, and has wrought all our works in us. Amen! It also sings of His wrath on the wicked. His fire poured out, visiting the unrighteous with destruction. What sets the elect apart from the wicked is not their own goodness, our own righteousness. But one simple and humbling thing; Lord, in trouble have they visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them. And His promise to those of us who have called upon His name; Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead. Amen. What a blessed hope we have in Jesus.

Revelation 12 And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars: 2 And she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered. 3 And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads. 4 And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born. 5 And she brought forth a man child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron: and her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne. 6 And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days. 7 And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels, 8 And prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven. 9 And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him... Revelation 19:15 And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God. Romans 11 15 For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead? 16 For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. 17 And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; 18 Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. 19 Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. 20 Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear:

Isaiah continues to speak the word of God, now against Israel and Judah. The princes who are drunk with wine and cannot rule justly. The priests and prophets, who err in vision and stumble in judgment. Vision often being the understanding and knowledge of the word of God, they preach vain things. Their tables full of vomit. Literally and spiritually. Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts. Hebrews 5:13-14 For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe. But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil. We learn the word, precept upon precept. Built like a wall, upon the cornerstone, level and plumb. Square and true. Line upon line. Here a little, there a little. Psalm 119:104 Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way. Jesus is that cornerstone laid for us. The rock of our salvation upon which we stand. Like the wise man who built his home upon it. Psalm 118:22 The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. Matthew 21:42 Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes? Acts 4:11 This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner. 1 Peter 2:7-8 Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed. There is no other foundation upon which man can built that doesn't come to naught, but Jesus. And we build up on that rock, precept by precept. Here a little, there a little. Until we are raised to judgment, and eternal life. Matthew 7:24 Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock 1 Corinthians 3:11-15 For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire. Amen Now the destruction of the Lord, His wrath, is like a farmer who plows his field, turning over the soil, so that he may plant seed, and harvest fruit. They beat the shafts of the plants with a rod to loosen the seeds. The Lord teaches them these things, and like all of creation, as a parable for His ways. This also cometh forth from the Lord of hosts, which is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in working. What a wonderful thing to know we are instructed by all creation to better know the Lord God. That His percepts are found in all of nature, that man have no excuse. Rejoice when the field is broken up, and plowed under. That the seeds may rise and live again, and bring forth fruit.

1 Corinthians 1:19 For it is written, I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent. Matthew 15:8 This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. Romans 9:21-23 Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour? What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Isaiah, preaching against the city of David, that city Jerusalem, here called Ariel, or the lion of God, and again saying the wisdom of the leaders and prophets will be rendered useless. Unable to understand the vision of the Lord, as a book sealed up to the wise and not understood by the unlearned. The wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid. The promise of the coming of Jesus, that the blind will see and the dead hear His word and the meek and poor shall rejoice in Him, the Holy One of Israel. These are echos of themes preached by Christ Himself and the Epistles of the Apostles. The word of God is powerful. And the scorners and the wicked one are brought to naught, Satan and those too wise for the wisdom of God, the proud and unbelieving, those that watch for iniquity, the opportunity to sin, brought low. Cut off. Those That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought. We see scoffers today, using "cancel culture" and PC policies to jump on men of God preaching, for using a word to describe sodomites, for an example, and then seek to destroy them over it. But in the end we shall not be ashamed in Him. He that redeemed Abraham, will redeem all who trust in the Lord. And come to the knowledge of the truth. Amen.

Jeremiah 42:19-22 The Lord hath said concerning you, O ye remnant of Judah; Go ye not into Egypt: know certainly that I have admonished you this day. For ye dissembled in your hearts, when ye sent me unto the Lord your God, saying, Pray for us unto the Lord our God; and according unto all that the Lord our God shall say, so declare unto us, and we will do it. And now I have this day declared it to you; but ye have not obeyed the voice of the Lord your God, nor any thing for the which he hath sent me unto you. Now therefore know certainly that ye shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence, in the place whither ye desire to go and to sojourn. Jeremiah 44:14 So that none of the remnant of Judah, which are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall escape or remain, that they should return into the land of Judah, to the which they have a desire to return to dwell there: for none shall return but such as shall escape. The prophetic warning to Judah, that when their time of tribulation came, the captivity to Babylon, not to flee to or trust in Egypt to save them, was fulfilled in Jeremiah's day. He also warned them, referring back to the prophets, beginning with Isaiah. God, knowing what they would do, warns against it. And you know those in Jerusalem who believed the word of God did not flee, and be destroyed in the way. The dual fulfillment here is also clear, the Holy One of Israel, the Lord Christ Jesus at His second coming and the wrath that pours out from His lips, the fire of Tophet, a name for Hell, is lit from the brimstone from His mouth, that kindles it. Egypt is a representation of the world, our pre-Christian life of sin, under the yoke of the law, slaves to sin. As the Bible says again and again of the Israelites being led by Moses, that in their freedom they would long to return to the bondage of Egypt out of fear or inconvenience. Exodus 13:17 And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt. This is written for our admonition, that we who are His children don't turn again to the world and to sin when we face tribulation. That trusting in Egypt is death. We all come out of Egypt. We all are baptized in the crossing, and sojourn in the wilderness, awaiting the promised land. The promise of paradise on the other side is the hope of our faith. Without that hope, we fear and faint. Relying on the world to save us is folly, we should suffer gladly that the Lord delivers us. The wicked will be punished. The Lord will fight for us, and destroy those that trouble us, and has a place prepared for them, deep and large, the pile is fire and much wood. The breath of the Lord is like a stream of brimstone. Amen

Psalm 20:7-8 Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the Lord our God. They are brought down and fallen: but we are risen, and stand upright. Continuing the woe against Judah for turning to Egypt, to the world and the things thereof, rather than to God. The Lord promises to deliver us, and in every trial, we have an opportunity to grow our faith, and we are not ashamed. He keeps His promise. God is faithful to deliver. Amen

Another prophecy of the endtimes, the rule of Christ Jesus, and His saints, the peace we shall have. The justice and wrath poured out on the wicked. The churl and the vile, the women at ease when they should be pleasing for mercy. God's promise of peace for the believing, of the bounty and plenty and strong defense of Him, always includes the just punishment of the wicked. They cannot be separated. God's love towards us, mercy and forgiveness, His grace, requires His wrath upon the ungodly. Revelation 6:10-11 and they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth? And white robes were given unto every one of them; and it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled. We should not only take comfort of our own salvation, but when we despair that the unrighteous prosper, we should praise God that vengeance is His, He will repay. Psalm 73 Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart. 2 But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped. 3 For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. 4 For there are no bands in their death: but their strength is firm. 5 They are not in trouble as other men; neither are they plagued like other men. 6 Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain; violence covereth them as a garment. 7 Their eyes stand out with fatness: they have more than heart could wish. 8 They are corrupt, and speak wickedly concerning oppression: they speak loftily. 9 They set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walketh through the earth. 10 Therefore his people return hither: and waters of a full cup are wrung out to them. 11 And they say, How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the most High? 12 Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches. 13 Verily I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocency. 14 For all the day long have I been plagued, and chastened every morning. 15 If I say, I will speak thus; behold, I should offend against the generation of thy children. 16 When I thought to know this, it was too painful for me; 17 Until I went into the sanctuary of God; then understood I their end. 18 Surely thou didst set them in slippery places: thou castedst them down into destruction. 19 How are they brought into desolation, as in a moment! they are utterly consumed with terrors. 20 As a dream when one awaketh; so, O Lord, when thou awakest, thou shalt despise their image. 21 Thus my heart was grieved, and I was pricked in my reins. 22 So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee. 23 Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand. 24 Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory. 25 Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee. 26 My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever. 27 For, lo, they that are far from thee shall perish: thou hast destroyed all them that go a whoring from thee. 28 But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord God, that I may declare all thy works.

Those that spoil, that come to a place that isn't theirs and take what they like, dealing treachery, will suffer vengeance, God promises. And the safety of Zion, that heavenly city of Jerusalem, will be where the Lord rules and He will protect us forever, amen. Micah 7:1-3 Woe is me! for I am as when they have gathered the summer fruits, as the grapegleanings of the vintage: there is no cluster to eat: my soul desired the firstripe fruit. The good man is perished out of the earth: and there is none upright among men: they all lie in wait for blood; they hunt every man his brother with a net. That they may do evil with both hands earnestly, the prince asketh, and the judge asketh for a reward; and the great man, he uttereth his mischievous desire: so they wrap it up. Micah 7:7 Therefore I will look unto the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me. Micah is the 33rd book of the Bible, we are halfway through the book of Isaiah. Praise the Lord for His promises to His people.

Revelation 6:12-17 And I beheld when he had opened the sixth seal, and, lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood; And the stars of heaven fell unto the earth, even as a fig tree casteth her untimely figs, when she is shaken of a mighty wind. And the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together; and every mountain and island were moved out of their places. And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand? The sure judgment of God against all nations is true. And who shall be able to stand? The destruction and desolation, where only carrion birds flourish, fed by the dead, and wild goats and beasts will live in the habitations that belonged to man. Edom destroyed. But the promise to those that seek out the book of the Lord, the Word of God, none shall fail. And all shall live in peace, on the land which He has provided us, forever. Amen

The promise of God to His people, to the righteous in Christ, to the redeemed from bondage, ransomed of the Lord by the blood of Jesus, to enter into the promised land. There are echos of the end of captivity for His people out of Babylon, which would come to pass centuries after Isaiah's prophecy, but like so much of his preaching, it points to the fulfillment of God's plan in the end times. And what a glorious day that will be.

Here in Isaiah 36 we have the third telling of this historical event, where the captain of the Assyrian horde has come down through Samaria, along the Jordan, from Lachish, the city of Dan in the north, unto the plains before Jerusalem in the South. Hezekiah is king over Judah, and while not a good king in the tradition of David, but he has trusted the Lord, preached by Isaiah, with his illness and been healed, being granted 15 years to his life by God. He had taken down altars to the false gods, in high places. And here the city is under siege. The Assyrian Rabshakeh, speaking in Hebrew, calls out to the King's advisors on the wall, telling them of the futility of their position and asking What confidence is this wherein thou trustest? What a question, and one our adversaries in the world, mockers and scoffers and those seeking us harm may ask. One our spiritual adversary, Satan, may corner us into answering. Rabshakeh says who will you trust? Egypt, a broken reed, nothing one could put their confidence in. For us, God uses Egypt as an example of the bondage to sin and the world. Or do you trust in the Lord? But notice it isn't the Lord God, but his natural man understanding of what God is, and what religion of the believers looks like. But if thou say to me, We trust in the Lord our God: is it not he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar? The false religion of worshipping God in high places and idols and altars, which the world sees vs our worship in our hearts, at the Temple of God's choosing. Hezekiah had done right, and Rabshakeh is mocking it. The world sees the Roman Catholic Church, or any of its splinters this way, as the true religion of Christianity. If we reject those trappings, they think we weaken God, or doubt our faith. We see this all the time, when the world makes fun of "Pastor Bob" with a strip mall church. The world respects the high places, the ornate temples made of hands. They don't fear the god of these places, but they understand it, the carnality of elegant churches, idols, altars. To the world, trusting the Lord humbly, and in weakness is foolish. But to us, strength. 2 Corinthians 12:8-10 For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.

For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake. Never for the "Jew's" sake. Never for the "covenant in the wilderness," never because the Jews were righteous and loyal to the Lord. They were ever backslidden and unfaithful, and in rare circumstances, with the right leadership, halfheartedly with God for a season. God protected the remnant of Judah for us, the believers of this world, that Jesus may come and fulfill His promise to David, and be put to death in the city God chose.

Again, Isaiah 38 retells 2 Kings 20, and King Hezekiah's illness unto death, his calling upon the Lord to save him, and the grace of God to extend his life 15 years. With the news from Isaiah, and the sign of the sun moving backwards in its path 10°, Hezekiah praises God. O Lord, by these things men live, and in all these things is the life of my spirit: so wilt thou recover me, and make me to live. Behold, for peace I had great bitterness: but thou hast in love to my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption: for thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back. For the grave cannot praise thee, death can not celebrate thee: they that go down into the pit cannot hope for thy truth. Both praise for his healing, but more, the king praises God for His salvation. That men, including himself, had no love of peace. There is none good. All have fallen short of the glory of God. But in His love, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Salvation was offered, a gift given by grace, and our soul delivered from corruption. Casting all our sins behind us. Reconciled with a perfect and righteous God. And those who forsake the gift, there is no hope for them. They that go down into the pit, into Hell, cannot hope for the Lord's truth. Settle with the Lord in the way. Because by judgment, you'll be held to every sin. To the whole debt. Now is the time. Today is the day. If you don't know for certain that you have eternal life, right now, that can never be lost, repent. Believe on Christ Jesus. Become one of the living. The children of the Father. Sons of God. Knowing: The Lord was ready to save me: therefore we will sing my songs to the stringed instruments all the days of our life in the house of the Lord. Rejoice in His salvation. Amen

Hezekiah, who had expressed so much faith and appreciation in God's mercy, saving him from death and granting him 15 years longer to live, crashes out when the envoys from Babylon visit him to congratulate him for his miraculous recovery. And instead of praising God and giving Him all glory and honor for it, shows them instead his wealth and treasure. This is a cautionary tale for Christians. At the moments of our Christian walk, where God has blessed us, and we have been humbled enough to seek the truth, and given opportunity to serve Him, is often the moment we fall the hardest. Spiritual triumph, wounded by pride. Our blessings are to give us opportunities to praise and sanctify the Lord to others who don't know His grace and mercy. And yet we not only hesitate to give Him the glory, we often take credit for ourselves. This will, as we know, come back to harm Judah, as their wealth will be remembered and covered by Babylon as its empire grows. Isaiah prophesies their captivity and Hezekiah's sons serving the Babylonian king. Yet, Hezekiah takes the wrong lesson from this warning, taking comfort that the worst will be for future generations, and not his to deal with. How familiar this is for us today. How our fathers fell to sin and pride, squandering the blessings of God, and leaving their children to deal with the inevitable consequences? That is why, even when we backslide, even when we let our pride get the better of us, and we do that which is wrong in the sight of God, that we turn again to Him in humility, seeking forgiveness. There are some mistakes we make, and sins we commit, that have long lasting repercussions. An act of fornication that results in a baby, or a disease. A marriage broken by adultery. A drunken night ending in death. Hezekiah had his pride become a cause for his children to be slaves and his nation made desolate, and he took selfish solace in the fact it wouldn't affect him. What a wicked thing. Put others, especially your children, above yourself and when you err, turn to the Lord for forgiveness least your sins rebound in future generations.

We are there in Isaiah 40, and the Spirit of the Lord has poured forth out of the prophet, to speak to the fathers and those of us unto whom the end of the world has come. And what words of power and promise! And praise God that The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever. The very nature of God revealed in this chapter, one of the greatest in the book of Isaiah, is echoed throughout scripture, especially the New Testament. Beginning with an irony, telling the false prophets of Jerusalem to speak words of comfort, that she is pardoned. That their warfare is over. As Jeremiah will, years later, talk about the false prophets preaching "peace, peace." But Judah, and eventually the world, will receive from the Lord's hand double for all her sins. The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the desert a highway for our God. A prophecy of John the Baptist, going before Jesus to make the King's Highway, the way of the Lord. Making the land flat, the way smooth, the lanes straight. In our hearts, that Jesus may come unto us. And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed. He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young. Jesus is that good Shepherd. He directs the Spirit of the Lord, teaching all things. John 16:13-14 Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come. He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you. And in the presence of the Lord God Almighty, by Whom all things are made, He counts all the nations, even Judah as so little as dust. A drop in the bucket. All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity. In His greatness, how can man seek to capture Him in an idol? Or an image? What likeness will ye compare Him to? The Catholics and her harlot daughters, making images of God, Christ Jesus or of man, attempting to in their spiritual poverty, without an oblation, having not the sacrifice of Jesus, they seek a cunning work of men to take His place. Have ye not known? have ye not heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning? have ye not understood from the foundations of the earth? It is the Lord, from everlasting, Who has created all things, the gold and silver and trees and stone...they are nothing to the Living God. All the wisdom and judgment of the earth is vanity. God fainteth not. He never shall grow weary. But all our lives will wither and come to naught. But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength. Our hope is in Him that never tires and Who created all things, and we shall be strong in Him. Never tire. Never be weary. Kept by the power of God. Amen

Isaiah continues to prophesy the coming of the Lord, the councilor, the redeemer, with glad tidings of the good news; the gospel of Christ. The isles, the gentile nations afar off, with their plated wooden images of dead gods, all vanity. But the power of the living God is undeniable. He that called out the righteous man, the Holy One of Israel, who set up the worm that is Jacob, to bring Him. The poor and need seeking water, that is the truth of God, the living water of Christ Jesus; I the Lord will hear them, I the God of Israel will not forsake them. I will open rivers in high places, and fountains in the midst of the valleys: I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water. We are those dry lands. We are the thirsty. John 7:38 He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. This is done that they may see, and know, and consider and understand. The hand of the Lord has done this. And all the vanity of man will fade. Amen.

Isaiah 42 continues preaching on Christ to come, Whom God is well pleased, come to make perfect the Law, and to lead the blind of the gentile isles, away from the dead idols to the straight ways, to paths they had not known. And of the children of Jacob, who are His blind and deaf servants, unwilling or unable to see, to cry out for restoration, they will be made jealous, and be spoiled. Not just the treasure of Jerusalem. Not just her gold and silver and the wealth of the temple. God has given Jacob, Israel, the Jews, over to the robbers. Because they were not obedient to the law. And what they spoiled wasn't of this world, but the treasure that is salvation in Christ. The temple destroyed by the Jews and raised up in 3 days. The Lord God sent the nations to spoil that treasure, Who is Jesus. To find salvation in Him. Psalm 107:5-9 Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them. Then they cried unto the Lord in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses. And he led them forth by the right way, that they might go to a city of habitation. Oh that men would praise the Lord for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men! For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.

The Lord God of Israel, the Redeemer, our Saviour. His holy Name being witnessed by His people to bring all the nations unto Him for forgiveness, that all may be justified. Held in His hand. Our sins and transgressions remembered no more. This was the plan for Jacob. This was the plan for His people. But thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob; but thou hast been weary of me, O Israel. Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary, and have given Jacob to the curse, and Israel to reproaches. This is why their covenant was ended. Not because the law given Moses in the wilderness to deliver unto the people was flawed. But the flaw was in them. Hebrews 8:6-9 But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. They continued not in His covenant. The flaw was with them. In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away. The old covenant was ended. A new testament in Christ was established. And every nation carries a righteous remnant of believers. Who are His and of His name. Christ Jesus. Psalm 86:7 In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee: for thou wilt answer me. John 10:28-30 and I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand. I and my Father are one.

Again, a wonderful picture of salvation and redemption by the Lord God, upon His servants who are Israel. The same believers in the Old Testament and New. The living waters promised in Christ. One shall say, I am the Lord's; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel. I believe this is a clear prophecy of what has become the situation after Jesus ascension, and here in these last days. Christians say we are the Lord's, and Jews of the 1st century, "We are of Jacob." And now, those who claim to be Israel. It also reflects the reality of Isaiah's time. The saved believers, the southern kingdom of Judah and the northern kingdom of Israel. Elect according to grace. Those who believe they are elect according to heritage. Those who claim election while being far from Him. That's what my thoughts are in this, and God reminds us, He is in charge over all. Thus saith the Lord the King of Israel, and his redeemer the Lord of hosts; I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God. And who, as I, shall call, and shall declare it, and set it in order for me, since I appointed the ancient people? and the things that are coming, and shall come, let them shew unto them. There is no God besides Him. Fear not. We who trust in Him shall not be ashamed. Verses 9-20, Isaiah in the Spirit, speaking the word of God, describes the vanity of the idolator. And perfectly describes the false religion of Jeroboam, and its modern version, Roman Catholicism. They make and fashion images of men, forming crucifixes; The carpenter stretcheth out his rule; he marketh it out with a line; he fitteth it with planes, and he marketh it out with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house. The same wood that warms him and cooks his food, he bows to and prays to. They cannot even comprehend how foolish it is to worship before a created thing that they also burn to ash. The residue they make an abomination of. And as the Lord reminds us of His promises to blot out our transgressions, to redeem us from sin, to never forget us, His sons and daughters, the Lord drops the name Cyrus. This is written in the 700s, BC. Cyrus will become king of the Medo-Persian Empire, in 559 BC. What a sure word of prophecy! Throughout Isaiah God makes promises for things to happen that are yet to come, short-term long-term and end times. And by the hearing of His word, we can grow in faith. Knowing that His word is true. What an incredible gift God has given us. We can rely on Him and never be ashamed.

Continuing the very clear, undeniable, easy to understand prophecy of God through Isaiah, of the future King of the Medo-Persian empire, more than a century off in the future. Isaiah 45 is one of the most powerful chapters in the Bible. God says He has named Cyrus as deliverer, for after the Babylonian captivity, still decades away, after the 70 years of desolation in Jerusalem as prophesied, the Babylonian empire will be over thrown, and Cyrus will free the Jews wot return, to rebuild the temple. That the line of David continued to Christ and the place God put His name would stand until it served its purpose, the death burial and resurrection of Jesus. And just as sure and specific and certain as this prophecy is for Cyrus, so it is for the Messiah. By this we may know there is no other God beside Him. He is the Lord, and there is none else. For all creation testifies, and all the prophets gave witness, and all the promises made to the faithful, and the evidence all around that those who trust in Him are never ashamed. God calls all His shots beforehand, and we see the results are true. And if these things are sure and true, then know the promise of salvation and eternal life in Christ Jesus is as well. Drop down, ye heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness: let the earth open, and let them bring forth salvation, and let righteousness spring up together; I the Lord have created it. The Lord has created all things that, in His time, in the end, salvation and righteousness are as a flood upon the earth. And like the flood of Noah, we shall be delivered and those that reject God will be destroyed. Those that chase after gods of their own hands, who worship the created more than the Creator, shall be confounded and ashamed when the day comes. But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end. The Lord openly declares these things, all that is right. His perfect law. His kept promises. His holy Name. I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear. John 5:37 And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. Philippians 2:9-11 Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father 1 John 5:7 For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. The word of God is true, let every man be a liar who rejects it. All that are incensed against Him shall be ashamed. Those who do not wish to retain God in their knowledge, who hold the truth in unrighteousness, they will be made to know He loves us. And in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and glory. Galatians 3:27-29 For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise. Romans 11:26-27 And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins. Amen For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me. This verse, a direct reference to Cyrus, is also a prophecy of Christians, under Jesus. Made sons of God and co-heirs with Christ. Those called by His name. The elect of Israel. That we are given God as a surname, adopted as sons and daughters in Him. For Jacob was His servant to bring about the Messiah, and the elect of Israel, the name Jacob is given by the Lord after a night of wrestling with Him over his past, and facing his future. Knowing Esau was riding towards him, with 400 men, Jacob went by himself to pray. And after lasting the night, prevailing, and being made lame by a touch of God to his hip, he relented to God's will, and was renamed Israel in Genesis 32:28. We become the elect of Israel by adoption. And we are called by His name, in Christ. And like Jacob, given a new name in the resurrection. Revelation 2:17 He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it. Amen

Psalm 115:4-8 Their idols are silver and gold, The work of men's hands. They have mouths, but they speak not: Eyes have they, but they see not: They have ears, but they hear not: Noses have they, but they smell not: They have hands, but they handle not: Feet have they, but they walk not: Neither speak they through their throat. But we serve the living God, Who bears us for our afflictions. Who carries us in our transgressions. Whose promises are kept, and Who we can depend on. Who does not rust nor rot nor decay. He is God and there is none else. There is none like Him. Amen

The reproach of the Chaldeans, Babylon, that in the end their destruction is assured as promised of God. That all their wisdom, sorcerers, prognosticators, seers, astrologers, and enchantments will fail them in the time of God's wrath. 2 Corinthians 1:12 For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward. They will be found naked, and ashamed. But not so those whose trust is in God; 2 Corinthians 5:1-3 For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens. For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven: If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked. (2 Corinthians is the 47th book of the Bible) So we have seen that those trusting in men, idols and witchcraft and sorcery, will all be found ashamed. Let down. But we who trust in Christ never will be.

The frustration of the Lord, Who is longsuffering to us-ward, Who would that no man perish, is fierce. To a people so stiff-necked that He describes the sinew of it as iron. Obstinate. Despite the Lord's constant warnings at the mouths of the prophets, promises made and kept. Things that could never be known by man, yet were revealed by His hand. And yet they did not believe. The Lord says He did these things that they could not credit their idols or their images. Thou hast heard, see all this; and will not ye declare it? I have shewed thee new things from this time, even hidden things, and thou didst not know them. Isaiah is full of such admonition, and in it Jesus is constantly being revealed unto them. Just short of spelling it out explicitly here and throughout hai preaching. In a few chapters, Isaiah 53, it will be all the more explicit. And yet they did not declare Him. They did not acknowledge the Lord that took them out of Egypt. They did not follow His precepts and commandments. They did not trust in Him that created all things and was their promised redemption. They heard, and knew not. For my name's sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off. God has promised the blessing of Abraham would be fulfilled. The covenant with David. And for His own sake, that those promises not be made void, He is refining Judah with affliction. But will deliver them from the Babylonians so that Jesus may come. The Lord our God, first and last. The alpha and omega. Ho Israel, repent. But they would not.

Jesus Christ, to Whom all the prophets gave witness. The redeemer of God. Luke 2:25-32 And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him. And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ. And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law, Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said, Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. The mistaken idea that no one in the Old Testament period understood that there would come a Christ, Who would be salvation to all who believed on Him, is false. Moses and the prophets all gave witness to His coming. And though they saw it afar off, most dying in faith having not seen Him, but persuaded of Him, many, right up to the birth of Jesus and His coming into His glory, waited, watching for him. Luke 2:36-38 And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity; And she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day. And she coming in that instant gave thanks likewise unto the Lord, and spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem. They heard the word of God preached, and believed. Faith cometh by hearing the word of God. And there were people looking forward to their redemption. A light to the Gentiles. That all nations be blessed in Him. The mighty one of Jacob, the son of David. They watched and waited for Him, just as we watch and wait for His return; By faith. Amen. The short-term prophecy, the comfort to the people Isaiah was preaching to, and the generation that followed, was that because of this Holy One, because of the Messiah, God would protect them, even through captivity. That their sons and daughters would be returned. That God would save their children, and contend with the Babylonian empire that took them for a season. We are given example after example of God, through the prophets, making a promise of things to come, both evil and good. And every time His truth is revealed by the events that He gave witness to, our faith can grow. That just as assuredly as Israel was scattered, and Judah went into captivity, so too were they delivered by the promise of the Lord. And just as surely as this came to pass, the Holy One of God would come to redeem all nations. The isles, or Gentiles. From the north and west, unto even Sinim, or the far east of China. All would come to know Him. Jesus, the only name under Heaven by which we are saved.

Isaiah, preaching the word of God against Jacob, against Judah, having visions of Christ, smitten on the back and pummeled in the face, silent, as flint. Not confounded. Knowing He would not be ashamed. Hebrews 12:2 Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. Romans 8:31 What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us? There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus. We who are lost, fearing the Lord, in the dark, we trust in the name of the Lord, and stay upon his God. And come into His beautiful light. Note the separation of the Son and the Father in how the prophet frames this. The understanding is there, 700 years before Christ. As it was in the beginning. They always looked to Jesus. And those who sought to make their own light in the darkness, a spark. An ember. Nothing but sorrow in their end. Hebrews 1:8-12 But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom. Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows. And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands: They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment; And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.

Harken ye righteous. The Lord God Who called Abram of Ur, a Chaldean, out from his country to be the father of nations, whose seed was Christ, and blessed him and increased him, the same Lord Who divided the waters of the Red Sea, that serpent Rahab (not the harlot, but the Egyptian sea), promises deliverance for Zion. A saviour. And just as God kept His promise to Abraham, freed those in Egypt, He will deliver Judah from their eventual captivity in Babylon. And more, He will deliver all those from many nations, who have His law upon their hearts, who are made righteous by His righteousness. We will see Him deliver us from death. Even as those that revile us decay away like old garments. Even as the earth passes away. We will live in Zion, New Jerusalem on a new earth under a new heaven, unto everlasting joy. The redeemed of the Lord shall return, and come singing into Zion. His salvation shall be forever. Amen

Continuing in Isaiah 52, this week of the passion, the sacrifice and triumph of Christ Jesus. Behold, my servant shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high. As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men. Luke 22:63-71 And the men that held Jesus mocked him, and smote him. And when they had blindfolded him, they struck him on the face, and asked him, saying, Prophesy, who is it that smote thee? And many other things blasphemously spake they against him. And as soon as it was day, the elders of the people and the chief priests and the scribes came together, and led him into their council, saying, Art thou the Christ? tell us. And he said unto them, If I tell you, ye will not believe: And if I also ask you, ye will not answer me, nor let me go. Hereafter shall the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God. Then said they all, Art thou then the Son of God? And he said unto them, Ye say that I am. And they said, What need we any further witness? for we ourselves have heard of his own mouth. Jesus was beaten, bloody and unrecognizable. Taunted and mocked. Ridiculed for our transgressions. As the prophet bare witness. According to the scriptures.

Today, marks the second of three days Jesus spent in Hell paying for our sins. It was pictured for us by God with the Feast of unleavened bread, the second of three sabbaths in a row following Christ's crucifixion as our Passover Lamb. Three days of no work, as Jesus did it all, as our burnt offering, provided by God, just as he provided one to Abraham taking the place of Isaac. Jesus blood on the mercy seat, washing away the sins of all who believe on His name. Acts 8:26-35 And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him. The place of the scripture which he read was this, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: and who shall declare his generation? for his life is taken from the earth. And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man? Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus. As we await the resurrection Sunday, commemorating the triumph of the Lord Jesus over death and Hell, after His suffering on the cross for our sins, let us remember that it was as according to scripture. How that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures. To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins. Here in. Isaiah 53, we see such clear prophecy of Christ. And a poignant reminder of what He suffered for our sake. That by His stripes, the vicious scourging Jesus received, we are healed. How He bare our iniquity. And was bruised for it. Carrying our sorrows. Thank you Lord Jesus for the gift of salvation, paid for by such a heavy price. Thank you for the scriptures that show your power and mercy. Knowing your love for us that while we were yet sinners, You died for us. And knowing, that as with all the scriptures, we can count on Your word to be true. Amen. Psalm 22:16-18 For dogs have compassed me: The assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: They pierced my hands and my feet. I may tell all my bones: They look and stare upon me. They part my garments among them, And cast lots upon my vesture. Zechariah 12:10 And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.

"But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator. For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth. Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood. For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you. Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry. And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and WITHOUT SHEDDING OF BLOOD IS NO REMISSION." Hebrews 9:11-22 ... "Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water." Hebrews 10:22 Today marks the 3rd day since the Jews had Jesus arrested, tortured and killed. It is the weekly Sabbath. Most of His disciples were in hiding or scattered. The Apostles huddled with some of the most faithful, in fear of the Jews and Romans, praying for themselves and their dead leader, and no doubt questioning their beliefs in the face of the reality that their master had been so viciously, and with brutal finality, been slain. That He lay entombed. Perhaps remembering His words to them in hope: John 14 Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me. 2 In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. 3 And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also. 4 And whither I go ye know, and the way ye know. Perhaps they remembered when Jesus told the Pharisees "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up," but as with the many dark sayings Jesus used in His ministry, did all fully understand? We are blessed beyond measure to KNOW the risen Christ, to have the Holy Spirit as comforter, to set our minds at ease in tribulation, but these early followers were living by faith alone, and I often think about how difficult and trying those 3 days and 3 nights must have been for that early congregation, especially that 'Saturday' morning. Not knowing they were just one day away from seeing Jesus alive and triumphant... His own followers may have recalled Jesus promise to rise again, and sought comfort in it, but the Jews who were enemies of Christ worried... Matthew 27 62 Now the next day, that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate, 63 Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again. 64 Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first. 65 Pilate said unto them, Ye have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as ye can. 66 So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch. Job 19 23 Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book! 24 That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever! 25 For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: 26 And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God: 27 Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; though my reins be consumed within me. What we've treated as a punchline to nog jokes is deadly serious, especially when you consider how dependent everything from healthcare to things like food service, are on engineering marvels created by White men over the past few generations. Roman concrete is one thing, but planes literally falling out of the sky, another.

Again, Isaiah is given the prophecy of Christ Jesus and the coming of the Holy One of Israel. The chapter opens with a call to come and drink freely, to eat without money, without a price. Just as Jesus preaches throughout the gospels, especially John 6 and 7. John 6:35 And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. John 7:37 If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. By grace, at no cost to us. Not the bread that satisfies not, paid for by our labors. But being full of His word, the goodness we delight in. Hear, and your soul shall live and I will make an everlasting covenant with you. You can hear the voice of Jesus echoing to Isaiah. A light to lighten the Gentiles, the nations that knew not. Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near. The Lord has mercy on those who turns unto Him, for God will abundantly pardon our sins. His word is the precious seed we bear as we share the gospel. And it will not return void. It will bring forth fruit, being seed to the sower and bread to the eater. The picture of salvation by growing grain, just as Jesus preaches by parable. To the Lord, the increase. The harvest. And we shall come rejoicing, bringing in the sheaves. Amen

Isaiah 56 continues a theme in these chapters which are primarily about Christ, and that is the adoption of strangers into the covenant. Of all the isles of man. The Gentiles. Not only in the post-Resurrection world of NT Christianity, but even then, during the captivity there were those saved by faith, worshipping the Living God. Nebuchadnezzar, for example, who in Daniel 4 sends out a message to the entire known world, in every tongue declaring the Lord. People who took hold of the covenant. Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people. The dual fulfillment is there, but the prophecy is of Christ either way. Meanwhile, the Jews who were to be His watchmen, who were supposed to be teachers of the law, they are blind. Ignorant. As dumb dogs, unable to bark, loving to slumber. As John the Baptist would say to them, they cannot Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance. As Jesus said, they are blind guides. But then, as it would be, and even now they seek their own gain. Preaching for filthy lucre sake. And being dead to sin, lacking the hope found of the Gentiles, they say, let us drink, nothing ever happens.

Isaiah continues preaching redemption in Christ, saying the righteous and the merciful men perish, being slain, but that the wicked don't consider that the humble and contrite actually are with God in Heaven. With Christ. They enter into peace. They are taken away from the evil which will come. But woe in the wicked. They have all gone aside, worshiping false idols, trusting in sorcery. Killing children as sacrifice. The wicked are as a troubled sea. Their lot is with the smooth stones of the river. With the mire.
