Peace, peace the Lord preaches to the contrite and humble, far and near. They will be all healed. But not the wicked. There is no peace for them.

Cry aloud, and spare not...one of the most quoted verses in scripture, used by pastors and preachers, lifting their voices like a trumpet to sound out the people's sins and transgressions. And those sins are many. Even among the church crowd. This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me, the Bible says. They seek God daily. Here, going before Him at the temple. Reading His ordinances and fasting. But we see it's in vain. They boast about these works, bragging about their fasts. Publicly proclaiming these fast days, that God has no part in giving. Matthew 6:16-18 Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face; That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly. But they fast for strife and debate, to lord over others. To place burdens on people grievous to be born. The Catholic Church and its harlot daughter, the Orthodox, spent much of the past weeks doing this. But that is not a fast God has chosen. To afflict themselves, publicly. To be seen of men and to guilt those who aren't as "holy." The fast the Lord has chosen is to comfort the afflicted, to loose the bands of wickedness, the burden of the law, especially the doctrine of men taught as commandments. To free men from every yoke, by faith in Him. To feed the hungry and to clothe the naked. To give comfort to the poor. Especially those of your own flesh. Your own family. Your nation. The same that Jesus asks of us. Matthew 25:35-40 For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. This is the affliction, this is the sacrifice God asks of us. Not doing without to be seen of men. To justify us before God as we continue in sin and pride. But sacrifice of our time and talents and wealth to help others in need. Without fanfare. And our light will so shine. Matthew 5:16 Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven...But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly. Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity. The Lord promises us redemption, restoration. The reestablishment of our nation. Blessings and hope for many generations after us. He seeks mercy and righteous judgment, not the blood of bulls and goats. Not fastings and vain words. If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Notice something here, that the word says the Sabbath is a "Him." The delight of the Holy One. Christ Jesus. Doing that which He did. Healing the sick. Tending to the broken hearted. The Lord of the Sabbath calling us to take the time, ceasing from our labors to help others. Not to be a burden, but to lift others from theirs. To rest in Jesus. And delight ourselves in the Lord. Amen

Fitting chapter, given my previous post. God telling Judah, and us today, that it isn't any failure or fault if His that we have trouble and tribulation. That He can still save. He can still hear cries for His help. The fault lies with us, when our iniquity has separated us from our God. When our sins have hidden His face from us. He chooses not to hear. This applies to our modern times, our nation and others that have fallen away from the truth, while paying lip service to the Lord. Shouting "Christ is King!" and doing little else to get right, to be saved. Everything that we do when we are separated from God rather than the world, leads to naught. It's as vain as expecting a spider's weaving to become a garment, rather than a snare. We grope for the wall like we are blind. Light has come into the world, but men preferred darkness because their deeds are wicked. Read the indictment against us in this chapter again. It is so fitting for modern America. And the Lord saw some turned from evil and they become prey. The righteous in Him are hated by the world. And so He gave us an intercessor, Jesus, and His salvation and righteousness sustains us. For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloak. This is the vestments of Jesus, and similarly we who are His are called to put on the armor He has provided us. Ephesians 6:11-17 Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand. Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace; Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. But notice vengeance is His clothing, and the promise of His vengeance upon those who love their iniquity more than the truth, will show the oppressors that our Redeemer has come. Amen

Revelation 21 And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea. 2 And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. 3 And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. 4 And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away. 5 And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. And he said unto me, Write: for these words are true and faithful. 6 And he said unto me, It is done. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely. 7 He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son. 8 But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death. 9 And there came unto me one of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues, and talked with me, saying, Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb's wife. 10 And he carried me away in the spirit to a great and high mountain, and shewed me that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, 11 Having the glory of God: and her light was like unto a stone most precious, even like a jasper stone, clear as crystal; 12 And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: 13 On the east three gates; on the north three gates; on the south three gates; and on the west three gates. 14 And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. 15 And he that talked with me had a golden reed to measure the city, and the gates thereof, and the wall thereof. 16 And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal. 17 And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel. 18 And the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass. 19 And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald; 20 The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolyte; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst. 21 And the twelve gates were twelve pearls: every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass. 22 And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it. 23 And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof. 24 And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it. 25 And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there. 26 And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. 27 And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb's book of life. The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory. Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended. What a beautiful promise, what a blessed hope. The eternal Kingdom of God, given to us. That we may walk continuously in His light, all mourning ended. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away. Amen. Even so, come Lord Jesus.

Luke 4:14-21 And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee: and there went out a fame of him through all the region round about. And he taught in their synagogues, being glorified of all. And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read. And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord. And he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened on him. And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears. The Lord Jesus read from Isaiah 61 in the synagogue in Galilee, the scriptures being fulfilled there before them. That the Christ the prophets gave witness to was there before them. And many asked, "isn't that the carpenter's son?" I have posted many times before that not only does this proclamation, written in Isaiah, and declared by Jesus, give witness to His ministry and His holy purpose and His wonderful salvation, but also serves as a mission statement for all Christians. In Him, we are filled with the Spirit. We are anointed Priests of the Lord. We are His Ministers, in Christ. We are to preach the gospel to the meek, to the poor. To give the good news to the brokenhearted. To preach deliverance to those captive in sin, under the bounds of the law. To bring the lost, who are blind to see, and set them at liberty. To preach the acceptable year of the Lord. John 12:47-48 And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day. Jesus reading Isaiah, leaves off before "the day of vengeance of our God." He was there, in His ministry to bring salvation. But in the last day, when He judges the world by His word, there shall come the day of vengeance. And in that day, all found to have received His word, who gave been judged and found righteous by His imputed righteousness, will be raised up. Glorified to all nations. Set as rulers over them. Like trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord. This is a promise of the resurrection. A covenant made with all believers. And for all our troubles and shame for His sake, we will be blessed with a double portion. Everlasting joy shall be upon us. I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels. We, like the seed that dies, and falls, and is sown, we will spring forth, to His glory and praise. Amen.

Isaiah 62 is a love letter from the Lord for the city of Jerusalem, the mountains of Zion, the land where God chooses to place His holy name. The valleys and the mountains made straight, and level for the King's Highway. The path of the King. Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzibah (the delight of), and thy land Beulah (the bride): for the Lord delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married. This again calls forward to the events described in Revelation 21, which I posted yesterday. The New Jerusalem that depends from Heaven, decked as a bride. People often talk about the wedding of the church to Christ. I know it's used as parable a couple times, but the actual feast is here and the bride that golden city, where Christ will reign forever. We've seen it again and again in the Chronicles and Kings, and from the prophets, that the only reason Judah wasn't destroyed like Sodom, like Israel, was the promise to David, that the Christ promised to Abraham would come from the King's lineage. And, every time, to keep Jerusalem as the place God chose to place His name. As the spot where Jesus would be offered. And where He would triumphantly reign. It was never the Jews. They were beneficiaries of God's plan. They were not His plan, themselves. And when the city was made desolate by the captivity, the exile to Babylon. And, in the Great Tribulation, when the abomination of desolation is made, when many would say that Jerusalem is "Forsaken," that it will not be. That Christ's redeemed will flock to Jerusalem, a crown of glory. A royal diadem. The symbol of His power. There have been arguments lately about what hill in Jerusalem is the correct spot for the Temple. Foolish debate, because it doesn't matter. Zion, Mt. Moriah, Jerusalem is the place, from Melchizedek, to Abraham bringing Issac to be sacrificed, to the crucifixion of Jesus, and His resurrection. What unbelieving Jews and Muslims do there doesn't matter. If a so-called 3rd temple is built, it won't be God's. If the Man of Perdition lays siege and slaughters the Jews in days of vengeance, and sits in the place of God declaring himself God, it won't matter. Because it is the Lord's and He will repay. It will be as a crown to Him. A holy bride. Amen.

Isaiah 63 begins a prayer of lament and repentance, appealing to the mercy of the vengeful Lord God, His vestments dyed in the blood of Edom and lands of the Jordan, coming for the days of vengeance against a wicked and gainsaying people. But also the year of the redeemed. For, with no man to rightly judge, He provided His own, and brought both salvation and fury. Verse 7, the prophet does as many men of God have done, and remind Him, and us, of His mercy and loving kindness. The greatness of all He has done for us. He is our Saviour. He carried Israel, and us, in the days of old, even as we rebelled and vexed the holy Spirit. And yes He turned against them, and us, as His enemy. Fit for destruction. But He also remembers the days of old, of leading Moses the shepherd, and his flock out of Egypt, across the dry ground holding back the sea. Through the wilderness, to the glory of His holy name. Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting. Praying for mercy. Reminding God of the promises made to us, the saved who are unknown to Abraham and rejected by the physical Israel. The Israel of God. And though we err and turn from His ways, they beg in prayer to return for our sakes. To save us. The remnant of Judah in captivity. Those of us now, scattered among Babylon, but united by Christ. The tribes of His inheritance. The prayer continues again in the following chapter.

1 Corinthians 2:9 But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. Isaiah 64 continues the lamentation for the destruction to come upon Judea, and the end times prophecy for the wrath of God upon the whole world. As the people in prayer, Isaiah gives voice to the godly repentance of the believer. Calling upon the Father to remember His sons during their tribulation and in the face of His wrath. We are as an unclean thing and all our righteousness are as filthy rags. There is none that doeth good. God's wrath is deserved. So the pleading of His people here, to spare us, is based on the promise of His mercy, not on our own works of righteousness. And the Lord will spare us the worst. And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened. So take heart. While the world is asking the rocks to fall on them to protect the ungodly from His fiery wrath, He will remember us who called upon His name. His people. And spare us His wrath.

Isaiah 65, the penultimate chapter, and here we see more promises for the people who were not a people, those called by a new name, for all of us waiting for redemption in every kindred and tongue. Christians. And the Jew becomes a curse and a byword and a parable. The holier than thou. God will repay against them and all who follow after them. The same for those that worship false gods, and idols, burning incense and working iniquity. Now for His servant's sake, there's a remnant saved. And out of Judah, a Savior. His servants will rejoice, while those that rejected Christ will be under the wrath, and the Lord God will slay them. A new heaven and new earth will come. An heavenly Jerusalem. There will be no more weeping or crying. The wolf and the lamb shall lie down together. And we will rejoice in His presence forever. Amen. Just to touch on a false doctrine that comes from people abusing this verse to say drinking alcohol is a blessing endorsed by God: Thus saith the Lord, As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy them all. First, this is a descriptive not proscriptive statement. There are times the Bible describes something, a parable, that's not explicitly stating that what it's describing is good. This is a parable about God not destroying all of Judah, because out of the line of David would come Christ. So He will not destroy them all in the Babylonian captivity. Second, 'one sayeth" indicates a hypothetical person may say, not that it is good or bad itself. Third, "new wine" is fresh squeezed juice. And that is a blessing. Jesus says we will drink it new with Him in His Kingdom. Hope that clarifies the matter. While I am on the subject of false doctrine coming from this chapter, those that claim this was changed; The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock.. That it "used to say the lamb lay down with the Lion! The Bible has been Mandela-effected!!" God's word is preserved by His power. It is an unchanging rock, settled in Heaven before the foundation of the world. So no, you're wrong. While it can be fun to have alternate theories of things of this world, when your schizo take leads to blasphemy, and profane babblings like this, take a step back and realize; sometimes you just are remembering an extra biblical account, or popular culture references. God's word doesn't change.

Zedekiah did that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done. Through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, till he had cast them out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. The Lord sends Babylon against Judah to punish them for their transgressions, and Zedekiah and the people harden their hearts and rebel against Nebuchadnezzar rather than repent towards God. And the Lord's wrath comes upon them, and they are besieged. For a year and a half Jerusalem are starved out by the Chaldean horde surrounding them. They die of famine and pestilence and war. Just as the unbelieving are slaughtered by the horsemen. The city is torn down, not one stone remaining upon another. They are made desolate. Empty. The king and his men flee to the wilderness and are captured. Zedekiah brought before the king for judgment. His seed is sniffed out before his eyes, and then he is blinded. Blind unto his death. Just as the Jews who rebelled against God were blinded, those who believed not on the Lord Jesus Christ. Blind and imprisoned until their death. Cut off. Then Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard carried away certain of the poor, the residue of the people. A remnant. The rest fell away, fell to the king of Babylon. The multitude. A falling away. But there was a remnant saved, and left behind to be vinedressers and husbandmen, tasked with bringing in the harvest. The increase of which belongs to the lord set over them. Just as Christians are, to bring forth fruit. After their kind. Servants of the Lord. The pillars of the temple were taken away. Broken down. Carried off to Babylon. Just as believers are the pillars of the temple of God, the body of Christ that is the church of believers. Just as we who are alive and remain will be broken by the antichrist when he makes war on the saints. Just as the abomination that maketh desolate will break the pillars, the saints. And the cauldrons and bowls and spoons and sniffers and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered. The holy vessels, used to minister, the same are saved Christians. Vessels of the Lord fitted for His purpose. Taken away. The refined silver. The brass. The pillars. This is the great tribulation and the martyrdom of the saints. And the 7 kings who set up Zedekiah, and his scribe, and the guards and all the ministers of the false king. A picture of the Beast and his prophet and the seven horns that give him his power...they are smote by the King set over them by God. But there are carried away a remnant who live. Who are brought out of great tribulation to serve the king. And the king of Babylon (at this time Evilmerodach), suffered not to leave Jehoiachin in prison, and lifted up Jehoiachin, to sit at his right hand. To be king of kings. Where he would eat bread every day of his life. Just as God the Father has lifted up His Son, the Lord Jesus. There are so many parallels here and I am not doing it justice. But I needed to write it out so I have a better outline of study. The details found here are repeated in Jeremiah 39, 2 Kings 25 and 2 Chronicles 36. God really wants us to see what happened to Zedekiah and the Jews at the hands of His servant Nebuchadnezzar. Taken in conjunction with Daniel, and especially Matthew 24, first and second Thessilonians, and Revelation, we see that when Jesus says all the prophets gave witness, we can understand better the way of the Lord. Also, study out the idea that we are the servants of God. The husbandmen and vinedressers. The pillars of the body of Christ. The temple of God. The holy vessels fitted to His purpose. These are important concepts that our the Christian life into perspective and will help you in your walk. I know it has helped me. Doing the will of the Father is our purpose. We were bought with a price, and it wasn't just so we could have self-improvement and "reach our potential." Or to hide away in fear. It was to be like Jeremiah, and boldly go into the city, before the kings and scribes, and the people, and preach the word of God. I hope this study through Jeremiah has helped all who read it. It helped me writing it out. It was a long trek and I am not quite done with the weeping prophet. We will go over Lamentations next, God willing. One of the most helpful things in understanding end times Bible prophecy that I can recommend is forgetting everything you've ever heard about the Jews and their role in it. And then let the Bible speak. Jews hold no role in in the end times aside from being utterly destroyed and cast into the lake of fire. They may help set up the antichrist and be betrayed so that the days of vengeance can occur. But other than that, they are meant to be a synagogue of Satan who will be made to see that God loved us who believe. God isn't waiting on them to build a third temple. The third temple is Christ and the body of believers. Anything they build will not be called the Temple of God. It'll be an abomination. God isn't waiting for them to return to doing sacrifices, and if they do, it too is an abomination. Blaspheming Jesus who is the only sacrifice.

I'm running late and I will come back to this but in the meantime here are a list of New Testament verses that directly quote or allude to Isaiah 66: Acts 7:49-50 Matthew 5:34-35 2 Thessalonians 1:7-8 Revelation 19:11-15 2 Peter 3:13 Revelation 21:1 Mark 9:42-48 A new Heaven and a new Earth, Jesus having the Earth as His footstool. Slaying with the sword that proceedeth out of His mouth. And fiery flame of judgment. And those who trust in Him entering into His rest. The final chapter of Isaiah, like the final book of the Bible, the Revelation of Jesus, perfectly encapsulates the hope that we have set before us. To Him did all prophets give witness. I'm looking back at my Isaiah 66 post and I don't see much else I could add. Except reading through the entire book of Isaiah, perhaps more so than any other Old Testament source other than maybe Psalms it's entirely about Jesus. It's one of the most relevant of the Old Testament books for Christians directly. Of course all of it is good and for our admonition. But chapter after chapter speaking of Christ, and God's judgment and mercy and the Lord's wrath upon a gainsaying people, and his deliverance for those who hold the faith, Isaiah holds a special place. There are plenty of videos out there that you can see where Christians in modern Israel read from Isaiah to Jews on the street, and ask them whether they think it's a Old Testament or New Testament passage. And of course they always get it wrong and claim that it's New Testament. Proving Jews really do not have any idea about anything from what they call "their Bible." And just as faith comes by the word of God, seeing all of those promises fulfilled over all of that length of time bolsters our faith. What a wonderful blessing the Lord is left us His word and not a church of men and traditions that are shifting sand.

Beginning in the book of the prophet Jeremiah, who lived in the southern Kingdom of Judah, roughly 600 years before Christ, and after the destruction of the northern Kingdom of Israel by the Assyrians. He was active during the time of King Josiah, who sought to return Judah to the right ways of the Lord, and had engaged in repairing the Temple, as well as tearing down the altars, groves and high places of Baal worship. (2 Kings 22-23) Jeremiah preached reformation and repentance towards the Lord as the King sought the same, seeking to make right what had been done by his grandfather Manasseh. During the renovation of the Temple Josiah was presented with a copy of the Law. And having it read, came to understand by faith what God wanted of His people. And while the efforts of Josiah and the prophets, including Jeremiah, kept the wrath of God at bay, ultimately it only delayed His punishment against this wicked people who had turned from Him. Babylon would invade and destroy them shortly after Josiah was killed in battle with Egypt at Megiddo, and his successors were exceedingly wicked. And so Jeremiah preached, unwillingly at first but with the word of God upon him, the prophet would witness the fall of the Temple and captivity of unfaithful Judah. God reveals to Jeremiah that He will use the armies from the North to come against Jerusalem, and tells Jeremiah that He will protect him as he preaches against the whoredoms of the Jews, who had turned to false gods. The Lord reminds Jeremiah of the history of the people, taken from out of Egypt to be a holy nation. That Israel went after God in the wilderness, and how He brought them to the promised land, and the bounty and blessings He bestowed on them. And yet they made His heritage an abomination. The people, the kings and priests did not seek the Lord, forsaking Him that is the fountain of living waters, to turn to empty manmade cisterns of dead idols. Passing their children through the fire to Baal. They turned from faith in the Lord, the Christ to come. The fountain of living waters as Jesus describes Himself. This is the faith that saves, in all ages. Calling upon the name of the Lord. The word of God upon Jeremiah, He says; Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me? The vineyard imagery, describing Israel as the vine God planted, is used throughout the NT to describe the final rejection of the Jews, who had become a strange vine, not producing fruit, cut off and burned as another people were grafted in. The destruction of his nation for their unfaithfulness to the Lord that Jeremiah witnessed is very relevant to any nation that calls itself by His name. We are witness to a similar time, with the same punishment due for our wickedness and deliverance available, by turning back to Christ. Because of the large number of smaller chapters in Jeremiah, I will likely be posting 2 or 3 chapters a day, and God willing, get to Jeremiah's book of Lamentations in short order. Much of it is very straightforward, and while I will keep the commentary light, I will still talk about things that stand out to me in this read through. Of all the prophets, Jeremiah has that 'literally me' feel, as he lived during a time we can relate to today. How he handles this gives us hope, not of earthly things but the better country we share an inheritance in with Christ.

Jeremiah preaching the word of God, to the Northern Kingdom of Israel, already decimated and scattered by the Assyrians, and her sister, the Southern Kingdom of Judah. And in it, the Lord says that these are sisters who have played the whore. That God had married them and kept them as a wife, but that they both have chased after other gods, committed adultery and polluted the land, and that Israel, the 10 tribes thereof, had already been divorced from Him. The Lord laments that Judah, even after seeing her backslidden sister be destroyed and put away by God, hadn't had genuine revival, turning back to Him. In the time of Josiah there was some effort at restoring the Temple and destroying the groves and idols, and returning to the right ways of the Lord. God says this is feigned. They had not turned with their whole heart. But for all this, the Lord promises that if the remnant of Israel or Judah, having been chastened to repentance, turns again to Him, He would heal them. And the form and nature of this healing is in Christ Jesus. How shall I put thee among the children, and give thee a pleasant land, a goodly heritage of the hosts of nations? and I said, Thou shalt call me, My father; and shalt not turn away from me. God tells them through the prophet that He will give them the land, that all nations shall be gathered to it, unto the name of the Lord. To His seat of power for the Kingdom, in Jerusalem. That once they've been gathered in His name, they shall not walk after the imagination of their evil heart. They won't turn to manmade cisterns, empty of water, but the the fountain of living waters that flow from Christ. That pastors of God's choosing shall instruct them. They shall take part in the goodly heritage of the host of nations. They shall call Him Father. And they shall not turn away from Him. The Lord says to the backslidden nations, turn back to Him and He will heal them. This powerful promise is fulfilled in Christ.

Chapter 4, and the Spirit of the Lord is upon Jeremiah, preaching to the people of Judah, the children of Israel, and warning them of destruction coming from the North, the lion of Babylon. God giving the prophet visions of an invasion, all the whole the supposed prophets of the Lord are preaching "peace, peace." (As we will see in a later chapter, they are falsely telling Judah that they are fine and God loves them, but they aren't speaking for God). The Lord tells the people to repent towards Him and He will stay His judgment. To the circumcision of the heart. Not of the flesh, the outward sign of being of the seed of Abraham, but the circumcision made without hands, of faith in the Lord. Romans 2:25-29 For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision. Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision? And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law? For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God. Colossians 2:11 In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ: Even as God is warning of utter destruction and the desolation of her cities, being spoiled by these invading armies, carried away into captivity, justified in His wrath, God offers His grace that if they but turn back to Him, He will repent. O Jerusalem, wash thine heart from wickedness, that thou mayest be saved. How long shall thy vain thoughts lodge within thee? We can hear in this the frustration and pleading of the Lord, longsuffering and merciful, at the end of His patience. Sorrowful and lamenting what He will do because they are a stiff-necked and gainsaying people. The same frustration Jesus felt, preaching to the Jews, 600yrs later. Matthew 23:37 O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! God says the punishment coming is due to their own wickedness, their bitter heart. Wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge. Their destruction is their own doing, and God laments this, as a husband would putting away his wife that he loves for her adultery. Jeremiah sees visions of desolation, cities sacked and spoiled. The sky black from smoke. The fields, destroyed. Even the birds fleeing, for there are no men left. And the Lord, who is a jealous God, asks what will Israel do when its destruction has come? He compares the nation to an old harlot. Decked in crimson, face caked with makeup, appealing to her lovers that she fornicated with, the other nations and their gods, and He says without Him. Without their land and riches. These lovers will turn and seek their lives. Without God they are vanity. The judgment of nations is by their works, and more, the fruit of those among them that call themselves by His name. 2 Chronicles 7:14 If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. This promise is extended to every nation, that has Christians living in it. And every nation on earth has saved Christians among them. Or those apostates calling themselves by His name, yet chasing idols and drunk on the fornications of their mother church. As we watch the inevitable destruction of our nation coming, as Jeremiah did in visions from the Lord, we can relate to him, and how he felt. Yet take comfort in the fact that even in his Lamentations, he held fast to the hope of the promise of the Lord. Jeremiah 4, a clear prophecy of the destruction of Jerusalem coming from Babylon, has the distinction of being the "proof text" for the first of many heresies found in the wicked Scofield study Bible. Written at the turn of the 20th century, but with roots back to Darby, Scofield took scripture and turned it on its head to embrace Zionism, dispensationalism, teach the wicked doctrines of the "failure of Christ church," and the Kingdom being given to the Jews. He also sought to take the then-current trends in popular science, falsely so-called, that had been developed by antichrists to shake faith in God and His creation, and square them with the Bible so that Christians would accept things like Darwinism and dinosaurs. Scofield first published in 1909, and just a decade later was the infamous Scopes Monkey trial, that saw Modernists clashing with Fundamentalists over evolution, among many other things. Scofield used his notes, interrupting the text of Scripture itself, column notes and foot notes, to add commentary and invent doctrine out of thin air. Even today, a century later, this toxic corruption has infiltrated a majority of evangelical and many Baptist churches. Just as Judaizers had already taken root in Protestant sects and their seminaries, Scofield was the foot in the door to Bible colleges and KJVO churches. But the heresies of C. I. Scofield were evident in the first chapter of the first book in the opening verses of the Bible. In Genesis 1, he interrupts God's creation, to invent the idea that between verse 1; In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And verse 2 And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters. That there was a span of an earlier creation, that millions or billions of years passed. That there was a "gap," between the initial creation, and the ultimate creation, and that this was proved by the vision of Jeremiah in chapter 4:23-26. He claims that this passage "clearly indicates" that the earth had undergone a "cataclysmic change as a result of divine judgement." That we could see evidence of this pre-Eden, pre-Adamic destruction. That Jeremiah was seeing a vision of this past event. That this would match the geologists of the era, and their theories of the earth being billions of years old. That the earth wasn't made fully formed and stocked with life, but that God had made it before as habitations for angels, who fell, and was destroyed and left void and without form until he renewed creation for Eden. The Gap theory was very popular for a time in American Evangelical circles, but is almost universally rejected today by believing Christians, despite their continued use of the Scofield, and acceptance of other heresy he taught. But if he is inventing things in the first verse of the first chapter. Why do they trust anything else he wrote?

For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace....Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them. Jeremiah, in the Spirit, is preaching hard against Judah, which has become totally corrupt, and faces judgment from the North, by the invading armies of Babylon which God is warning He will allow to conquer and spoil them. And the prophets and priests are telling the people "Peace. Peace" when there is no peace. They speak soothing words, withholding judgement, leaving the people with a false sense of security. That everything is fine. That their sacrifices and their expensive, imported incense, the performative religious acts they do, will offset the Idolatry, fornication and wickedness. Jeremiah preaches that this is not acceptable to the Lord and they will be spoiled and left desolate. Reprobate, rejected by God. A millennium after God takes the children out of Israel, clearing the land of the nations that committed abominations, driving then out before them, and here they sit facing the same judgment. The northern kingdom of 10 tribes, wiped out and dispersed by the Assyrians, and Judah about to be overrun by Babylonians. And despite the warnings of the prophet, none of them repent of their ways. They break the covenant and despite God's longsuffering, His wrath is upon them. How can we not help but see the parallels and understand we face the same judgment? God judges nations by their works, and especially by those who call themselves by His name. If those claiming Him, who say they are Israel, fall away, He is going to cut them off. It is a real 🎯 you are here-moment.

The preaching of the word of God continues, Jeremiah prophesying in the Spirit that God is casting His judgment upon a wicked and perverse generation of Judah. As He frequently does, the Lord, being long-suffering and full of mercy and grace, extends His hand first. Saying; Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place. Because the judgment of nations is done on this earth. And the wickedness of those who are His people will be met with the rod of correction and reproof. We serve the living God and as His sons, the spiritual seed of Abraham, we too face this judgment for our inequity and the inequity of the people. But, because of His love, grace is always available to those sons who repent. The prodigal who returns home. The nation where the people who call themselves by His name turn back towards Him, God promises to heal. God instructs Jeremiah to preach at the door of the temple, to those in Judah entering in for sacrifice and burnt offerings, but who outside the temple blaspheme God. Serving other gods. Committing wickedness; they steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not, and yet out of habit and vain faith they return to His temple to do the performative religious acts, that do not save them. Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, saith the Lord. This is the scripture Jesus preaches during His scourging of the moneychangers in the Temple; Matthew 21:13 And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves. It's the same spirit that gripped the Pharisees, rote practices of ordinances but nothing given to the weightier matters of the law; Matthew 23:23 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone God says He has spoken to them, warning them, calling out to repent and they didn't hear. They answered not. When God says this, He obviously means it literally, that through the prophets He has instructed His people and warned them, but more; He had recently allowed the entire Northern Kingdom, and the 10 tribes therein, to be destroyed and scattered by the Assyrians, for just such behavior. The whole seed of Ephraim, being the most prominent tribe of Israel, represents those northern 10 tribes. He reminds them "I have cast out all of thy brethren." God gives His people chances. Repeatedly. He gives unsaved people multiple chances as well. The Spirit moving to rebuke the world that they may come to believe. But eventually, be it judgment upon a nation that is destroyed, judgment against a backslidden believer where they are rebuked and eventually called home if they don't respond, or to the unbelievers who don't wish to retain God in their knowledge, and are made reprobate. God gives us multiple chances and warnings to repent towards Him and His mercies. God says to Jeremiah, don't even bother praying for intercession. He is done with these people. This is on them, their last chance. It is a change of heart He seeks, repentance towards belief on Him. Not acts of religion, not vain works. But trusting in Him, and in love, doing right to others. Not oppressing the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow. Not shedding innocent blood. Nor walking after other gods. God says; For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in that day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: but this thing I commanded them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you. This is the Gospel of the Lord. Obey His voice. Believe His word, and He will be our God and we His people. And then to walk in His ways, obey His commandments, that it may be well with us. They are for our benefit. Salvation by faith, adoption to be His sons, sanctification to our benefit, that we may be holy because He is holy. This is the only dispensation that there ever has been. The dispensation of grace offered by God through faith, unto adoption, and by love unto obedience of His commandments. In this, God also wants those Jews who were going into the temple, to pay lip service to the ordinances and sacrifices, while not having the heart of a believer, that these acts cannot save them. No flesh is saved by works of the law. They were given as a means to understand the promised Christ. They were given after the promise that if they believed on the Lord, He'd be their God and they'd be His people. Just as Abraham was saved by faith before circumcision. The blood of bulls and goats didn't save them. And to remind them, God says he will destroy the temple that they are counting on to save them. Just as He previously destroyed Shiloh, the sight of the Tabernacle in the North, over run by Philistines and Assyrians, and laying in ruin during the days of Jeremiah. The sacraments and the temple were a gift to those already justified by faith. Not the cause or means of that faith. Faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God. OT and NT. And as we know, God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets...the word of God came upon those He sent. And the people did not harken unto them. None believe the report. And so, the judgment of God is just, being provoked to wrath by a stiff-necked and gainsaying people. Since the day that your fathers came forth out of the land of Egypt unto this day I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early and sending them: Yet they hearkened not unto me, nor inclined their ear, but hardened their neck: they did worse than their fathers. And so, God says the time is coming where the Temple itself and all the high places and altars to false gods they had set up, will be destroyed. Babylon is coming. Let's not overlook the obvious; that God not only rebukes those who seek to be justified by their sacraments and ceremony, of vain works that betray their adulterous hearts, but also gives specific example of the Idolatry these supposed children of God have added to their worship. The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto other gods, that they may provoke me to anger. Do they provoke me to anger? saith the Lord: do they not provoke themselves to the confusion of their own faces? The preaching in chapter 7 destroys the idea of sacraments over faith, works over belief, and the serving of idols, specifically the worship of "the queen of heaven." Of course the Catholic perversion of the Bible, the Douay–Rheims, has to include a note about this mention of the false god the people baked cakes to, holding feasts for. Because otherwise, someone might question this if they read it.

1 Thessalonians 5:1-3 But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape. Jeremiah continues his fire breathing preaching against the people of Judah. And in chapter 8, God's judgment again singles out the false prophets and in this passage, the scribes, for being worthless to the people. The prophets claiming there is peace in the land and with God. That the abominations the people have committed aren't coming to a head. That the wrath of God wasn't coming. The scribes, transcribing copies of the law, by the letter and not the spirit, that the people should repent towards God. God uses the timing of things found in nature, the crane and the storm in their daily migration at dawn and dusk. As the harvest comes in fall when the summer is over. These signs are ours to see as well. And we who are sober and watchful are given these signs that we may know tribulation is coming for a people. Matthew 24:32-33 Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors. The times and seasons are observable to us, but to the backslidden and to the unregenerate, the day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night. But we know the signs, as Christ told us; Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many. And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places.All these are the beginning of sorrows. The judgment of nations or the final day of the Lord, the signs and the seasons are known to us, if we remain vigilant and blamelessly walking in the Spirit, ready to be delivered. Psalms 69:21 They gave me also gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. Matthew 27:34 They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof, he would not drink. 2 Corinthians 5:21 For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. Jeremiah 8 I will surely consume them, saith the Lord: there shall be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf shall fade; and the things that I have given them shall pass away from them. Why do we sit still? assemble yourselves, and let us enter into the defenced cities, and let us be silent there: for the Lord our God hath put us to silence, and given us water of gall to drink, because we have sinned against the Lord. The bitter gall, given to drink of those who sinned against the Lord, given to Christ Jesus as the psalmist's prophesying, said. That when He became sin for us, they fed Him gall mixed with water, that we be saved from this bitter pill.

Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men. Jeremiah 9 continues his prophesying, the hard preaching of the words of God against the children of Israel that remain in Judea. And in it, the lamentation to seek to flee from Jerusalem and the wickedness of this generation, and go to the wilderness, to live off grid, and be away from the evil people, uncircumcised in the heart. But God calls upon Jeremiah to preach in the city, by the gates of the Temple. To tell them of the pending destruction their forsaking Him has brought up on them. This same impulse is given to Christians today. To flee the world, to get to a redoubt in the wilderness. To be far from the fallen society that, like just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked. But, like the prophets, and like Christ Himself, we go to Jerusalem. We are called to go to the population centers and preach the acceptable year of the Lord. To seek that which is lost. To be a light in that darkness. We can't be a light to others if we are hidden in the woods. And so we are in the world, not of it. Rather than coveting a RETVRN to a past we never knew, or a rustic compound in the hills, we are supposed to bloom where the good Lord has planted us. To be a blessing to those around us. To be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ. Not to flee persecution, and the tribulations that come to every believer, living for the Lord. To glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us. James 1:12 Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him. Romans 8:18 For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. James 1:2-4 My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing. We who believe on Christ have already overcome this fallen world. Because He has overcome death and Hell for us. We shouldn't be black pilled. We may wail with lamentations for our people to repent, but standfast in the faith that has saved us. John 16:33 These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

We are there in Jeremiah chapter 10, and the Lord, speaking through the prophet by the Spirit is casting judgments upon Judah, the remaining children of Israel, this time focusing on their adopting the heathen practices of idol worshiping of graven images. Wood carvings plated with molten metals, hammered into place and carried about for feasts and religious practices. He begins by warning them not to be caught up in the signs of the sky. Astrology and the movement of the lights in the firmament, given as we read in Genesis as a way to mark time, but being used by those who worship idols and small gods that are of their own wicked imagination. To scare people into thinking catastrophe was nigh. Babylonians especially had very advanced system of astrological prophesying, and God says this is vanity. Just as the workman and the founder, cutting down trees to make idols to Baal or the Queen of Heaven are vain. It is important to see things as God sees them. And as He is the creator of all things, His view of the superstitious nonsense men invents to explain His creation, including to worship the things He created, is both insulting to a jealous God, and laughably foolish. Romans 1:21-25 Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. We worship the living God, through Whom all things were made. The heathen in their fear worship the sun, the moon, the stars. Idols made of wood and stone and molten metals. Psalm 115:5-8 They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not: They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not: They have hands, but they handle not: feet have they, but they walk not: neither speak they through their throat. They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them. Acts 17:22-31 Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, To The Unknown God. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Neither is worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation; That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring. Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man's device. And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead. The Lord is consistently pointing out the vanity, the utter uselessness of these false gods. How foolish it is to bow and serve dead things as gods, that cannot save anyone. They are an invention of man's own vain imagination. And yet the children of Judah, even those going to Temple and continuing the Levitical ceremonial ordinances and laws, had allowed this idolatry in to their cities. They baked cakes to the "queen of heaven." They participated in feasts to these false gods. They were made to fear the heavens God created, rather than the God who created them. But they are altogether brutish and foolish: the stock is a doctrine of vanities. And for this cause God is bringing destruction upon Judah, and the graven images and idols decked with golden plates will be destroyed, along with the carvers and founders who made them; But the Lord is the true God, he is the living God, and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his indignation. Thus shall ye say unto them, The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens. ... Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them. They are vanity, and the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish. The next verse is a prophetic statement of the coming Christ; that despite the people being cast out of the land, and the cities spoiled, there is a portion of Jacob to come; The portion of Jacob is not like them: for he is the former of all things; and Israel is the rod of his inheritance: The Lord of hosts is his name. God's wrath is cleansing. Making strait the path that leads to His righteousness. God, in His wrath against them, is grieved. It pains Him to bring destruction to His people. My tabernacle is spoiled, and all my cords are broken: my children are gone forth of me, and they are not: there is none to stretch forth my tent any more, and to set up my curtains. The Tabernacle in the wilderness, a figure of the saved believer, prepared for the indwelling of God. The physical sign of a believing Israel, long destroyed in Shiloh. There are none that believe. The pastors don't guide the flock to the Lord. God will then scatter the sheep. Jeremiah begs that the destruction come to the heathen instead. To those that had brought their vain traditions the children of Israel are caught up in, for they have eaten up Jacob, and devoured him, and consumed him, and have made his habitation desolate. Colossians 2:16-23 Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. There are many false teachers, Reddit theologians and sincere but misled believers, who have taken Jeremiah 10 out of context, to make the claim that this chapter isn't about graven images, carved, fashioned and decked with plated gold and silver, idols that are being worshipped and feared as if they have power, and saying that it is explicitly about the tradition of the Christmas tree. That it is, preaching against decorating your house with a plant while celebrating the birth of Christ Jesus. That the practice of having house plants and decorative trees is itself paganism. But what does God instruct? Isaiah 60:13 The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious. The Bible doesn't teach against use of plants as decoration. It shows us God uses evergreen trees to beautify His temple. No one bows and serves a decorative house plant, they beautify their homes with them. No one worships a pine tree except pagan "druid" LARPers. Even the most secular reprobate consumerist, who strips Christ from Christmas and makes it entirely about snowmen and reindeer and coveting things, doesn't look at the plastic tree covered in lights and tinsel in the corner of their living room and thinks, "I shall worship this." There are plenty of reasons to not want to participate in traditional Christmas trappings, especially as they have become in the modern, consumerist world of greed. The lie of Santa, the works-based system that you have to be good, "repent of your sins or you don't get a present!" The profane and the blasphemous way our Jewish-subverted culture has secularized it all. But most believing Christians see the season as simply a feast celebrating the miracle of the birth of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. And regardless of your conviction, Romans 14 should apply; 1 Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations. 2 For one believeth that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eateth herbs. 3 Let not him that eateth despise him that eateth not; and let not him which eateth not judge him that eateth: for God hath received him. 4 Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand. 5 One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind. 6 He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord; and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard it. No one should judge against someone who doesn't want to celebrate even the most faithful of Christmas celebrations, and no one should judge those who do. And they certainly shouldn't abuse and twist Jeremiah 10 to justify their doctrines of men to level railing accusations against people who just think it's a nice thing to do, while keeping Christ as the center of their lives. Jeremiah 10 is talking about worshiping graven images as the heathen do. The Queen of Heaven, specifically. It is not talking about a decoration in your house.

Chapter 11, picking up after the prophet Jeremiah has prayed for his people and that God's wrath fall on the heathen who had led the Israelites to other gods, bowing to and serving idols, instead. Here, the word of the Lord tells him no, not to pray for Judah. That their abominations had sealed God's judgment. That they did not believe the word of God, keep the covenant made with their fathers, and instead believed on other gods, setting up altars and burning incense to them. I will note that the Lord says that on every street in Jerusalem, there are altars set to offer incense to other gods, which, in cities under the sway of Roman Catholicism, we see the same. Parish churches dedicated to this house god, or that, in the name of supposed "saints," but which are all altars of Baal. John 15:1-8 I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you. Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. Romans 11:17-25 And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.
