But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. God's command to honor our parents by caring for them was given a "loophole" by the Pharisees, that a man could claim poverty and not support them in their need by declaring his wealth to be "Corban," or that is a gift intended to the temple or priesthood, even as he retained the possession for his own use. This is a famous passage of the Gospel, also found in Mark 7:6-13, where Jesus berates the hypocrisy of the Pharisses, and points out how they themselves subvert God's law in favor of their own. Teaching for commandments the doctrine of men. But we see in this exchange how seriously the Lord takes this obligation. That dishonorable children should die the death. That their blood is upon themselves. They are cursed. This is tied in to the idea that we are to honor the widows and provide judgment for the fatherless. Those who have no family to care for them or parents to honor and obey. James 1:27 Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world. These obligations led to instructions to the church on how it must be done. 1 Timothy 5:3-8 Honour widows that are widows indeed. But if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God. Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day. But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth. And these things give in charge, that they may be blameless. But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. There is more regarding this, but we can see that God has thought through all the various situations, and that the spirit of the law is in how we care for those whom we honor, and that our parents are there to be obeyed, just as all the God-given hierarchies on Earth. John 3:16-18 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God. Acts 16:30-31 And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. This is the Gospel of faith, taught throughout the Bible. But it is derisively called "easy-believism" by those seeking to bring another gospel of works and self-righteousness. If believing the Gospel for salvation were "easy," then why do so many people struggle with trusting in Christ Jesus alone for their salvation? Why does every false religion reject this simple faith for works and penance? Matthew 7:13-14 Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it. Believing on Christ alone for salvation is the narrow way. The strait gate. And there really are few who find it. Pride and vanity and inability to trust the word of God keeps people from letting go and trusting by faith. They want reassurance that it "worked" before they can let go. They are carrying so much of a burden, and yoked by the law, that they cannot fit through that strait gate. Like a camel trying to pass through the eye of a needle. And so they seek a wider path to their own destruction. Or they want to force their way through by exhibiting signs of deserving it through their own acts of righteousness, which the Bible calls filthy rags. Greasing the entrance by their own good intentions, so that they can accept that they "deserve" to enter. Not realizing none deserve it, but we are given entrance through Christ. They want to know without trust, so that they may believe, and so they never can come to the knowledge of the truth. Because faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. And without visible evidence, they doubt, and are given false hope from the "Repent-of-your-sins" types who claim that they may know they are saved if they do certain acts, and behave a certain way. But that false hope gives way when any weight is put upon it, because their standards are impossible to achieve in the flesh. It is impossible to pass through that gate carrying our own works, which are wood, hay and stubble, fit to be burned. We don't begin to be sanctified until we are in the kingdom already. Until we have passed through that gate. Without faith, it is impossible to please God. So don't be fooled. Salvation is easy, from a works standpoint because it doesn't require any effort from us to believe that Jesus paid it all. But it is hard from a human standpoint, letting go of all the burdens that keep us from passing through.

Matthew 24:35 Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away. In Jeremiah 36, the word of the Lord comes upon the prophet telling him to write the words of prophecy God had given him in a scroll, and to have the word of God read in the temple and to the people of Jerusalem. With the aid of a scribe named Baruch, he does just that. And when Baruch reads it in the temple, during a declared feast to the Lord, saying Babylon would certainly destroy Judah and leave the land desolate, it pricked the ears of certain princes of the kingdom, who knowing the danger to the prophet and scribe, told them to go into hiding while they conveyed the word to the king. And when the king heard it, he cut up the scroll and cast it into the fire and indeed sought their lives, but God hid them. And God said to write the words again in another scroll, the scripture not being hid, impossible to destroy. Because the word of God is spirit and life, not the paper it is confined to, but the truth that is from everlasting to everlasting. Just as in the centuries since Pentecost, as New Testament Christians and their churches, led of the Spirit, wrote down the word of God, and just as the apostate false church sought to destroy those scrolls and manuscripts, and to kill the servants of God who held them. Often burning the man and the parchment together. But God's word endures. And the word endures because there are always wicked men, like Jehoiakim, and vile deeds to be preached against. And the truth of God is eternal. Psalm 12:6-8 The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. Thou shalt keep them, O Lord, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever. The wicked walk on every side, when the vilest men are exalted. It is also worth pointing out that when the words of the book are read, it is during a fast to the Lord. The people were called to the temple for the fast, and yet this is a prophecy of judgment against them. God took no account for this act of piousness. Their sin of Judah was too great in His eyes. The judgement had been made, Babylon would have her for her adultery, that the children of Israel would turn to God from their whoredoms. There are times when people, who knowing the judgment of God against them, do religious acts of outward piousness. They fast, make long prayer. Act holier than thou. As Jesus says in Matthew 6; Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. We see how the hypocrites have that outward appearance to be seen of men. Like Jesus says, they are whited sepulchers, beautiful on the outside, but inside, stinking of death. Luke 18:10-14 Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican. The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess. And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted. The people who heard the word of God through Jeremiah believed in vain that their performative acts of penance and fasting would offset the sin in their hearts, their trust in idols, their adoption of the customs of the heathen. Their sin and degeneracy. They needed to repent, to think again, to know God's judgment is real and there is only one way, God's way. And all the beating of their chest and sackcloth and ashes, fasting and outward signs of religion couldn't save them. And this ties into the renewed theme of the week; repentance. The thing most people "repent of" isn't their sins. Most people know sin is bad and hate it and don't like themselves for it. These Jews in Jerusalem for the fast knew in their hearts they were in sin, just as people do today. They have a conscience and the Spirit convicting them, least they be reprobate. What people most often repent of are the false beliefs they have about God. About His judgment. About their own righteousness or how they can escape punishment for their sins. "Oh I thought idols would save me." "I thought the law would save me." "I thought maybe hell wasn't real." "I didn't know my works weren't enough." It's literally what they are being called to repentance from in NT scripture. The Jews thinking by their being Abraham's seed they were going to inherit the kingdom no matter what. That they could achieve their own righteousness by works of the law and keeping the traditions of men. That the Kingdom of Heaven was theirs on this earth. That the Messiah would be political. A man of war. That circumcision availed them. The Greeks believed their dead idols and false gods, that they superstitiously bowed to and served, would save them. That God wasn't real. They worshipped the created more than the Creator who is blessed forever, amen. Jews and Greeks alike didn't believe Jesus was the Christ. They sought a sign, and wisdom. But the power to be saved was in the word of God. The Gospel preached and believed. Repentance from dead works and vain traditions and towards God. Reconsidering the way to the Kingdom of Heaven, and believing. Just as in Jeremiah's day. Just as it is today.

Proverbs 1 20 Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets: 21 She crieth in the chief place of concourse, in the openings of the gates: in the city she uttereth her words, saying, 22 How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge? 23 Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you. 24 Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded; 25 But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: 26 I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh; 27 When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. 28 Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: 29 For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord Matthew 23 32 Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers. 33 Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell? 34 Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city: 35 That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar. 36 Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation. 37 O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! 38 Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. In Jeremiah 37, we see the king and his princes, those in power besieged by Babylon. They had not harkened to the Lord and did not listen to the wisdom of the word of God, preached by the prophet Jeremiah. But in their calamity they sought him to pray for their salvation from the Chaldean horde. In a like manner, many men will wait until the foxhole is being shelled to ask God for deliverance. To protect their lives. Even as they reject His word, and salvation of their souls. They shout out "Oh my God!" with no faith. They want to eat their cake and have it too. But God again and again tells us that He calls early, and often. That wisdom is crying out her voice in the streets. That, as a mother hen, the Lord seeks to gather us as she would chicks under her wing, but they would not listen. And they slew the prophets and did what they wanted, and so when destruction is due, God laughs at their calamity. Salvation, be it the individual soul liberty of those justified in Christ, or the physical salvation of a nation, is not extended indefinitely. God is longsuffering. He is mercy and His grace abounds. But He is clear. There comes a time for both people and nations, where His patience runs out and He scourges with a rod of iron. His wrath is kindled. Too late, reprobate. This has application in the saved Christian's life as well. He wants to form us into vessels fit for His use, that we may bring forth fruit after our kind. But if we resist Him and live for ourselves not heeding His word, separating ourselves to the Gospel, becoming backslidden, being reproached again and again and ignoring it, God will eventually destroy you. Punishment will be more severe for us than the wicked who prosper. Or taking us home earlier than maybe we would have been. At some point it is too late, even for the saved. And so when the armies of Egypt offer the Judeans a false hope, and scare off the Babylonians, the rulers turn on Jeremiah and shut him up in prison at Jonathan the scribes house. Rather than considering the years he spent preaching the word of God, telling them Babylon was going to come against them while their own false prophets preached "peace and safety," they seek to blame him for his prophesying that Babylon would return. They had turned to him for prayer in their hour of need, but when they had a false hope, they turned against him again. Most of us have witnessed this. People in our lives who are only receptive to the word so long as they face tribulation, and then the moment they see relief, discarding everything preached to them. But the king was fearful, and sought the word of the Lord, only to again return the prophet to prison when he preached destruction, howbeit with some added comfort, for fear of the Lord. I should note, the cycle of turning to the Lord in tribulation, only to gain the prosperity of fools, the good times and blessings that may come in relief, but then in that prosperity, turning back to sin and not listening to the word of God, is something that afflicts many Christians. It has me. I have had periods of my life where, walking in the spirit during rough times, and being delivered and given blessings and grace, get comfortable and forget what brought me low to begin with. Sliding back to old ways that had brought me troubles to begin with. To forget the Lord and His deliverance. This is why it is vitally important for a Christian to not wait until there's trouble in their life to take their walk seriously. To turn to the Lord in praise and thanksgiving when times are good. To humble yourself and understand that all blessings and tribulation are of God and work for good to those who love Him. To seek His wisdom early. To be constant in prayer and in His word. To do all things in Him. That His will be done. Life's ups and downs become less volatile and the waters calm. And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. Then he arose, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm. And he said unto them, Where is your faith?

John 7:13 Howbeit no man spake openly of him for fear of the Jews. John 9:22 These words spake his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue. John 19:38 And after this Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus. John 20:19 Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you The fear of the Jews. The Jews who sought to kill Jeremiah. The Jews who carry the blood of all the prophets from Abel to Zachariah. A to Z. Who'd slain the Lord Jesus and who are contrary to all men. Jeremiah, who had preached destruction by the Babylonians, prophesying what had now come to pass, now was relaying the word of the Lord from prison, during the siege of Jerusalem, to surrender and live. In their fear and pride, the princes of the city, the high ranking politicians and clergy, sought Jeremiah's life for demoralizing the people, surrounded and without much food already. They took the prophet and threw him in a pit full of mire, where he sank into the muck, left to starve and die. But a believer, an Ethiopian eunuch serving in Zedekiah's court, interestingly enough, brought the matter to the king's attention. And so the king, who we have seen, was a double-minded man, who feared the Lord but also feared his men and the judgment of the people, sent to retrieve Jeremiah. 30 men working with makeshift straps of fabric, were needed to pull him from the mire. And the king comes to him for private council. He promised the prophet he can speak freely. That he won't have him put to death. But, he pleads, tell him the word of the Lord. Then said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah, Thus saith the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel; If thou wilt assuredly go forth unto the king of Babylon's princes, then thy soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire; and thou shalt live, and thine house: But if thou wilt not go forth to the king of Babylon's princes, then shall this city be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and thou shalt not escape out of their hand. Surrender and live. Fight and die. And in his fear of the Jews, and in his his pride, the king refuses. He fears the captured Jews will mock him for obeying the word of God. Jeremiah again tells him he has a simple choice. Obey and trust in the word of the Lord or all that he fears will come true. The princes of Babylon will have him in derision. The women will even mock him, as if Zedekiah were trapped in mire as Jeremiah had been. But fearful and double-minded, the king returns Jeremiah to his original prison in the court of Johnathan, and swears him to secrecy. And there the prophet remained until Babylon had taken the city.

2 Kings 25 And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he, and all his host, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it; and they built forts against it round about. 2 And the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah. 3 And on the ninth day of the fourth month the famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land. 4 And the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls, which is by the king's garden: (now the Chaldees were against the city round about:) and the king went the way toward the plain. 5 And the army of the Chaldees pursued after the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho: and all his army were scattered from him. 6 So they took the king, and brought him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him. 7 And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon. 8 And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, unto Jerusalem: 9 And he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man's house burnt he with fire. 10 And all the army of the Chaldees, that were with the captain of the guard, brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about. 11 Now the rest of the people that were left in the city, and the fugitives that fell away to the king of Babylon, with the remnant of the multitude, did Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carry away. 12 But the captain of the guard left of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen. 13 And the pillars of brass that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the brasen sea that was in the house of the Lord, did the Chaldees break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon. 14 And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away. 15 And the firepans, and the bowls, and such things as were of gold, in gold, and of silver, in silver, the captain of the guard took away. 16 The two pillars, one sea, and the bases which Solomon had made for the house of the Lord; the brass of all these vessels was without weight. 17 The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and the chapiter upon it was brass: and the height of the chapiter three cubits; and the wreathen work, and pomegranates upon the chapiter round about, all of brass: and like unto these had the second pillar with wreathen work. 18 And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door: 19 And out of the city he took an officer that was set over the men of war, and five men of them that were in the king's presence, which were found in the city, and the principal scribe of the host, which mustered the people of the land, and threescore men of the people of the land that were found in the city: 20 And Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took these, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah: 21 And the king of Babylon smote them, and slew them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away out of their land. 22 And as for the people that remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler. 23 And when all the captains of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, there came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Careah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men. 24 And Gedaliah sware to them, and to their men, and said unto them, Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon; and it shall be well with you. 25 But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah. 26 And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose, and came to Egypt: for they were afraid of the Chaldees. 27 And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, that Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison; 28 And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon; 29 And changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life. 30 And his allowance was a continual allowance given him of the king, a daily rate for every day, all the days of his life. God delivers His judgment finally, and destroys Jerusalem. Zedekiah is blinded, the last thing he sees are his sons being murdered before him. But the Ethiopian eunuch is delivered, by his faith. And Jeremiah is rescued from prison to be set up in the court of the Babylonian governor. Seeing the story from multiple angles shows us the importance God places on it.

2 Kings 25 22 And as for the people that remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler. 23 And when all the captains of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, there came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Careah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men. 24 And Gedaliah sware to them, and to their men, and said unto them, Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon; and it shall be well with you. 25 But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah. 26 And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose, and came to Egypt: for they were afraid of the Chaldees. The captivity underway, we see that the captain of the guard, of the Chaldeans, freed Jeremiah from his bonds and set him at liberty to go where he liked, with provisions and reward, freed in the name of the Lord. The people who resisted heeding God's word are slain or led away captive to serve the Babylonian king. The poor and oppressed in the land of Judah are given the fields and vineyards and told to live peacefully. And those Jews who had fled to other lands returned. As God had said through the prophet, so it was. And then a particular Jew, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, using trickery, took matters into his own hands and murdered Gedaliah, the governor, and also killed collaborators and those that came down from Samaria, formerly Israel, with gifts. And though the rebels were chased from the land and slain, Ishmael escaped to the Ammonites. And the people, for fear of the Chaldeans who may seek to punish them for Ishmael's treachery, fled to Egypt. These all are a figure of sin and salvation, bondage and liberty. Using our own works and judgment, going against God's will to establish our own. Fleeing back to the yoke of bondage in sin. Jeremiah believed the Lord and it was given to him liberty. The people oppressed, set free. The wicked slain or taken away. But Ishmael sought to establish his own ways and will. By his own works. He goes against God's judgement in rebellion, and the people flee back to Egypt, where their forefathers had been in bondage. Egypt acting as a picture of sin so often in scripture. These things happened and were written that we can see the nature of God and man. We often cannot see how the will of God is better than our own flawed understanding of how things should be. And when we take matters into our own hands to "fix" it, we make things worse, and turn to sin.

2 Thessilonians 1 Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: 2 Grace unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. 3 We are bound to thank God always for you, brethren, as it is meet, because that your faith groweth exceedingly, and the charity of every one of you all toward each other aboundeth; 4 So that we ourselves glory in you in the churches of God for your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that ye endure: 5 Which is a manifest token of the righteous judgment of God, that ye may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which ye also suffer: 6 Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you; 7 And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, 8 In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: 9 Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power 1 Peter 4:17 For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God? Having been made desolate, spoiled. Many dead, more led away to captivity, and now, having the governor placed over them slain by one of their own, the remnant of Judah left in Jerusalem are desperate and full of fear. And in fear of destruction, they turn to Jeremiah, claiming to seek God's will for them in the calamity that's ensued. They say they want God to show them the way wherein they may walk. The thing they may do, to escape destruction. They know the word of the Lord is with Jeremiah, who had for years and years preached the coming destruction, despite stocks and smiting, being jailed and left to die in mire. And all he prophesied has come to pass. And they swear to the Lord that good or evil, they shall do as God tells them. This is the way so many of us are, unsaved or saved. Those who come to inquire of the Lord, "What must we do to be saved?" Or those who are children of God, and yet not walking after His will. They come to calamity, they see destruction ahead. They know they need to harken unto the word of God. They even will go to the godly to inquire, "What may we do?" swearing to obey. But in their hearts, they've already decided on Egypt; to sin. These men of Judah are told to trust in the Lord. To stay in the land, to not fear Nebuchadnezzar. To trust the Lord, that He is with you to save you, and deliver you from his hand. God promises them peace, mercy, to be returned to their own land. If they believe the word of God, they shall be saved. Note they didn't have to do anything other than believe that He would deliver them. That God repented of His wrath, if they simply obey His word. They didn't have to go anywhere. Do anything. Just believe. But God knows the heart of man, and He knew they hadn't asked Jeremiah to hear the truth, but to be told what they wanted to hear. That it was ok to flee to Egypt. That they should take it up on them to save themselves. The Lord promises them that if they don't believe on Him that delivers the faithful, they will be destroyed. That in Egypt, they will die by the sword and famine and pestilence. That they would become an execration, a reproach, a curse. That people would use their fate as a warning to all those who do not obey the good news given by the word of God. Unsaved people today will inquire of us, asking what they must do to be saved. And most will hear the gospel and refuse to obey it. They will seek their own works as justification. Or flee back to sin, as these Jews fled to Egypt, ignoring the warning of their destruction. And some saved Christians, who believed the gospel and know the word of God is true, that He is faithful, will still fall into sin and in tribulation, refuse to standfast in the faith, but as the house of God, turn from Him disobeying His word, to their destruction. As Peter asks us; If God will destroy those who are His, chastening every son He receives, if His judgment begins in His own house, against His people, what will He do to those who don't obey the Gospel?

2 Timothy 3 This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. 2 For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, 3 Without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, despisers of those that are good, 4 Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; 5 Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away. 6 For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts, 7 Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. 8 Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. 9 But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as their's also was. 10 But thou hast fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, charity, patience, 11 Persecutions, afflictions, which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me. 12 Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution. 13 But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived. 14 But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them; 15 And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. 16 All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: 17 That the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works. 2 Timothy 4:3-4 For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; and they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables. And so when there is tribulation and calamity and imminent destruction, perilous times that shall come, there will be proud men like Azariah and Johanan, with itching ears, unwilling to hear the truth, and turning away to their own devices. And their folly becomes manifest as they are swiftly destroyed. Just as today, there are false teachers who gather huge followings, in the megachurches and television ministries, preaching lies and damnable heresies. Telling the people "peace, peace," when there is no peace. Leading the people to Egypt, spiritually, and so to their own destruction. And the greater the impending doom, the greater the tribulation, the more evil men and seducers there will be, waxing worse and worse. Deceiving and being deceived. Just as there is great opportunity for revival in tribulation, and many will seek the Lord sincerely and humbly when faced with troubles, so too is there always a falling away. Apostasy. False prophets, itching ears and a willingness to be lied to if it feels good, despite the clear word of God. Now the Lord says to Jeremiah, go to the gate of the Pharaoh in Egypt, and place great stones in the clay at the entrance, and preach that His servant, Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne upon these stones, and destroy Egypt, spoiling their cities, destroying their temples and burning their palaces. That the Chaldeans will slay whom God will, and lead captive whom He will. That the king will wear Egypt as a shepherd puts on a cloak. In this, we see a picture of the coming of the Lord, Jesus Christ. Who is the King, the Father's servant. Who will build his throne on the lively stones of believers, upon the foundation laid by Jesus. In triumph over sin and death. Smashing idols, breaking the images of the false gods. Sending those who obeyed not the word of God to their destruction. Amen

Women. Let all the children of the Catholic Church, who are so very dear to us, hear these words of ours. Behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith the Lord: but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest. Giving us our life as a prey, a Biblical term that means wherever we go, God is protecting us. That our life is His and under Him, even as all else is lost and His wrath is pouring out on all flesh, we shall be spared. What a blessing to be the sons of the living God! Seek not great things unto ourselves. Don't build up treasure here on earth. Worry for nothing. Fear only God. And know that assuredly, in all places, whither you go, the Lord of our faith and deliverance has given our life as a prey unto us.

Revelation 19 And after these things I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto the Lord our God: 2 For true and righteous are his judgments: for he hath judged the great whore, which did corrupt the earth with her fornication, and hath avenged the blood of his servants at her hand. 3 And again they said, Alleluia And her smoke rose up for ever and ever. 4 And the four and twenty elders and the four beasts fell down and worshipped God that sat on the throne, saying, Amen; Alleluia. 5 And a voice came out of the throne, saying, Praise our God, all ye his servants, and ye that fear him, both small and great. 6 And I heard as it were the voice of a great multitude, and as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth. 7 Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. 8 And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints. 9 And he saith unto me, Write, Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of God. 10 And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Jesus: worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy. 11 And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. 12 His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. 13 And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God. 14 And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean. 15 And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God. 16 And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, King Of Kings, And Lord Of Lords. 17 And I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the fowls that fly in the midst of heaven, Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God; 18 That ye may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses, and of them that sit on them, and the flesh of all men, both free and bond, both small and great. 19 And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army. 20 And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone. 21 And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh. Jeremiah receives the word of God, Who had prophesied against Judah, against those who were idolatrous, against those who fought against Babylon, against those who didn't surrender unto Babylon, against those who fled to Egypt. Now, He turns his wrath on the Gentiles of Egypt, and prophecies of their armies destruction and the spoiling of their homeland. God judges nations and His armies faint not. And just as they rose against His servant Nebuchadnezzar, and were destroyed, so will it be when Jesus returns, the remnant of Judah, the seed which shall return and be in rest and ease and none shall make Him afraid. Remember, there is an unbroken line of believers, living faith to faith, saved by the gospel and bearing fruit after their own kind, from the shores of the Jordan to all believers today. That's not a theory. It's a fact. And despite the best effort of the Whore to eradicate us, there is always a remnant to carry the seed of God's word to a new generation of believers. Amen.

This part of Jeremiah, where the armies of Egypt take our Philistines, Babylon destroys Egypt, Judah is made desolate, Moab, Ammonites... Babylon itself, God takes care of His business in an elegant way that is amazing in its complexity but beautiful in simplicity. And the prophecy against the Gentiles and the reminder of the destruction of Israel and the decimation of the Jews is a picture of the wrath to come in the end times. A window into the judgment of the day of the Lord.

Revelation 18 And after these things I saw another angel come down from heaven, having great power; and the earth was lightened with his glory. 2 And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird. 3 For all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication, and the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth are waxed rich through the abundance of her delicacies. 4 And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues. 5 For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities. 6 Reward her even as she rewarded you, and double unto her double according to her works: in the cup which she hath filled fill to her double. 7 How much she hath glorified herself, and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her: for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow. 8 Therefore shall her plagues come in one day, death, and mourning, and famine; and she shall be utterly burned with fire: for strong is the Lord God who judgeth her. 9 And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning, 10 Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come. 11 And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more: 12 The merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet, and all thyine wood, and all manner vessels of ivory, and all manner vessels of most precious wood, and of brass, and iron, and marble, 13 And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and beasts, and sheep, and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men. 14 And the fruits that thy soul lusted after are departed from thee, and all things which were dainty and goodly are departed from thee, and thou shalt find them no more at all. 15 The merchants of these things, which were made rich by her, shall stand afar off for the fear of her torment, weeping and wailing, 16 And saying, Alas, alas that great city, that was clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold, and precious stones, and pearls! 17 For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off, 18 And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city! 19 And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate. 20 Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her. 21 And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone, and cast it into the sea, saying, Thus with violence shall that great city Babylon be thrown down, and shall be found no more at all. 22 And the voice of harpers, and musicians, and of pipers, and trumpeters, shall be heard no more at all in thee; and no craftsman, of whatsoever craft he be, shall be found any more in thee; and the sound of a millstone shall be heard no more at all in thee; 23 And the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride shall be heard no more at all in thee: for thy merchants were the great men of the earth; for by thy sorceries were all nations deceived. 24 And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth. As we near the end of the Book of Jeremiah, we see the prophecy against Babylon, which soon would be crushed by the Medes, establishing the Medo-Persian Empire. Cyrus the Great will eventually restore the remnant of Judah to their land, after the 70 years of captivity, and the 2nd Temple will be built. But the Lord used Babylon to crush the rebellion of the Jews against Him. To winnow the wheat from the chaff, just as He will the armies of the Beast in the days of vengeance. In this prophecy, we see dual imagery being used; predictions of the soon to come fall of that great Golden empire, but also of the end times. Of the Lord Jesus and the final destruction of that spirit of Babylon, which works even today. And the promise of eternal peace for God's people, the saints who believed on His word. Because God will have justice for the blood of the innocent, the prophets and if the saints that were all slain upon the earth. The symbology of these chapters and how they tie in to Daniel and Ezekiel and Revelation is deep. She who is upon many waters. The cup that makes the rulers of the earth drunk. The fornication of idols and false gods. The innocent babes who had been passed through the fire to Baal being part of the army of Christ. The harvest time soon to come. Babylon without foundation or cornerstone, while the Kingdom of Heaven is founded upon the Rock that is Christ. The mountains falling on them as Zion rises. The portion of Jacob is not like them; for he is the former of all things: and Israel is the rod of his inheritance: the Lord of hosts is his name. The glory of Christ made manifest. Chapter 52 will wrap up the book of Jeremiah, and then I will go through Lamentations, which the prophet also wrote. We may then go through Daniel and then we shall see where the Lord takes us. The relevance of Jeremiah really comes into play with the current thing. The punishment by God against the wicked Jews who have forsaken Him, killed His prophets and His Son. The wrath is upon them. But also the destruction of the nation used against them. His will be done and may it be that we can use the opportunity to win souls and edify His church.

The final chapter of Jeremiah, and what seems to be a recap of events already covered here, and in 2 Kings. The siege of Jerusalem, the rebellion against the King of Babylon, sent by God to carry out His wrath. The destruction of the Jews for their transgressions, idolatry and lack of faith in the Living God. Shedding of innocent blood. The men fleeing, falling away. The captives taken away, the rest put down by the sword, pestilence and famine. The children of Zedekiah slain in front of him, his eyes put out. The captain of the guard saving some of the poor to be servants in the kingdom. Others left behind to be vinedressers and husbandmen. The pillars smashed and the temple made desolate and the destruction of the vessels fitted to His purpose within the temple. The elevation of Jehoiachin, lifted up from prison and set in his throne above the other kings. Changed our of his prison garments and given new clothes, eating bread continually. It's all a picture of the end times.

The book of Lamentations is the poetic book of Jeremiah the "weeping prophet." In it, the desolation of Jerusalem and the sins of the people of Judah, as well as the goodness of God, are described in poetic language. The passages progress from this dismal and dismayed beginning to a bitter understanding of their predicament. Much like the progression Jeremiah has in the early chapters of his main book, where he goes from protest and prayer for the salvation of his people, to grave acceptance and faith in the right judgments of the Lord. The psalms contained in the 4 short chapters are a comfort in themselves to me when facing tribulation. Things could be much worse. And also a reminder of God's wrath against the ungodly. How often could we say that our signs are many and hearts faint? But unlike Judah, we have a comforter that's with us at all times; the holy Spirit. To know we've never been abandoned or left to our enemies, for the presence of the Lord, the living God, dwells within us. As Jesus tells us in John 14: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also. Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father. And whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If ye shall ask any thing in my name, I will do it. If ye love me, keep my commandments. And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you. I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you. So in tribulation, rejoice. We have not been left as Jerusalem. We have a comforter, if we believe on Jesus, trusting His word. And as we walk in Him, so too does the Spirit indwelling us. Jesus promises us He will not leave us comfortless. One of the major themes of the prophets, aside from the promise of deliverance in the promise of the Lord, is the judgment of God upon those who chase after other gods. Who commit fornication with them, metaphorically. The whoredoms of the people, who He consistently compares to a woman caught in adultery, whose lovers have abandoned her in her downfall. That she is like a woman exposed, naked to the world, ashamed. The Lord is longsuffering and merciful, His patience and grace are abundant and His love for us who are His is unending. But those who fall away to apostasy, Idolatry, faith in strange gods, while still calling themselves His, provokes Him to wrath. God's name is jealousy. So, in our times where the largest sects calling themselves "Christian," are decked in scarlet and purple, clad in gold and jewels, and bowing and serving idols, putting faith in the creation over the Creator, lighting candles and incense to the "queen of heaven," it stirs God to wrath. The abominations of the heathen, the shedding of innocent blood, violence, sexual perversions...all of these the Lord hates, but it is that adultery of those harlots that really stirs Him to wrath. With this perspective, the woman taken in adultery story from the Gospels, takes on added context: John 8:3-11 And the scribes and Pharisees brought unto him a woman taken in adultery; and when they had set her in the midst, They say unto him, Master, this woman was taken in adultery, in the very act. Now Moses in the law commanded us, that such should be stoned: but what sayest thou? This they said, tempting him, that they might have to accuse him. But Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground, as though he heard them not. So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her. And again he stooped down, and wrote on the ground. And they which heard it, being convicted by their own conscience, went out one by one, beginning at the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst. When Jesus had lifted up himself, and saw none but the woman, he said unto her, Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee? She said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more. Now the scribes sought to test Jesus and make Him choose; either keep the law as they saw it, and stone the woman angering the Romans, or speak against the law, angering the Jews. But as we know, Jesus simply said 'He that is without sin among you, cast the first stone." The truth was they didn't bring her before Him in good faith, they didn't bring the man she had supposedly committed this crime unto death with, that he may face the same justice. But their real sin was their own adultery against God. The hypocrisy wasn't so much in their judgement of the woman, but in their unfaithfulness to the Lord. And then Jesus, having shown them their own adulterous hearts, tells the woman to go and sin no more. Which spiritually, in that context of whoredoms against God, is a call to repentance towards Christ. (not a call to sinless perfection and works salvation)

Lamentations chapter 2, like chapter 1 and 4, is 22 verses, because these poems are written in an acrostic format, where each verse is started by a letter in the alphabet, in this case the 22 letters of the Hebrew language. Verse 3, as we will see, is 66 verses, because it uses the same format, but repeats 3 lines per letter. It is interesting that God's poetry loses nothing in their beauty being translated to English, the poems and Psalms not relying on a meter or rhyme. And of course, these poems of lamentation are Jeremiah's weeping over the destruction of Judah by the Babylonians, but clearly by the hand of God. The first chapter describing Jerusalem as a widow and an adulterous, left desolate and friendless. The second, a daughter left without hope, covered in a cloud in his anger, and cast down from previous highs, brought low by His wrath. The prophet describes how the Lord has torn down their habitations, their walls and strongholds, their temple and altars, kings and princes, priests and prophets. Taken everything from them. That their children beg for wine (juice) and bread in hunger. The Lord was as an enemy, He bent his bow against them as an enemy. His wrath was upon them as He violently took away their Tabernacle, cast off the altar, ended the law, the sacrifices...taken from them everything. Only a remnant saved, carried away to a far kingdom. All by the hand of God. The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; thou hast slain them in the day of thine anger; thou hast killed, and not pitied. Thou hast called as in a solemn day my terrors round about, so that in the day of the Lord's anger none escaped nor remained: those that I have swaddled and brought up hath mine enemy consumed. This it will be in the day of the Lord. The same will happen to the nations of the world. Their temples and kings will be cut off. Their strongholds, even the very mountains they flee to, will be struck down. And the streets will be littered with the bodies of the young and old. None will escape the anger of the Lord except those carried away to His kingdom, His servants, on that great and terrible day.

Lamentations 3 is one of the most beautiful and heartfelt poetic works of the Bible, which is saying a lot considering the beauty of the Psalms. But in the Spirit Jeremiah captures so many things relevant to the life of a believer; the misery of being mired in sin, having God against us, as His enemy, pictures of the suffering of Christ for our sins, salvation by calling upon His name, the humility and faith gained in tribulation, and the imprecatory prayer against those who rise against us, and the prayers for our deliverance from their hands. It is an emotional rollercoaster, where for 20 verses we are left in the worst state of man, with images of Jesus' suffering used to describe this lowly state. The gall, the derision, the turning of the other cheek when struck. Bearing the yoke. Being cut off, prayers unheard; Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? It echos Psalm 22: Psalm 22 My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring? 2 O my God, I cry in the day time, but thou hearest not; and in the night season, and am not silent. 3 But thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Israel. 4 Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them. 5 They cried unto thee, and were delivered: they trusted in thee, and were not confounded. 6 But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people. 7 All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying, 8 He trusted on the Lord that he would deliver him: let him deliver him, seeing he delighted in him. 9 But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother's breasts. 10 I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother's belly. 11 Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help. 12 Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round. 13 They gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion. 14 I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels. 15 My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death. 16 For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet. 17 I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me. 18 They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture. 19 But be not thou far from me, O Lord: O my strength, haste thee to help me. 20 Deliver my soul from the sword; my darling from the power of the dog. 21 Save me from the lion's mouth: for thou hast heard me from the horns of the unicorns. 22 I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee. 23 Ye that fear the Lord, praise him; all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel. 24 For he hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; neither hath he hid his face from him; but when he cried unto him, he heard. 25 My praise shall be of thee in the great congregation: I will pay my vows before them that fear him. 26 The meek shall eat and be satisfied: they shall praise the Lord that seek him: your heart shall live for ever. 27 All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the Lord: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee. 28 For the kingdom is the Lord's: and he is the governor among the nations. 29 All they that be fat upon earth shall eat and worship: all they that go down to the dust shall bow before him: and none can keep alive his own soul. 30 A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation. 31 They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this. Powerful understanding that as we were, (or are yet) unregenerate sinners, we have the rod against us, being provoked by the Spirit towards repentance, and as low as we feel, Christ Jesus paid a far worse penalty, for our sins not His. And in this remembrance, is our blessed hope: My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is humbled in me. This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness. The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him. The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord. And in this hope, we call upon the name of the Lord, and are filled with the Spirit of His promises. We are assured of our lives being redeemed in Him. His mercies and compassion new every morning. We are called to pick up our cross every day, so if we stumble and backslide, if we turn to the left or the right, God is merciful in calling us back to the straight paths. Regardless of the temptations and tribulations that beset us. Even though, as the weeping prophet progresses through the verse; we remember our pain and our adversaries. We have been humbled and understand our own iniquities. We know we are only redeemed in His name. By the blood of Christ. But still, we tearfully know the suffering of life and the cares of the world. And yet our hope remains because God is steadfast and faithful. And so, knowing His love for us, we call out to Him for deliverance. We ask our enemies face His justice. Some may repent towards God. Some may be destroyed utterly, reprobate and cast off. But God's will be done, and our deliverance assured. I called upon thy name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon. Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry. Thou drewest near in the day that I called upon thee: thou saidst, Fear not. O Lord, thou hast pleaded the causes of my soul; thou hast redeemed my life. O Lord, thou hast seen my wrong: judge thou my cause. Remember, Jeremiah was literally thrown in a pit of mire, the depths of a prison, for the cause of his faith. And here, again echoing Christ's decent onto Hell for our transgressions, a burnt offering for our sin, we in our lowest points as believers likewise call out for our deliverance. And the Lord says; Fear not. Jesus pleads our case, redeems our soul in His blood, by His sacrifice. Drawing near to us. And so we ask Him to judge our cause. That His will be done. When you have believed, there is no calamity or trials that the Lord will not help us overcome. We simply must ask and He will plead our cause and judge those who are against us, and deliverance is assured. Nothing will come between us and His mercies. So be not afraid. Amen

Lamentations chapter 4 continues the series of acrostic poems by the prophet Jeremiah, lamenting or mourning the desolation of Judah and destruction of Jerusalem by the Babylonians physically, but under the wrath of God. And as we have seen, the weeping prophet uses allegory to paint a picture of the evil he has witnessed. The horrors he prophesied come to pass. The sons of Zion are like the spoiled gold if the temple, turned to earthen clay pots. Basically worthless. The mammals of the sea, likely seals or small whales, that give suck to their pups, but the daughters of Jerusalem have become like ostriches that abandon their eggs in the wilderness. The babies' tongues are stuck to the roof of their mouths for hunger. There is no bread for the children. Rich men who fared sumptuously are eating dung. Jeremiah writes that the destruction of Sodom wasn't as brutal and horrific as Jerusalem, because at least it was quick and complete. Here the starving draws out their suffering. This under the vow of the Nazarites, who would be by clean living for a short period, be considered the peak of good health, now are sunken and gaunt. The women have cooked the flesh of their own children for want of food. And this is all because of the wrath of God, who is long suffering and merciful and quick to repent of evil against His people when they repent towards Him. And yet, they were left destroyed and desolate. Spoiled and carried away to captivity. Jeremiah calls out the false prophets who shed the blood of the innocent to defend their heresies. Blind guides, as Christ called them, here wandering the streets, polluted in blood of the dead. Unclean. The Lord no longer regarding them, just as He no longer regarded Israel after the flesh in Hebrews 8:9; Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers In the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; Because they continued not in my covenant, And I regarded them not, saith the Lord. And the prophet is left weeping at the dismay that has come upon the daughter of Zion. The final stanzas of lamentations for includes a prophecy against Edom. As we will see in Ezekiel and Obadiah, Eden was destroyed because they rejoiced and mocked the destruction of Israel. We can develop that further later when it comes, but it is something to keep in mind that the brother of Israel faced God's wrath, Just as the final chapters of Jeremiah detailed the destruction of Egypt and the surrounding nations and ultimately Babylon. God judges nations based on their works. Even as he judges individuals based on their faith. It's an important distinction to keep in mind as we rightly divide the word of God. Genesis 1:11 And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so. Matthew 21:43 Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof. Matthew 7:16-18 Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Philippians 1:4-11 Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy, For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now; Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace. For God is my record, how greatly I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ. And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment; That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ. Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God. Romans 1:16-17 For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith. I am a saved Christian. Born again by the faith that was shared to me by another saved Christian, who in turn believed and was converted by yet another saved. Christian. A line of succession going back to the beginning of the world. That the just live by faith and bear fruit after its own kind. A line of believers stretching back to Adam. To Abel. To Seth and Enos. The same faith of Abraham who believed the Lord and it was counted upon him for righteousness. The same faith that makes up the record of the "Hall of faith," in Hebrews chapter 11. The same faith preached by John, the Baptist in the wilderness, taught by Christ Himself during His earthly ministry, given to the apostles as the keys to overcome death and hell. Preached on the day of Pentecost. Given to the Jews and to the Greek. The salvation that is by calling upon the name of the Lord. By believing on the finished work of Christ Jesus as the propitiation of our sin. And, like the blood of the prophets from Abel to Zechariah, and of Jesus and the Apostles, and of the believers persecuted by the Jews and the Romans, a trail of blood that links believing Christians today to those that were martyred for the same faith in the same Gospel of grace and reconciliation. A trail of blood that continued through the persecution by Constantine's cult, through the dark ages, during the Reformation, under Bloody Mary, and that will mark the great tribulation to come. It is an unbroken chain of believers saved by faith. And sadly, the world hates us for it and there is a similar line, paved in blood.

The final chapter of Lamentations, a summary of the famine and devastation that comes from God rejecting a nation. His wrath upon them. But the prophet ends with the promise of the coming Christ. The truth that the Lord is forever upon the throne. Even as the reprobate nation is destroyed. Turn thou us unto thee, O Lord, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old. This is a prayer for our people today, who have fallen so far away. Who became wise in their own conceits thinking America would continue to have the blessings of liberty without a Christian people. That a nation of idolaters and abominations would remain one nation, under God, for all time. But it too is cut off and burned, for the turning away from the Lord. So we should remember that there is no political solution to a spiritual problem. That it is the believers of a nation that determine if God's judgment comes upon it. There is only one way to turn around the collapse of a nation, and it is by revival. 2 Chronicles 7:14 If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. This is the promise of God.

Beginning Ezekiel, and the prophet is among the captives of Judah, held by Babylon, when the revelations of the Lord came upon him. Familiar description of the angels, living creatures with four faces and four wings and the bodies of men. Each part of a means of movement, wheels or spheres within one another. Turning each way, fast as lightning. Rings about them filled with eyes. A firmament upon the heads, a flow or an aura, and under it, as on the ark, wings stretched towards the other. The noise of their wings like great waters, or as the voice of God. And above this firmament, a throne and upon it the likeness of a man, covered in the appearance of fire, bright and with a rainbow about them. And with that, the prophet fell upon his face and heard a voice... As strange as all this is, and as many artists and others have tried to depict it, I think our own minds' eye is the best representation, and still we cannot comprehend it. But like similar visions given Daniel and John the Apostle, it describes the Heavenly throne of the Almighty. Revelation 4:1-8 After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter. And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald. And round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold. And out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices: and there were seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God. And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal: and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four beasts full of eyes before and behind. And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle. And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.

Revelation 10:8-11 And the voice which I heard from heaven spake unto me again, and said, Go and take the little book which is open in the hand of the angel which standeth upon the sea and upon the earth. And I went unto the angel, and said unto him, Give me the little book. And he said unto me, Take it, and eat it up; and it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey. And I took the little book out of the angel's hand, and ate it up; and it was in my mouth sweet as honey: and as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter. And he said unto me, Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings. And so, continuing in Ezekiel 2, a commission is given, and words and knowledge, as the Spirit comes upon the prophet. He is given the ministry towards the children of Israel, a rebellious people. He is told it will be hard, dangerous even, but to be not afraid, and warned not to be rebellious against the Lord as the others are. It's clear that he had a choice in the matter, although there's really no choice when presented this way. But we serve God by free will. And we also are given the Spirit and His word to consume, and though surrounded by disobedient children of man, dangers and mockery, we can choose to obey. To be used by God. To have no fear. John is given a book to eat, and a mission field to address, and his account has influenced millions. We should heed their prophecy and seek to be servants of the living God. Spreading that word.

So, Ezekiel eats the scroll of the word of God, sweet as honey. And the Lord commissions Ezekiel to go among to the house of Israel, and to speak God's word to those in captivity with him in Babylon. The Lord says that he is sending him among the people he knows and the language he speaks. Not among many strange people with many hard languages. But says if He had sent him to preach to them, they'd believe, but these Jews who should know better and understand his speech won't believe, because they are impudent and hardhearted. Hard headed. A rebellious house. This reflects the eventual turn towards the Gentiles in the New Testament. That the Jews would not believe, and hardened their hearts, but the people who knew not God gladly accepted His word. The appearance of the Lord departs, and the prophet goes to his home and he sat astonished at what had happened, for seven days. Then the Lord came upon him again, and tells Ezekiel that he has been made a watchman unto the house of Israel, a theme that will carry throughout the book, and that has great relevance to saved believers today. The watchman, upon the tower and the walls, is there to sound the trumpet in case of danger or attack, that in warning those in his charge, they may be prepared to act. God says that if He says the wicked will surely die, and we don't warn them, his sins may be the reason but his blood is on our heads too. And if you give warning, and they choose not to accept it, and act, then their blood isn't on you. You've done your part. The Lord even clarifies further; not just the wicked who need to be warned, but the righteous, that their sin will lead them to death. That their works of righteousness won't be remembered. But our failure to warn them of this means we will bear some responsibility for it. We have to warn them, that even when they eventually sin (there is none righteous, no not one), they will still have eternal life having been warned, and believed God's word. This is an awesome responsibility. It is the same great commission, given by Christ to all believers. Many times you will hear preaching from soul-winning churches that what we really are doing is soul-warning, and it is so true. Only the person you're warning can take the gospel you give them, the Spirit working on them, and believe. But when we fail to warn people, their blood really is on our heads. Go soul-winning. The Lord commands Ezekiel to remain in his house until God calls on him to preach. That the rebellious people will put him in bonds. That he will be struck dumb of his own words, but the Spirit will give him the word of God. Similar to what Jesus says to the apostles: Matthew 10:17 But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues; And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles. But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak. For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you. We are the watchmen appointed by the Lord, sent to warn others. And if they be rebellious, and put us in bonds, He will fill us with the Spirit to speak His word. Not our own. Amen

Poor Ezekiel. God commands Ezekiel to perform symbolic acts to foreshadow the judgment on Jerusalem and Judah. He is instructed to draw Jerusalem on a clay tablet and stage a siege against it with a wall, battering rams, and camps, representing the city’s impending destruction. Ezekiel is told to lie on his left side for 390 days to bear Israel’s iniquity and on his right side for 40 days for Judah’s sins, each day symbolizing a year of punishment. God also commands him to eat a meager ration of bread made from mixed grains and pulse (beans and lentils), baked over dung, to signify the scarcity and defilement of food that the starving people will endure during the siege. Originally, human dung, but to appease Ezekiel, God allows him to use cow dung. Hardly better, but apt given the situation. These acts serve as a powerful sign to the Jews of God’s judgment for their disobedience. The 390 years align with the capture of Judah by the Syrian "king of the North," the Seleucid empire, which would see Antiochus IV Epiphanes, the figure of the antichrist, that vile man, take power in the region. The Lord asks much of the prophet. We should be grateful we are given such a light yoke.
