The Lord tells Ezekiel to shave his head bald, and his beard, and divide the hair in three that he may burn a third, smite a third with a knife and scatter a third to the wind. This represents His judgment on the people. Remember, from the beginning God has told Ezekiel to do these things among the children of Israel, in the captivity, that they may come to repentance. But, as He said they are a rebellious people and won't listen. The performative nature of these tasks set before Ezekiel are dramatic. Some, like his fasting on dung bread and laying on his sides, take place over a long period of time. This act, shaving his hair and using it as an example of the judgment of God, is quicker and more dramatic. All of it is designed to explicitly teach what God wants them to know, but like the parables of Christ, they must have seemed like outlandish and wild acts to those without an ear to hear. And as crazy as it seemed to others, Ezekiel did it all without hesitation. God asks so much less of us, giving His word to the lost. Yet many Christians today will not go out of their way to give the gospel to others. Consider Ezekiel and the humility and obedience in the exercises he did to spread God's word, and get over yourself, your fear, your pride, and find a local church that goes door-knocking. Bear fruit. Be salt. Let your light so shine. Glorify God.

The Lord tells Ezekiel to turn to the mountains and preach against them, and against the hills, rivers and valleys. The locations of the high places, groves and temples full of idols that Israel had turned to worship. It is important to remember that the prophet is charged with performing this preaching in view of others, that they may hear and not believe, being a stubborn and stiff-necked, rebellious people. God hates Idolatry. He despises the altars and high place made to desecrate His word. To lead people to practice adultery, calling upon others to save them, rather than His holy name. What Ezekiel and the other prophets preached still stands today. And so we rejoice when a temple made of man's hands, filled with blasphemy and Idolatry is destroyed. We cheer for its destruction. That they will be made to know that He is the Lord

Luke 21:20-22 And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. The wrath of God against the wicked is a promise, just as sure as salvation in Christ. They shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold shall be removed: their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord: they shall not satisfy their souls, neither fill their bowels: because it is the stumblingblock of their iniquity. Covetousness is the sin of idolatry, the Bible says. And for the rich men, that store up treasure on earth, it is harder for them to enter into the kingdom of Heaven than for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle. The stumbling block of their iniquity is their greed. Especially the Jews, who were and are respecters of persons in that regard. Also from Luke 21, 1-4; And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury. And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites. And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had. The love of money is the root of all evil. You cannot serve God and Mammon. This chapter also reminds me of the destruction of Babylon in Revelation 18:9-19; And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning, Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come. And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more: The merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet, and all thyine wood, and all manner vessels of ivory, and all manner vessels of most precious wood, and of brass, and iron, and marble, And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and beasts, and sheep, and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men. And the fruits that thy soul lusted after are departed from thee, and all things which were dainty and goodly are departed from thee, and thou shalt find them no more at all. The merchants of these things, which were made rich by her, shall stand afar off for the fear of her torment, weeping and wailing, And saying, Alas, alas that great city, that was clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold, and precious stones, and pearls! For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off, And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city! And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate. And through it all, His wrath revealed from Heaven, saying; I will do unto them after their way, and according to their deserts will I judge them; and they shall know that I am the Lord. Amen

Romans 1:19-25 Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. Here in Ezekiel 8, the prophet is lifted up by the hand of God, by his hair, and transported spiritually to Jerusalem, to witness the abominations of Judah. He is shown an idol set up inside the gates, an image of jealousy. Exodus 34:14 For thou shalt worship no other god: for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God He sees the glory of the God of Israel, as he had in chapter 1, and He shows the prophet more abominations, including a hidden chamber filled with idols, and 70 men led by one, Jaazaniah, offering strange fire of incense to their idols in secret. In a hole in the wall, thinking they his themselves from God. This is a wicked, hidden cult with great men of Judah involved, in secret. Our modern minds think of Masons and Jewish tunnels and attempts to hide their sin from God. Yet the Lord says He will show Ezekiel greater abominations. He then shows him two groups of people, the women publicly "weeping for Tammuz," and men facing the East Gate of the Temple, facing the rising Sun to worship it, rather than the altar, the laver, the holy of holies therein, to the West. They have turned their land to violence and they put the branch to their nose, they thumb their noses at God. Publicly. We often think about the secret societies and satanic cabals that rule the nations, and the evil they do, and it is true they exist even today. But notice God finds the practices of the people, who are openly worshipping false gods worse than the things that go on in secret. And the Lord judges the nation that turns from Him. He will not spare them or have outt upon them. He will not hear their cries.

Revelation 7:1-12 And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree. And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God: and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, Saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads. And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel. Of the tribe of Juda were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Reuben were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Gad were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Aser were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Nephthalim were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Manasses were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Simeon were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Levi were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Issachar were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Zabulon were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Joseph were sealed twelve thousand. Of the tribe of Benjamin were sealed twelve thousand. After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands; And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb. And all the angels stood round about the throne, and about the elders and the four beasts, and fell before the throne on their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, Amen: Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever. Amen. Continuing in Ezekiel 9, the prophet is still being given a vision of Jerusalem, filled with abominations. Some secret, some open and flagrant. Where the people say the Lord had forsaken the earth, or that He seeth not. And the Lord, come down from the mercy seat, to the threshold of the temple, orders an angel with an inkhorn to set a mark the foreheads of the men who wept and sighed over the abominations in their midst. A righteous remnant. Those that had charge over the city, the 6 men the Lord summons with their weapons of destruction, I believe angels of the city that kept watch over it. And He orders them to fill the courtyard of the temple with the dead, slaying utterly the old, young, maids and little children that have not the mark. Of course, Satan has his counterfeit mark; Revelation 13:16 And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads And he orders those that will not worship the beast and his image, and take the mark be killed, making war with the saints. Martyring those who have the testimony of Christ. This is what the beast is copying. But God has sealed us with the Spirit unto redemption. And those 144K that will come during the wrath will be likewise sealed. God protects His own, while the beast will damn many to torment in the time to come and eternity. Our Lord will not forsake us. Amen

Ezekiel 10 describes a vivid and wild vision of God's glory departing from the temple in Jerusalem. Ezekiel sees the cherubim, angelic beings with four faces and wings, accompanied by wheels full of eyes, moving in unison with the divine presence. The glory of the Lord, depicted as a radiant cloud, rises from the cherubim and moves to the temple's threshold, signifying God’s judgment and withdrawal from an unfaithful people. He was no longer present in the Temple. The man clothed in linen is instructed to take burning coals from between the cherubim and scatter them over the city, destroying it with fire. Ezekiel says these living creatures, or the beasts in Heaven from revelation, are the same as his first visions, in case there were any doubt. I do not think we can process with our human minds the sights of these things. The Lord pulled away a veil and showed them to the prophet, and he is trying his best in the Spirit to make us understand the glory of what he saw. Jerusalem being made desolate is the point, however. There in the 6th year of Babylonian captivity, destruction has come to them for their wicked abominations.

The present vision of Jerusalem given to Ezekiel by the glory of the Lord concludes. Here, the prophet is shown the East Gate, and 25 men, princes of the people. Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah among them. The Lord says these men devise mischief and give wicked counsel. They tell everyone that they are safe, as safe as meat in a pot. Flesh in a caldron. So build houses, make plans, settle in. It's all going to be ok. But the Lord has other plans. Because of the murder and violence on the city, and the blood of the slain, He says He will bring them out of the city, even to the borders of the country and the sword shall fall on them. And they shall know He is the Lord. And as Ezekiel prophesied, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. The reality of the revelation of the Lord comes upon Ezekiel, and he cries for his people, asking if the Lord shall wipe all of them out, making a full end of the remnant of Israel. God says that He has cast them out of the land because of their presumption that they are entitled to us, absent faith in the Lord. He says that, in their diaspora, He will be as a little sanctuary for them in the lands He scatters them to, and that He will gather them again, that they take away the abominations, the idols and rejection of God. Dispensationalists love the next part; Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord God; I will even gather you from the people, and assemble you out of the countries where ye have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel. And they shall come thither, and they shall take away all the detestable things thereof and all the abominations thereof from thence. And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh: That they may walk in my statutes, and keep mine ordinances, and do them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God. But they fail to recognize that this is a promise to the faithful, the righteous by faith, not for every one. But as for them whose heart walketh after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I will recompense their way upon their own heads, saith the Lord God. God's promises are always for the faithful. Without faith, it is impossible to please God. Ezekiel is returned to Chaldea, to Babylon and there he preaches all that was shown unto him to those in captivity. That things at home aren't going well. That the faithful will be protected wherever they may be, and God's promise is to bring them home again. This vision is as much for us as it is for them. We are in Babylon, even today. But our hearts are quickened and we will be called home, to the land we've been promised, that heavenly country. So we stay faithful unto the end, secure in this knowledge. Amen

Ezekiel 12 begins with the Lord instructing the prophet to pack and move his belongings in the sight of the people. To do so without looking them in the eye, even covering his face that he not be able to see the ground. To dig a hole in the walls, as if escaping the city, in twilight, as if sneaking out. Without explanation, Ezekiel obeys the command of the Lord. And in the morning, the Lord explains to Ezekiel that this demonstration to a rebellious people, who having eyes to see are blind, was to show them the manner they will enter into captivity, attempting to flee. Not only them, but specifically the prince in Jerusalem, King Zedekiah of Judah, who was blinded by the Babylonians and taken captive to Babylon. We have covered this event as described in Jeremiah 39:7 and 2 Kings 25:7. ...I will bring him to Babylon to the land of the Chaldeans; yet shall he not see it, though he shall die there. The performative preaching is given as a sign to the people that they may know, when it came to pass, that He is the Lord, and it is from Him these things are done. Further, He says, that He will spare some that are scattered abroad, and led to captivity, that they may be a sign and a testimony to the wrath of God against their own abominations to all nations. Basically living to tell the tale of how they came to be scattered and destroyed for their own wickedness, which gives glory and praise to God. One of the chief ways the Lord makes himself known is by His wrath. They shall know that He is the Lord. God instructs Ezekiel to then perform a sign, of eating bread and drinking water in fear and carefulness, as the people will as they are facing invasion and captivity, the desolation of Judah. And again, the word of God came to him, and says there is a proverb in the land that offends the Lord. That their days are prolonged and every vision faileth. That things are fine, and the prophecy of God is not coming true. Much like the scoffers we have in these last days; 2 Peter 3:3-4 Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation. The Lord God hates scoffers, and says to Ezekiel that He will make this proverb to cease. The day is at hand, not prolonged. And the effect of every vision will be made true. For I am the Lord: I will speak, and the word that I shall speak shall come to pass; it shall be no more prolonged: for in your days, O rebellious house, will I say the word, and will perform it, saith the Lord God. Fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and their lack of fear or respect has angered Him. Imagine the fury of the Lord today. But the days are short and will not be prolonged, but the word which He has spoken shall be done. Even so, hurry Lord. Amen

The word of the Lord comes against the false prophets of the kan, saying "Peace, peace" when there is no peace. Who tell the people they are safe in their sins. That God's judgment isn't upon them. God compares them to someone who applied bad, untempered mortar to a wall. The wall easily collapses. God promises to expose them just as this, that they be ashamed before the people they lied to. Then He tells Ezekiel to preach against the women who prophesy from their own hearts, the daughters of Israel who are pillows to all armholes and make kerchiefs upon the head of every statue, large and small to hunt souls. To entrap men until them with lies. I don't know what the significance of these adornments means, other than it seems to be a style of comfort and beauty of whores or priestesses of Babylon, who lead good men to lust, who turn others against the righteous, and who prop up the evil with their lies. And they do it for very little material gain, they just enjoy corrupting the people. But in the end all false teachers are exposed and the people are made to know He is the Lord. The same today as in Ezekiel's day. The Osteens and Joyce Myers/"God isn't mad at you!" crowd. They will be made ashamed. Their names will not be in the books of our people. Those they misled will cry against them in their torment. They will be made to know He is the Lord.

Ezekiel 14 opens with elders of Israel coming before the prophet to hear him, but the Lord speaks to Ezekiel, saying that they have idols in their hearts and the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. They have coveted other things before the Lord God. They are unjust and filled with their sins. And so the Lord says they should be told to repent, and turn from their idols, turn away their faces from abominations. Otherwise, when anyone, Israelites and strangers in the land, seek a prophet, He will set His face against them. And the prophets will lie to them. And the Lord God says He is the means of deceiving them by the words of that prophet. In other words, He will give them strong delusion, that they believe a lie. 2 Thessalonians 2:11-12 And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: that they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness The Lord also says that the false prophet will be as punished as these idolatrous men, and all become a proverb and a byword, that Israel turns back towards God. Then the Lord gives Ezekiel His word, that when God sets out to destroy a land as wicked as Israel, that even if Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, He would only save them themselves from it. The illustration that 3 renown righteous men would not be sufficient to save a nation that had backslidden to the point of Judah in this day. No children. No remnant. Only the righteous men themselves. This establishes a few things that we may know from other scripture. One that, as Abraham argued with the Lord concerning Sodom and Gomorrah, that the presence of the righteous is generally sufficient to stave off judgement, at least for a time. We are the salt of the earth. We preserve the world unto judgment, but eventually it isn't sufficient and God's wrath comes due. Second, when this judgment comes, only the saved are spared. Only those made righteous by faith in the blood are not appointed to wrath. Third, it is interesting that Daniel, a contemporary of Ezekiel has, by this time, been noticed of God. It isn't clear that Ezekiel himself may know of Daniel, although the youth was made a president of the Babylonian empire early in captivity. But the Lord knows, and knowing we'd know, he is held up as an example. Finally, there is a tendency of God's mercy, that when it isn't a final judgment, when it serves His needs, He will save the family of the righteous from that judgment. As 8 were saved by the righteousness of Noah. As Lot's wife (almost!) and his daughters are saved from Sodom. As the remnant of sons and daughters mentioned here in Exikiel 14. For thus saith the Lord God; How much more when I send my four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, and the famine, and the noisome beast, and the pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast? Yet, behold, therein shall be left a remnant that shall be brought forth, both sons and daughters The remnant was left for His sake. For His name's sake and the city where He had chosen to place His name. To ensure the line of David continues and that Jerusalem stands, awaiting the Messiah that would come from both, Christ Jesus. During study on Revelation 6 last night, verse 8; And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth. I noticed the same plagues against man from yesterday's reading in Ezekiel 14. Sword, hunger, death and beasts in Revelation, sword, famine, pestilence and beasts. The wrath and judgment of God.

John 15:1-3 I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you. Romans 11:17-21 And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. In Ezekiel 15, the word of the Lord came unto the prophet, and asks what is the vine tree, what good is it? It does no work. It isn't used for any task. It grows, it is only fit to be burned. The Lord compares the inhabitants of Jerusalem to this vine, and that fire shall devour them like it becomes their trespasses. Now, Jesus is the true vine, and the branches those people who are His and produce fruit, more saved people. And branches that don't are purged, the Bible says. Cut off. Fit to burn. But it is interesting that the wood of the vine tree, when it is whole and growing, does no work. Just as we are supported by the root, which is Christ, without works.

In Ezekiel 16, Jerusalem is personified as a woman whom God rescued, adorned, and entered into a covenant with (verses 6–14), akin to a marriage. However, her persistent idolatry and unfaithfulness (v15–34) provoke God’s judgment, described in terms of punishment and abandonment (v 35–43). The chapter reads as a writ of divorce. God breaking up with her, in a spiritual metaphor. When God found her, she (Judah specifically here, but Israel generally), they were as the Canaanites. Worse, they were abandoned. Alone. Again this isn't literal and genetic, but their spiritual condition. Abram was a Chaldean. Jacob was a Hebrew, as Abraham lived in Hebron. There was intermarriage with the Canaanites, but the analogy is not about lineage but beliefs and idolatry. When God lays out their abominations, giving the fine clothing, incense and worship to strange gods that was meant for Him, and murdered the children He gave them it is adultery and worse than the abominations of Samaria (Israel) or even Sodom. The idea that what they did was worse than Sodom and her daughters, the like cities around them, is a theme. The worst place imaginable, and yet unfaithful Judah is worse: Isaiah 1:9 Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah. Matthew 11:24 But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee. They despised their oath. They broke the covenant. They behaved like their sisters, humanity that didn't know better or didn't have the privilege that He had bestowed upon them. The line of David. The glory of Solomon. The oracles of God, the Temple, the blessing and the promise. And so God is righteous to divorce them. But, despite this condemnation, the Lord leaves room for hope. Christ is coming. And not only would Judah be restored, but her "sisters," the Gentiles. That He will establish His covenant, and we shall know He is the Lord. Maybe...just hear me out...maybe they mean the same thing. Both "tektōn" (Greek) and "carpenter" describe skilled craftsmen who contribute to building buildings and structures, particularly but not exclusively through woodworking. In the context of Mark 6:3, both terms suggest Jesus was involved in skilled construction-related work, including being a framer, designing and building the structural elements of buildings, e.g., wooden beams, framing, roofs, etc...as well as the stonework and the like. Knowing that He framed the world, that He is the corner stone, the right angle, the foundation...all these construction terms and concepts, brings the spiritual to life. So there is no contradiction. I thank God His word was settled in Heaven before the framing of the world, amen.

This parable, a riddle posed to the people of Jerusalem, is difficult to follow, but God gives the answers. A great eagle (representing the king of Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar) comes to Lebanon (symbolizing Jerusalem), takes the highest branch of a cedar (the king of Judah, Jehoiachin), and carries it to a land of merchants (Babylon). The eagle then takes “seed of the land” (Zedekiah, a new king from the royal line) and plants it in fertile soil by abundant waters, where it grows into a low, spreading vine (Judah under Zedekiah’s rule, dependent on Babylon). Another great eagle (representing Egypt) appears, and the vine (Zedekiah) turns toward it, seeking support, despite being planted in good soil. This symbolizes Zedekiah’s rebellion against Babylon by seeking an alliance with Egypt. And so, the Lord asks, can they prosper? By turning to Egypt and asking for horses and men to push out the Babylonian rule, they insult God and seek to mollify His judgment. So no, they will not prosper. It's vain. And so, Egypt’s help will fail Judah. Babylon will overpower Jerusalem because Zedekiah despised his oath and covenant with Nebuchadnezzar. An oath made in the Lord's name. 2 Chronicles 36:13 And he also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God: but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart from turning unto the Lord God of Israel. This betrayal and violation of the covenant means that nothing that follows will prosper. But the Lord Himself has another covenant, made with David, for a Messiah. And so, God turns the parable to Himself as the eagle, and that He will plant a cutting on Zion, cropped off the top of that cedar, representing David's lineage. A goodly cedar shall bring forth boughs, many branches bearing fruit. And under it shall dwell all fowl of every wing, the saved from many nations, and in His shadow shall we dwell. He shall exalt the low tree, being down the high tree, dry up the green tree (unbelieving Jews) and make the dry tree flourish, the faithful Gentiles. I the Lord have spoken and have done it. Centuries before the physical birth of Jesus, it is already done. Amen

This prophecy of Ezekiel is an often cited chapter regarding the doctrine of "original sin," which it clearly teaches against. But it is also cited by workies as to why turning from sin is part of salvation. But as always, we need to look at the context. First, the parable among the children of Israel in Judah, that the fathers ate sour grapes, but the children's teeth are on edge, has to be understood. And it is something many of us are guilty of saying. The judgment against the people had come, and Babylon was bringing them into captivity, and slaying many. So the younger generation was blaming the sins of the older generation for their troubles. That their fathers had eaten the sour grapes but they were the ones with the taste in their mouth. That God's judgment was unfair, and they were being punished for the sins of the father. We often blame Boomers for ruining the country they inherited, and it is true. They set up high places and committed adultery and violence and rejected the God of their fathers. But many who complain the loudest about this are themselves living the same way, or worse. Revival is on us, today and our present generation. As it says in verse 14, Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father's sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like...he shall surely live. It is up to us to get right, regardless of the hole dug by our parents. This is true regardless of the age we live in. And if we haven't, there's always time for turning from our own sins, and walking in righteousness, through Christ. The Lord has no pleasure in the deaths of the wicked, but rejoices in those who turn to Him and live. The word of the Lord shuts down the idea of original sin condemning us. The sins and the righteousness of each generation are their own. A man isn't judged by the sins of their father or his righteousness, but by theirs. And vice versa. We aren't condemned by Adam's sin, but by our own. We have his nature, being sons. But we all make our own way. But the Lord challenged the people saying He is unfair, because in fact they did as their fathers. As for the use of this to teach "repent of your sins" for salvation, we understand that this is in the context of a nation being judged. While God's judgment is upon the wicked, and His mercy is upon those that walk in His ways, the wrath upon a people is based on their nation's sin. He will spare the righteous from His wrath. That's a promise. 1 Thessalonians 5:9 For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ Romans 5:8-9 But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. And here, in Ezekiel's day, God is reserving a righteous remnant that would survive, and thrive, under captivity. The assumption is that if they are walking in His ways and keeping His precepts, they are doing so by faith. Ezekiel 18 encourages that commitment. The need for it in saved people. Note the warning to the backslidden is their death along with the unrighteous. But we know that judgment is just, but not eternal, because once saved always saved. God will take a backslidden Christian home in chastisement. So we should have a certain fearful looking over the shoulder when we seek to sin. Cast away from you all your transgressions, whereby ye have transgressed; and make you a new heart and a new spirit: for why will ye die, O house of Israel? For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord God: wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye. It's funny that the libertines in the new Evangelical movement who are pushing the idea that God's not angry with you when you sin, Don't read this and understand exactly why separation is so important. Why extending your days upon this Earth by following God's commandments is so necessary. That a man who is righteous can end up backsliding into sin, even sin unto death like adultery. God, like a parent takes no pleasure in the punishment of the wicked. But that doesn't mean He won't engage in it.

It's important in understanding this particular prophecy of God that this is not about salvation, it is about life on this earth, and soul in this sense means the person. Spirit and body together form a soul. Now with that understanding, let us consider the opening verse. What mean ye, that ye use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge? The saying refers to the idea that the children of Israel are claiming that God is judging unfairly by punishing them for what their parents did. What their immediate forefathers got up to. That they ate sour grapes but it's the children whose teeth are on edge. It's important to keep this chapter of Ezekiel in mind when we're looking at the boomer question. God judges us fairly on this earth, saved or unsaved. We may suffer from the sins of a father, but our own inequities are what we are punished with. Just as a just man may have an unjust son, so too can an unjust man have a just son. It is the keeping of the statutes and doctrines of God that prolongs ones life and brings blessings to it. It is being mired in sin that brings ruin and physical death, regardless of your faith in Christ. If anything you're chastised even more so as a child of God. So while it is well and good to point out the sins of the father, that we may learn from them and not do them, we can't blame our troubles on God punishing us for our father's sake. It's entirely up to us to forge ahead in a righteous life. Basically, people need to understand; the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him. You have no one to blame but yourself. No matter how wicked your father or mother may have been, your life on this earth, and eternal life to come is entirely up to us.

A lamentation, a song of mourning, given for the princes of Israel, the kings of Judah, sons of David. For Jehoahaz and Jehoiachin. Jehoahaz was taken to Egypt. Jehoiachin was taken to Babylon. Woe to them, and the people who now are subject to their captors. Woe to Jerusalem. When the Northern Kingdom split from the line of David in 931 BC, when Jeroboam’s reign begins in 1 Kings 12, it is important to note they falsely called themselves "Israel" too. They rejected the covenant and the anointing and the religion of their fathers. The same as today. It is amazing that God uses the Northern Kingdom of Israel in the Old Testament to represent both the apostate nation calling itself Israel today, and the apostate false religion of Catholicism.

And so, in the 7th year of Babylonian occupation and captivity, in the 5th month and tenth day, the elders of Israel come to Ezekiel to enquire the Lord. Jeremiah 52:12-13 Now in the fifth month, in the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, which served the king of Babylon, into Jerusalem, And burned the house of the Lord, and the king's house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, and all the houses of the great men, burned he with fire: The burning of Jerusalem and destruction of the temple occurs in what most agree, the 11th year of captivity (19 years after Nebuchadnezzar began to rule Babylon). 4 years to the day after this meeting in Ezekiel 20. Keep this in mind as we go. They inquire of the Lord, but God says He is not to be enquired of by them. Instead, He says to judge them, to hold forth in the word of God against them. To preach hard against their sin. Many people today claim to "want to know God's will for their lives," and say they are seeking truth, but they flee from hard preaching from the word of God against their sin. Right here we see that God has no interest in being enquired of when your heart isn't right. God says to cause them to know the abominations of their fathers. We know from Ezekiel 18 that the Lord doesn't hold the sons responsible for the sins of the father, so what is the purpose? As we read we see it is to condemn them for their own. Much like Jesus rebuking the Jews; Matthew 23:29-32 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets. Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets. Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers. And so, God lays out the dispensations of man; from the day He lifted up his hand, revealing to them in the land of Egypt, to His bringing them forth, to His gift of the promised land, all to proclaim that He would be their God. And He commanded them to cast away their idols and false gods. The abominations among them, yet they would not. But He spared them from being wiped out utterly in the midst of Canaan, for His name's sake after Moses appeal to the Lord; Exodus 32:11-12 And Moses besought the Lord his God, and said, Lord, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains, and to consume them from the face of the earth? Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people. But, God lifted His hand that the parents who sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play, who believed the 10 bad spies and not Caleb and Joshua, that they would not enter into the land. But, He said to their children Walk ye not in the statutes of your fathers, neither observe their judgments, nor defile yourselves with their idols, to keep His statutes, His judgments; the law. And keep the ordinances and Sabbaths, as a sign that they may know He is the Lord our God. But they rebelled too. And He did not utterly destroy them, again for His name's sake among the heathen. And so He scattered them, the northern kingdom, among all the heathen countries, because they consistently went after their fathers' idols and committed their fathers' abominations. Centuries of rebellion, generation after generation. With God's wrath kindled, but sparing them destruction for His name's sake. Jesus Christ. This cycle continued, and in Judah as well. Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live. He gave them over to strong delusion, that they may believe a lie. He allowed them to see what happens when they trusted their own foolish hearts that were darkened. Romans 1:21-25 Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. They went to the high places, Bamah in Hebrew, instead of the mount of the Lord, the Temple of Zion in Jerusalem. They worshiped idols in His name and offered sacrifice to them, and ultimately passed their own sons through the fire to Baal. Even those that sat down to enquire of the Lord this day. Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers? and commit ye whoredom after their abominations? God pleads with them as He did with their fathers, that His word against them would prick them in their hardened hearts. That they turn from the sins of their father to embrace the truth of the Lord God. To that end, He says He will put them to the rod. And destruction and desolation. That He will purge the unrighteous from among them. But if they repented not, so be it. The Lord asks one thing of them, stop doing their gifts and offerings and abominations to their idols in HIS holy name. For in mine holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel, saith the Lord God, there shall all the house of Israel, all of them in the land, serve me: there will I accept them, and there will I require your offerings, and the firstfruits of your oblations, with all your holy things. This isn't only the restoration of Jerusalem after the captivity. But a prophecy of what would come. This is the Kingdom of Heaven. This is the holy reign of Christ. This is the final assembly of believers, who will be sanctified before the heathen for His holy name, Jesus. And we shall know that He is the Lord. Finally, the chapter ends with another prophecy; Moreover the word of the Lord came unto me, saying, Son of man, set thy face toward the south, and drop thy word toward the south, and prophesy against the forest of the south field...Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I will kindle a fire in thee, and it shall devour every green tree in thee, and every dry tree: the flaming flame shall not be quenched, and all faces from the south to the north shall be burned therein. And all flesh shall see that I the Lord have kindled it: it shall not be quenched. There, in the fifth month, the tenth day of the month, in the 7th year of captivity, the word of the Lord, Ezekiel in the Spirit, says the South shall be burned with fiery flames. And the elders of Israel gathered there that day ask, "Is this a parable?" They assume it is figurative. That it is some kind of figure. In a few short years, on the anniversary of this date, they will see that He is the Lord God as Jerusalem burns. With all the talk about "legalism" and preaching against standards, and calling "the old paths" divisive, you have to wonder if the compromisers actually read chapters like Ezekiel 20. The children of Israel continually left His statutes, and His judgments, which if a man do, he shall even live in them - old paths that He gave them, that they might know that He is the Lord that sanctified them. They compromised. They said to themselves "Why offer at the temple? We have high places. We can give our sweet savor to this idol in His name. We can keep our own sabbaths, not His." And so each generation filled themselves up with the measure of their fathers, and rejected more and more the path of the Lord. The people compromising today, claiming to be doing the will of God by telling people to not worry about keeping the law, that it be well with them. To not have moral standards and behavior. They are a stubborn and rebellious people. And you'll note that God eventually will give them up to their own delusions. To allow them to go on down the road to perdition. If they don't hear His voice and see the value in His statutes, then He eventually will leave them to wallow in that mire. To return to their vomit. And the fiery flames will consume them. Something I have posted about frequently, but bears repeating again in the context of the prophets, and even here in Ezekiel 20, notice that the commandments of God, His statutes and judgments aren't held over the people as punishment or "just because I say so," but that it be well with us, that we dwell long in the land, that it is a sign unto us that we are His people and He is our Lord. That we may know He is God. It's always given as a positive thing for us. Wisdom. Knowledge. All come from fear of the Lord and to the best of our fleshly abilities, walking in His judgment. The old paths. Neither turning to the Left or the Right. People claiming to be saved Christians who still see the law as something grievous, as something we don't need, well they sound like Satan in the garden. A murderer from the first. Who hated Adam and Eve, and wanted them to fall and die just as he was condemned himself. Shame on saved pastors denying the blessing of the law to their flock. Be ye holy as He is holy.

Again, the word of the Lord comes upon the prophet, and again to preach against Jerusalem, and all Israel that remained there, that the sword was come to slay them for their sin, and captivity to separate the righteous from the wicked. It sure seems like God was cursing Israel. The sword would come in three waves. And along with Judah, the Babylonians would wipe out the Ammonites in their land. The princes of Jerusalem, the Davidic line would be have their crown removed, the diadem taken and it shall be no more until he come whose right it is; and I will give it him. Amen It is interesting to note that the Babylonians were at the crossroads between Judah and Amon, and we're using divination, the reading of organs like the liver of an animal, to determine which way to go. God says he would give them a false divination, that they do His will. When we have a decision to make, and we consult any other source but God, understand that He may well give you a false divination, allow bad advice or words that tickles your itching ear, to give you what you want, and plenty of it. Or to be used for His purpose, but your own destruction. Seek ye first the Kingdom of God. Start in His word and in prayer. Delight yourself in the word of the Lord. Know His ways. Then enter into prayer, understanding that His grace is sufficient. Content with whatever His will may be. Then will He give you what you need. It may not be what your heart wants, but it will be what serves Him.

Leviticus 20 And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying, 2 Again, thou shalt say to the children of Israel, Whosoever he be of the children of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn in Israel, that giveth any of his seed unto Molech; he shall surely be put to death: the people of the land shall stone him with stones. 3 And I will set my face against that man, and will cut him off from among his people; because he hath given of his seed unto Molech, to defile my sanctuary, and to profane my holy name. 4 And if the people of the land do any ways hide their eyes from the man, when he giveth of his seed unto Molech, and kill him not: 5 Then I will set my face against that man, and against his family, and will cut him off, and all that go a whoring after him, to commit whoredom with Molech, from among their people. 6 And the soul that turneth after such as have familiar spirits, and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, I will even set my face against that soul, and will cut him off from among his people. 7 Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy: for I am the Lord your God. 8 And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am the Lord which sanctify you. 9 For every one that curseth his father or his mother shall be surely put to death: he hath cursed his father or his mother; his blood shall be upon him. 10 And the man that committeth adultery with another man's wife, even he that committeth adultery with his neighbour's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death. 11 And the man that lieth with his father's wife hath uncovered his father's nakedness: both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them. 12 And if a man lie with his daughter in law, both of them shall surely be put to death: they have wrought confusion; their blood shall be upon them. 13 If a man also lie with mankind, as he lieth with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them. 14 And if a man take a wife and her mother, it is wickedness: they shall be burnt with fire, both he and they; that there be no wickedness among you. 15 And if a man lie with a beast, he shall surely be put to death: and ye shall slay the beast. 16 And if a woman approach unto any beast, and lie down thereto, thou shalt kill the woman, and the beast: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them. 17 And if a man shall take his sister, his father's daughter, or his mother's daughter, and see her nakedness, and she see his nakedness; it is a wicked thing; and they shall be cut off in the sight of their people: he hath uncovered his sister's nakedness; he shall bear his iniquity. 18 And if a man shall lie with a woman having her sickness, and shall uncover her nakedness; he hath discovered her fountain, and she hath uncovered the fountain of her blood: and both of them shall be cut off from among their people. 19 And thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy mother's sister, nor of thy father's sister: for he uncovereth his near kin: they shall bear their iniquity. 20 And if a man shall lie with his uncle's wife, he hath uncovered his uncle's nakedness: they shall bear their sin; they shall die childless. 21 And if a man shall take his brother's wife, it is an unclean thing: he hath uncovered his brother's nakedness; they shall be childless. 22 Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all my judgments, and do them: that the land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out. 23 And ye shall not walk in the manners of the nation, which I cast out before you: for they committed all these things, and therefore I abhorred them. 24 But I have said unto you, Ye shall inherit their land, and I will give it unto you to possess it, a land that floweth with milk and honey: I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from other people. 25 Ye shall therefore put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean: and ye shall not make your souls abominable by beast, or by fowl, or by any manner of living thing that creepeth on the ground, which I have separated from you as unclean. 26 And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine. 27 A man also or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, shall surely be put to death: they shall stone them with stones: their blood shall be upon them. We see here in the preaching against Jerusalem, where the Lord demands the prophet tell the Jews of their abominations and His judgment, that much of it mirrors those things given to Moses in the wilderness. The things God proclaimed should be dealt with by death. That the blood be upon the wicked and not on the people in the land. But the children of Israel failed to uphold their end of the covenant and now faced the promised judgment. Hebrews 8:7-9 For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I Made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. The longsuffering of God, that nearly 1,000 years passed from Sinai and the law to the utter destruction of Jerusalem, was taken by the people to mean God wasn't present. That He no longer cared. That maybe He wasn't real. His mercy and calls to repentance, ignored. The grace He offers men because of His love, taken advantage of. For greed and lust. And false prophets preaching lies, saying "The Lord has spoken," when He hadn't. And devouring widow's houses and taking advantage of the poor and the fatherless. Matthew 23:13-15 But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves. The Lord looked for the righteous to be the salt that preserves, and found none. Just like in Sodom, where He told Moses if there were found just 10 righteous men, He would spare the cities. And so He promises to gather the wicked and melt them in flame like the molten metals they make their abominations with. For sacrifice in the mountains. For their idolatry, for their shedding of blood. For their degeneracy. Extortion, usury, greed. They have become as dross. Impurities in the silver, cast out. Jeremiah 6:30 Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them. Therefore have I poured out mine indignation upon them; I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath: their own way have I recompensed upon their heads, saith the Lord God. Their own way. God recompenses every man by his works. The wages of sin. Here, in this life, nations are judged. And in the end, every man shall give an account, judged by the book. Thrown into the lake of fire. Burned like dross. Praise God that we have Jesus. That we may avoid that which we deserve. Romans 6:23 For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen!

The word of the Lord gives a scathing sermon against the whoredoms of Israel and Judah. Where some prophecy is more obscure, parables and dark sayings, this is plain and undeniable in its meaning. God is very specific as to what it is all about. The adultery of His people. The fornication in Egypt, that He took them out from. And the adultery of Samaria with Assyria. And the whoredoms of Judah with Babylon, Assyria and Egypt. Their blood is upon them. The wrath abiding to the uttermost. What else is there to say? The judgment is come for their idolatry and lewdness and the blood upon their heads. Their defilement of the holy city and the Tabernacle. And ye shall know I am the Lord God. The current debates over the role of modern Israel, Zionism and dispensationalism in Christianity rests on the idea that the Jews are and always have been God's chosen people. His elect by the law and the covenant. That He would always bless Israel. The false understanding many professing Christians have is that in the Old Testament, Jews were the heroes of the story. That while they had their faults, God never rejected them, and in the New Testament, other than some of their leaders, they still were God's chosen, and so someday, all physical Israel would be saved. It is impossible to read the prophets and come away with the idea that the Jews are generally the good guys. They were always a stiff-necked rebellious people who needed to be punished to do right, and even then rarely repented. Full of complaints. Full of formication and adultery. From Egypt through Babylonian captivity, and beyond. They were continually cursed and spoken against by the word of God.

Again, the prophecy came upon the holy man of God, to preach the destruction that had come upon Jerusalem by the will of the Lord. The first act God has Ezekiel perform, on that specific day, is to burn and render a sacrifice that's left to boil and seethe, the scum not removed and the pot made molten. Thus would they be. He no longer would seek to purify them of their iniquity. It was too late. His judgement had come and they were not going to get another chance. I the Lord have spoken it: it shall come to pass, and I will do it; I will not go back, neither will I spare, neither will I repent; according to thy ways, and according to thy doings, shall they judge thee, saith the Lord God. Then the word of the Lord came unto Ezekiel and tells him the saddest of the prophecies he was asked to perform. The Lord took his wife from him, and Ezekiel is instructed not to mourn, but to dress for travel, his tire, or turban upon his head, his shoes on his feet. Without eating the bread of mourning. No tears or weeping. I am crying for the prophet now. I can't help it. He speaks to the people, and at evening his wife died. And in the morning, he does as he was commanded. What faith and obedience. Heartbreaking obedience to the Lord. And the people ask why, and Ezekiel tells them that they too will lose their spouses, and children and those they care about, and like him, they will be unable to mourn, being led away or fleeing. And those that escape will come to him, and he will not be dumb or silent but a sign unto them that they may know that He is the Lord.

In Ezekiel 25, the Lord proclaims His judgment against the nations surrounding Judah for their sins. The Ammonites are judged for their malicious joy and scornful rejoicing over the destruction of Judah's sanctuary, the desolation of the land, and the captivity of the house of Judah. The Moabites are condemned for saying that the house of Judah is like all other heathen nations, when God had chosen them for His people. Edom is judged for its vengeful actions against the house of Judah, taking revenge with great spite during their calamity and tribulation. The Philistines are judged for their perpetual enmity and vengeful actions against Judah, seeking to destroy it with malice over the generations. The correct attitude when seeing God's wrath upon a people should be introspection, and examination. Especially when it is on people who call themselves by His name. Professing Christians. What do they do that you do? What mistakes can be learned from. Turn towards God in fear. Etc...Are a better reaction. Know that He is the Lord God, and get right. God's judgment is just and perfect. But we aren't. Never lose sight of that.

Isaiah 23:1-4 The burden of Tyre. Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them. Be still, ye inhabitants of the isle; thou whom the merchants of Zidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished.And by great waters the seed of Sihor, the harvest of the river, is her revenue; and she is a mart of nations. Be thou ashamed, O Zidon: for the sea hath spoken, even the strength of the sea, saying, I travail not, nor bring forth children, neither do I nourish up young men, nor bring up virgins. Joel 3:4-6 Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head; Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things: The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border. Amos 1:9-10 Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant: But I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour the palaces thereof. Zechariah 9:2-4 And Hamath also shall border thereby; Tyrus, and Zidon, though it be very wise. And Tyrus did build herself a strong hold, and heaped up silver as the dust, and fine gold as the mire of the streets. Behold, the Lord will cast her out, and he will smite her power in the sea; and she shall be devoured with fire. As in the previous chapter, Ezekiel 26 contains prophecy against another nation, not Israel and Judah. Here, it is the Phoenician land of Tyre, their city of Zidon, in Palestine. The coasts of the Mediterranean. A Semitic people, a great seafaring empire of trade, and who, at many times throughout the history of Israel, were friends and allies. It is likely that there were many believers among them. They helped build Solomon's temple, and provided great ships to increase the king's wealth. In many ways, Tyre serves as a picture of the believing Gentiles of the early Christians, the pillars Jesus builds His church of. Like cedars of Lebanon. And like the gathering of wealth from abroad to bring home to Zion. But here, centuries later as Babylon rises in power, Tyre falls to the wrath of God. Their sin, like the other nations mentioned in chapter 25, include mocking the fate of Judah, its desolation and captivity. Of seeking to take advantage and loot and pillage what's left in Judea. As we see in the other prophets, God's word of judgement was given repeatedly to them, that they had no excuse. We should also note that, while God held Jerusalem and the line of David, His chosen place and lineage to bring about the Christ, the Messiah, He did not focus all of His attentions only on Israel. He is the God of all nations. His will was always that all men come unto Him. Israel itself was meant to be a beacon of light unto the nations. A peculiar people. A royal priesthood. But their failure led to our gain, amen. Ultimately, the covenant with Israel was done away with, and only the new and better testament remains. Salvation in the blood of Jesus. Amen.

Revelation 18:10-19 Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come. And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more: The merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet, and all thyine wood, and all manner vessels of ivory, and all manner vessels of most precious wood, and of brass, and iron, and marble, And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and beasts, and sheep, and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men. And the fruits that thy soul lusted after are departed from thee, and all things which were dainty and goodly are departed from thee, and thou shalt find them no more at all. The merchants of these things, which were made rich by her, shall stand afar off for the fear of her torment, weeping and wailing, And saying, Alas, alas that great city, that was clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold, and precious stones, and pearls! For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off, And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city! And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate. Here in Ezekiel 27 we find the second of three chapters dedicated to the Lord's judgment against Tyre, and the great trading and seafaring Phoenician empire, at the hand of Babylon. Its destruction here echoes the fall of the great Babylon in the end times, an empire of abominations, known for its great trade and merchandise throughout the world. The mourning of those who depended on them seen in similar terms. Throwing dust on their heads. Wailing. Nothing, not riches and ships and political favors with all the kings of the earth, can withstand the wrath when it comes.

Here, in the 11th year of captivity, as dated by the prophet Ezekiel, the word of the Lord continues to speak against Tyre. The great capital of Sidon, or Zidon. The Phoenician shipping empire, just outside of Israel that had for a long time been allies, and trading partners of Israel and Judah. But who in those days were spoiling the desolation left by the Babylonians in the land. God's wrath is both on the people, their nation and the king. Here, roughly 16 years after the elevation of Daniel to the 3rd in command by Nebuchadnezzar, the Lord says he was as wise as Daniel, but his pride in declaring himself God is his downfall. The prophecy continues into a description of the king, whose name is irrelevant as it applies to the entire kingship of Tyre, and compares their fall to Lucifer. Found in Eden, full of beauty and wisdom, the workmanship of musical instruments prepared in him the day he was created; this is Satan. A dual description. It is important to note that Satan was created, and created with beauty, wisdom and purpose. The anointed cherub. Perfect in his ways until iniquity was found in him. Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness: I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee. The kingdom of Tyre was like unto Lucifer. Having access to the Lord through kinship and close contact with Israel. Created for the purpose of helping the kingdom of Israel, and the creation of the temple. But its merchandise eventually corrupted both nations. The nation and king and capital shall fall. Just as the other nations surrounding Judah that are as thorns in the side, shall all fall. And when the Jews returned from captivity, there would be fewer threats. Most would come from Samaria, the former Northern Kingdom of Israel, and the remnant of Moab and Ammonites. But the historical enemies of the Philistines, many Canaanites, Tyre's corruption and the Assyrians, all gone. Judged by God.

Continuing the prophecies against the nations in proximity to Judah, we have in Ezekiel 29 two against the kingdom of Egypt. The first prophecy, in the 10th year, 10th month, 12th day (around 587 BC), was given during the siege of Jerusalem, before its fall in 586 BC (the 11th year by the prophets reckoning, which uses the reign of King Zedekiah as a starting point). This is when Egypt was still a potential player in the region, promising aid to Judah against Babylon. God's anger at the Jews who turned to Egypt for help is found throughout the prophets, particularly Jeremiah. Because Egypt represents the old, unsaved life of Christians, under bondage to sin, we can draw an application here to not turn to the world for help when we are in trouble, but to turn only the the Lord. God says Egypt is like a staff of a reed, the hollow and weak grass that grows by a river. Especially the Nile. That Israel leaned on for support, but it buckles immediately and they bruise their shoulder and put them in the ground. We should look at the world's solutions to our problems the same way. Weak and insufficient, knocking us on our butts when we rely on them. The second prophecy is made 16 years later, (571 BC) and comes after Nebuchadnezzar’s prolonged siege of Tyre (circa 585–572 BC), which was costly and yielded little reward, as Tyre’s island fortress was difficult to conquer, although it destroyed Tyre's power. This later prophecy clarifies that Egypt would be given to Nebuchadnezzar as a “wage” for his efforts against Tyre. The word of God said that Egypt would be scattered and taken into captivity for 40 years, (echoing the 40 years Israel spent in the wilderness) and when it gathered again, it would never be as powerful. This way, when Cyrus gives the go-ahead to the Jews to rebuild Jerusalem, there's no temptation to lean again on Egypt. In your Christian walk, this sort of thing may happen, where the supports you have among friends, family, alcohol and drugs, old habits and lifestyles, even hobbies and activities, may be taken from you for a season, long enough to not be available to you for support or shelter, and if they ever come back around, their weakness is obvious. You cannot count on them. It is the Lord only we can depend on. Amen. We see in the prophets that there was a timeline given, specific events and kingdoms would come to be exactly as God said. That we may know He is the Lord. Nations that God said would never recover, didn't. Egypt was never a power again. Assyria was gone. Babylon never rebuilt. Etc... In that process, we also see how events put in motion the very things that led to the future prophecy of Medo-Persians, Alexander the Great, the Hellenistic and Ptolemy kingdoms, and ultimately Rome for the time of Christ. The fulfillment of Ezekiel’s prophecies, with Babylon and later Persia, weakening key Middle Eastern and African nations, created favorable conditions for Alexander’s rapid conquests by reducing any resistance. This, in turn, set the stage for Rome by leaving a fragmented, Hellenistic world that Rome could easily conquer and absorb. While Ezekiel’s focus is divine judgment, the historical outcomes align with the prophesied decline of these nations, directly shaping the things yet to come. It isn't just God calling His shots, it is how God uses all things to His will. Stepping back and seeing the overall picture, measured in centuries, it is hard not to see, that we may know that He is the Lord.

As God promised, Egypt is made the basest of kingdoms, and is brought low. Its allies, like broken arms, unable to hold a sword. Pharaoh is destroyed. The kings they would have by this name were weaker and weaker. Persia would rule, then Greeks. The people scattered. Babylon triumphant over the nations of Egypt's strength. And they shall know that He is the Lord. God certainly wanted to prove that He is Lord God over all to the heathens. Planting seeds that would bear fruit as the gospel was preached. His wrath revealed from Heaven, that no men have an excuse.

God's message to Pharaoh, showing the Egyptian king the power of God against Assyria, is a pretty apt message for the 4th of July. What other nation has been made as fair than America? It has shot up like the cedars, its roots by great waters. He hath shot up his top among the thick boughs, and his heart is lifted up in his height. This message is fitting and will come to pass on this nation. When is entirely up to saved believers. We are the salt of the earth, but so many have lost their savour. Good for nothing but being trampled underfoot. Churches that don't preach the gospel, pastors that don't preach the whole word of God. Members who don't go soul-winning. Who live like the world in all they do. Zero separation unto the things of God. If the uncircumcised nations of heathens fell, if Israel was destroyed for their iniquity, imagine how much greater America's fall will be. It will be biblical. Alas, alas that great city, that was clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold, and precious stones, and pearls! For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off, And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city! And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate. Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her. God bless America.

The word of the Lord against the nations comes to an end with lamentation for the King of Egypt, and her people, and those of the other nations upon whom God's judgment had come. A picture of the day of the Lord and the wrath poured out on the unbelieving, the uncircumcised cast down to the pit. And when I shall put thee out, I will cover the heaven, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light. All the bright lights of heaven will I make dark over thee, and set darkness upon thy land, saith the Lord God. Familiar language. Prophetic for us. History for Egypt and the others. In Ezekiel 32, God pronounces judgments against several nations, referring to them by their patriarchal names, descendants of Shem and Japheth, with Babylon as the instrument of judgment. Asshur is there and all her company: his graves are about him: all of them slain, fallen by the sword. These are the Assyrians, of Shem, who God says their graves line the pit, fallen by the sword. Elam (from Shem), a land between Israel and modern Iran, Meshech and Tubal (from Japheth), corresponding to tribes in Asia Minor, in what is now Turkey; Edom (from Shem through Esau), the nation south of Judah; Zidon, or Tyre (Sidon, from Ham through Canaan), the Phoenician city-state in modern Lebanon; and the princes of the north, likely referring to various northern tribes or city-states, remnants of Hittite or other groups in Syria or Asia Minor. These nations faced divine judgment for their actions against Israel over the centuries, with Babylon as the executing power of God. I believe in the end times, when the spirit of Babylon comes upon that one world government, and the second horseman rides, bringing war. And similar destruction will fall upon similar nations. A copy of this Old Testament judgment, led by the beast. Acting as Babylon. But regardless, the truth is the end of an era had come for the region. Kingdoms fell. World empires grew, and the spirit of Babylon continues. Right until the end of days. Amen

Acts 20:31-32 Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears. And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified. Acts 20:25-26 And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more. Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men. Ezekiel 33 contains a lot of doctrine, and is one of the most often cited chapters of the prophet. Due to time and density, I will break it down over a few days. The Parable of the Watchman is told in verses 1-9, and the idea of being a watchman, warning for danger is given, a trope used earlier in Ezekiel 3; If you recall, God appoints Ezekiel as a watchman for the house of Israel, instructing him to warn the people of God’s judgment. If Ezekiel warns the wicked and they do not turn, their blood is on their own heads. If he fails to warn them, their blood is on his hands. Ezekiel 3:17 Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. Here, in Ezekiel 33, the word of the Lord establishes this be understood to all the watchmen appointed to warn of the impending judgment, coming in the form of Babylon. The sword which is coming against Judah for her sin. A good watchman sounds the trumpet, notifying the people of danger, and should they not heed it, the watchman is free from their blood. But if the watchman doesn't sound the horn, he carries the blood of all those he could have warned. In the days of siege warfare and raids, this was serious stuff. And again, in OT days, quite literal. In the New Testament we are given these parables and stories for our own admonition and to teach us spiritual things, as Paul's application in Acts shows us, warning others about death and Hell, the coming judgment, removes their blood from our heads. Soul-winning, or rather soul warning, is a responsibility for all saved Christians. That whenever we have the opportunity, we should be sounding the alarm. Blowing the trumpet. Warning others of the danger of an unregenerate life. Paul says he has done this, and is pure of the blood of all men. When we miss opportunity to warn others, to share the gospel, we are like the watchman who fails to sound the alarm. Derelict Christians. And those who we could have warned and didn't, God says his blood will I require at the watchman's hand. When we go out into the highways and hedges to compel others to come to the Lord, or tell our friends and family about eternal life and damnation, we cannot force them to accept the invitation. That is between the Spirit and them. But we can and must warn them. I know it weighs heavy on my heart the number of people I have passed on giving the gospel too. The regret of hearing someone you know died, that you never warned. Feeling that blood on your head. I think every Christian, even babes in Christ, have had this feeling. "Oh, how I wish I had warned them!" is a common lament. How much more then should we feel that burden when we don't go soul-winning? When given a church, an opportunity to door knock, and we don't go? It's one thing to wake to a fire in your own house, and warn your family to flee. But if you passed the home of strangers, and saw a fire spreading, wouldn't you bang on the door to get them to evacuate? Or would you pass on by, leaving them to burn? We cannot reach everyone. It would be difficult to quit our jobs, abandon our family and make evangelizing the world out only purpose. But everyone can spare a few hours a week to go soul-winning. If you aren't part of a church, join one, even if it is for this sole purpose. Organized door knocking is more profitable, and having a place to send the souls won to be taught all things and be baptized is crucial. If you go to church, and they don't have soul-winning, ask the pastor to start a program. Offer to organize it. There are faithful people who would make excellent watchmen, sitting on the sidelines for lack of a program. Warn souls. Be pure of the blood of all men. Following the parable of the watchmen, Ezekiel preaches a message to the people; repent and be saved. The prophet preaches that if the righteous do wicked, are backslidden and not right with God, they will perish in the judgment of Judah.
