But if the wicked turn to God, restore their pledges and right their wrongs and walk in His statutes, they are forgiven. He shall not die during their tribulation. Yet the children of thy people say, The way of the Lord is not equal. Man says it isn't fair that the wicked be saved by getting right, and their sins are no longer held against them, when their righteousness is forgotten with every sin. They say the Lord's judgment isn't fair. O ye house of Israel, I will judge you every one after his ways. God's mercy on the sinner who repents isn't fair, it is grace. We all deserve worse. That Him for His grace. The righteous sin, and think they are better than the wicked who sinned and gets right. This hypocritical judgment is iniquity. It's one of the things God hates the most. This portion of Ezekiel 33 is about physical salvation, with a spiritual picture for us today. Many make the entire message spiritual, and apply this to salvation, that you can lose salvation or that we must turn from our sins to be saved. But the context is the physical destruction of Jerusalem and her people. The spiritual and practical application for believers is that we are His people, as saved Christians. We are Israel. And so, in this life, God will withhold His wrath and chastening to those believers who, however backslidden, come back to the statutes of life; the commandments. The way of the Lord. While God's wrath is kindled against the backslidden believer who sins, despite their past righteousness. In practical terms; if you are now living in sin - fornicating, lying, defrauding others, violent, hypocritical, covetous, worldly...or not in prayer, not reading your Bible, not attending church or soul-winning, it does not matter what works of righteousness you were doing before. They don't buy you a pass. You can't coast on "Well, I used to go to church and I used to go soul-winning. I did it for years!" If you've stopped, you aren't right with God. And if a greater sinner than you ever were, who never did those things in their life, starts today, they are more right with God than you. And if you don't think that's fair, you are committing inequity. You are no different than the people who said the way of the Lord is not equal, who were destroyed by the Babylonians. Again, this applies to chastening of believers. We are saved by grace through faith, not of ourselves. It is a gift of God. But the blessings of this world come when you are right with God. And He withdraws His protection when those who call themselves by His name don't walk in His ways. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. If you aren't right, get right. Life is but a vapour. The time is now. Don't rest on your laurels, but press forward for the mark of a triumphant Christian life. And shame on pussyfooting pastors who scratch itching ears, to tell their flock that the statutes of life aren't for them. That God isn't mad at them, saying "sin so grace may abound!" God's law is there that it be well with us on the earth. Not to put us in bonds, but to free us. To save us from destruction. To keep our paths straight. A light before our feet. Shame on those that try to take our eyes from that light and to leave that path. Ezekiel 33 concludes, the destruction of Jerusalem has happened. One who escaped comes to the prophet in the evening and tells him, but the hand of God keeps Ezekiel from responding until the morning came, and he was no longer struck dumb. And he receives the word of God. The Lord says that those from the wastes and wilderness of Judah, who escaped out of the desolation of Jerusalem speak, saying that because Abraham was one, and was promised land, that they being many deserve the inheritance. This is the argument made by Jews today. The basis of Zionism. The false doctrine that because they are children of the law, and many, the promise of the land given Abraham should apply even more so to them. Matthew 3:9 And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. The promises and inheritance was never given a people because of who they were. But by the condition of what they did. A condition repeatedly given. Exodus 19:5 Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine Hebrews 8:7-9 For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord. The word of the Lord upon Ezekiel stresses these same points. They are filled with violence and Idolatry and adultery and abominations. For this, God says He will lay the land most desolate because of their abominations. Then they shall know He is the Lord. Finally, the Lord brings to Ezekiel's attention those that were listening to his preaching, who gathered in their doorways to hear him whenever he spoke. Who called others to hear the burden of God placed on the prophet. The Lord says, they come and listen but do not do what is told them. For with their mouth they show much love, but their heart is full of covetousness. Isaiah 29:13 Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me... Matthew 15:8 This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. God compares their vain pleasure im hearing the word of God preached to those listening to a song. It's got a good beat, and the singer is talented, but it has no deeper meaning than that for them. How many professing Christians, even in solid fundamental churches, are there just to enjoy the show? For the ambiance and the vibe? How many Sunday morning-glories show up to a service, check the box, hear the word, and let it drip off them like water off a duck? The Bible says in James 1:22-25 But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves. For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was. But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed. Are you like those that attended Ezekiel's preaching, but took nothing from it? Whose hearts continued in covetousness? Like those who play church and see it as a social occasion, and aren't transformed by the hearing of the word? Spending time with God's word should change you. We should have ready hearts and open ears and not just be there for the fellowship. But to be a doer of the work, that we may be blessed. But when destruction comes to pass, (and lo, it will come), they shall know that a prophet has been among them. That the word of God is true. But they will be caught sleeping. Unprofitable servants. It will come as a thief in the night, and they will not be prepared. Ready your hearts and be attentive listeners and doers. Amen

Psalm 23 The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. 2 He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. 3 He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake. 4 Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me. 5 Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. 6 Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever. John 10:11-18 I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep. But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth: and the wolf catcheth them, and scattereth the sheep. The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep. I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine. As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again. No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father. Jesus is the promised Shepherd. He maketh us lie down in green pastures. He searches out for the lost. He heals us he feeds us and watches over us from our enemies. He judges the other cattle for their treatment of his sheep and the pasture that he had given them and the waters he had provided them. Notice here in Ezekiel 34, which begins the hopeful prophecies of Salvation in the last part of the book, that the Lord says Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out. He uses this assurance a few times. When Jesus says I am the Good Shepherd, He is directly stating that he is the Lord. Further down, we see even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd. Just as Jesus is the Son of God, He is a son of David. And there are sheep of other folds that he brings in and makes us one fold. This is the promise. It is not to Jews after the flesh. It is not to a physical nation of Israel. Although certainly the fold has sheep from among them. But the bad shepherds are the religious leaders, false prophets and wayward priests of Israel. And further the Lord says he will judge His flock, and cattle with cattle, these are the physical Jews, after the flesh. He's clearly delineating between believers and unbelievers. Between His sheep who hear His voice and those that trample down the fields and pollute the waters. The promise of eternal peace, safety and security, freedom from attack of enemies without and corruption from within, is all given to His flock. The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. Amen This is a good proof text against those who claim that Jesus never called himself God or declared that He is the Lord. It's a good proof text against Zionism and the idea that Jews have a special dispensation given them. It's a good proof text that the prophets all spoke of Christ. Keep Ezekiel 34 in your repertoire.

It wouldn't be a prophetic book without the judgment against Edom. Mount Seir. Idumea. The nation of Esau. We know the story of Jacob, coming subtly to his father Isaac and posing as Esau, received the blessing reserved for the first born by trickery. And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father. And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing. And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me? Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck. And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him While Edom the man reconciled with his brother, Israel, the people of his nation had an antagonistic relationship with the children of Israel. Refusing them in their time in the wilderness, and often taking up the sword against Israel, their cousins. Malachi 1:1-4 The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by Malachi. I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever. And by this judgment, Judah was to know that the Lord repays. His judgments against those that come against us as His children will happen. It is assured.

Reading through Ezekiel 36 and 37, and remembering that Hal Lindsey used these chapters as the basis for his hyper dispensationalist Zionist writings in the 1970s. He had a very popular book that absolutely tainted the discussion around end times Bible prophecy, even after his predictions failed to occur. Hal Lindsey, in The Late Great Planet Earth (1970) and later works, made several specific end-times predictions that failed to materialize. He suggested the rapture might occur in 1988, 40 years after Israel’s 1948 founding, based on his reading of Matthew 24:34, but no such event happened. He predicted the Soviet Union, as “Gog” from Ezekiel 38-39, would invade Israel, which never occurred before the USSR’s 1991 collapse. Lindsey also linked the European Economic Community, a precursor to the EU, to a revived Roman Empire led by the Antichrist, but the EEC’s evolution into the EU didn’t align with his vision. Because the eec had at one time, 10 Nations, he claimed it was the ten horns found in Revelation. He foresaw a 200-million-man Chinese army attacking Israel (Revelation 9:16), which never materialized, and a rebuilt Jerusalem Temple, which remains unconstructed. These unfulfilled predictions, tied to 1970s geopolitical fears, drew criticism for their speculative nature and weakened Lindsey’s credibility among some evangelicals. The popularity of the book, which sold over 30 million copies, cemented many of the key ideas into the public consciousness. Having prophesied against Israel, throughout Judah and earning of their coming judgment, and having prophesied against the heathen nations that surround them for laughing at their calamity, saying "Aha!" and seeking to take advantage of the situation, God's word upon Ezekiel begins to shift towards prophecy of restoration and redemption in the future. Preaching to the mountains, to the desolate land filled with wastes, the Lord says He will fill up the land, increase the people, the corn, the beasts, and make the desolate overflow. To bring back to life that which was dead. That all will know, He is the Lord. Dual meaning here, that is the promise of restoring Jerusalem after the Babylonian captivity, and as we will see, a future restoration of His people Israel, under a new covenant and promise. First we should note, it is not because of the Jews that God would restore them from captivity; But I had pity for mine holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the heathen, whither they went. Therefore say unto the house of Israel, thus saith the Lord God; I do not this for your sakes, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went. Just as we have seen elsewhere, it is always His holy name and the city where He chose to place it. Not the people. God is doing this despite their ways, because they caused His holy name to be blasphemed among the heathen. Sometimes we are blessed openly, not because we deserve it, but because our sins have given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme Him. Sometimes we are blessed simply to sanctify His name. The second half of Ezekiel 36 drifts into end times prophecy. A new promise, which we have seen made elsewhere, where He will give a new heart, and a new spirit within the people, and His Spirit within, and cause us by the law in our hearts to walk in His statutes, and to keep His commandments. To dwell in the land of the fathers. And ye shall be My people, and I will be your God. Jeremiah 31:31-34 Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they brake, although I was an husband unto them, saith the Lord: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the Lord, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people. And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the Lord: for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more. Hebrews 10:16-17 This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them; And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more. This promise is fulfilled in Christ. This is not fulfilled by the UN creating the modern state of Israel. They have not gotten a new heart. They have not accepted Christ. Their desolation has not become like the garden of Eden. They are not ashamed and confounded, remembering their sin, loathing themselves for their iniquity. This promise of restoration is done to the Israel of God, both OT and NT believers, in the end times. Not unbelieving Jews today.

We are in Ezekiel 37, perhaps the most well known passage in the prophetic book, and the preaching of the valley of dry bones. Them bones, them bones, them dry bones. It is one of the clearest prophecies of the resurrection and millennial kingdom of believers in the Old Testament. In the second part of the chapter, He has the prophet show two sticks to the people, one Judah, the other Ephraim, or Israel, the Northern Kingdom, and they are miraculously joined in the prophet's hand. Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel. And ye shall know that I am the Lord, when I have opened your graves, O my people, and brought you up out of your graves, And shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live. Not only shall the graves give up their dead, and risen bodies be made whole, and the winds from the four corners give life, but God says He shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live, and be ruled over as one nation, the Israel of God, under David, my servant - Christ Jesus. Many dispensationalists today will claim this is a prophecy for "the Jews." God says no, He will gather all the people to their land. They will say this was fulfilled in 1948. John Hagee and Hal Lindsey and other famous dispensationalist Zionists have pushed this idea, repeatedly in their efforts to pervert Christian judgment regarding the modern state claiming to be Israel. They teach that Ezekiel 37 and the valley of dry bones prophecy refers to the restoration of Israel in 1948, and falsely interprets the vision as a symbolic representation of the "Jewish people's return to their land after centuries of exile." In this view, the dry bones coming to life signify the physical and national rebirth of Israel, with the reestablishment of the state in 1948 seen as a fulfillment of "God's promise." One of the most wicked aspects of dispensationalism is that it gives holy promises to believers to unbelieving Jews. It makes firm promises into vague and dark sayings, to justify their false teachings. The literal resurrection is promised. The Spirit of God indwelling us. The Kingdom of Christ, ruled by Jesus. Not godless antichrists, who reject Him. We will be joined as one Kingdom, the Israel of God, made up of believers from Adam through the final Christian saved before the day of the Lord comes. This is a promise to those of us in the New Testament, as much as it was to believers in Ezekiel's day. Amen

Revelation 20:1-10 And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season. And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection. Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years. And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog, and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them. And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever. Here in Ezekiel 38, the prophet is given the vision of Gog, and Magog which is reflected in John's Revelation of Jesus Christ, chapter 20. They both are the same prophecy, describing the same future event. A lot of people get confused about Gog and Magog. There is a lot of eschatology and charts and predictions about who these are and what it means in current times. God is not the author of confusion. In the previous chapter Ezekiel prophesied about the coming millennial Kingdom. The resurrection of them dry bones and a restoration of Zion, and that beloved city, under the reign of Christ, the Son of David. Jesus ruling and reigning. Note the setting, after many days, in the later years. The mountains of Israel that had been waste, is dwelling safely those brought forth from many nations, God's people of Israel. And these nations will have an evil thought, and seek to spoil the camp of the saints. Cities without walls. The redeemed of God living peacefully. Satan deceiving the heathen to go against Jesus and His saints. To spoil us. This will be a day of wrath and the armies of innumerable people will be destroyed by fire and other supernatural means. And the Lord will be sanctified by these events. There is no dual fulfilment here. This is a future event that has no happened. The nations of Japheth and Ham mentioned fall on both sides. It's not ethnic, there's people of all nations in Jerusalem and in the armies of Gog. We don't know what the maps will look like in the millennial Kingdom. We don't know how that will shake out, over the 1,000 years of Christ ruling with a rod of iron, and we who are saved His priests. It isn't difficult to understand as long as you're willing to accept this is a literal future event. And Gog and Magog are armies of the world, not one or two nations that fit some current geopolitical theories. During the 1940s to 1990s, various theories emerged about the identities of Gog and Magog, often reflecting the geopolitical climate of the time. In the 1940s, some Christians associated Gog and Magog with Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan, tying them to their roles as aggressors in World War II. From the 1950s through the 1980s, it became popular in evangelical circles to identify Gog as the Soviet Union and Magog as its satellite states or China, driven by Cold War fears of communism. In the 1980s, Ronald Reagan and New Christian Right leaders specifically linked Gog to the Soviet Union, emphasizing its communistic and atheistic nature. Following the Soviet Union's collapse in the 1990s, some speculated Gog and Magog could represent Russia and allies like Iran, influenced by Middle Eastern conflicts. By the late 1990s, George W. Bush connected Gog to Iraq, citing biblical prophecy especially post-9/11. These interpretations consistently mapped biblical figures onto contemporary geopolitical rivals, ignoring the timing given in scripture. They would conflate the battle of Armageddon that comes at the return of Christ on the day of the Lord, at the beginning of wrath and before the Millennium, with the events described here, which occurs afterwards. Handy to blame your current enemies as the enemies of God. But it isn't cut and dry and it is not possible to prove who makes up the final army of Satan when we're are always more than 1,000 years away from it happening. Of course this confusion and political opportunism in end times Bible prophecy gained more and more traction with the adoption of dispensationalism and Zionism, post 1948. Where the Jews being given Israel by the UN was seen as the fulfillment of the dry bones prophecy (it wasn't). Then they would just conflate Armageddon and Gog and Magog and make whoever the Jews were against into these armies of the beast. They had to confuse the timing of every event on God's prophetic calendar to do this. They had to make the simple understanding of the times and seasons into a complex group of theories with charts and maps and every other thing but the word of God. And as their theories and set dates failed their proponents, it didn't matter because their lies crept into the vernacular, and infected the conversation. As I posted about the other day, Hal Lindsey's failed doomsday predictions didn't stop his twisted views from taking hold, lingering till today.

Revelation 19:17-20 And I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the fowls that fly in the midst of heaven, Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God; That ye may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of captains, and the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses, and of them that sit on them, and the flesh of all men, both free and bond, both small and great. And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him that sat on the horse, and against his army. And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone. The end time events continue to be prophesied, and while the same events seem to be portrayed, it seems that the post-millennial battle of Gog and Magog in Revelation 20 is described in Ezekiel 38, while today's reading of Ezekiel 39 more closely aligns with the pre-millennial battle of Armageddon. This likely has caused the confusion many have regarding the timing, but as Fundamentalists, we should always defer to the NT reading, as offering greater clarity. Either way, it's a slaughter by the supernatural means of God. A feast for the carrion birds. A promise of God's judgment and justice. Getting commentary support for the Fundamentalist view that the New Testament clarifies prophecy that the Old Testament saw through a glass darkly, is difficult because most commentaries and writing on Ezekiel 38-39 is dispensational. And they all see it through the lens of modern Israel and Zionism. Matthew Henry (1662–1714), A non-dispensational premillennialist, views Ezekiel 38–39 as a unified prophecy of a future attack on God’s people, defeated by divine intervention. But he saw the New Testament, particularly Revelation, as clarifying its eschatological significance. He connects Ezekiel 39:17–20 (birds’ feast) to Revelation 19:17–21 (pre-millennial battle) and Ezekiel 38’s Gog-Magog to Revelation 20:7–10 (post-millennial rebellion), but treats Ezekiel 38–39 as a single prophecy. James Burton Coffman (1905–2006), a premillennialist with non-dispensational leanings, Coffman interprets Ezekiel 38–39 as a single “world-judgment” prophecy, with Revelation providing clarity. He aligns Ezekiel 39:17–20 with Revelation 19:17–18 (pre-millennial battle) and notes Ezekiel 38’s Gog-Magog terminology resembles Revelation 20:7–10 (post-millennial rebellion). While not explicitly arguing for two events or a reversed order, he suggests Ezekiel's prophecy conflates imagery that Revelation properly separates into pre- and post-millennial battles. What we should take away from this is it is ok to not know, and trust God's word. The dispensationalist view is that the OT prophecy is entirely about Tribulation, where Revelation 20 is an entirely different battle. But this is Jew-focused understanding, to say Gog and Magog will invade Israel before the wrath, that it is current and geopolitical, and imminent. Then, there's another opinion, that Gog and Magog of Ezekiel 38-39 is entirely the same as the post-millenial battle of Revelation 20, with added details. The 7 years of burying bodies and burning weapons happens between the defeat of their armies and the casting of Satan into the lake of fire, and the Great White Throne judgment. Between Revelation 20:10 and 11. That Revelation is the highlights, and Ezekiel 39 gives more details. We know the millennium applies to Satan's captivity bound in Hell, not the entire period that the Kingdom exists on Earth. We don't know the length of the little season. We don't know the amount of time that passes to build the armies and gather weapons in that multitude. We don't have any indication (no " immediately after") to tell us that following the battle of Revelation 20, Gog and Magog, how much time elapses before the judgment of the Dead. This theory postulates that Ezekiel 37 is the resurrection, Ezekiel 38 is the millennial reign into the battle of Gog and Magog, and Ezekiel 39 just provides additional details of the aftermath of the battle. Maybe! This is why it is so foolish to hold a hard and fast opinion about end times Bible prophecy that leads you to break fellowship with other gospel professing Christians. The good news is that if you have trusted on the blood of Christ and accepted that free gift of Salvation, we will be there to witness it. And in the end that's more important than arguing over the timing of things then, today.

As we enter the final chapters of Ezekiel, 40-48, we are given one last prophetic vision of the Lord, and again, as in earlier prophecies, an angelic being is given as a tour guide of sorts to the man of God. Ezekiel’s visions are often revealed by divine messengers delivering profound messages about judgment and restoration. In Ezekiel 1:4-28, he encounters the four cherubim, radiant beings with four faces (man, lion, ox, eagle), wings, and wheels. They show him God’s glory on the throne. In Ezekiel 8:1-16, the fiery, amber-skinned figure shows the prophet God’s glory in the temple in Jerusalem, and the corruption of the temple, exposing the abomination of idols, Tammuz worship, and sun worship. In Ezekiel 10:1-22, the cherubim reappear, moving with God’s glory as He departs the temple, confirming the withdrawal of divine presence due to the abominations and sin of the Jews. Finally, in Ezekiel 40:1-47, a bronze-like man with a measuring rod and line appears to show Ezekiel a detailed vision of a new temple, and a vision of future restoration. Recall Ezekiel 8:1-3; Then I beheld, and lo a likeness as the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, as the appearance of brightness, as the colour of amber. And he put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate that looketh toward the north; where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy. And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the vision that I saw in the plain. Here, he writes behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate. Similar, but not identical descriptions. Also, the concept of the reed and measure is repeated in John's encounter in Revelation 11:1-2; And there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and them that worship therein. But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles: and the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months. The text does not explicitly state that John completes the act of measuring nor does the Bible record the dimensions of the measurements if he had. But in Ezekiel 40 onward, the bronze-like man meticulously measures the temple with highly detailed dimensions of the temple. The being measures the temple's walls, gates, courts, chambers, and pillars. He gives the layout of each, along with the purpose for many of the inner chambers described. His reed is 6 cubits long, with each cubit being roughly 18 inches plus 1 handspan (6 inches), making a cubit 24 inches. Thus, the reed is 6 cubits or 144 inches, so approximately 12 feet. Solomon’s Temple (1 Kings 6) was 60 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high. Each cubit is 18 inches, so the temple was 90 feet long, 30 feet wide, and 45 feet high. Ezekiel’s Temple is described as 100 cubits long, 100 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high. Each cubit is 24 inches, so the temple was 200 feet long, 200 feet wide, and 60 feet high. Much, much larger footprint. Ezekiel’s vision includes a vast outer area (about 5100 feet square), far exceeding Solomon’s Temple courts. Contrast this with the 2nd Temple of Ezra and Nehemiah’s Temple, which was 60 cubits long, 60 cubits wide, and 60 cubits high. Each cubit is 18 inches, so the temple was 90 feet long, 90 feet wide, and 90 feet high. This discrepancy is important to keep in mind when trying to discern what Ezekiel's vision is describing. Obviously both the 1st and 2nd Temples were built on Mt Moriah, the site of Abraham's aborted sacrifice of Isaac. The site of the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, which David purchased and made sacrifice to end the plague on his people for his sin of counting them. Where Solomon built his temple. Today, it is called the Temple Mount, and is much disputed between the Muslims and Jews, as it is the site of a mosque. But the relevant thing to understand is that, despite the destruction and clearing of the land by the Romans, the site isn't sufficiently large enough to fit Ezekiel's temple. Ezekiel’s temple complex (1000 x 1000 feet) would fit within the Temple Mount’s dimensions (1600 x 900 feet), occupying less than half its area of roughly 35 acres. However, the complex’s vast outer area (500 reeds square, approximately 5100 feet square or 1 mile square) is too large for the current Temple Mount, suggesting a significant topographical change, like a supernaturally elevated Mount Zion, would be needed to accommodate its building. All this math to say, the main theories about what exactly Ezekiel is being shown here, could possibly be correct, but none completely line up with other scripture, history and current topographical reality, in a neat and clear way. Could this be a command for the 2nd Temple that fell short? Zerubbabel’s temple, smaller in footprint and lacking the expansive courts of Ezekiel’s vision, didn’t match the grand design. This could reflect practical limitations—limited resources, a smaller population, or Persian oversight—falling short of God’s ideal blueprint. Some Jewish traditions suggest the returned exiles’ efforts were a partial fulfillment, constrained by their circumstances. For all have fallen short of the glory of God. This theory is especially plausible given the timing of the prophecy. Ezekiel’s temple vision occurs in the 25th year of his exile, around 573 BC, counting from his deportation in 597 BC with King Jehoiachin. Jeremiah’s prophecy predicts a 70-year exile for Judah, starting with the first Babylonian siege in 605 BC, when Nebuchadnezzar took captives like Daniel. By 573 BC, this marks roughly the 33rd year of Jeremiah’s 70-year timeline. Nearly the halfway point of the captivity. Also, the description of the sacrifices and the continued elevation of the Levitical line of the sons of Zadok (rather than Aaron, a change made by Solomon in 1 Kings 2) as the high priests, marks it as of the time of the 2nd Temple. It would be counter to the New Testament that we are under to have a priestly caste and animal sacrifices in a temple that, as we will see, has the presence of God within. But again, the problem is that if this was the expectation of God's perfect plan that the Jews returning from captivity failed to achieve, it wouldn't fit on the very site that was given. Assuming cubits are consistent. There are other theories we can explore as this continues. But again, we see through a glass darkly and we should be open to the idea that some things we just don't know.

It sounds lovely. A great Temple, a house of God. Ezekiel's vision continues and gives the dimensions for the temple, and descriptions of the ornate framing and runners on the walls, as well as carving on doors and window frames. Was the image I posted something like it described? Maybe. We don't know. It is similar to how Solomon's temple is described in 1 Kings 6 And the cedar of the house within was carved with knops and open flowers: all was cedar; there was no stone seen...And he carved all the walls of the house round about with carved figures of cherubims and palm trees and open flowers, within and without...The two doors also were of olive tree; and he carved upon them carvings of cherubims and palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold, and spread gold upon the cherubims, and upon the palm trees. These verses are actually cited by Catholics to justify the images and idols they use in worship. That somehow having decorative trim and accents to beautify the House of God is the same as making an image of a human to bow before and serve. They aren't the same thing. Yesterday we looked at the theory that the prophecy found in Ezekiel 40-48 is a picture of a grand design for the 2nd Temple to be built at the end of captivity. A design that the returning Jews failed to achieve, that they fell short of the glory of God. A picture of the shortcomings of the Old Testament, and a picture of why we needed the New. Another theory regarding Ezekiel's temple is that it describes a future 3rd Temple, a pre-trib, pre-millennial reconstruction undertaken by the Jews in modern Israel, with the help of Zionist dispensationalist Christians, in order to have a place for the Antichrist to defile. 2 Thessalonians 2:3-4 Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God. Now this seems to be a clear prophecy of a 3rd Temple. That there will be a place where sacrifices will be made for the beast to stop, and the abomination of desolation: Daniel 9:27 And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate. But a few things are wrong with this theory. As we will see, the presence of God will come into the temple described to Ezekiel. And the sacrifices and the priesthood of Zadok are given in upcoming chapters, as acceptable and commanded of God. If there is a 3rd Temple, it will not have the blessing of the Father. No sacrifice they make will be pleasing, as they were never what He desired. They were always a picture of Jesus and His sacrifice, which was done once and for all. It is finished. No other sacrifice exists. God would not enter into a house of abominations run by unbelieving Jews. Jews who have no idea who is of Zadok. There are other theories we will look at, but this one seems to be a stretch.

The prophecy of the Temple given Ezekiel continues. Here, finishing dimensions and moving towards purpose of some of the chambers; to separate the holy, the set apart, from the profane and unclean. The separated chambers were where the priests would eat the most holy things, and lay the most holy things; the meat offering, the sin offering and the trespass offering for the Lord. The priests are instructed to change their clothes, putting on other garments to even approach these holy chambers and offerings. Spiritually, the application is made for us, as a holy priesthood, to separate ourselves unto the Lord. To keep our inner chambers, our heart and mind, pure of the profane. To make room in our spirit to commune with the Lord. To have separation. Of course we have the offerings of Christ Jesus. We consume His word as meat. We are dressed in His righteousness, clothed in white garments He provides. Not of our own clothes, which are filthy rags. As the man who tried to crash the wedding feast in his own clothes, and was cast out into outer darkness. So, we should prepare ourselves before the Lord. With prayer, with praise and thanksgiving. Putting off the profane. Cleansing ourselves from the world. 2 Corinthians 6:17 Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you. Biblical separation is a command, and it is usually found alongside the will of God that we be separated unto His works, His gospel, the ministry He chooses for us as His servant in Christ. This doesn't mean that if you had or have struggles with sin that you're done, defiled and unusable. It doesn't mean sinless perfection is required to be saved. It means the more we purify ourselves, the more sin we get out of our life, the more we walk in the Spirit, the more we are conformed to the image He has for us, and the more useful we are as a vessel in His holy service. That's what all these carnal ordinances and Levitical rules represent. Beginning today, make a commitment to be of more use to the Lord by being separated unto His works that He has prepared for us. Don't just check the box and continue on as the world does, but be that peculiar people. Relish the opportunity. It's never too late to commit yourself to ministering. But cleanse yourself day by day that you be more and more useful to Him that bought you with a price. Another theory offered for Ezekiel's Temple, is that this would be a temple in the Millennial Kingdom. That the Church is raptured and "not mentioned again after Revelation 3." That the Kingdom is for the Jews. I would note that Jews aren't mentioned again after chapter 3, and the mentions there aren't good. But the dispensationalists would have us believe that in the millennium, temple sacrifice returns. That the OT was salvation by works, and we are in the covenant of grace which goes away at the pre-trib rapture. This is obviously unbiblical and another gospel. The Jews after the flesh are only promised days of vengeance and being cast out of the Kingdom into outer darkness. Sacrifices never took away sin. It was always by faith. For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. Jesus Christ is the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. It was always His blood that believers trusted on, and that faith counted for righteousness. So we reject that theory as preposterous.

Ezekiel 10:18 Then the glory of the Lord departed from off the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubims. Ezekiel 11:23 And the glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain which is on the east side of the city. The prophecy of Ezekiel's Temple continues, and with much of the measurements and ordinances given, the prophet, and the angelic man with him, witness the return of the glory of God through the east gate, as Ezekiel says, in the like manner he had watched Him depart in the vision of destruction seen in Ezekiel 9-11. Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern. Here, we are given the purpose of this vision. That this is the pattern of what an ashamed and chastened people would need to restore the glory of God in their midst. The Lord provides the details of the altar and the sacrifices. The priests and the atonement. The sins of the people are great, putting up pillars to their gods where His temple was, His footstool. The corpses of their kings placed where the sanctified and holy unto God were meant to be. Abominations that caused the desolation and destruction. Restitution and reconciliation offered by ritual cleansing and a resumption of the sacrifices and sin offering. Another theory regarding Ezekiel's temple is that it is a picture of the Temple in Eternity. That when the last of creation is burned like a scroll, and a New Heaven and New Earth have been given us by God, that this temple would be in place. Of course, only those justified in Christ Jesus will remain, and our sins will He remember no more. Our sanctification and redemption will be long past, washed clean in Christ. So we reject this theory as well. Given the context of Ezekiel 43, we can understand that this is the model of what God would require for a repentant Jewish people, to fully restore the glory among them. The model given them as a nation. Not individual salvation, which is always personal, and by faith in the promises of God, but as a people. A nation. Blessed to have the Lord among them. The standards were high. Near impossible. But achievable, or God wouldn't have presented it to them. But like the Law, all have fallen short. Haggai 2:3 Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing? The temple would never return to this Glory, until the temple of Christ came, was torn down, and on the third day raised up. John 2:19-20 Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? But he spake of the temple of his body. Ezekiel 43’s vision of a glorious temple, when compared to the historical reality of the 2nd Temple, suggests a “falling short” that points to a greater fulfillment. Taken in that point of view, it underscores the need for Jesus Christ, who embodies the true temple, restores God’s presence, and fulfills the prophetic hope of a renewed covenant. And with it a new nation, of every kindred and tongue. The Kingdom of God. To further refute the Temple of Eternity theory; Revelation 21:22-23 And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it. And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof. The heavenly Jerusalem has no temple, because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple. Ezekiel describes a very physical building, with very specific dimensions and chambers and purposes. The doors and windows. The altar. None of this exists or is needed in the eternal state, because the Lord is with us. No need for the Sun or light, because His glory is our light. His glory will not depart. His glory will not therefore return, because He will be ever present with us. Sacrifice will not be needed, as our sins are remembered no more. Amen

Looking back at Ezekiel 44, we find the giving of ordinances for the priests and the temple, beginning with the command that the East Gate, which the presence of the Lord would enter through, would remain shut and not be for any man to enter, but for the prince, or king, to enter via a porch entrance of the gate, a smaller door within it. That he would enter and sit before it to eat bread before the Lord, and go out the same. Ezekiel is then taken to the North Gate, and falls to his knees when he sees the glory of the Lord filling the house of the Lord, the temple. He is again instructed to see with his eyes and hear with his ears, that he may tell others. This command is repeatedly used in Ezekiel, and is found throughout scripture in other contexts as instructions for the righteous. For the saved. We are told to observe, hear and repeat to others. Even to the rebellious. We are to preach His word and ways to the lost, and if they don't heed, like the man who ignores the warning trumpet, it is on them. Here, God says to Israel, let this teaching suffice you of all your abominations. He is telling them what they need to do to get right. God talks about the bringing in of strangers, foreigners (and their idols), who are not His people, into the house of the Lord, polluting it. Note, that He sets aside the allowance of non-Israelites who are either circumcised of the heart, or flesh. Who are saved believers or are assimilated into the nation. The provision for the circumcision of the heart among strangers seems to be a broadening of the terms. In other places, there has been an appeal for the children of Israel to circumcise their hearts towards the Lord. Such as the appeal to the rebellious people in Deuteronomy 10:6 Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked. An appeal repeated several times, including Jeremiah 4:4 Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: lest my fury come forth like fire, and burn that none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings. In the New Testament, it is only the circumcision of the heart that is welcome to the Lord. Romans 2:28-29 For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God. So, we see the progression. Hebrews after the flesh are circumcised, beginning with Abraham. In the wilderness, mostly in Deuteronomy and Leviticus, the circumcised of the flesh are asked to circumcise their hearts as well. By the beginning of captivity, it is a plea to get saved, and avoid the coming destruction. Here, in the midst of the captivity, when discussing an OT Temple that could be, it is included to count for Gentiles who believed. In the New Testament, it becomes the only circumcision that matters. Continuing the instructions for the priests, God judges the Levites who had served abominations in the Temple, that they are still His and servants, but in this potential Temple, they aren't allowed to be part of that which is holy, or sacred. Only the men of Zadok's lineage who did not betray the Lord. But we know, knowing that 400yrs later, in the second Temple, the Sadducees, those of Zadok, don't even believe the spiritual things of God and deny salvation and the resurrection. All Levites are instructed to either marry Israelite virgins, or if needed, to remarry a priest's widow. This prohibition on mixed marriage for the Levites brings a mass divorcement in Ezra's time after the captivity. Ezra 10:10-12 And Ezra the priest stood up, and said unto them, Ye have transgressed, and have taken strange wives, to increase the trespass of Israel. Now therefore make confession unto the Lord God of your fathers, and do his pleasure: and separate yourselves from the people of the land, and from the strange wives. Then all the congregation answered and said with a loud voice, As thou hast said, so must we do. They are also told to separate themselves, to not go near the dead, except near kin, and to ritually cleanse themselves afterwards. The high priests to wear linen, clothes they won't sweat in, not wool, etc ...All carnal ordinances and dietary restrictions that were done away with in Christ, in the New Testament, because of the necessary change in the priesthood. In the context of the view that these prophecies being given as a promise contingent on the people getting right, being meet for repentance, and receiving Christ Jesus as King, the instructions were for a time that would never come. An end-times that would never be. That had they circumcised themselves of the heart, they would have been blessed to see the restoration and the glory of God among them, forever. That Ezekiel is being used to try and gather Jerusalem as a hen would gather her chicks. To make them ashamed that they repent. Instead of life, they chose death and kill the Son as they killed the servants, the prophets, before Him, and lose these promises forever.

Here in Ezekiel 45, the instructions for a temple and a time where there will be a priesthood of Zadok, Levites given land by cast lots for suburbs around the restored Temple. And sacrifices made for various offerings, the measure of which are given for "just balances," precise volumes, that nothing is cheated or anyone give more than another. Similar to the existing Levitical laws, given unto Moses, the prophesied Temple in Ezekiel 40-48 has similar Old Testament offerings and carnal ordinances, Sabbaths and holy days, done away with in the reformation of the New Testament. We have looked at 4 main theories regarding this prophecy.; that it is symbolic and represents the church in Christ and Jesus our temple. That it is literal, meant to be the design for the 2nd Temple Ezra will begin after captivity. That they fell short in grandeur and size. That it is a future Temple, for the 3rd Temple leading up to the beginning of the Tribulation. That it is a Temple in the millennial Kingdom, or in the eternal Kingdom. All these theories have problems that make them more and more unlikely to be true. The secret things are His and we see through a glass darkly, but surely there's a purpose and a reason for Ezekiel to cap off his end times prophecies, that extend back to chapter 33. That the restoration promised also applies to the prophecy of the Temple. Which brings us to another theory which I truthfully hadn't considered before. The interpretation of "what could have been." First, we must acknowledge that God knows the end from the beginning, and the invisible things of what hasn't happened yet. Isaiah 46:9-10 Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure. God knows our decisions before we make them, but also allows us the free will to make them, and gives constant appeals to repentance, and encourages us to choose His ways and seek His paths. The Lord gave the covenant to Israel through Moses with this clear understanding. Deuteronomy 30:15-20 See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it. But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them. God made these conditional promises to Israel as a nation, with the foreknowledge that they would fail. Unlike the Abrahamic and Davidic covenants, which were mostly unconditional (depending on the men themselves to believe God, and have it counted for righteousness), the Mosaic covenant, with the commandments and Levitical laws, depended on the people to keep up their end in order to obtain the Kingdom and the promises and the blessings that would come if they would. And in His grace, multiple opportunities for restitution if they failed. 2 Chronicles 7:14 If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. Ezekiel is no different. It is the explicit purpose of the Temple prophecy, giving the people a promise, contingent on their getting right: Ezekiel 43:10-11 Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern. And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, shew them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the goings out thereof, and the comings in thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the laws thereof: and write it in their sight, that they may keep the whole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them. The promises given the people included Christ, and a Kingdom, if they repented towards the Law and God. Zachariah 6:12-15 Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is The Branch; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord: Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the temple of the Lord. And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of the Lord, and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me unto you. And this shall come to pass, if ye will diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God. They could be children of the Kingdom if they were ashamed of their abominations, took the chastening God consistently gave them, and like the heathen of Nineveh, turned from the wicked ways, God sent prophets, and they killed them. God wiped out the Northern Kingdom as an example. He brings Judah into bondage under Babylon, and makes His holy city desolate. All to goad them to come to repentance that they would be His people, and He would be their God. Matthew 23:37 O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! While spiritual salvation was always by grace through faith for individuals, without any other conditions, the national promises were always contingent on works. Separation, sacrifice and ritual cleansing to maintain the presence of the glory of God, which we saw earlier in Ezekiel, went out from the Temple, and here in these prophecies, promised to return, if they got right. And the Law was perfect and glorious to that end. The fault wasn't with that covenant, but with the people. Hebrews 8:6-8 But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second. For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah The moral law and commandments, which are still in effect today in the NT, were a schoolmaster to lead us to Christ for salvation. Same then as today. Even the law written in our hearts, for the Gentiles without the advantage of the oracles of God. All have sinned and fallen short, so we need a spiritual redeemer. But the laws of sanctification and reconciliation for the physical nation were not only doable, but God gave pretty explicit instructions on how to maintain it, which some of the time - during the period of the Wilderness, the entry into the promised land, here and there during the time of Judges and Kings, they managed to keep. And had God's blessings upon them. Israel was meant to be a light unto the world. Showing all nations that if they did these things and sought after God, they would be blessed as well. Eventually, it would lead to the culmination of the time of Christ, the BRANCH, The Lord, the King of Kings, coming to establish all of the end times promises of the Kingdom given to the people. In the city He chose to place His name. In the line of David as promised. And they would not. So, when Jesus did come, the leaders of the Jews were unable to deliver a people meet for repentance. They, being teachers of the Law were blind guides, thinking that whatever promises they had, were deserved being "Abraham's seed." That their added rituals and Pharisaical cleansings meant they deserved both the spiritual salvation and the restoration of their earthly kingdom. And rather than being ready for the Kingdom, they were instead cut off and cast out. Matthew 8:11-12 And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. This is why they expected a conquering Christ and an earthly kingdom. This is why they placed more value in the carnal and forgot the spiritual things of God, like mercy and judgment. Their entitled attitudes, after so long a period of judgment and chastisement against Israel by God to get them to get right, was the result of hardened hearts and stuff necks. And so they killed Christ and His death and blood entered us into a new testament, a better covenant. With better promises. Not a physical nation of the law and circumcision of the flesh, but a spiritual nation and a people circumcised of the heart. And with the fading away of the Mosaic covenant, there was a necessary change made to the law. Hebrews 7:12 For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law. The end to the Levitical priesthood of Aaron or Zadok, an end to sacrifices and diverse washings and Sabbaths and carnal ordinances. All these things satisfied in Jesus. But the end of the Old Testament also meant the elimination of certain aspects of the end times prophecies. Not all, but some. Just as the children of Israel who left Egypt and were promised Canaan, yet died in the wilderness, just as Saul was given two chances to be part of the lineage of Christ (once from his own anointment, and a second chance through his daughter Mical and David), just as all the other people who had a promise made that they lost by their own actions. 1 Samuel 13:13-14 And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever. But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the Lord hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the Lord commanded thee. Just as David would have built the first Temple, but his actions ended that, and Solomon built it instead. These missed opportunities didn't make God a liar when He promised them. But He rightly withdrew them when those the promises were made to didn't keep up their end. All this to say that the 5th theory of Ezekiel's Temple is that it is a picture of a promise for an end-times that will now never be. That God was promising the Jews in captivity a chance to make things right. That by His grace and mercy and longsuffering, He was telling them of the glory of the Kingdom of God that He had in mind for them IF they turned back and were faithful. An alternate ending of things that, though He knew wouldn't come, God was graciously offering Israel, one last time. And so Jesus came not to judge the world, which He would have had they listened, but to offer salvation. John 12:47 And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. God continued to see His will done, by other means. Because, despite the Calvinist protests, we are given free will, yet our God is not weak and beggarly as Calvin's having to micromanage everything to reach a conclusion He desires. The Lord can let all creation do as all creatures will, and regardless of our choices, still will His Kingdom come. And so, Ezekiel's Temple will never be. It was an offer that isn't. Not because of a flaw with God, but with the people. An alternate universe, where Ezekiel 40-48 serves as Revelation. It's the most glaring example of what could have been in the Old Testament end-times prophecy. An achievable promise, rejected by those it was promised to. And so the implications of this Theory are broad and deep. It would apply to just about every covenant promise made with conditions to the people of Israel in the Old Testament and any differences between Old Testament prophecy of end times and New. Ezekiel's Battle of Gog and Magog has some different aspects to it than Revelation's. They still happen, As described by John from the Revelation given him, and the difference is what could have been versus what will be now that the Old Testament is done away with. Necessary changes. The millennial Kingdom references in Old Testament prophecy very slightly from what we are clearly taught in the new New Testament. All of the little nuances and seeming contradictions and places where people trying to rightly divide the word of God are jamming Square pegs into round holes to make the prophecies we are given in the New Testament fit with the promises given in the Old. One of the evils of dispensationalism is that it has so badly blinded everyone, but even we who reject it are so used to dealing with everything on their terms. What if that's just a huge mistake. What if we need to scrap everything that comes out of Darby and Schofield and dispensationalism entirely, and take a new view of the Old Testament through the lens of the New? Honestly, this might be the most important post of my Bible study. It reframes quite a bit of uncertainty that I've had that I've had and a bunch of pieces are clicking into place because of the implications. Trying to keep this frame of reference going forward while simultaneously looking back and applying it is going to be a challenge but I think it's the right thing to do. I think it's how we rightly divide the word. That the only difference of dispensations doesn't revolve around salvation which was always by grace through faith, but two major dispensations of how things would have gone or will go. And of course the practical application for Christians today that we should take away from this is that concept of missed opportunities. Of promises made by God that we just miss out on because of our own choices. Ways that we could be used by God and blessed by God, and anointings to His purpose, what could have been... All undone by sin and stubbornness and self-will. And even if we have made mistakes in our past that could have made things turn out different had we done the right thing, there's still reconciliation with God because we are saved. There are still opportunities that He has for us because he can use anyone for His purpose. If we turn from our wicked ways, and walk in His paths, and hold His judgments, we can be restored and do great works for the Lord. I realize that almost no one is going to read all of this however I highly recommend that you do. If you have problems differentiating the seeming contradictions of the Old Testament and the New Testament and why things were the way they were and what changed and all of that this study is going to help you. How is it possible that people voted for number three number five and number six? Are there really Maniacs out there who think the Bible teaches that the millennial kingdom is for the Jews? Or that God would approve a third Temple built by unbelieving Jews? Or that Revelation is lying when it says there is no temple in eternity because Christ and Jesus are our Temple? I am not posting today to encourage everyone to go read yesterday's. It may change your understanding forever, and that's not hyperbole.

The Temple of Ezekiel prophecy continues, with the laying down of the law; the customs and ordinances that would be observed in this Temple, the House of the Lord. The East Gate remains closed, but the inner gate of the courtyard that faces it would be opened on the Sabbaths and holy days. The prince, who would enter in by the porch would be by the pillar, and give his offerings, and worship there. The people would enter either by the North Gate or the South Gate, but we're not allowed to leave by the way they came in. This is a picture of our spiritual state upon entering into the house of God. We shouldn't leave the same as we came in. It should change us, by the hearing of the word and the worship of the Lord. The law is given that the prince should not take the inheritance of others by force or imminent domain, but only that which is his. And if he give an inheritance to his son, it is forever. Just as the inheritance the Father gives the Son is. But if it be to a servant, it be returned in the year of liberty. Jubilee. That the people will not be scattered. There are further instructions for the places of boiling and baking and slaying the sacrifices the people bring. All a picture of the lamb. If things had been different, and Jesus hadn't been killed, these sanctification rituals would have continued. But in His sacrifice, we are cleansed by the Spirit. A better covenant.

Psalm 1:1-4 Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away. Zachariah 14:1-4,8 Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, and thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee. For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city shall be taken, and the houses rifled, and the women ravished; and half of the city shall go forth into captivity, and the residue of the people shall not be cut off from the city. Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle. And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west, and there shall be a very great valley; and half of the mountain shall remove toward the north, and half of it toward the south...And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the former sea, and half of them toward the hinder sea: in summer and in winter shall it be. John 7:38-39 He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. (But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.) Revelation 22:1-2 And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. Here in the penultimate chapter of Ezekiel, continuing with the prophecy of the Temple, we find the prophet brought out with the man guiding him before, who had the measure in his hands, and observing the flowing of water out of the altar and beyond the Temple and the courtyard. And the further they went, the deeper the water became, from his ankle to his knees, to his loins. Eventually, to a mighty river that could not be passed over, deep enough to swim in. Returning to the river's brink, the shore along a steep rise, and there he observed the trees on both sides. The angels tells him that the waters themselves that issue out of the Temple will eventually fill the desert, and the seas, healing all they touch, everything shall live whither the river cometh. Living waters emanating from Jerusalem, trees lining their banks. In Psalm 1, the Bible says we who delight in the Lord and His word are like unto trees planted by a river, that brings forth fruit, and the leaves shall not whither. The prophet Zachariah preaches that in the day of the Lord, among the other things that occur, would be Jesus splitting the mount of Olives in Jerusalem, and in that day living waters shall go out from Jerusalem. In the gospel of John, Jesus says that out of the belly of believers shall flow rivers of living water, and that this was a picture of the Spirit which they that believe on Him should receive. Later, in the Revelation of Jesus given John, the new Heaven and heavenly Jerusalem has a river, and the tree of life upon it, which gives 12 different fruits every month, and whose leaves were for healing the nations. The natural application for the initial prophecy given Ezekiel is a restored kingdom, with a river of waters healing the land, trees grown up from its shores, and full of all types of fish in abundance. But spiritually, this is fulfilled in the ministry of Christ, and the spreading of the Gospel, as living waters, the Spirit, and wherever it went, healing the nations, and believers being as trees bearing fruit, other believers, springing up alongside the brink. Prophetically, this matches the pattern in the end times shown John, of New Jerusalem. If you are like the righteous man in Psalm 1, the believer in John 7, you are a tree bearing fruit, and from you flows the Spirit, living waters, His word. Notice, the river begins in Jerusalem and gets deeper and deeper the further it travels. And note too, that there are miry places, salt marshes that shall not be healed. That the Mt Olive prophecy in Zachariah talks about the split, and a war between Judah. There are those who will not receive the truth. There were Jews who would not believe, and they killed Christ and persecuted His followers. Finally, in the final verse of Ezekiel 47, we are again shown that this The empire and Kingdom would not be exclusive to the Hebrews. The 12 tribes of Israel given land, Joseph's double portion making up for the Levites, are joined by strangers among them, the circumcised of the heart talked about in chapter 46. These Gentiles are given the same inheritance, the same birthright of those among the tribes of Israel. Wherever they sojourn, in whatever tribe they settle, there it will be for them and inheritance. Ephesians 2:12-19 That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world: But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby: And came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh. For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father. Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God This shows regardless of the covenant, regardless of which Testament that man was under, it was never exclusive to the Jews. Never. It was always about those circumcised of the heart and believing on Christ, calling upon His name. There is neither Jew nor Greek. The Dispensationalist Zionists seek to exclude the Gentiles from the inheritance and the promises. To say that Jews are the seed of Abraham, rather than all who believe on THE seed, being singular; Christ Jesus. They ignore the inconvenient truths in the New Testament, but you can see that they also ignore those prophecies in the Old. They have the spirit of Edom, like Esau, giving away the inheritance for pottage. God's redemptive plan was ALWAYS to include people from every nation, kindred and tongue. It always did, as we see in multiple OT figures who came to believe. Many grafted into the line of Christ (Tamar, Ruth, Rahab, likely also Bathsheba). The genetic false gospel of special favors to the Jews was always unbiblical. Regardless of how the prophecies ultimately played out.

Here in the final chapter of Ezekiel, we are given a division of land in the city, its suburbs and a grid roughly 50 miles by 20, as an oblation, or a holy section for the Levites, priests of Zadok, and a portion for the prince and the Temple. The land is divided systematically among the twelve tribes, with a central holy portion for the sanctuary. The chapter begins by assigning land to seven tribes north of the holy oblation, from the northern border of the land and descending southward. Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh and Ephraim (Joseph's double portion), Ruben and Judah which borders the holy oblation. These stacked portions are as wide as the land reserved for the city, roughly 50miles. Their height is not clear but seems to be an equal division. Perhaps this is an idealized, God-designed Israel.
