Just as He allotted the tribes in the wilderness, He does so here in a way less spread out and uneven than the lots cast when Joshua divided the land. South of the oblation, the holy area, are plots for the remaining tribes, Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad. The dimensions are given but other than a quick calculation, I don't know exactly. But it is orderly and symmetrical, and logical. The size of the the overall area is significantly smaller than the New Jerusalem that comes down from Heaven in Revelation 21. And he carried me away in the spirit to a great and high mountain, and shewed me that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, Having the glory of God: and her light was like unto a stone most precious, even like a jasper stone, clear as crystal; And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel: On the east three gates; on the north three gates; on the south three gates; and on the west three gates. And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. And he that talked with me had a golden reed to measure the city, and the gates thereof, and the wall thereof. And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal. And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel. This city is significantly larger, and a cube. But it contains the same 12 gates, each named for a tribe of Israel. Again, Ezekiel's Temple seems to be an idealized design, but to be made with human hands whereas the heavenly city is made by God, and its glory and size and treasure is infinitely greater. This design and God's plans for man can be debated, but the fact that God has greater things in store for us than we can ever imagine, if we simply obey Him and His commandments, and seek to do His will. We have all fallen short. We won't love Him as we should until the resurrection. We won't be perfect until then. But we can be useful and conform to the will of the Lord that we may be used by Him. Separate. In order. Not of confusion and the chaos that our sinful lives create. The more we walk with God and spend time with Jesus, we should be changed. We should understand the promises He has made us, out of the abundance of Christ's love and mercy, requires sacrifice and commitment. That we not quench the Spirit, or deny His influence. Not feeding the flesh. I fail at it daily, but God's mercies are fresh each morning. So we should pick up our cross and seek to be followers of Him, doers of the law not hearers only. Only God knows the secret things He has in store for us when we do. Amen

The captivity of Judah, long prophesied, begins. And the Lord gave Jerusalem and her king to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. And with it much of the vessels of Solomon's temple, brought to Shinar, and the house of Nebuchadnezzar's god. This will be important later, after the captivity ends under Cyrus of the Persians. And among the captives, those of David's lineage, of Judah, were brought into the service of the king as eunuchs. In hopes the highborn would have better intellect and ability to learn the Babylonian tongue, Chaldean, as well as its learning and ways, to better serve the king. We meet Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, and they are given Chaldean names; Daniel the name of Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, of Shadrach; and to Mishael, of Meshach; and to Azariah, of Abednego. (I still call the three Rack, Shack and Benny. Old habits die hard) In a show of magnanimity, the king allows the eunuchs to eat of his meat and drink, the food apparently offered to his god. With the intent that they grow to be nourished enough to stand before the king and serve him. But Daniel asks the prince of the eunuchs, his overseer, if rather than defile themselves with the meat and drink offered to idols, if he and the three others may eat pulse, that is lentils. Daniel, meek and faithful, doesn't rebel against the authority in his life, and yet doesn't compromise his faith and love of God. He instead asks permission. When the prince of the eunuchs explains that it would get him in trouble if they seem to be less healthy than those who ate the king's portion, Daniel offers him a compromise; feed them 10 days and try them. If they aren't any worse for it, then honor this request. Many people today hate the idea of submitting to authority. They want to riot in the daytime, and seek to use their faith to justify their rebellion. They say they won't pay taxes, despite Jesus saying to render unto Caesar. Despite clear commands to render duty and honor and tribute to those set above us by God. Men refusing to submit to any authority. Refusing to join a church and submit themselves to a pastor. Who slack off at work, and constantly disrespecting their bosses. This encourages the feminism that tells wives to rebel against husbands, and children against parents. Ultimately, it is rebellion against God. The Bible says For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. But what if authority over you asks you to do something that would offend God? Daniel shows us how it is done. Meekly asking to be tried, the overseer agrees and after 10 days the four are healthier looking than all the other eunuchs. Daniel honored the authority in his life and pleased God. An example for us to follow. And so after the 3 years of preparation, the king brought the eunuchs in and found none as excellent as Daniel and the others. 10 times better than all the magicians and astrologers that were in all his realm. And so now Daniel as well as Rack, Shack and Benny, in are on good terms with the King. And Daniel will continue as an advisor over the next several monarchs. In a position to do Godly things for the Lord in an ungodly place. This is why it's so important for us to be a good witness in the world. If we have secular jobs we have to let the light of God shine through us. As we will see later on it will lead to great things for the Lord. But it starts with obedience and humility.

Blessed be the name of God for ever and ever: for wisdom and might are his: And he changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding: He revealeth the deep and secret things: he knoweth what is in the darkness, and the light dwelleth with him. I thank thee, and praise thee, O thou God of my fathers, who hast given me wisdom and might, and hast made known unto me now what we desired of thee. Before I begin, I want to recognize that Daniel's prayer, blessing the Lord our God should be ours as well. Our God is an awesome God. I've written about it before, especially in the prophets, that the prophecies of the Bible are so precise, prescient and perfect, that it is impossible to believe anything other than an omniscient God could have made them known. The Old Testament is for our admonition, to instruct us in the ways of righteousness and make known the mystery of the gospel. That faith comes from hearing the word of God. How can you not see Daniel 2 as evidence of things unseen? The substance of things hoped for? How can it be read, and from our vantage point, and not lead one to fall to their knees and worship the living God who made his future, our past, known to Daniel? And then, knowing this, how can you hear the promises of God in Christ, eternal life, the resurrection of the dead and His everlasting Kingdom and not trust that they are true? So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Now Daniel 2 is a familiar story. King Nebuchadnezzar has a dream that troubles him, and he cannot recall what it was, but seeks someone to tell him the dream and its meaning. And all the wizards and wise men of Chaldea cannot do this impossible task. The king orders that all his advisors be put to death for their inability to do this, including Daniel and his friends, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah (Rack, Shack and Benny). But Daniel stays the hand of the man, Arioch the king's captain, by asking him to give Daniel time, and a promise that the Jewish eunuch could find out the kings dream and interpretation. And in prayer the matter is made known to him by God. And he brings it to Nebuchadnezzar. That the king dreamed of an idol, a collosal image. Head of gold, chest and two arms of silver, belly and thighs of brass, legs of iron and feet, iron mixed with clay. And the interpretation thereof, The Head of Gold: Babylonian Empire The Chest and Arms of Silver: Medo-Persian Empire The Belly and Thighs of Brass (Bronze): Greek Empire (Macedonian, under Alexander the Great) Legs of Iron, the Roman Empire Feet of Iron and Clay: the Roman Empire divided, and then scattered among the nations. This is the history that came to pass. And then we see Jesus. The stone cut from the mountain, without hands. The stone the builders rejected. The foundation upon which is built the everlasting Kingdom. Destroying the kingdoms of men. Matthew 21:42 Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes? Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure. Mark 12:10 And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner Peter to the Sanhedrin in Acts 4:11 This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner. Because we know the empires came to pass, and the truth of the prophecy, how can we doubt the promise of God in Christ? Isn't it marvelous in your sight? 1 Peter 2:4-8 To whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God, and precious, Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded. Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed. I would be remiss to not mention that the great king Nebuchadnezzar, upon hearing his dream and the interpretation thereof, fell to his knees and praised the living God. The king answered unto Daniel, and said, Of a truth it is, that your God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, seeing thou couldest reveal this secret. Again, faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Nebuchadnezzar isn't quite there yet, but he will come to understand the truth of this statement, and proclaim it throughout the world.

And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, along with Daniel, were established as leaders in Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar. And as such, called to the dedication of the massive image the king had commissioned. And there, at this idol, when the music played, all were to fall down and worship the image. But the three friends of Daniel were accused by certain Chaldeans before the king. And when asked, they told the truth knowing it could kill them. If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up. As we know, Nebuchadnezzar orders the fiery furnace to be stoked 7 times hotter, and the men in their coats and pants and hats, brought into the fire. A fire so hot it killed their guards who escorted them. Of course, Nebuchadnezzar sees four men in the fire where He'd cast only three. The fourth, he describes as like the Son of God. For there in the midst of the fire was Jesus, and the three faithful protected from the flames by Him. They're called out, unharmed, not even smelling of smoke. They were willing to die for their Lord, and by faith knew if He did not rescue them from the fire, they'd be with Him regardless. As Christians often say, "don't threaten me with Heaven." Then the king declared the truth of God, that there is no god like unto Him. The King had seen the truth and proclaimed it to all the world. We will soon see where this leads. The parallel of this is in the end times prophecy of the abomination of desolation, the antichrist setting himself up as God and making all men take his Mark, and worship the beast and his image. Revelation 13:15-17 And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed. And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name. We know that this is the means by which the beast and his false prophet will determine who are the saints, and make war on we who do not bow before him and worship him as God. And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them: and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations. And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. Contrary to the false "pre-trib" timeline, which removes the saints from the earth, the beast will make war with the saints. And we will be separated from the reprobates who take the mark, targeting us for martyrdom. Many of those that are alive and remain will face a decision like Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. We will be accused and told to worship or be killed. But we know if we shall endure to the end of this great tribulation, we shall be saved. That it will be cut short for our sakes and Jesus will visibly come to gather us before the pouring out of God's wrath. So as Jesus told us, watch.

Daniel 4, written in Aramaic from the hand of king Nebuchadnezzar, in the form of a proclamation to the whole world, tells of the king's final arc, these past 4 chapters, towards accepting the Lord God, the most high. In a way, the first 4 chapters of Daniel are Nebuchadnezzar's story as much as Daniel's. We see from the beginning of the captivity, throughout the other prophets like Jeremiah, that the king is called God's servant. That the Lord uses him to bring desolation to Jerusalem and refine the people of Judah as of fire. Preparing the way for Christ to come 500 years later. But in this arc we see there's more. Nebuchadnezzar is convinced by the wisdom and excellent spirit of Daniel, the miracle of the fiery furnace, and here by the humbling by God against his pride, and confesses that He is above all, even the mightiest king. His testimony, that Daniel had given him the interpretation of the dream, full knowledge of what God had judged against him, and the opportunity on his own to get right, to break off his sins by righteousness and showing mercy to the poor. To get saved and live according to God's word. He ignored it, and after a year of God's long-suffering, the curse fell upon him. This proclamation went out to every nation. Nebuchadnezzar willingly told the world about the seven years of humiliation he was given by God. To live in the fields like a beast. Without his faculties or riches. Lost to madness. Restored at God's command after the 7 years, humbled and a new man. In it, we see how merciful God truly is. How in ways big and small, through the Spirit, he tries to bring men to repentance. That even the mighty and the most based have ministering spirits over us. That God will give us room to repent, time to get right on our own. And He will humble the proud to show them their error. God would that none perish. But it falls on us to respond to Him. I imagine that this testimony, and the truth of God's power and judgment, brought many outside of the captive Jews to believe. Add to this the scattered remnant of Israel, and the seeds for those Gentiles, the nations of men to believe on Christ when the time came, was all part of God's plan. Everything working towards Christ and the new testament. One last point; God chastens whom He would, scourging every son. Too many Christians get comfortable in the blessings and protection God provides us. Like Nebuchadnezzar, we not only take things for granted, but begin to pridefully take credit for the things in our life that are by the grace of God. He heard God's word and forgot all about it. He became prideful and paid for it. I think mental illness is often from God, making us deal with the cognitive dissonance of our lies and self-deception and the truth of His word. Don't be surprised if you continue down the road, backslidden, to have this type of punishment. I have both observed it and experienced a fraction of it. Don't let it happen to you!

Some time has passed, and Nebuchadnezzar's son, Belshazzar has taken the throne of Babylon. And we find him using the vessels of the temple of God, taken in the captivity, to drink wine and praise images and idols. They were gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone. Some Catholics will deny that they do this very thing by claiming they aren't carved images, but we see here every type of idol, from carved to hewn to cast. All abominations in God's eye. And so part of the hand of God appears to the king and writes upon the wall. The king cannot understand it, but is struck with terror. Knees knocking, he calls for the wise men of the kingdom to interpret for him. Of course, they cannot. But the queen recalls Daniel and what he had done for Nebuchadnezzar, his excellent spirit, being filled with the spirit of God. They call for him, the king promising to give him power as the 3rd over the kingdom, a chain of gold etc. But Daniel says he doesn't need riches and power, he will do it for nothing. Daniel reminds Belshazzar how his father came to know the true and living God. Not serving dead idols, but being convinced by his 7 years of madness that there is one God, the most high. Who gives us our next breath. Who sets up and tears down who He will. Belshazzar, Daniel says, has forgotten the lesson that was hard taught to his father, and in pride had done a wicked thing. So, the writing on the wall spelled his doom. Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin. God had numbered his kingdom and finished it. It has been judged and found wanting. The kingdom will be divided and given to the Medes and the Persians. Just as the great image in Nebuchadnezzar's dream, the chest and arms of silver. Daniel is rewarded according to what the king had said. But it was too late. That night, Belshazzar was slain. As children, we should honor our parents, regardless of their own failings. One of the chief ways we can console ourselves if they are lacking is to learn from their mistakes. To see God's wrath upon them, the misery of their lives or their repentance unto God, and take wisdom from it.

Here in Daniel 6, the Medo-Persian empire has assumed power over what was Babylon, and Daniel exceeded all men beside the king, because of his faith and excellent spirit. And the princes and wise men under him plotted to have him lose the favor of king Darius. Tricking the king into signing an immutable law; for 30 days all who petition God or men rather than the king would be thrown in a lion's den. Of course they knew Daniel was faithful in prayer, praying to God three times a day on his knees, towards Jerusalem. Caught in prayer, they take him to the king, who despite not wanting to harm Daniel, is caught by his own decree. Daniel is thrown in, and the king prays that God protect him, and was up all night fasting and weeping for Daniel. In the morning, Darius sought after Daniel at the mouth of the den, and Daniel is alive. The angel of the Lord had protected him. For innocence was found in him. The king rejoiced, sentencing those that plotted against Daniel, and their families, to die the death they had sought for him. King Darius then wrote to all people and nations, in every language praising God. That Daniel's God is the living God, steadfast and true. Fear Him. His Kingdom shall never be destroyed but His dominion lasts forever. This now is the second king of a mighty empire that has declared the glory of God because of Daniel's faith.

Matthew 5 continued: 33 Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: 34 But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: 35 Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. 36 Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. 37 But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. 38 Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: 39 But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also. 40 And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also. 41 And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. 42 Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away. 43 Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. 44 But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; 45 That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust. 46 For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same? 47 And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the publicans so? 48 Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect. One of the messages of the sermon on the mount, in fact it's primary theme, is achieving excellence. Going above and beyond the bare minimum, striving for perfection, which means being complete. Whole. That if we think it's enough to not commit adultery, it isn't, for even the thought of adultery is sin. Even hate in your heart is murder. If someone compels you to walk a mile with them, go two. If they take you coat, give them your cloak. Loving your enemies, not just the brethren. Going the extra mile, excelling, being perfect. We see in Daniel that he had the spirit of excellence within him. He was blameless in his work. He did more, meekly and humbly, in God's name, serving Him. And it paid dividends with blessings from God and promotion over others. This of course led to their resentment, but they couldn't find anything to accuse Daniel of, except for his faith. Make them come at us for our faith having nothing else with which to attack you. Being blameless and excellent. Working diligently on everything you do. Going that extra mile. Heaping coals on your enemies by praying for them and meekly and honestly dealing with all. Giving tribute to whom tribute is due. Rendering custom. Make those that hate and resent you for your faith persecute you for it. Make it the only thing they can lay charge to you with. And when you are thrown in the lions den, or put in the fiery furnace, put you in bonds like Paul, or whatever else they use to attack your faith, believe that God will deliver you.

Sitting upon many waters, which are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues. Who is this great whore? This mother of harlots? This city on 7 mountains, that sits on many waters? Who has martyred the saints of Jesus and committed fornication and blasphemy and other abominations against God? The city on seven hills is Rome. Its whore, the false religion and apostate church of the Roman Catholics. The harlot daughters all the other false religions that have sprung from it. The Orthodox and the Protestant. All those calling themselves Christ's, professing themselves to be holy and true. But drunk in her fornications. Idolatry. Blasphemy. The abominations of her golden cup. The power of her political control, given by the kings that committed adultery with her. The murder of millions of believers, in a trail of blood, as this empire of miry clay and iron has conquered much of the earth. In the end, the 7th empire as described by Daniel (we will look at Daniel 7 tomorrow, along with the destruction of Babylon), will give the beast power to reign and will promote the worship of the beast who was, is not and is again. The fatal wound and Satan bringing the antichrist back to life as the man of perdition, and installing him as the head of the final one world government and religion for a short space. Daniel 7:7-14 After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet of it: and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns. I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire. A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened. I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame. As concerning the rest of the beasts, they had their dominion taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and time. I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed. And so, as the vials and trumps come to an end, the three and a half years of wrath poured out, special judgment is given against that great city, Babylon. This is prophetic in the OT of both the actual Babylonian empire, but also the future empire represented in night visions and dreams interpreted by Daniel, and preached by the other prophets, which as we see in scripture, all speak of God's wrath followed by the coming of Christ and His kingdom. When Jesus said that to Him gave all the prophets witness, we can see just how true that is. And as we near the end of the judgement of the earth, and draw near to Christ's reign, the beast is readying the armies of man to resist Jesus and His saints. Man has been in constant torment and fear from locusts from Hell, waters turned bitter and turned to blood. Fire from the sky and earthquakes. Giant hail. A relentless pouring out of God's wrath. And at the end of all this, the representation of Babylon, the nation at the heart of the one world empire, is utterly destroyed in the span of an hour. Saved for last, God allows the people of the earth to see His righteous judgement upon it for the blood of the martyrs and the drunkenness of its fornication and abominations. It is difficult not to see the United States as this city, especially given the merchants lament at the destruction of a great consumer nation. I believe that there is always a seat of Babylon, a country that embodies its spirit. Rome. London. The United States. It is possible that should God be even more longsuffering than we reckon, it could be Hong Kong or some other nation that becomes the center for the beast. Every man feels like surely these must be the final days. I can't even imagine how they felt in WW2 for example. And yet even more horrors and evil were to come. But reading this chapter, and the way it is described, it's difficult not to see things falling into place, faster and faster now. The beginning of sorrows feels imminent. And we long for the day when the angels sing out "Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her." Daniel 10 begins a series of prophecy, given to Daniel by an angel, of the things to come over a fairly long period of time, and in great detail. It may be the most difficult to follow but most rewarding of all the prophets. To get the picture, Daniel now has served many kings and seen the end of the Babylonian empire, as the Medo-Persian empire has risen in its place. And through it all, his excellent spirit, faith and meekness has served to make him one of the presidents of the empire. He still is serving in this role over the Babylonian area of the Chaldeans. Cyrus, a Persian king who plays a great role in ending the captivity of the Jews, is ruling from Persia. If you recall, Cyrus was predicted by name, revealed unto Isaiah by the Spirit, as well as the entire captivity. As we just saw in Daniel 9, he was studying Jeremiah and understood that the 70 years of captivity was near its end, because of the prophecy Jeremiah had made. Daniel himself had interpreted a dream of Nebuchadnezzar, that showed a great image with a golden head, representing the Babylonians, and a chest and arms of silver representing the Medo-Persians. Then belly and thighs of brass, representing the Grecian empire of Alexander the Great. Finally legs of iron, being Rome, and feet of iron mixed with clay, the fractured kingdoms that have come since, still containing bits of the Roman empire with them, of which America is represented, today. The prophecy of this is astounding, given Daniel was seeing things hundreds and hundreds of years later. In chapter 7, Daniel receives a vision of four beasts representing the same successive kingdoms, culminating in a "kingdom of the Son of Man," Christ Jesus, that will ultimately reign forever. In chapter 8, Daniel talked with the angel Gabriel, who explained the vision he had. The vision, which includes a ram, a goat, and a large horn, is a prophecy about the rise and fall of world empires, particularly the Medo-Persian and Greek empires, and the persecution of the Jews that will follow. All heavy with dual fulfillment for the end times. So, an elderly Daniel, who by this point had been in captivity for close to 70 years, although blessed to rule while a servant, is deep in mourning for his people. Praying for redemption from their captivity as promised by the Lord. He is fasting and praying intensely, for 3 weeks, in supplication to the Lord for mercy for the sins of the people. And so it begins Timeline of Days in Daniel 7 - 12 I. Daniel 8:13-14 – Vision of the Sanctuary Cleansing Daniel 8:13-14 Then I heard one saint speaking, and another saint said unto that certain saint which spake, How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot? And he said unto me, Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed. II. Daniel 12:11-12 – Specific Time Periods Daniel 12:11-12 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. III. Timeframe Breakdown Total Period: 7 Years Daniel 9:27 And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease… - The "week" equals 7 prophetic years, calculated as 2,520 days (7 x 360-day lunar year+a “leap month" of 30 days). First Half: 3.5 Years (Tribulation of the Saints, 1,260 Days) Daniel 7:25 And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time. - This period of 1,260 days (3.5 x 360) represents the tribulation where the saints face persecution. Midpoint: Abomination of Desolation Daniel 9:27 …and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate… - Occurs at the 1,260-day mark, splitting the 7 years. Second Half: 3.5 Years (Great Tribulation, 1,260 Days + 30 Days) Daniel 7:25 …a time and times and the dividing of time. - Extends to 1,290 days: Daniel 12:11 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. - Extra 30 Days: The 1,290 days include the 1,260 days of the second half plus an additional 30 days, likely an intercalary month in the Jewish lunar calendar to align the 360-day prophetic years with the solar calendar, ensuring proper timing of events. Additional 45 Days (Great Tribulation Concludes) Daniel 12:12 Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. - The 1,335 days extend 45 days beyond the 1,290 days (1,335 - 1,290 = 45). - Total 75 Days: The 30 days (1,290 - 1,260) plus 45 days (1,335 - 1,290) form a 75-day period of intensified great tribulation, overlapping the second half’s end, concluding key events. Wrath of God: 3.5 Years (Post-1,335 Days) The remaining time after the 1,335 days (approximately 1,260 days, calculated as 2,520 total days minus 1,260 tribulation days and 75 great tribulation days) aligns with the period of God’s wrath, following the conclusion of the great tribulation.

The prophecy that came upon Daniel in chapter 9 carries with it multiple applications, both present at his time, in the 1st century with Christ, and in the end times. Great arguments have been made among Christians and those who profess to be as to the exact meaning of Gabriel's revelation to Daniel. Was it meaning the destruction of the temple that would be built? Daniel has figured out the 70 years of captivity and desolation of Jerusalem that God foretold Jeremiah was drawing near. And after the captivity, they would return to the city God chose, and build it. Was it referring to the end times? When the beast tramples Jerusalem underfoot, before the second coming of Christ? All of this? As I read it, the thing that I focused on wasn't the mystery of these things, and their meaning, but instead the faith of Daniel and his humility before the Lord. He read the word of God and believing it to be true, began to plea for mercy, with a contrite heart before God. Daniel reads the curse in the law of Moses, and acknowledges that the Lord has justly judged against Israel and Judah. That their predicament is of their own making. Their own trespass against the Lord. He confesses this sin, and says not of their righteousness, but by His mercy, Lord save us. Daniel's prayer should be the main focus of this chapter. As Gabriel says, "thou art greatly beloved." Daniel, we are told repeatedly, had an excellent spirit. He had great faith and humility. He prayed multiple times a day. He sought peace with others. He trusted in the Lord, and served the authority God put in his life with humility, always doing his best. And here, reading the words of Jeremiah and understanding them in the Spirit and knowing the promises of God given his people, centuries before, he turns to God in supplication and meekness, seeking forgiveness and mercy. Not for himself but for his people. What a model Daniel is for us. Especially in these last days. The spiritual applications to take from Daniel should exceed whatever timing and charts and arguments over what he was told. We may have different opinions, may think this applies to the 3.5yrs of tribulation (I do), or whatever pre-trib promises the dispensationalists might take from it. But if we all held to the spirit of Daniel, and prayed like him and served like him and sought to be pleasing to God, even in a wicked kingdom, even as we are in spiritual Babylon, those things would work themselves out. But we would be pleasing to God. And our people would be delivered, just as He promises. I have to also point to the prophecy of Jesus' first coming. It is wild how God gave Daniel this vision of the "seventy weeks," laying out a timeline that points right to Jesus. Gabriel tells Daniel about 490 years—seventy weeks of years—starting from the decree to rebuild Jerusalem (around 457 BC, give or take, with Artaxerxes’ decree). Fast forward 69 of those weeks (483 years), and you land in the time of Jesus’ ministry, around 27-30 AD. The Messiah is "cut off" being the crucifixion. God dropped a prophecy hundreds of years earlier, nailing the timing of His Son’s arrival and sacrifice. Like in Isaiah and Jeremiah, God was saying, “I’ve got this all planned out, and I’m showing you I’m in control.” The precision blows my mind—centuries before Jesus walked the earth, God gave Daniel the timing, and it played out just as He said. Some folks debate the exact dates or lean into a future fulfillment, but seeing those 69 weeks line up with Christ’s coming? That’s the power of God’s Word shining through. It’s a reminder that when God speaks, it’s as good as done.

And so it begins And so, the story picks up at the side of the Tigris River, Hiddekel as its called here. And there appears to him an angel with great wonder in his appearance. The others with Daniel do not see him, but a great quaking, or fear befell the other men and they fled. Daniel describes the appearance of this messenger as wearing garments of linen and gold, his body like beryl, a crystalline or silicate mineral, like aquamarine and emeralds. His face had the appearance of lightening, his eyes as lamps of fire and his arms and feet as polished brass. His voice like the voice of a multitude. I have heard people say this is Gabriel, but Daniel had already met that angel, and his appearance was as a man and did not cause the reaction this sight gives him. Daniel passes out in shock and struggles throughout to gain his composure. The description reminds me of how Jesus is described in Revelation 1. And I turned to see the voice that spake with me. And being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks; And in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man, clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle. But as we know, he was also a type of the Antichrist. And the things he did were a precursor to what would come. Daniel Chapter 11: A Prophetic Overview (533 B.C. - 164 B.C.) Daniel receives this prophecy in the third year of Cyrus (Cyrus the Great, ~536 B.C.), delivered by an angel who strengthened Darius the Mede (~539 B.C.) in his first year (v. 1). The chapter outlines historical events from the Persian Empire through the Greek kingdoms, focusing on conflicts between the King of the North (Seleucid Empire) and the King of the South (Ptolemaic Empire), leading to Antiochus Epiphanes’ actions, foreshadowing end-times events. Verse-by-Verse Summary: - v. 1: The angel recalls supporting Darius the Mede (~539 B.C.) during his reign’s start. - v. 2: After Cyrus (Cyrus the Great, ~559–530 B.C.), three kings arise: Cambyses II (~530–522 B.C.), Darius I (~522–486 B.C.), and Ahasuerus (Xerxes I, ~486–465 B.C.), the richest, who attacks Greece, leading to battles like Thermopylae (~480 B.C.). - v. 3-4: Alexander the Great (~336–323 B.C.) conquers widely but dies young, his empire splitting among four generals: Ptolemy (Egypt), Seleucus (Mesopotamia), Lysimachus (Asia Minor), and Cassander (Greece) (~323 B.C.). - v. 5: Ptolemy I Soter (~323–283 B.C.), King of the South (Egypt), grows strong, but Seleucus I Nicator (~311–281 B.C.), King of the North (Mesopotamia), becomes stronger. - v. 6: Berenice, daughter of Ptolemy II Philadelphus (~283–246 B.C.), marries Antiochus II Theos (~261–246 B.C.) to form an alliance (~252 B.C.), but the deal fails after Ptolemy’s death, and Berenice is abandoned. - v. 7-8: Ptolemy III Euergetes (~246–222 B.C.), a relative of Berenice, invades the North, defeats Seleucus II Callinicus (~246–225 B.C.), and returns to Egypt with captives and treasures (~241 B.C.). - v. 9-10: Ptolemy III returns home, but Seleucus II’s sons, Seleucus III Ceraunus (~225–223 B.C.) and Antiochus III the Great (~223–187 B.C.), assemble forces to retaliate. - v. 11-12: Ptolemy IV Philopator (~221–204 B.C.) defeats Antiochus III (~219 B.C.), but his prideful victory doesn’t strengthen him. - v. 13-15: Antiochus III returns with a larger army, allies with others against Ptolemy V Epiphanes (~204–180 B.C.), and captures fortified cities (~200 B.C.). - v. 14: Jewish opportunists try to exploit the conflict for gain but fail (~200 B.C.). - v. 16: Antiochus III defeats Ptolemy V and occupies Israel, harming it (~198 B.C.). - v. 17: Antiochus III sends his daughter, Cleopatra I (~193–176 B.C.), to marry Ptolemy V (~192 B.C.), but she sides with Egypt, thwarting his plan. - v. 18-19: Antiochus III wins naval battles but is defeated by a Roman prince (Scipio Asiaticus, ~190 B.C.), returns home, and dies (~187 B.C.). - v. 20: Seleucus IV Philopator (~187–175 B.C.) focuses on taxation but dies mysteriously, not in battle (~175 B.C.). - v. 21-22: Antiochus IV Epiphanes (~175–164 B.C.), a vile person, seizes power through flattery, defeats opponents, and kills the high priest (Onias III, ~171 B.C.), the “prince of the covenant.” - v. 23-24: Antiochus IV makes deceptive alliances, gains strength, and uses occult practices to conquer strongholds (~170 B.C.). - v. 25-26: Antiochus IV defeats Ptolemy VI Philometor (~170–164 B.C.) in battle, aided by betrayal within Egypt (~169 B.C.). - v. 27: Antiochus IV and Ptolemy VI negotiate deceitfully, but their plans fail (~169 B.C.). - v. 28: Antiochus IV returns home, plotting against Israel’s religion (~168 B.C.). - v. 29-30: Antiochus IV’s second campaign against Egypt is halted by Roman ships (Popilius Laenas, ~168 B.C.), and he turns his anger on Israel, allying with apostate Jews. - v. 31: Antiochus IV and apostate Jews desecrate the temple, stop sacrifices, and set up a statue of Zeus, the “abomination that maketh desolate” (~168 B.C.). - v. 32: Antiochus IV empowers apostate Jews, but faithful Jews resist and perform exploits (~168 B.C.). - v. 33-35: Faithful Jews teach others but face persecution, martyrdom, and trials, receiving some help (~168–164 B.C.). - v. 36-37: Antiochus IV exalts himself above all gods, possibly as a sodomite, rejecting traditional deities (~168 B.C.). - v. 38-39: Antiochus IV worships an impersonal “god of forces,” promoting it with riches and dividing land for gain (~168 B.C.). - v. 40-43: Antiochus IV defeats Ptolemy VI again, conquers Egypt, Libya, and Ethiopia, but spares Edom, Moab, and Ammon (~167 B.C.). - v. 44-45: Antiochus IV, disturbed by eastern and northern news, sets up his palace in Israel between the seas, but dies without human hand (~164 B.C.). Daniel 11 meticulously details historical events from the Persian kings to Antiochus Epiphanes’ desecration of the temple, fulfilled between 533 B.C. and 164 B.C. While historically accurate, it foreshadows end-times events involving a future Antichrist, abomination of desolation, and persecution of God’s people, as elaborated in Daniel 12. This chapter underscores the precision of biblical prophecy and its dual application to history and the future. Antiochus IV Epiphanes in Daniel 11 serves as a historical type of the Antichrist through his deceptive rise, persecution of God’s people, desecration of the temple, self-exaltation, military conquests, and ultimate downfall. While Antiochus fulfilled many aspects of Daniel 11 historically, New Testament passages (e.g., Matthew 24, 2 Thessalonians 2, Revelation 13) point to a future figure—the Antichrist—who will embody these traits on a global scale before being defeated by Christ. This typological connection underscores the continuity of biblical prophecy, dual fulfillment - with Antiochus as a foreshadowing of the ultimate “man of sin," the Antichrist. Feel free to share it far and wide. It's further proof that God's word is true. Antiochus IV Epiphanes (c. 215–164 BC), a Seleucid king, is generally accepted as the "vile person" found in Daniel 11. Antiochus IV obtains his kingdom by flatteries, reflecting his usurpation through cunning. His military campaigns, particularly against Egypt, match his invasions of the Ptolemaic kingdom, marked by deceit and temporary alliances. The reference to defiling the sanctuary corresponds to his temple desecration in Jerusalem, and his self-exaltation, declaring himself as God, is echoed in his epithet "Epiphanes" (meaning "God Manifest"). His fierce countenance and understanding of dark sentences fit his reputation for ruthless ambition and strategic manipulation. He ruled Syria from 175 BC until his death. Born as Mithridates, he adopted the name Antiochus upon ascending the throne. He was a son of Antiochus III the Great and gained power after his brother Seleucus IV’s assassination, seizing the throne from the rightful heir, Demetrius I. Known for his ambition and erratic behavior, he sought to expand Seleucid influence, campaigning against Egypt and imposing Hellenistic culture on Judea, which sparked the Maccabean Revolt. His desecration of the Jerusalem Temple, banning Jewish practices, and setting up an altar to Zeus cemented his notoriety. Historical records, including 1 Maccabees and Josephus, claim that in 167 BC, he desecrated the temple by erecting an altar to Zeus Olympios, where sacrifices, including pigs, were offered, as part of his campaign to enforce Hellenistic, or Greek, worship. While he claimed divine status for himself, Zeus was the "god of forces" he brought on Jerusalem. The god of his fathers, Apollo, was traditionally revered as the divine patron of the Seleucid dynasty, symbolizing royal legitimacy, and in doing so, he rejected the god of his fathers. The Seleucid Empire remained formally independent until 63 BC, when Roman general Pompey the Great annexed Syria as a Roman province after defeating the last Seleucid rulers, effectively ending Seleucid sovereignty and placing Judea, Galilee and Samaria under Roman authority. And this was why, in Jesus' day, Rome ruled, but Greek was the lingua franca of their region. Daniel 8:13-14 – Vision of the Sanctuary Cleansing Daniel 8:13-14 Then I heard one saint speaking, and another saint said unto that certain saint which spake, How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot? Daniel 12:11-12 – Specific Time Periods Daniel 12:11-12 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. III. Timeframe Breakdown Total Period: 7 Years Daniel 9:27 And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease… - The "week" equals 7 prophetic years, calculated as 2,520 days (7 x 360-day lunar year+a “leap month" of 30 days). First Half: 3.5 Years (Tribulation of the Saints, 1,260 Days) Daniel 7:25 And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time. - This period of 1,260 days (3.5 x 360) represents the tribulation where the saints face persecution. Midpoint: Abomination of Desolation Daniel 9:27 …and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate… - Occurs at the 1,260-day mark, splitting the 7 years. Second Half: 3.5 Years (Great Tribulation, 1,260 Days + 30 Days) Daniel 7:25 …a time and times and the dividing of time. - Extends to 1,290 days: Daniel 12:11 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. - Extra 30 Days: The 1,290 days include the 1,260 days of the second half plus an additional 30 days, likely an intercalary month in the Jewish lunar calendar to align the 360-day prophetic years with the solar calendar, ensuring proper timing of events. Additional 45 Days (Great Tribulation Concludes) Daniel 12:12 Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. - The 1,335 days extend 45 days beyond the 1,290 days (1,335 - 1,290 = 45). - Total 75 Days: The 30 days (1,290 - 1,260) plus 45 days (1,335 - 1,290) form a 75-day period of intensified great tribulation, overlapping the second half’s end, concluding key events. Wrath of God: 3.5 Years (Post-1,335 Days) The remaining time after the 1,335 days (approximately 1,260 days, calculated as 2,520 total days minus 1,260 tribulation days and 75 great tribulation days) aligns with the period of God’s wrath, following the conclusion of the great tribulation.

A time where the plenty of God is taken away. No king, no sacrifice, no priestly duties, no image to bow to. And yet He wants them to know by this preaching that the Lord expects them to suffer through this loss and still maintain their faithfulness to Him. Something they weren't able to do in plenty, now do in tribulation. But why? Because of the promise of the Lord, that in the latter end of things, they will seek the Lord their God and David their king, being Christ Jesus, and receive His goodness once again. We are all given the choice. He would rather we come to him by His mercy and gratitude for the blessings of His love upon us. But absent that, our coming to Him in hard times for the blessed promise of His goodness in Christ is worthy too. Or we can continue in drunkenness and idolatry, and the desolation and famine that comes with sin. Continuing in death.

Continuing the preaching against Israel, its people are wicked, especially even their priests, those low men that were established by Jeroboam, when he introduced idolatry to the people and caused all Israel to sin. Hosea preaches hard against their sins; the violence and bloodshed, the drunkenness, the literal whoredoms and adultery, and spiritual; chasing after false gods. The Lord says that if they don't wish to retain Him in their knowledge, they will perish for that lack of knowledge. If the priests won't reprove and rebuke sin, then they are in common cause with it. Let their sins consume them. God won't even scourge them for backsliding. They've been given up and given over, a reprobate nation. They go to the stocks for advice, that is to wooden idols, sacrifices in groves, seeking favor of their dead gods. So the living God says let their daughters and wives go whoring as they have to Him. What a wicked time, and the destruction of Israel was long past due. Only the longsuffering love of the Lord stayed their end. The Lord does make provision to keep the evil out of Judah, that the false religion and fornications of the North, the Idolatry of Ephraim, would not spread into the Southern Kingdom, for now. What a condemnation. And it is the same righteous judgement of God that will be passed on to the world, even as Judah, or that is saved Christians today, are spared. It may seem like the wicked prosper and go unpunished, but as we see here, that is a punishment in itself. Allowing the blood to heap against them, their own sins to make them miserable, even as they compound. And then, destruction. Perfect is the judgment of God

The Lord is not happy with Israel. The priests and kings having led the people to ruin. Ephraim, Judah, Benjamin, all get named along with greater Israel for their condemnation. Is there any judgment upon a nation as fearsome as their seeking the Lord and not being able to find Him, because He has withdrawn Himself from them? Jeremiah 6:30 Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them. God is long-suffering, He is mercy that He will repent of evil He would do to a people if they turn from their wicked ways, and seek His face. But at some point, He will withdraw the offer, and allow His wrath to pour out on the wicked. This is the same for individuals. Reprobation is real. The hour of salvation is here, now. Don't put it off. Seek Him while He can be found. Isaiah 55:6-7 Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon. 2 Corinthians 6:2 For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation. Matthew 13:14-15 And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. The false idea that it is never too late with God for people to get right and get saved, that as long as you live, there's always a chance for salvation, has led so many to Hell. They put off to tomorrow the gift of grace. They stay in the pleasures of sin for a season, rather than esteeming the reproach of Christ, or having respect for the recompense of the reward. But rather, like Pharaoh, they harden their hearts and stiffen their necks and dull their hearing. They seek after vain jangling and smooth preaching, and those telling them "peace and safety" when there is no peace. Like Israel, they chase after idols and put their faith in horses and chariots, turning towards Egypt spiritually. Or worse, pitching their tents towards Sodom. God's wrath comes like a thief in the night, His judgment is righteous and true. Wake to Him and seek peace in Christ while you can. Before it is "too late, Reprobate!"

Hosea continues prophesying against Israel, primarily Ephraim and here, Gilead which is a territory of Manasseh, East of the Jordan, but also the Southern Kingdom of Judah. There are false gods, idols, and worse, violence and murder among them. The prophet begins with an appeal to repentance, turning towards the Lord to heal that which He has smitten them with in His righteous wrath. He says if they do, on the 3rd day they would be risen up, a prophetic reference to the resurrection of Christ. He says, Then shall we know, if we follow in to know the Lord: his going forth is prepared as the morning; Christ's coming was preordained and as inevitable as the sunrise, the morning star. His coming as the rain, the former rains of the spring, the later rains of fall and the harvest. I believe that is prophetic of the two comings of Jesus. Just as the Spring and Fall feasts point to His first and second coming. These rains bringing life in abundance. He follows this comparison of Jesus to the seasonal rains with a lament if the goodness of Israel, which Hosea compares to the fleeting morning cloud, or the quick to evaporate dew upon the grass. In relation to the Christian life, I have experienced this of myself. The intents of the morning to pick up that cross, beginning the day with prayer and scripture, only to see the goodness fade with the day like the dew. Drawing the stray moisture from the air around us, rather than being soaked in the rains, and so losing steam throughout the day. The Lord has slain them with His word, reproved by the prophets speaking in the Spirit, the law convicting them for their deeds. His judgments as a light, piercing the darkness of their sin. For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. Psalm 40:6-8 Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. Hebrews 10:7-10 Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God. Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. God's will for us is that we show the same mercy towards others He extended to us. The sacrifices and ordinances of the OT were for their understanding, that the children of God had a means of picturing the sacrifice of Christ to come, Jesus being the only true sacrifice for sin. But the blood of the testament with God for forgiveness and eternal life exists as a gift for our benefit, that we may know we have that relationship. That we become sons of God, so that we may know love. Mercy. Charity. His will for our lives and our obedience, that it be well with us. Jesus is the door. But there is a pasture He leads us to, in rest that we can magnify His light to guide others from the darkness. But they have dealt treacherously with God, and left the covenant with Him. The priests murder in the way by consent. They don't preach against the violence, and so they are accessories to it. They don't preach mercy and forgiveness, or the faith of eternal life in God, and so they murder their flock by condemnation to Hell. As John the Baptist preached against the religious leaders of the Jews; Matthew 3:7-8 But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance And as Christ Himself does; Matthew 23:23 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Religious leaders who don't teach judgment, mercy and faith are blind guides, the Bible says. They make proselytes twofold more the child of Hell than themselves. Finally the word of God tells them that because of the horrors He has seen by their disobedience, violence and adultery with idols, that His judgment is coming. For Ephraim and the rest of Israel, facing total destruction. And the return of captivity for Judah, which would come roughly 200 years from this preaching. God's judgment is sure, but He is longsuffering and would that no man perish. Repentance towards God can heal the land, and delay His wrath. But it is in the hearts of men to do wickedly. Deuteronomy 11:26-28 Behold, I set before you this day a blessing and a curse; A blessing, if ye obey the commandments of the LORD your God, which I command you this day: And a curse, if ye will not obey the commandments of the LORD your God, but turn aside out of the way which I command you this day, to go after other gods, which ye have not known.

Continuing the preaching of the word of God by the prophet Hosea, chapter 7 leads from chapter 5 where the prophet tells the people that the Lord will rend them like a lion, and 6, which opened to an appeal to those with ears to hear to turn back to the Lord to be healed from those wounds. Hosea 7 tells us why God hasn't reached out to heal them; their heart is not towards Him. The people think God has forgotten their sin, and so their doings have become undeniably wicked. Samaria, the Northern Kingdom of Israel, and down into Ephraim, all the people do wickedly. They are thieves and robbers. They commit violence. And their King and princes, the captains of their communities, are glad with it. Their lies please the rulers. Lord knows, modern Christians understand what that is like, to see the wicked and ungodly defended by lies, repeated by the rulers of this world. Rejecting the judgment of God and His word. Hosea begins an analogy, a parable of a baker who stoked the fire for the ovens at night, leaving dough to proof while he sleeps, that it is ready and roaring hot in the morning. So to are the hearts of this adulterous generation. Their trusting in other gods and the idols that represent them has primed them to do great evil. The leaven of sin takes hold, and the fires burn hot so the opportunity for sin is ever ready. The king is drunken with the princess, and takes his place with the scorners, those haters of God and His word. The judges God raised up are gone. No one with discernment remains among their leaders. There are no saved men among them to bring them to the truth. None have called upon the name of the Lord. Ephraim have taken for themselves strange women, given their daughters to outlandish men. Mixed with the heathen. A cake not turned, burned on one side, and uncooked on the other. And by allowing their people to be overrun and diluted by these mixed marriages, the strangers among them have devoured their strength, and the people don't even realize it. Despite all the warnings and natural consequences and the reproval of God, they still won't listen. He compares Ephraim to a silly dove, a bird calling out to Egypt, as the people would do to help them, rather than the Lord, and yet going to Assyria, scattered to their ultimate destruction. Mating calls to one nation, migrating to another. Silly. Woe unto them! for they have fled from me: destruction unto them! because they have transgressed against me: though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me. They have the sweet offer of salvation, by faith in Christ to come, their sins redeemed, but they hold the truth in unrighteousness. They do not wish to retain God in their knowledge. And so the Lord will destroy them for that lack of knowledge.

For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind... The destruction of Israel and the judgment of God against them comes from their own hands. Their own choices. Their rejection of reconciliation. Their trusting in strangers, foreign kings and princes, and especially their trust in dead idols. Not only the foreign gods of the heathens surrounding them and among them, but the idols they set before themselves as representation of the Lord. The golden calves Jeroboam made, and which the unqualified priests offer sacrifice to in the name of the living God. False Christianity is the same as the religion of Samaria, of Israel. Practiced in Ephraim. Known in Dan. Jeroboam built two golden calves and placed them in the cities of Bethel, on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin and the other in the north, in Dan. Soon all of Samaria would be overrun by the Assyrians, who would carry away and slay the populations, and replace them with strangers from many nations. Made a vessel wherein is no pleasure. Desolate. Struck with famine. What little food they grew, taken by the strangers among them. And Judah, which had remained somewhat loyal to the Lord, built up walled cities, trusting in their own works to save them, would soon after be taken captive by the Babylonians. They should have trusted in the Lord. I have written to him the great things of my law, but they were counted as a strange thing. Today, Biblical fundamentalism is seen as a strange thing, an atavistic anachronism. A throwback to a time where people weren't as "enlightened." Where the "critical text reading" of scripture didn't exist. Where common people just didn't know that the Bible "isn't literal," that it was outdated and written to the "culture at the time." Today, we have such "wisdom," from our intellectual betters, graduates of Seminary School, who studied Greek for a few semesters, and know that the average Christian just cannot understand such archaic language and concepts. Those thinking themselves wise became fools. The law of God became a strange thing to them, and so they lean on their own understanding. This is why we must study to be approved by God, not men. To compare spiritual things with spiritual. To search the scriptures to see if things are so. To know God and His word, and in the Spirit come to see His wisdom and judgment, and not our own. Israel followed man's wisdom. They added idols and icons to venerate in their worship, set their own standards for priests, set their own holy days, and feasts, their own standards. Teaching for commandments the doctrines of men. Holding scripture out as a strange thing, and instead trusting in tradition. Trading the unchanging rock of God for shifting sands. And this sowing the wind, they reap the whirlwind. BTW if you notice, the sin of Israel, specifically Jeroboam, was the same as the sin of the Roman Catholic Church, and her harlot daughters. And it has led to the same destruction in our day.

The curse of Ephraim by the Lord, as spoken by the prophet Hosea in the Spirit. Their threshing floors are empty, their winepress fails them, they are scattered to Egypt and Assyria. They no longer can offer sacrifice to the Lord, but rather eat of polluted bread. Their judgment has come. They were warned. All Israel shall see the judgment. The prophets driven mad by their inequities, hated in the house of God by the people. They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah, the rape of the Levite's concubine by the sodomites in Benjamin, back in Judges 19. The abominations that nearly destroyed Benjamin utterly. The Lord laments that in Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, He found a people as wild grapes in the wilderness. That they were as the first ripe figs of the early summer. This reminds us of the comparison to wild vine of the gentiles, grafted in; Romans 11:11-21 For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. The root is Christ. He is the true vine. But if Gentiles were graft in by the gospel, so too were the original branches of the patriarchs. Wild grapes the Lord prepared a vineyard for. Here, He is about to hew off a branch in Ephraim, and cast it into the fire. Just as the Lord blessed Israel through Balaam for their righteousness, and so Balaam made them to sin at Baalpeor that they be cursed, so God is reminded by the evil Ephraim has done. Balaam counseled Balak to bring whoredoms, both physical with fornication among the daughters of Midian, and to sacrifice and eat meat given to Baalpeor. And this brought destruction. 24,000 Israelites died in a plague of judgment after committing sins of idol worship and fornication at Baalpeor. Ephraim, and all Israel, had willingly chased after the same. Their children shall die. They will bring others to be passed through the fire, to be murdered. The Lord promises they will have not a man left when He is done with them. Give them, O Lord: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts. What a curse. I will drive them out of mine house, I will love them no more: all their princes are revolters. At Gilgal, they crossed into the promised land, setting up the circle of 12 stones where the waters of the Jordan parted for them. The Lord says this place of triumph is where He began to hate them, for their turning from Him. Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up, they shall bear no fruit: yea, though they bring forth, yet will I slay even the beloved fruit of their womb. What a curse to be of a nation under the wrath of God. Where birthrates are declining, where even those babies conceived are brought to murderers to be slain. Where even those that survive are killed. What a wicked generation to have such evil visited upon it. Sounds familiar. My God will cast them away, because they did not hearken unto him: and they shall be wanderers among the nations. The idea that those calling themselves Jews today are entitled to the promised land, that God's covenant was unconditional and forever, is put to lie throughout the Old Testament, and confirmed as not the case in the New. Dispensationalist Zionism requires an ignorance of scripture to maintain its false doctrine.

Again, Hosea preaches against Israel. And again, brings up the fruitless vine, the vanity of their trust in idols, the golden calves they've worshiped, the priests who led them to believe lies. Their kings and mighty men failed them. The sin of Israel and the righteous judgment that is falling on them, and their looming destruction by the Assyrians. And again a repeal to repentance towards God. Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap in mercy; break up your fallow ground: for it is time to seek the Lord, till he come and rain righteousness upon you. God's desire is to chastise them for their iniquity. That rather than sow righteousness and gather the fruit thereof, they sowed wickedness and reaped iniquity and the fruit gathered are lies. The high places also of Aven, the sin of Israel, shall be destroyed: the thorn and the thistle shall come up on their altars; and they shall say to the mountains, Cover us; and to the hills, Fall on us. Luke 23:29-30 For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck. Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us. Hosea is actually quoted or prophecies referenced multiple times in the New Testament. Revelation 6:15-17 And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand? Hosea 2:23 And I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God. Romans 9:25-26 As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; And her beloved, which was not beloved. And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; There shall they be called the children of the living God. 1 Peter 2:9-10 But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy. Hosea 6:6 For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. Matthew 9:13 But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. Matthew 12:7 But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. God delighting in mercy and right judgement over sacrifices is a theme of scripture. Psalm 51:16-17 For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise. Psalm 40:6-8 Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. Isaiah 1:11 To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the Lord: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats. Jeremiah 7:21-23 Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you. Hebrews 10:4-10 For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins. Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure. Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God. Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law. Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. The sacrifices were always for man, not God. Even the greatest and only true sacrifice for sin, the blood of Christ Jesus, is for our benefit, not God's. He wishes us to seek Him. To obey, and to confess to Him when we fall short. To turn to Him continually. And to show mercy and judgement and love, one to another. Forgiving and being forgiven. Being sown in righteousness by faith, and reaping the fruit, bringing in the sheaves. Others brought to the truth, calling upon the name of the Lord. Taking care of the widow. Judging the fatherless. Esteeming the profit of others more than ourselves. The sacrifices were to show the Israelites of Christ to come, and satisfy that itch in us that there must be blood to pay for our inequities. Upon the unrighteous, blood is required of blood. But the purpose of Jesus' sacrifice is that we have settled that debt of sin forever, washed clean in His blood, that we may go forth in mercy and His light so shine from us.

Matthew 2:13 And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. Truly, as God called Israel out of Egypt, so too would the Father call His Son, Christ Jesus from the West, into the promised land. And just as He came into His own, and the received Him not, Israelites turned away from the Lord to Baalim, and Baal Peor, and images and serving idols with incense. The word of the Lord was given them, teaching Israel how to be healed, but they knew it not. He led them like cattle and led them with love and led them with freedom and liberty in Christ and with blessings of plenty, and still they didn't harken to Him. Instead, the backslid, and so Assyria would rule them, and the sword destroy them and their cities, all because of their own counsels, all by their own choice. The Lord says it isn't His desire to destroy them for destruction's sake, to make them as Admah and Zeboim, as they were destroyed along with Sodom. He doesn't enter into the city as men, seeking to destroy, but as the Holy One, chastening them that they turn to Him again. To come to repentance towards the gospel of grace and reconciliation in Christ. Ephraim compasseth me about with lies, and the house of Israel with deceit: but Judah yet ruleth with God, and is faithful with the saints. Israel may have chosen their own destruction, by lies and deceit and their lack of knowledge. But in Judah they yet ruleth with God, faithful with the saints, again pointing to the coming Messiah. 2 Peter 3:9 The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance. Romans 11:1-5 I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life. But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. It is important to recognize that it isn't by ethnicity or nation that God saves or condemns, but by belief and unbelieving. The destruction of the Northern Kingdom of Israel was for their unbelief. The eventual destruction of Judea was for rejecting Christ. At the end of the world, on that great and terrible day of the Lord, the wrath will come on the whole earth for unbelief, the righteous remnant spared, and Jesus will get rule with all His saints. Romans 11:15-21,30-32 For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead? For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches.
