And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee... For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all. The love of God is conditional on belief in His word. The Bible says, without faith it is impossible to please God. His children are children by faith, adopted as sons of God through Christ. Heirs according to His promise, made Abraham's seed for belief. Those that remain in unbelief are cast into the fire by their own choice. By their own counsels.

Ephraim feedeth on the wind; Israel are placing their hopes against desolation and famine on Egypt and Assyria, not God. This reminds me of Jesus, speaking to Nicodemus in John 3 about how the Spirit seems to man; The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth. And also in 2 Peter 2, clouds that are carried with a tempest, clouds without water, in Jude 1:12. Carried to and fro by winds of doctrine from Ephesians 4:14. But, God is not in the wind; 1 Kings 19:11-14 And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entering in of the cave. And, behold, there came a voice unto him, and said, What doest thou here, Elijah? And he said, I have been very jealous for the Lord God of hosts: because the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away. But even then, the Lord had reserved unto Him 7,000 men who had not bowed the knee to Baal, and God had work for Elijah to do. Even as the world looks for answers in the wind, and seeks truth from clouds without water, and is carried about by the winds of doctrines, and even as they forsake His covenant in Christ and kill His prophets and seek our lives, yet we know God is not in the wind. He isn't in the tempest. The Lord our God is in the still small voice, heard in our spirit, and He has work for us to do. The Lord is wroth with Israel, listing the sins of Ephraim, faithlessness, Idolatry, wickedness. But also with Judah; The Lord hath also a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways. If Israel are the unsaved and the reprobate, Judah, at this time, remained fairly faithful, and represents the saved. Keeping the legacy of the covenants with Aaron and David, the priesthood and the king. Not perfectly. As Jesus said to the churches in Revelation 2 and 3, Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee. The Lord promises to scourge His sons. Judah and Israel, who started strong in Jacob, who fought to be first, grabbing Esau's heel, who wrestled with the angel and prevailed, who wept and made supplication in Bethel and spoke to Us, Even the Lord God of hosts, the Lord is His memorial, meaning Christ Jesus. So God reminds Judah of His mercy; Therefore turn thou to thy God: keep mercy and judgment and wait on thy God continually. The same promise to the saved, who may backslide and be chastened. Turn back to the Lord and be forgiven. But Ephraim, the Northern Kingdom of Israel, declares they are blameless. Without sin. Undeserving of God's wrath, and so opposing themselves. And I that am the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt will yet make thee to dwell in tabernacles, as in the days of the solemn feast. I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets. I that am the Lord thy God. I am Who am as God spoke to the prophet Moses, who led them out of Egypt. Even as Jesus says, Before Abraham, I am. Hebrews 1:1-2 God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds To Him gave all the prophets witnesses. He spoke to them with visions also, and with similitudes, or parables. And by the ministry of the prophets. And yet they would not hear, ears dull. Eyes blind to the truth. They multiply their deceptions. Ephraim provoked him to anger most bitterly: therefore shall he leave his blood upon him, and his reproach shall his Lord return unto him. God allows Israel to suffer for their own sins. No mercy is given them, only His reproach. They were warned and chastened and blessed, and given the same oracles of God as Judah. But they sowed the wind. They will reap the whirlwind.

1 Corinthians 15:55-58 O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law. But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord. I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction: repentance shall be hid from mine eyes. Again, Israel, represented by Ephraim, is preached against for their sins, and Hosea prophesying their coming destruction. The word of the Lord says that when they humbled themselves, trembling, He was merciful and gave them blessings in abundance. But that in their abundance, they turned from Him to sin. God again compares them to a cloud without water, a morning cloud that rises up to be burned off in the heat of the day. Morning dew that evaporates as the sun rises. Chaff that blows away easily. Smoke that rises and dissipates. As James describes our own short lives on this earth; Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away. But Hosea is preaching to a nation, and God has been longsuffering towards it, and yet they continued in a downward spiral of sin. When we are blessed by the Lord, it should humble us. Not make us exalt ourselves. Not grow comfortable. But learn to be grateful in good times and bad, always turning towards the Lord. Humble ourselves, because it is by His good pleasure. O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself; but in me is thine help. Christ Jesus, the only begotten Son. That in Him shall there be a King. God reminds them, they demanded a human king, despite His warnings. And in His anger He gave them Saul, and now all these generations later, it has availed them not. The Lord took away their king in His wrath. Israel is as a baby who won't leave the womb, despite their mother's travail. And so her sorrows are multiplied upon them. Samaria will become desolate, for she rebelled against her God.

Hebrews 13:15-16 By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name. But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased. Here, in the final chapter of Hosea, the Lord speaks through the prophet to make one final appeal of the gospel, that whosoever believes be saved. He calls for Israel to repentance towards God, that they have fallen in their sin. (For all have fallen short) Take with you words, and turn to the Lord: say unto him, Take away all iniquity, and receive us graciously, this is a sinner's prayer. (That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth...) We are offered the free gift of eternal life in Christ, by the promise of a gracious God, Who takes away our sins, by the confession of our mouths. By the calves, the sin offering of our lips. Giving thanks to His name. False gods shall not save us, nor the works of our hands. Note the double meaning here, both idols and literally the trust in our own works. For the Lord God is Father to the fatherless, in His mercy. He heals our backsliding, loves us freely. We are no longer appointed to His wrath. The Lord promises we will be watered as the lilies of the field. Taking root, spreading out like an olive tree. Growing as the vine. And Ephraim, all Israel, will bring forth His fruit. After their kind. Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? prudent, and he shall know them? for the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors shall fall therein. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. There are those who don't believe the word of God, and who say that the gospel given in the New Testament is different than the dispensation of the Old. Some even believe the lie that there is yet another gospel given by Paul to the Gentiles, that somehow differs from Christ's own words. But to Him gave all the prophets witnesses, from righteous Abel to Zachariah. And the gospel of salvation has always been this, as clearly shown in Hosea 14. Faith in God to deliver us from our sin, and the wages of death we have earned. By the offering of our mouth, and the praise of His holy name. Amen.

The prophecy of Amos begins, telling us he was a herdsman, a keeper of sheep in Tekoa, Judah, southeast of Bethlehem. A simple man, contemporary with Jonah, Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah. Preaching of the destruction of Israel to come, and as here, in Amos 1, the judgment against the nations surrounding all Israel. He lists Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, and Moab, a circle with Israel and Judah in the center. For three transgressions...,and for four God judges each for their violence and treachery and betrayal. This poetic formula of listing one less, plus one is used similarly in Proverbs 6:16-19; These six things doth the LORD hate: Yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, And hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, Feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, And he that soweth discord among brethren. It always strikes me as being even more damning. As there's enough already, but here's yet another. Amos will turn to the children of Israel soon enough.

Amos 2 continues the cursing of the lands about Israel, and now Israel and Judah themselves. Moab, for their evil against Edom and its king. As with the other nations before them, the violence and cruelty. But for Judah, their sin is more personal, the rejection of God and His commandments, the faith of their fathers and their leaving the old paths God had established. And for Israel, the betrayal of the righteous, the ill treatment of the poor, sexual immorality and perversions, the fornication at their altars. The Lord reminds them through the prophet of all He had done for His people. The destruction of the Giants that possessed the land He brought them into from slavery in Egypt. The prophets and holy men of God that gave them judgment, preaching His word. And they corrupted them and silenced them. The blood of the prophets on their heads. Great was their deserved destruction.

The word of the Lord continues to be preached by Amos. He is of the southern kingdom, sent to preach in the north to Israel if their coming destruction. God says of all nations, they only has He known and so His right to judge against them is right and true. To whom much was given... The prophet compares this warning of his preaching to the sound of the trumpet and the roar of a lion, the warning sounds that man takes heed of. Here he is warning of the spoil to come from Egypt, and against the false altars and idols of Samaria. The riches of the great houses will be destroyed. All as a testimony to the house of Jacob, the people of Judah. Their brothers destroyed for their sins. A warning to the southern kingdom. One they do not take to heart. 2 John 1-3 The elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth; and not I only, but also all they that have known the truth; For the truth's sake, which dwelleth in us, and shall be with us for ever. Grace be with you, mercy, and peace, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love. Once again, if a person has believed in their heart that Jesus Christ died for their sins, and received the baptism of the holy Spirit, made a child of God, they can NEVER lose their salvation. And further, THEY CAN NEVER fall into apostasy. They may backslide, become castaway and chastised by God, not produce works or fruits and even forget their own salvation, but they will NEVER believe anything other than the truth of the gospel, because the truth dwells within us and shall be with us forever. If a person who claims to be a Christian departs from the faith to believe something else as true, a false gospel or atheism or any other deception, the truth was never in them.

The burden of the Lord by Amos continues, and the preaching against Israel. God reminds the disobedient that He has given them multiple chances to repent towards Him. Their cattle, the kine of Bashan, led away by their nose rings. Want of bread. Drought and famine, mildew and mold in their gardens and vineyards. Curses similar to what He brought against Egypt in the days of Moses and Pharaoh. Israel's sons killed by the sword. Destruction as Sodom and Gomorrah visited upon them, and yet they would not harken to the Lord. His longsuffering at an end, He tells them to prepare to meet their God. They are under His judgment, and who can stand? Our God is a consuming fire.

Amos 5 continues the prophesying against Israel, whose destruction is nigh. There is no salvation for her. God's judgment and righteousness are at hand. But, as always, there are a remnant of believers still in the land. Illustrating this in verse 3, in each of the decimated cities. A remnant because of the promise of the Lord that those who seek Him shall live. Note that the number is not set in stone, it is an example. The remnant aren't chosen by God, and it isn't a promise that there will be a tenth spared. As with this entire chapter, it is an encouragement to repent towards God. Many Dispensationalists put the wrong emphasis of there being a remnant on God to elect one. To be a Calvinist God Who forces certain men to be saved. They sometimes argue that verses like this are a guarantee that God has decided to set some people aside to be saved, rather than a process by which they can be. And so, the emphasis should be on the promise, that those who call on His name shall be saved. Amos, speaking the word of God warns, seek Him, not Bethel in the Northern Kingdom of Israel where a golden calf was set up by King Jeroboam as a false religion. Not in Gilgal, on the Jordan where idolatrous practices to false gods were held. These vain hopes would come to naught. Seek the Lord and ye shall live! Failing that, He promises His wrath will consume them. And they, specifically the children of Joseph, 'all Ephraim" as the prophets call the Northern Kingdom of Israel, deserve it. They turn right judgment to wormwood, thinking it bitter, rejecting the way of righteousness. They rebuke prophets, hating them that preach God's word. They take advantage of the poor and the weak. They build up their riches by their unrighteousness. They afflict the just, take bribes and turn aside the poor seeking help. They show no mercy and so God's mercy is gone from them. But the offer stands; Seek him that maketh the seven stars and Orion, and turneth the shadow of death into the morning, and maketh the day dark with night: that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name: That strengtheneth the spoiled against the strong, so that the spoiled shall come against the fortress. Amos preaches against sin and warns of the coming judgment, and the offer of hope in salvation by faith in the Lord. Just as we are called to do today. Amos continues, calling upon that remnant of Joseph, those who seek the Lord, to hate the evil and love the good, that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious to them in this tribulation. We need to keep this in mind, ourselves. Things are going to be bad, waxing worse and worse. The patience of the saints, our "enduring to the end," is found in this instruction to hate evil, love good and establish judgement and righteousness. Too many false teachers assert that perseverance is for our spiritual salvation, that we could lose the free gift of eternal life, but that is not the context or meaning of it. It is for grace and protection during tribulation and persecution. Matthew 24:9-13 Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many. And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved. Saved from the persecution. Saved out of great tribulation. Revelation 7:14 And I said unto him, Sir, thou knowest. And he said to me, These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light. Those unsaved masses calling for the day of the Lord to escape the judgment against them for their wickedness, God compares to a man fleeing a lion and meeting a bear, or seeking shelter in a house, only to be bitten by a snake. So too, the fake believers in their solemn assemblies, offering sacrifices as if that's what justifies them before God, and calling upon Him to come quickly...they are the very reason God's wrath is upon them. Hosea 6:6 For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. Performative acts of worship, in Ephraim, to a golden calf worshipped in His name, do not please God. The blood of bulls and goats never washed away their sin. He took no pleasure in their songs and burnt offerings while they lived without faith, mercy and right judgement. Disobedient to the commandments that God gave them that it be well with them, and they should live long in the land. God reminds us that the children of Israel in the wilderness offered sacrifices at the Tabernacle for 40 years, and yet they did not enter the promised land. How much worse these who have borne the tabernacle of Moloch and Chiun, false and foreign gods, and the images thereof, including the star of their false God, which they invented themselves. Today they call it the star of David. This message is obviously very relevant. Today we have Catholic-made churches claiming to worship the true Lord, with idols and sacrifices of bread and wine made to them. We have evangelicals yoked to unbelieving Jews, trying to hasten the day of the Lord, and carrying the star of their god. And God of hosts, the Lord, Christ Jesus, will destroy them and carry them into captivity when that great and wonderful day comes. And there will be darkness and lamentation, wailing and gnashing of teeth.

Amos preaches against Jerusalem, Zion, where they feel safe in their sins compared to the North. Their wealth and palaces hated by God. The Lord describes their land as better than any in all Assyria, or of the Philistines. Their riches and excess in food. Their luxury of being able to work on music and new instruments, comfortable beds, drinking wine out of bowls. He promised their destruction. Tearing down the great houses. Killing the princess there. Captivity and affliction. They aren't going to escape His judgement. It is important to keep in mind that God only kept Judah from being utterly destroyed like the rest of Israel, for two reasons; His promise to David that Jesus would come from his line, and the city Jerusalem, where He chose to place His name. People who place the importance of Jerusalem on the Jews who occupy it, that Judah was spared destruction for their sakes', somehow, aren't rightly dividing the word. It is plain and clear: 1 Kings 11:32 But he shall have one tribe for my servant David's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel. This explanation is given by God repeatedly, leading up to the judgment against Israel and the Babylonian captivity, and it only makes sense in the context of Christ Jesus. Isaiah 1:9 Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah. That remnant includes the 14 generations from David to Jesus. Psalm 110 The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool. 2 The Lord shall send the rod of thy strength out of Zion: rule thou in the midst of thine enemies. 3 Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power, in the beauties of holiness from the womb of the morning: thou hast the dew of thy youth. 4 The Lord hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek. 5 The Lord at thy right hand shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath. 6 He shall judge among the heathen, he shall fill the places with the dead bodies; he shall wound the heads over many countries. 7 He shall drink of the brook in the way: therefore shall he lift up the head.

Amos, preaching against Israel, at Bethel, the site of the false religion of Jeroboam. Where the idols and false priesthood that claimed to represent the true God of Israel were. Essentially, the Vatican for the Northern Kingdom. And Amos is preaching their doom. He dreamt of grasshoppers destroying the latter growth of the second harvest. After the taxation of the King had taken his in the first harvest. Eating up what remained. And the prophet prayed for his people, Judah, O Lord God, forgive, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small. Pleading for a savior. And God replies with another vision, of fire consuming a part of the deep. And again the prophet gave intercession for his people; O Lord God, cease, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small. And the Lord repented. Changing His mind against the judgment that would have consumed all Israel. And He shows Amos another vision, the Lord standing upon a wall, set by a plumbline, a measure of perfect straightness and square. And the wall was built by this plumbline, set in the midst of the people of Israel, with the promise I will not again pass by them any more. Jesus is that plumbline. The stone the builders rejected, perfect and square, the cornerstone upon which all is built. The guide to know perfect justice. The hope to rise up from Jacob. For this the Lord repented, but not the entire judgment. The high places of Issac, that is Israel, shall be made desolate and the sanctuaries laid waste. And the house of their king, Jeroboam, slain by sword. All things we know followed in time. The. Amaziah the false priest there in Bethel, maybe his generations "Pope," spoke out against Amos. Accusing him against the King for his preaching, and saying to go preach in Judah, for money. Accusing him basically of sedition against the Northern Kingdom, and that he only preached for filthy lucre. O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there. Amos replies that he was no prophet, but was employed and had a living before being called of God to preach. For Amaziah's railing, Amos preaches harder against them, and says the priest's wife shall become a harlot in the streets of a polluted land, as Israel will surely be made desolate, carried away into captivity. The short term prophecy, that Judah would be spared the total destruction of Israel, to allow the plumbline to be set, to spare some of those from the latter harvest, when the locusts from hell and the fire against the deep is loosed, His wrath, following the Kings mowing. His harvest in the resurrection at the end of the tribulation, is clearly meant to be of Christ. Powerful prophecy.

Continuing the preaching of Amos against the Northern Kingdom of Israel, especially against the false religion of Jeroboam. The Lord shows Amos a basket of summer fruit. The early harvest. Those He has gathered unto Himself. Like the wheat in the dream of the grasshopper, the vision of the fall harvest being devoured before it springs fully up, the Lord says that He shall pass again no more. Israel is being cut off in unbelief. The word of God taken from their hearts. Ears made dull for hearing. And all those who swore by the false idols, the Sin of Samaria, shall fall and never rise again. This false religion of Jeroboam, which lasted hundreds of years and flourished, even as the true religion in Judea waxed and waned. This is a prophetic sign of the Roman Catholic Church, and its Orthodox and mainline Protestant churches. They set up false idols, claimed they were the living God, made up their own feasts, and ceremony, priesthood and sacrifices. Keeping their vain traditions and so God shut up their hearts to the truth. In the end His judgment is upon them and they will be utterly destroyed. Now as then.

The word of the Lord, as preached by Amos, contains very clear language and promises. Not as rich in dark saying and vague symbols as people portray the books of the prophets. He tells Amos, smite the lintel of the door that the posts shake and fall on the heads of the Israelites, and the Lord will slay all of them with the sword. A reverse Passover, where the blood of the lamb on the lintel saved the people. No matter where they seek to hide, the Lord shall have their lives. Dug underground to Hell, the tops of mountains, the bottom of the sea, even surrendering to captivity, there is no escaping the wrath against Israel, nor the end times wrath it pictures. The Lord is mighty, and all powerful. Amen! The Lord is His name. Are ye not as children of the Ethiopians unto me, O children of Israel? saith the Lord. Have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt? and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir? The Israelites of the Northern Kingdom are utterly disowned. No better than the Ethiopian. Just as He took the children of Israel from Egypt, He says, so too He took the Philistines from Caphtor, which is Crete and the Syrians from Southern Babylon, which is Kir. They aren't the only nation taken and moved by God to a new land, and made mighty. And they aren't the only people He chooses to destroy. It is humbling to know He thinks no more of these people, called by His name and who betrayed Him, than the heathen nations who are their enemies. Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth; saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the Lord. Because that remnant of Jacob will lead to Christ, and the promise the Lord made unto David, and the place, Jerusalem, which He placed His name, in Jesus. He sifted them as He does all nations. And all the sinners of His people slain. Wew. With the promise of wrath and destruction, God the long-suffering and merciful offers that blessed hope. In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this. Jesus, the Son of David, restored to His throne in His Kingdom. And the promise is not just to believing Israel, or to the "Jews," but even to Edom, to the heathen which are called by His name. To the remnant of the Gentiles that believe on Christ. His people, Israel, to the paradise of His eternal Kingdom. And they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them, saith the Lord thy God.

One thing to note regarding God's destruction of Edom, this follows hundreds of years of blessing them with the land of Seir which was promised unto Esau. But their betrayals against Israel, worship of false gods, taking advantage to raid Jerusalem with the Babylonians, it was enough and God took their land and made it desolate. So many dispensationalists rest their Zionism on "God keeps His promises!" with no recognition or understanding that covenants have conditions. That God judges nations on earth. Here we have an example of a promised land, kept by God, given warning by God through David, and ultimately destroyed for their iniquities. But there were remnants of Edom still. After desolation by the Nabateans, they migrated to the southern part of Judea and came to be called Idumeans. We are told by history that in B.C. 47 Julius Caesar made Antipater, a "wily Idumaean," "procurator of Judea, who divided his territories between his" "four sons, Galilee falling to the lot of Herod, who was" "afterwards appointed tetrarch of Judea by Mark Antony (B.C. 40). Herod the great, told of Jesus' birth by the three wise men, orders the slaying of all males under the age of 2 throughout the land. Matthew 2:1:2 Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, aying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him. Matthew 2:16 Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men. After his death, Joseph is told to return from Egypt, where they had fled with Jesus. Then Herod's son, Herod Archelaus took power. Then there was Herod Antipas. This is the Herod who had John the Baptist killed and questioned Jesus before the crucifixion. There is Herod Agrippa I who had James martyred, whose death is mentioned in Acts 12. Agrippa II was to whom Paul preaches to in Acts 25 and 26. Bunch of Herods. In the end, we are told by history, when there was a rebellion against Rome in 70AD, it included the ethnic line of Judah. The remnants of Benjamin and Levi. And whatever Edomites who remained. All constituted what became known collectively as Jews. And, according to the history, all were wiped out and scattered abroad, forbidden by Rome to return to Judea. Much speculation has risen out of these events and about these people. It is a rabbi hole that can be fascinating to go down, but what matters really is what God's word clearly says. We can't know anything else for certain, as it becomes arguing genealogies and Jewish fables. What I believe is that, because there is no genetic or ethnic role in salvation, that it is individual souls that are saved, that flesh profiteth nothing, that to here is neither Jew nor Greek, pursuit of the racial lines of Edom and Jews, the tribes of Israelites, etc, should really only be looked at in a carnal, earthly way. A fun pass time. Something to wonder about in our idleness. Spiritually, whatever happened to them is irrelevant. We know Jews, falsely so-called, Synagogue of Satan, those who say they are Jews but are not, are spiritually Edom. Regardless of what Kaiser Sose origin story they muddy the waters with. They were taken out of the physical promised land for rejection of Christ. Whatever claim they had to the promise ended with the fulfilment of the blessing, which is in Jesus. And if the Jews who are spiritually Edom, who sold their birthright and blessing for earthly things, are actual sons of Esau, who is Edom, seeking to steal back the birthright Jacob took, it doesn't change anything for us who are spiritually Israel. We know they are antichrists. We know the Gospel is the truth. We look forward to a better country, a kingdom we are inheritors of through God's grace and mercy, in Christ. Let them squabble over dessert sand. Let them persecute us in Jesus' name. We have already overcome.

During the reign of King Jeroboam II of Israel, many prophets were turned towards the northern kingdom to preach the word of God, and the southern kingdom, then under the rule of Uzziah. Amos was a contemporary of Jonah. They preached repentance towards the truth of God, in the face of sin in the land and fearsome threats of their neighbors, primarily at this time against the Assyrians. So when Jonah is called by God to go preach in Nineveh, a city in the heart of Assyria, to warn them of their pending destruction, Jonah refuses the Lord. Jonah is faithful and fearful of God. He is a saved believer, who has understanding of God's wrath and power. Yet he risks running away to avoid preaching to the heathen as the burden of the Lord came upon him. While Jonah may have feared for his safety, going among the heathen who had warred against Israel and Judah, as we will see, he simply did not wish to give his enemies the chance to hear the truth and avoid God's wrath. And we all know the story. He sets out for Spain, the exact opposite direction. Hiring passage on a ship. And the storm comes up on them, and the men of the vessel vainly call upon their false gods, before determining that Jonah was the source of their tribulation. And that the God he had testified to them was responsible for the tempest. Ultimately, Jonah offers his life for theirs, and they reluctantly cast him overboard where he is swallowed by a great fish, prepared by God for this purpose. And Jonah spends three days and nights in its belly. We are also all familiar with the picture of Christ in Jonah. Matthew 12:38-41 Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from thee. But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here. Christ being greater than Jonah, or any other man, is obvious (although not to the Jews seeking after a sign). But the picture of the Son perfectly obeying the will of the Father, even unto death, that His enemies be given a chance at repentance towards the truth of the gospel contrasts starkly with the prophet who did all he could to avoid it. It is funny how, despite Jonah not wanting to preach the Lord to the heathen, he still manages to get the men of Joppa to believe on the Lord God. He is literally the worst prophet and yet God uses him mightily. Often Christians are reluctant to preach the word to others. We bury our talent of silver. We put our light under a bushel. We flee to Tarshish, running to the things of this world seeking to avoid our responsibility. And even in our dereliction, God uses us to proclaim His truth. How much more so if we let Him shape us into worthy vessels? We shouldn't need to be swallowed up by a whale to be dragged back to where we need to be to do God's will. But if that's what it takes, He won't hesitate. It is hard to kick against the pricks, as Jesus said to Saul on the road to Damascus. The Bible says to know to do good and to do it not is a sin. Make this new year the year you dedicate yourself to doing the will of the Lord. To soul-winning and preaching His word, even to your enemies. To stop running away. Don't make God send the storm.

Psalm 18:4-6 The sorrows of death compassed me, and the floods of ungodly men made me afraid. The sorrows of hell compassed me about: the snares of death prevented me. In my distress I called upon the Lord, and cried unto my God: he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, even into his ears. Psalms 16:10 For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption Jonah 2 in light of the Gospels, shows the reluctant prophet as a type of Jesus, the willing Son. The three days and nights in Hell being the sign Jesus said would be ignored by the Jews, even as the Gentiles of Nineveh received the word. The prayer of Jonah echos many lines of the Psalms, where David cries out for salvation, calling upon the name of the Lord for relief. Psalm 69:1-3 Save me, O God; For the waters are come in unto my soul. I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me. I am weary of my crying: my throat is dried: Mine eyes fail while I wait for my God. The form and function of the prayer, like the Psalms, show us how we should be in times of distress and tribulation. Constantly turning to the Lord to be our salvation, remembering His loving kindness. Thanksgiving in the face of adversity. Knowing God will not forsake you or fail you. When we are at the end of our rope, our soul fainting, we can know He hears us. Even at the depths of the sea. Even were we in Hell itself. The Lord hears and delivers us. Amen. They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy. Don't deceive yourself when faced with chastisement of the Lord. Don't tell yourself lying vanities about your situation and the sin that led you there. God is long-suffering and merciful to a humble heart, calling out to Him. But you forsake mercy when you stay in denial. For whatever else Jonah was, he did not deny his sin. He willingly gave himself up for the sailors on the ship. He admitted to God that he was lost without His mercy. 1 John 1:7-9 But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. Confession of our sin to God is not for His sake, although a lying tongue is a thing that He hates. Confession, telling the truth in our heart about what it is we have done, what we do, is for our sake; that we may know His mercy and forgiveness and be cleaned from all unrighteousness. Internalizing this mindset when it comes to your walk with God is a key to understanding and growing in faith.

And so we find Jonah where God needed him to be, finally, reluctantly, and the prophet preaches to the Assyrians of Nineveh of the judgment of God against them, and that in 40 days they shall be overthrown. The hearts of those in the city, from least to great to king, all believe the word of God, and turn from their wicked ways, putting away from the violence, and God seeing their works, repented of the evil He had said He would do, and did it not. This sincere conversion of faith in the word, led not only to turning from sin but to mourning of it, in sackcloth and fasting. It is worth noting that the Lord gave them 40 days to get right, and it looks like they did almost immediately. God is generous and merciful for giving second chances. Given the proximity and the back and forth war, and peace and trade, many Assyrians had heard of and seen the works of the God of Israel. Many seeds were sown, and watered for this one man to bring forth this much fruit. Long before Jonah was called, the Lord had helped create fertile ground in their hearts. Just as Jonah had no understanding of what God had in store, and ran from the divine appointment the Lord had arranged, we have no idea the place people we meet are in. How much work has been done by the Spirit before us. John 16:7-11 Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged. The Spirit is ploughing the hearts and minds of the world. Reproving them. God's mercy is revealed from Heaven in those of us who have believed. His wrath against the ungodly. By creation itself, that men have no excuse. But the Spirit works on them too, with the conscience given every man, to reprove sinners. And so when Jesus says the harvest is plentiful, but the laborers few, he is talking to us. How often are we Jonahs, running from the calling? He led an entire gentile city of Idolatry to call upon the name of the Lord. The rewards for such works are great in Heaven. Matthew 6:19-21 Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: for where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. How much gold, silver and precious stones do we leave by the wayside for not responding to the call like Jonah? 1 Corinthians 3:12-15 Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire. How can they believe if there is no preacher? Romans 10:14-15 How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! The story of Jonah is about soul-winning. It is about the tendency of saved believers running from this obligation. Of having a bad spirit, fear, resentment towards others, lacking the mercy and compassion of the Lord that He has graciously given us, and denying it to others. Of covering the light with a bushel. Preach the gospel to every creature. Praise the good news and glad tidings to the ends of the earth. Let God use you for great things, refining you in the fire that you may be even more useful to Him. Don't be like Jonah. Especially as we will see in Jonah 4.

Poor Jonah, used mightily by God and miserable in his anger. Still hoping Nineveh be destroyed, praying for it. Willing to sit and wait for its destruction, while knowing and acknowledging the Lord is merciful and longsuffering, even to Assyrians who are enemies of Israel at this time. Stubborn to the end, telling God he'd rather die angry than get a good spirit, and see things the way the Lord sees them. And God prepares a gourd, as He had a great fish, and it grows in a night and gives Jonah shade for a day. And He prepared a worm to wither it in the night, killing it. And God prepared a fierce East wind, a cloudless sky from it, and Jonah fainted from the sun, wishing he could die. God asks again if Jonah's anger is serving him well; Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And stubborn Jonah says it is well with him to be angry, even unto death. The prophet seething. God shows him that he has pity for the plight of a gourd, which Jonah had no hand in making, but took the shade from, and yet none for a city of 120,000. God made the gourd and made the men (and much cattle), and it was His mercy to give. Showing the people right from wrong through His word, preached by Jonah. It's a tough lesson. There's no indication that Jonah learned it. He may have been angry unto death at this. A poor spirit throughout. And yet the Lord showed the same mercy and longsuffering to him as the Ninevites. Matthew 5:44-45 But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust. Romans 9:15-16 For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy. Proverbs 25:21-23 If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee. The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue. Perhaps the hardest thing in the Christian life, showing mercy to those who hate us and whom we hate. But if God chooses us to be a blessing to another, it isn't on us to question why. We shouldn't be as Jonah. And if they are hardened against us, that's on them. Our mercy will be as hot coals upon their head. Romans 12:20 Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head. Note the spiritual application of this. Your enemy hungers and thirsts. For what? Food and water? Or truth and the repentance unto faith in Christ? Will the coals of fire make them angrier and dug in against you? Or remind them of the Hell that awaits them? Will you withhold that bread that came down from Heaven? The waters of life that you've drank? Are there many who don't know their right hand from left? Only God knows. Remember the mercy God showed you, and let that be what guides your spirit. Don't be as Jonah, and let your anger consume you. You have pity on the things God prepared for you when they are gone. The trivial and incidental blessings, like the shade of a gourd. When God prepares you to be that gourd, to be a blessing to others, let him use you. Don't let the worm of anger eat away and wither you.

Continuing the prophets, Micah is preaching in the time before the destruction of Israel and the desolation and captivity of Judah, in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. His burden of the Lord, the word come upon him, is very specific and clear. He lists places in Samaria and Judah, their sins and the destruction that's due them. It is amazing how the Lord sent so many prophets, even those not mentioned in scripture, with the same warnings against their idols, graven images, false religion and worship of foreign gods, fornication, murder...and it largely went unheeded. Just like modern times. And as with modern times, the prophets also brought the hope of salvation in the heir of God, the glory of Israel, the Messiah, Christ Jesus. Then, as now we are to preach the whole word of God, rebuking sin, spelling out the wrath that is to come, while showing the redemption possible for individuals who believe on the Lord. The promise of the Father to deliver us through His Son. The Word of God made flesh. All the prophets gave witness, speaking by the word of God. That word became flesh. The promise kept just as surely as the promise to destroy Israel and the high places and groves and walled cities came true. Amen. Continuing a thought from the study of Hosea; Christ could be preached to unbelievers through the book of Micah, just as Jesus was preached to the Ethiopian Eunuch by Phillip, using Isaiah 53. Micah, like the other prophets, preached judgment for sin, the holiness of God, the truth of His mercy and His Messiah, and redemption by faith in His word, and a call to sanctification and separation for us once saved. We are blessed to have the clear Gospels, but you can see how there were always a righteous remnant. 7,000 who hadn't bowed the knee to Baal. How the Old Testament was entirely about Jesus and salvation has always been by faith, calling upon the name of the Lord.

One of the most common push-backs against the gospel by unbelievers is "if God is real and just, why do bad things happen?" And "What about those people and their sins, which are so much worse than mine?!" It is a way for them to dodge responsibility for their own sins, and avoid judgment against themselves. Hypocrisy. But Christians shouldn't struggle with an answer to the charge. The Bible is not only about the grace and mercy God extends towards sinners in Christ, and the promises of forgiveness and redemption, but it is a book of judgments against evildoers. It is evidence of God's wrath against the workers of iniquity, and His promise to those who are meek and humble that their oppressors will surely be punished by an almighty Lord. Revelation 6:9-10 And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth? Vengeance is mine, sayeth the Lord, and He will repay. They shall reap what they've sown. Micah preaches against Israel, those children of Jacob who have done wickedly. Woe to them that devise iniquity! They shall have their reward. Those who covet and steal, by force and violence. Who take what isn't theirs and even taking a man's inheritance. God says He has devised evil against them that He will not allow them to escape. That what they've spoiled will be taken from them. That what they own will be stripped away. They won't have even the inheritance cast by lots as sons of Jacob, because they shall be made desolate by His judgement against them. These wicked people who try to silence preaching of the word against them, because the word of God shames them. In the Great White Throne judgment where the dead are judged and cast into the lake of fire, the Bible says they shall be judged by the books of scripture; by the law: Revelation 20:11-12 And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them. And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works. Preaching the whole council of God, in season and out, reproving the world of their sin, makes the wicked angry in their shame. They hate the righteousness of God. God says, Do not my words do good to him that walketh uprightly? They are for our own instruction and admonition, that it be well for us. Yet the wicked hate the truth. They seek darkness, and spurn the light. The charge against the children of Israel that they pull off both robe and garment from peaceful passersby shows the level of petty wickedness they engage in. It brings to mind Jesus' instructions to us that is any take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also. Our meekness isn't a weakness. It shows the just judgment against those petty enough to rob us. It provides them with the opportunity to feel shame for their actions. Turning the other cheek gives them to opportunity to affirm their rejection of God and His law, or to be shamed and humbled before it. But these wicked people don't want to hear it. They want to hear preaching that justifies their sins, their violence and drunkenness. Finally, Micah again prophesying about Christ: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men. The breaker is come up before them: they have broken up, and have passed through the gate, and are gone out by it: and their king shall pass before them, and the Lord on the head of them. This promise is to we who are saved, who are the Israel of God and seed of Abraham by faith as much as it applies to believers in the Old Testament. We should take comfort that the enemies of the Lord, haters of truth, the violent and degenerate, the thieves and the liars, all will face God's wrath. That they chose evil and rejected the opportunity to be saved. That God will repay. Why do bad things happen? Men decide to do them. Why does God "allow" it to happen? He doesn't, but instead visits evil upon evil. We can rejoice knowing the wicked will have their day of judgement, even as we praise Him for our salvation with fear and trembling.

Tutus 1:10-11 For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake. Jude 1:11 Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. Isaiah 30:9-13 That this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the Lord: Which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits: Get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us. Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon: Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant. Jeremiah 6:14 They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace. Micah 3 turns the prophet's focus on the false teachers and prophets, and the people who, having itching ears and wishing to not hear the word of God, but soothing things, justifying their sin. The violence of what they are doing is conveyed as flaying skin and biting with their teeth, breaking bones and devouring them. As Jesus preached in Matthew 23:14-15 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves. The seers and diviners will be made ashamed, their prophecy and predictions failing. They will seek God, and there will be no answer. The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? none evil can come upon us. For filthy lucre's sake, they give the false sense of security and peace with God, while allowing the abominations of the people run wild. Joel Osteen and the like do it today. Feel-good, hollowed-out, carnal Christianity. The Catholics and other denominations, putting their accumulation of riches and power above the truth of God. That abhor judgment, and pervert all equity, building up blood against the nations. The wrath of God is upon them. And all will be settled by His rod of iron. Amen.

Isaiah 2:1-4 The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem. And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord's house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more. Jeremiah 31:6 For there shall be a day, that the watchmen upon the mount Ephraim shall cry, Arise ye, and let us go up to Zion unto the Lord our God. John 6:45 It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me. Micah 4 sees the prophecy of the Lord, Christ Jesus, and the Millennial Kingdom to come, concepts repeated in the other books of the prophets, the blessed hope we have in Christ, an inheritance incorruptible. The birthing pangs of Israel, during the time of the prophet; the destruction of Israel, bringing it low, and the captivity of Judah, all serve to bring about the conditions needed for Jesus' birth. Establishing God's word, made flesh. And there, in Mount Zion, holy Jerusalem, the place the Lord has placed His name forever, shall Jesus rule and reign. Hebrews 12:22-29 But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect, And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel. See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape, if we turn away from him that speaketh from heaven: Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven. And this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain. Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear: For our God is a consuming fire.

Here in Micah 5 the prophet gives the word of God clearly and easily understandable to us, the coming of Christ Jesus in peace and deliverance, and His second coming, bringing wrath and destruction on the heathen nations. There's prophecy about the end of Assyria, which was brought low by the Babylonians after its destruction of the Northern Kingdom of Israel, keeping the Assyrians from doing the same to Judah. But primarily, this chapter is about Christ. It hardly needs any commentary, it is so clear. Birth in Bethlehem. Smiting the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek. The ruler coming forth from Judah who's going forth have been from old, from everlasting. Jesus. The unbelieving Jews, so-called, who today say "Jesus doesn't appear in the Old Testament! None of the prophecies fit!" are liars. Antichrists. If they believed Moses and the prophets they'd believe on Him. But they reject the Son and have not the Father, despite being blessed with the oracles of God. Reading the prophets, I am constantly reminded of 1 Corinthians 15:1-4; Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand; By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain. For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures. It was always according to the scriptures. It was foretold. Jesus is the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. He is of old, from everlasting. The same yesterday, today and forever. Amen. We have a more sure word of prophecy. These things are written that we may know we have eternal life. That God's report is true, and every man who receives it not is a liar.

Numbers 23:5-12 And the Lord put a word in Balaam's mouth, and said, Return unto Balak, and thus thou shalt speak. And he returned unto him, and, lo, he stood by his burnt sacrifice, he, and all the princes of Moab. And he took up his parable, and said, Balak the king of Moab hath brought me from Aram, out of the mountains of the east, saying, Come, curse me Jacob, and come, defy Israel. How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? or how shall I defy, whom the Lord hath not defied? For from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I behold him: lo, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations. Who can count the dust of Jacob, and the number of the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his! And Balak said unto Balaam, What hast thou done unto me? I took thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast blessed them altogether. And he answered and said, Must I not take heed to speak that which the Lord hath put in my mouth? Numbers 31:16 Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the LORD in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the LORD. Micah 6 sees the prophet giving to the people of Israel the testimony of the Lord, Who is making His case to the world against those who had been His people. And even as Balaam could not but speak the words God gave him to speak, the prophet Micah rings out the charges against his countrymen. The Lord reminds them of His grace towards them, leading them out of Egypt, delivering them through the wilderness into the land they now possess (though not for long). He reminds them of Balaam being unable to curse them, at Balak the Moabite's hire. The righteousness of God is evident in the righteousness of the people. How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? or how shall I defy, whom the Lord hath not defied? But even so, the council of Balaam was that if you wanted to curse the children of Israel, Balak had to make them sin against the Lord. And so Moab sent her daughters to commit whoredoms with fornication and bringing idols and false gods among them, until God sent a plague to smites His people, they had brought a curse on themselves. The Lord reiterates His often stated position that it isn't the blood of rams and goats that pleases Him, but faith and mercy and judgement. To do justly and walk humbly with God. The blood offerings were a picture of Christ. Not the means of salvation themselves. What good are dead works if they aren't given in faith? Trappings of religion rather than pure religion, undefiled; James 1:27 Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world. As Jesus rebuked the Pharisees; Matthew 23:23 Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. In His displeasure, God tells them that His longsuffering mercy is over. That those who deal violently, dishonestly and with lies are now going to be punished by His wrath, and none shall stand. Therefore also will I make thee sick in smiting thee, in making thee desolate because of thy sins. Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy casting down shall be in the midst of thee; and thou shalt take hold, but shalt not deliver; and that which thou deliverest will I give up to the sword. Thou shalt sow, but thou shalt not reap; thou shalt tread the olives, but thou shalt not anoint thee with oil; and sweet wine, but shalt not drink wine. They walk in the statutes of Ahab and his wicked father, Omri. Worshiping false gods while doing wickedly. And now they will be made a desolation. A reproach. A hissing. A warning and parable among the nations. God revealed by His wrath upon those who were His people, and who chose to go the way of Balaam instead.

Luke 12:51-53 Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three. The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. Micah 7, the final chapter of this book of prophecy. Micah was a contemporary of Isaiah and Hosea, and prophesied during time before the tragic fall of the Northern Kingdom of Israel to the Assyrian Empire. Yet, as we have seen, much of his preaching is of Christ. Of the Lord as a redeemer, full of mercy. Micah laments that the fruit of the vine is picked clean. There are none that do good, all are evil. The good men perished off the earth. Princes and judges are corrupt, seeking bribes. The mighty men, dishonest and cruel. He advises that as their destruction is nigh, trust not a friend, or a guide, or even your lover. Better to keep silent than be betrayed. There is dual prophecy here, both of the prophets near future, and the time of reformation in Christ. Verse 6 is quoted by Jesus, explaining what the division and distrust will be from; following Him. Unbelieving relatives and friends will betray us, yet He is faithful. The enemies are in our own house. If we can't trust leaders, or the walls and watchmen set to protect us. If we can't trust our friends or relatives because of their iniquity, what shall we do? Look unto the Lord and wait for the God of our salvation. God will hear and deliver us. Our enemies will be made ashamed by His glory. I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness....Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy. Here is the faith we have in Christ and the grace of God the Father. That despite our sins and the wages of death they have purchased, we have the Council of Christ. Jesus is our mediator, Who pleads our case with His imputed righteousness covering our debts. We are pardoned for our inequities. God's grace is due to His mercy, which He delights in. He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea. Psalm 103:1-15 Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies; Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle's. The Lord executeth righteousness and judgment for all that are oppressed. He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel. The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy. He will not always chide: neither will he keep his anger for ever. He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities. For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is his mercy toward them that fear him. As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us. Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him. Great is the mercy of our God, and the righteousness of Christ Jesus, that we may be forgiven in Him! Amen To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.

Nahum the Elkoshite, which may be a gentile city, had the word of the Lord to deliver against Nineveh, the Assyrian city, that today is located in the Mosul area of Northern Iraq. This is 100 years after Jonah, who was given the same burden against Nineveh, that led to a revival and temporary stay of the wrath of God. Jonah 3:10 And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not. Unlike Jonah, Nahum appears more than willing to go to the heathen with this message of warning. Nineveh was filled with violence and Idolatry, their fish God, Dagon and their queen of heaven goddess, Inanna. (These are linked to the Catholic Church, but that's a different post for another day). Assyria had acted as the means of destruction for the northern kingdom of Israel, who were utterly wiped out as punishment by God for the sin of worshipping false gods, sodomy and other abominations. But now, God turned His wrath on them. This is a similar pattern of what we saw on the prophecies against Babylon, from Zephaniah and Habakkuk. That the instrument used for the destruction of Judah would itself be judged. God judges nations. Here in Nahum 1, the Lord promises their destruction, while giving warning to Judah. The wicked nation of Assyria that had made their brothers desolate in Israel, now becomes a warning and reminder to the remnant nation of the Southern kingdom to stay faithful. And in it, a promise of Christ, a deliverer, him that brings good tidings, publishing peace.

Nahum 2 continues the prophecy of Nahum, preached against the Assyrian city of Nineveh, warning against their pending judgment by God against them. Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian hordes are coming to destroy the great city of an empire, and the Lord has given them this warning. That because they had destroyed Israel, spoiling her to desolation, cutting off their vine, that is ending their lineage, and attacked Judah, now the hammer of the Earth is upon them, he that dasheth in pieces. Jeremiah 50:22-23 A sound of battle is in the land, and of great destruction. How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations! Now Babylon has come against Nineveh to make it desolate too. The word of the Lord says to the men of Nineveh to ready their armaments, defend their ramparts, to do everything they can to defend the city, but it will be futile. They are going to be destroyed. Red with blood as their armies are, and the fir trees shall shake, the proud men of the city, so far above others, trembling at the chariots of the Babylonians. The gates of the rivers, the city entrance at the Euphrates, shall be opened and the palace dissolved, overrun and emptied. Their queen led away captive, Huzzab, the established one, brought out by her maids to horror and shame. Despite the age of the city and it's might, they will flee from its destruction and not look back. When God decides to use a nation as His hammer, to visit wrath upon another in judgment, He doesn't mess around. Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts. Are there any more frightening words to hear than that? Our God is a consuming fire. And it is a fearful thing to fall into His hands.

The final prophecy against Nineveh by Nahum the prophet. The city is gone and there is no escape from the judgment. That bloody city, the armies that laid waste to other nations, and had corpses piled about them, now it was their turn. Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts. The comparison of Nineveh and the Assyrian empire to the whore of Babylon in Revelation seems obvious; Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters: With whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication. The adultery of the whore, leading nations from God and to worship her idols and false gods and goddesses, to become drunk on the wine of her fornication. To sell nations through her whoredoms and witchcraft. Isn't that the spirit of Babylon? Wasn't it upon Assyria? And then upon Babylon herself, the Medes and the Persians. The Greeks and the Romans. And even to this day there is that spirit of rebellion and Idolatry, adultery and bloodshed. Abominations. The prophet reminds Nineveh of the city of No, in Ethiopia. A mighty city between Egypt and Ethiopia, upon many waters, defended well by natural defenses. And the Assyrians cut it down. Now they would feel the same wrath, as Nebuchadnezzar, the Chaldeans and the Medes, came to destroy their capital. Again, the word of God mocks them in their tribulation. He says build up your defenses. Lay brick and mortar. It won't matter. There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous. And just as He promised, and as Nahum preached, Nineveh was destroyed. 1 Corinthians 10:11 Now all these things happened unto them for examples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come. When Jesus came to the world as the son of man, it was not as the prophets of old. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. His mission was to show there is peace and goodwill available with the Father, to preach repentance and salvation, grace and mercy to heal the sinner and gather the lost. But, even in that, as he neared the cross, Christ preached hard against the sin of the Pharisees and the Jews, their destruction to come for the blood of the prophets, and the blood of Christ that they would shed. The other prophets that came before Christ preached wrath and destruction, of His coming and salvation, but never a man spoke as He did. But, most of the prophecy of the wrath of His judgment, Jesus gave warning through John, in Revelation. Today, many ignore the warnings outright. Some argue endlessly about the details, claiming knowledge and insight about the people and events, ascribing to current political and religious leaders traits of the beast and Babylon, and still more choose to believe the hey will be taken out of the way before Tribulation comes, and so they check out, and miss the point for believers. We are to preach the same message of salvation, mercy and grace to every creature. To share the gospel far and wide. Not to hunker down in fear, in remote villages, or cabins in the woods. Not to dwell in chat rooms and online platforms seeking "hidden knowledge." We are to gather together, in real life, even more so as the hour draws nigh; Hebrews 10:24-25 And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching. And let us share the good news of salvation in Christ to every creature, now before the judgment comes. And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature. The great commission is a command. The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord. The time to be Nahum will come. But for now we are to be as Jonah, and bring the truth of God's mercy to an evil and untoward generation. To a people who know not God. And who knows, maybe they will turn from their wicked ways and God will repent of the evil He would do. Even if it is for only a hundred years or so, as was the case in Nineveh, in the time between the revival a reluctant Jonah led, and the destruction Nahum preached. It is still more souls won to the Lord and to Him the increase.

Habakkuk was a prophet and contemporary of Jeremiah, preaching during the time leading up to and during the Babylonian captivity. He begins by saying the burden which he did see. Just as in Jeremiah we see that the prophets called being given the word of God the burden of the Lord. Jeremiah 23:36-40 mocks the false prophets who continually claim the burden of the Lord. But Habakkuk sincerely carries this burden, beginning with his crying out to the Lord in anger and frustration at the state of Judah in his day. There is violence, strife, contention and spoiling or thefts, the law isn't being enforced and corruption keeps right judgment from being made. The wicked are prospering and are protected by the government while the righteous are victimized. Sounds familiar. In verse 5, God begins to respond. The Lord says He will work a wonder in the prophet's days, rising up the Chaldeans, the Babylonian empire, and they will invade Judah and possess it. God says they are terrible and mighty, even their horses like leopards fiercer than wolves. That their armies will gather up Judah to captivity, scoff at their kings, and the cities will be destroyed by them. God also gives Habakkuk the prophecy that the king of Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar, shall take credit for this wonder God wrought against Judah. Then shall his mind change, and he shall pass over, and offend, imputing this his power unto his god. (This is fulfilled in Daniel 4, another study for another day) Habakkuk replies, respectfully but a bit incredulous. Art thou not from everlasting, O Lord my God, mine Holy One? we shall not die. O Lord, thou hast ordained them for judgment; and, O mighty God, thou hast established them for correction. Thou art of purer eyes than to behold evil, and canst not look on iniquity: wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy tongue when the wicked devoureth the man that is more righteous than he? He asks how God could use the wicked Nebuchadnezzar and the heathen Chaldeans to destroy Judah, that as bad as it is, they are still more righteous than Babylon. They make men no more than fish to be caught in nets, slaying nations, and then worship the net rather than the Almighty God who established them. Worshiping the creature more than the Creator. Therefore they sacrifice unto their net, and burn incense unto their drag; because by them their portion is fat, and their meat plenteous.Shall they therefore empty their net, and not spare continually to slay the nations? He asks, what about their judgment? It is so familiar to us, today, and likely this story resonated with believers throughout Biblical history. We decry our own nation falling from grace to judgment.
