We call out to God to deliver us, to punish the wicked, and set right the sins in the land. A Christian nation that has fallen away. But when God rises up the heathen, the wicked, the Muslim and the Jew and the pagans of India and the godless of China, and we are beset from all sides by the worst, whom God has raised up, we ask how can this be that the wicked devoureth the man that is more righteous than he? But God will explain that while He may use the wicked to judge the more righteous, they too will face His judgement.

Habakkuk 2 continues the prophet's dialogue with God and the burden places on him by the Lord. Habakkuk compares his waiting for the word as a watchman on a tower. Having asked God why, as evil as Judah is, that wicked Babylon would be used to destroy them. He awaits his reproval, and the Lord answered him, telling him to record what He said, in plain words that they may be read and understood, to be preached and affect the hearer. The Lord says the vision He is granting Habakkuk may take a while to come to fruition, but it surely will. The Lord begins describing Nebuchadnezzar, ruler of the Babylonian empire, both specifically and generally as a nation. This is a very common device used by God throughout the prophets. The empire can be the King, the capital city, the empire itself, or its people. He begins, Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith. Contrasting Nebuchadnezzar and his pride with the just, who live by faith places an understanding that for all his power and standing, he is not as the just, the righteousness of believers, humbled to receive God by faith. He drinks, and is proud, and never satisfied, constantly expanding his empire as Hell enlarges, and like death, can't be satisfied. The picture of Nebuchadnezzar's unquenchable desire for more lands to conquer and spoil being like Hell, in that it is continually growing to fit more and more taken into captivity by it, or as consistent and relentless as death, never being satisfied, never being full, is both poetic and insightful to his character, and doctrine. Death and Hell are as an empire ruining nations. But Jesus is victorious over it and delivers us from the captivity. And the people, as the saints in Heaven cry out for God's wrath, seek justice and judgment against Babylon, saying Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? God promises their vengeance will come from Him; Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee; because of men's blood, and for the violence of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein. For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea. Again, as dual fulfillment, this is a prophecy against Babylon and its king, and of the end times. God will repay. Vengeance is His. The whole world will know His glory and righteousness, and woe be unto them that face His wrath. Amen Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink, that puttest thy bottle to him, and makest him drunken also, that thou mayest look on their nakedness! Thou art filled with shame for glory: drink thou also, and let thy foreskin be uncovered: the cup of the Lord's right hand shall be turned unto thee, and shameful spewing shall be on thy glory This is an allegory for the sins of Babylon, and sound doctrine on drunkenness and the warped and perverse results of it. Its neighbors, the nations it takes over and the abominations of false gods they introduce to the captives are compared to alcohol being given to take advantage of another. Similar to the Great Whore, Mystery Babylon; And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication...with whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication. But, it also is a stark reminder of what alcohol does to people, and the disgusting things that come about from it. God promises that for this sin, or leading others to drunkenness that they may be taken advantage of, Nebuchadnezzar's own nakedness will be revealed instead. His own shame and humiliation will be exposed. When we read Daniel 4, we will see this. Finally, Habakkuk receives this gem; What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols? Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach! Behold, it is laid over with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it. But the Lord is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him. The truth of idolatry is its vanity. The idea that man can make a god of his own hands. That there is even a fraction of divinity and power in them is foolishness. And the people who today bow and serve idols, kneeling and offering prayers to them, lighting candles and incense and telling themselves that these lifeless statutes and carvings and molten images are a representation of the holy or divine are just as foolish as the maker of heaven images described here by the Lord. God is in His temple, sitting on His throne. Our God lives, and is not found in anything created by man's hands or in temples made of stone. The earth is His footstool. All creation is a testament to His power.

The final chapter of the prophet Habakkuk is a song, written in the Spirit, apparently upon a stringed instrument for the chief singer to sing. A Shigionoth may be the name of that instrument. It is also thought to be a style of prayerful song, but the Bible defines itself, and the closing verse indicates it was an instrument used to write this prayerful song. Habakkuk writes of his fear of the word of the Lord he received, of the judgment against wicked Judah by the hands of the Chaldeans, and the judgment that will come upon Nebuchadnezzar and Babylon after they are used by the Lord for this purpose. The prophet asks that in the midst of the years, during this time, that in His wrath God remembers His mercy. He recounts that God came up from the South, from Tenant and mount Paran, in the wilderness where the children of Israel came, up towards the promised land. That His glory filled the heavens and the earth full of His praise, His brightness as the light. This is the Lord that was with them, the fathers in the wilderness who entered into the promised land as His people, and He their God. He had horns coming out of His hand...horns being leaders in the Bible, God sets up captains and kings over people and takes them down. He sent pestilence and fire before them, and drove the nations of Canaanites asunder. The mountains scattered and hills did bow, the great nations that were there before Israel. He asks, Was the Lord displeased against the rivers? was thine anger against the rivers? was thy wrath against the sea, that thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation? We know that His wrath was against the people and their abominations. But the prophet is poetically saying that even the mountains and rivers were affected by the fury of God's wrath. Even the oceans deep, and the sun and moon stood still; Joshua 10:13 And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, Until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day. The prophet sings that God marched through the land in indignation and thresh the heathen in anger, while being the salvation and deliverer for His children, and even for salvation with thine anointed, a mention of Christ to whom all prophets gave witness. It is important to remember this, that the promise of salvation in His anointed, (Christ means anointed one, Messiah) was the faith of the Israelites in the wilderness, and of the saved throughout the Old Testament. Habakkuk describes how the Lord destroyed the rulers and delivered the land to them in violence and wrath. And then he says his lips quivered and he trembled and rottenness entered his bones knowing that the same wrathful vengeance was coming against Judah in his day. That the Lord would be doing to them what He did to the people before them. Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls: Yet I will rejoice in the Lord, I will joy in the God of my salvation. Even so, in this time of tribulation and even in the desolation he describes, Habakkuk says he will find joy in the God of his salvation. He will rest in the day if trouble. This is a great illustration of the way we, as saved believers, should approach the Great Tribulation should it come in our day, or even individual troubles we may have. In the midst of days, the Lord remembers His mercy. We have rest. We find joy in the God of our salvation. We would do well to remember this. The Lord God is my strength. Amen.

Jeremiah 23:16-17 Thus saith the Lord of hosts, Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord. They say still unto them that despise me, The Lord hath said, Ye shall have peace; and they say unto every one that walketh after the imagination of his own heart, No evil shall come upon you. When we read the words of the prophets in the Bible, they preach hard against sin and corruption and false ways that man has devised. They tell of the pending judgment of the Lord against the wicked. They tell kings and nations that the wrath is come upon them. Zephaniah preaching in the time before the Babylonian captivity, during the time of Jeremiah and Habakkuk and others, clearly and with power explains what God is going to do to Judah. We can tell the false prophets, Jeremiah says, by their preaching pleasant things that are easy on the ears, preaching "Peace, peace" when there is no peace. That "God is love" and He doesn't judge you, continue in your sin. The world is full of these false prophets today. New Evangelicals and "progressive" Christians and even in some formerly hard preaching Baptist circles. The "seeker sensitive" churches and big time "prosperity Gospel" grifters. The skinny jeans and laser shows and rock concert "worship services," that are "LGBTQ Welcoming" and that push for abortion, broken homes, that biblical families are "oppressive," and teach fornication isn't always a sin. But God's word is clear: I will utterly consume all things from off the land, saith the Lord. Speaking through Zephaniah, the Lord promises that He will cut off the remnant of Baal from the land, the idols and priests, those that worship the stars and the things of heaven, who give lip service to the Lord while swearing to the gods of the Canaanites. Those who seek Him not, and those that refused to seek Him on His terms but made up their own paths. The Lord says that nothing will protect them. Not the walls of the cities, not the caverns they dwell in. That the things they build for themselves they will not partake in. None of their wealth or the things they trusted in over Him will save them from His wrath. Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the Lord's wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land. That's how you can identify a true man of God. They preach hard, a warning, using the word of the Lord, that man may come to repentance and turn towards Him for salvation and mercy, in the hour of tribulation against the righteous, the profit of the wicked and the wrath that follows. Amen

God judges nations. While the judgment of man comes after our physical death (and it is appointed unto men, once to die, but after this the judgment). But the judgment of nations is here on this earth, and is a collective judgment of the people in their land. The prophets, as we have seen, are sent by God with warnings and rebuke, calling the lost to repentance, nations to reform, Kings to fear the Lord. Zephaniah is calling the people of Judah, and ultimately all the world, to turn to the Lord in meekness, seeking righteousness. Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger. He warns of the destruction that will befall all nations that have not turned towards Him, and that persecute His people. The Lord will be terrible unto them. The burden of the Lord upon the prophet says that men shall worship the Lord, every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen. The prophecy of Zephaniah 2 is both to the Jews of his time, but also shows that His people are not confined only to them, but of the meek and humble who believe on His name throughout the world. And the destruction of all nations will be not only to the various nations called out here, but the wrath will be poured out on all the earth against those that transgressed against Him and His people, in the day if the Lord's anger. The day of the Lord is coming. Christ will return in judgment. Before the day passes, before the fierce and terrible day of the Lord come, seek ye the Lord. Before it is too late.

In the first chapter of Zephaniah, we heard the prophet preach rebuke against Judah, and God's pending wrath upon the nation, soon to be taken for 70 years of captivity to Babylon. In the second chapter, Zephaniah preached against all the nations, and their pending judgment. Here in Zephaniah 3, the final chapter of the minor prophet's rebuke, God gives His judgment on Jerusalem herself, that filthy and polluted city. Because those in Jerusalem did not obey the voice of God, receive their correction and turn to the Lord, He promises to destroy the city. Because of the oppression there, the corrupt princes, the leaders of the city who judged unrighteously, their corruption like ravening lions and wolves, greedily making prey of the people. Not even stopping to gnaw the bones. And her prophets were light and treacherous persons, preaching feel-good sermons, saying "peace, peace" when there was no peace. And meanwhile they polluted the sanctuary, and done violence to the law, transgressing and excusing transgressions, calling the word of rebuke that God demands be preached, the "burden of the Lord." But, the Lord is there in the midst of the city. And His judgments were not slack. And yet, for all the fury of God against the ungodly, His wrath against the wicked revealed from Heaven, it was not sufficient to bring them to shame. The Lord's warnings were not heeded; I have cut off the nations: their towers are desolate; I made their streets waste, that none passeth by: their cities are destroyed, so that there is no man, that there is none inhabitant. I said, Surely thou wilt fear me, thou wilt receive instruction; so their dwelling should not be cut off, howsoever I punished them: but they rose early, and corrupted all their doings. The frustration of a holy God, against the people in the very city He chose to place His name, the holy moly they took pride in, where they had the advantage of the oracles of God, the temple and the priesthood, the seat of the King, of the line of David, the wealth and wisdom of Solomon, and the example of the nations all around them being destroyed again and again by His power...the rebuke of the prophets carrying the burden of the Lord...and they would not. The same frustration expressed by Jesus, in their midst, as He was in Zephaniah's time; Matthew 23:37-39 O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord. And so the prophecy given Zephaniah turns to the rebuke facing the holy city in that time. God says he will remove from there the haughty and prideful, the corrupt leaders and wicked men of Jerusalem, killed or carried away into captivity. But, as we saw in 2 Kings, and in Jeremiah, God left behind a remnant, of the poor and the afflicted. Left by Babylon to be laborers in the field. To work the vineyard. To tend to the flocks and be husbandmen to the land. And they shall trust in the name of the Lord. The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid. This prophetic verse refers primarily to those left behind from the captivity, but is also talking about the believers who followed Christ in His ministry, the Apostles and disciples, and applies to the larger Christian population through the ages, and especially to those of us saved, in the resurrection, in New Jerusalem. What a wonderful picture of that glorious day. Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel; be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. The Lord hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy: the king of Israel, even the Lord, is in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more. These final verses are more than just the promise to return the captives from Babylon, 70 years later. It is an eternal promise to we, as believers. Our King in the midst of us, seeing evil no more. Our transgressions gone. No fear. Working the vineyards of the Lord, His servants forevermore. He will save us, and rejoice over us. Singing songs of joy, resting in love. And I will gather them that are sorrowful for the solemn assembly, who are of thee, to whom the reproach of it was a burden. Luke 4:14-19 And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord. And the promise to make us a name among all the people of the earth, to let the unbelieving know that He has loved us, and that we are not ashamed, reminds me of Jesus prophecy in Revelation 3:9; Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. What a wonderful God, Who loves us so! And shame on the dispensationalists who try to take our inheritance and our blessing, and give it to those who hate Christ. To sell this inheritance for a bowl of pottage to those that are spiritual Edom.

Haggai the prophet is given the word of the Lord, in the 70th year of captivity, roughly 520 BC. During the rule of Darius the Great. Cyrus the great, his predecessor had allowed the Jews who wished to, to settle Jerusalem again. Even authorized the rebuilding of the temple. However, after Cyrus death, and the political instability before Darius took the reigns, most Jews remained scattered and the captivity continued, work on the 2nd Temple didn't progress. Here, God says the people live in cieled houses, that is finished and furnished paneled dwellings, as the house of God stood waste. The Lord tells them through the prophet that they are in famine and their efforts amount to nothing, because they have not prioritized His Temple. And so the preaching stirs the heart of Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest. And they began the work of the rebuilding of the 2nd Temple. Ye looked for much, and, lo it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house. How relevant a verse for us today in America, where there are empty churches, dying congregations of senior saints, and no young people there building the local church up. We chase riches and our own wants and desires, and ignore the gathering of the called out assembly of God. It isn't even to labor, though sometimes your job may interfere with attending Sunday service. It is mostly pleasure and leisure, golf and cookouts and youth sports. Shopping. Dining out. Watching NFL, gambling and drinking. We look for much and it comes to little and we wonder why. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house and turn on the 80" 4K, gorging yourself with pizza and wings and beer. If you are not part of a local independent fundamentalist NT soul-winning church, get out and join one. Plug in and pitch in. Build the church of Jesus by building up your local church, and winning souls to Christ.

The word of the Lord concerning the restoration of the Temple by the remnant of Judah, under the government of Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest continues. The work has begun, but not been completed. He shames the elders among them who remember the old Temple, and encourages them that the gold and silver needed will come, if they just build it. God will provide. So many Christians stumble in their walk, establishing the foundation which is Christ, maybe even beginning to do what He has called them to, but then just trail off. They worry about the next steps, not having what they need to succeed in their minds, being discouraged and giving up. But it is God that began that work in you, and it is God Who will provide the materials and circumstances that we need to see it through. Be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts. A couple months later, Haggai in the Spirit inquired of the priests, does that which is holy touching that which is not holy, make it holy? The priests rightly answer, no. And does that which is unclean touch it, shall it be unclean? Yes. Of course. So then that which is holy doesn't make that which is not holy clean, and that which is unclean makes even that which is holy unclean. You can't get something clean and holy out of that which is unholy and unclean by contact. By mingling. A little dirt in water makes all the water dirty. Haggai says this is the state of the people, they have no means of sanctification not having the Temple and the ordinances. And so all the work they offer is unclean. And due to this, the Lord has made their works less profitable than they expect, less oil pressed, their crops covered with mold and disease. God says that even as the foundation is laid, He will bless their efforts again. Again, this has applications in the Christian life. Where we are in sin, and under reproach, feeling like we are never getting ahead. We need to cleanse ourselves, and make ourselves holy, separated unto His work. Then He will bless our efforts. Finally the word comes to Haggai, letting Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, of the line of David know he is chosen, anointed to be king and of his line comes Christ Jesus. Matthew 1:12-16 And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel; And Zorobabel begat Abiud; and Abiud begat Eliakim; and Eliakim begat Azor; And Azor begat Sadoc; and Sadoc begat Achim; and Achim begat Eliud; And Eliud begat Eleazar; and Eleazar begat Matthan; and Matthan begat Jacob; And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ. There is some controversy or confusion among "scholars" given slight variations in the genealogy given in Luke, surrounding both Zerubbabel's father (given as Neri) and different sons named. But these aren't identical genealogies, but giving us Mary and Joseph's lines, and there are explanations offered by many for the apparent discrepancy. I think we shouldn't be worried about it. Titus 3:9 But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.

Zechariah begins with the prophet receiving the word of God, telling him to preach to the people that the Lord wants reconciliation with them. That if they turn to Him, He will restore them. To not be as their fathers, stiff-necked and rebellious, and who didn't harken to Him. Here, at the end of the 70 year exile and captivity, Zechariah's message mirrors Haggai. Zechariah and Haggai were contemporary prophets ministering around 520 BC, during the second year of Darius I of Persia, when the Jewish exiles had returned from Babylon to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple. Haggai’s primary message was to urge the people to resume work on the temple, which had stalled due to opposition and apathy. Zechariah’s visions, including those of the red horses and four carpenters, were similarly meant to encourage the people by affirming God’s presence, judgment on their enemies, and His commitment to restore Jerusalem. The Lord reminds them that their fathers and their prophets are dead. But His word and statutes remain. That the Lord of hosts had done to them according to their ways. They got what they deserve. A short time later, Zechariah is given a vision, a man riding a red horse, standing among myrtle trees, with other horses with him, red horses, red speckled with white and pure white. The angel tells the prophet that he will explain, and as he does, the man among the trees, the Lord of hosts Himself, says that these are they whom the Lord hath sent to walk the earth, to and fro. These answer to the Lord saying they have walked their routes and they found the earth to be still and at rest. There are a few interpretations of this, and what the horses represent. I will tell you mine. That the red are judgment and wrath, war. The speckled are wrath tempered with mercy. The white, the mercy of the Lord upon the people. Their role, to travel about ready to exact judgment on nations. Their report, everything at that moment was at peace. I could be wrong. The. The angel guiding Zechariah asks the man, the Lord of hosts, (pre-incarnate Christ Jesus? I think so. A theophany), he asks "How long wily though not have mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah?" Noting the 70 years they've been desolate. And the Lord answered the angel that talked with me with good words and comfortable words. And the angel instructs the prophet; Cry thou, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy. That He is displeased with the heathen who are at peace, given their role in the desolation and captivity of Judah. That the Lord returns to Jerusalem with mercies, that His house will be rebuilt. That prosperity will spread out from Jerusalem, and the Lord shall comfort Zion, and shall choose Jerusalem. As earlier prophets spoke, the city where the Lord chose to place His name. Then Zechariah receives another vision, seeing four horns, those nations whose rulers scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem. Assyria, Babylonians, Persians and Egypt (in my opinion). And that there were 4 carpenters who come to fray these horns, to cause them terror and to be cast out. Again, there's speculation as to who these four are, or what it means that four builders come and restore Jerusalem. I think the simplest explanation are the 4 figures we are given who are responsible for the restoration of the Temple and the practices among the people. Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest, also contemporaries of the prophets, but also Ezra and Nehemiah. Zerubbabel and Joshua (520 BC), Ezra (458 BC) and Nehemiah (445 BC) came later. This makes sense to me. But again, I could be wrong.

Isaiah 2:2-4 And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the Lord's house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more. Isaiah 26:1-4 In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah; We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks. Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in. Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee. Trust ye in the Lord for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength Isaiah 60:18 Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise. Here in Zechariah 2, we see the prophet again encouraging the people to rebuild and restore, knowing that the Lord is with them and will be their strength, if they only keep His ways. The angel that Zechariah sees in his vision, like those that appeared to Ezekiel and John, is measuring, this time the size of the city, Jerusalem. The angels speak, and the one saying to tell Zechariah that the city will be so large, with the multitude of men and cattle, that there isn't a physical wall to protect them, but a wall of fire, the glory of God in her midst. Similarly, we see in Isaiah this same concept, that God's Salvation is the wall. His salvation is the bulwark. The second major theme repeated from Isaiah is the understanding that all nations shall flow into the city, to Zion. The nation of the righteous who keeps the truth. This has been consistently the promise of God for Judah. And in the Old Testament times of Zerubbabel, and Ezra and Nehemiah, it was a promise to the physical nation, as well as a prophecy of the end times Kingdom that would include all people who believed. That He shall choose Jerusalem again. And when Jesus came, the Messiah, they slew Him and hanged Him on a tree. So it becomes what could have been. So now, in the New and better Testament, there is a similar, but different Kingdom. A millennial Kingdom of believers from all nations, still. And the peace of swords becoming plowshares. But the children of the Kingdom shall be cast out for unbelief. Salvation is the wall. Without faith and trust in that, there is no part for them. But all those that believe are given the inheritance and blessings, the promises of God.

Zechariah 3 presents the prophet with a vision of the high priest Joshua, in the time of Zerubbabel and the restoration of the Temple in Jerusalem. And the angel of the Lord stood before him, and Satan at his right hand to resist him. To accuse him and tempt him. The Lord rebukes Satan, the adversary, just as in Jude, where angels, even archangels, who all are mightier than man, don't bring railing accusations or curses against the Devil, but say "the Lord rebukes thee." There are many who have built an entire ministry on the basis of "rebuking Satan," railing against the devil. Not resisting him, that he flees, but they themselves speaking evil of dignities, railing against things they don't understand. They often come with a false gospel, adding works or strange doctrines. Charismatics and charlatans. But the Lord rebukes Satan here, saying that Joshua was an iron plucked from the fire. His instrument. Even as the Lord set His name on Jerusalem, so He had chosen Joshua to be His high priest. In the vision, Joshua is arrayed in filthy garments. And those that stood before him are ordered to take them away, that the Lord would clothe him in a change of raiment. Making him clean. Just as Jude writes of saving some by fear, pulling them from the fire, hating even the garments spotted by the flesh. Just as Jesus promises to clothe those who believe on His name in white. For the priests of the Old Testament must be cleansed and sanctified, made holy by diverse washings and sacrifices, but Joshua, without the temple and without the purification rituals was made clean by grace through faith by the living God. Joshua is given a fair mitre, a head covering for the office, and fine garments, as the angel of the Lord stood by. And again, we are given a conditional promise to the high priest, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou shalt also judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee places to walk among these that stand by. The angels around him. Then he is told through the prophet, that the Lord will bring forth His servant, the Branch, a promise of Christ Jesus. He says He will lay before Joshua a stone, that rock of salvation as Christ is called; Isaiah 28:16 Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste. As in 1 Peter 2:6-9 Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded. Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed. But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light The image of Christ as the foundation, the corner stone, perfect and square, and the sanctification in Him of the royal priesthood, carrying over from the Old Testament, done away with, and given to a new priesthood of believers, washed clean in the blood. The Lord of hosts says, I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree. That blessed day, at the coming of the Lord of hosts. Amen.

Zechariah 4 11 Then answered I, and said unto him, What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the candlestick and upon the left side thereof? 12 And I answered again, and said unto him, What be these two olive branches which through the two golden pipes empty the golden oil out of themselves? 13 And he answered me and said, Knowest thou not what these be? And I said, No, my lord. 14 Then said he, These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth. Revelation 11 3 And I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and threescore days, clothed in sackcloth. 4 These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth. 5 And if any man will hurt them, fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies: and if any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed. 6 These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy: and have power over waters to turn them to blood, and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will. 7 And when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them. 8 And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified. 9 And they of the people and kindreds and tongues and nations shall see their dead bodies three days and an half, and shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves. 10 And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth. 11 And after three days and an half the spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them. 12 And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them. 13 And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven. 14 The second woe is past; and, behold, the third woe cometh quickly. There are those who falsely teach that end times Bible prophecy is of the past, that the resurrections already happened, that the millennial reign of Christ is figurative or past, that there is no such thing as the believers dead and sleeping as well as those alive being caught up together in the clouds to meet Jesus at his second coming, that the scripture is unknowable and impossible to understand, etc. These false teachers always depend on the ignorance of scripture of their audience, and almost always uses extra biblical sources and the vein philosophies of man to justify their views. But it's scripture like this that they completely overlook or hand wave, because at no time have two witnesses of God come down preaching in Jerusalem, been slain by the beast their bodies lay in the streets for 3 Days visible to the world who rejoice at this, and then, resurrected by God and ascended into heaven in front of the whole world. Clear narratives like this that are found in multiple places in scripture, ignored because it upsets their false doctrines. Revelation 11:3-6 And I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and threescore days, clothed in sackcloth.These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth. And if any man will hurt them, fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies: and if any man will hurt them, he must in this manner be killed. These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy: and have power over waters to turn them to blood, and to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will. We are in Zechariah 4 and the prophet is visited by an angel and a vision, as out of a deep sleep. He sees a golden candle stick with 7 candles, fed by oil from a bowl, with pipes from 2 olive trees beside it. Confused the prophet asks what it is he is being shown. This is pictured in the instructions for the Tabernacle; Exodus 25:31-37 And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same. And six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side: Three bowls made like unto almonds, with a knop and a flower in one branch; and three bowls made like almonds in the other branch, with a knop and a flower: so in the six branches that come out of the candlestick. And in the candlesticks shall be four bowls made like unto almonds, with their knops and their flowers. And there shall be a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, according to the six branches that proceed out of the candlestick. Their knops and their branches shall be of the same: all it shall be one beaten work of pure gold. And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof: and they shall light the lamps thereof, that they may give light over against it. Exodus 27:20-21 And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always. In the tabernacle of the congregation without the vail, which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the Lord: it shall be a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel. In the Bible, such as the Parable of the Ten Virgins (Matthew 25), lamp oil is a symbol of the Holy Spirit and spiritual preparedness. Here it is the same, the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, that it is by God's Spirit he shall restore the temple and Jerusalem. The candles are described as being fed continuously by the two olive trees, so filled with oil they pipe it out to fill the bowls directly from their branches. Without a press and refinement. Pure. In Revelation we learn that the two olive trees that are before the Lord, are the two witnesses. Two great men of God who give prophecy, by the word of God. There are theories as to who these two men are. Many say Moses and Elijah, those who stood glorified with Christ on the mount of transfiguration. Others believe Elijah and Enoch, both taken up into Heaven, translated without death. But it would make sense that either way, the continuous light of God's word, fed with the oil of His Spirit, would be upon the rebuilding of the Temple. Where Zerubbabel had laid a foundation but hadn't completed it yet. The candles themselves represent the Spirit of God upon churches. Upon the house of God. Revelation 1:18-20 I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death. Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter; The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches. The 7 candles are also tied to the 7 Spirits of the Lord; Revelation 1:4 John to the seven churches which are in Asia: Grace be unto you, and peace, from him which is, and which was, and which is to come; and from the seven Spirits which are before his throne; Isaiah 11:2 And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord Revelation 5:6 And I beheld, and, lo, in the midst of the throne and of the four beasts, and in the midst of the elders, stood a Lamb as it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent forth into all the earth. These "spirits" are all aspects of THE Spirit, and are upon Christ Jesus. Note too, the 7 eyes. Zechariah 3:9 For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes: behold, I will engrave the graving thereof, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. This prophecy of Christ is repeated here in Zechariah 4, the seven eyes which are the eyes of the Lord that run to and fro through the whole earth. Omniscience. Short term application, the encouragement to Zerubbabel to finish what they'd started, making it a priority. The need for the Temple to make the place, Jerusalem, sanctified for the purpose of it being where the Lord chose to place His name. For the coming of Jesus. To bring forth the headstone, the cornerstone, the rock the builders rejected. The rock of our salvation, crying out "Grace, grace!" Practical application today, I would say the message to Zerubbabel is the same message to the 7 churches, and is for our edification as well. Build upon the foundation that is Christ. Have the lamps that never go out, fueled by the oil that comes from the word of God, His Spirit poured out like oil. Long-term, the prophecy shows that as it is in Heaven, it will be on earth, and the two witnesses will play their role in the wrath that is to come. Amen.

Zechariah 5 begins a series of very symbolic visions for the prophet. The angelic guides explain their representation, though their ultimate meaning may be left open to interpretation. The first is a vision of a roll, or scroll, a length of parchment flying in the sky, 20 cubits long and 10 wide. The angel says that this scroll contains a curse against those that steal and those that swear, falsely in God's name, that they shall be cut off. That their house shall be consumed and the timber of it. I believe that this means the house, as in the family and the structure, both. This is gone out to the world, not confined to Israel or Judah. God promises there is a recompense for their error. A curse for their sin. Thieves never prosper, and those that swear falsely are eventually done in by their own lies. Then the angel shows Zechariah another vision; an ephah, or basically a measured container, according to Webster's 1832 "an ancient Hebrew dry measure equivalent to a bushel." And in the ephah, a woman representing wickedness, kept in by a lead lid weighing a talent. She is carried by two female angelic beings with wings like storks, to the land of Shinar, which is Babylon. This is cryptic and while we can see what it represents in the text, it is difficult to determine what it means. I think it is the spirit of the whore, Mystery Babylon, being delivered to its place, where that same spirit will rest on empires and kings, who become drunk in her fornication, from Revelation 17; Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters: With whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication. So he carried me away in the spirit into the wilderness: and I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns. And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication: And upon her forehead was a name written, Mystery, Babylon The Great, The Mother Of Harlots And Abominations Of The Earth. And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus: and when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration.

Zechariah is given a vision of four chariots, come from between mountains of brass, representing the four spirits of the heavens. They are given a likeness of horses of different colors. A red horse, a black, a white horse and grisled and bay horses, (speckled or spotted (grisled) and of a reddish-brown (bay) color). The angel says the black go forth into the north country, and the white after them. The grisled go forth to the south. The bay goes to and fro among the earth. The red horse chariot isn't mentioned again in the text. The voice Zechariah hears says that the black and white horses have quieted His spirit in the north country. Reminiscent of this; Revelation 6:1-8 And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seals, and I heard, as it were the noise of thunder, one of the four beasts saying, Come and see. And I saw, and behold a white horse: and he that sat on him had a bow; and a crown was given unto him: and he went forth conquering, and to conquer. And when he had opened the second seal, I heard the second beast say, Come and see. And there went out another horse that was red: and power was given to him that sat thereon to take peace from the earth, and that they should kill one another: and there was given unto him a great sword. And when he had opened the third seal, I heard the third beast say, Come and see. And I beheld, and lo a black horse; and he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand. And I heard a voice in the midst of the four beasts say, A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny; and see thou hurt not the oil and the wine. And when he had opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth beast say, Come and see. And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth. If white were conquest and black famine and pestilence, then the Lord saying He was satisfied with the judgment He had laid upon the north. The Red of war was not part of it. I don't know for sure this interpretation is the correct one, but it would be fitting. In Zechariah 1:8-11, he saw a similar sight; I saw by night, and behold a man riding upon a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees that were in the bottom; and behind him were there red horses, speckled, and white. Then said I, O my lord, what are these? And the angel that talked with me said unto me, I will shew thee what these be. And the man that stood among the myrtle trees answered and said, These are they whom the Lord hath sent to walk to and fro through the earth. And they answered the angel of the Lord that stood among the myrtle trees, and said, We have walked to and fro through the earth, and, behold, all the earth sitteth still, and is at rest. Here, the angel is telling Zechariah that there is peace on the earth at this time, while referencing primarily red horses. This vision seems complimentary to the earlier one. Then Zechariah is given the word of the Lord saying to him to gather 3 men, who had been taken into captivity, and bring them out of Babylon to go to the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, and there make Joshua the high priest of the Levites crowns, and set them upon his head and deliver this prophecy: Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is The Branch; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord: Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. This is a prophecy of Christ, both King and High Priest. The term "The Branch" is a messianic title used elsewhere in the Old Testament, such as Isaiah 11:1 And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots and Jeremiah 23:5 I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper. This signifies a descendant of David, pointing to the Messiah being a son of David. The dual role of Jesus in being both King and Priest is referenced in Hebrews 7:11-28, where Jesus is described as a priest after the order of Melchizedek, who was both king of Salem and high priest.

Here, in the return from the exile in Babylon, the people send men to Jerusalem to inquire about the fasting the Jews had begun while in captivity. They would "weep" during the 5th month, Av, commemorating the time of the desolation of Jerusalem and destruction of the temple. Fasting over their loss. 2 Kings 25:8-9 And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, unto Jerusalem: And he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man's house burnt he with fire. And the Lord mentions the similar fast in the 7th month, commemorating the slaying of the Jewish governor Babylon had set over the people; And as for the people that remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler....But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah. But the word of the Lord comes to the prophet, asking When ye fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh month, even those seventy years, did ye at all fast unto me, even to me? Their fasts were self-centered, remembering their own woes, not to God to bring them out of the situation. Neither were their feasts, when they ate and drank, it was for themselves, not to honor Him. He references the prophets that came before the captivity, Isaiah and Jeremiah and others, who told them what to do to get right and avoid the destruction that came. To show judgment and mercy. Not grand acts of fasting and weeping. When things were good, they ignored the prophets. As things improved with the end of captivity, they still hadn't learned the lesson in many ways. Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, Execute true judgment, and shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother: And oppress not the widow, nor the fatherless, the stranger, nor the poor; and let none of you imagine evil against his brother in your heart. This is what is pleasing to God, not the blood of bulls and goats. Not the religious acts of piety. Not fasts and rituals. To do unto others. To love thy neighbor. To care for the fatherless and widows. James 1:27 Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world. This is what God expects of His people. But they had hardened their hearts. And so God says when He cried to them, they wouldn't hear, and so when they would weep for Jerusalem and the Temple, ultimately for themselves, He would not hear them. That He made Jerusalem desolate for their failure to hear. They should be more worried about that judgment than if they should continue in fasts they invented to console themselves. Today, many Christians worry more about the outward acts of religion over the spiritual things of God. They play church, and make a long pretense of prayer, and get into "worship services," getting ecstatic over worldly sounding music, or engaging in fasts and other rituals, that satisfy their needs and excite the flesh, but do nothing for honoring God or doing what He has commanded us. Dead works and vain traditions, but no mercy or judgment for the lost, the poor, the widow, the fatherless. Luke 18:12-14 I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess. And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted. Hosea 6:6 For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. Matthew 12:7 But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. God doesn't care about where you sit in church, sitting in the chief seats, or your religious acts that show everyone else how holy you claim to be. But He cares about what's in your heart and how you treat others. You can be the most separated person in the pews, but if you look down on others, and hold yourself as better than, you're separated unto yourself. Not the gospel of God. Like these men who inquired of the Lord.

Zechariah 8 begins with the reminder that our God is a jealous God, fearfully protective of His people. Exodus 34:14 For thou shalt worship no other god: for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God He was jealous with great fury. Jerusalem's adultery was an abomination to Him. But now, the Lord says He has returned to Zion, the holy mountain and dwells in the midst of the city, which shall be called the city of truth. Again we see the appeal to the Jews, to do the things God has commanded, and to see these wondrous things come to pass. He promises that once again, the streets would be filled, with old and young. Dwelling in safety, protected by the Lord. Marvellous in their eyes, as well as His. A delight for the Lord to restore them. Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness. What an awesome thing to hear from an all powerful and mighty God. This is the Lord's attitude towards all His children, even today. Even for you. He wants to heal us, restore us and be our God and for us to be His people. What love He has for us! Our God is Jealous. We should be faithful to Him. And so the word of the Lord is preached by Zachariah, that now in the building of the Temple, they shall know prosperity. Men have work, and their efforts bear fruit, the ground shall give her increase, and they shall possess all things. He says that just as they were a curse among the heathen, made a byword for their ways and destruction, so too, He promises they will be a blessing. Because just as He published them when their fathers provoked Him to wrath, and He repented not of what He said He would do to them, now His promise of blessings is just as assured. If... God commands they speak the truth, execute right judgment, in truth and peace, not bearing false witness, or swearing false oaths. Not imagining evil in their hearts towards their neighbors, but loving them. Not doing the things God hates. Proverbs 6:16-19 These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren. Just as the men had asked about the fasting they'd taken up by tradition in exile, the Lord lists all such fasts that they do, and says instead these shall be feasts in Jerusalem if they love the truth and peace. And He promises that if they do these things, it shall come to pass that there shall come people, from all nations and tongues to pray to the Lord in Jerusalem. Even grabbing the hem of the Jew, saying they will go with the , for they have heard that God is with them. Another promise where the Jews fell short to achieve, but that is fulfilled in Christ. They were to be a light unto the Gentiles, to be teachers of the word. Instead they were blind guides, and taught for commandments the doctrines of men. Unable to bring forth fruit. Hypocrites and vipers. So, instead of salvation being of the Jews, as the prophets said, it was by Jesus from the Jews. The promised Kingdom of God delayed, and for His people who believe on Christ, rather than the nation which had all the advantages. Even the oracles of God.

Matthew 21:5 Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass. The burden of the word of the Lord, the inspired prophet speaking the word of God, saying that peace will be on the land, even to the cities of Syria, as all eyes of the nations will be as the tribes of Israel, being towards the Lord. This establishes the prophetic sayings context, towards a future time when all men look to Christ. The greater border, to Tyre, cast down by the Lord despite its wealth, and to Gaza and Ekron, their kings deposed and the land made desolate. Ashod and the Philistines, all under the wrath. This aspect of end times prophecy is cherry picked by modern Jews to justify their goal of Greater Israel. They seek to establish by their own works the Kingdom they've been cut off from. Of course it will come to naught. When Christ establishes His millennial kingdom, the heathen against Him will be gone, leaving only remnants that are for the Lord. Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass. We all know the story from the Gospels, of Jesus triumphant entry into Jerusalem on the foal of an ass, cheered by the Jews who within a weeks time would cry, "Crucify Him!" Jesus, who would deliver peace among the heathen, cutting off the oppression of the chariots and horses, the foreign armies against Israel, had they obeyed the conditional covenants and promises made by God. Still, at His coming we will see Him establish His Kingdom, over the ends of the Earth. By His blood, those prisoners of sin, oh wretched men that we are, set free from Hell. He says to turn to the stronghold, as prisoners of hope rather than sin, and He will render double unto thee. Great is His reward. The Lord makes an allusion that Judah will be bent as a bow, with all Israel as the arrows. That Israel will be against Greece as a sword of a nighty man. It is supernaturally inspired for Zechariah to mention Greece here. At the time of the prophet Zechariah, who is generally dated to around 520–518 BC, during the early Persian empire, Greece was not yet a dominant world power but was emerging as a significant cultural and political force. But it was fragmented city-states and not unified under Alexander yet. As we have seen in Daniel, the Lord has predicted for them the rise of Greece as an empire, and its eventual role during the Ptolemaic period that followed Alexander the Great of destroying Zidon, Tyre, and taming of Syria and Egypt, Philistine and other enemies of Judah. But, in the NT context of the Messiah, the war-like weapons of Jerusalem and Israel against the Greeks becomes a conquest by the gospel. The sword, the word of God. The understanding that it is the Lord of hosts, Jesus Christ, Who is God, shall be their defense. Shall subdue all kingdoms, the King of kings, Lord of all. Not simply a human king. And all the people will rejoice at the harvest. Amen.

Chapter 10 continues the burden of the Lord upon Zechariah, to preach to those returning from exile, to encourage them and give them understanding for the punishment they'd had. The Lord promises them that their prayers will be heard, that the droughts and famine they'd had would be no more, if they turned to Him rather than the idols and false prophets preaching lies, as their fathers did. That the later rain of the late spring would come again when they inquired of Him to provide. These blind guides, vipers, the diviners and those that told them there was peace when there was no peace, kindled His anger. And the sheep they led astray suffered for it. Out of God comes all things. The right angle foundation, the nail that holds, the battle bow and also every oppressor they faced. All of God. The good and the bad. And so, with that knowledge His promise of their being mighty is assured. Faith cometh by hearing. We read and hear His word, and see it is true. The promises of the gathering together of His people out of every nation is a future prophecy for the end. When Jesus gathers the elect. When the Kingdom is established. When He hisses for us, to gather us under His wing as a hen would gather her chicks. Matthew 23:37 O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! But His children by faith will come, for He has redeemed us. Our return unto Him with the increase of our labors, bringing in the sheaves, is a promise. And I will strengthen them in the Lord; and they shall walk up and down in his name, saith the Lord.

Continuing in Zechariah, we see the prophet turn from active encouragement in previous chapters to a more negative message and future prophecy against Judah. The doors of Lebanon, the cedars, the oaks of Bashan, which is the fertile eastern bank of the Jordan, these represent the built temple, the great city Jerusalem, forged by the timber from these areas. Zechariah is prophesying their destruction, when reconstruction has hardly even begun. The leaders, the shepherds, howl at their loss, the young lions roar, because the pride of Jordan is spoiled by false teachers and bad leadership at the judgment of God against them. These wicked leaders, God says, slay the people and hold themselves not guilty. They sell them into servitude and think they are bless by the riches that comes to them for the price of men. The shepherds have no pity for their flock. And God says this is His judgement on the Jews. Sort of the flip side of Jeremiah 3:15 And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding. So, Zechariah preaches the destruction of the people at the hands of their neighbors and the kings and the Lord will not deliver them as He has so many times. As He just had from captivity. This is a future event. God will feed the flock to the slaughter. This all could be a prophecy of 70AD and the destruction of Jerusalem. The temple, as Christ said would come. Not on stone standing upon another. The scattering and spoil of the pride of the Jordan. The burning of the cedars and oaks. Or dual fulfilment with the days of vengeance, the end times prophecy of the destruction of Israel. Luke 21:21-22 Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. The prophet takes up two shepherd staves, and on one staff he writes "Beauty" and the other is called "Bands." He says three shepherds he cut off in one month, and that he hated them and they hated him. False teachers, it seems. I can't say if this is Zechariah rebuking them, and taking their followers away from them, or God speaking directly that He did this to them. Either way, the flock of Judah is then cut off. He breaks the staff "Beauty," which is the covenant with the people. Note the poor of the flock who believed on Him knew this was the word of the Lord. As a prophecy of Christ, and the new covenant that was established, the poor knew Jesus was the Word of the Lord. Then he asks the people for his price as shepherd, and they set it at 30 pieces of silver. The parallel is obvious. Matthew 26:14-15 Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver. The good Shepherd, valued at only a lowly sum, 30 pieces of silver to be betrayed. And says to cast the sum to the potter. Matthew 27:3-7 Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself. And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in. The act of throwing the money to the potter was a symbolic rejection in Zechariah, and the purchase of the potter's field with the money is the fulfilment. Then Zechariah breaks the second staff, "Bands," and says this represents the Jews broken from Israel. As Israel as a nation was long gone at this point, and given the context, it is clearly a prophecy of Christ, and in the New covenant, unbelieving Jews are broken off from the Israel of God, which is made up of all believers. This is followed by a prophecy of an evil shepherd, who treats his flock evilly. The antichrist? Does this mean the hr will have a wounded right arm and right eye? Maybe. I don't know. It would be interesting if this turns out to be the case. He will suffer a fatal wound to the head, we know. It could very well be.

Chapter 12 of Zechariah continues with the burden of the Lord, the word that has come to the prophet, regarding the future of Judah and Jerusalem. With the authority of the omnipotent God, the Lord says this power is upon the protection of Jerusalem, and Judah. That when they will face invasion and siege, His power will protect them, even if all people on the earth come against them. They will be smitten with astonishment, as if they drank of the cup of trembling. That Judah will be as a burdensome stone. The leaders of Judah will see their strength in the people and their faith in the Lord of hosts, their God. Though there be fire all about it, Jerusalem shall stand. The people will be as mighty as David, and the house of David shall be as God, the angel of the Lord before them. The prophecy is a promise to protect Judah and the city of Jerusalem specifically, from all the invasions and wars to come over the next 5 centuries. A promise fulfilled through the time of Jesus, Who of the flesh is of the house of David. "Shall be as God." The prophecy shifts from the historical promise of protection to a future fulfilment in Christ. And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications: and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son... John 19:37 And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced. Interesting to consider that having hundreds of years of divine protection after being thoroughly devastated by the Babylonians, was both a blessing and a curse for the Jews. Obviously they remained under the protectorate God, even as Rome eventually conquered the region. Jerusalem stood. The people were generally unaffected by all of the turmoil in the time in between. Persia, Greece, the Ptolemaic empires, Rome... Jerusalem and the temple stood. The line of David was protected. But the lack of affliction also caused most Jews to forget about grace and supplication, to not be ready for repentance when Christ came. Unable to believe on Him Who was sent. Jesus came into His own and How own received Him not. And of course, they lost the hedge of protection and as Jesus foretold, Jerusalem was sacked and burned and the Temple destroyed in 70AD. It is easy to forget the power of God upon us when things are going well, just as it can be easy to gripe and complain at petty inconvenience when we have it so good. Having sure and steady faith in the promises of God, good times or bad, when we are abased and when we abound, is a key skill to develop in the Christian life. Being content. Knowing His grace is sufficient. Not allowing complacency to lead to taking God for granted.

Jeremiah 2:13 For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water. John 4:10-14 Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water. The woman saith unto him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: from whence then hast thou that living water? Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle? Jesus answered and said unto her, Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. John 7:38-39 He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. (But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.) Revelation 22:17 And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely. Zechariah 13 continues the prophetic vision of the previous chapter, and builds upon it. In that day, they look upon the one they pierced, the one they sold for 20 pieces of silver, the one who fulfills the promise to David of an eternal King, the promise of a high priest forever, that breaks the staff of "Beauty," that is the old covenant, that breaks the staff of "Bonds" that separates Jews from Israel, that puts families apart from one another, bringing division even among father and son, mother and daughter, the good shepherd, will bring forth a fountain of living water. He will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications, and their sin and uncleanliness will He remember no more. The false gods will be cut off, their idols gone, no remnant of their religion or the prophets that spoke lies will remain. And one shall say unto him, What are these wounds in thine hands? Then he shall answer, Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends. Jesus, wounded for our transgression, by His stripes are we healed. Smite the shepherd and the sheep will be scattered. Matthew 26:31 Then saith Jesus unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad. The unbelieving will be cut off, the third part refined as with silver, or with gold. And they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God. Amen Once you are saved, when you hear the truth and believe it unto salvation, you will never reject it utterly. You will never turn fully away from it, to seek another way of salvation. Once you have partaken and drank the water of life, you will never thirst again. How could you? The Spirit is now within you, satisfying that thirst for truth. The bread, His words of eternal life are eaten, and you will never hunger again. It's hard not to see this truth everywhere in the Bible when you look for it. The promise of God that all who believe shall not be condemned. That all who drink freely of those living waters will never thirst again, let alone for something less than the truth of God's promise. The Spirit of truth does not leave room for the spirit of error. For the spirit of antichrist. For the spirit of Babylon. It is not possible to deceive the very elect. The unbelieving antichrist Jews will say that Jesus didn't fulfill the prophets description of the Messiah, and yet to Him gave all prophets witnesses. It isn't hyperbole, or a false claim, but a matter of fact. They deny the witness of the Spirit, as seen in these prophetic books. Jesus Christ was preached from the foundation of the world. I forgot to mention this, and someone reminded me, this verse stating that 2/3 of the Jews will be killed in the days of vengeance leaving only a third part, is actually a key belief of dispensationalism. Which is pretty wild when you think about it. They cannot wait to build the third Temple and have the Antichrist kill 2/3 of all Jews.

Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, and thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee. End-times prophecy is given, the day of the Lord is assured. But just before His return, Jerusalem will be set upon by an army of all nations. The Days of Vengeance, led by the Antichrist. The city taken, trampled underfoot by the nations. The Gentiles. Luke 21:22-24 For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people. And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. Jesus returns with His saints, and splits the Mt of Olives in two. A valley running East to West. The site of Christ's Olivet Discourse. The unnatural light describes the earth illuminated by the glory of Jesus. The sun and moon darkened. The stars not giving their light, as described also in Matthew 24. A great curse is upon those that rose up. A consumption without death. Similar to the sores and suffering in the wrath described in Revelation. And the rivers of living water, the Spirit of God, will flow out to the ends of the earth. And the nations during the millennium will come up to the feasts in Jerusalem, the prophet says, and if any do not, they will have rain held back. Some interpretations hold that the OT feasts will be honored in the NT Kingdom. But as we discussed in the study of Ezekiel, OT prophecy still retained elements of the Old Covenant, while the Revelation of Jesus Christ in the New Testament changes things slightly to better reflect that new covenant made necessary by the failure of the Jews. Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness. Common pots and pans for normal cooking will be as holy as the temple's vessels. I think this is symbolic of the glorified saints being sanctified, that even common is holy. The no more the Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts indicating no more heathen, no more tares in the wheat. But the Lord will reign from Zion. Amen

Malachi, the last prophet before John the Baptist, likely preached to the restored Jerusalem sometime during the absence of Nehemiah, when the leader returned to Persia, as we saw in the last chapters of his book. When the people immediately turned again to sin and iniquity. The theme of the Lord turning from the people whom He loved, and provoking jealousy by prophesying that the heathen would come to Him is clear and unmistakable. The burden of the Lord comes upon the prophet, and he preaches the word, that the people, especially the priests, have turned from Him, saying He doesn't love them, and they curse the table of offerings He instituted. He says Jacob have I loved, and Esau have I hated, pointing to the destruction of Edom while Jerusalem stands restored. He says that the nation of Edom, from the same seed of Abraham through Isaac, brother to Jacob, is cursed to show them His love. That the Lord be magnified in Israel. And yet, they do not honor Him as sons should a Father, or as servants a Master. They despise His holy name. They offer corrupt sacrifices. Polluted bread upon the altar. They say the table of the Lord is contemptible. Romans 11:9-10 And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumblingblock, and a recompence unto them: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway. God is cursing them as David cursed the people. God asks, if they brought the sacrifices of the lame, the blind, the polluted to their Persian appointed Governor, would he be pleased with it? How should He, being the Lord of hosts? Malachi says, I pray you beseech God that He will be gracious unto us. Because God no longer is respecting them as persons. He regards them no more.
