Their altar and offerings He rejects. And so, He says that His name, the name of Christ Jesus, shall be great among the Gentiles. A pure offering. But ye have profaned it, in that ye say, The table of the Lord is polluted; and the fruit thereof, even his meat, is contemptible. They were already rejecting Christ. 400 years before His coming. This is important to understand, that it was finding fault with THEM that another covenant, a better testament, offered to the nations of the world, in the blood of Christ. He curses them, and the deceiver, both the priests that gives a corrupt sacrifice while saving the pure, male ram, unspotted, for himself. And their father, Satan. The deceiver whose deeds they do. Because the Lord's name is dreadful among the heathen. Dreadful meaning inspiring fear and awe. And they would accept Him the Jews rejected.

Malachi, the last prophet before the days of the coming of Christ, continues to preach the word of God against the Jews. First Levi and her priests, then Judah and her foreign brides. Their iniquity and calling evil good and good evil. Their table has become a snare. Their adultery is to the covenant God made with their fathers, and to Him. And here, in Malachi 2:15, we see the reason behind the covenant, the Old Testament given to Moses in the wilderness. That He may seek a godly seed. While some will say this is about Israel, it is, like God's promise to Abraham, seed singular. As of one. Galatians 3:16-17 Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ. And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect. The promise was always Christ. And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed. This was always the gospel. This was always the promise. The good news. And the fault for the first testament ending was with the people. The Lord hates putting away. And so in death, their marriage was ended, even the death of Christ. The law says The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead. They slew their Husband, and hung Him on a tree.

The burden of the Lord upon Malachi continues, and the prophecy of Christ Jesus. That a messenger would come before Him, John the Baptist, and the Lord shall suddenly come into His temple. Fulfilled both literally and in coming in the flesh. His body a temple. The messenger of the covenant. The promise kept, and a new covenant made. He shall come. And as that promise was kept, so shall He come again. Sitting as judge. As a refiner of silver and of gold. As fuller's soap makes garments white. The offering made in righteousness. His body and blood. An offering pleasant to the Lord. He says, judging Judah that they have withheld in tithe and offerings. Robbing God, and will be sifted as wheat for it. Verse 5 reminds me of Revelation 21:8 But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death. The immutable God, He changes not. He again calls for repentance towards Him, to turn again to the Lord of hosts, but they would not. The unbelieving, calling faith vain. Scoffers as in the last days. They call the proud happy! "Gay pride." They promote those who work wickedness. But those who fear the Lord are His, and His promises to us are true. That all who seek Him are found and made sons of God. Spared as sons, from our sins. Amen

Matthew 17:10-13 And his disciples asked him, saying, Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come? And Jesus answered and said unto them, Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things. But I say unto you, That Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them. Then the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist. Malachi, the final prophet of the Old Testament, finishes with the coming of an Elijah, before the judgment and the wrath. To turn the hearts of men towards their fathers and their children, that they fear the name of the Lord be healed by the Sun of righteousness, Jesus Christ. Of course it was John making straight the path for the King. And it was the Son of righteousness Who was raised with healing in His wings. God's grace is such that despite His holy name, and the righteousness to smite the earth with a curse, He gave another chance at redemption for all men first. That the world may be healed. We are in that time. Redeem it, for it is short. Life, a vapor. The harvest is ready. Go forth and rejoice, bringing in the sheaves. Go soul-winning!

The Gospel of Matthew begins with the lineage of the man, Christ Jesus, the promised seed of Abraham, through the root of Jesse, the son of David, heir by right to the throne of the earthly kingdom of Judah, yet not just a man, not of this world, born of the Holy Spirit, the Son of God. Heir to all things, through whom all things were created. Joseph, Jesus' stepfather, engaged to Mary, with thoughts of putting the pregnant fiancee away, privately, given her condition. But the angel of the Lord visits him to say that she bears God's word, the promise of a redeemer, to take away the sins of His people. Fulfilling the prophecy, preached by Isaiah: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us. And Joseph took Mary for his wife, and did not lay with her until after Jesus was born, so that He may be born of a virgin. (Note it doesn't say "never" but "till.")

Sorry to be so late, what a day I had. And thankfully, Matthew 2 is a very straightforward chapter. The call backs to prophetic scripture in the birth of Jesus continue, establishing the testimony that Jesus is the Christ foretold. We see the wise men of the east, who came seeking Jesus at his birth, who are not Hebrews, and yet aware of the promise of God and who worshiped him, bestowing gifts of kings. As we saw in chapter 1, by right, Jesus was King of the Jews. Herod, in jealous anger repeated the horror of Pharaoh, and the murder of the male children under his rule, as was done in the days of Moses. At the angels behest, Joseph takes Jesus and Mary to Egypt, eventually returning again in fulfillment of scripture. In many ways echoing the story of Moses, yet to deliver us spiritually to the promised land rather than the physical salvation of Exodus. Had a works-based heretic tell me this verse proves you have to do good works to be saved. John 5:28-29 Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.

The prophet who comes before Christ. The voice crying out in the wilderness. Telling all men to turn towards God, that the Messiah is coming. John the Baptist. Jesus cousin, raised by his righteous parents, bringing people to salvation and baptising believers, by immersion, in much water. Baptism not being the putting away of sin, but the answer of a good conscience by those who have called upon the name of the Lord for forgiveness of sin and everlasting life. The same unbroken line of faith from John to modern, NT Christians. (Note it's not John the Catholic or John the Lutheran) He eschews comfort. Eats ze bugs. And rips face with hard preaching. Matthew 3 captures a moment of John's style of fire-breathing, hellfire and damnation preaching, in this case against the Pharisees and Sadducees. The religious leaders of Judea, come down to be seen where the actions at. Maybe to be baptized to seem holy. But John calls them out. O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Much as Jesus would later, as detailed in Matthew 7 and 23, he calls out these hypocrites, this generation of vipers, false preachers who bear bad fruit. Not souls won, ready to accept Christ. They bring forth no fruit, thistles. False prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Then he goes after their reliance on being special boys, born from Abraham, saying God could make a rock a son of Abraham. That their being Jews isn't going to save them. (RIP Dispensationalism). He tells these reprobate hypocrites that Jesus who's coming, will sort them like chafe from wheat, into the fire. Cut down their tree, throw it in the fire. Brimstone-throwing preaching. Amen! And Jesus, our Lord comes, whose shoes we aren't worthy to unlatch. And he goes down into the water, and straightway rises up out of the water with the Holy Ghost upon Him. And the blessing of the Father is given to the Son. Amen. I can't begin to understand any saved Christian who doesn't like hellfire and brimstone hard preaching, against sin. Against wickedness.

Following Jesus' baptism and the announcement of the Father that this was His Son in Whom He was well pleased and the anointing by the Holy Ghost, Jesus went into the wilderness to fast. Knowing hunger, being in the flesh, He was tested and tried of all things and yet sinless. When Satan came and likewise tempted Him with rewards of the flesh, twisting scripture to do it, Jesus cites the word to both rebuke the devil and keep Himself pure. This is how Satan attacks us all. He wanders the earth like a ravening lion, seeking who he can devour. He is before God the Father accusing believers, day and night. He gets us to give in to lusts of the flesh, and if possible, gets us to justify it as God's will by twisting His word. Same as with Eve in the garden. Same as with the Son of God in the wilderness. And unlike Eve, Jesus rebuke sends the devil packing, defeated and angels are sent to minister to Christ. Matthew then tells the story of the beginning of Jesus' ministry, the recruitment of some of the apostles from Galilee, having gone there to avoid Judea after the arrest of John the Baptist. The willingness of the apostles to leave father, home, job, everything to follow Christ is an example to all believers and seekers. As we know from Gospel of John, they were seeking the Messiah of the prophets already, and heard their master's voice when He called. Knowing the scriptures, they knew His word, and the promise and so, when called heard His voice. This is why we are reminded that scripture said that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God. It's Jesus' first lesson to us. We live by His word.

Here in Matthew 5 we are given a taste of the preaching of Jesus. The themes and doctrines which Jesus taught in this sermon on the mount, starting with what are called the beatitudes, the blessings of those with certain traits pleasing to God. The poor in spirit, even the least of the saved, are partakers of the inheritance, the Kingdom of Heaven. Those that mourn, longing for those loved ones sleeping in Christ will have a comforter in the Holy Spirit, and in the promise of the resurrection. The meek, those who humble themselves before the Lord and live with that understanding of their status as inheritors being only by grace and mercy from God, not of their own deeds. Those who hunger and thirst for righteousness will be filled. Those who earnestly seek salvation, His wisdom, the imputed righteousness of Jesus, God promises it will be given to them. And that we will drink of the living water of Christ and never thirst again, eat of the bread that is Jesus, and never hunger. The merciful will receive mercy, the pure of heart will see God. It is that mercy from God that makes us pure of heart. Blessed are the peacemakers, they are the children of God. Not the children of the darkness, of disobedience but the children of the light, who obey the Gospel and share it with others, bringing peace to them with God in His goodwill. Making peace with our enemies, and heaping coals upon their heads. Making peace with the beloved, so we may have unity in the members of the body of Christ, following the head that is Jesus. And blessed are we who may be persecuted for His name's sake. For the cause of Christ. Saved Christians are these things, and these blessings are a promise to those faithful that we should strive to exemplify that we may fully receive the inheritance and blessings as a child of God. Throughout scripture we see that the children of man are given a share of inheritance and a blessing for their future, and God is no different a Father. We are blessed with reward beyond measure, eternal life, filled with His righteousness. Let's redeem the time and not squander the gifts by being contrary to these ideals. Matthew 5 continues 13 Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. 14 Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid. 15 Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house. 16 Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. Jesus addresses the Jews to whom He's preaching, and reminds them of the Israelites' role in being chosen by God, to be the example. A light unto the world. To be the salt of the earth giving savor to God's word, bringing it to all men. And having lost that purpose, being worthless and cast out. All those who call themselves by His name are called to this ministry, and all risk the same end of being trampled under foot if they lose their savor. Hide their light. Not winning souls and providing living examples of the power of the gospel. No longer giving off the glory of God to guide the lost. 17 Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. 18 For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled. 19 Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven. 20 For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven. Jesus tells us that the law of God, being perfect and preserved, isn't being upended by what He preached or His eventual death and resurrection, but fulfilling all things in the end. That all shall be made subject to Him, the earth as His footstool and the promise of the Kingdom kept for the children of God. The Jews hearing this being familiar with scripture, knowing the law, the prophets and the promise, would understand, at least those with ears to hear. Those seeking righteousness. Unlike the claimed righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, who taught loopholes and exceptions to God's law and accused Jesus of seeking to destroy it, we must have the righteousness of Christ to enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, exceeding those hypocrites' false idea of righteousness.
Posting for comparison sake, just read it. You can see for yourself the consistency in the message of what's being preached. You know this is what Jesus is talking about, right? Learn to heap coals.

The sermon of Jesus Christ on the mount continues. I rather think this is representative of Jesus preaching during His earthly ministry, and many themes here are repeated in the other Gospels to showcase and teach us His perfect and flawless doctrine. Give alms in secret to men, for our Father will reward you. Pray in secret, not making a show of it, and the Father who knows all our needs before we do will openly reward you. Don't pray as the heathen do, with vain repetitions thinking they will be heard for much speaking. Don't place your heart on treasures in this world, material wealth, but rather treasure what you may lay up in Heaven. Don't make a public show of fasting and doing without. Don't even let anyone know that you are fasting. Essentially, don't act like the Catholic Church. Jesus says that they who pray and give alms in public to fanfare, who fast, abstaining from meats, giving up treats, to be seen as holy to men, those who pray with novenas and rosaries, repeating the same words again and again, a vain prayer of repetition, those who place their treasure on earth, serving mammon, materialists with gilded shrines and golden fixtures, ornate buildings full of idols...all these get their reward, Christ assures us. And it isn't a blessing but a curse. No man can serve two masters, as scripture says. You can't serve an earthly, fleshly, material god of this world, and serve the Father. He will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. And so Jesus tells us that worry for materialism, for vain glory, for grudges held, debt unforgiven, the accumulation of things, this is serving Mammon. Not God. Not seeking the Kingdom of Heaven. Eyes full of darkness. Worry is a prayer to the god of this world. Fear is the worship of him. But we are children of the light and are looking forward to a better country, establishing the works thereof. Storing up the crowns and precious stones of heavenly rewards. Keeping our eyes turned to Heaven. Taking no thought for what we wear, shelter, food. Trusting God to provide for our needs as He does for His creation throughout nature. Living faith to faith. Unafraid. Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof. Don't worry about tomorrow, if the Lord blesses us with a tomorrow, He will provide. The evil of today is sufficient enough without adding cares for things yet to come. But keep in faith. He will provide.

Matthew 7 contains some of the most quoted, and misquoted red-letter scripture of the Gospels. The culmination of Jesus' preaching at the mount. He warns of hypocrisy in judgement, not considering your sin as you cast judgment on another's. Many cite this as meaning never judge another, but we who are saved by faith are called to judge even the angels. It's in God's law, His word that we express judgement having already been judged, found wanting, and healed and made whole in Christ. But hypocrites, the saved especially, will face reproach for the lack of grace and self-awareness they show others. We judge in God's word, with the same mercy He has shown us in our sin. Removing the beam from our eye that we may help remove the mote in our brother's. Righteous judgement. Jesus warns against reprobates, dogs. Swine. Ministering unto them the things of God, that gives them an opening to destroy you. I consider churches that accept sodomites into their midst examples of this. "They repented!" and 2 years later they are arrested for molestation in a church's youth group. Many such cases, and even the best church can fall prey to this. Everyone who asks of the Father, spiritual things, be it salvation, wisdom, knowledge, blessings...God will give. This is a promise from Christ Himself. Everyone means everyone. No special boys, but whosoever will come to call upon the name of the Lord. In all things, if you want men to live upright and Godly, start with yourself. It is the ultimate implication of loving thy neighbor as thyself. Again, judgment without hypocrisy. Being blameless. We turn a nation towards God by being Godly ourselves, and letting His light shine through us to guide others knocking, seeking truth, to Him. It allows us to remove the beam, and help others with their mote. Stay on the strait and narrow. Don't look for shortcuts into heaven than the path of salvation laid out in the Gospel. It is an easy way, but most people carry burdens that prevents them from entering. Beware false prophets, ravenous wolves seeking to destroy. You can identify them, despite their sheep's clothing, by the fruit they produce. This is what true fruit inspection means. Too many false prophets turn this scripture on its head, and produce hypocrites, self-righteous fruit inspectors, judging the motes in everyone's eye but ignoring the beams they have themselves. We are to judge if a pastor or church leader, a prophet or preacher is false or not by inspection of their fruit. Their followers. Are they loving and saved, humble and meek? Hypocrites and holier than thou? Good fruit or poison? And from there, knowing that a good tree brings forth good fruit, and that the unsaved and corrupted cannot bring someone to salvation and truth, evaluate the man claiming to be of God. A very quick way to evaluate this is lack of actual soul winning. The more a false pastor misleads their flock, the less evangelism they will engage in. It's not the sole metric, and doesn't always hold true (JW for example), but it is one means of recognition. But if their fruit isn't producing good fruit after its kind, but rather engaged in judging and works of self-righteousness, focusing on themselves rather than others, this is thistles not figs. These works-based false teachers have sacraments and rites, idols and vain traditions that create wide paths and broad gates, where those on it see an easier path, that ultimately leads to destruction. All of their works focus on themselves. The sacraments they perform are selfish, their rosaries and novenas, about them. Trying to save themselves from the pits of Hell, rather than genuine charity and love. And they never win a soul to Christ. They can't produce fruit meet for repentance. They claim to cast out devils and bless houses, while laying up treasure for themselves here on Earth. And thus burdened, are unable to fit through the strait gate and unable to walk the narrow way. And thinking themselves righteous, when they come before Jesus touting their works, he says depart from me I never knew you. (Proving you don't lose salvation. He doesn't say he used to know them, but never did) In verses 21-23, Jesus lays in to those selfish and vain workers of iniquity, but many unsaved people trapped in false doctrine twist this verse to mean you must do works to be saved. "You must do the will of the Father see!" But what is the will of the Father? Jesus tells us; This is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day. We are building our house upon the solid rock of the word. Living the sayings of scripture, embodied in Christ. Doing the will of the Father. Those who ignore scripture, rely on shifting traditions of man and their ever-changing doctrines, are building upon sand. I am never not amazed at Jesus flawless Doctrine

In chapter 8 of Matthew, we are given testimony of Jesus' curing the faithful leper and the faithful Roman centurion's servant. This is an occasion for Jesus to preach against the Jews who were rejecting Him, and to prophesy about the coming of the Gentiles being made heirs to the kingdom. There is a lot of talk among both dispensationalist Evangelicals and atheist/agnostic/pagan hard right that Jews are still God's chosen, that Christianity is a Jewish trick and that Jewish hatred of Gentiles over the past 2000 years is due to our being White. None are true, and it all stems from their being cast into outer darkness in disbelief, and Gentiles being graft in. The spectrum of political conservatives and those to the right of them on the spectrum comes from a basic misunderstanding of God, scripture and salvation. The errors expressed may differ but they stem from that same misunderstanding. Peter's mother in law being healed is also documented. Her springing up to serve them is touching. Jesus tells the leper to not mention His role in healing and to go render sacrifice in the temple, as they are still under the old covenant, is to keep the Pharisees from coming after Jesus immediately. He often does this during the Gospels, cognizant of when His time will be, and the work He yet has to do. The famous miracle of Jesus calming the seas and taming the storm at His command, where His disciples, fearful had to wake Jesus, who trusting His Father slept through the tumult. They lacking faith were certain they'd die. We are given an alternate account of the casting out of demons into a herd of swine in the country of the Gergesenes. A similar version is told in Mark 5, for example, where it is one man, possessed by a legion of demons. This is a reminder that we have 4 testimonies told by human perspective, but filtered through the Holy Spirit. Just as witnesses to an accident see or recall details differently, the overall picture is true and we get the idea being given. The devil's recognize who He is and acknowledge their eventual fate of being cast into Hell by the Son of God. The incident makes the people of Gergesenes afraid of Christ, and beg Him to leave. Sometimes the power of God has that effect on the unbelieving, when confronted with the truth they'd rather deal with demons besetting them than witness His power, or the power of His word. A pattern emerges reading through this part of the Book of Matthew, where we see Jesus attracting large crowds and then departing from them. Sometimes being asked to depart, but mostly his leaving and preaching to his disciples, his "little flock." If you remember in the previous chapter he describes the path forward as narrow and strait. In this chapter Jesus tells a disciple begging leave to bury his father, to let the dead bury the dead. Stick around we're talking about eternal life. Basically to cast off the burdens, the attachments and fears and cares of this world. Jesus flees the crowds to preach to the faithful. Bestowing healing and miracles on those with faith, despite attracting a throng of people. Some of whom might be disappointed in Jesus, expecting something more than a humble and meek man doing the will of the Father

Through 7, 8 and Matthew 9, we see Jesus attracting multitudes, yet He deals with the individuals He meets. The miracles bring crowds, but the focus is on those few who in faith call upon Jesus to heal them. The man with palsy taken to Christ by his friends, all full of faith, is told his faith has brought him forgiveness of his sin. Jesus physically heals him as well, but note the order of things. We're given a simple and short story of the calling of Matthew, a publican. A tax collector for the empire. Called, he goes. Jesus meets with sinners to give them the good news, to bring them to righteousness, turning towards God and believing on Him. These miracles and His preaching have the Pharisees and scribes besides themselves. The whole need not a physician. Some wicked people make it a point to say "Jesus was friends with sinners and partied with them!" But the truth is, Jesus ministers to all, for all are sinners. But he didn't "party," but acted as a physician to the sick. Ministering the Gospel. The disciples of John the Baptist ask why Jesus' disciples feast while they themselves fast, and Jesus explained they have Him but for a short time. The time for fasting is to come. When the new man within the believers has room for the sanctification and growth of the Spirit that comes from fasting. Jesus uses cloth being mended and skins, containing grape juice to be preserved as a parable. For the unworn cloth will rend the rip further, and the old, cracked and weakened bottles will burst with unpreserved and fermented juice it produces. Jesus then brings the daughter of a certain local ruler back to life, the rulers faith overcoming the scoffers gathered at her death, who doubt the power of Christ. And as Jesus fame grew for the miracles, even more crowds turned out for Him. Blind men beg to be healed, and they are. And despite His seeking to keep some of these miracles a secret, His fame grows and the multitudes come. His compassion for these lost sheep is touching. God would that all men come to salvation. He laments how few laborers there are to harvest the many who are seeking Him. This is as true today as then. The harvest is plentiful, we are called to go out and bring the increase to God. When casting out a devil, we see the bitter Pharisees accusing Jesus of doing it in the devil's name. Later in Matthew they say "This fellow doth not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils." It's a common accusation that they charge Jesus with, in envy and fear that their power and position was being challenged by Him. It's this resentment and projection that ultimately lead to the Jews killing Christ. The narrative of Matthew is very straightforward, regarding Jesus miracles and appeal to those of the time of His earthly ministry, but focuses on Jesus as the son of David, the promised Messiah. The Christ. John's portrait of Jesus as the Son of God, Luke's as the son of man, and Mark as the suffering servant, all combined to give us a clearer picture of who Jesus is. What a blessing it is to have these accounts.

Now Jesus had been attracting multitudes with miracles and saying "The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few," sent off the 12 to set about gathering the many unto Him, praying the laborers increase. At this time, before being lifted up on the cross, so as to call all men, the focus of Jesus earthly ministry was targeting Israelites indeed, to let them know the Christ promised by the prophets was here. Gathering the lost sheep of Israel to let them know the kingdom of Heaven is at hand. He grants the apostles power to heal the sick, raise the dead, cast out devils. He instructs them to take no provisions or worry for anything, because as the scriptures say, 'for the workman is worthy of his meat.' This is to be a soul winning marathon like no other. 2 by 2 he sent them out, to the highways and hedges. House to house. City to city. And Jesus lays a curse of those who refuse to hear, the cities that drive them out, the places they shake the dust off; Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city. Those Jews in their time of judgment will have it worse than Sodom, having disciples of Christ before then, preaching the truth of God's word and rejecting this final plea of peace and goodwill to the men of Israel. He then warns of the wolves that will beset them. The men who will seek to challenge and imprison then, the rulers they will be brought before, both during this ministry and in the future, prophecy of what's to come to all of them (save Judas the reprobate traitor, who had his own reward). Jesus teaches how the Holy Spirit, the inward dwelling aspect of the godhead, the Holy Ghost within, will lead them to remembrance all things, and give them what to say should they stand before council, persecuted for His name's sake. This is a promise to all believers, that the comforter, the Holy Spirit indwelling can and will give us what to say in the hour of our tribulation. And that if we endure the trials and tribulations to the end, we shall be saved from them. Physically. Either by death of the flesh to heavenly reward, or by other means, such as the flood saving Noah from the wicked scoffers of his day, or just Lot delivered from the filth of Sodom. Many take this verse out of context, and will claim "saved" always means justified by God, redeemed, made righteous. Most instances of the word saved in the Bible refer to rescue of the flesh, not salvation of the soul. Rightly dividing the word, we see that Jesus tells them what they are being saved from, and it's not Hell in this context, but the tribulations and persecution to come. "Preservation of the saints" is a misapplication of the concept, and in many damnable heresies, is used to keep people from the truth of the Gospel, constantly worried the sins they commit after being born again are damning them, that if they backslide they lose their gift of eternal life. Depending on their own works to keep them justified, they remain perishing. It's a wicked false doctrine. Jesus continues His instructions, telling them that God is watching over them, and what we preach, fearlessly from the rooftops as it were, may bring condemnation by men, division within even our own families. The peace of God given by His Son to those that believe will not bring peace on earth between men. They will hate us for His name's sake. Those that accuse Jesus of being Beelzebub will accuse us likewise. If you have been born again for any length of time, you have experienced this. Especially within family. Those that know us best and who refuse the truth, resent and turn on us, accusing our every deed, hating us for His grace within us. Our sins thrown against us, and lies used to accuse. That's why Jesus says if we love our parents or siblings or children more than Him, we aren't worthy. We must carry the cross, despising the shame, just as He did. Not caring for our very life, willing to die for God's will, just as Jesus did. Again, a mistake many make is stripping the context of taking up the cross from the persecution Jesus is warning of, and making it about our own struggles with the flesh. "Repenting of sin." Taking up selfish or self-centered burdens, denial of our lusts, whatever. While that could be an application of the struggle of sanctification in our Christian walk, the context here is deliberately about persecution for Christ, while doing the will of the Father. Going out and soul winning, sharing the Gospel, being public ministers for Jesus. And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. So, understanding we are to not have cares for this world, nor place earthly attachments over Christ, be it family, comfort, food, shelter, or even our own lives, to proclaim Jesus and confess Him before men, expecting tribulation and persecution, for the glory of God and His kingdom. And in return Jesus will confess us before the Father. And in our faith, sharing the good news to all who will receive it. And the promise made to us; He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. Amen

Now, having sent out His Apostles to preach and win souls, Jesus does the same, and as He journeys to spread God's word and will that all come to repentance, turning from their false belief and to the truth of the promise found in scripture, faith in Christ, while performing miracles that God may be gloried and the stiff-necked and the lost turn back to God the Father. And John the Baptist, isolated and long kept in prison for his faith, finds it shaken. He sends two of his followers to confirm that Jesus is the Christ John preached was coming. As Jesus describes him, John is one of the greatest men of God ever to live, none born of man who are greater, and he had his doubts that came in tribulation and persecution. Jesus says he is the Elias, which was for to come from Malachi 4:5. That other prophets prophesied of him. That from the beginning of John's ministry, the kingdom of Heaven is like a besieged city for all the masses of souls won by that voice crying out in the wilderness. The Son of God heaps praise on his harbinger. And, as in previous chapters of Matthew, Jesus takes the occasion of what's happening to preach, and it is hard preaching. He preaches against the willful lack of appreciation of the message by the crowds. The lack of faith found in some who haven't ears to hear, who say the austere John, in camel's hair and eating locusts is from the devil, and Jesus who comes as the celebratory bridegroom, is also. That the message, being the same, is still not received by this wicked generation. Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not. When you have the Son of God among your people, He and His disciples healing and performing miracles, raising the dead, casting out demons, and crowding to hear doctrine preached and scripture explained, and still, as stubborn and stiff-necked as ever, reject the Gospel and cling to their false ways, Jesus says they are worse than Sodom. Than the fallen kingdom of Tyre. Their fate will be an even greater a reproach. And having shamed the people, Jesus turns again to the faithful with a message of hope. Thanking God the Father for keeping these wicked out of the kingdom with their spiritual blindness, while cherishing those who come to him, like children. Delivered by the Father unto Him. And through Jesus, having the Father also. The only way to God. And to the faithful, a promise of rest in Christ. Taking up the yoke of salvation, a light burden, casting off the heaviness of this world, of sin, of judgment, of the bondage of law, resting in the perfect work of Jesus Christ. Sharing the same Gospel that gave us rest with others. Amen.

There are quite a few things going on in this chapter, lots of doctrine and preaching by Christ, mostly against the holy men of Judah, the scribes and Pharisees. Those who had been entrusted with teaching and keeping God's will, and who had perverted it to be hypocritical vipers. They reproach Jesus and His disciples for gleaning and eating corn on a sabbath, Jesus reminds them of scripture, that the man of God and those with them may profane the day if doing God's will. Soon, the sabbath would be done away with in Christ, where no day would be esteemed above another. Our rest in Him. A picture of not working on the day of rest, we are entered into the Sabbath of Christ without works, but faith alone. And our works aren't needed, except to do good, to do the will of the Father. To find the lost sheep. To heal those that are broken. This is the spiritual application for salvation and the our purpose of sharing the Gospel that the Sabbath pictured in the OT. And as the Jews plot to snare Jesus, He withdraws and heals the multitudes gathered before him, telling them not to speak of it, to the furtherance of the glory of God the Father, and His word; Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles. He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets. A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory. And in his name shall the Gentiles trust Having cast out a devil that was causing a man to be blind and dumb, healing him, the crowd wondered that such things came from a man, the son of David, heir to his lineage. And again, the Pharisees sought to slander Him, saying Jesus cast out devils in Beelzebub's name. A house divided against itself cannot stand, and likewise the devil cannot cast himself out and heal. Satan's kingdom then would fall, and isn't that a good thing? But the Pharisees' children went forth claiming to cast out evil spirits in God's name, so Jesus asks, wouldn't their accusations hold against their own? Hypocrites, full of envy and deceit. Blaspheming the Holy Ghost that was upon Christ, claiming the power to heal was from Satan instead. Jesus teaches that they may slander Him, and be forgiven, but those who falsely accused the Holy Ghost are reprobate. Damned, twice-dead. O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. As we are judged by our word, and calling upon the name of the Lord, are saved, so to those who speak evil will be judged, and their every word revealed at judgment. Imagine being in that position, where every evil, dishonest, covetous, snarky, insulting, embarrassing, wrathful, perverse and blasphemous thing we have thought to say is made known to all, before being cast into the lake of fire? Thank you Lord for my escape in Christ. Then the Pharisees, in flattery, ask Jesus as rabbi, give us a sign. Understanding that throughout this whole chapter, as well as Jesus' earthly ministry, in the presence of the same scribes who called him Beelzebub, Jesus has healed the multitudes, cast out devils, and preached perfect amazing Doctrine from scripture. And yet this crooked and perverse generation seeks after a sign, and Jesus says that no sign shall be given them other than the sign of Jonas. Foreshadowing his own death burial and resurrection, 3 days in the heart of the Earth. And he compares them to the citizens of Nineveh who when God saw they had repented from their evil Works spared the city destruction. He says they will be judged with more favor, having believed the prophet of God. Jesus tells them that the Queen of Sheba, who came laden with treasure to sit at the feet of Solomon and hear his wisdom will partake in the judgment, along with the Gentile believers that will come and these supposed holy men of Judah will be judged by them. Those who think their salvation comes from their position, their station, their lineage, will all face judgment while those who believed, including the Gentiles, will be the generation of those who see the kingdom of God. Amen. Finally, we see a story of Jesus mother, mary, and his half brothers, who have arrived seeking an audience with him as he preaches to his disciples. When he's made aware of it by the crowd, he asks and answers, in verses the Catholics who worship Mary despise; Who is my mother? and who are my brethren? And he stretched forth his hand toward his disciples, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren! For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother. One other thing I overlooked, where Jesus teaches about people who clean up their own lives, sitting right themselves without God to cleanse the evil spirits from them, and who, in the end our worse off than had they never made the effort. There's understanding here, that our simple repenting of sins, so to speak, giving up serious bad habits and addictions and behaviors, alone without God, is vanity. And those who do so may well no longer engage in the behaviors, but yet will suffer judgment just the same. Real healing comes through Christ and our faith in Him that saves a wretch like us. It's not enough to simply turn your life around. It's not enough to turn over a new leaf. Even the most wicked man among us can quit smoking, or lose 50 lb. Even a reprobate can give generously to a charity. But without God, these efforts are in vain.

How does anyone give commentary on Matthew 13, when Jesus Himself gives His own, explaining the parables to His disciples as He tells them? Of the sower, we see the unsaved, the carnal Christian, the zealous who backslide, and the fruitful Christian who brings forth more of his kind, manifold. The tares, reprobates among the faithful. False prophets and infiltrators. The Judas. The Kingdom of Heaven grown enormous from a tiny seed of faith, a precious treasure, a pearl worth any price. He explains He spoke in parables that those with faith shall receive more, and those with little faith lose even that. Let him who have ears to hear... Deuteronomy 29:4 Yet the LORD hath not given you an heart to perceive, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day. Isaiah 6:9 And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Jeremiah 5:21 Hear now this, O foolish people, and without understanding; which have eyes, and see not; which have ears, and hear not: And when Jesus says that the tares should be burned in the fire, the wailing and gnashing of teeth, he is preaching on Hell. Matthew 18 is a lesson in humility and forgiveness. The humble nature of a child and the debt incurred by trespass, and the good king who has forgiven all, and yet some ungrateful men cannot bring themselves to show a hint of the grace that's been extended to us. The apostles ask Jesus, "who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven?" Jesus points to a child, an innocent who oblivious to the law, and unable to offend, humble and without pride, represents those who have been brought low by the truth of the Gospel, and fearing the Father, accepting His grace, just as a child is dependent and helpless before their father. To be converted, to repent, is to accept His will, to obey the Gospel, to accept we deserve death and humbly cry for mercy, and in His grace, the Father gives it to us, redeemed by Christ, forgiven all debt incurred by our sin. Jesus continues this lesson when Peter asks how often should we forgive a brother. The law says 3 times, he doubles it and again and asks is 7 times enough? Jesus replies, 70 times 7, indicating an order of magnitude greater than the letter of the law. To essentially always forgive those seeking it. And, spinning off of this, Jesus teaches how to ask for forgiveness ourselves, and what to do if a so-called brother refuses. That we ask in private, then before witnesses, as pertaining to God's law, and then, if he refuses still, to put him out and treat him as an unregenerate sinner. A publican. A heathen. Because lack of forgiveness and grace is a sign of an unsaved heart. He tells the parable of the unforgiven servant, who beseeching the king to be forgiven a massive debt, then refuses to release a fellow servant a relatively minor one. This lack of grace means he didn't humbly partake in the same from the king, and undeserving, is cast into prison for torment. And so it is for all men. The Bible says Jesus paid the debt for all men. Those who seek that forgiveness in truth and reconciliation of grace will by nature show grace upon those who have wronged them. Not perfectly, we may need reminders, we may need the presence of witnesses to our stubborn pride to see our error. But holding a grudge against one who has sincerely asked to be forgiven is evidence of pride and arrogance, and a sign one has no understanding of the humility of receiving grace from God for our own trespass. It is a humbling feeling to know you are in the hands of the Living God, and deserve death and Hell, and yet, He forgives. The prideful cannot understand because they cannot admit to themselves their own debt. They can't receive His mercy, because they think it unfair or overcharged, or worse, doesn't exist. To them is forgiveness denied and the full price extracted. But we forgive as we have been forgiven. We understand that there but for the grace of God go I. Even if we sometimes need a reminder to. And our forgiveness should be as longsuffering and loving as that which was shown to us. If you are holding a grudge against someone, and cannot let it go, you aren't right with God. If you're truly saved, you know the feeling of grace, extended to you. Forgive. And if you can't understand grace, and hold on to your grievance, you will find yourself before the strait gate unable to enter. Like a camel entering the eye of a needle, unable to pass. Let go and humble yourself to God in Jesus name, and receive His grace. Amen. I have much to say about the eye offend thee/millstone portion of the chapter, but I am running late for work. Will touch on it soon. One thing that just occurred to me, when thinking of the grace that God the Father and Jesus the Son extend to us. Jesus says, back in Matthew 12, that all manner of sin and blasphemy, including blasphemies against him and God the Father, shall be forgiven of men. (Blasphemies against the Holy Spirit being the only unforgivable sin in this regard. For who would blaspheme the Holy Ghost but a reprobate?) If our creator and savior can forgive great offense directed at them, how can we not do likewise for the petty squabbles of this life? If the spirit is truly within us and we are under grace, cognizant of what we deserve and aware of the mercy that's been shown on us, how can we not forgive others? And dwelling on this concept of forgiveness, debts, reconciliation, redemption, the wages of sin and the gift of eternal life, which is given an ernest of the Spirit within us, testaments of inheritance and promises... This is the nature of God's law. There are rewards and debts. There is Grace and unmerited gifts. It is an economy of faith. And because it is of God, it is perfect in balancing the ledgers.
