Who the lord expected little of. He just buried it until the return, not even joining in where the work of others may have given increase to what he was left. He is an unsaved person who knowing of Jesus, thought wickedly of Him, and didn't accept the gift of salvation, not even to just be partaker of the joy of the Lord. The unprofitable servant gives his excuse; "Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed." It is important to remember that in scripture, what a man might say, especially one representative of the unsaved, isn't necessarily true. That while the narration of the Bible is truth, the words uttered by characters aren't always. Jesus is not a cruel master. We see this in the parable where he takes into account our ability, and asks little of us considering. He rewards generously those good and faithful to Him. So the unprofitable servant claims it was fear of an unjust Lord that led him to squander and reject that which was given him. And the Lord says if that were true, and you actually thought that of me, you'd have at least tried out of fear. Many who refuse to believe claiming the worst of God, that He is unjust, and takes what isn't His to take, don't actually follow through on their fear. For if they believed it, they'd have done their duty out of that fear. God prefers we accept the gift, the salvation He offers and to make the most of what's given us, out of love and loyalty to Him. But He isn't opposed to it being received in fear for His wrath. The promise of God through Christ Jesus is the reward for the faithful servant, and the eternal punishment of those who reject Him. For unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath. And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. This is the offer made in the testimony of God, His word. Some use these parables to teach that you can lose your salvation. That the foolish virgins and the unprofitable servant were saved, and having been sinful or disobedient, had lost their shot at Heaven. But there is nothing to this, for ALL are called. We all, every person, has been given the truth, written in our hearts, through creation, and have no excuse. God will that none perish. Every name is in the book of life until it's blotted out. When one dies, or is given over to reprobation or, in the end, refuses to repent and believe when the day of the Lord is come, it's too late. They are damned to eternal fire. To eternal torment. The foolish virgins and unprofitable servant believed falsely, and what had been given them, the chance to enter into the joy of the Lord, is taken from them. Salvation cannot be lost, only refused. Consider, had the five foolish virgins filled their lamps with oil at the first, they may still have slumbered and been lazy regarding their waiting for his return, but they still would have had that oil, the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, and still would have entered into the wedding with the five wise virgins. Similarly, Jesus says that had the unprofitable servant simply thrown in the one talent of silver giving him, his own salvation, with others seeking to increase the harvest, he would have still entered into the joy of the Lord, the Kingdom of Heaven. The Bible says in Romans 4:5 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. And while I would rather have great rewards in the kingdom, being given responsibility over much, or even responsibility over little, the goal is to be present at the bridegroom's wedding feast, to enter into the joy of the Lord. Far too many reject the gift. Bury it in the ground and don't even use it for themselves, let alone accept it and bring increase to the Father, honoring the Son. Rounding out the chapter, Jesus gives us a summation of the end, that He will gather His sheep unto Him, and the goats, the unbelieving, be cast into Hell. Christ's rationale, that those who are His extended charity to the needy brethren, and by this, perhaps unwittingly as it is painted by Him, did so unto Him; Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me...Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Again, works-based heresy puts it that it's these acts of charity, which is the love shown others as a reflection of the light of God, the grace He's shown us magnified by our works is the means of entering into the Kingdom, rather than the way by which our faith is shown. How we are separated from the goats as His sheep. As the Bible says in James 1; Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world. Religion is the practice of our faith. This is how it is lived. And note that the sheep didn't even consider the gain, that it was truly Jesus being helped rather than a stranger. It was just what they did. As Paul reminds us; Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares. And to the goats, Jesus says; Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me. The significance of their not having charity in their hearts from God's grace is reflected in their spiritual condition. Finally, there is a wicked doctrine that circulates among the unsaved, pushed by vipers that there is no Kingdom of Heaven, that our reward and inheritance is of the earth, and that there is no Hell, that the damned do not face eternal torment and burning for their sin. Many pushing this false doctrine claim Jesus never spoke of either, and that Hell and the grave are the same. Some use corrupt versions of the Bible to claim foolish things such as Sheol being different than Hades, that "Abraham's bosom" is a place rather than a body part, a paradise inside or along side Hell. They use semantics and concordances, pedantic reasoning and ignore the actual text and context regarding both. It has been a snare and a stumbling block for many. Some see the idea of eternal punishment as 'unjust,' and like the unprofitable servant, accuse God of being unjustified in His condemnation. Others will paint believers as the offenders, offering up an "unfair" God, when, in their mind, God is love and so he "wouldn't subject people to eternal torment just for not believing in Jesus." They may even trot out the old "what about the savage in the jungle, hmm? Is that fair??" chestnut. All of this is natural man foolishness as both the promise of Heaven and eternal life, along with Hell and eternal torment are given throughout scripture, and as just Matthew 25 demonstrates. Jesus says the Kingdom of Heaven is like the wedding of the bridegroom, to which the 5 wise virgins are let in to, the door shut to the fools, whom the bridegroom says he never knew. He doesn't say the millennial reign on earth. He doesn't say the New Earth of revelation. He consistently says the Kingdom is of Heaven. It is our promise and reward, both now after our physical death, (to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord) and our inheritance in the resurrection. But what of Hell? Is it simply being shut out of Heaven? Again, in Matthew 25 Jesus tells us details of the unbelievers' fate. Of the unprofitable servant, He says "cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth." This is a formula used throughout Matthew by Jesus to describe Hell. Wailing and gnashing of teeth. Torment and agony. But is 'outer darkness' Hell? Revelation 14 says of the damned; The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name. Tormented with fire and brimstone, the smoke of their torment ascending forever and ever. Sounds like Hell. As an aside, some wishy-washy Christians will claim that Hell is actually just the "separation from Jesus," when here we see the burning torment of the damned is done in His presence. Revelation 20 tells us; the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever...And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire. Further, Revelation 21; But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death. And Revelation 22, after telling of those who have overcome are within the Holy City, that without are dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whosoever loveth and maketh a lie. Back in Matthew 25, Jesus says "Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels....And these shall go away into everlasting punishment." Everlasting fire. Everlasting punishment. But to the righteous, life eternal. This is the biblical teaching on Hell. It's a real place, in the pit of the earth for now, and later cast into the outer darkness, the lake of fire, after the physical world is destroyed, after the millennium has ended and the White Throne Judgment of the unrighteous is done. So do not be fooled. Hell is very real, and God is not slack regarding His promises. He is perfectly righteous and holy. And if He says throughout His word that eternal torment, punishment, burning, is what awaits those not clothed in the righteousness of Jesus then you can believe it is true.

We know the story. The finals days. The anointing of precious oil. The greed of Judas leading finally to betrayal. The last supper on the preparation day, before the Passover and the slaying of the lamb without blemish. That Jesus knew from the start who would betray Him. Jesus using the bread, unleavened for the feast days, and wine, the unfermented juice of the vine as a symbol of the new testament to begin with His death and fulfilled in His resurrection. That it is His blood shed on the cross that is for the remission of sins. A sin offering on Passover. The promise; But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom. (Note Jesus says that it is just juice of the fruit of the vine, not literal blood) The sorrowful prayer at the garden. The sleeping Apostles, their spirit willing but their flesh weak. The surrender to God the Father's will. The betrayal. Arrest. The cutting off of the servant's ear, and the warning not to take up swords to defend Him. The Passover lamb taken before the high priest to be examined before the sacrifice. The denials by Peter as Jesus foretold. This is the truth of the last days before His crucifixion. Where Jesus gave up His life, to be betrayed, beaten and accused, the shepherd smitten, the sheep scattered. But how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be?

As the lamb without blemish is led away by the chief priests to Pilate, we are told Judas Iscariot, who had betrayed Christ for 30 pieces of silver, repented, changed his mind, thought better of what he'd done, and saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. Psalms 41:9 - Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me. Zechariah 11:12 - And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver. Judas, rebuffed by the priests of the temple, and unable to come to salvation having been damned by his rejection of the truth, hanged himself, and the 30 pieces of silver used to buy a potters field for the graves of strangers. Luke 22:22 For the Son of man indeed goeth, as it hath been determined: but woe unto that man through whom he is betrayed! Repenting of a wrong done doesn't equate with believing on Christ for salvation. Jesus said to His Apostles, of Judas "Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?” And as he hanged himself, the Bible tells us the details of his fate; Acts 1:18 Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out. 19 And it was known unto all the dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, that is to say, The field of blood. 20 For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take. 21 Wherefore of these men which have companied with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, 22 Beginning from the baptism of John, unto that same day that he was taken up from us, must one be ordained to be a witness with us of his resurrection. 23 And they appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias. 24 And they prayed, and said, Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen, 25 That he may take part of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place. "His own place" being a euphemism for Hell, a place man earns for himself, (as opposed to Heaven by which no man can earn their way in to possess). I will note that in modern translations, they remove the word "repented" here, and replace it with "felt remorse," because the idea that Judas repented would conflict with the false teaching of turning from sin to be saved, rather than faith in Christ, and it would lead people to question if Judas repented, if he is in Heaven. Again, reminding us that bad doctrine begets bad doctrine and confusion. And they have to further change God's word to take on new meaning to support it. Now, as before the high priest Caiaphas in chapter 26, Jesus refuses to answer the false accusations made of Him. Pilate is awestruck at His reticence, that was prophesied in scripture; Isaiah 53:7 He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth. Now we are told at Passover, the Roman governor would release a prisoner to the pleasure of the people, and knowing Jesus was innocent of the charges made, gave the priests and the mob of Jews gathered a choice; free Jesus or free a known murderer and true insurrectionist, Barabbas. And so we are told Pilate asked "Whether of the twain will ye that I release unto you?" They said, Barabbas. Pilate saith unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? They all say unto him, Let him be crucified. And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified. And so Pilate, unable to change their mind said, "I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it." To which the Jews answered; "His blood be on us, and on our children." And so Jews, unrepentant and antichrist, are, according to scripture, accursed to this day. The wrath of God upon them to the uttermost. His blood upon them that deny Jesus is the son of God. And so, releasing Barabbas, and having Jesus scourged, receiving lashes before being turned over to be crucified, Pilate plays his role. Isaiah 53:5 But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed. The soldiers beat Him and mocked Him, calling Jesus the "King of the Jews," crowning Him with thorns, stripping Him naked, humiliating Jesus, who had come to save even them that did this, and Jesus suffered it all anyway, despite His power, to do the will of the Father, a dutiful Son. They beat him and took His garments, and cast lots among them to divvy them up. Then took Him to the cross, nailing Him there, and lifting Him up among thieves. Isaiah 53:12 Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors. Mocking that Jesus should save Himself, that His God whom He trusted should save Him. Psalm 22:6-19 But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people. All they that see me laugh me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying, He trusted on the Lord that he would deliver him: let him deliver him, seeing he delighted in him. But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother's breasts. I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother's belly. Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help. Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round. They gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion. I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels. My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death. For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet. I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me. They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture. But be not thou far from me, O Lord: O my strength, haste thee to help me. Hebrews 12:2 Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. And as Jesus Christ came to the end of His work on the cross, He cried out in Aramaic, the primary language of His youth, here on earth; Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Quitting Psalm 22:1 My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring? And so, Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost. And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent; And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose, And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many. Now when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and those things that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God. Truly. The bodily resurrection of believers shouldn't be confused with the final resurrection of all saints into glorified bodies. It is understood that these were like the young girl, or Jesus' friend Lazarus, risen to die again, but saved unto eternal life. The veil of separation in the temple, representing the separation of God and His Spirit from man, is torn, that separation removed. The sacrifice made, His blood given for remission of sin. We learn of the Marys, faithful to the end mourning Him. Of Joseph of Arimathea, and the grave he provided for Christ's body. Isaiah 53:9 And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth. And in fear, those that slay Him set guard over His tomb, against the prophecy Jesus had made that on the 3rd day, He would rise again.

The Gospel of Mark begins with a speedrun of Jesus' start to His earthly ministry. Starting with scripture prophesying John the Baptist heralding Christ's arrival with the baptism of repentance, the outward acknowledging of accepting the truth, of our being sinners, in need of salvation and the truth of Jesus being the Christ. The remission of sins through the confession of our sorry state, washed by the water in anticipation of the Spirit to come in His resurrection. The Holy Ghost. Jesus comes and is baptized, immersed in the river Jordan, coming straightway up from the water, and the heavens and the Spirit and the Father all give witness and testimony to Jesus, anointed as the Christ. The Messiah who John and all the prophets gave witness to, finally come. Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Mark gives us a very quick synopsis of the temptation in the wilderness, and Jesus calling the first Apostles, Simon Peter and Andrew his brother, sons of Jonas. James and John, sons of Zebedee, the "sons of thunder." Jesus preaches in the Synagogue, astonishing men with his doctrine, and he drives a demon out of a man, who when seeing Christ near, begins to call Him out as the Son of God. Mark notes later, as in the other Gospels, that Jesus suffers not the devil's he casts out to say who He is, that the faith of those who follow be not in the wonders but the word, and the glory of God. Turning toward God in faith, trusting on Jesus, while still under the law of Moses until His death and resurrection. This is why he admonishes the leper to simply go and offer the sacrifice after he is healed, that God may glory, and he be a testimony unto the priests. And Jesus healed many and cast out devils, and many followed. He left for Galilee, then into the wilderness, the outskirts of towns, the crowds following Him, from every quarter. Jesus, moved with compassion. The leper believes, and calls upon Jesus to heal him, and Jesus, moved with compassion does so. This is the purest form of the Gospel. The mercy and grace of Jesus' compassion on us, who in faith call upon His name and are made whole. He being the sacrifice for atonement. He being the blood shed for remission of our sins. Now, no longer the picture of Christ to come with the blood of bulls and goats in the law of Moses, but of His precious blood, sprinkled on the Mercy Seat. Jesus have mercy on me, a sinner. Acknowledging we are sick in spirit as the leper was in the flesh. And in the same faith, calling out to Him, "If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean." If you believe that in your heart, call upon His name. Right where you are, today. Don't wait, for The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.

The healing of the man lowered by 4 into a full house where Jesus was preaching is a beautiful picture how many with faith may bring us to salvation. Jesus forgiving his sins, and then healing his flesh in opposition to the scribes questioning in their hearts His authority gives a definitive statement of the divinity of Christ. "Who can forgive sins but God only?" Exactly. Notice it's the faith expressed, not only of the man with palsy, but those who bring him to Jesus that moves Christ. It is the faith that leads to His forgiveness of sin. The healing of infirmity comes after. This is such a picture of salvation and the moving of the Spirit in a saved Christian's life. And notice, all to the glory of God. "They were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion." Next we see Jesus call upon a publican, a tax collector, identified here and in Luke as Levi, but better known as the Apostle Matthew. Jesus calls him from his position collecting tax on the goods coming into port in Capernaum and bids the publican to follow Him and he does. A Levite publican, a double blow to the worldly Pharisees. One of their own collecting tribute for Rome. No greater sinner in their mind, and to dine with one, that would be "unclean." Jesus' answer to their outrage, that He was here as a physician, to heal the sick, calling the sinners to repentance towards God, as the righteous have no need of a "doctor," is a backhanded insult to the Pharisees. They are not righteous. There is none righteous by the works of the law, and certainly not these hypocrites. But their own conceit would keep them from seeing His point. In matters of righteousness we are all in need of a physician, Christ Jesus. We shouldn't lose sight of that truth, and understand it's not the sins that make us clean or unclean. It's not our own righteousness in following the law, but our hearts and spirit of faith in Christ Jesus to impute His righteousness on us that heals. That makes us clean. Washed in the blood. There is a natural man argument that many unsaved scoffers and reprobates make is that Jesus "hung out with the sinners" and not the "holy rollers." They take this verse and blaspheme, claiming Jesus liked to "party with sinners" to excuse their own unregenerate lifestyle. Of course they meltdown when you correct them that He certainly preached to the sinners to bring them out of sin, but actually hung out with, was friends with, His Apostles and closest disciples. That physicians don't "hang out" with the sick, they treat them to be well. This understanding escapes them, and I have seen more than a few Christians unable to make this distinction and get confused or browbeaten into not calling out sin. Ignoring the sickness. Enabling the worst behaviors, simply to not be seen as a "Pharisee." Both the hypocritical fruit inspectors and degenerates are sick and in need of a physician. The chapter ends with two more challenges by the scribes and Pharisees to Jesus and His correction of their error. First, they accuse Jesus and His disciples of not being pious enough to fast, and use the austere ministry of John the Baptist and his followers fasting to lend more credence to their own self-righteous fasting. To build a stronger "got ya" against Christ. And once again, Christ answers them with unassailable doctrine. How can they fast in the presence of the bridegroom? They celebrate while He is with them, and will fast once He's gone. Jesus says one doesn't patch an old garment with new cloth, or place new wine in old skins, as a parable to what would happen. The cloth would rend from the inflexibility of the new cloth. The wine, fresh juice would ferment and tear the old skins. So to, He is saying He isn't there to "patch" the old failed ways of the Pharisees, to mend the old law. He's there to fulfill it and make it new again. Mark shifts to another instance of the so-called holy men challenging Christ and the behavior of His disciples, as they glean corn in a field to eat on a sabbath. Jesus uses the example of David and his men when they were fleeing his enemies, eating the shew bread of the temple, despite that being reserved for the priests. That the sabbath was made for men, not men to the sabbath. The Sabbath was designed to picture the rest we have in Jesus after salvation. It was meant to give rest to the weary. To teach as a schoolmaster the truth of Christ to the Hebrews. It wasn't meant to be a way of showing super righteousness by how closely you followed the tradition of man that sprung up around it. As a pups exercise to be seen of others. That the rest we have in Jesus is the same. It's not our actions that sully us, but the context and spirit by which we commit them. All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not. It is similar to the story in Matthew 15 where the Pharisees again question Jesus and His disciples, when they don't wash their hands in the ritual way before eating. Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught? But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man. A common teaching of Christ is emphasis on the spirit and heart by which we sin, the same as the spirit and heart of how we have faith. That it is the thought of wrath that is murder, thought of lust that is adultery. What our intent and what is in our hearts that God judges when we are His. This is a higher standard than the Pharisees' outward displays of righteousness, while inwards they are ravenous wolves, full of sin. However it cuts both ways, where in the trappings of what man sees as outward signs of sin may well be just their idea of what righteous looks like. Who put appearance over substance. Who sin in their hearts, polishing the outside of the cup, but defile themselves inwardly by their hearts. As Jesus said to these hypocrites “Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess." It is perspective we should all keep in mind. What many miss regarding repentance in the Gospels is that Jesus had come to lead the people trapped in the works-based, hypocritical heresy that had become the religion of the Pharisees, and the hopeless secularism of the Sadducees. The state of religion in Judea and Jews in general, turning from the faith of their fathers and the prophets, and towards the self-righteous faith of outward appearance, the circumcision of the flesh over the circumcision of the heart. When Jesus says to repent, He isn't talking about cleaning up your life, and trying to live more in line with the law. That's the false religion of the Pharisee that He repeatedly condemns. He calls sinners to repentance, towards God. Towards the salvation of faith in grace He is there to fulfill. The remission of sins that is the result of repentance unto faith. Then the healing of the body. Then the turning from sin. We go to the doctor to be healed. We don't get healed to see the doctor. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. The righteous in Christ should turn away from their sin. Put away and mortify the lusts of the flesh and the warring members of the old man. To feed the new man and walk in the spirit. But it is the sick of spirit, those dead inside that He came to heal that they could be made whole. That the Spirit could quicken ours in our faith. Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins. The hopelessness in hypocrisy of works-based religions, like much of what is considered modern Christianity. Like what is called Judaism. Like what is the religion of the Pharisees. This is such a snare and a trap, as it keeps people mired in their sin, unable to come to forgiveness while they're in their flesh. Because our flesh, our natural man, our old man willfully sins. It's our nature. And as long as people are trapped in a cycle of trying to justify themselves to God by turning from their sin, or engaging in ceremony and sacrament, denying themselves the healing power of Jesus, they become trapped. This stumbling block and snare keeps so many people from even attempting to get right with God. And the faithless religion of the sadducees, which denies the power of God, the promise of Heaven, the Resurrection in Christ and forgiveness of sins, is equally a trap. Many who rationalize their way into atheism, reform theology, Calvinism, the catechism of the Roman Catholic church, or the so-called apostolic traditions of the Orthodox, who don't take a literal view of the Bible while adopting the trappings of it, seeking to become righteous in their own wisdom and knowledge, rather than the wisdom and knowledge of the Lord. These false ways and spiritual traps are what Jesus came to call sinners to repent of that they may be healed. That their sins be forgiven, that they may sin no more.

Mark 3 sets the same pattern we've seen in the other Gospels, of Jesus healing or teaching and the Jews who oppose God trying to use the occasion to be rid of Him. Here, Christ heals a man's withered hand on the Sabbath. As we have just read in Mark 2, Jesus continues to make this point, that it is lawful to do good on a sabbath. That Sabbaths were made for men, not men for the Sabbath. He is the Sabbath. Failing to lay hands on Him, Jesus makes His way to the sea, and multitudes came to see Him from all about the region, so much so He asks a boat be ready to help Him depart, should the crowd be too much. He heals the multitudes, and gains more who flock to see the wonders, and glory God, and some unto believing on Him as the son of God by faith. This is important, as He reprimands the unclean spirits He casts out to silence their proclamation that Jesus is Christ, the Son of God. We see that then, after retreating to the sea, Jesus then goes to the mountains, continuing to preach to the masses following Him. He formally ordains the 12 Apostles to preach and heal in His stead, so as to minister to the crowds that have gathered. And because people from all over Galilee, Judea, and beyond have come to see Him, and the proximity of Nazareth to Capernaum, where much of Christ's ministry had been, His family, mother and half-brothers and friends He grew up become concerned, not knowing who Jesus truly is. They thought Him crazy. But the scribes accused Him of being from Satan, and the Holy Ghost by which He cast out these demons, they label an unclean spirit. A blasphemy He warns is unforgivable, and is a way to reprobation and damnation. As Jesus says a house divided cannot stand, as if Satan turned on his own. How can Satan cast out Satan? And all sins of men will be forgiven. This is important. A penitent believer will be forgiven all manner of sins, but the blasphemy of the Holy Ghost and deliberately changing God's word (Rev 22). These are direct causes of reprobation that most Christians will accept. The will also concede death without believing is final, and damned. But they often struggle with the idea that some, not wishing to retain God in their knowledge are turned over by Him to a reprobate mind. A rejected mind. Hearts hardened. Conscience seared. Twice-dead. Unable to come to the knowledge of the truth. This is the case for many of these Pharisees and scribes. Such was the case for many in the Old Testament, Cain and Pharaoh for example. It continues to be the case today. And because people confuse reprobation, a spiritual state of man, finally rejected of God, and the unnatural lusts and sins committed by reprobates, they argue, that if all sins be forgiven, then there is no such thing as "too late, reprobate." This puts the sodomite cart before the horse. Unnatural sin is not the cause of reprobation, but a symptom that it's occurred. It is important to get that right. It's never about the sin itself, but the state of a man's heart towards God. Belief unto salvation. Unbelief and vain beliefs of the unsaved which can be overcome with the word and repented of unto faith, or rejection of belief to the point God gives up, stops shining the light. The Spirit no longer calls. Three states one may be in, two final before physical death, one final at that death. The chapter closes out with an exchange that Catholics hate to hear; Jesus' mother Mary, and his half siblings down from Nazareth to check on Jesus thinking him "beside himself", or crazy in other words. This and the parallel passages in the other Gospels recounting the incident show that Jesus was the first born of a virgin, Mary, but that she and Joseph had other children together and so she was not some sort of perpetual virgin. This is extra biblical nonsense, and part of a cult that worships a false goddess called the Queen of Heaven. Further it shows that Jesus didn't venerate his mother over anyone else who believed. God is not a respecter of persons. We are called to love Jesus more than our own mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers. And to love our fellow believers as brothers. Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee. And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brethren? And he looked round about on them which sat about him, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren! For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother. We who are saved, who are heirs to the kingdom of heaven, are adopted sons of God. The Bible says Jesus is not ashamed to call us brethren. We are a Holy Family. And while at least two of Jesus' half Brothers and his mother Mary, were saved by faith and joint heirs with us, and given glory in heaven for their work for the Lord, they aren't of the same status and stature as God himself. They are not meant to be treated as anything more than a fellow believer. And this example in Jesus' life exemplifies this principle. Worshiping, that is kneeling in prayer and praise, before statues, graven images made of Stone and metal and wood, to call upon the names of man to petition God our Father, is one of the greatest blasphemies short of blaspheming the Holy Ghost. There is no biblical instruction that justifies this false doctrine, and there are examples such as this, that clearly show the proper relationship between Christ and us as believers, and his earthly blood relatives in Mary. The logic of man that justifies this blasphemy is undone by the wisdom of God. If you want to honor the mother of Christ on earth, then be as Jesus' mother and sisters and brothers, believing on Him for salvation alone.

In Mark 4 we see another parallel passage, this time with Matthew 13 which we studied a few weeks ago. (it's repeated in Luke 8 as well, which God willing we shall see soon) The parable of the sower is another instance of the nature of creation existing that Jesus, the word of God though whom all things were created, may use it as example to explain the heavenly things of God. The physical to understand the spiritual. For we who are saved, the greater lesson is how we rightly divide the word, understanding that His words are spirit. That His words are eternal life, and what that means. That creation speaks the word of God for those with ears to hear and eyes to see. Who aren't without deep roots, who aren't choked out by thorns. That we may be fertile soil and bring forth fruit after our kind, 100 fold. And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them. Jesus used clearly discerned pictures of the natural, the physical, to help us understand the spiritual, the unseen, that we who are seeking God's truth or who have received the quickening of our spirit may receive faith, which the Bible says is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. He uses the seen to give us insight to the unseen. This is what I was getting at yesterday. But to the carnally minded all things are physical, literal. Materialists see Jesus parables as Nicodemus did; taken to absurd levels or autistic literalism and missing the actual spiritual application. This is what the Bible means by "the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned." The natural man is earthly. They rely on the wisdom of man. They lean unto their own understanding. They are those by the wayside where the word is sown and Satan cometh immediately, and taketh it away. And as we see in the parable of the sower, as Jesus explains, there are saved Christians who are the stoney ground. They hear the word and believe, but having nothing to take hold of, being unprofitable, without a church, without reading their Bible, without seeking to learn the deeper things of God, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they are offended. There are Christians who hear the word and are saved, but are among thorns, the cares of the world. They allow covetousness and lust to choke them out, and become unable to bear fruit. To get more people saved by their example. Unprofitable to God or to others. We should seek to grow roots, deep in fertile soil which is God's word and His ways that we may win souls to Christ and bring in the harvest for the Lord. The lesson of why Jesus uses parables, and the true nature of creation to serve as that parable is given us that we may receive more. That having been given eternal life, and having been made alive in the spirit, we may be given yet more. It's the opposite of gnosticism, where the secrets are revealed by measures, and final "enlightenment" kept hidden until one archives the ability to see. The Bible way is that we seeking enlightenment are given it immediately, if we believe God's word. Then our knowledge grows the more we receive it, freely given. The light put on a candlestick, not hidden under a bushel. It's not hid from those who ask. It's freely given with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given. It's up to you if you be stoney ground. It's up to you if you allow thorns to choke you out. It's up to you if you be fertile soil. What you ask for is what you're given, to those that hear. For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath. He that hath not, those without ears to hear, those by the wayside, they are given the chance to receive the word. The seed is sown in their hearts. But even this is taken away eventually. God doesn't shine His light on all men forever. The Spirit tries for a time, but if you don't want to hear the truth, if the seed can't spring up on your hardened heart, compacted like the well-worn soil of the pathway by the wayside, He will take His light away to shine on more fertile hearts. Then it is too late. So is the kingdom of God. Jesus uses all these things of His own creation to make simple the ways of God to us. And a man sows seed, which grows after its kind, blade, and ear and fruit. He doesn't make it grow, it just does, and when it is ripe for the harvest he brings in the bounty. And so is the Kingdom of Heaven. The seed is the word, Jesus tells us, and it will spring and grow up, he knoweth not how. Meaning God, represented as the farmer doesn't dictate to the seed that it germinate, that it sprout, when it should flower and bud, that it bear fruit. Only that it will as it will, and in due season be ready for harvest. Obviously God knows how, but the point is He doesn't determine which seed sprouts, or the nature of how it grows. It's a rebuke of Calvinism, but it is meant to give us understanding of the Kingdom and our role in it. Both as the sowers and the sheaves. How Heaven grows. And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it? We are privy to these lessons. We are not given the parable only, for those with ears to hear, but given their meaning. Nothing hid. And scripture gives us the meaning that we who believe may gain deeper understanding. Heaven is like a mustard seed, tiny but that grows massive trees, with branches spanning out, each branching further. We are the branches sprung out from the seed. We can trace our lineage in terms of believers who led others to Christ, who led still others, who eventually were those who brought us to salvation. Like a family tree, stretching back to the seed that was sown. For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ. For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit. For the body is not one member, but many. (1 Corinthians 12) The Kingdom of Heaven is like this. And for our understanding all of creation exists. And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it. But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples. Last, we are given another version of the account of Jesus calming the seas. Where the disciples traveling by boat with Him across Galilee are taken by fear for the storm. They find Jesus asleep and wake Him in fear that they may perish. He rebukes the wind and tells the sea to be still, and then rebukes them for their lack of faith. Just as we will be buffeted by storms in this life, so too should we have the peace of Jesus, without fear. Not perishing but preserved in faith. Knowing all creation serves Him, and that eternal life is ours, how can we be afraid? What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him? The creator of all things commands all things. If He be for us, who can stand against us? A common refrain of the worldly scoffers that God is "cruel," and "how can a just God sens us to Hell knowing we can't be perfect?" This ignorance is the bad fruit of the damnable heresies of works-based religions that teach we must earn our way to Heaven, that our own righteousness keeps us from Hell. There are none righteous no not one. The wages of sin is death. But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. God is just. God is love. And He gave us the hope in Christ, that all who believe on Jesus are saved. Just as we are, sealed unto the day of redemption. Everlasting life, given as a gift, that can never be lost or taken away. Regardless of our own righteousness, which the Bible says are filthy rags. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the GIFT OF GOD: Not of works, lest any man should boast. Even to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. As Jesus, who cannot lie said; And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand. I and my Father are one. If you have been one of those who felt lost and hopeless because you were told God only saves the righteous, and that if you become Christian, you have to be perfect or face Hell, understand that this is not what the Bible teaches. That there is hope. That God's grace is unto you in Christ just as you are.

As we have seen so often in the Gospel of Mark, each chapter seems to have a casting out of devils, a purging of unclean spirits, or a physical healing by faith, and here we get both. Jesus having left the Western shores of Galilee, arrives in the east near Decapolis, the 10 cities. Here he meets the man possessed by a legion of unclean spirits, which had left him wild, among the death of the tombs in the local graveyard. Cutting himself. Unable to be restrained by normal means. A danger to himself and others. Many such cases today. The man possessed by legion, overtaken by the unclean spirits falls in worship, that is kneeling before Jesus, and the devils beg for mercy. It's important to note that this is what worship means in the Bible. Not some sort of special feeling or praise, that is subtly different than veneration. It means to fall to your knees before someone or something. The devils were obviously not worshiping Christ as believers, but because He is the Son of God, and they fear Him. They ask that they may be cast into a herd of swine and Jesus agrees. The swine then, 2000 of them, run off the cliffs into the sea. The healed man, grateful, seeks to follow Christ but instead, Jesus calls on him to return to his friends to share the power of God that he may be glorified. The miracle also causes consternation among the Gentiles of the city, and they beg Christ to leave them, and He does. Returning to the other side of the sea, throngs wait on Jesus, to be healed and to hear Him preach. A woman with a blood disease, in faith touches Jesus garment and her faith and His virtue heal her. Just as we are healed by our faith in His righteousness, spiritually. And in one of the most touching stories of faith and the mercy of Christ, Jesus resurrects the young girl for the faith of her father, Jairus. A leader in the synagogue, knowledgeable of scripture, and desperate for his beloved daughter. Jesus takes mercy on her, and says in Aramaic, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise. The mercy of Christ and His love for us makes me cry. Especially as a father. And again faith has made her whole. It is such a wonder and a blessing to know He holds such love for us. Amen.

There is so much narrative packed into Mark 6, it really is dense with both stories of Christ and the meaning of His ministry for us as believers. Even Jesus found it hard to testify among His own. Those who knew Him best, sinless as He is, and yet doubted. His own half brothers and sisters. For many Christians who become born again as adults, to families that aren't believers, we know this feel. A prophet is not received by his own. Not even Christ. Faith that begets faith. The Lord provides. The sending out of the 12 to the highways and hedges. The fear of Herod's guilty conscience, the fate of John the Baptist, and the surmising by the people to who Jesus is. The feeding of the masses, the miracle of the loaves and fishes. Even His disciples had grown too hardened of heart to comprehend His power as God, yet man. Taking it for granted, so much as so they wondered at Jesus walking on water or commanding the winds, again. How many of us take the daily blessings, the absolute miracles God works in our lives for granted. Even the salvation that Jesus provides and the Spirit within us? How often are we astonished at the work of God, when we should have the faith to expect that in Him all things are possible. Including our needs, as the Apostles out evangelizing found. Be grateful for the smallest blessings. See everything as a gift from God, and His love will shine through you. And you will see wonders greater than this. How many of us lack even the faith of those who flocked to see Jesus. To touch but His hem and be healed? We believe. We are saved and trusting on Christ alone. We know we have eternal life and will see Him gather is up into the clouds. And yet we struggle with fear and worry about money or food or the cares of this world. How many of us have hardened hearts? Psalm 51:12-14 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee. Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness. Like David, we need to pray that we are restored to the joy of our initial repentance unto belief. Crucifying ourselves daily, picking up that cross. Keeping the perspective of eternity in mind, as we look towards the better country, the Kingdom to come. 2 Kings 4 42 And there came a man from Baalshalisha, and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in the husk thereof. And he said, Give unto the people, that they may eat. 43 And his servitor said, What, should I set this before an hundred men? He said again, Give the people, that they may eat: for thus saith the Lord, They shall eat, and shall leave thereof. 44 So he set it before them, and they did eat, and left thereof, according to the word of the Lord. The Lord provides the faithful, even when to our fleshly senses it seems impossible.

The repudiation of following what is the tradition of men, worshiping God in vain, continues. Jesus Christ in condemning the hypocrisy of the Pharisees gives us insight to all who are like them, leaving the commandments of God to embrace the traditions of man, and lose their way. Such is the Catholic Church today. So to its daughters. Making their own commandments and rituals, which do nothing spiritually for them, which don't please God, and often bring His wrath. Leaving the Biblical doctrines God has given us to chase idols and false sacrament, rites and rituals of pagans. Seeking to be given grace by increments, doled out by men rather than God. So to here, the Pharisees and scribes come to accuse the disciples for not engaging in ritual hand washing prior to eating which was their human tradition, not a command of God. Jesus calls them out on this hypocrisy. Jesus points out that these vipers have condoned men dishonoring their parents, by declaring their own wealth to be "Corban" that is, belonging to God (despite their keeping it and using it for themselves), cutting off their parents from support which God commands us to provide. (See Matthew 15 parallel study) In Mark 7's version of this event, we get greater clarity on Jesus' preaching to the people of the hypocrisy of the Pharisees and then, further explanation to the Apostles, where He is exasperated at their lack of understanding; Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him; Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats? And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man. For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man. It is what is in our hearts, our old man's mind of the flesh that wars with the new man created of the Spirit within us. When we are born again, we have the benefit of a quickened spirit, and the indwelling of the holy Ghost, but we still struggle with sin because it is in our thoughts and feelings, still taken by the flesh. By what comes out of us, what originates inside us. And while this is also a rebuke of continuing dietary laws meant to instruct Israel on the law and the ways of Christ, or similar traditions of man today, like the silly "no meat on Fridays" thing, the important lesson is in how our nature is regarding sin. We will have foolish thoughts our entire life on this Earth. Thoughts of envy and wrath, fear and lusts. Unbidden. And saying things of strife and contentions, for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. The key is to walk with the Spirit, in God's word and in prayer, that the heart be filled with His righteousness and not our own sinful flesh. It doesn't stop us sinning but it makes it less out of our control, giving it over to Christ. I was posting commentary on the Gentile woman who comes to Jesus asking Him to cast The devil out of her daughter, and His telling her that until the children were full, the dogs shouldn't be fed. Her clever retort that even the dogs catch crumbs as they fall to the floor moves Jesus to mercy and he heals her daughter. This showed both the faith of the woman, and her ability to hear and understand Jesus' parable. He wasn't literally calling Gentiles dogs in a derogatory way, he was making a point that his earthly ministry was to the Lost tribes of Israel, the sheep that needed to be gathered back to their master. By showing ears to hear, and understanding she showed that she hears her master's voice. Many dispensationalists and Jews use these passages and their parallel in other Gospels, to promote a wicked idea that Jesus was for the Jews, and that the conversion of the Gentiles later by the Great Commission was some sort of special boy thing. Jesus came on his earthly ministry to those who had been given the oracles of god, the words of the prophet, the law written out not just in their hearts but in stone and in parchment, published about. That they should have recognized Him for who He is, the Christ, before He was lifted up on the cross, calling all men unto redemption. To them much was given. What advantage then hath the Jew? This is that advantage. But in all things, in all ways, Jesus was sent to take away the sins of the whole world. Now there are many theories as to who represents the true tribes of Israel, and who the Jews who say they are but are not might be. I am not ignorant of them, and I have my own theories and preferences regarding this, that match what many of you believe. But the striving and debate that surround these theories often venture too close to foolish genealogies and Jewish fables. Some of which are a Kaiser Sose effort by Jews to cloud their origin and past, making them out to be more powerful or sinister than they can be. And ideas promoted by others who wish to make salvation one of blood rather than faith, of flesh rather than spirit. This is a huge mistake. We have individual soul liberty. We are freed in Christ one by one, by a free will faith. And we are also damned by that same free will when we choose not to obey the gospel. And some, not wishing to retain God in their knowledge while here on Earth make the free will choice to harden their hearts and are turned over, given up to reprobation. Now, some are blessed to be born into a nation of peoples whose hearts are inclined to the Lord. To us is given the oracles of God. To be born in a Christian majority nation is an advantage similar to that of the Jew in the first century compared to the Greek. Today we have this advantage over China, India or Israel. And though many of us fail to come to saving faith in Christ, none of our nation is ignorant to his existence and the good news of His resurrection. Amen. And just as some of us are blessed to be born into a nation inclined towards God, some are born into a nation that so utterly rejects Him, that there are few seeking to find Him. God judges nations by their collective works, here on earth. He judges man by their faith, individually, for the Kingdom to come. It is not by flesh and blood that we are saved, but by faith and spirit. Never lose sight of that, regardless of what theory you hold. Even the dogs received the crumbs. Think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. If you believe that the "real" lost tribes are the Gentiles of Europe, and the jew are resentful Edomites, antithetical by their nature to all that is good, fantastic. You might be right, who is to say? All theories of men have roots in some truth and it's as likely as anything else. I may even agree with most of it. But if you then further surmise that, because of that lineage, because of genealogies, you are a special boy saved by genes, and others born rejected of God, then you're the same as a chosenite Jew who thought to say to themselves "we have Abraham as our father."

I see men as trees, walking. And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign? Perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened? Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember? And whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ. And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again. And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him. But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men. This is the theme of Mark chapter 8, isn't it? The blind, being shown the light, yet not fully seeing. Of seeking a sign and yet missing the signs all around them. Of seeing the truth, as trees, walking; blurry and not quite focused enough to understand the details and see it's true shape, like poor Peter. Or blind entirely like the Pharisees, asking for light when it's shining bright before then. The healing of the blind man is the healing of the faithful, who at first see the light as if afar off, bringing some clarity out of the darkness. Seeing how things move, the shapes of things. But once saved, come fully into the light. Having our vision healed by the word of God, that we may see clearly. The Apostles, despite having understanding, witnessing the feeding of 5000, the 4000, with a handful of loaves and a couple of fishes, filling all men up, and like the grace of God, with an abundance left over, stumble like the blind man with his partial sight restored. Missing the truth of it, though knowing Jesus was Christ. This was why Jesus cautioned those He healed to say nothing of it to others. Both to protect them that were healed from the adversaries, the Pharisees and Sadducees and scribes, and to show signs and wonders that His sheep may see and believe, but not proclaiming them to those of that wicked generation, seeking after a sign, evidence of who Jesus is, while missing the signs all around them. That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them. Jesus' exasperated sigh at the inability of His own closest disciples not understanding precisely who He is, and protesting what He must do on the cross that the glory of God be made manifest is something many Christians today feel when talking to those who call Jesus "Lord, Lord" and then proceed to talk of their works. Who call themselves by His name, Christians, and yet cannot see the truth when presented to them. Who, sensing the light and seeing the movement, yet see men as trees, walking. Unable to discern the shapes of things. Missing the signs of the times. Not comprehending the wonders shown in Christ. And as Jesus says, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men. They savor the thing of man, not the things of God. And so they remain blind to the full truth. Their faith is in vain. For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth. When believers are faced with those full of zeal for the Lord, but going about to establish their own righteousness rather than the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ, we sigh in exasperation and ask, "are ye hearts still hardened?" If Jesus felt that way, who being God is longsuffering and patient, it is understandable that we too can reach that point when dealing with the heresies and false understanding that so many have today. Don't get down. Don't become bitter and wrathful. I speak to myself as much as the few who may read this. Be edified by the love Jesus showed in continuing to reveal the truth to those that genuinely were seeking it. The lost who hear His voice. It can be frustrating, but don't give up. You may be the water that brings a seed to fruit someday. And if you are still savoring the things of man over God, if you're still seeing things unclearly. If you haven't put your full faith and trust in the Lord Jesus Christ to provide you with his righteousness, lacking your own and having no way for you to obtain it yourself, then believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and confess him with your mouth and be saved. Given eternal life. Becoming an heir to the kingdom of God. Because if you're trusting in your works even for a fraction of your salvation, no matter how much you say to him "Lord, Lord," He never knew you. And you will perish. Repent that He may open your eyes with His amazing Grace.

Jesus continues to prepare the Apostles for what is to come. His death, and by which manner, and His resurrection into power and glory. We are given an account of the transfiguration of Christ before Peter, James and John. With the spirit of Moses and Elijah beside Him, Jesus in His full glory, and the voice of the Father from Heaven, as if from a cloud, "This is my beloved Son: hear him." Such will He be at His return. We get another example of Peter, the stone, stumbling over what to say. Let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias. For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid. It's easy to mock Peter and his continual struggle for understanding, but he represents us in the Gospels. Faithful and seeking understanding. We've all be as Peter before the word of God. Then we are privy to the Apostles asking Jesus about a contention with the scribes, who doubting Christ has come claim that "Elias must come first." That they claim to know the prophets and that the conditions have not been met for the Messiah to come. Of course Jesus corrects them. Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nought. But I say unto you, That Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him. This speaking of John the Baptist, and his manner of death, the same as the prophets of old. The scribes, not believing miss the signs, a recurring theme of Mark and the Gospels. Next we are told of the casting out of the dumb spirit. How the Apostles and disciples were unable to heal the son brought by his father who, in his pain and in need, calls upon the name of the Lord, in faith and praying for still more faith, that his son may be healed. Jesus has mercy and heals the son, who is struck dead by the departure of the devil within him. And Jesus raises him up immediately, restored. If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth. This is what we must always keep in mind. It will guide you through anything, fearlessly. In peace. The Bible says "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus." Amen. Since we are condemned under the law, and sin is transgression of the law, Jesus says it is better to physically cut off a limb or pluck out our eye than enter into Hell. And lucky for us, we have liberty from that fate, through faith in Christ and His imputed righteousness, so that we aren't hobbling around half blind to avoid damnation. But note what Jesus tells us about Hell. Christ describes Hell as a place of fire that never shall be quenched: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched. He says sinners will be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched, cast into hell fire. This isn't allegory. It's not a parable. It isn't a mistranslation of the Greek, or a later doctrine cobbled together by extra-Biblical sources. It is how Jesus Christ, the word made flesh, describes the eternal damnation of Hell. Also, outer darkness, where there is wailing and gnashing of teeth. Where the smoke of their torment rises forever. Burned of the fire that comes forth from God, and the damned are burned in Christ's presence, along with Satan and the fallen, for eternity. We don't even need to do a full study of Hell in the Bible to arrive at this point, we can simply take Jesus' word for it here in Mark 9. It is not just the grave. It isn't being outside the presence of God, in fact the Bible says it is in His presence this torment occurs. It isn't a place ruled by the Devil, he burns alongside those he deceived. If you do not believe that we have a reward, a wage, due us by our sin, and applied by a just and loving God for those who loved the world more than Him, then you have no reason to believe you need saving. Repent and believe that you may be spared this fate. I was going to do a full study on Hell and all of its appearances in the Bible, but frankly it's answering a fool and his folly at this point, beating a dead horse. The promise of Heaven and the warning of hell is the heart of the gospel. The good news is that we are spared that by a God who so loved us He gave us His only begotten Son, that whoever believes on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life. Eternal life. They will live forever in His presence, in the Kingdom of Heaven. Amen On the "wE gAvE yU tHa cAnNoN" thing; They say, “the Bible did not exist yet”. Except all those books did exist as individual scrolls rolled up in the first century. (45-96 AD)...The primitive church DID have the Scriptures in the OT (T.aN.aKh.) (Torah, Nebiim (prophets) and “Khetovim” (writings = wisdom and poetic books) and various churches had copies of some or several of the NT gospels and / or letters at a time; (it took time for all the churches to get all the 27 scrolls at their particular church), the NT writings as individual rolled up scrolls, sent to different places / different churches. But more importantly, we know that God's word was in the beginning, always was. And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth. God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds; For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness. The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away. The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times. Thou shalt keep them, O Lord, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever. God spake the word, the Spirit inspired the word, Christ fulfilled the word. And God has promised to preserve His word for all time. Men taking credit for it are blasphemous, and those that deny the Spirit moved among men to communicate it and preserve it risk the unpardonable sin.

The first section of Mark 10 deals with a common theme of the Gospels, the Jews attempt to trap Jesus with gotcha questions, believing they were more clever than the Son of God. Here it is Pharisees tempting Jesus with a question regarding divorce, and again we see by its nature and their response to His question back that the myth that Pharisees we're "too strict" regarding the law, and that Christ was some liberal hippy is absurd. The Pharisees suggest Moses' allowance for putting away a betrothed for fornication was carte blanche for divorce, and superseded the law. Jesus corrects them of that notion. It was the hardness of your hearts, He says. That the lack of forgiveness and understanding regarding God's law led to making an exception, but that all who divorced and remarried are guilty of adultery. Both man and wife. By using the word of God, scripture, Jesus shut up the tempters. Divorce is ugly. It destroys whole nations. It creates the idea for many that marriage is based on what's good or convenient for the individual man or woman, rather than an instrument of God. We are His. All we have is His, we are but stewards on this earth. And marriage, the blessing of a husband or wife, is no different. And the vows to God He holds us to. But by cheapening the concept and making it culturally accepted to divorce, first for cause, which leads inevitably to no-fault divorce, Satan puts enmity between the sexes and gets us to violate God's law. (Full disclosure, I am divorced and remarried (to a widow, so she's good) but this makes me an adulterer. It doesn't matter the circumstances. It doesn't matter the excuse. It is this because Jesus says it is and so we know it is true. But, thankfully we are forgiven in Jesus) Divorce is one of the tools Satan uses to lead us as a nation, down a dark path of sin that he can accuse us of before God. First he gets us to justify divorce. And by this he makes a generation of us adulterers. Then fornication and living in sin, cohabitation becomes normalized because if divorce is not only allowed but considered inevitable, what's the point of marriage? And if marriage can be dissolved at any time, and we are going to be considered adulterers anyway, why wait? And so adultery becomes normalized. And if divorce harms children, and divorces inevitable, then why have them in the first place? And if it's up to us and our convenience, marriage being just an arrangement for man, rather than a gift from God, why not treat having children the same. And so birth control, abortion become the norm. And Satan keeps accusing. And if the children feel that they are a burden rather than a blessing, and if life is so cheap and that it can be murdered in the womb, and if none of it matters and parents have no responsibility for their own children, then predators are loose upon them. And they are traumatized and groomed into sodomy and worse. And Satan has more with which to accuse. You can draw a clear and bright line from the modern woes of trans kids being deformed and castrated straight back to the baby boom generation clamoring for divorce to be normalized. In for a penny in for a pound, and Satan accuses us the more. The culture that we grow up in is like the water a fish swims in and if Satan can corrupt it, through our own vice and lusts, he will poison that water so that future generations will grow up thinking that the toxins they swim in is normal. It primes the pump so to speak. And so people of my generation and younger who did think to get married, always have the distrust and temptation of divorce sown in our hearts, making it seem like a viable option and making us set against one another from the moment we say "I do." Knowing we had an out and would not be shunned or looked down upon by man, many of us failed to do the things to maintain the marriage. Many spouses have one foot out the door, looking for any cause to confirm the distrust in their hearts sown by the wicked culture that we have. And while it's all well and good to blame groomers, and point at sodomites, we deceive ourselves if we do not take it all the way back to prohibiting divorce and treating it as an affront to God, a sin that leavens the whole lump. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder. Next, in Mark 10 we see Jesus suffering the children to come to Him, teaching that to enter into the Kingdom of Heaven we must be as little children. Both as innocent as they are, and as humble and full of belief. We gain the innocence from Christ's imputed righteousness, by humbling ourselves to ask and understanding why we need it. Amen. I have a post about the bookend presented in Mark 10, between the rich young man and the poor old beggar and what we can learn from the stories concerning them. I may just hold off until tomorrow to give it justice. It's just been a hectic day at work, but productive and giving glory to God and being a good testimony to a few people who I think we're very receptive. Not that I think anybody's hanging on bated breath, but in case one or two of you are wondering where the rest is it will be forthcoming. And to the story of the rich young man, presented in Mark 10 and as we also read in parallel passage of Matthew 19, a few weeks ago. In Mark we see it in slightly different light, as the young man comes off more sincere in this telling, but is identical in result and reason for it. He begins by flattering Jesus as "good master," and tempting him, Jesus asks why he's called Him good when there is no one good but God. This truth is important, because it is both a rhetorical question Jesus is using to give the young rich man the opportunity to understand that Jesus is God, for He is good. But also serves to set up the exchange to follow. That there is none righteous by the deeds of the law. There is none that does good. All have fallen short of the glory of God. But as we see, this young man misses both points and asks his original question, "what must I do to gain eternal life?" And he asks this sitting next to the way, the truth and the light, maintaining that he has observed all the commandments of the law since the days of his youth. He is sitting next to the sinless perfection of Christ, claiming to be 'good.' Jesus, looking upon him with love as it says here in Mark, tells him then, if this is true, "sell all your possessions, give up everything to the poor, and follow me." And the rich young man declined and goes his own way. People delude themselves regarding their own righteousness. We consider ourselves more righteous than we are, especially in comparison to other people who we are certain are far worse sinners. And the more possessions we have, the more material wealth, the more we can dilute ourselves into thinking that to have such blessings God must favor us. That we must be doing something right. We develop a pride, a comfort in the material, and neglecting the spiritual, are trapped by our riches. We have to come to Jesus as little children, who own nothing, are full of trust and wonder, innocent and fearful of God knowing that we're sinners. In contrast, the Rich Young Man comes with a pride and arrogance, and unable to come to the truth about himself or Christ Jesus. Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God! It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. And they were astonished out of measure, saying among themselves, Who then can be saved? And Jesus looking upon them saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible. It is impossible for man to be righteous. But with God all things are possible. If you're trusting in anything of this world, you are like a camel trying to pass through the eye of a needle.
