Given as contrast to the rich young man, we learn of blind Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, who sat by the highway side begging. A man with nothing, and further blind of sight. The rich young man having everything, and being able to look Jesus directly in the eye and not see Him for who He was, compared to a blind beggar, Bartimaeus, who lacking sight, has faith enough to truly see, crying out repeatedly "Thou son of David, have mercy on me." And when Jesus showed mercy on him, asking what he'd have Him do, he replied "Lord, that I might receive my sight." And healing the blind beggar Bartimaeus, Jesus says "Go thy way, thou faith has made thee whole." But unlike the young man earlier, Bartimaeus, having already obtained eternal life, his faith having made him whole, having called upon the name of the Lord for mercy, leaves what little he has to follow Jesus. (Which is why we know his name) One man, relying on his own righteousness, unable to see that the Son of David, the Son of man, the Son of God, the Christ, sat beside him. And unable to part with the things of this world, to be healed, to follow Christ, he departs unsaved and damned. The other, Bartimaeus, is a picture of salvation. Coming as beggars to call upon the Lord for mercy and to be healed, having faith that He is as He promised. And having been healed, and stripped of our cares for this world, become followers of Christ. It is a presentation of faith vs works. Of physical sight and spiritual blindness. Of following Christ in faith vs trusting in your self, and going your own way. Continuing the study of Mark 10 this morning. Such a dense work, the Gospel of Mark tells less of a linear narrative, and tends to place similar themes and complimentary and contrasting stories together, as it progresses through Christ's ministry. And so, day 3 of one chapter. Then Peter began to say unto him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee. And Jesus answered and said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel's, But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life. But many that are first shall be last; and the last first. This follows the rich young man, who bidden to leave his material wealth and follow Jesus, declines, even though the potential for eternal life presents itself, (for this was what he was asking on, and Jesus knowing his heart so tested him) The apostles wondered at the saying that if someone like the rich young man couldn't enter into Heaven, who then can? And Jesus replied no man can, but with God all things are possible. Amen. But now, Peter who isn't the quickest, has it dawn on him that they all have done exactly this. They've left behind their families and trade and possessions to follow Christ. And here Jesus makes a promise, as Lord. He says those that have sacrificed of this world for His sake and the furtherance of the Gospel shall receive 100 fold on this earth. Gaining houses, family, children and lands, and of course the gift of eternal life in the next world. Some twisted vipers take this to a covetous and greedy place, pushing a prosperity false gospel. That God will make you a millionaire of you do good works. But this is not what Jesus says. First, this perversion ignores the "persecutions" part. 100 fold in all these things, and persecutions. Tribulations. These false teachers claim that tribulation and persecution are signs of God's judgment against people. An answer for sin. They think they are entitled to comfort and riches, being holier than thou. It's sick. But further, Jesus isn't saying we are blessed with material wealth. He says we will have houses and lands. Those of fellow believers, those of different lands. Just as He told them when first sending them out to preach the Gospel, from Mark 6: And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits; and commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse: But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats. And he said unto them, In what place soever ye enter into an house, there abide till ye depart from that place. They had homes and lands and their needs met, 100 fold and more. And as for family, as Jesus said when His half-brothers and sisters and mother came to see Him; Whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother. Just as the Apostles write in their epistles, those who they have brought to Christ are their children, sons in Jesus who they have begotten with the Gospel. This is the blessing of wealth and family those who abandon everything and suffer for His sake receive here on earth, along with the persecution that brings them rewards in Heaven. Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake. ... If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified. ... Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. Prosperity false gospel is about laying up riches on earth, accumulated corruptible wealth stored up here. But Christians are called to forsake materialistic wealth and seek a better country, with incorruptible rewards of God. This is not to say that we are blessed in measure by material things with which we need, and a large family is also a blessing from God, but these blessings are undeserved and given by His love, as scripture says; If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him? ... Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them: how much more are ye better than the fowls? ... But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus. God fills our needs. Not our wants, lusts and desires. Coveting has its own reward, and it isn't in blessings. But grateful and humble people who trust in the Lord will see their needs met. Of this I have no doubt, having the evidence of experience and faith. So pray for help when needed, but covet nothing in this life but the opportunity to earn riches in the next. But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him. Amen And they were in the way going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus went before them: and they were amazed; and as they followed, they were afraid. And he took again the twelve, and began to tell them what things should happen unto him, Saying, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests, and unto the scribes; and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the Gentiles: And they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit upon him, and shall kill him: and the third day he shall rise again. Jesus spoke in parables to the masses, that only those who were truly meet for repentance could hear, but to those who believed and followed, He kept nothing from them, including the manner of His death and resurrection. Again, there are false teachers out there that deny Jesus claimed to be God, or that He didn't preach on His death, burial and resurrection, and of course they are liars, deceiving those who don't know scripture. Like Satan tricking Eve by misquoting God's word, they can only fool those who don't know the Bible or believe it is true, who use arguments of man and are offended by scripture. The Bible says to prove all things, comparing spiritual with spiritual, scripture to scripture. Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. ... All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works. ... Teach me thy way, O LORD; I will walk in thy truth: unite my heart to fear thy name. ... Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever. And so we gain wisdom and knowledge by studying God's word. Not by endless argument and debate. Not by strivings about the law. Not by answering fools in their folly. But by the word of God. Finally, we see the bitter rivalry and divisions among the Apostles continued, even after Jesus taught them that the first shall be last, and the last first, that great are those in the Kingdom of Heaven who abased themselves to serve others here on Earth. And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come unto him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall desire. And he said unto them, What would ye that I should do for you? They said unto him, Grant unto us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glory. But Jesus said unto them, Ye know not what ye ask: can ye drink of the cup that I drink of? and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? And they said unto him, We can. And Jesus said unto them, Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of; and with the baptism that I am baptized withal shall ye be baptized: But to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give; but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared. And when the ten heard it, they began to be much displeased with James and John. But Jesus called them to him, and saith unto them, Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them. But so shall it not be among you: but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all. For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many. We know from scripture James was martyred for the Gospel, baptized with the same as Jesus, drinking that same cup, while as a mercy perhaps to their mother (Matthew 20), spared John the fate of all His Apostles, and allowed him to die of old age, the author of much of the New Testament. But regardless of their design on greatness in Heaven, on earth this brought even more contentiousness among the disciples. Jesus again takes the opportunity to explain that it is not about being lifted up in greatness like the rulers of this world, who are served by many, but being a lowly servant to many. Just as He, the Son of God was for us, a sacrifice. And more, Jesus promises us, as good and trusty servants, that in His return He will again serve us; Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them. What a blessing. What a God who so loves us. And if He, without sin, who cannot lie, who is Holy and True, the King of Kings, Lord of all, can humble Himself to serve us, how can we do anything less to those we meet every day? With meekness and grace, we are called to be in service to others, in Christ's name, just as He has for us. And the last shall be first. Amen.

The chapter opens with Mark's telling of what is popularly known as Palm Sunday, though it occurred on a Saturday. The Jerusalem crowd hailing Jesus, riding on the colt of an ass as in prophecy, as he arrives for the Passover, of which He will be the sacrifice. The colt is there where He said, and they allow the disciples to take it, as He said. Because everything in this world is God's and His to use for His glory. Then we have a telling of the fruitless fig tree. Jesus, seeking fruit finds none and curses the tree that it will produce no fruit forever after, and the tree is withered and destroyed from its root. No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever... And in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots. And Peter calling to remembrance saith unto him, Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away. It is not "replacement theology," it is the taking away of the Kingdom for failing to provide fruit, not bringing souls meet for repentance unto salvation. For rejecting the stone, cut without hands, laid as the cornerstone before the foundation of the world. For the "God's not done with the Jews!" false doctrine, this story is twisted, because a plain reading is perfectly understandable. We see more in Matthew 23; And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away. This is a literal story that holds obvious symbolism regarding the Jews, here at the end of Christ's earthly ministry. Fruit, as always in the Gospel, means saved believers, those faithful to God and saved by His promise, in His Son, Jesus. It's reminiscent of a parable in Luke 13:6-9; He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground? And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down. The tree is Judah. The Lord, God the Father, the dresser, Jesus Christ. His earthly ministry, to the lost sheep of Israel was the final attempt to produce fruit of that tree. And having no more fruit, it was cut down and destroyed. God's word is clear, it is forever that the tree is destroyed. It is cut down. It is cast into the fire. Never to bloom again. The dispensationalist lies are built on denying scripture. Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves; And would not suffer that any man should carry any vessel through the temple. And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves. Mark 11 tells us of the second clearing of the moneychangers in the temple, something Jesus did at the beginning of His ministry, and here in its final week. Eaten up by His zeal, and full of wrath at the Jews making merchandise out of His Father's house, Jesus drives them out and flips tables, and this is seen by many as the final straw for the Pharisees and scribes. They now affirm that they seek to kill Him. He has disrupted their graft. Their filthy lucre. Have faith in God. For verily I say unto you, That whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that those things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatsoever he saith. Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them. This is not simply an affirmation to put on Instagram. It's not just a "hang in there, God provides" pick me up for a daily inspirational devotion. It is a promise from God. All He asks is your forgiveness for others as He has forgiven you. To not hold grudges. To let things that aren't important in this life, and keep you from earning the rewards of the next, to let them go. When ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses. But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses. Now, all our sin is forgiven and forgotten in Christ Jesus, at judgment. All believers are in the Book of Life, and so saved. But on earth, God still punishes the disobedient believers, His chastisement falls on those He loves. For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons. And we are to confess our sins to God asking for forgiveness; If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. But how can we humble ourselves to ask for forgiveness for disobeying God when we hold back forgiveness from those who've wronged us? Forgive our trespasses as we forgive others is part of the model for prayer Jesus provides. Lack of forgiveness is a burden. In the same measure we give mercy and extend grace, the Bible says, is what we receive. Be mindful of this, and in faith unfeigned, without the burdens of hate and a lack of grace, go boldly before God with your needs. And the Lord God, who cannot lie, promises He will provide. Finally we see the murderous Jews attempting to tempt Jesus into saying something they may use to justify His death, and once again, Jesus silences them by their own hypocrisy. This is the proper way to deal with such matters. Not reacting and railing, but trusting in God, being blameless and allowing their own internal contradictions and corruption to hamstring your enemies. Using scripture when needed. Forcing them to persecute you directly for His name's sake and for the word. When we spiral in anger and get drawn into debate, all we do is give them the hook to hang us with. Instead, Jesus shows us how petty and foolish they are, exposing them. This lesson in meekness as strength is often lost by believers. It's good to be constantly reminded of throughout the Gospels.

Following the story of the fig tree which Jesus cursed for not producing fruit, He tells a parable. The master leaving a vineyard to be tended sends for the gathering, and the husbandmen he'd entrusted with the land beat and kill his messengers. He sends his only begotten son and they plot to kill him and take the inheritance for themselves. With this not so thinly veiled analogy, Jesus puts the Jews who are seeking to kill Him on notice. They discern that Jesus is talking about them. Unlike most of His parables that fell on deaf ears. The Bible says "they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way." It is amazing to us who believe that there are those who knowing the truth, seek to silence it, even with the Son of the Lord standing there in their presence. Even with the history of the Jews, who killed the prophets of God, and now plot to do the same to Christ. They wish to not retain the word of God and the truth of Christ in their knowledge. They sought instead to take the inheritance of an earthly kingdom for themselves by His death. They worship the creation more than the creator. And God turned them over, gave them up, to a reprobate mind to do those things which are inconvenient. Reprobate silver men shall call them. Again, the dispensationalist idea that the Jews held a special place and God wasn't through with them yet, is a lie. They were given the advantage of the oracles of God and the ministry of Jesus Christ in the flesh, and rather than repent towards God, they sought to destroy Him. And like the master of the vineyard, he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others. It does not say He will take it from them for a time. He destroys them and gives the Kingdom to those who will produce fruit, giving God the increase, in His Son's name. And in a familiar fashion, Jesus again corrects them by citing scripture, have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner: This was the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes? Jesus asks this question and makes the statement that they do not know scripture continuously in His dealings with the holy men of the Jews. It is with scripture He rebukes Satan in the wilderness and it is with scripture that He rebukes the Pharisees and Sadducees and scribes. It is with scripture that we are told to correct and rebuke those in error today. To think not of what we shall say, but allowing the Holy Spirit, through whom all wisdom and understanding is given unto us, to bring all things into remembrance that we, knowing the scriptures, will be able to rightly answer our accusers. It is important to say this as even today, even good men, saved by faith, lean on their own understanding and logic, and are offended by others offering scripture to correct those in error. But what's missed, I think, is that God, who is a loving God, just and true, and who, the Bible says readily gives wisdom to all who seek it, doesn't think it unreasonable to say "Have ye not read this scripture?" to man. God gave us His word to be understood. He gave us His word that we may know Him. He inspired it, preserved it and sent men of God to preach it, because in His mind He thinks that it is clear and understandable when given the oracles of God. That in Him nothing is hidden. God finds it reasonable to ask this because it is reasonable to expect those who say they are of God to know the word of God. And that His word isn't some great mystery, but revealed to us if we take the time to know what it actually says. Not of any private interpretation, but the clear word. Those who say you cannot understand it, need interpretation and scholars to tell you what it means, who claim hidden esoteric mumbo jumbo is the true purpose of scripture, rather than revealing to all men the truth, are vipers and liars, sons of Satan. Like the Pharisees and scribes, keeping others from the knowledge of the truth, and in doing so, blinding themselves forever. I'm probably going to divide this chapter up too there's too much there. But I do hope people take the time to reflect on what I'm saying and consider biblical fundamentalism as the only way. God expects us to know the scriptures for a reason, they exist for a reason and it isn't just a mystify people and keep you spiraling down rabbit holes. But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God. I do find it odd that people who are ostensibly Christian hate being told what the word of God says. They will mock you for quoting scripture when it is entirely relevant what the word of God says regarding something. Nothing is more relevant. They claim to have faith, which the Bible says comes from hearing the word of God, and yet they cast doubt on scripture. They questioned the preservation, they questioned the inspiration, they questioned the origin and the meaning. They attempt to apply their own reasoning and understanding and reckoning and apply it to God, and if He falls short of their own understanding they reject Him and his word for their own. They say things like "well I don't think a loving God would..." Or reason "I hate this thing and I love God so God also hates this thing here let me twist the scripture into saying that He agrees with me." It's just arrogance and pride and foolishness. And when a fundamentalist corrects them because we have knowledge of the word, we've actually read it and it isn't very hard to understand, they get furious with us because it upsets their own conceits. Because they've fallen for the oldest trick that Satan has, twisting the word of God. Still have half the chapter left, but it is amazing how God's word is not only always relevant, but His timing in presenting us with it is flawless. Continuing Mark chapter 12, we find the Sadducees come to bat, the Pharisees having struck out. They represent the secular Judaism we see today. Reform Jews make up the vast majority of so-called religious Jews, who eschew the spiritual and teach that there is no Heaven or Hell, and no resurrection. They believe they are to become gods on this earth, and teach that by their works, "healing the world" or tikkun olam as they call it, they can make a paradise on Earth where Jews naturally are the leaders of a global kingdom. It isn't very far removed from the Orthodox Jew/Pharisaical religion of works-based righteousness and their inheritance of an earthly kingdom in the "time to come," just a bit more honest about their worship of self over God. They seek to trip up Jesus with a very natural man Reddit-tier question regarding the law and the resurrection, thinking the one exposes a flaw in the other, and so bringing the entire thing down. Jesus shows their sophistry easily. Angels cannot marry, or have relations the way humans do. In the resurrection, our glorified bodies will be like theirs. (This is an unpopular take in our circles, but I am unmoved in my understanding that the Bible says at no time has God called the angels His sons, they cannot breed, and throughout scripture sons of God always refers to those saved by faith, who called upon His name for salvation, from the time of Seth onward) Jesus again, being the word made flesh, having perfect understanding of all things as the creator of all things, could not be tested of natural man who cannot receive the things of God as they are spiritually discerned. We are called to be as knowledgeable in these spiritual matters by understanding of scripture, that when the Kingdom comes, and the millennial reign over Earth takes place, we will serve as judges, stewards over those born in those days. And the least shall be first. The meek shall inherit the kingdom. Those who increased the master's yield by 100 fold will be given much, and those that buried what they were given will rule over nothing. Amen. So study to show yourself approved unto God that you may be fruitful now, and a good and faithful servant in the Kingdom. This scribe is getting it. He knows the scriptures and sees that Jesus has answered all that the Pharisees and Sadducees have come at Him with, as the scribe likely knows the scriptures better than they do, given his station. And he asks what is a defining question of Christ, to give the greatest commandment of God. And Jesus Christ the Son of God, the word, sums up the whole of the law on two points: Love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment. And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. Some say here Jesus has invented new doctrine, because they not knowing the scriptures don't know that Jesus has simply quoted the first of the 10 commandments from Exodus and that loving thy neighbor as yourself comes from Leviticus. On these two points rests the whole of the Law. (Some like to point at love thy neighbor' as new doctrine, to say Jesus was more liberal and hippy-dippy than the God of the OT, but Leviticus 19:18 where this is found, is located in the same teachings that deal with stoning sodomites and adulterers) The scribe agrees with Jesus answer, and adds to it from scripture prompting Jesus to say how near the Kingdom he is. Both physically, being in the presence of Christ, and spiritually, being so close to the truth, having faith from the word. The contrast between this scribe and the Pharisees and Sadducees, is the difference between earnestly seeking the knowledge of God from his word and thinking themselves wise becoming fools. Many such cases. People with a predetermined idea of what they want God's word to say cannot be swayed from their belief in themselves. From their own reasoning. But those who earnestly seek wisdom, and humbly allow God's word to reveal it to them gain understanding. It's just how it works. For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding. He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous: he is a buckler to them that walk uprightly. He keepeth the paths of judgment, and preserveth the way of his saints Jesus having exposed the errors of the hypocrite Pharisees and Sadducees now took aim at the scribes asking how say they that the Christ is the son of David, quoting Psalm 110: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool. 2 The LORD shall send the rod of thy strength out of Zion: rule thou in the midst of thine enemies. 3 Thy people shall be willing in the day of thy power, in the beauties of holiness from the womb of the morning: thou hast the dew of thy youth. 4 The LORD hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek. 5 The Lord at thy right hand shall strike through kings in the day of his wrath. 6 He shall judge among the heathen, he shall fill the places with the dead bodies; he shall wound the heads over many countries. Jesus asks how can a physical son be called Lord by David, himself a king at the writing of the Psalm. And Jesus notes the indication of God the Father, LORD, proclaiming the Adonai, the Lord, Christ, the anointed, the Messiah, is so much more than an earthly king, or a son of David. The crowd who welcomed Him with palms and praise just days before all recognized Jesus as the son of David, promised by God through the prophets, but here Jesus makes clear what exactly that means. That He is the Christ that is seated at the right hand of God, and the people who he was teaching to received this teaching gladly. Then, turning to rebuke the scribes who should know better than the people, who should have been those to proclaim the truth, being keepers of the law, Jesus exposes what their actual priorities are; being seen, being honored, being special boys given praise, preferential treatment and working their way in to widows houses to drain them of their wealth with their false teachings and spirituality without the Spirit. Many such cases today, both in Christianity and in secular spiritual nonsense. Giving long public prayers to show how righteous they are. Wearing long robes to denote their high station, sitting in the choice seats of the synagogue as lords over the common people, using the word of God as their own wealth and prestige, like the parable of the unjust steward from Luke 16. And they earn themselves a greater condemnation, being given worse punishment in Hell for their transgression. As we come to the end of Mark 12 (wew), we see a simple teaching of Jesus to His disciples, the example of the old woman, who by faith gives all of the pittance she has, and shows that she's given more than the rich men making a show of their tithes. It's not wealth that God respects, but are willingness to have faith and believe regardless of how little wealth we have. It's about faith, not our works. And it's an important lesson that we should all take to heart. We should give all we have unto God without worry, and knowing that His blessings are enough. Amen The disproved theory of Evolution of the species, which has become unfalsifiable nonsense requiring increasingly foolish leaps, requiring the constant changing of factors like time frame, scale, etc as each presents a problem. Rather than abandoning the theory, adherents simply say the natural observations and assumptions that disprove it must be wrong. Including the math of time and adaptation that definitively debunks it. Meanwhile, Biblical creation is proved as the testimony of God, and explains the kinds and types, impossible adaptations, incredible beauty, complexity of systems and gives us a true accounting of the origin of race and nations, and the boundaries and habitations thereof. Nonbelievers have faith in science, falsely so-called and the theories of Jews and Masons and Jesuits that tickle their ears and appeal to their conceits, so much so that the shifting narratives used to buttress it fail to even elicit a blip of cognitive dissonance. I have zero interest in debating the theory of evolution versus the Bible. Arguing against hypotheses that are made to confirm a predetermined idea or outcome, that shift constantly to fit new or contradictory information, that are forever unfalsifiable and have no room for an explanation other than chance, or lip service to a vague deity's hand on the scale, is fruitless. Things spiritually discerned and proven by personal observations of the wonders of God and His kept promises, and His Holy Spirit that resides within we who are saved. End times Bible prophecy. The one area of study where we continue to see through a glass darkly. But, for the elects' sake, those of us chosen in Christ, who diligently keep watch, we have been given the knowledge of the signs of the season that we not be caught unawares. That Jesus doesn't come as a thief in the night to those with eyes to see. And so, here in Mark's version of the Olivet discourse, where Jesus teaches some of the apostles, and by way of the Holy Spirit, teaches ourselves, what will be and what to look for, that we may be ready and be saved, should the great tribulation come in our day. First, in response to a disciple wondering at the great temple, Jesus says not a stone on top of another will remain standing. This prophecy was fulfilled in 70AD. Some mistake this as meaning all that follows was fulfilled at that time, which is not supported. Jesus tells us of future events, far outlasting the 1st century, and signs that we have yet to see. Biblical teaching is that we have been in the "end times" from the moment of Jesus ascension on Pentecost. These are the last days. And until the abomination of desolation is revealed and the sun and moon darkens, that like the fig tree budding signals summer, and Christ returns in His glory in the clouds, as angels gather we elect to join Him, we shall remain in these, the last days. And so Jesus begins by warning "Take heed lest any man deceive you." There will be false Christs who, if it were possible would deceive even believers. This we have seen throughout history, and witness it today. Many would be Messiahs, especially of the Jew, rising in prominence and power. False prophets and accused fake churches, claiming to be of Christ. Jesus and the apostles warn of this for good reason. Even now there are many antichrists. And thus shall it be till the end. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many. And when ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars, be ye not troubled: for such things must needs be; but the end shall not be yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be earthquakes in divers places, and there shall be famines and troubles: these are the beginnings of sorrows. Jesus is still giving warning to not be deceived as to when the end comes. He says we will hear of wars and rumors of wars. Great kingdoms clashing. But we aren't to be troubled, because that's not the sign of His coming. These things are always happening. Same with earthquakes and famines and other tribulations, both man made and naturally occurring, that the superstitious and the fearful seize on to say "this is it! It must be the end of the world!" Be not troubled, the end is not yet. This is just the beginning of sorrows. These are things that simply are. That must be. So, he's warned us that we should watch for false Christ's and not be troubled or seek as a sign things like wars and disasters. What the natural man would see as a sign. And further, as a warning to His disciples, says they are going to be brought before rulers and the Jews of the synagogue of Satan to be persecuted and murdered for His name's sake. And that the Gospel must first be published in every nation. He is still warning them that they not be afraid. That they not take their persecution as the sign that the end is here, and understand that it is a testimony against the rulers of this world and how the Gospel is spread to every creature. He is encouraging them, and us as Christians to understand that this is still the case throughout the last days. First century AD, right up until the end. Remember the apostles there asked for the signs to know when the day of redemption would be, and so Jesus is laying the groundwork for what NOT to take as a sign that His return was imminent. False Christs, wars and calamity, disasters and famines, the persecution of the saints in the publishing of the Gospel to all nations. He's saying these things will all happen for sure, but be not troubled, it isn't the end. He gives them, and by inspiration of the word, future believers, the assurance that their persecution will be for God's glory, and that the Holy Ghost will give them what to say as a testimony. Knowing scripture by the Spirit and knowing He brings all things to remembrance that the word of God be made known. It is an assurance, a promise of the Lord. Now the brother shall betray the brother to death, and the father the son; and children shall rise up against their parents, and shall cause them to be put to death. And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved. Understand the context of that last verse, that it is enduring persecution that Christ promises will occur, that those already saved spiritually will be saved physically. Even if by death of the body. Even if by rapture at His return. We are saved from that persecution. So endure. This is not a verse on spiritual salvation, and those who try and make it about that intentionally strip it of it's actual context. Don't be fooled. Now, having laid out these stipulations, Jesus has given so that we may not be deceived into thinking His return was imminent, He segues to the actual day of the Lord they asked of. When ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, (let him that readeth understand) The parenthetical statement of for our benefit. We who are still here on Earth when it comes will understand. This is the sign we look for. Not false messiahs. Not wars or famines or earthquakes. Not persecution that seems overwhelming. Not betrayals by family and friends, or hatred of us for His name. These things will always occur. They must be. But when we see the abomination of desolation stand where it ought not, we should know the day of the Lord is nigh. Jesus warns that all who may be in Judea should flee, shifting His focus from 'ye' to 'they.' That those present there shouldn't even take time to grab their coat. This is described in the parallel passage of Luke 21 as "the days of Vengeance" and it is my belief, comparing scripture with Mark, Luke and Matthew 24, that the vengeance is upon the Jews for their role in setting up the beast to put the abomination of desolation in the midst of Jerusalem. The antichrist turning on them and destroying them. Either way, it's yet another sign when it comes upon them. And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. There is a lot of speculation as to what this means, but it seems pretty cut and dry. Jerusalem was trodden down by Rome, an empire of Gentiles, and it remains so, under Jews who say they are but are not. They that are in Judea. Until the harvest. Until the fullness of the Gentiles has come. When the increase is gathered, the sheaves brought in. The day of the Lord is the harvest. With all biblical end times prophecy there is dual fulfillment, and as we see frequently throughout the Bible, things that fit prophecy are but a picture of the thing to come. But even understanding this, I still see this as fairly straightforward prophecy, given the frequent analogies of the harvest. The fullness of the season. And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring; Men's hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken. And Jesus says this is when you know for sure that His coming is soon. There are those who say that the resurrection is passed, or that we are already in the millennial reign. The Sun and Moon darkening is the consistent signal the day of the Lord is here throughout the Old Testament prophecy and the New. This has not happened. And what follows certainly has never happened. The triumphant return of Jesus in the clouds, visible to all men. And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh. This is the sign. This is how you know for sure. This is the Great Tribulation such as never has been, followed by Sun and Moon darkening, and Christ's return and the gathering of the elect. The fullness of the Gentiles come in. And so this is the parable of the fig tree. This is the sign that it's soon. So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand. Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled. This last verse confuses many. They ignore that this generation refers to the people alive and present when these things come to pass, and instead say that Jesus was speaking directly to the apostles in front of Him and their generation. It's this confusion and other deliberate distortions of these scriptures that dispensationalists seize on to change the plain meaning of the Olivet discourse regarding the end times. They make it more complicated than it is, and trust those they are misleading won't understand the scripture. Exactly what Christ gave warning to beware. Continuing in Mark 13; And except that the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh should be saved: but for the elect's sake, whom he hath chosen, he hath shortened the days. And then if any man shall say to you, Lo, here is Christ; or, lo, he is there; believe him not: For false Christs and false prophets shall rise, and shall shew signs and wonders, to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect. But take ye heed: behold, I have foretold you all things. Jesus says again, don't be fooled. Behold, I have foretold you all things. And so, knowing these things he has foretold us, and keeping His warnings in mind, we can know when His day is near, for He gives us the signs and the timing. ..In those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, And the stars of heaven shall fall, and the powers that are in heaven shall be shaken. And then shall they see the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power and glory. And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven. In those days. AFTER the tribulation. The return. The rapture. The promise of eternal life given in the day of redemption, the Great Day of the Lord come at last! Amen. And so, knowing all this, and understanding what to look out for and what to be wary against, what shall we do? Christ tells us. But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father. Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is. For the Son of Man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch. Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning; Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping. And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch. Watch. Be prepared. Be sober and vigilant. Not carried away by the cares of this world. Not in fear of the tribulation of this world. Not fooled by false prophets. We are to watch and be good stewards who sow increase for the Lord. Be like the virgins prepared for the bridegroom, who filled their lamps with oil. Be like a servant left with 10 talents of silver, who increased his master's treasure. Watch and be ready, that on that great day Jesus greats you saying "well done my trusty servants. Well done."

Here we have Mark's version of events leading to the crucifixion of Jesus. Like most of Mark, it is condensed but packed with narrative and meaning. Like some of Mark's Gospel, details change slightly from the other three, though all of it is there. The difference in timing and point of view, but the testimony the same. Unlike those who came to bear false witness against Christ before the high priests. We see the familiar anointing by the woman with the precious oils. Hear of Judas' decision to betray Him because of it. See the last supper feast, Jesus breaking the bread and blessing the wine, saying He won't drink the new wine, fresh juice of the vine, again until He drinks it in the Kingdom of God. And while Jesus says the bread represents His body, broken on the cross, and the wine, the blood to be shed of the new testament, He clearly doesn't believe it is literally His blood, or else why say that? Christianity is not a cannibal cult. Jesus goes to pray, exceedingly sorrowful at His fate, but resigned to it. Peter and the others sleep when they should be on watch. Peter swears he would die with Jesus, but He tells Peter of his future denials, knowing all things that must happen. Judas betrayal with a kiss. The ear of one of the guards cut off. The disciples scatter. He is arrested. A detail found only in Mark, a boy wrapped in a linen blanket appears and the guards go to grab him, but he runs off naked. It is an odd account but most believe that a young Mark is that boy, his mother's house being in Jerusalem (Acts 12:12). Next we see the false accusations, but Jesus condemned by the truth that He is the Christ. I believe this is important, that they did not turn Jesus over to be crucified for false claims and lies, but they murdered the Son of God for the truth that He was Christ. In the garden, 3 times Peter swears he will stay with Jesus unto death. Jesus tells him to watch and pray that he be not tempted. Yet three times Peter is found sleeping. Peter denies Jesus 3 times when called out, breaking that vow. Had he stayed awake, watching, praying, perhaps Peter then would have had the courage to not deny Christ and honor his vows. In the previous chapter, Jesus warns us the same as Peter, to keep watch for Him. To be vigilant and sober and ready for persecution that will inevitably come for those who standfast in His name as we await Jesus return. To pray for the strength to suffer without fear. And most of us, like Peter, read that admonition in Mark 13, and vow to God in ourselves that we will surely be vigilant, and never back down or deny Him, even unto death. Just as Peter does in the garden. And just like Peter, many Christians, if not all, have periods in their lives where we fall asleep, spiritually. Where we are accused by the unsaved in Jesus' name, and deny Him. Where our vows of vigilance and devotion are forgotten and abandoned. And when we are reminded of Jesus' words, we fall to our knees weeping, like Peter, understanding how unworthy we are of Christ. So, let us learn the lesson of Peter, to stay awake and in prayer that we may not fail when tempted, that we remain vigilant for His return. That we won't deny Him when troubles come because we love Him that the world hates. 1 Peter 2:18-25 Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward. For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God. For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed. For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls. And so we begin the Gospel according to Luke, the physician who journeyed with the apostle Paul, and was companion to evangelists throughout the churches. This (and the book of Acts), written as letters to "Theophilus." The identity of whom is subject to debate, but the term means "friend of God," and may be a general salutation to the saved, given the context; a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us...That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed. Luke begins his recitation of events, not with genealogies of Mary and Joseph as Mark or Matthew, or the divine origins of Christ as God the way John does, but tells us the tale of John the Baptist's miraculous birth to Zacharias and Elizabeth. Here we see their lineage is of Levi and or Aaron, the tribe of the priests of the temple. Zacharias (Zachariah) of the order of Abijah, the course of Abia in the Greek. When David was king he divided up the sons of Levi into various orders or courses, that they be born into tasks within the temple. The course of Abia was responsible for maintaining the altar of incense. It was at this task that Zacharias was visited by the angel of the Lord, Gabriel, who brought God's promise that their prayers for a child would be answered as they were barren and in their old age. That they shall have a son and name him John, who will be a prophet making way for the coming of the Lord, that the children of Israel shall he turn to the Lord their God. And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to make ready a people prepared for the Lord. John was given the ministry to bring the children of Israel to turn to God, to repent. This is the meaning of repentance, to turn towards something. To turn the hearts of the fathers towards their children, to turn the disobedient towards the wisdom of the just. To make a people mete for repentance. To make them ready for Jesus Christ that they might believe. When John is in the wilderness calling the people to repent, this is what it means. Zacharias expresses doubt, and is struck dumb by the angel for unbelief, until the time of this birth be fulfilled. Elizabeth becomes pregnant with John, and glorifies God for His mercy that He take away her reproach among men. Her embarrassment at being without child. She hides her condition for 5 months. At the 6th, Gabriel appears unto Mary. A lowly virgin living in Galilee, in the city of Nazareth, in an area outside of Judea, formerly of the northern kingdom. Samaria. And we are told she is betrothed to Joseph, a descendant of David. Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women. He tells her that she will bear a son, and name him Jesus. That He will be the heir promised of David who will be called the Son of the Highest and the Lord God. That He will rule forever, in a kingdom without end. Mary asks how can this be, seeing she knows not man. And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God. And to shore up her faith, Gabriel tells her of her cousin Elizabeth and her miraculous pregnancy. For with God nothing shall be impossible. This is important to note. Mary, as well as Zacharias and Elizabeth, all are blessed by God. Full glory and honor is given Him by Whom all things are possible. Zacharias and Elizabeth, we are told, were righteous in their faith and perfect in their ways. Not without sin (doubting the angel of the Lord is a sin), but chosen to be blessed for their faith. So too was Mary. She gives consent to God to be used by Him in this manner, saying she is His handmaid, a servant. She believes God's word and is blessed with His promise. Just as the patriarchs and prophets were. Not because she was "sinless" or righteous on her own, but because she had faith and it was counted on for righteousness. Mary then departs for Judea to visit Elizabeth, who, when she hears the greeting from Mary feels the baby in her womb leap for joy. As God had promised, the Holy Ghost would be upon John, and here He comes upon Elizabeth as well, who hearing Mary's story, begins to prophesy; Blessed is she that believed: for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord. Mary is blessed among women because she believed. The blessing is from God. She is "full of grace," not because she is special, deserving, or "strong in the force," or anything like that. Grace is a gift unearned, given by God. Also overtaken by the Holy Ghost, Mary replies to Elizabeth; My soul doth magnify the Lord, And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name. You see the emphasis here is always on God and His handiwork. Not on Mary for being the vessel. And God is faithful and true, keeping His promises; As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever. We learn that Mary spent the remainder of Elizabeth's term with her, and departed. John is born and so named, as the angel instructed Zacharias. When people who know them hear this, they question why. And when mute Zacharias writes in faith that his son's name is John, he is freed from the curse and able to speak again. And the Holy Ghost comes upon him, and he gives praise to God almighty, prophesying in His name; Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David; As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us; To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham, That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear, In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life. And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways; To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins, Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us, To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace. This is the promise of the Lord given witness by all the prophets. Don't miss this. Zacharias is showing, in the Spirit, how all is being fulfilled. With the mercy of God is with them. That his son shall prepare His way. To give knowledge of salvation, by the remission of sins. A light. A guide. Showing the way of peace. Because in sin, man is at enmity with God. But in Christ, God is offering peace on earth, goodwill towards man. This is what was promised Abraham. Moses. David. All the prophets, up to and including John. Jesus is come. I would note that the gospel of Luke is the most thorough regarding the nativity of Jesus. It's what Linus quotes from in the Charlie Brown Christmas special. It's often what we think of and read from at Christmas time. And as Luke writes, this is a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us. And so we should notice what is absent. Those things which are not commonly believed among the first century Christians to whom this gospel is addressed. There is no mention of the immaculate conception of Mary. There is no indication she was born without sin. While she exclaims in the Spirit that future generations shall call her blessed, it isn't because of a special quality of her's, but by the works of God to whom she's a servant. Mary does the will of God through faith, and in faith is blessed among women to be chosen to bear the incarnation of Christ Jesus. This is the grace that God bestows upon her for her faith. For her willingness to believe. Just like the Old Testament saints, Mary believed and it was counted upon her for righteousness. She was saved by faith alone and chosen because of that faith. The Bible says that without faith we cannot please God. Mary could not please God without faith. Zacharias and Elizabeth could not please God without faith. None of them could be righteous absent their belief that God has provided them remission of sins in his mercy. Given the gift of salvation from His grace. Removing this concept from the gospel, those that worship Mary missed the entire point and so they cannot understand God's mercy and they cannot receive God's grace.

1 Timothy 3:16 And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory. Christ is born. Peace and goodwill from God to men. Merry Christmas Luke 2 brings us to familiar ground with the recounting of the nativity of Jesus. Every man in the modern world has heard the details of this story, even if they choose not to believe them. How all the world was taxed by Caesar, and returning to the city of David, where Joseph's lineage came from, Mary gave birth, laying Jesus in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn. Tidings of great joy, which shall be to all the people. (All the people, not some, not chosen, all) For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord. The shepherds gather to witness that which the angels told them, and they spread the word throughout the countryside. Early evangelists, and those they preached to wondered at what they were told. And Mary pondered these things in her heart. After eight days, as was fitting the old covenant still in effect until the day of His resurrection, they took Jesus to the temple to be circumcised and be presented to the Lord. Simeon, who we are told was just by his faith in the coming Christ had the Holy Ghost upon him, and he came by His prompting to see the child, being told that before his death he would witness the Lord's Christ. The promise of the expected Christ was the faith that saved those who came before Jesus incarnation. Just as faith in His perfect work saves now. Trusting God's word, His promises and covenants. It has always been the sole means of salvation. And again, the promise is to all people. And again, Mary wonders at these things as Simeon in the Spirit prophesies that Jesus will fall and rise, and that it will be as if a sword pierces her soul, as the spear pierces His side. They encounter Anna, a prophetess who in her old age as a widow, works in the temple for God. In the instant she saw the baby, she gave thanks to God and went and told all those who in faith looking forward to the redemption that the Messiah was here. And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him. Jesus, being fully man and fully God, was born as we are. He grew as we do. He waxed in spirit and filled with wisdom, meaning He grew into these things. When we see the story of a young Jesus who tarries behind in the temple after going with His family to celebrate the feast of Passover, it is often portrayed as Jesus instructing the scribes there. But the Bible tells us that Jesus was seeking knowledge and understanding from them. Yes He was fully God, but in the flesh, He was tempted, tested, in all things as we are, being fully man as well. He waxed in spirit. He filled in wisdom. He grew physically and in knowledge. And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions. And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers. He astonished them with His ability to understand, but He sought to gain wisdom and knowledge. He was about His Father's business. Some believe he came out of the womb with the full knowledge of everything, and had the whole word of God memorized in His heart, being the author of it. But this story found only in Luke paints a picture of a child who had to grow into a man as we do. And while He was perfect in His ways and without sin, that didn't mean He didn't hunger, thirst or have to devote Himself to learn scripture, just as we do. Jesus' did the will of His Father as an example to us. And God calls upon us to hear His word, question the meaning, learn His statutes, and commit His word to our hearts. Things that take discipline and faith, of which Jesus was the ultimate example. And again, Mary took these things and remembered them, trying to understand just what it meant, that Jesus was Christ. For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. The implications of this are important to consider. That Jesus as man had to, at every step of His life, choose to do the will of the Father, putting that above His own will and the weaknesses of the flesh He resided in. Jesus had to choose to be without sin, though He suffered in the flesh. He chose to learn the word of God as a man would. Devote His time and energy to pleasing His heavenly Father and honoring His earthly parents. Not letting discomfort, cold, hunger, thirst, frustrations, humiliation, or any other thing being Him to sin. Yes the grace of God was upon Him. But we who are saved have a similar grace, but still sin. He grew, He waxed in the Spirit. He grew in knowledge and wisdom, one day at a time, choosing at every opportunity to do the will of Him Who sent Him, so that He could call us to do the same. In that grace. In that love. Amen.
