Romans 13:1-7 Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. 2 Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. 3 For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: 4 For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. 5 Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake. 6 For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing. 7 Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour. If the state has rules on how tribute and custom are collected, then follow them to the edification of the Church and obedience to God's ordained powers that be. If those rules contradict the higher power, especially the highest, God, then we defer to that higher power. Simple as. Matthew 17 24 And when they were come to Capernaum, they that received tribute money came to Peter, and said, Doth not your master pay tribute? 25 He saith, Yes. And when he was come into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying, What thinkest thou, Simon? of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers? 26 Peter saith unto him, Of strangers. Jesus saith unto him, Then are the children free. 27 Notwithstanding, lest we should offend them, go thou to the sea, and cast an hook, and take up the fish that first cometh up; and when thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a piece of money: that take, and give unto them for me and thee. I am seeing this as a stumbling stone and a snare among otherwise good people who confess the Gospel. It is not a primary or even tertiary doctrine in scripture. It's akin to saying that if a church buys a van for its ministry that it doesn't have to be registered or the driver doesn't have to be licensed. It's the "AM I BEING DETAINED?!?" sovereign citizen of doctrines. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. First John, the epistle, is written to the saved. Here the Bible tells us if we the saved, want fellowship with God and one another, to walk with God, to confess our sins to Him, and be forgiven them all by Christ, washed clean in His blood. But some claim sinless perfection, and believe what saves them is their not sinning. According to the Bible they are liars: 7 But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. 8 If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. 9 If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. 10 If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us. In 1 John 2, he brings the point home: 1 John 2 My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous: 2 And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world. 3 And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments. 4 He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him. 5 But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the love of God perfected: hereby know we that we are in him. 6 He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked. 7 Brethren, I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which ye have heard from the beginning. 8 Again, a new commandment I write unto you, which thing is true in him and in you: because the darkness is past, and the true light now shineth. 9 He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now. 10 He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him. 11 But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes. 12 I write unto you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name's sake. Note he is writing to brethren. To the children of God, babes in Christ. He is edifying them and encouraging them to walk with God, to avoid sin and not deny it, but understand that if we are honest we confess our sins, and they are forgiven already in Christ. Because we are sons of God. The correct answer is A. B is an acceptable misunderstanding of the meaning, that basically is just a semantic error, not heretical and doesn't impact the end result, although it does sow confusion when presenting the Gospel to the unsaved, because of the prevalence of C and D. C and D are damnable heresy. If you believe either, repent. I would also add that, so far in our reading of John, where many have believed on Jesus and been saved by that faith, none have "repented" but all have confessed He is the Christ Romans 3:25 - Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; 1 John 2:2 - And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world. 1 John 4:10 - Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins. John 3:16 - For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. Hebrews 9:14 - How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? 2 Corinthians 5:21 - For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. Psalm 103:12 - As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us. 13 Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him. 14 For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust. 2 Corinthians 5:19 - To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation. Titus 3 - 5 Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; 6 Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; 7 That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. Philippians 3:9 - And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith: Isaiah 53:11 - He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities. Galatians 2:16 - Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. Jesus took on our sin and paid the price for all of it. He was the propitiation. The ransom. The sacrifice. By believing this, we take on His righteousness. His blood washes us clean. We are clothed in White of his perfection, our sins forgotten. It is an exchange. That is the testament.

Chapter 10 is a continuation from John 9, and Jesus continues to offer analogy and parable, "dark sayings" so to speak, which call back to scripture that every Jew, especially the Pharisees should recognize, and yet they continue to be blind in their own conceit. This spiritual blindness exists in the world, even today, and once you see it in action you can have no doubt it is supernatural, of God. Jesus compares himself to the door of the sheepfold, all must enter in through Him. He is the Good Shepherd of Psalm 23. The sheep who follow Him know His voice. He will die for the sheep. All who come to the sheep not in His name, not through Christ, are thieves. His sheep will not follow them for they know God's word and hear His voice. Jesus says that from other flocks will he bring into the fold, meaning the Gentiles. He compares the Pharisees and other false leaders as hirelings. Those who preach for filthy lucre's sake and don't love the sheep they are charging a wage to care for. That the Father loves the Son, so as to take even the Son's life that, being the Christ, He will take it again, proving in the resurrection who He says He is. All passages even unsaved but honest seekers of truth can read and understand. Hear and believe. And yet the Jews argued among themselves in disbelief. Despite Jesus openly preaching and doing works of wonders in God's name, testifying that He is Christ, the Jews still need a clear statement, but as Jesus says, He's given it and they cannot hear. They are not His sheep. Then, again as He has in each preceding chapter, Jesus gives the Gospel of salvation by faith, unto eternal life, that His sheep may hear and believe. Jesus says "My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand. I and my Father are one." Like we have seen repeatedly, Jesus spells it out and explains His parables and analogies in clear, unmistakable language. Those who hear the Gospel and believe the truth Jesus gives eternal life. They shall never perish. No man can take them, that is make them unbelievers, bring them to repent of their faith, having repented into belief. No man. Not ourselves, not another. Once you are saved you are always saved, always His, always His sheep. And in case you had any doubt about it, you're not only kept in Jesus' hands, but also God the Father's, who is greater than all. Who created everything, through Christ, who gave up His Son to save us, in Christ, and no one, no force, no act, nothing, can pluck us from His hand. Jesus and God, His Father are one. And the Jews not being His sheep cannot hear His voice. They cannot come to believe. And so they took up stones to kill Jesus. Just as we see so much today, people who are unwilling to believe that Jesus paid it all, that we who believe have eternal life, that it can never be lost, that He is the Son, and He is God, and in God the Father's grace and Jesus' the Son's death and resurrection, our sins are forgiven, the debt paid and His righteousness given to us to make us sons, heirs to this promise. And the Spirit that quickens our dead spirit, bringing it alive, making us born again, sealed unto the end of the world, is the living testimony of God within us, that we may know this promise is true, that we are saved and have everlasting life. Part or all, they doubt. And many still doubt today. They doubt Jesus is God. They doubt that He paid it all. They doubt eternal, everlasting and immorality mean what they mean. They doubt, and in doubt they don't hear His voice. They don't follow when called. And thieves and robbers come and take them. And again, as we have seen each time Jesus gives the Gospel, there is no mention of what we must do other than believing Him, and taking God at His word. There is no mention of works being required, nothing about turning from sin, nothing about our being able to lose it, nothing about it being a limited atonement. But it is a gift of eternal life for the whole world if they but believe. The sole condition given. Unsaved detractors of the Biblical Gospel say it is "easy believism," and dismiss it. If it were easy to believe that Jesus paid it all, there'd be a lot more saved Christians. If it were easy to believe and obey the Gospel, turning from what you're placing faith in, like works, repentance of sin, denomination, status and cares of this world...if it were easy, you'd be saved. As it turns out, yes, salvation is easy but it is incredibly hard to accept. And so strait is the gate and narrow the way which leadeth unto life and few there be who find it.

Jesus wept. The shortest verse in the Bible and perhaps one of the most powerful. Here his friend Lazarus has died, and his sisters are mourning and the emotion overwhelms Jesus even knowing He can and will raise Lazarus up. The pain of life and grief is something that Jesus being fully man experienced and understands. “For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.” Hebrew 4:15 And so, Jesus wept. And then raised Lazarus from the dead. It's one of the most beautiful stories of His ministry on earth, and as Martha testifies her faith that her brother shared, that he shall rise again in the resurrection of the last day. Jesus expounds on this with the full Gospel, yet again: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Martha confesses the truth of the Gospel Jesus gives, the truth her brother and sister also believe. That those who believe on Him shall never die, but he shall live. This is salvation by faith and eternal security, yet again. 11 chapters in and in every one so far, this is the good news as given by Christ. If you doubt His word is true, I don't know what else one could say to bring you to believe. We see earlier in the chapter that upon hearing the news of Lazarus, the apostles are concerned about the Jews wanting to kill Jesus. The other running theme of the Gospel of John. After Jesus miraculous resurrection of his friend Lazarus, we see again that many got saved and believed on Him, but others ran to tell the Pharisees. And again, the Pharisees, more concerned about the Romans and their own power and status in the vassal nation of Judea, that they again plot to kill Jesus. Caiaphas, the High Priest says that it is expedient to kill Jesus to save their nation, meaning in the worldly sense, but as John notes, he was also giving prophecy of the truth, that by one man should die, not only for that one nation but for all nations of those that believe. This miracle of raising Lazarus from the dead, after 4 days, witnessed by many, was the final straw. And faced with a choice of protecting their worldly things, or repenting and believing on Jesus Christ, they put the order out to find Him and kill Him. I was talking about this yesterday, the fundamental difference between people of faith and people of fear determines everything. If you're investing your energy in outrage and fear, you're going to be useless in any movement that actually organically comes up and arises. If your people aren't turning towards God they're not going to make it, it's that simple. The only way we're going to be rid of the Jewish menace is if we unite as a nationalist movement of White Christians, by winning people to the Lord and having as many Godly children as possible, so that we can get a check on the temptations that they offer long enough to boot them the fuck out for offering them in the first place None of your philosophies are explicitly anti-sodomite, anti-reprobate, anti-jew, and full of blessings like serving as a son of God saved by Christ's blood, born again. And for real, if you're suddenly living in a minority majority county, and you can't go cuz you just can't afford to leave? You're better off going soul winning to the heathens than bitching about it on the internet to feds.

Here we see the lead up to the final week of Jesus ministry on earth. He sits and eats with Martha, Mary, Lazarus and the apostles 6 days before Passover. This is the Friday before His death. Christ is anointed, His feet washed with the hair of Mary, the sister of Lazarus. Judas, being a reprobate thief begrudged the expensive ointment used to honor the Lord, and as we often see with those that creep in unawares, he hides his avarice behind "helping the poor," virtue signaling to cover up his own greed. John gives us an update on how the miracle of Lazarus being risen from the dead has given the people an undeniable sign that Jesus is Messiah, and we see that many, including some of the leaders of the Jews come to believe, but status and fear of the Pharisees stops them from confessing the truth. Many Christians today suffer from this, embarrassed, afraid. Unwilling to offend or put their worldly status in jeopardy for confessing Christ is their savior. In a panic, the Pharisees plot not only to kill Jesus but Lazarus too, least his living, eating and drinking among men, be a testimony of Jesus power and God's glory. We see the triumphant entrance into Jerusalem that Saturday morning, fulfilled prophecy and the throngs that will later condemn Jesus just a few days later, hailing Him as King of Israel. The Greeks arrive, looking for the man who has caused this commotion and whom had done these signs and wonders. "Sir, we would see Jesus." This is the final signal that His time was at hand. The Gentiles seeking Him out. The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified. And Jesus gives the Gospel, yet again. And Jesus, resigned to His purpose, glorifies His Father, who answers Him with a voice from Heaven, not for Jesus sake, as He says, but for those assembled that they might believe. Jesus prophesies His own crucifixion, showing that all men are drawn unto Him by His death on the cross. Becoming the sin of all men, to save those who see Him and believe. Because even with these signs and wonders, many still cannot believe. They did not believe God's report, and so, having chosen not to see even when it was spelled out for them, even as He spoke from Heaven, God blinds them, turning them over. Harding their hearts unto reprobation. Jesus again gives the Gospel, asking men not to believe Him only but the word of Him who sent Him. In verse 48, Jesus makes clear that it is not He that judges man, but rather man is judged by the word of God, and our belief or disbelief of that record. He is here to save the world, to fulfill all things, and to keep the commandment of God, which is life everlasting for all who believe His word.

Chapter 13 is a fairly straightforward account. Jesus' last supper before Passover, where He washes the apostle's feet, in an act to teach them of the humility and love for one another that will exemplify to others the love the saved have in Christ. Note, in the Gospel of John, he is who "Jesus loved," who was laying on His bosom. His hour drawing near, he reveals the son of perdition, Judas, that it is he who will betray him. Satan himself enters Judas the unbelieving, sending him on his way to the Pharisees after Jesus shows him He knows. Jesus again explains His mission, so that afterwards they may know He was who He said. Peter is the foil twice in the chapter, first being overly zealous to show Jesus how much he loves Him, tries to stop Christ from washing his feet. Once corrected, Peter, dumb as his nickname, a stone, says "well then, wash my whole body!" Later Peter again in his zeal proclaims his devotion, only to again be corrected by Jesus, and that he will actually deny Christ 3 times. Sometimes, like Peter we get so anxious to please God that we get our own ideas of what that means and what we must do. Instead of slowing down and listening to what God will have us do. And often, we find correction comes in His word, in prayer and when tempted for what we swear, to show it as the folly it is. Peter did great things for the Lord when he stopped to listen. Another note on this chapter, John's account of the last supper. As we have said throughout the Gospel according to John, this is written specifically to the unsaved so that they may understand and come to salvation by faith. So it is important to recognize that there is no account of the breaking of bread and blessing of wine, which were symbols used to explain Jesus' coming trials and death in the other Gospel accounts. If a ceremony of eating bread and drinking wine were necessary for salvation, it would be mentioned here. Of course if it were mentioned, it would contradict the entire message of God's grace giving us eternal life through belief on His Son found in every chapter.

John 14 is Jesus' final, very personal and impassioned, sermon to the disciples. His hour come, he wants to reemphasize to the believers to not despair and to trust God, as they've trusted Him. I am moved to tears almost every time I read this chapter. His promise that He is going to prepare a place for them (and us), "if it were not so, I would have told you," is a loving plea of a brother and friend, entering His darkest hour yet more concerned with their coming trials, doubt and fear. These are saved brothers and sisters of Christ, they know where He is going, they know the way. Thomas and Philip being the foils here allowing Jesus to give them reminder of the doctrines that He taught that they believed on. "How can we know the way?" Jesus answers with possibly the 2nd most well known verse in the Bible; "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me." He is the only way, there is no ecumenical path. It's Christ Jesus or Hell. Jesus and His Father are one, but the works Jesus does and the words He speaks are those of the Father. Jesus encourages then in that faith, that as He does the Father's work on the cross, in Hell, so to will His believers out of the same Love. His confidence in them that they will do even greater works for God (how is that even possible?) is edifying and encouraging. Because He won't be here but in Heaven, and they have many years ahead of them, and we have the time allotted us on Earth, longer than the 3 years Jesus' ministry lasted, we could potentially bring so many more to Him. It's a high bar, but Jesus believes in us as we believed in Him. He asks if they love Him keep His commandments, promises that what they ask of Him, He will give. This is the nature of the believer building their relationship with the Lord. Our fellowship with God the Father through Jesus. Jesus tells them of the Holy Ghost, the Comforter, that once come abides in the believer forever. His promise to not leave His disciples comfortless is also a message to we who believe, and have the Spirit inside us, forever. What a blessing. What a relief in our times we are tested. He tells them of His resurrection, they will see Him live, and know that what He said of the Father and Jesus' work there was true. He promises that in our keeping God's commandments, doing the will of the Father, Jesus will be there manifest with them. A promise that holds true today. If we walk in the word, live in faith, sow the seeds and reap the harvest of new believers, be comforted from fear. He that loves Jesus loves the Father that sent him, and does as He asks us. Jesus tells them the nature of the 3rd person of the trinity, the Holy Ghost. The Comforter. Who, dwelling within us gives us discernment to understand the word, as He teaches us all things and brings to remembrances those doctrines and scripture we've been taught. In Him is peace, to not be troubled or afraid. The disciples would have much to fear in the coming days, and Jesus is assuring them. Our troubles are little in comparison. Why be afraid? Do you not have the Comforter? The disciples wouldn't until Pentecost! Just the words of Jesus and faith in His promise. He tells them to rejoice in these coming days, because of that faith in that promise, and the power and faithfulness of God the Father. With that He says His final goodbye, that He won't get to speak to them much again as the goes willingly to His fate. The prince of this world coming for Him. But Jesus is resigned to do His Father's will, and finishes with that resignation; "Arise, let us go hence." In before some works-spurg says "see, you have to obey commandments to be saved!" They cite this moving speech to His saved apostles and disciples, conflating Jesus final encouragement to them with the Gospel of salvation by faith that's been preached by Christ to the masses for 13 chapters, unable to understand the difference between salvation and sanctification, the faith that saves and the love that shines from the saved. False doctrine in search of whatever hook they can find to hang it on. The worst part is those who do this don't even keep the commandments, never go soul winning, never share the Gospel with strangers. They are constantly involved with their own piety and self-absorbed, vain and dead 'works' that benefit only themselves in their theology of self-righteousness. Fruit inspectors, hypocrites and fools. I don't know who needs to hear this, but convincing someone to convert to your particular denomination, with how based and trad their services are, their vain traditions, architecture and earthly treasures, political power or philosophies and theologies of man, is not giving the Gospel and getting people saved. You're not a soul winning by convincing people to believe your denomination's false doctrines of subscription-based Grace doled out through works, and finding out later if you did enough to merit heaven. That's not the simplicity of Christ, that is not the blessed hope found in Him. It is only through giving the gospel of grace by faith, In Christ alone unto eternal salvation, the good news as proclaimed throughout the New Testament. Sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: How do you say you have hope within you when you say to someone that maybe they were chosen, or maybe they'll do enough works, or maybe they'll stick with it till the end repenting of enough sins, and maybe they might have to go to mythical purgatory and suffer, because what Christ did wasn't sufficient for you. That's not hope, and it certainly isn't meekness and it shows a lack of fear of God, adding to his word knowing the price that pays. Doing works and sacraments, trying not to sin, etc for righteousness or to keep the salvation given by Christ is not love. It's not charity if it's for your benefit. It is a transaction. Love is not transactional. Grace is not contingent on conditions, because it is unearned. Undeserved. Unconditional love. The Bible says that God pays us for our labors, if they are works that don't burn up like wood hay and stubble. If they have eternal value. But His grace is given freely as a gift. It is selfish, because it's done for an ulterior motive rather than simply love, of the Father or of the Son, or of others. Fear of damnation should lead you to understanding that our only righteousness is in Christ, imputed by His blood. Not keep you in line and doing works to earn your way into heaven.

A slight continuation of John chapter 14, Jesus is giving His saved followers final instructions, calling on them to win souls for God. The fruit they bear are converted and saved Christians, who like a branch of a vine then produce more fruit, and so on. Branching out and on, one long vine back to Him, the true vine. God the Father being the husbandman, the planter of the vine, the one who receives the fruit. We are called as Christians to be meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work. To live in the word, reading scripture, in prayer, sanctified, abiding in Christ so that we may be able to bring forth that fruit. If we don't, if we stay carnal, stay in the flesh, not living in Christ but instead the world, we become useless. Withered and dead, producing no fruit. And God "fires" us. Some take this verse out of context to say that we can lose our salvation and that we are cast to Hell, but every mention of fire isn't about Hell. Rightly dividing the word of God often comes down to knowing if it's being addressed to saved or unsaved, about salvation or about another topic. This is one of those cases. We should glorify the Father by being soul winning examples, bearing much fruit. Being Christ's disciples. Not all saved believers rise to this. In fact few do. These are the commandments mentioned in v10, the preceding 9 verses. Not the 10 commandments, but being worthy Christians bearing fruit. It's specific context to the chapter. Jesus tells his disciples and the apostles that if they do this, live sanctified lives seeking to be fruitful, living in Him, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full. There is no greater joy in a Christian life than winning someone to Christ. Family, friends or strangers. It is unspeakably wonderful. This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you. Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends. Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you. Again, the passion and emotion of these final words to His disciples on His way to be arrested and crucified, are heartfelt pleas. How can you not be His friend? How can we not love one another in Christ after what He did for us? If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you. Jesus is preparing them for the tribulations ahead. If He, the Lord is hated, then His servants can expect the same. Because they not only hate the young Lord, but His Father as well. And it wouldn't be a chapter of John without a reminder of who the Jews are. Jesus coming brought the matter to a head, and the Jews rejecting Him, hating Him, revealed they hated the Father and, as reprobates, condemned themselves. They hated Him without a cause. Jesus again tells them that the Holy Ghost will come unto them, filling them with the spirit, the same as happens to us, today who are saved and born again. He prepares them for their mission as He prepares to take to the cross. I picture these things being preached to His disciples as they walk from the hall they held their supper in. Jesus making His way slowly to the Garden of Gethsemane. Maybe bidding farewell to some as they peel off. Anxious to give them all final instructions, providing them with everything they need as His friends. Chapters 14 - 17 are like long goodbye from a friend, a brother. It's beautiful

The Spirit of God, the Holy Ghost, which was foretold by the prophets who were moved by Him to receive the word of God, inspired, and promised of Christ Jesus to us, the Comforter. That He may dwell within us, the Father and the Son, in the Spirit. Who quickens our dead spirit, our stoney heart, and makes us live again. Who comforts us in tribulations. Who seals us as His own, the earnest of our inheritance in Christ; Ephesians 4:30 And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption. Ephesians 1:13-14 In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory. This is the promise, that we who are saved may know we are His, and that we know we have eternal life, adopted as joint-heirs, made sons of God; Romans 8:16 The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God. We who the Spirit indwells are given the power to free those we share the truth with from their sins, to be born again of the Spirit as we were. Through the Gospel, which is given by the Spirit of Truth, that by hearing the inspired word of God, they may believe, and by faith be saved, that they may save others in His name, by that same Spirit. Or, if they have not the Spirit of truth, to be condemned, opposing themselves. Anathema. All men are called by the Spirit, God the Father having lifted up the Son, because the Spirit of the Comforter works to reproved the world of sin, righteousness and judgment. That they may know they need salvation, and believe. And all knowledge is given by the Holy Ghost, who teaches us all things, making God's word understandable, as we hear His voice and follow Him. And bringing all things to remembrance, that we may be able to give a ready answer for the hope we have in Him. And by making our prayers effectual, even as we in our sin don't know what we need, the Spirit makes intercession for us before God in Christ's name. Beginning a study on the gifts of the Holy Spirit, and His fruit that we receive within us. First we must establish that He is Who was sent of Jesus and promised of God. His most important role, testifying that Jesus is the Christ. 1 John 5:7-9 For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one. John 18 is a condensed version of the capture and first trial of Jesus. Documenting the betrayal of Judas, Peter's defensive attack on a servant of the High Priest and his denial of Christ three times before the cock crowed as Jesus had told him he would. We see Pilate testing Jesus and finding no fault in Him. Understand this being the Wednesday of the passion week, and it is Passover day, as we are told the guards were careful not to defile themselves so they could participate in the Passover feast. The parallel with the lamb being brought before the high priest and inspected by the leaders to make certain it is without blemish, just as Jesus is the lamb whose blood keeps us from death. Note that the Jews are not allowed under Roman law to execute anyone, and were they able, their methods of capital punishment were stoning or sword. Only the Romans crucified, or hang offenders from a tree. To fulfill the scriptures, Christ had to be lifted up. Curiously, Deuteronomy 21 (a very interesting chapter in itself), contains this prohibition: 22 And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree: 23 His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled, which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance. Hanging from a tree is not one of the punishments in God's law, but here this will come into play for Christ's sake. (See also Genesis 22, Numbers 21:9, Psalm 22:14-18, Isaiah 53) Jesus states "Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice," and this conditional statement is key to the Gospel and our atonement in faith. Those who can't hear, don't believe, aren't looking for truth. Matthew 7 7 Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: 8 For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened. As we saw in John 14, Jesus said "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me." The truth is God's word. Jesus is the word made flesh. It is testified by witnesses. It is a report to be believed and trusted. "Verily, verily..." Chapter 18 ends as 19 begins with the Jews choosing Barabbas over Jesus, who Pilate continues to call the King of the Jews, in a mocking fashion. It wouldn't be a chapter of John without a reminder that the Jews are the enemies of God.

If you recall, John 18 ends with Pilate saying he could find no fault at all in Jesus and so he offered to the Jews a choice: Ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews? Then cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. They chose a thief and a criminal, choosing sin over the lamb without blemish. Chapter 19 continues this scene. Pilate has Jesus scourged (by His stripes we are healed), and dressed as a mockery of a king, and having been beaten and punished and made a laughingstock (Psalm 22:6-8), Jesus is again presented to the assembly of Jews, and again Pilate gives them a choice to repent, and again the crowd chants "Crucify him!" Pilate as we see, knows the killing of Jesus is wrong, and he is washing his hands of it by giving the Jews the decision. He says to them to take Jesus and kill him themselves, and the Jews, knowing the button to push accuse Pilate of disloyalty to Caesar. Thus, on the third chance the Jews condemn Jesus, and Pilate orders His death. Despite his misgivings. Despite his fear that this is truly the Son of God. Knowing He is innocent. Now again, we have the timing of things from John. This is the preparation day for Passover. It is the 6th day since Jesus supper with Mary and Lazarus, 5th day from the triumphant ride into Jerusalem on the weekly Sabbath, Saturday. This is the Wednesday of their week, Passover, a high Sabbath begins at 6pm. This aligns with the first Passover which was a picture of the Christ to come. The lamb chosen without blemish, brought before the high priest on the preparation day. Slaughtered and burned in a fire, a holocaust or burnt offering. His blood what saves those of us cloaked in it. Passover day is followed by the high holy Sabbath of the feast of unleavened bread, Friday. Saturday is the weekly Sabbath. Three days without work, as Jesus does it all, we can do nothing. Healing us during Sabbath, just as He did so many times to the blind and lame during His ministry. It is why 3 days and 3 nights He will spend dead, in Hell, paying it all for our sin. This is the New Testament. This is why these days were set by God in the Old Testament. This is the greatest of prophecy fulfilled. And the faith that saved in the Old Testament, the faith that saved since Adam, is in the blood of the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. It's a beautiful picture of Jesus and the Gospel, of faith without works, of the same dispensation of salvation for all man's history. And so it's no wonder corrupt false churches teach none of it by their calendar. Of course the sacrifice recalls Genesis 22 Abraham and Isaac, and the purification sacrifice laid out in Leviticus 14, the mount in Jerusalem being where Abraham brought his son. Issac who carried the wood up the hill. God providing the ram, caught by the head in a thicket of thorns. We see God tell Moses that the sacrifice for him that is to be cleansed two birds alive and clean, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop. We see the wood of the cross, the scarlet of the blood, and the hyssop, the same used by the Roman guard to give Jesus the vinegar to drink. We see one bird placed in an earthen vessel, as Jesus was placed in flesh. We see it sacrificed and burned, its blood put on the living bird, which is then set free. Everything points to Jesus and everything in the law was a picture of Him to come, so that the Jews would have no excuse. We see that, before His death, Jesus gives responsibility for caring of His mother to John, keeping the law of the first born son having responsibility for his widowed mother. Catholics use this verse as proof of their sky queen heresy, when it is simply Jesus not sinning even as He became all sin. (The running water on the earthen vessel in Leviticus 14, keeping the sacrifice clean even as it is offered). Now we run into our friend Nicodemus again, for his 3rd appearance in the Gospel of John. He with believer Joseph of Arimathea, set about entombment of Christ. They are working against the clock. Jesus dies at 3pm, Wednesday. He must be in the tomb by 6. As we saw the other day, Deuteronomy 21:23, a bit of non sequitur in the law, requires the taking down of a hanged man's body before the evening so as it won't hang all night. This appeal to the law is given by the men as to why they must bring Jesus down from the cross. With the 3 Sabbaths in a row, had they not, it would have been impossible. Another example of what seems like random OT scripture, pointing to Jesus and facilitating what had to happen. John again describes Nicodemus in the unflattering terms of his having come to Jesus by night. And again we see Nicodemus trying to do the right things, to be a good person, giving 100lbs of spices and fragrance for the tomb and body. An over the top expression of works that many do today, in hopes it may save them. Even as he has the Passover lamb acted out by Christ, he is still trusting in his works. I don't think Nicodemus was saved, at least not at this point. Maybe he repented after the resurrection. The Bible doesn't say, but all 3 of his appearances are cautionary. (Naturally, he is hailed as an example of a great Christian, and is a saint in the Catholic Church) Finally, we see in the selection of His tomb fulfilment of Isaiah 53:9 And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth. Laid in His tomb before the 6pm start of Passover, Jesus begins His 3 days and nights in Hell. As we approach the end of John, I hope that any of you who gave this study a chance and got something out of it, even if you don't agree with everything I wrote, at least take the scripture to heart. That Jesus is the Son of God. He is the Christ. That His sacrifice purchased the gift of salvation for all who believe, and we are saved with that faith, given eternal life that can never be lost or taken. That no works or "repenting of sin" is mentioned, and I pray the incongruities and discrepancies between the inspired and preserved word of God presented in the Gospel of John, and the vain traditions of man offered by various denominations, serves as a way to wake up some to the truth.

The final chapter in the Gospel of John is a kind of postscript to John's account of his time with Jesus during His earthly ministry and after His resurrection, a personal recounting of one of the appearances of the risen Christ, and a redemption arc for the apostle Peter. Now, during this time, after having been shown their faith wasn't in vain, that Jesus is the Christ and the Son of God, but prior to His final ascension on Pentecost, it seems that some of the disciples, Simon Peter chief among them, grew restless absent their Lord. Jesus appeared unto them but wasn't the ever present fixture leading them He had been for the past 3 years. Yes they were saved, yes they knew they had salvation, and yes they knew God's word was true, and yet when left to their own devices, Peter and the others returned to their old ways. Gone a fishing. This is something many if not most newer Christians experience, or even young Christians brought up in the faith. The rush of joy and the zeal for our Lord gives way to our habits and old life, or, without direction fades to mundane tasks of this world instead of living for the God who bought them. As David, a man after God's own heart wrote: Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation; and uphold me with Thy free spirit. It happens to the best of us. That level of zeal is difficult to maintain at times. Peter, one of the greatest Christians, who did so much for the Lord experienced this, and his leadership role lead him to take others along with him, back to the everyday life they'd left behind following Jesus. Not backslidden in sin necessarily, but back to the grind of the world. Carnal but not sinful. More aimless than lost. And here Jesus intervenes. After an unsuccessful night of fishing, Jesus appears on the shore and in a familiar manner to earlier stories in the Gospels, He directs them to cast their empty nets another way, and they are amazed at the fill of the catch. I think this is both real and a picture of the ministry to come in the great commission and the disciples being "fishers of men." That where there's sparsity of "fish" among the Jews, Jesus is showing them that casting a wider net out in a different direction, to the Gentiles, that the nets will be overflowing and yet not burst. As many fish as they can haul in. Jesus dines with Peter, John, Thomas and the others, feeding them bread and fish He provides, over the fire He built. A picture of things. The risen Christ is a bodily resurrection, Jesus eats. He's not a ghost or spirit, but risen in the flesh. After they eat, Jesus tempts Peter three times with the question "Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me?" And Peter, three times, swears that he does, and that Jesus knows that he does. Just as Peter had denied Jesus thrice before the cock crowed just weeks earlier, Jesus has given him a chance to redeem himself, and direction for his life if he truly loved Jesus. "Feed my sheep." This is the direction given to all saved believers, to be part of that royal priesthood. To be His disciples. To share the Gospel and win the souls of those lost sheep. To be fishers of men. It's a personal and touching form of the great commission. Jesus indicates to Peter where his discipleship shall lead, and John as narrator explains to the reader that it's to a martyrs death that glorified God if Peter follows Him. If he feeds His sheep. With that understanding, Jesus says "Follow me," and Peter does, with John coming along. Here we see another instance of Peters personality, why Jesus named him a stone. Peter, processing the death he should die for his following Jesus and feeding His sheep turns and points to John and says basically, "what about him?" It's classic Simon Peter. Jesus' reply, "If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me." is a gentle rebuke and reminder that we aren't to worry so much about how other saved Christians walk their Christian life, but rather concentrate on our own. If one does nothing, that's not excuse for ourselves. It's funny that John tells us there were still Nicodemuses among them who took literally Jesus' words, focusing on the wrong thing, and John takes the time to explain and correct. If he hadn't, there would be doctrines today of an immortal earthly John wondering about until the second coming, and he knows it. Finally John, who throughout his Gospel has referred to himself in various ways, removes all doubt as to who is the narrator here, that he is the disciple whom Jesus loved, and that his testimony is true. It's a wonderful postscript, given that we may believe, and ends boasting of the great works of Jesus Christ, too many to ever document. The world itself cannot contain the books that should be written. Amen This finishes my study on John. It helped me to read it through and write out my thoughts and the Spirit directed meaning of it all. I hope it helped edify others. We know John is the only Gospel written expressly to the unsaved that they may know they have eternal life, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God. The savior of all people, especially to those who believe. Amen. If you are not 100% sure that if you died today you will be with Jesus in heaven for eternity, please take this time to sincerely listen to this presentation of the gospel (for faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God). Not the satanic gibberish of the Charismatics and so-called Pentecostals, but clear understandable language of those assembled there. Not the mistaken doctrine that the disciples spoke Hebrew or Aramaic or Greek, and those assembled heard it in their own languages, but if speaking to a Mede or Libyan or whatever land the pilgrims were from, they were able to communicate the Gospel to them. How do we know this? By the reaction of the Jews from Jerusalem, who mocked what they heard as unintelligible chatter as their being drunken. This is when Peter gives a blistering sermon addressed specifically to those mocking, and an indictment of the Jews of Judea. Peter says obviously they aren't drunken, being only 9 in the morning, but that it's fulfilled prophecy. He then quotes Joel regarding how in the last days the sons and daughters will prophesy, and uses that verse to then lead them the further prophecy of Joel of the second coming of Christ. Peter is not simply defending their speaking in tongues, but like Jesus did repeatedly in His ministry, Peter is using scripture they should be familiar with to bring them the Gospel. He quotes Joel 3's warning of what the day of the Lord will look like, and indicating to the crowd that it is all coming true. Warning them that if they are seeing sons and daughters with signs and wonders, preaching the word, maybe they should take heed of what the rest of scripture says. That "Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved." This is the Gospel. He continues, making clear precisely who Jesus is, what He did, that He did it among them as they well know, and that despite their knowledge they killed Christ. Peter lays the blame for this squarely on the Jews in Jerusalem. Continuing the Gospel, Peter tells them of the resurrection, Jesus overcoming death, and points to Psalm 16 where David writing in the Spirit, gives prophecy of Jesus. Peter reminds them that David wasn't speaking of himself as his body was buried in the sepulchre. That David was speaking of Christ to come, which the disciples were testifying they had seen risen, first hand. Peter explains that having fulfilled God's promise, they had received the Holy Ghost, and the masses witness of this miracle of the tongues is evidence that all of this is true. Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly, that God hath made the same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ. Hearing the Gospel and the truth of the good news and changing their minds, accepting the truth, understanding the role they played in killing the Son of God, they believed.
