Just as Catholicism makes it about their earthly church. All heresy is based on taking the focus away from the glory of God through Christ Jesus and making it man's. The creature putting themselves above the Creator, who is blessed forever amen. Is God then unrighteous? Is it unfair that some are saved and others burned, that those who are elected in faith through Christ are shaped to His purpose, while those who reject the faith and deny the truth have their hearts eventually hardened, cut off and burned? Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will? Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour? That Jesua would be born of a woman, live, be crucified and raised again, to be made Lord as His son, and that all who believe be given eternal life, sealed by the Spirit and given hope to the resurrection, heirs to the Kingdom. Here Paul begins dealing with the JQ. Having established God's word, His grace, our faith, the doctrine of Christ and the condition of the saved being heirs to the promise, adopted sons, he turns to explaining the unrepentant Jew's position with God, relative to the old covenant and salvation in Christ. Replacement theology is the theme. Dispies hate this. Note what the stumblingstone preventing the Jews from being partakers of the promise; faith. The problem with taking an implication from a partial bit of scripture and forming a Doctrine around it is obvious when you apply it to something like this. So if someone offers a Doctrine that's based on a partial verse taken out of context that appears to contradict clearly stated Doctrine we shouldn't then hammer it till it fits but discard it as being incorrect.

I went over Romans 9 last night to show it is about Israel after the flesh, and not, as some falsely teach, about God choosing who gets saved as individuals. Although God may harden the hearts of those who reject Him, salvation is offered to everyone. And thus a remnant of Israel is saved. As Paul attested in himself and other believing Jews. But now there is Israel of the heart founded in faith through Christ, to His glory. The blindness in part, that has come over the circumcision of the flesh that salvation is come to the Gentiles circumcised of the heart. But the promise of Christ, the inheritance in Him, once kept, the old covenant was done away with. What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, which followed not after righteousness, have attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith. But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, hath not attained to the law of righteousness. Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. Clear and concise, inarguable. Israel did not attain the law of righteousness because they sought it of works, and stumbled at the idea of faith in Christ being the means of their salvation. Romans 10 Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved. For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth. Continuing the same thought, that Paul wishes that his brethren after the flesh be saved by the faith that has given him eternal life, but they failed by not believing. They trusted in their works. Their zeal for God wasn't by knowledge, and they sought to obtain their own righteousness. But there are none righteous. No not one. But the righteousness of Christ is enough, for those that believe the Gospel, beautifully laid out here in chapter 10; But what saith it? For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. And with that statement of the faith, Paul ties it back in to the larger point; there is no Jew or Gentile with respect to God. Only believers and the unbelieving. For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek: for the same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? This is an important idea for saved Christians to grasp. That for all the efforts made to send people tracts, pocket New Testaments, door hangers and invitations to church, and our own attempts to get people to believe by our rephrasing and paraphrasing and using logic, none of it saves. Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. The power is in the word. The Spirit works through the word, given by believers to bring men to faith. And so we should not hide that light under a bushel. We should shout it from the rooftops. For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth. But back to Paul's lament; Israel has heard. They had the advantage of the oracles of God. They had the law. They had the testimony of Moses and the prophets, the warnings and appeals made by a longsuffering and faithful God, Who would have gathered them up as His, but they would not. They killed the prophets, they killed Christ Jesus, and are contrary to all men. And so they are shut out of the kingdom and are hurled into outer darkness with wailing and gnashing of teeth. Tearfully seeking repentance, but there is none to be found.

Verse 1, Paul prays that his fellow Israelites of the flesh be saved, by what? Faith. Verse 2, because of their zeal for the Lord which he testifies is real. Many unsaved Israelites loved and wanted to serve God, zealously. But not according to knowledge. Knowledge of what? The Gospel of Christ which is faith. I feel this same way for all those who I know, in real life and online, that I work with and am friends with, who zealously serve God the way they know, but not according to knowledge, doing so with vain works of the law, and so, are not saved. Why? Because Christ is the end of the law of righteousness, to EVERYONE who believes on Him. Once you obey the Gospel, that is believe on Jesus Christ and His perfect work on the cross, death, burial and resurrection, you do not have to rely on works of the law to try and obtain righteousness. Paul says stop wondering who is going to heaven or hell based on their adherence to the law, because doing so denies that we are made righteous in Christ, by faith, and so denies His work that we are counting on. And what is the word of faith that we preach? It's right there in your heart if you're saved, and the Spirit puts it on your tongue to be shared; That if thou confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus and shalt believe in thine heart that God raised him from the dead, THOU SHALL BE SAVED. Period. This is the Gospel. To obey the Gospel is to believe this one truth. There's nothing else regarding righteousness and eternal life to know. There is no secret trick, no hidden gnostic secret. There is no catch. No strings. No being worthy, because no one is worthy of the righteousness of Christ. Just believe. And whosoever believes is saved. Not a chosen people. Not a limited few, picked to believe. Not those who do works, indulge in sacraments, keep Sabbaths, go to church...but those who believe the report given, by whom all prophets testified, given by Jesus Christ in the flesh, and shared by His disciples straight through unto this day. For scripture says "Whosoever believeth on Him shall not be ashamed." And because there is no difference between "Jew and Greek," there is no "chosen people." Dispensationalism rests entirely on the idea that there is, and so they deny the word of God. For whosoever call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. Adam believed. Able believed. Seth called upon His name. Enoch believed. Noah believed. Abraham believed and it was counted upon him for righteousness. Sara, Issac, Joseph, Moses, Joshua..all OT saints, they all are said to have believed and called upon the name of the Lord. That's it. There is no "and..." There is no church you must join, sacrament you must have, no works of the law, no special boy status, no hypocritical "fruit inspection." No other act, regardless of zeal and sincere hope in those acts, can save anyone. So, having shown the saved to whom Paul writes that the Jews of the flesh, even the zealous for God but stuck in the law of righteousness aren't saved, he instructs how to get them saved. That the purpose of the believer is to preach the Gospel, using God's word so that the unsaved hear, and by hearing believe, and believing, call upon the name of the Lord. And then sending them to do the same. Verse 16 says it plainly: The Jews (and all unsaved, Jew or Greek), have not obeyed the Gospel, because they have not believed our report. This is what obedience to the Gospel is; believing it. This is the will of the Father, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day How many of you are zealously trying to gain righteousness and get to heaven by the works of the law? By following carnal ordinances, sacrifices and holy days? The Bible says those works are hay and stubble. They burn up, and only the work God has made us to do, in serving Him is giving the report of the good news by which we have hope unto eternal life to others that they may be saved. Works without faith in Christ as the sole means of salvation are dead and cannot save anyone. Faith, even to him that worketh not, saves. God doesn't hear the prayers of those who don't depend on faith alone for righteousness, or care about their works: Matthew 7 21 Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. 22 Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? 23 And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity. Please do not be like the Jews Paul is writing about. Do not be among those counting on their works before Christ. If you believe that God so loved you that he sent His only begotten Son, Jesus Christ, to live, die and be raised again so that all who believe on Him have eternal life, that can never be taken away or lost, never earned or deserved, given in grace, then confess with thy mouth, call upon the name of the Lord and be saved. And if you obey the Gospel and believe on Jesus Christ as the only way you're going to heaven, the Holy Spirit will bring your dead spirit to life and God will begin working in your life. And if you then read His word daily, reflect on His law day and night, He will bring you understanding. His word will tell you if the church you attend or the denomination you had put your faith in is true. Comparing spiritual with spiritual, you will be shown what doctrines you may have been told are a lie. I am confident in the power of the word of the living God, that if you do, you will be blessed with wisdom and knowledge of the truth. Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for trad Caths, Orthos, special boys, works-based heretics, evangelical cons... is, that they might be saved. For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth James 2 is not an argument against the Gospel of salvation by faith alone in grace alone. You can't just drop "but faith without works is dead" out of context of the topic, who it was written to, etc. You also have to explain away the dozens of clear verses that say it's not of works at all, least any man should boast. "But James 2" is an ignorant, lazy argument of people who don't read the Bible and couldn't understand it if they did being natural men, no matter how zealously they cling to it. They're ignorant of the knowledge of the Gospel, as Paul said in Romans 10.

Romans 11, the culmination of many of the arguments made throughout the epistle, definitively shows that unbelieving Jews have been cut off, to the benefit of the Gentiles, for the glory of God. And yet there are some who cherry pick certain isolated statements, out of context, to teach the opposite; that unbelieving Jews, trusting their works and lineage, and not of grace and faith, are still heirs. So let's break it down. Paul had just concluded that they are a disobedient and gainsaying people. God tried. As Christ put it in Matthew 23:37; O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! So, what then? Are they all cut off? God forbid, for Paul is an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. They cannot be all cut of simply by being Israel after the flesh, or Paul wouldn't be saved. God has not cast away his people which he foreknew. We have already seen that Paul has already written in Romans 8 that those who believe, God foreknew. That same foreknowledge of believers. This is a conditional statement. It's not "God has not cast away His people," but His people that are saved. And to make this point clear, Paul quotes Elijah, who was cursing Israel for their unbelief and seeking the prophet's life. God's reply to Elijah is that there was a remnant of Israel who were saved by faith, who had no bent the knee to Baal. Who were still faithful. By comparing his present time to Elijah's, Paul deliberately specifies that there is a remnant, just as he himself is a remnant, according to the election of grace. That is, a chosen people by grace, believers. Even of the Jews at that present time, as he himself is proof of. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work. With this aside, Paul lays the final nail in the coffin of the idea of works based salvation. The election of grace is to the glory of God, boasting excluded. Unmerited, but accessed by faith, as we have shown in earlier chapters. What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for. But the election hath obtained it. The rest were blinded. Way back in Romans 1 Paul firmly establishes that the Glory of God is revealed from heaven by the mercy He has shown on the believer, and His wrath on those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. That His abundant grace is shown by the forgiveness of sin, even to the Gentile, the same as with the Jew, and that forgiveness in grace reveals His glory from Heaven, so that none have any excuse. That mercy, through us calls others to believe. That wrath on the unbelieving, calls others to believe. All to His glory. Verse 11:11 relies on this established understanding. Have they stumbled that they should fall? No. God forbid. But rather they have stumbled that Gentiles be saved. Why? To provoke the unbelieving Jews to jealousy. Because it all serves to reveal the glory of God. It's not about us. It's not about the Jews. It is about God being glorified through His grace, revealed through His mercy and wrath. So consider this context as we read the next verse; Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness? Paul says he is speaking to the Gentiles here. Asking them a question as the apostle to them; if the world is made rich in Christ because the unregenerate Jews fell, can you imagine how much more the glory of God would be revealed by their coming to believe? Recall that Paul's still talking about his own wish, that his brethren after the flesh be saved. He has already concluded that only a remnant are, and that blindness has come on the rest. That only by being part of the election of grace, given to believers, that they can be saved and made heirs in Christ. God is not a respecter of persons. There is no Jew or Greek in Christ. In that context, we can see Paul's wish for them expressed by the rhetorical question he asks the reader; if their fall was to bring salvation to the world, how much greater would it be if the salvation of the world brought them back? If by any means I may provoke to emulation then which are of my flesh, and might save some of them. This is the point of the jealousy God hopes to provoke in them. That some might be saved. If...may...might...some. Many dispensationalists will twist this series of conditions to mean "will" and "all." For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead? This is the entire point of Paul's arguments about the Jews. They are cast off. They are blinded. They are reprobate, just as Jeremiah preached against Israel; Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them. But wouldn't it be wonderful if the veil were lifted that they may come to believe on Christ? Now the dispensationalist will say that in the end, on the day of redemption, they will look up and see Jesus coming in the clouds and believe and be saved. But that is taught nowhere in scripture. Paul gives us the actual means by which some may be saved. Provoked to jealousy. Provoked to emulation. By what? The mercy and grace shown believers by God. By His glory revealed in the believing Gentiles. The people who were not a people. This theme runs throughout the epistle. There is no glory but God's. And this is how it is revealed. Mercy and wrath. It is not up to us to ask why some are fitted to mercy and others to wrath. This isn't God picking and choosing, but providing the means of salvation, and foreknowledge of who would avail themselves, all elect in Christ Jesus. All who are predestinated by faith in Him to be conformed to Him and His likeness. All who believe become elect and because God predestinated all who believe to be elect and adoption and promises and blessings and to be the seed of Abraham, the father of faith, whether Jew or Gentile. It's the process that was put in place, by the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. And so knowing this, and having shown the Gentiles of the sorry state of the fallen Jews, Paul warns against thinking Gentiles are some kind of special boys, falling victim to their own conceits the way the Jews have. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. If generations of Christians began taking for granted the grace given to them, and assuming it is because they are better than the unregenerate Jews in terms of their own righteousness, they too could be cut off. Blinded just the same. Some take Paul's caution to the Gentiles to mean something entirely different, that the Jews are saved by some other means. But we have systematically proved by going through Romans that that isn't the case. Some will say the holy root are the Jews, and that while some branches are cut off and others grafted in, they still are the chosen of God by genetics. But the true vine is Jesus. It is entirely by grace. There is no difference. If they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again. Simple as. All this is to encourage mercy for their enemies for the Gospels sake, that Christians can maybe convert some by believing on Christ. That some of the Judaizers might get saved. For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all. Israel was to be a light unto the unbelieving world. Now the believing world is to be a light to unbelieving Jews. All to God's glory. O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out! For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor? Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen. For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in. And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins. Here is the crux of the dispensationalist heresy. Their main proof text. "All Israel shall be saved." But we know this is not Israel of the flesh. That not all Israel which are of Israel. Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. And we see the conditional terms of how all Israel is saved; that a deliverer comes out of Zion, to turn away ungodliness in Jacob. Who will take away their sins. That is Christ Jesus. The promise is made in and through Him. And so, as it is written, all Israel shall be saved. The fullness of the Gentiles is the day of redemption. The second coming of Christ Jesus. The day of the Lord. Where the dead in Christ rise and the elect are gathered, and God's wrath is poured out in the unbelieving world. Paul is saying that partial blindness, that veil over their hearts, is going to remain in place until the end of the world. But all Israel, the sons of God adopted by faith, who are the true seed of Abraham, shall be saved. Anyone who tries to justify Dispensationalism to defend their Zionist fever dreams and heretical end times doctrine has to rely on making each argument in a vacuum. Stripping proof texts from their surrounding meaning. By ignoring contradictions and clear verses, to make doctrine from non sequiturs. But when we compare scripture to scripture, their doctrines fall apart. That is why they will make sweeping proclamations and assertions and arguments that are only backed by the stripped-away proof text, and not by the whole context of Scripture. It is why their false teachers will discourage reading the Bible yourself. Studying to be approved before God. They will over complicate it, make you doubt the word. Use false translations, study guides and charts. Tell you you have to "God back to the Greek!" or Hebrew. Imply that if you don't understand it the way they present it, you must not be saved. And inevitably, they will use Judaizing to bring a false gospel of works to reinforce their own wicked doctrines. Dispensationalism has crept in to good, KJV, Bible believing churches with the right Gospel, no doubt. And many saved Christians are misled by it. But if you look at how far along the spectrum of Dispensationalism they are, the more damnable heresy creeps in. A little leaven leavens the whole lump.

Matthew 13 15 For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. 16 But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear. 17 For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them. Psalm 69 22 Let their table become a snare before them: and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap. 23 Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not; and make their loins continually to shake. 24 Pour out thine indignation upon them, and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them. 25 Let their habitation be desolate; and let none dwell in their tents. And so, Paul having settled the matter regarding Israel after the flesh, that none are saved without faith in Christ, same as the Gentiles, dead under sin just as the Gentiles are, that any zeal they show towards God, without faith, is out of ignorance and going about to establish their own righteousness, all together vain; He continues stating his fervent desire that his brothers after the flesh repent, and be saved. This chapter is abused into teaching a false doctrine that all Jews, even the modern "Jews" (who say they are Jews but do lie), are still God's chosen people and thus still are going to be saved, despite being apostate and denying Christ Jesus. They will derisively dismiss the idea that non-believing Jews are cut off and cast out, ears dulled and hearts waxen, unable to believe, as "Replacement Theology." But the epistle to the Romans demonstrates with finality that all who don't believe are cut off, and that it is one continuation of faith that saves. The same for Jew and Greek. The offer to the Greek came after Christ was lifted up, but it is the same offer. The same gift of eternal life in Christ through faith. Being chosen to be God's people by our belief, not by seed. Wild olive branches grafted in to the root that is found in Israel, as unbelieving Jews are cut off and burned. Paul begins the chapter giving a rhetorical question to the conclusions he reached regarding apostate Jews in the previous chapters. Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. Why? Because he himself is of the Jews and a believer. So were most of the early churches. The remnant of those elect in grace, predestined in Christ (not as Calvinism teaches, but by our faith through Christ, not the other way around). If he, Paul is saved then not all of Israel is cast away. God hath not cast away his people who he foreknew. Again, those that are saved and in whom He works to make vessels fitted to His use. It is the same foreknowledge of the elect, those that would believe, not saying every Jew. The prophet Elijah cursing Israel for their unbelief, saying "Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life," is reminded by God that He has a remnant of believers still. As wicked and apostate as Israel got, there were still 7,000 who had not bowed the knee to Baal. Paul using this to say that even then, there were Jews who believed and got saved. That all of them were not cast out. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. The remnant is according to what? The election of grace. Which is as he already established, being saved by faith calling upon the name of the Lord. This is a conditional statement. Dispensationalism always ignores conditional statements regarding the Jews to make these things apply to all of them. And, as an aside he makes yet another statement of salvation by faith and not of works; And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work. There is no grace if you worked for it. There is no working for it if it is of grace. What then? If only a remnant remains of those who believed, then Israel as a nation has not obtained righteousness (they seek to establish their own), but the election in grace, believers, have obtained righteousness by faith. And the rest were blinded. Which brings us back to chapter 1 and the reprobate doctrine. God chooses to blind those who will not believe, giving them up and giving them over. According as it is written, God hath given them the spirit of slumber, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear. As Jesus said in Matthew 13, eyes closed, dull of hearing, hearts waxed gross, they cannot hear the word of God and believe. As David wrote, cursing Israel in Psalm 69; Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back alway. (Note all the cursing of Israel in the prophets and Jesus' preaching. They were not afraid of being cursed for it. The "bless them that bless thee, curse them that curse thee" being fulfilled in Jesus, not anyone calling themselves Jew) Paul hopes that, as God said repeatedly in the OT through the prophets, He will provoke them to jealousy by the salvation of the Gentiles. By giving the Kingdom to another people, they will repent. Paul says that if God is glorified in the salvation of the Gentiles by the destruction of the Jews, imagine how much more glory God would have if the Jews as a nation, would repent and believe? Before getting back into the chapter itself, I want to reiterate that whatever else they are, Modern Jews are not the sons of Judah from the Old Testament. Whether they are Edomites or Khazarians, or some other people, regardless of what Kaiser Sose origin story and Jewish fables, We know they are not the descendants of the 12 tribes of Israel. To the extent they may have some of Abraham's blood in them, So does most of the world. The one defining characteristic of all modern Jews, and by modern I mean going back to the first few centuries AD, or the foundation of Judaism 400 years after Christ, all Jews hold as their primary identity the rejection of Jesus. Be they Ashkenazi, Arabic, Turkish, Polish, Reformed, orthodox, atheist, conservative or liberal... Every single Jew is an antichrist. And God will make of them a synagogue of Satan. Reprobate silver will men call them. For they have been given up and rejected by God. I make this caveat because as we know, dispensationalism is about modern Jews, not the 12 tribes of Israel which no longer exist and haven't existed since 70 AD. When they say that they think that God isn't finished with the Jews or that all the Jews will end up being saved at the second coming of Christ, they are talking about this reprobate group that the Bible says aren't actually Jews. They aren't even Israel after the flesh let alone spiritual Israel, which are all believers. And God has cursed them. Continuing the thought, Paul uses a parable, a picture of what has happened, that the natural root of salvation came through Israel, and though some of those branches were broken off and burned, the Gentiles were grafted in. All by grace through faith. And Paul warns the Gentiles not to think too highly of themselves, that it is by God's grace and to His purpose that this has happened. We aren't naturally supposed to be there, being wild olive trees, and the tree of the vineyard that God has grown with care is pruned of the branches that aren't producing fruit, and grafted us in that will produce in an abundance, but again the glory is His. Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. We shouldn't fall to the same arrogance as the unbelieving Jews. To think we are special boys. There is no Jew or Greek in Christ. Keep humility about our situation. We all deserve Hell and Death. We are there simply by the grace and the purpose of God. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. Well there means, good. Correct. You are right. The Jews were cut off that we may be grafted in. So true. But be not high-minded, or proud, because of God did that to the nation he tended for thousands of years, He could easily do that to the Gentiles. The other nations. Fullness being synonymous with the harvest. The fruit coming in. It isn't some esoteric hidden meaning. Paul says that blindness in part (there's a remnant that believed, remember) has happened until the harvest of the nations is ready. God likens all of this to a vineyard throughout scripture. The spring feasts and fall feasts point to the first and second coming, the sowing and the harvest. The fruits we produce are saved Christians we've led to Christ. The increase, the bounty of the harvest is God's. We are servants, husbandmen. He is the Lord of the harvest. For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. Many find it unfair that some are cut off, they refuse to believe the Reprobate Doctrine, they doubt the judgment of God. They think He must have some secret plan to win them back. A plan B. That even with the law, the Jews were condemned and without it, so were the Gentiles. That the Gospel of faith alone in grace alone of the resurrection, into His kingdom, was the promise that faith was placed in. Without works. To him that worketh not. That this election of grace applies to the Gentile as much as the Jew. That there is no difference between Jew and the Greek, that if all are condemned, then all are saved in Jesus if they believe. It's flawless doctrine, relentlessly building on itself. Here in Romans 11 Paul is finishing the thought of what to say about the physical Israel, the Jews, given all this doctrine. What does the Gospel of Christ mean pertaining to the old covenant? Same as the Greek who are grafted in to the promise by their faith. Verse 6 has God hammer again the point that salvation is not by works. It is 100% by faith, least it no more be of grace. Because it is a gift and the rewards for work is a debt owed. (Works-based heretics BTHO, again) So, having established that the Jews after the flesh have to believe, Paul circles back to Romans 1 and reprobate doctrine, calling in mind the imprecatory prayer of David to blind the wicked who reject the truth of God, unto damnation. However, Paul prays that the Gentiles receiving the blessing and promises, being grafted in, provoked his kinsmen to repentance. That they turn from stubborn unbelief to accepting the Gospel. That they who are believe would be sent, preaching the word, and by hearing, physical Israel believe and be grafted in again. That by his own example living for Christ he gets his nation to want to emulate him and be saved. This plea is a familiar lament to many Christians. We all have unsaved relatives, often close. Friends, coworkers. People for whom we earnestly pray accept the free gift of salvation but who have hardened their hearts. Paul's example of being worthy of emulation is a model for us, that we live the Gospel in a way that draws them to the light and softens their hearts that they may be willing to believe. The warning to Gentiles against becoming arrogant regarding their position relative to grace and the reprobate silver nation of Jews should also be taken to heart. A Godly nation can easily turn from the truth and be burned in the fire, just as easily as recalcitrant Israel could have a revival in Christ and be graft back in. Prodigals restored as heirs. Dispies falsely make this an unconditional statement rather than an argument; that Jews will be graft in regardless of their own belief or wickedness. Paul has built his case, in the Spirit, that everything here is contingent on believing God's law and promises, whom all men know, and knowing are condemned without excuse, except they believe in the gospel, which is of faith in Christ's crucifixion and resurrection for the remission of all sins, that this is a gift available to everyone, without works, entirely of grace, but that God doesn't hold it out to be taken indefinitely, and that at some point He will cut off the unbelieving, reject and turn them over to reprobation. Individual salvation to eternal life, or a physical nation on earth, it's the same. Romans is one thesis. It's one argument. Not context-free series of non sequiturs and fortune cookie verses, that seemingly contradicts others when taken out of context. (This applies to the entire Bible. It's ONE testimony, God's, and one theme, His love for us) This is a powerful and sobering thought. Knowing your dad or mom, sister or brother, son or daughter, reject the Gospel and on the road to reprobation, or who are trapped in their zeal without knowledge, working their way to Hell by not obeying the Gospel. We know God is perfectly just. We know in His love we are saved, undeserved, entirely by grace, because we have believed the report. But do we live in a way that these people who we care about can emulate? Would they want to? What advantage do they see in accepting salvation, in how you live? Are you fearful? Do you stress from the news of the world, the fake and gay theater the beast system presents to keep the cattle in pens for slaughter? Do you live in gratitude and prayer to God in Jesus name? Do you read your Bible and go to church? Do you boldly proclaim the Gospel to every creature, giving a ready and meek answer to the lively hope you have in Christ? This is our calling; spread the Good News with the joy that comes with knowing. Not trying to obtain sinless perfection, (though we should flee sin). Not self-flagellation for sins God's already forgiven in Christ. Not trying to score points with works, chasing "merit" and subscription based "grace." Not smugly sitting in our vain conceit of being "chosen," and so being holier than thou "fruit inspectors." None of that brings the saving knowledge of the Gospel to anyone. It's selfish, self-righteous and if you're sincerely saved by faith, it's squandering the gift you've been given. And I ask this not as a perfect example myself. I fail at much of this too often, but it's what we are called to do. As an offender I am chief. That's why we are encouraged to take up the cross daily. The yoke of Christ is light. The harvest is plentiful but laborers few. Let's GOOOO

Having established all things, Paul now begins the practical application of the doctrines he has laid out. My favorite sermons are those that really tear into the meat of the word and then give practical application, how that doctrine can change your life and make you more able to work for God. Knowledge and wisdom. It isn't enough to know the word or have understanding of how it all connects, without taking the implications and applying it to our lives. How to be doers of the word and not hearers only. Paul, in the letter to the Romans, lays out some heavy doctrine in dense language, the revelation of God, the reprobate doctrine, salvation by grace through faith alone, to the Greek and Jew alike, the understanding of God's grace and the purpose of our salvation. And the understanding of a spiritual Israel, not of the flesh. But what then? Chapter 12, in clear and concise language tells us. That we present our bodies as a loving sacrifice, without blemish, which is our service, separated to the Gospel. Be holy that we may be better able to be of service to God. Vessels fitted for glory. Blameless. This isn't an appeal to hit the gym and not eat poorly. Our bodies are corruptible, and flesh is going to lead us to sin. It is about walking in the spirit that we may not fulfil the lusts of that flesh, and by example bring others to Christ. He writes, be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, which comes from walking in the spirit. To know the will of God. Proving, testing to see what is acceptable. We are to remain humble, understanding that to every man of faith God has shaped to a purpose. Not all have the same gifts, the same talents, but all are members of the same body, which is Christ. None more important or less important. A similar theme Found in 1 Corinthians 12: But now are they many members, yet but one body. And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you. And so each of us should seek to use the talents we have to edify the whole of the body of believers. Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching; Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness. So, to our measure, we all make perfect the will of God. And we see too, that attitude is everything. Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good. Dissimulation is deceit, dishonesty regarding intent. Concealing motives. Love without dissimilation requires also to abhor, to hate, that which is evil. Speaking the truth in love. There is no love in manipulation or in hidden agendas. There is no love without hate. These two tendencies of the world, to see all relationships as transactional, and so what men call love is often manipulative and controlling. Toxic. And with this toxic false love comes the lack of judgment, calling nothing evil. Tolerating all manner of corruption and perversion. "Not judging" but allowing others to do as they will and calling it good. It is codependency, an allowance for other's sin that we then can remain in our own. This isn't love. God's love is without manipulation. It is freely given. We don't have to work for it. Unconditional. To avail ourselves of it, we have to believe He so loved us He gave His only begotten Son. But His love came first, while we were yet sinners. And God hates evil. Many falsely say "God is love" and ignore His holy nature and the revelation of wrath against the wicked. His word telling us of abominations to Him. For example: Proverbs 6:16-19 These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren. The wicked slogan of the prideful sodomites, "Love is Love," is simply putting evil for good, bitter for sweet. It is impossible to love without hate. As we covered yesterday in the first half of chapter 12, faced with the truth of the Gospel and having repented towards God, being changed by the Spirit, sealed unto redemption, with eternity awaiting and goodwill with the Father through adoption as His sons, then we should live as His. To His purpose and glory, not frustrating the grace of God. Not for our benefit; we don't sanctify ourselves and walk in the Spirit to save ourselves from the wages of sin, as we are justified by Christ's righteousness without works of the law, but rather being freed from that fear and the yoke we were under as servants to death, we can become servants to life. We establish the law. Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets. And so, continuing to wrest the implications of salvation, Paul writes; Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another. As Jesus asked us to love our brethren in Him. We should put the profit of our brothers and sisters in Christ above our own. With humility and meekness, being ministering servants. Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord. This is not only in our service to God for His works; winning souls, edifying the brethren, ministering to the afflicted, having hospitality and a generous spirit, but literally too, at work. A Christian is an exemplary employee when they see their work is for God, and a reflection of His work in us. Colossians 3:22-25 Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God; And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men; Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ. But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons. The Bible doesn't say we should serve our bosses if they are saved. If they are Godly. It makes no distinction, and would apply even as slaves. We work, we don't rob our employers, because we work for God. Note the similarity with what John the Baptist preached to the newly converted to Christ in Luke 3: And the people asked him, saying, What shall we do then? He answereth and saith unto them, He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise. Then came also publicans to be baptized, and said unto him, Master, what shall we do? And he said unto them, Exact no more than that which is appointed you. And the soldiers likewise demanded of him, saying, And what shall we do? And he said unto them, Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages. It's the same message. If we love God and we understand eternity in the spirit, then this short time in the flesh is His. And if we love our neighbor, we should seek their profit above our own. And He will repay. Matthew 6:19-21 Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. Get the picture here, if we are humble. Meek. Knowing we are saved. Knowing the love of God and the peace in Christ, act like it. Not in pride, dishonesty. Not taking more than we are due. Our work reflecting the Spirit of God. That we may, by example be part of that revelation from Heaven of His mercy, that His light be magnified in us, drawing others to Him. Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer. Be cheerful. Not a doomer. You have the hope of Christ, act like it. Not fearful, but let that joy come off of you. It is contagious. Be patient in tribulation. This applies obviously to the persecution for our faith, in Christ. But it is more than that. Try not to let the petty frustrations of this world get to you, lead you to wrath, being a bad report to the Gospel we live by. Continuing in prayer, always. Talk to God throughout the day. Give Him thanks and praise. While we shouldn't make a show of prayer, as is the habit of some, we shouldn't be ashamed to ask God's blessings for others and praise for when He answers or blesses. Think of the Philippian Jailer, who was saved by Paul and Silas, and the church planted there that did great things for the Lord. It all came about because, despite being in chains and captive, they sang hymns and Psalms and cheerfully held themselves out as content even in tribulation. Philippians 2:1-5 If there be therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies, Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be likeminded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind. Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality. Bless them which persecute you: bless, and curse not. Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep. We see the simplicity of this love, repeated throughout the New Testament. Be generous. Charitable. Merciful. Hospitable. Bless them that curse you. Turn the other cheek. Trust in God to repay, for vengeance is His. As Jesus says in Matthew 5: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away. Don't let your pride, covetousness, wrath and offense at the inequities of the ungodly be a snare for your carnal mind. God has you. And if you suffer loss for Him, He will repay with rewards greater than you can imagine, and crush our enemies for His sake under His heel. This is the promise of the Gospel, as much as our redemption and eternal life. Every knee shall bow. We will rule and reign with Christ, and He has a rod of iron to correct the ungodly. Better we practice our faith, our religion that is, with this in mind. James 1:27 Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world. As I pointed out during our study of Luke, Jesus gives us a mission statement to live by: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord. Amen! Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits. This admonition, to be of the same mind, is repeated in the epistles, that the churches which receive them understand that we all share one goal. Serve one Gospel. Look forward with certainty, the same hope. It is why one of the 7 things God hates is a sower of discord among the brethren. It is why church discipline exists. But a church that is of one mind can do great things for the Lord. But more so, see that the same caution to be of one mind, not at variance and strife, is coupled with the warning to Mind not high things, to not put ourselves as better than others, but rather condensed to the lowly. To not be wise in our own conceits. Don't be a special boy. If you have wisdom, if you have knowledge, it came from God and isn't yours. Be humble. If facing someone who isn't as far in their Christian walk as you, be patient and longsuffering and offer guidance, because that is why God gave you that knowledge. Don't be high-minded. Don't get caught up in theologies and intellectual pursuit, thinking you're better than the unlearned. Special boys, your Calvinists, reform types, trad Caths, etc, full of vanity and the wisdom of the world, hold themselves up as better than others, full of hypocrisy. But we shouldn't be. Rather knowing that we serve God and love others, seek their profit, not our own vainglory. This is also speaking of not being a respecter of persons in a material sense. Understand that the more lowly and sinful and broken a person is, there's a strong likelihood that they will be receptive to the Gospel. Don't think better of yourself because someone is poor, uneducated, simple, not of your class or status. They aren't beneath you. Be their servants, ministering the Gospel in love. Jesus Christ who is the holy Son of God, was made flesh, subject to the corruption of the world, made sin for our sakes, suffering the humiliation of the cross, pain and death, the fires of Hell, all for our benefit, while we were yet sinners. Keep that in mind. Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men. If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. You can see the theme building. And it reflects everything that Jesus taught in his earthly ministry. It is the serious implication for our faith. Love one another. Love your neighbor as yourself. It's the whole of the law. And you'll note also, as this list of commands given us goes on, The harder and harder it is for the carnal mind to accept. That is, when you walk in the spirit you understand these things and you're less likely to be brought into a snare of wrath or greed or dishonesty and corruption, manipulating others. Because you grow in faith in the certainty of your hope. Because you see God working in your life and all around you. His work revealed to us from the heavens in His wrath and in His love. We live faith to faith. Not just in that we bring others to belief, but that our faith grows. As it is written, the just shall live by faith. You're hospitable and generous to others because you know God gave you what you have and He'll provide again. Your patient and long-suffering with others because you know He was patient in long suffering with you. When you didn't deserve it. You are just in your judgments and fair and honest in your dealings because God was just in His judgment and merciful to you, in truth. And you don't seek vengeance because you know that that belongs to God. And you know that He is not slack when it comes to delivering just punishment on the wicked. Just as Sodom and Gomorrah are held up for an example. And so as much as possible, an important caveat that will cover more extensively in chapter 13, but as much as possible, we live peaceably with all men. This is the implication of our faith, and the understanding of our hope, and a meek and humble acknowledgment of our condition. To better be servants of God. Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord. Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good. And so just finishing up the chapter. We see that this doesn't just apply to brethren, It doesn't just apply to our neighbors, but it really does apply to our enemies as well. But not in the sense our detractors claim; the weakness that they perceive from this. But in truth. Its strength. Again, I'm going to cover this more tomorrow God willing. But we see that in our faith there is understanding of the nature of God. That He will repay. And in our well-doing, in our charity to those who persecute us, curse us, and who do evil to us, we heap hot coals upon their head. It enrages the truly wicked when we show, by our faith, kindness towards them in need. When we turn the other cheek. For those that aren't necessarily wicked but worldly, this provides an opportunity for them to see the love of God through us and wins many of them over. 9 times out of 10 when someone offends you and you turn the other cheek and offer it to them, which isn't an act of submission but of defiance, you will see that most people back down. Where they may have struck an anger, literally or metaphorically, they will be made to feel ashamed. It humbles them and often brings about peace. Making an enemy into a friend. But knowing the wicked, that it frustrates them being that they are implacable and unmerciful and full of all unrighteousness, we can take comfort in the fact that by our defiant and cheerful service to the gospel, by our faith in the Lord to repay with vengeance that is His, they are made more miserable. And God given more glory. They will be punished in this world and the next. While we will have an eternity with God and His love.

Having reached the culmination of his instruction to the saints in Rome on the doctrines implicit in the faith, Paul begins to close out his epistle to them with exhortation for practical living in that faith. What having that blessed assurance of forgiveness and eternal life then means. We are called to live blameless. Our bodies kept pure and acceptable. Not abused by our lusts, marred by our sins. Presentable in our service which is preaching the gospel. Being not caught up in the trends and immorality of this world, but renewing our mind with His word to prove all things by scripture and the spirit, to discern what's true. What's God's will. We don't have to guess or search. It's in the Bible. Paul then explains understanding your own individual calling, and pursuing it for God. That we are to love without dissimulation; pretense. Not hiding what we are or couching it in subtlety. Openly loving as a reflection of God's love to us, shining on others. And to love means hating evil and clinging to good, not just some feel good selfish emotional rationalizing and enabling. And in that love, live in the faith, being a good brother in Christ, example in the world, trusting God for Him to take vengeance. To love your enemies. To overcome evil with good. This is setting up the next chapter, 13, and one of the doctrines most of "our guys" struggle with and we will look at tomorrow. I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation It's today, friend.
