I might make Romans 13 a planned multiday study. I have a dozen scripture excerpts and whole chapters for reference. It would be impossible in a single day. And people are going to be offended. But at least you will know from the Bible what God says if you stick it out. That's my hope at least.🙏🏻 Throughout the epistle to the Romans, we see Paul in the Spirit, building stone upon stone the doctrines of theology upon the foundation of Christ. The implications of our faith and the religion of following it. That God gave His only begotten Son Christ Jesus, that by faith we are saved from the grip of death and the wrath of Hell. Every man. Jew and Gentile. Great and lowly. God is not a respecter of persons. We are in the flesh, and sinful, even once we are saved, spirit quickened, and sealed by His Spirit, unto the day of redemption. But that being our hope, we know that in that day we will be raised, corruptible to incorruptible, into everlasting life. And so, being freed from the burden of sin and death, we then should live like it. As much as possible live peaceably with all men. Loving our neighbors. Loving our enemies. Seeking the profit of our brethren. Serving our masters in our work as if we are working for God himself, because we are. Showing mercy, as mercy has been shown us. Longsuffering as God has with us. Obedient, as Christ was obedient to the cross, even for our sakes. Even as we were enemies of God, that we may, in Him not only have peace with the Father, but become heirs to the Kingdom. Adopted brothers of Christ. That we may rule and reign with Him in the Millennial Kingdom. Don't you know we shall judge angels? And if heirs to a kingdom, princes. And if princes, then we are servants ministering to those we have rule over. And our ministry is determined by our willingness to sacrifice and serve here on Earth. We are given talents of silver by the master while He is gone. And some of us will seek its increase, and use the talents given us to bring forth more, that the Lord at His return can say Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things. Galatians 3:21-29/4:1-7 Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law. But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe. But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise. Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father. Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. And so, knowing we are sons, heirs, princes to a Kingdom, a better country which we seek, seek it diligently. And if under tutors and governors, schoolmasters until the day appointed, then we are to learn to better serve when appointed in that day. And we learn patience. We learn right judgment. We learn the law and the will of God that we may better serve those entrusted to us in the Kingdom, by serving those we are given in this world. We serve God. With our whole heart, soul and mind, we are to love Him. And if we love Him, obey His commandments. As children, we are given to obey our parents. Commanded so, but with promise that we will live long upon the earth if we do. Honoring them, not just with obedience but in caring for them when they are old. Supporting them in their end years. Paying honor. God doesn't say "if the parent is good." He doesn't say if they are believers, it is then saved or unsaved. We are told to love our neighbors as ourselves. The whole of the law and commandments is fulfilled in this. How? In service. With hospitality. Grace and charity. Putting their profit above our own. We learn to minister that we may rule justly. We are to be holy because He is holy. And how can he trust us with much when we squandered the talents we were given? How can we rule others, when we are rebellious and wicked? We become husbands, and expect wives to submit, as they should, but men are to submit to God, and love their wife as Christ loved us, who did so unto death. When men don't submit themselves to God, when they don't love their wives as if they were their own flesh (which they are, joined together by God), then wives no longer submit. Wives are to submit to the husband, and when they don't, their children see and learn to rebel. They no longer honor their parents. When a nation has rebellious and seditious men, unfaithful women, unruly children, then they are punished by God. And God uses the ministers of government to hand out His punishment, that the nation either repents, or is destroyed. And while the unregenerate people that make up the majority of the nation may wax worse and worse, we who are a light unto the world, are told to obey the higher powers. To seek to find ways to please even wicked kings, but always keeping the word of God as our final authority. And by doing so we may be punished. We may be persecuted. We may be thrown into a fiery furnace. Or a lion's den. We may be like the son of Israel, Joseph, sold into captivity and then thrown in prison for being faithful when tempted by the Pharaoh's wife. But these things are done so that the glory of God may be revealed, and more are drawn to the truth. And to the Lord goes the increase. As the prophets were slain. As the Apostles were martyred. As Christ Himself died that the glory of God could be revealed. And so we obey God. We love our wives. Our wives submitting, teach our children. Our children in honoring us learn to fear God. Fearing God and in faith they do great things. And if the evil spirits that rule this world, the principalities that we wrest with, not of flesh and blood, but spiritual, if they seek our lives for it, then rejoice. It will be to the glory of God, and our rewards will be greater than we can convince of. "But I don't like it. I don't like being told what to do. I am obviously better, morally, intellectually, in every way, than my parents, than my boss, than my rulers." The same spirit of rebellion that Satan loosed into the world. God created earthly hierarchies for His purpose. To shape the clay as the potter sees fit. To make vessels fitted for destruction and fitted for honor. Who is the clay to question it? Now if your father tells you to lie, or steal. Or to dishonor God, worship idols, to kill. If he tells you to disobey a higher authority, we have no obligation to. Like Daniel, we do have an obligation to show them an alternative way. God's way. There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it. And so, with every authority. There's never an occasion to partake in another man's sin. There is always a way out, even if that way is to sacrifice yourself that another may not sin, or that those who witness understand the right path, and may be converted by your conversation; which is in the Bible, our behavior. Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Paul and Silas, in Philippi, offended the Jews and were brought before magistrates, given stripes being scourged, and thrown into prison for the Gospel. And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them. And, in their chaste conversation, in their behavior that showed their faith, when an earthquake came and tare down the walls of the prison, they remained, obedient to the charge. And the Philippian Jailer, scared not only for his life had they escaped, but afraid of the God they held their faith in, brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house. And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway. They even remained in prison that the magistrates who had ordered them released in private, would have to come to release them publicly, to the magistrates' shame. And the church of the Philippians was born and grew, and did mighty things for God, because of the obedience of Paul and Silas. To God and to government, even the government that unjustly persecuted them. And this is a pattern we see, God using the persecution of believers, even of Christ, to give the increase. God uses the weak things of this world to confound the strong. And in doing so, they are often converted. Nebuchadnezzar believed, and repented of the evil He would do. Kings came around to free all Judah from captivity. Publicans, centurions, even some Pharisees, all men with power and authority came to believe, and in doing so were given the same spirit we are. To be good ministers, to rightly judge. Paul, despite his being able to be released when arrested in Jerusalem, rather went to Rome in chains that he may minister the Gospel to the house of Caesar. This world isn't ours and the things of it are at best wood, hay and stubble, but the treasure we seek is of Heaven and incorruptible. Things of eternal value. And when we look at the eternal, this mortal life is given perspective. And rendering to Caesar what is Caesar's is a trifling thing. Paying custom and tribute; taxes, is nothing. God provided us what we have and will again. Even from the mouth of a fish. And if we are defrauded, Jesus says to not only let it go, but offer more. They take your coat, give them your cloak also. If they force you to walk a mile, go two. If they strike you, give them your other cheek that they may see what they are doing for what it is, and make the decision in your defiance to either strike again, or in shame back down. And perhaps by your chaste conversation be converted. By your stripes they may be healed. And so, knowing all this, what then? What further hope have we than eternity? Laying up treasure in Heaven? Giving glory to God in our tribulation that more may benefit? What else could we possibly need? God. In His grace and love promises us one more thing; Vengeance. He will repay. And all who have wronged Him, who have persecuted His sons and daughters, will repay. For He is a consuming fire. We aren't simply "Christ-cucks" acting as punching bags. We aren't floor mats to be trampled on. We have the Spirit inside us, we have blessing upon blessing given us. We see God move in our lives in mighty ways, when we walk after the spirit, and we have felt the reproach of God, who scourges every son, when we walk after the flesh. The natural man receiveth not the things of God for they are spiritually discerned. They can't understand this. The worldly men are full of fear and without hope because they don't believe, and not having faith, they cannot see. 1 Corinthians 1:25-29 Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men. For ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called: But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence. Don't be ashamed of the Gospel, for it is the power of God unto salvation and in it we will never be ashamed. God will always deliver. For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing. Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour. Not paying taxes and breaking the law regarding how they are administered, even to a church, is a sin. You can pray they be lowered. You can be thankful God has made your church exempt. You can even take advantage of the various ways to structure your finances or your church's finances in a way that best serves to maintain the Spirit of the law and service to the Gospel. But a so-called pastor in a living room church, refusing to obey the law and encouraging others to do the same almost always is a false prophet and as damaging to the cause of Christ as a false prophet who abuses the system to create a 501c3 in order to mislead people, too. They are the same. I will finish the rest of Romans 13 tomorrow. I want to say that the scripture speaks to all of this directly and emphatically. This isn't my opinion. My opinion is fleshly and worldly and I feel all those things most of you do. Anger. Impatience. Wrathful. Outraged and disgusted and wishing for violence and sedition against our enemies, destruction of those that govern us, hate of taxes. Despising the beast system. All of it. I am guilty. But this is what the Bible teaches and we can see, by studying it out, why it does. It isn't a trick by the Jews to make Gentiles compliant. They riot and seek their own vengeance too. They teach us to hate and riot and resent the powers that be. They sow sedition and revolution. They hate the way of Christ. I pray for our people that we turn to God that He may give us His blessings again. Amen Finishing off the chapter, days in the making. The implications of our salvation and the practical application of it. The law is made whole by our faith. No longer a burden, but a blessing. We establish the law. By putting on Lord Jesus Christ, making no provision for the flesh, we walk in the light. And if we are ministers to that light, we feed the spirit and are given blessings and divine appointments and opportunities to test out patience and give freely to others, knowing that the day of our salvation from the world is nearer than when we believed. Time is short. Our redemption is at hand. Either in the death of the body, going to be with the Lord to be raised up on that last day into glory, or by His coming. Either way, time is short. Don't waste it walking as the unsaved do. The hopeless. But love others with the understanding of our hope, shared in Christ. Amen God bless you all.

Romans 13 continues the theme of how saved Christians are to behave. It begins telling us God's view of earthly authority. Parents, bosses, civic leaders, law enforcement, all authorities under God, wicked and cruel or righteous and kind, to serve His will. Of course we are to follow the higher law of God when earthly authority contradicts it. We are to obey God rather than man, but if at all possible to live peaceably with all men. Many of us bristle at this. It requires our subjection and faith that God will protect and deliver us. Paying custom and tribute to people we know are wicked, stupid, foolish, deceitful is a hard thing to swallow. Not going into reactionary spirals. Not acting from fear. Honoring God by honoring those he's placed in authority over you. Starting with parents for children, husbands for wives, bosses for husbands. When authority places you in conflict with God, meekly and in His name refuse, but attempt to offer a solution, even one that may harm your interests short term, that you may render what is acceptable to God and in doing so be rewarded long term. This is so hard in our current year. But if it's fake and gay, can't be voted out, can't be fed posted, and God is with you anyways, what more can we do but live in Godly subjection? At worse be persecuted for His sake and be rewarded here and for eternity. At best be an example as to how God delivers His sons and daughters from tribulation so that others may believe, and in doing so change the nature of the people, turning them towards God. This is how the Bible teaches us we change who rules over us to a more benevolent or tolerable authority. It's how we win. Hard lesson in faith. Not participating in wickedness, even at a financial loss or loss of "freedoms" while maintaining faith in God to see you though, results in the wickedness passing you by and those pursuing it being undone, every time. It's often our choosing sides on fake and gay matters (things beyond first principles), that creates the conditions of our persecution. Using our wanting to maintain or achieve preferences against us is one of Satan's oldest tricks. And owe no man anything, except the love that is fulfilment of the law. Pay your bills. Live within your means. Don't become indebted according to your own covetousness, be it financially or in obligation. Far too many agree to terms of obligation in exchange for nothing but affirmation of bias and enabling support for sin. It's how grifters make merchandise of you. It's a mental and spiritual usury. Just a quick one on Romans 4:5-8 and those who say "sure, Christ died for our sins before we got saved, but you have to work off and repent of your sins after to stay saved" : ...5 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. 6 Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, 7 Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven (past), and whose sins are covered (present). 8 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin (future). Salvation is a one time gift that covers all sin.

2 Timothy 3:16-17 All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works. Titus 3 Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, 2 To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men. 3 For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another. 4 But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared, 5 Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; 6 Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; 7 That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. 8 This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men. 9 But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain. 10 A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; 11 Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself. 1 Timothy 6 Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed. 2 And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren; but rather do them service, because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit. These things teach and exhort. 3 If any man teach otherwise, and consent not to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness; 4 He is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings, 5 Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself. 6 But godliness with contentment is great gain. 7 For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. 8 And having food and raiment let us be therewith content. 9 But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition. 10 For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows. 11 But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness. Ephesians 4:14-16 That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive; But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ: From whom the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth, according to the effectual working in the measure of every part, maketh increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love. Romans chapter 14 is Paul giving particular application to these things regarding the consequences of our faith, turning it inwardly onto brothers in Christ; our role in edifying one another rather than debating and striving in doubtful disputations about things not clearly taught in scripture. Something we see ourselves in any church or fellowship with other churches or individual Christians. The Bible says we are to be a whole body fitly joined together, repeatedly stating we should be of one mind regarding the Gospel and the ministry of it. That if there are disputes between us, or trespasses against us, that we work it out within the congregation. Even unto church discipline. But in all things we are to strive together for the Gospel, and because of this, and loving one another, we shouldn't judge one another over things the Bible isn't firm on. Understand that the Bible is the final authority on all matters of faith and practice. All scripture is given by God that we may be throughly furnished to all good works. Perfect. Complete. Especially with the catch-all, love each other as you love yourself. Putting others needs before your own. And the profit of others before yours. As much as possible live peaceably with all men. And so, chapter 14 begins with a hypothetical situation to illustrate the point Paul is building to. Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations. This caveat is important to understand what he is proposing; A person weak in the faith may hold themselves to a higher standard than the Bible calls for, that we being more stable in the faith may see as silly. Right up front Paul is warning not to use the occasion to argue with them. Especially of they are so weak of faith, or babes, that either may dig in their heels at rebuke, and add to the Gospel their opinions. Doubtful disputations, arguments about unimportant things that ultimately rest on "if you disagree you aren't saved." Get the picture here. We can assume these are both saved Christians who simply disagree on a matter of separation and sanctification that aren't spelled out, explicitly or implicitly in scripture. Paul uses eating of meat vs vegetarians, but He also applies it to celebration of holidays, even the first day of the week as sacred. Other than the strong admonishment against eating meat sacrificed to idols in 1 Corinthians for example, even if you don't think the idol is anything but wood or molten metal, is clear. And the giving to us that all food is clean and good to eat, that is blessed in Christ by our thanksgiving, there is nothing that says we have to eat meat. Just as there's nothing against abstaining. But one weak in the faith and consumed by guilt at eating an animal, or who sees holidays as unnecessary or even wrong in their conscience, we should be patient with. We shouldn't push them to do what's wrong in their mind, to stumble. Even if you think they're fools. To love them, we shouldn't place stumbling blocks but rather edify them. Our job isn't to judge one another who believe and are not in open sin regarding clear teachings, over petty matters. An example may be something like The woman shall not wear that which pertaineth unto a man, and applying it to all things, even specifically women's attire that has a shared element to what the male version is. Tee-shirts. Sweatshirts. Hoodies. Taking it beyond not crossdressing and wearing modest apparel as scripture teaches, but extending it to a higher level. Just because they have a higher standard than the Bible calls for doesn't mean you should mock it or ridicule it, and by God if it is in your church and it is their standards and it isn't being placed as a work of righteousness, than not only remain quiet about it, but hold to it. Better to dress in the manner that is greater than the Bible calls for than to sow discord among the brethren and bring others to sin. And by the same token, those weaker in the faith should learn not to judge another's walk, if it is keeping with the spirit of the law, but maybe not to your liking. We are to build each other up. Stand fast for what's true, in love. If the Bible says it and they are against it. Correct them. If the Bible gives us liberty to determine for ourselves what's right (again outside clear teachings) then don't worry about others who don't see it yet. If you celebrate Christmas or Thanksgiving, and do it to Christ, giving thanks to God, and someone else doesn't, it shouldn't bother you. Or vice versa. We will give account to God. Don't judge His servants by your own terms. If some brothers see it as unclean and you don't, both being fully persuaded, let the matter settle, but the onus is on both to not give the other occasion to stumble at their own conscience. This can be very hard for many. Especially those who, despite being saved and understanding their righteousness is as filthy rags, take their sanctification in all things very seriously. They see some, in their mind, abuse the liberty we have been given in Christ. Those who do not strive as they strive. Who don't go to church as much as they do. Who don't read the Bible sufficiently enough for them. Who go soul winning sporadically, if at all when you're out there grinding. Those people need your encouragement. Not your scorn, least we think better of ourselves than we ought. Becoming hypocrites. Edify them and show them the blessings of the work that they may emulate you. People who take matters of this life and this world too seriously, who worry about money. Who worry about politics. Who, being weak in the faith feel like we have to be active in supporting candidates to keep "evil from gaining" or something. Who are prepping a bunker and are terrified of persecution, stocking up on ammo and freeze dried food. These to me are people weak in the faith, and I try not to judge. I have been there myself. And while it is important to be ready for things that may happen, and aware of what's going on, to be afraid and give in to the troubles of the world is wrong. But many weak in the faith do it and believe they are serving God when they do. We should receive them, but not to doubtful disputations. Not in strife. I am using examples of how to apply this, and if they aren't perfect don't judge me. But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things... Try saying something like "I'm not judging you, but I can show you from the Bible what the word says." But don't argue. Save admonishment for actual clear doctrines, not your opinions, and not to lord over someone who isn't as far along in their Christian walk as you. (Or who. Being stronger in the faith, acting in that faith but to you, seems wrong)

Romans 14 is often confused by the unsaved with works salvation, but it's addressing those with faith, brothers in Christ, weak in the faith they may be, who add as sin things not inherently sinful, to their own judgement in service to God. It's also twisted by some who take the liberty found in Christ as a license to sin, saying "The Spirit hasn't convicted me on that" as they engage in wickedness clearly commanded against in the Bible. What Paul is speaking to is holier than thou judgments of those with higher standards than even God's, or the mocking of those who see it as vain and foolish, knowing the liberty we have, obeying commandments but not adding things like not eating meat. Both serve God and are acting in their conscience, and to get a brother to stumble in his belief is to occasion them to sin, even if the thing itself objectively isn't sinful. Basically, not being a fruit inspector and minding your own business when someone holds themselves to a higher standard to the glory of God and their service to Him, even if you know it's a little silly. Again, there are conditional statements and orders of operations here that tell us the specific context of what's being preached. As always, scripture references itself to provide the full picture. That's why we study the whole Bible, comparing spiritual with spiritual, not just taking a verse out of context, stripped of the conditionals and order, removed from supporting scripture. You can't form doctrine around a verse or two and your assumptions and own reasonings, to fit doctrine you've decided on. You have to let God's word tell you what it means directly. God is not an author of confusion. The Bible defines itself and gives clear unambiguous statements for doctrine. Matthew 15:11-20 11 Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man. 12 Then came his disciples, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying? 13 But he answered and said, Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up. 14 Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch. 15 Then answered Peter and said unto him, Declare unto us this parable. 16 And Jesus said, Are ye also yet without understanding? 17 Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught? 18 But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. 19 For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies: 20 These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man. 1 Corinthians 10:23-29 23 All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not. 24 Let no man seek his own, but every man another's wealth. 25 Whatsoever is sold in the shambles, that eat, asking no question for conscience sake: 26 For the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof. 27 If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and ye be disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience sake. 28 But if any man say unto you, this is offered in sacrifice unto idols, eat not for his sake that shewed it, and for conscience sake: for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof: 29 Conscience, I say, not thine own, but of the other: for why is my liberty judged of another man's conscience? Dietary laws amended to the sanctification process of the believer often end in the place where "Pharisees were offended" having made those carnal ordinances into works of righteousness themselves. Jesus declares the vanity of these carnal ordinances and dietary laws. Paul reminds that in Jesus all things are good for meat (meat means food to eat in the Bible, not just flesh of animals). But the greater good is loving your brothers and not tempting them to betray what they see as separation and sanctification. To not offend their conscience to please yours. To not be spiteful to those weaker in the faith. To not give them occasion to stumble in their walk.

Romans 15 We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves. 2 Let every one of us please his neighbour for his good to edification. 3 For even Christ pleased not himself; but, as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproached thee fell on me. 4 For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope. 5 Now the God of patience and consolation grant you to be likeminded one toward another according to Christ Jesus: 6 That ye may with one mind and one mouth glorify God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. 7 Wherefore receive ye one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God. 8 Now I say that Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made unto the fathers: 9 And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name. 10 And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people. 11 And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people. 12 And again, Esaias saith, There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles; in him shall the Gentiles trust. To finish the study of Dispensationalism in light of Romans, we skip ahead to chapter 15. Chapters 12-14 describe the behavior expected of a saved Christian, that by our example in the mercy of God, we may provoke the Jew to emulation that they might be saved. Chapter 12; Love. Love of each other and patience and meekness and longsuffering. Living peaceably with all men as an example of the Love shown us of God. Love even to our enemies that it may drive them to anger, or lead them to repent. Chapter 13; Obedience to the hierarchy established by God on earth to His purposes. Chapter 14; Understanding and patience to new believers and those weak in the faith. Gently correcting and not giving them offense that they stumble and backslide. It is this behavior that reveals God's mercy from Heaven, that He may have the glory. This is in the context of understanding the Jews are cut off and Gentiles graft in but that the whole world may come to the knowledge of the truth. In summary, Paul encourages us that the Gospel of God by which he stands was always meant for the Gentiles, too. That adopting them into the promise was always God's plan. That He so loved the world, He had always inspired the prophets to preach of the salvation to come in Christ. Least any should be doubt. That the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy. Amen. Oh, I would be remiss if I forgot this one niggling misunderstanding of Romans 15:25-27; But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints. For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem. It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things. This has been used by unbelieving Jews to claim Christians have an obligation to financially support them, and used by heathens to claim the same. (It is funny how much false doctrine overlaps between the Jew and the heathens) This portion of scripture refers directly to the famine in Jerusalem mentioned in Acts, and the collection among the churches in Asia Minor to benefit the church of believers there in Jerusalem. It is not a freestanding commandment. It is not to the unbelieving Jews. It was for that time and that place and in that context. Brothers in Christ should always seek to give alms to those brethren who are without. Especially if they are of the churches that sent out evangelists who got your church converted and planted in the first place. Nothing more or less. That about sums it up. There is nothing taught in Romans that supports dispensationalism or an "eternal covenant" with Jews after the flesh. Not in 60's AD. Especially not today. I hope this helped edify and give understanding, that God's glory may be revealed in us. Amen

Romans 15 caps off the doctrines of Christ that Paul has laid out for us, the truth of God and His word, finally shared throughout the world to every nation. Carrying over the admonishment of chapter 14, to those stronger in the faith and with better understanding of scripture to be mindful of those weaker than us, babes in Christ. Those easily led to sin by their own devices. To not judge, but support. We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not please ourselves. This is spiritual. The true religion. We put too much emphasis on our own comfort and satisfaction and not the needs of others. When Paul writes to please our neighbors, it isn't as manpleasers, not being weak and being obsequious. But being meek, and leading them for their good and edification. Building people up. This is a hard concept for many. A healthy person can put aside their own wants and desires to make another stronger, and in doing so, shine the light of God that they may come to believe. To ask you the reason for your hope. And so whatever small things you do for them, do it with cheer and charity. Not enabling or partaking in sin, but by example as we are given by the Spirit. Just as Christ by example led us to His truth. He took the pains of our sin upon Himself, loved us, shows compassion for the afflicted, but never once backs down to say what's right. Preaching the truth in love, with all long-suffering. For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope. This is another proof text for scripture being the means by which we learn the doctrines of God. God's word is powerful and where our hope comes from, the object of our faith. The truth of God's word. Paul's prayer is that the patience and consolation of the Gospel, taught in scriptures, the understanding of the implications of our shared faith and common salvation, would bring the churches in Rome, and the thousands of churches that have read Romans, to be likeminded regarding these things, that they may in one accord glorify God. That they may receive each other and the brethren in peace and patience and love, the way Jesus received us to the glory of God. To reveal the righteousness of God to the nations through our salvation. Continuing, Paul reinforces his ministry to the Gentiles, the nations of the world outside of Israel. That scripture has declared that they shall come under God's mercy and so he preaches the Lord Jesus Christ throughout the world. But as it is written, To whom he was not spoken of, they shall see: and they that have not heard shall understand. And this blessing has resounded throughout the centuries that we may come to the same faith, the same foundation of Christ, and be justified by the grace of God. Revealed from heaven by those that come before us. Faith to faith. As Paul begins to wrap up the letter with his intentions to visit the churches in Rome, which he will eventually if not in the manner he thinks as he wrote this, he delves into some of the plans he has made that will delay his journey. One of those things is the bringing of alms to the church at Jerusalem, collected from the churches throughout Asia Minor and Greece to benefit the believers there suffering through a great famine, as we were shown in Acts 11: And in these days came prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch. And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar. Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judaea. This is discussed in other epistles, and is very specific to the time and place and need. It is about saved brethren in the Jerusalem of that time, in the famine that plagued the land as it drew nearer and nearer to its destruction. Relief from the other churches of believers, that the brethren of saved believing Jews and others in that church may ride out the hardship to the glory of God. Many enemies of the Gospel take the following verses from Romans 15 and twist them into something else; But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints. For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem. It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things. Unbelieving Jews twist this to guilt Christians into supporting all Jews. All the time. Begging for money in the most obscene ways, and tricking those weak in the faith into thinking they are mandated to fund "Israel" forever. But we have been made partakers of their spiritual things only in Christ. The need was temporary. For believers. Brethren caught in the midst of God's wrath upon the rest of the Jews. Others cite this passage in the same manner as the unrepentant Jews, claiming we are cucked by our faith, and required to serve Jews. Someone in the ApeMountain chat was asking about the verses in Revelation 2 and 3 where Jesus tells John about His issues with the 7 various independent churches. The question was basically aren't those verses where Jesus tells the churches to repent or He will "remove thy candlestick" saying they are going to lose their salvation? The answer is a resounding no. As the Bible makes clear in Revelation 1:12-20, the candlesticks represent the churches themselves and their fellowship and blessing with Jesus: 12 And I turned to see the voice that spake with me. And being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks; 13 And in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man, clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle. 14 His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire; 15 And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many waters. 16 And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength. 17 And when I saw him, I fell at his feet as dead. And he laid his right hand upon me, saying unto me, Fear not; I am the first and the last: 18 I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death. 19 Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter; 20 The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches. There's a myth that the dark sayings in Revelation are mysterious, but frequently when John seems confused or unsure Jesus or an angel will say "here's what this means." Obviously some remains through a glass darkly, but much of it is explained. When Christ says "Repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick," He is literally speaking of their authority, hedge of protection, etc, as His church in fellowship with Him. He doesn't threaten those saints with damnation, because that would contradict the Gospel given that led them to being God's servants. Jesus repeatedly says something like "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches" in His letters to these churches. Far too many do not have an ear to hear. BTW the false doctrine of "Church ages" that claim there are seven church ages that correspond with how each is described in Revelation, and claiming that we now live in a Laodicean era of lukewarm churches, is foolishness. There are always churches in all ages that have these traits, that's the point of the verses.

It is a foolish and easily debunked heresy of a false gospel that requires one to "rightly divide the word" in a way that ignores Biblical accounts and clear scripture. These false teachers claimed new revelation, that they'd been shown this truth by the Spirit, and that all of the Christians of that day who opposed them were in fact the false teachers, gate keeping this "hidden truth" from being discovered, of the "mystery" revealed to Paul. My main understanding comes from interaction with its postulates, and searching scriptures to see if what they were saying was true. It isn't, and so obviously false and another gospel, that it's almost impossible as a saved Christian to understand how they could believe what they do without being given over to strong delusion. It also serves as a sort of mirror to the heresy of the "Hebrew Roots" movement that claims Christians should adopt OT laws and customs. Hyperdispensationalists teach, for example, that water baptism plays no part whatsoever in Christian tradition, after Paul received his "mystery." It is also a strange cousin to those who deny Paul's writing, and say that the Apostle was a false prophet. That he taught a different gospel than Jesus, an equally absurd and easily exposed heresy. The Bullingerists and the Paul-deniers agree in principle, differing only in if he was of God or not. Galatians 3 For this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles, 2 If ye have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me to you-ward: 3 How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words, 4 Whereby, when ye read, ye may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ) 5 Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit; 6 That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel: 7 Whereof I was made a minister, according to the gift of the grace of God given unto me by the effectual working of his power. 8 Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; 9 And to make all men see what is the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ: 10 To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God, 11 According to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord: 12 In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him. 13 Wherefore I desire that ye faint not at my tribulations for you, which is your glory. 14 For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, 15 Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, 16 That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man; 17 That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love, 18 May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; 19 And to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fulness of God. 20 Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us, 21 Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen. Galatians 3 plays a foundational role in this hyperdispensationalist "Grace movement," as it's the main source for their teaching that Paul had a new mystery revealed unto him by Jesus, and it was a different gospel for the Gentile. But that's not what this says at all, in fact, as God often does in His word, He presents the idea of an unknown, a mystery, a dark saying, and then provides the answer key to understanding it. God is not the author of confusion. Here, in verse 6, we have the answer to the mystery Paul is talking about; that the Gentiles should be fellow heirs with the believing Jews. Partakers of the Fathers promise in Christ, by the Gospel. Partakers and heirs OF THE SAME BODY. By the same Gospel. And that Gospel is identical to the one given by Jesus in John 3:16. Salvation by grace through faith. Eternal life for all who believe on His name. Further Paul expounds that this mystery, of Christ going to the Gentiles that all nations be blessed, was always the plan, from the foundation of the world, and as explained in Galatians 3:8; And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed. Genesis 22:18 and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice. Romans 4:3 Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Genesis 15:6 And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness. The same Gospel. The same faith. Believing God's promise is true, being made righteous by His grace and the blood of His Son. In Whom all nations are blessed

Continuing the study of Spiritual Gifts, I want to refer to 1 Corinthians 12, which has the clearest writing on the topic, but first to establish the context of the epistle. Note Paul is writing at the request of a sister in Christ who reports that the church in Corinth has some troubles. Pride has set some brethren against others in respect to multiple issues. The first being the source of their salvation, making it about the minister of the Gospel they received the word from, using the who as a way to puff themselves up. Paul and Apollos and Cephas camps, claiming a purer lineage in Christ. Of course Paul destroys this idea quickly. It isn't the minister, who sowed or watered or harvested, but the Lord who gains the increase. And, as Paul says that his wish is the church at Corinth be of one mind in Christ, not filled with such divisions, because a church being united in the body of Christ is able to do great things for the Lord. But it can't if pride is giving way to error. Seeking our own glory, not glorying in the Lord. Paul reminds them that God uses the weak, the seemingly foolish, to confound the wise and being to naught things that are, so that no flesh can glory in His presence. Basically, to be humble and stop thinking you are a special boy. That not many wise men after the flesh, mighty men, nobles, are called. The wisdom of this world is not the wisdom of God. And so it is in that spirit that Paul reminds them that they are there only in Christ, who God has made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption. And so, Paul says if we are thankful for the grace of God given us in Christ, that in everything we are enriched by Him, in utterance and knowledge, which we already have seen is of the Spirit of God. And in that humility and understanding and gratitude, that even as the testimony of Christ is confirmed in us by that meek attitude, we shall come behind in no gift, meaning we can become more perfect or complete.

Paul, as always begins with greetings, and as always, is writing to the saved believers in Christ. He had helped stablish this church in Corinth back in Acts 18, and so personally had led many of the church there to Christ. If you recall he was with Priscilla and Aquila there, and that they had also found a brother, baptized by John the Baptist, Apollos, to whom they introduced Jesus as the Christ, making his faith complete. This will be important to keep in mind as we read this epistle. Paul greets them as saints, as are all who call upon the name of the Lord. Who are sanctified by Jesus. And even as they were sanctified by the testimony of Christ, Paul expresses that God's grace continue to bless them in all things, so that they receive all spiritual gifts and knowledge and wisdom. This is the prayer we should have for ourselves and others in our church and those who share our faith. That by their faith, and God's grace they receive understanding and grow in their Christian life to be made more perfect, and in doing so become better use for God. We see the promise of the coming of Christ, who will confirm us to the end, blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ, His second coming. The day of the resurrection and rapture. We are sealed unto judgment with a gift of eternal life that can never be lost or taken away. Jesus redeems us. God confirms us. The Spirit seals us. God is faithful. After his greeting and the establishment or, re-establishment of the shared belief that unites those in Corinth, Paul gets to the heart of the matter in that he has heard reports of division in the church. Those who had been saved by Paul, or Apollos or Peter, and even those who had been saved during the ministry of Jesus Christ, are beginning to form schisms and divisions. Paul is admonishing this, and points out that the baptism and who did it is incidental to the saving faith in Christ Jesus, in whose name they were baptized all. We see this a lot today, people treating what should be a unifying faith as a scene, and bickering about personalities within the scene. This is a real problem and, the denominational splits that we see in the church later all stem from it. Especially the schism that gives birth to the Roman Catholic Church 300 years later, and all of the devastation to Christianity that spun out of it. Paul reminds them that the baptism isn't what they're there for, but to preach the gospel. Here Paul makes several doctrinal statements regarding the preaching of the Gospel that are both sublime truth, and yet obvious to those of us who are saved upon hearing it. That the preaching of the Cross appears to be foolish to those who are either seeking after a sign from God, or to be reasoned with into faith. As Jesus said the only sign the Jews would receive was that of Jonas, of his being in the belly of the Earth for three days and three nights to be risen again. And for the greeks, who sought a reason above all, giving them faith which is the evidence of things unseen, in lieu of logic, appears to be foolishness. We all know people today who are constantly looking for supernatural signs from God before they can commit to believing, or physical evidence of the truth of the Bible from secular sources. Or who seek to impose their own logic on matters that are spiritual. And who stuff at the simplicity of the Gospel as it's presented, despite our knowledge of the power of God that is within it. Similar to the Epistle of James that we read over the weekend, Paul notes that the proud and wealthy, the powerful etc, are less likely to receive the Gospel because God uses our weaknesses to become our strength. Our humility and meekness becomes power in the hands of a believing Son of God. And what many see as foolishness, or weakness and passivity, or supposed slave mentality, is actually the wisdom of God expressed through our understanding, patience, long suffering, and the love that we show to all. A lot of people grapple with this even saved Christians. They seek their own vengeance, they carry the wrath that belongs to God, they grow impatient with His perfect timing. For those who are not saved by faith, these things are a snare and a stumbling block, their pride being caught in those traps. And Paul explains to us too that this all is in service of glory to God. That none of our works, or who we know, or any other ways that man might justify himself in his own wisdom and conceit, but that all we are and all our wisdom and knowledge, sanctification and redemption, comes from God himself and so all the glory goes to him. Paul taking the Gospel to the Gentiles as his primary mission does not mean he had a different Gospel for them, and doesn't mean he only converted Gentiles. Peter being the Apostle to the circumcision doesn't mean he only converted Jews, or had a different Gospel. Anyone teaching that they had two different Gospels or that there is a difference between Jew and Gentile when it comes to salvation, is teaching heresy. If they bring a false Gospel of works for some, or "dispensations" that change the nature of salvation by grace through faith, they are bringing another Gospel and are accursed. Galatians 1:8-9 But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so say I now again, if any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.

Continuing this study on Spiritual Gifts, here in 1 Corinthians 2. Paul is writing to the church at Corinth to address divisions there, the first being those disputing about who is better among them by the minister of the gospel they'd received it by. Paul, who along with Apollos and Peter, is being touted by some as greater, and so he humbly seeks to set the record straight. That he didn't preach to them with excellency of words and speech, an orator, or with particular wisdom and logic, as the Greeks taught in their vain philosophy. He declared the testimony of God win meekness and in fear, and in much trembling. Bringing to them the knowledge of Christ crucified, a demonstration to them of the Spirit, and the power of God. The wisdom of the world is brought to nothing by the wisdom of God. But that wisdom is only revealed, can only be known, by His Spirit. This is a gift of the Spirit, that all are called and those that believe bear witness to the power of God and by the understanding of His word through the Holy Ghost. The things of God are unknown to man, but by the Spirit of God. Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God. This is important. Without first believing the Gospel, preached by the power of the word of God, and the understanding by the Spirit, the things of God are foolishness to man. The Holy Ghost teaches, not the wisdom of men, not of the world, but the spiritual things of God. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual. But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned. The knowledge and understanding of the things of God is a gift of the Holy Ghost. The Spirit of God gives us understanding, from His word. This is why so many who deny the simple Gospel, and chase after the wisdom of men, who seek knowledge of the world rather than the spiritual things of God, say such foolish things regarding God, salvation, doctrine and scripture. They cannot understand because these things are spiritually discerned. They are given us of the Spirit through the word. This gift of the Spirit, understanding of the things of God. Even the deep things, the meat of the word, comes from studying scripture, to be approved by God. As we seek, so to He gives wisdom and understanding freely, through the Spirit within us. We often run into people, especially now online, who are lost in heresy. Who have, what seems to us, foolish understanding of basic doctrines, that we try to correct from clear scripture, and they cannot see it. They are spiritually blind. They trust the wisdom of other men and their own logic, given of the world, to try and figure out what are the spiritual things of God. Because they don't seek the truth, but validation for their own ideas, they cannot receive that gift of understanding the Spirit provides. This can even strike the saved, misled by itching ears to hear false doctrine given by theologians and tradition, and every other thing but comparing spiritual things to spiritual. They may be led to understanding by being reproached with scripture. They aren't completely blind. But they still have to be willing to receive it. Paul, inspired by the Spirit and preaching the word of God by letter, to be read to the Corinthians, is doing exactly this; Showing those willing to be given understanding, the wisdom of God. For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? but we have the mind of Christ.

Second chapter of First Corinthians, Paul is still establishing a few things, making certain basic stipulations regarding the faith, before getting to his main topic of settling disputes that have come up in Corinth. In chapter one, he speaks to the faith they share for salvation, and the fellowship of the sons of God that they should have in that faith and Spirit, given all wisdom and understanding come from God in that Spirit. That unlike the Jews who ask for signs and evidence and the Greeks logic, but that God's wisdom comes from faith and meekness, that the strengths of this world are weakness, and our weakness, God's strength. Paul continues this theme in chapter 2. Paul says he was determined when he came professing nothing of the world, but only Christ when evangelizing to them in the first place, and Him crucified. Reminding them he was with them as they heard and knew the truth and accepted it with fear. Paul humbly says it wasn't his oratory or logic, but the power of the word that convicted them. That word is the "hidden wisdom" of Christ Jesus, written before creation. The reference to "mystery being revealed" isn't gnosticism, but that Jesus being the Christ, "to whom all the prophets gave witness" is the mystery revealed. Christianity is an anti-gnostic religion, in that knowledge of who Christ Jesus is and what He did and why is the great mystery that is told us plainly in the Gospel. It's the entry point to the full enlightenment for the novice, not some secret kept for the adept. It's a mystery, only so far as Jesus identity, and kept only for those prior to His resurrection. Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit... (Ephesians 3:1-6) Paul furthers the doctrine of understanding the word. That it is only in those quickened by the Spirit that all things of the wisdom of God are revealed through His word. For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God...But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned. The wisdom of God is available to all who believe the Gospel and stay in His word. But to those who don't believe, who can't humble themselves to admit they are sinners deserving death, that they are incapable of being righteous enough to justify themselves through their works or repenting of sin, and that our only hope is the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ, freely given through God's grace, God's wisdom is denied them. They can't understand scripture. They stumble over the word. They are offended, snared, trapped in their own pride. Or blinded by their own rejection of God and kept blind by Him. If you are a believer who has done any kind of soul winning, preaching the Gospel, or even engaged with others regarding scripture online, you will quickly see this inability to understand by the non-believer. It's often just their own reliance on the wisdom of the world that conflicts with the truth of God's word, but sometimes you see that it is a supernatural blindness. It can be disconcerting to show someone clear verse that is clearly understood, and they cannot see it, no matter how you present it or how many supporting verses you share. The spiritual blindness is real, and further proof of the power of God and His word. Having established these truths and basic understandings, Paul has set up what will follow, and has subtly separated those people in Corinth by reminding them that hear that they have the mind of Christ and should share understanding and common wisdom, from God and His word, in the Spirit. Just as the Gospel is foolishness to some of the unsaved, the word of God used in correction and reproach should resonate with believers. Hard preaching against sin or heresy should click, be understood, when weighed by the saved, comparing spiritual with spiritual. We can be carnally minded at times, and deny truth when it's presented to us. Rationalizing and putting the cares of the world, or its wisdom, before the wisdom of God. But preaching on scriptural truth should prick our hearts. His sheep hear His voice. We may not like what's being revealed to us or hard preaching against our own conceits, but the Spirit within us recognizes it and it should move us. And if we are willing to sincerely put God's wisdom before our own pitiful fleshly wisdom, we should find it edifying. Paul is laying that groundwork for his chastisement that follows.

Remember, this letter to the church at Corinth is to rebuke strife and divisions regarding earthly things among spiritual brethren. Paul uses carnal, of the flesh, to refer to the things of this world that aren't spiritual. He says he can't even speak to them of spiritual things because they are yet carnal. Babes in Christ who barely can digest the milk of the word, let alone the meat, the harder things of God. His reproach is to say they are yet carnal, and he gives evidence of their arguments over who they got saved by. What minister of God planted the seed or watered that seed or harvested them unto repentance towards God is unimportant. All believers have a minister from who they heard the word, and believing the word, had faith. We are all called to be such ministers, but to God is the increase. To God is the bounty that none of the husbandmen can glory. And when we are in heaven, our works in this regard will be judged. And what we do will be determined by fire, as to whether or not it is wood hay and stubble, to be burned away as unimportant, or precious jewels and gold and silver with which we will be rewarded for our labor. Things of hay and stubble will be these unimportant worldly matters in which we might be right, or diligent in what we do, but with no real spiritual value. Nothing that adds to the glory of God or magnifies His word. Winning souls to Christ, helping the poor and the fatherless, the widows, being doers of the word and not hearers only, those things are rewarded by God in the judgment. Our common foundation is Jesus Christ, and what we build upon that foundation honestly comes down to whether it gives glory to God or not. And your going to the right denomination, adhering to traditions of men, engaging in sacraments and rites, having the correct opinion about a political dispute or a question of genealogies, or the shape of the realm that we inhabit... All of that is wood, hay and stubble. Don't get it confused, and be carnal. Seek the higher things of God comparing spiritual with spiritual, and in your discipleship put away the strife and divisions that the world serves up to us. They are snares. And they use our own pride and subjective nature as hooks to snare us on. This is what Paul means by being a fool to the world. We should know nothing other than what God reveals, because the wisdom of the world is foolishness to Him. There are other doctrines that we can take from this that are important to note. For example notice the Paul says that regardless of our works being judged as wood hay and stubble, burning away and leaving nothing we are still saved by our faith. We lose reward that we might have expected thinking that what we did was of significance to God, but often our pride and conceits can trick us into thinking that hay and stubble are precious stones. The dispute between them regarding Paul, Apollos, Peter, could EASILY be something like the shape of the realm or if nephilim were angelic in origin, or if mountains are trees... Something as simple as whether or not to support a political party or candidate. Pineapple and pizza. These are carnal. That's not to say that discussing it and wondering about it having fun discussions regarding it is necessarily wrong. I enjoy them. But putting them in primacy over the spiritual is foolishness and carnal.

Continuing from chapter 3, which ended; Therefore let no man glory in men. For all things are your's; Whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come; all are your's;And ye are Christ's; and Christ is God's. Paul, having established that the role of the minister by whom they received the Gospel is nothing to glory about, now furthers the thought to remind them that, despite that, the apostles are to be heeded as God's appointed to their role. Human as they are, fools to the world, appointed to death. Weak in the flesh. Despised by man. All this to set up what follows. The sending of Timothy, and the promise that God willing, Paul would go too. And the threat; will he come with a rod or in love? His reproach to them at Corinth continues...

Paul, having established the groundwork begins his reproach of the puffed-up Corinthian congregation, who have division and contention over what are foolish things, all the while, we learn, they are tolerating the worst of sins among them. A member apparently has been fornicating with his step-mother, a sin so disgusting that even the heathens in Corinth find it gross. And by accepting this creep in the church for their gatherings, the prideful members fighting over who the minister of the Gospel they received the word from, for status and boasting, overlook how they appear to others and lose the moral authority to win souls and live Godly themselves. A little leaven. Yeast in the Bible often is used to describe sin, and we see from Paul's analogy that as Jesus is the Passover lamb, our Christian life should be like the feast of unleavened bread that immediately follows. The feasts given by God in the Old Testament serving again as a picture of the Gospel to come. But introduction of a little leaven will mean the entire lump of dough will be soon leavened, as the yeast grows within. Jesus taught of church discipline in Matthew 18, that following a process of airing the trespasses of a brother, first alone, then with witness, then before the entire church if the person won't take the reproach, they should be cast out. And let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican. Here, Paul is expounding on this doctrine. Delivering one who won't repent and turn back to God from their backslidden action to Satan, cast out of the church, left to letting their sin destroy their flesh, in the hopes that either the severity of the rebuke brings them back, or hastening their death, that they be called home in grace (assuming they were saved in the first place). Destruction of flesh but saving the spirit. Further, to keep away condemnation by the world of those who are proclaiming to be God's people, we are called to take this discipline seriously. Far too many churches today, even doctrinally sound ones full of believers, fail at this simple task. They have among them fornicators, the covetous, extortioners and idolaters...and many are just as puffed-up, holier than thou fruit inspectors, while the leaven of sin metastasizes within their own church.

Building on the theme of having proper judgement and chastising the Christians at Corinth for lacking it, being puffed-up, respecters of persons regarding who they are, who they were ministered the Gospel by, unwilling or unable to judge a congregant who not only is engaged in fornication, but with his father's wife, being a poor example of God's people to the Gentiles around them they are to reach, and now taking brethren before the secular judges for defrauding one another....Paul has about had it. As he says in chapter 5, he's not even there, but the reports have left him judging them. That he would come with a rod to correct them if he could. The saved in Christ, when His kingdom comes on Earth during the millennium where the beast is locked in Hell, will rule and reign with Him. It is a merit system of knowledge of God's law, His judgements and our work for him, that will determine to what extent our role will be, but we are all called. As Paul says, we will judge the world...we will judge angels! And so he is rebuking them for going before unsaved magistrates for differences between brothers. Bad enough they defraud one another and further, but to go to judgement before fornicators, idolaters, adulterers, effeminate, abusers of themselves with mankind, thieves, the covetous, drunkards, revilers and extortioners...the secular unsaved of this world, Paul is disgusted. It would be better to just take the L and let the matter go than this. It would be even better to go before the least esteemed believers in their church to mediate, than rely on the corrupt secular government of this world to be judged by those who are not inheritors of the kingdom, such as they are. Paul subtlety reminds them that they too were unregenerate sinners as these, but for the blood of Christ, so as to knock down their puffed-up pride should they take it that way. There but for the grace of God were we. There's some bad doctrine and controversy regarding these verses and especially surrounding "abusers of themselves with mankind." Some of the modern translations that so badly butcher the word, make the phrase into being a Sodomite, or specifically the bottom in a queer relationship. They then extrapolate out that "such were some of you" to arrive at the doctrine that f@gg0ts can get saved. Never mind the context. Never mind this passage isn't regarding salvation but judgment. Never mind that the phrase being translated only appears twice in scripture, and no where else in any form to draw that conclusion. And never mind that it directly contradicts Romans 1 and other scripture on sodomites and the reprobate doctrine. Its actual meaning can be debated, but it certainly isn't that. Most non-pozzed interpret it from context clues of its second appearance in 1 Timothy 1:8-10: 8 But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; 9 Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, 10 For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine ...where the same phrase is translated as "defile themselves with mankind," rather than "abuse," but the same meaning is intended. They take its proximity to whoremonger to say it indicates being a prostitute. There is a school of thought, long out of favor, that it means masturbation. Self-abuse being a common term for the act back in the day. I lean towards this, but it's difficult to say. The larger context of chapter 6 here, that our bodies are a temple of God, and that fornication is a sin against our own body, hints that it could be any manner of fornication, including prostitution and masturbating. "But muh effeminate!" Effeminate does not automatically mean being a queer. It means not being manly, carrying yourself as a woman would. Metrosexual f@gg0try. People will say anything to be rid of the reprobate doctrine and get Sodomites into their church to molest the kids! Others, stripping the context of taking matters before secular judgment, draw out a doctrine of Repent of your sins-works salvation. That "see if you engage in these sins, you're not saved. You won't inherit the kingdom of God!" This ignores the following verses in which Paul says that we are washed and sanctified in Christ, not by how well we can quit sinning. That, as Paul says, "all things are lawful" to us, but not expedient. We have liberty from our sin through Jesus, but it's not in our best interests to willfully sin, especially fornication. That there's a cost. That it's harmful, because God has made it so. There are consequences for abusing yourself this way should we take this liberty to fornicate like a harlot, God forbid. Not only do they give exception for monogamous relationships outside of marriage, cohabitation etc, where they claim that since they are" in love" it's just as good as marriage, but even to the point where they forgive the whore-mongering and harlotry of their members. Allowing that leaven to leaven the whole lump as it were. By being soft on fornication, they not only are being contrary to God's law but they're opening their own members up to self-abuse in this regard. God tells us that it's not only a sin but harmful to us and yet, most churches won't even preach against it except to teenagers perhaps. It was such an important Doctrine, that in Acts of the Apostles where they are debating the things they can tell other churches that they should be wary of regarding the Jews and circumcision, and idolatry and the like, they make it a point to speak out against fornication.
