The final chapter of Ephesians, Paul continues to build on the idea that we are not to despise government, the hierarchies put in place by God, but to honor and respect them, even when they are cruel to us. For we aren't theirs, but God's and what we do in our labors is His. Be it a husband, a mother, a child, a master or a servant, a king or a subject. If they aren't demanding we sin, truly sin in the despising of God, worship of idols or the blasphemy of the Spirit, and the like, we should in all good conscience work that which we can do, upright. This bothers many. "How can I obey and serve a cruel and ungodly master? A wicked husband? Dishonorable parents? A beast-system state?" The Bible tells us with faith, meekness, serving God and by our actions, convert the lost. I find that those that bristle the most at this were raised without proper fear and respect for their parents, due to whatever reason, although mostly having the rod spared or worse, used in anger, bringing their children to wrath. And as the relationship with the father goes, so to becomes their relationship with all superiors, and in the end, their relationship with God. We should, as Christians, seek to be blameless. Be the hardest worker at your job. Be the most honest. Take the least advantage and support and uplift others, not being a respecter of persons. Diligent and happy. Having faith in God who rewards us, Paul says, Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free. This is not weakness, but strength. For the powers that be have authority from God, be they wicked or just, those who bear the sword do it to the fear of the unrighteous. 1 Peter 3, which echos this sentiment, shows us how regardless the situation, we win: 13 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? 14 But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; Or 2 Peter 2: 4 For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment; 5 And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly; 6 And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; 7 And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: 8 (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;) 9 The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished: 10 But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities. Of course Romans 13, which causes so much turmoil to those who hate authority: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. 2 Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. 3 For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: 4 For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. 5 Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake. 6 For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing. 7 Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour. This idea of rendering unto Caesar, of not being offensive to any man, does not require us to sin, to tolerate those who hate God, to do those things that displease Him and violate His will. We answer to the higher power for conscience sake, to Christ who is Lord over all. But in all else? Don't be offensive. Render custom and duty and tribute to whom it is due, without complaint. We see this at work in Daniel 1: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon unto Jerusalem, and besieged it. 2 And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with part of the vessels of the house of God: which he carried into the land of Shinar to the house of his god; and he brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god. 3 And the king spake unto Ashpenaz the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring certain of the children of Israel, and of the king's seed, and of the princes; 4 Children in whom was no blemish, but well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science, and such as had ability in them to stand in the king's palace, and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans. 5 And the king appointed them a daily provision of the king's meat, and of the wine which he drank: so nourishing them three years, that at the end thereof they might stand before the king. 6 Now among these were of the children of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah: 7 Unto whom the prince of the eunuchs gave names: for he gave unto Daniel the name of Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, of Shadrach; and to Mishael, of Meshach; and to Azariah, of Abednego. 8 But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself. 9 Now God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love with the prince of the eunuchs. 10 And the prince of the eunuchs said unto Daniel, I fear my lord the king, who hath appointed your meat and your drink: for why should he see your faces worse liking than the children which are of your sort? then shall ye make me endanger my head to the king. 11 Then said Daniel to Melzar, whom the prince of the eunuchs had set over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, 12 Prove thy servants, I beseech thee, ten days; and let them give us pulse to eat, and water to drink. 13 Then let our countenances be looked upon before thee, and the countenance of the children that eat of the portion of the king's meat: and as thou seest, deal with thy servants. 14 So he consented to them in this matter, and proved them ten days. 15 And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king's meat. 16 Thus Melzar took away the portion of their meat, and the wine that they should drink; and gave them pulse. Here Daniel and the other believers don't wish to defile themselves with eating the kings sacrifices, but they don't seek to offend the head of the servants they serve. So they meekly make a deal to find a better compromise. The eunuch, afraid if they passed on the food the king provided, they'd be miserable and weak and sickly. Daniel says, let us eat pulse (grains), and in 10 days we will look just as healthy and happy. In faith, Daniel served God and the men over him. And God gave them strength and nourishment. And of course we know about the faith of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, where Christ delivered them of the fiery furnace. And so we honor our parents, the first commandment with a promise from God, that in doing so we are blessed. We work diligently and with all humility and fear, because we work for God. And we are to remain humble and honest in our dealings, if we are bond or free. We can do this if we remember we are outfitted with the whole armor of God. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Girding our loins with truth, the breastplate of righteousness, your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace, the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked, the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit which is the word of God. We are equipped with these things, when we walk in them. And if we walk in them, we should have no fear of the wicked. We are prepared with truth, not dissimulation, protected from blame by being righteous, prepared to give good answer for our hope everywhere we go, with the good news of God's peace with man in Christ Jesus. Our faith a shield against all attacks, no matter how fiery. Protected with the sure knowledge and confidence of our salvation. And armed with the sword of the Spirit, the word of God, which is quick and powerful, sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. For, If God be for us, who can be against us? So, Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying. Knowing these, as natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed, speak evil of the things that they understand not; and shall utterly perish in their own corruption; And shall receive the reward of unrighteousness, as they that count it pleasure to riot in the day time. And pray, Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked; from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity. God is good, all the time amen.

Paul writes to the churches at Philippi from his bonds in Rome, chained 24/7to a guard, in house arrest for Christ. He gives greeting to the believers there, wishing grace and peace, assuring them of his confidence in their salvation and prayers that they grow even more stedfast with the news of his affliction, rather than be troubled or discouraged. Even in chains, hopeful and joyous. Even with threat of death, to which Paul writes would be better, to be with Christ than to live in the flesh, but that there are needs to be met while still here, and accepting God's will either way. What an example to the early churches, who all suffered some tribulation. Paul notes that there are some preachers using his bonds to inspire more to partake in the Gospel, and some, who out of envy for his renown, preach out of spite for Paul, and yet Paul sees even the good in that, because the preaching of the good news of salvation is all we should care about. Not ourselves or our reputation. Once Philippians is over I may take a break from the NT book-by-book reading to go back to either the minor Prophets in the OT, or possibly Gospel of Matthew. Maybe both. I feel the need to have some meat of the word under our belts heading in to Colossians and especially Thessalonians. I reserve the right to pray on it and do as the Spirit leads. And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment;That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ. Pray your love abound. For knowledge and judgement. Approve things that are excellent, be pure, sincere, without offense. Many put knowledge of the things of this world before love, and miss out on the wisdom of God and discernment that comes from love. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you. To be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord. Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also. He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son. To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne. To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God. God is outside of time. All creation is within time. Angels, man, souls, spirit, corruptible and incorruptible. The souls of the saved will see Heaven. The souls of the damned go to Hell. Until the first resurrection of the saints into glorified bodies, and the White Throne Judgment sends those tormented in Hell to the lake of fire for eternity. There is a Heaven right now, and a Hell. The current Heaven and Earth pass away and a New Heaven and a New Earth come, which all saved inherit a part in. Revelation 19 11 And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. 12 His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself. 13 And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God. 14 And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean. 15 And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God. 16 And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, King Of Kings, And Lord Of Lords. Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are the poor of spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of Heaven Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand Just to expand upon this point and why I believe the Bible teaches a intermediate stage for those in Christ whose physical body passes away now, before the day of the Lord, before the first resurrection, that our souls go to Heaven, not sleep or instantly regain consciousness at the resurrection as if no time had passed. Most will agree that the Damned await in hell until the white Throne judgment where by they are cast into the lake of Fire. That their torment is immediate and without cease. The Bible also talks about The souls of the righteous in Christ crying out "how long?" to God, awaiting His wrath. Both of these imply that to us, to our souls or to our bodies, flesh or spirit, that we still exist within time as the created. That everlasting and eternal have no meaning outside of time. That it's only the Creator who exists outside of time, time being a creation itself. Our corruptible bodies do change in the twinkling of an eye, corruption taking on incorruption. But when quickened, by grace through faith, our spirit never dies. Nor does it sleep.

The first 4 verses continue the well wishes of the first chapter, where Paul is assuring those whom he has confidence in their salvation, to pray for wisdom and knowledge and act in love. Esteeming others better than ourselves, obedient to God's will. Here, Paul beautifully uses Jesus as our perfect example of service to others, love and complete obedience to the will of the Father. It chokes me up, and fills me with that blessed hope of the day every knee bows to the greatest name in and under Heaven. And we should obey this will, working outwardly our salvation that is inward. Not having dead faith but doing the work of His will and good pleasure, just as Jesus showed and as Paul strives for. That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world. Paul then gives assurance of Timothy and Epaphroditus who he is sending in his stead, being in bondage. Philippians is one of my favorite epistles, for it's clear meaning and beautiful prose. It is easily understood and straightforward doctrine on sanctification and doing works of the Lord. However many works-based false teachers use the "work out your own salvation with fear and trembling" line to teach that you cannot be assured salvation, and that we must do works to be saved. This out of context understanding is contrary to scripture, even scripture within the same epistle. In chapter 1 Paul says: For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now; Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, ye all are partakers of my grace. He has confidence in them, that they partake in the same grace that saved him. This is only conditioned on their having fellowship in the same Gospel he preached to them, not on their works, and with not doubt that God works in them. It is another case of reading the whole of scripture and comparing it with itself, saving us from bad doctrine.

Paul turns to the matter of adhering to the law and circumcision, a theme of epistles stemming from the decision made in Acts to warn against adding to the gospel of faith by Judaizers. Paul argues to these Gentiles, that if birth, circumcision and zeal for the law saved anyone, it would be Paul, but he counts all his own "righteousness" as dung, so that he may gain Christ. He warns to beware the dogs, reprobates sneaking in and judaizing churches, subverting houses, crept in unawares. Evil workers. They of the circumcision. Paul says they are the enemies of the cross of Christ. Because believers are not circumcised of the flesh, but of the heart. Saved by faith, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith: That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection. Paul does remind us that despite our having the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ, we should strive for sanctification, to be more perfect, more complete in our walk. Striving for the mark. Nevertheless, whereto we have already attained, let us walk by the same rule, let us mind the same thing. Obeying the law, not for our own righteousness but for the love of God. Not walking as the reprobates do, glorying in the sins of the flesh. Their end is destruction, but ours is in Heaven and eternal life. And to be clear, the enemies of the cross of Christ are those who try to convince others they need to do the works of the law or acts of the flesh in order to be saved. Those who try to convince people to trust in what Paul calls dung, our own works, turning from sin, baptism, anything added to the faith in Christ alone, makes them enemies of the cross. Approve that which is excellent. Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God. The fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace. The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, And he who is wise wins souls. And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith. Press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. Let us therefore, as many as be perfect, be thus minded, whereto we have already attained, let us walk by the same rule, let us mind the same thing. John 11:25-26 Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this? Well? Believest thou this?

Paul ends what is one of the most beautifully written thank you notes of all time. Full of exhortation and doctrine, blessings and thanks. Lessons for how to live for God and be at peace in Christ. Rejoice in the Lord always: and I say again rejoice.Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand. Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. This should be the default state of your Christian life. Joy, not worrying and fearful for the cares of this world but trusting, in prayer and supplication to the Lord, in thanksgiving for the blessings and the tribulation by which the Spirit strengthens us. Having the peace with God that comes from being Christ's. If your walk isn't this, if troubles of the world weigh you down to bitterness, anger, resentment, envy and strife, then know it doesn't have to be this way. Walk less in the flesh and more in the spirit. In daily prayer, scripture reading, singing songs of praise and the psalms. Knowing with confidence your blessed assurance, that God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus. Think upon things of virtue, honesty, pure, true. Meditate on the law of God, and you will learn to praise Him and be content with whatever state you find yourself in. Abased or abounding. Satisfied with what you have, thankful to God that you have it. Knowing for certain in faith that you can do all things through Christ which strengthens us. Living faith to faith. And be fruitful, not as the world measures in wealth and status, but in souls won by your faithful service to God, reached by His word, a path lit by the light of your example. For me, in my journey here, it was fear and concerns of this world that led me consistently to misery, anger and resentment. The Bible warns us against this inclination of man, towards faith in all things. And in the paradox of the wisdom of God, it is accepting on faith that these things don't matter, where you will see the most change. That you're willing to count for loss but gain in Christ are the areas God will bless you the most abundantly. Fear for family, work, relationships with others...all the trauma and drama of this world, all things work for good when you love God and trust Him, thankful regardless of outcome. Just have to let go. The more you do, the more you stay in the word and do what your supposed to, without worry or fear or entitled expectations of what you "deserve" the more you will find you get what you need. And the more you bring people you love to the same peace, that passes all understanding, that comes from the grace God shows His children. Paul thanks them again for what was a care package the Philippians took it upon themselves to send him. He pours out thanks and praise to them, for thinking of him in his bondage, under house arrest in Rome. He gets in one last clever aside to show how even in duress, all things work for good. All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar's household. A sly nod to the will of God working through our tribulation to bring others to Him, even to the most powerful in an empire, even by the most lowly of us, in chains. I've heard pastors preach sermons on Philippians that can be summed up, beautifully, that the primary message of the epistle is joy. Rejoicing in our salvation. The joy of knowing Jesus. The Joy with which we should live our lives. Rejoicing for the Lord. It's why it's one of my favorite books of the Bible, and hopefully that message of joy comes through in your reading of it. According to my earnest expectation and my hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether it be by life, or by death. For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain. Yea, and if I be offered upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I joy, and rejoice with you all. In prison, literally chained to a centurion in Rome, uncertain of his future but caring not for his life, (for to be absent the body is to be present with the Lord) and his hope, Paul's ernest expectation, which is, by definition what faith is. What hope is. An earnest expectation, we sincerely expect this to happen, that God who cannot lie has promised our salvation and eternal life through faith in His Son Jesus Christ. And in that knowledge, that belief, Paul says whether it be his life or death, whether he sees the Philippians again or not, that he will have joy, and rejoice. Amen. Amen.

Here in the opening of Paul's letter to the saints at Colosse, we have one of the most eloquent descriptions of who Jesus is and our shared faith in Him. Note again, Paul prays for God's grace, and the peace that comes from it for those reading. It is only possible to have peace by having peace with God, and that peace is only possible by being partakers of His grace. And all knowledge and wisdom of God's word comes from Him, and those sincerely seeking it. Paul wishes all this that the Colossians may continue being fruitful, sharing the faith and winning more to the body of the church, which is Christ's. Preached to every creature. Strengthened with His glorious power, that we may endure all things with longsuffering and patience and joy. Delivered with His blood. Redeemed by Him. Partakers of the inheritance of the light, saved from the darkness. Translated into the Kingdom of Heaven. (This is the biblical meaning of being translated in regards to our spiritual state, and the Kingdom. It is not the bodily assumption of our corruptible flesh, as some presume, but a change of our spirit, quickened by the Holy Ghost, made acceptable by the blood) Jesus is the express image of God the Father, and made through Jesus, all that has been created is His, who was before all things. Who is the first fruits of the resurrection, so that He may have preeminence in even that, making peace with God through the cross, reconciling all things. And for us who are grounded and settled to this Gospel of reconciliation: And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now hath he reconciled. In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight. We who were dead in sin, enemies of God through our wicked works, made unblameable and unreproveable before God, reconciled with the Father by the Son. Our sins forever forgiven. And Paul made a minister unto the Gentiles, suffering in the flesh for the Gospel's sake, to edify, build up, the body which is the congregation of believers, serving the head which is Christ Jesus. Rejoicing in this suffering, Paul encourages us with this joy, that we may preach to every man and win every man to the same peace we have through grace in Christ.

Paul continues his greeting to the churches in Colosse, including a shout out to the early church in Laodicea, churches he himself didn't establish in person, as the Gospel has been preached throughout the world, faith to faith, to the Gentiles, beyond even Paul's direct ministry. All believers, members of the body of which Jesus is the head, united in spirit, in the joy of peace with God through grace and faith, sharing the goal of bringing increase, the harvest of fruit of righteousness, winning souls to Christ with the Gospel of reconciliation. Bringing forth fruit meet for repentance. Turning those that heard and believe towards God. We see in epistle after epistle, in the Acts of the apostles, in Jesus' own ministry, and His sending of disciples out, two by two into the highways and hedges. We see it in John the Baptist's preaching in the wilderness. It is faith shared and souls won. To God the increase. The so called holy men, vipers chastised by John and Jesus Himself, Peter and Paul, were unable to bring forth this fruit, to lead believers to Christ. Neither can false prophets, and yet they are here in Colosse as they were in Galatia, Ephesus, in the Judean wilderness, as Satan himself, trying to lead the churches astray, causing others to sin, and damning souls with their doctrines of works. It's the same play as Satan in the desert with Christ. We see it today. They beguile us with enticing words, to spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ. Paul is again writing to warn the churches of the Judaizers, who were demanding a return to Hebrew roots by the newly grafted Gentiles, adherence to the Law, the carnal ordinances and the circumcision of the flesh. The acts and works and vain traditions of men, dietary laws, esteeming days over others, all done away with in Christ as they were a foreshadowing of Him. This is told to us, over and over again, because it is Satan's main play against us. Giant red flags that should warn us of false preachers who creep in among us to lead some astray. It is the bulk of the NT outside the Gospel by which we are saved for a reason. Even more so than instruction against sin, Paul and James and Peter and Jude write to warn the churches to avoid these doctrines of men and appeal to the flesh, and remind us we are of a spiritual circumcision.

Romans 7 14 For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin. 15 For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I. 16 If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good. 17 Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me. 18 For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not. 19 For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do. 20 Now if I do that I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me. I would that all who believe on Christ for salvation come to the understanding that, as befitting a quickened spirit, a new man, we put off the lusts of the flesh and put on the things of God. Mortifying our members, being dead to sin. But as Paul explains, this isn't automatic. It isn't even a necessity to salvation, as he is writing we who are saved by faith in Christ. And because it is not automatic, and yet our new man cries out for us to be holy, many men take advantage of this conflict, warning within our members. They come with philosophy and vain deceit; that is the ideas of men that claim to know truth, often that is hidden, that doesn't come from scripture. Or from traditions of men, that things that come from the vain beliefs, and are adopted as religious practices, must be followed. These things aren't of Christ. Christ in whom we not only have died with and been quickened, and redeemed, our sins done away with and the ordinances taken away. Nailed to His cross. Therefore, we should not allow any man to judge us in meat, or in drink, or in respect to an holiday, or new moon, or sabbath, all of which were shadows of Christ, or any other condition that they teach for doctrine that are commandments of men and offered in their place. This means that the vain philosophy of men, as well as the old testament strictures, have no power over we who are saved by faith in Christ. And men who place these things as stumbling blocks and snares are attempting to beguile us. Trapping us into things like voluntary humility, that is sackcloth and ashes. Self-flagellation. Aestheticism, the denial of self for the purpose of self-righteousness (Touch not; taste not; handle not; Which all are to perish with the using). Weird doctrines like the worship of angels (or saints). Things that they haven't seen themselves, but imagine in their fleshly mind. Things other than Christ who is the head of us who are saved. Don't be misled by people who indeed seem holy, who may be able to make an argument of men in the wisdom of how they worship in their humility and neglecting things of the body. Unsaved and even reprobates, can fast for example. They may live without gluttony or abstaining from alcohol. They may be even living "cleaner" than some saved Christians. They may refuse to celebrate certain holidays or feasts, citing earthly reasons and the denial of themselves as a form of righteousness. But these are all lies and not of Christ, in whom is liberty. Chapter 3 goes into details of how a saved Christian should seek to clean up their lives. These things that should be done because we are free in Christ and dead to the flesh. Not because man tells us to. Not to show our own holiness but to put off these deeds as new creatures, not beholden to the things of the flesh. But renewed in the knowledge of Christ, as the elect of God. Using the wisdom of His doctrines to teach and rebuke one another. Giving thanks to God through Christ Jesus. It is the subtle difference between legalism and rejoicing that we are free in grace. And discernment is required. And here's the thing. I don't just pronounce things as doctrine. I lay out in a methodical way the scripture that I'm depending on for doctrine. I go verse by verse chapter by chapter book by book through the Bible; including posting nearly every other relevant reference and passage, so that there can be no misunderstanding what I believe. And while someone doesn't have to agree with all of the conclusions that I've made, They have to admit that they're done from scripture and that they are done in good faith, hiding nothing.

Paul's focus shifts to now-familiar themes. If we be saved, children of light, then seek the things of Heaven. The word of God. The glory of Jesus. The resurrection to come and being raptured, caught up, into the clouds with Him in glory. For this cause, we should mortify our members against sin of the flesh, even as Jesus preached (later in today's Matthew study), "if an eye offend thee, pluck it out." We who are heirs keep our bodies in submission and our thoughts to what's pure, good and holy. Lusts of the flesh, lust, which is the longing for what's not yours, worshiping in the Idolatry of covetousness. As it is written, in James 4: From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members? Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not. Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts. These sins are the reason for God's wrath upon the children of disobedience to the Gospel, but we are children of the light, the shining city in the hill. The light we have inside is a reflection and magnifying of the love God shines on us, so don't hide it, but hold it high for all to see that they might be partakers with us. Putting off anger, wrath, Malice, blasphemy, filthy conversation, the behavior of the unsaved that acts as a bushel to hide our light and turn some away from the truth within us. We put on the new man, have honest dealings with one another ("Let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay" - also Matt 5), doing everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, in thanks to God the Father by Christ's name. And if we are in the new man, and we have put away the lusts of the flesh, if we mortify our members, having honest dealings with one another, edifying with songs of praise and teaching the doctrines of God in psalms, our light shining as a guide to the truth for others to follow, then what does this look like? Wives submitting to their husbands, husbands loving their wives, children honoring their parents, fathers judging their children righteously, not in wrath, not frustrating them, but as God the Father has loved you. And, at work? Heartily and without malice or anger, do what you're asked, because we work for God, already rewarded with the kingdom of which we are heirs. Diligently and honestly setting out to complete what is required of you, with joy and a meek spirit and the confidence of your salvation. Those who do wrong will have their reward, just as you will for your faithful service. God is not a respecter of persons, and master or boss or elected leader, all alike will face His wrath for their transgressions. That's not on us to determine. It is on us to account for ourselves in all that we do, because we do it in Jesus' name. Many bristle at this. Be the best husband, wife, child, employee, neighbor, regardless of whatever else. Being blameless. Not dimming the reflection of the light that you walk in. If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. So many struggle with this concept. Some false prophets and natural men claim that this submission to authority and the powers that be, given by God, as some sort of perversion by Paul, but we see it again in Matthew 5, preached by Jesus in the beatitudes. A study on that will be posted hopefully this afternoon. Working 12hr days lately

The final chapter of Colossians, the first verse of which is really the last of the though carried in Chapter 3. Everyone is subject to the Lord, and has a master in heaven. The powers that be are to be honored and feared, and not to be abused should you be husband, master, minister, bishop. Being not a respecter of persons, as God is not. Loving our enemies, rejoicing in the Spirit. And so, continue in prayer, thanksgiving, praying God brings opportunities to share His Gospel with others. The mystery of Christ which the preaching of had Paul in chains. He asks for prayers that he be able to deliver the same to those who held him captive and this magnify the Lord. He encourages us to walk in wisdom towards those who lack it, making the best use of our limited time. Speaking with grace seasoned with salt. This is a skill that comes from being in the word and reflecting on the grace God has shown us. It is speaking the truth in love and understanding. Being longsuffering, but not afraid to say what God's word says. To speak what He's spoken unto us. Not in malice or spite, but with understanding of the human condition of the unregenerate sinners we interact with, that some might be saved. It can be hard sometimes, at least for me, but the reward that comes from it is most excellent. Paul concludes this epistle, (hand written himself whereas some were transcribed) with shout-outs to many fellow ministers who did great things for God. Luke, that author of the Gospel and Acts is mentioned. Barnabas' nephew. Paul is always ready to give credit to the many who labored in the Gospel with him, as we should be generous to praise the good work of others, and name them. God being just and true gave them the honor of being known throughout the ages. Paul asks that this epistle be also delivered unto the church at Laodicea, and an epistle delivered there to be read in Colosse. Would love to read this "lost letter." Although, some believe that the letter to Philemon is this epistle, some scholars debate whether it was simply another that was redundant to known epistles, going over similar themes and using similar language. History shows multiple forgeries we're attempted in the early days of the 2nd century. Like any book mentioned in the Bible but not reproduced, Satan leaps at the chance to introduce blasphemy with the implied authority of being mentioned in scripture. Of course Laodicea is one of the churches Jesus addresses in Revelation 3, the lukewarm church that lost it's fire for the gospel in the comfort of the material wealth they had, who Christ calls to repent unto zeal or see the church lost.

From the risen Christ in Matthew 28, giving the Great Commission to His Apostles; All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world. Amen. Here, in 1 Thessalonians 1, we see the fruit of this command to give the Gospel to every creature play out. Paul, Silvanus and Timothy, writing to the church in Thessalonica, hailing them "in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ," write about their work for the Lord in spreading the same Gospel that they received from Paul and the other evangelists, throughout Asia Minor. For our gospel came not unto you in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Ghost, and in much assurance; as ye know what manner of men we were among you for your sake. Ye became followers of us, and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Ghost. So that ye were ensamples to all that believe in Macedonia and Achaia. For from you sounded out the word of the Lord not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith to God-ward is spread abroad; so that we need not to speak any thing. It is amazing that within a few years of Christ's resurrection and ascension, churches had sprung up throughout the world, dedicated to the same Gospel as He preached, and the prophets gave witness too. A light shining out into the world leading all men to repent towards the living and true God; And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come. To understand the power of the word as it is given, and that power a testimony of its truth, is to understand how it would be possible to convince so many disparate peoples to come to the saving faith in Christ, not from firsthand account or witness, but by the Holy Ghost moving in those spreading the good news in every place your faith to God-ward is spread abroad; so that we need not to speak any thing. Living faith to faith. Building the body of Christ. Amen

Continuing to exhort the church at Thessalonica, Paul reminds them of their conversion, repenting towards the Gospel, and of how Paul and his helpers behaved among them, just as they preached the truth of Christ Jesus in Philippi, a city a few hours west, in northern Greece. It was there in Acts 16, where Paul and Silas are accused of causing "exceeding trouble" by those who protested the gospel being preached, and brought them before magistrates, had them scourged, and finally jailed Paul and Silas. All of which came to serve the glory of God even the more, getting their jailer and his family saved, and planting a church. And we are told here, that it is this time in Philippi that the members of the church of Thessalonica would recognize how shamefully treated they were for their mission, and understand that they came to them boldly with the word of God, through much tribulation, without guile or flattery, but with the stripes of suffering and still proclaiming the truth. That they were willing to give them not just the Gospel, but give up their own lives to proclaim it, because it is truth, and out of the love they feel towards them that received it. Paul then reminds them of how, like his own children, he gave them not just the good news of Christ that brought to them salvation and the Spirit, but further exhortation to live blamelessly, as is befitting a saved Christian. To walk worthy of the call they answered, worthy of the God that saved them. A reminder that it is not just saving souls that we should do, but then building upon that salvation, encouraging and edifying babes in Christ, as we would our own children, to walk a Christian walk. Preaching against sin and towards the path of righteousness. Even in tribulation and contentions by man, but pleasing to God. Paul compares them and their tribulation and persecution they are suffering to the churches in Judea, and their persecution by the Jews. Following after the churches in Christ, to be likewise afflicted, persecuted by the Macedonians, their fellow countrymen. Wrapping up the chapter, Paul laments having spent little time with them, wishing it could have been more and, regretting that Satan had hindered his plans to return to them, assures that they will be together at Christ's return, and as souls won, be Paul and Silas' glory and joy. A crown of rejoicing, given as reward. Every soul we help bring towards Christ and reconciliation with God through the blood of the lamb, whether it be a seed sown, watered or harvested, is our glory and joy in Christ's coming. Our reward at His judgment of our works. A crown given us, a precious stone, after the wood, hay and stubble are burned away. 1 Corinthians 3:9-15 For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry, ye are God's building. According to the grace of God which is given unto me, as a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.

Continuing the topic at hand from Chapter 2 regarding the persecution and tribulations the church at had been reportedly going through, Paul says He, Timothy and Silas were concerned for them and their faith, that they in their troubles have been believing in vain, and turned from practicing the faith. Unable to wait any longer, they dispatched Timothy, and he returned with good news that they were just as strong and stedfast, unmoving, as ever. Establish and comfort means to to strengthen, to edify and be a bulwark. In modern terms, comfort is seen as weakening. Coddling, but it's meaning in the Bible is to strengthen in tribulation. This is why the Holy Spirit is called the comforter by Jesus. The evangelists sought to be a comforting encouragement to the saints in Thessalonica, but their stedfast unmoving faith, he says, actually brought comfort to him. He expounds on the idea that all Christians will see tribulations, and persecution for His name's sake. He reminds them of that, and is warning us against being discouraged. Believers can be like the seed from Jesus' parable of the sower, that; ...fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away. Jesus explained; ...he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it; Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended. These are saved Christians, but who aren't firmly established. Who aren't stedfast. Who, having shallow roots and not grown deep enough in faith, are moved by troubles. Wilting and producing no fruit when the heat is turned up. This is why it is important for us to stay in the word, in prayer, and exercising our faith to the benefit of others, that our roots are strong and we be immovable, stedfast and not offended by the inevitable persecution and troubles that come our way. But Paul's fears of this are assuaged by Timothy's report, the Thessalonians were engaged and their faith alive, despite the persecution by their countrymen for that faith. Paul sends prayers of blessings and restates his fervent desire to come and visit them, and reiterates that they take hope in the returning of Jesus Christ and the gathering of believers unto Him. This is a point made at the end of chapter 1 and again in 2, now fleshed out even more so in chapter 3; And the Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another, and toward all men, even as we do toward you: To the end he may stablish your hearts unblameable in holiness before God, even our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints. This hope, the thing that we are convinced of by the evidence of faith, should remain a comfort. That the Christ who saved us is returning, and in that day, our resurrection. The gathering of the elect, of all saints. In the worst of tribulation, even unto death, this blessed assurance of eternal life in Jesus name establishes us firmly, so that we may not be moved. A rock unmoving. It is the second coming and the rapture of the saints, the resurrection, the promise of being heirs to the Kingdom of Heaven, that Satan attacks with lies, so as to undermine that hope in those who he was unable to keep from salvation. To make those who believed unfruitful. Easily offended in persecution. To render them hopeless, and thus unable to do God's will and save more souls. To make their faith dead, being alone, as they withdraw like the Pharisees who believed on Jesus, but kept quiet for fear of the Jews. To this end, Satan pushes lies such as the resurrection is past, that it is metaphorical, that the millennium reign is allegory, or already taking place. That the rapture isn't real, the lie that the gathering doesn't appear in scripture, or that it will occur before facing tribulation, so as to make believers be caught unawares. He attacks the idea of Heaven being our inheritance, of Hell being eternal or real. Preterism, amillennialism, post millennialism, pre-trib rapture, dispensationalism, "church ages," and other heresy, all designed to undermine our hope and leave us with no root in ourselves, on shifting sand. Not established, and so withering when the sun gets to hot. Too many Christians believe the lie that God's word isn't preserved, that it's too difficult to understand, that they need others to explain every jot and tittle, never spending time in the word themselves. Never growing roots. These shallow Christians are often carnal, worldly, carried away by the cares of this world. Afraid, angry, unable to show mercy, unable to be fruitful. Having no charity. Substituting the pure religion of being undefiled before God; visiting the fatherless and widows in their affliction, being unspotted from the world, soul winning...they instead cling to meaningless trappings of denomination, the church they attend, the rites and rituals they keep, making big shows of prayer, superficial expressions designed to justify them before man. And so absent the roots, and not having faith in every Word of God being pure, they are unprepared for tribulations and divisions, and are left hopeless. Withered. Don't fall into that trap! Don't let Satan snare you. Study to be approved unto God. Prove all things. Comparing scripture with scripture. Grow roots and be established that you may be unmoving in tribulation. The snare often used by satan, of creating the feeling of anger, wrath, outrage, and fear of what will come is baited with outrageous stories of Injustice and wicked evils visited upon the innocent, or threats of it. That will lure people into the snare someone or some policies will save you. Trusting in man. And like an animal caught in a trap, you can see the flailing and desperate lashing out, the anger and rage. Reactionary spirals. Don't get caught in this trap. If you see the warning signs within you. If you feel yourself giving your heart over to wickedness and wrath, irrational fear... Understand you're in a net left by Satan. And the only way to Free yourself is to take the peace and comfort of God's word to heart

James 5:7 Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain. Lamentations 3:25 The LORD is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. Psalms 27:14 Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD. Habakkuk 2:3 For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry. Isaiah 40:31 But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint. Again and again in scripture, these examples are just a few of the encouraging verses teaching patience and promise. Those that say to "be not afraid." That we should work diligently as good servants, for the benefit of others. To be steadfast knowing we have overcome, so that when tribulation comes we know that God will deliver us in the end. That all who live Godly will suffer in this life, and it's ok. Don't fear tribulation. But we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience.

Amen. What more needs to be said about this? Knowing we have eternal life, and knowing Christ will return, and we shall be gathered to meet Him, sleeping, dead in the flesh, or alive at His coming, we then should strive to sanctification, being holy as He is holy. As the Spirit within us is holy. Do not fornicate. Do not indulge the lusts of the flesh. Do not deceive brothers in Christ. Be diligent in our work. Meek in our manner that we may be blameless before those we may give the Gospel to. The sins a reprobate mind may invent runs to those sins not common to man, unnatural lusts. Reprobate isn't a synonym with depravity or degeneracy. It is the cause of such behavior. This is why you may have a 40yo murderer, a serial fornicator, an adulterous person, a drunkard or whatever, who, overcome with guilt and coming to the realization of what awaits them, accepts the Gospel sincerely, and you may have a 14yo who has hardly left the house, let alone committed grave sin, who willfully blasphemes the Holy Spirit and rejects God utterly, and is given over to reprobation. It's not about the sin but your relationship with God. Most people fall in neither the camp of the saints or the reprobate, they are just unregenerate sinners, with all too common lusts of the flesh. There is hope for them until they die, least they become reprobate.

Today we begin the series called "the Pastoral Epistles," Paul's letters to Timothy and Titus, respectively, giving them doctrine on planting churches and the only two biblical church offices; Bishop and Deacon. Bishop being the pastor, or head of a local independent NT church, and deacon being an assistive role, aiding the pastor in the administration of the church. Here Paul writes to Timothy, his "son" in Christ, whom the last Apostle had won to the Lord, and who he is asking to remain in Ephesus, planting churches. The doctrines he teaches are instrumental in how God wishes to see our local churches established and run. In their roles as evangelist, Timothy and Titus are instrumental in passing on this instruction to those called to the offices. Most denominations ignore this teaching, entirely. The very notion of denomination, central control, unqualified priests, unbiblical hierarchies and the like, spreading bad doctrine by decree. Even OIFB churches, who as Baptists recognize the two offices doctrine, have abandoned the traditional training of future pastors, evangelists and church planting and embraced the unbiblical Bible College racket, siphoning off potential men of God and other young people, to feed them into a collegiate system that does more to promote and spread heresy than anything else. God's plan for churches is to train up future leaders, be pastor-led, and to go out soul winning, evangelizing a receptive community, and eventually planting a church and sending off a pastor, who then repeats the process. Some pastors grew so far and fast, they took pride in establishment of their Christian schools and Bible colleges, and for many, it was their eventual downfall in their service to the Lord. So, as we wade into the doctrines laid out here, we see that Timothy is charged with instructing those he finds called to the office of bishop, or pastor as we call it in modern times (terms that come from overseeing a flock of sheep), that they give no heed to fables and genealogies that lead to foolish questions, and don't edify the congregation. This is similarly given to Titus, avoiding Jewish fables and endless genealogies to instruct the future leaders of these churches. At the time of this writing, many of the apocryphal books had been in circulation, non-inspired and many heretical concepts, being used by Jews and similarly creeping in to the new Christian churches. The ramifications of rejecting the teachings of the pastoral epistles can still be felt today, with apostate false church of Rome, which uses unqualified men in unbiblical positions and uses the apocrypha, Jewish fables, to create doctrines. Not just the fables of the already existing books during Paul's day, such as using Maccabees to create the lie of purgatory, but false gospels of Thomas and Andrew, for example, which they've adopted their Mary-worship from. Of course we have the genealogies attempting to paint "seeds of Abraham" as special, continued in dispensationalist heresy today. Paul continues to say that, in instruction of these leaders to also stress the importance of charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned. The gracious love for others that comes from having a good conscience before God, being blameless and regenerate in the faith of Christ. Unfeigned, sincere. While all saved have reconciliation with God regarding their sin, it is a spiritual maturity that brings one to this gracious and merciful charitable love for others. There are some, Paul informs us, that having neglected this trait, and professing themselves wise, have become fools. Vain jangling. Just pontificating on the matters of the law, and works, and neglecting the faith, and forgiveness and grace. Many such cases, even today. Paul does caution that the law of God is good, in itself, for its purpose, which he lays out here. His admonition is against the legalistic works-based false teachers, not the law itself, which we who are saved have liberty from, but that the law continues to serve as a schoolmaster, and is for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine. To bring them to the knowledge of the Gospel, or at the very least, to punish wrongdoing on earth and to keep an orderly society, understanding that the majority of people are not saved. To many people, both believers and naturally, unbelievers, see no benefit or roles in God's law being used today. "That was for those times. Not for today." But, as we see from this list of sins, there is a clear need to maintain God's law regardless of what current year is. Whoremongers and whores, who defile themselves with mankind, murderers, liars and every other thing that is contrary to good teaching from scripture. It's a broad list, and we understand why there remains a need to enforce these things. There is an element of libertarian Christian that doesn't just reject the Levitical laws and carnal ordinances, done away with in Christ, but see no need to enforce the laws of God, written in our hearts and proclaimed from Adam on by God. They take their liberty for license to sin, and will not support the role of government and the law to protect people from evil and bring people to the understanding that there is sin and punishment, which is key to coming to repentance and accepting salvation. But, those sincere in the faith and who understand the charity, the gracious love given by God to them, as sinners and able to show that love to others, are able and fit for the ministry. Paul uses himself as an example of this, that being a chief of sinners, who did evil against believers, was so changed by God and the gospel of reconciliation in Jesus, that has made him effective in the ministry he was appointed to, and the glory of God it has allowed him. He encourages Timothy with this, and warns against those who, having been put away from the faith, who are reprobate, two of whom Paul names, infamous for their attempts to shipwreck, to lead to ruin, the faith of others. Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.

Paul, having laid out his instruction to Timothy, and his role in establishment of churches of the Ephesians, and giving some basic commands in that regard, and a warning against reprobate false prophets, moves therefore to spell out a broader doctrine that applies to all Christians. It is how to develop the men to have the temperament that will produce those fit for the office and called to that ministry, and how to edify the church, bringing in more believers. The first point, praying for all men, supplications, or asking of God for favor, thanksgiving for the blessings He bestows, intercessions that the Spirit may work to bring about outcomes that give glory to God. This is our instruction for the rulers of this world as much as the beggars, that we may live peaceably. Not given to fear or wrath. This causes many to bristle, but as much as possible we are to live peaceably and without offense, with all men, so we may in all godliness and honesty, bring others to the truth. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; We are to be a testimony to the truth of this. That our prayers and faith be lived out in a way that brings others to this truth. Doubt and wrath show a lack of faith and offends others from the truth. Simple as. The spiralling people do when it comes to the cares of this world, or their fearful outbursts show a lack of faith in the same God who they are supposed to be magnifying and giving glory to, as witness to others. Note that Jesus is our sole mediator for intercession with God. Not spirits of men. Not idols or priests. When we pray for others it is asking Jesus to intercede, God in His name to bless, the holy Spirit to give comfort. Also, the Bible says the will of God our savior that ALL MEN come to believe. It isn't a select few as Calvinism would claim, and it is our calling to help make God's will manifest. So men should be holy, in prayer, without fear, peaceable, without doubt and wrath. Praying for all men to come to the truth, even for the government that God may grant us peace, allowing more to be saved. In a similar manner, women have a role as well. Just as men who are unruly and fearful offer a bad testimony so to do women who dress immodestly, who are ostentatious in their appearance. Not only because of the obvious temptations, but as speaking to their character as Godly women. The two admonitions, one for men and one for women, have the same root context. That we show outward signs of the faith that is saved us to better bring others to salvation. It's often the men who are most fearful and wrathful, who have the loudest voice in pointing out to women not to dress shamefully. In this regard they are hypocrites. Women should do that which is pleasing to God, but so should men, we have an equal role in winning souls to Christ. Wear those rolls differ, the Bible says women aren't to teach, because, like eve, they are prone to being deceived regarding God's word. This is just the truth of it, and it is a sentiment found throughout the Epistles, and borne out by experience. This is not to excuse Adam and condemn eve, but rather just clarifying rules and natural tendencies to better demonstrate God's will. Paul goes on to say that it is in bearing children, and raising them up in a Godly way, that women have the greater influence than men leading the church. That they are saved, preserved and protected, by the generations of children that they bring into the world and give witness to God to, that they may be His. Too many cherry pick these verses and create an artificial men versus women divide. It is about roles and responsibilities, understanding there are differences between men and women. And we have different deficiencies and negative tendencies that can trip us up in our walk with God. But we should take comfort that when we follow God's will, we have the opportunity to bring Him glory just the same. This is a rushed breakdown of the chapter, but I hope those with ears to hear understand my meaning. This is one of those difficult concepts God teaches us, that is full of nuance, and is far more balanced then people would believe. Especially the tendency of men who are derelict in their role, yet insistent women be dedicated in theirs. Also a lot of men are weak in the spirit and fearful in the flesh, and struggle with the idea that they too answer to a hierarchy, that exists for God's will. And in their impatience with God's longsuffering, and their fear which comes from lack of faith, their doubt which causes them to come to wrath rather than leaving it up to God, they are as a woman who is dressed like a harlot as far as their testimony is concerned. And while a woman should not be allowed to teach in a church, neither should a fearful and wrathful man. Isaiah 45 ²¹Tell ye, and bring them near; yea, let them take counsel together: who hath declared this from ancient time? who hath told it from that time? have not I the Lord? and there is no God else beside me; a just God and a Saviour; there is none beside me. ²²Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else. ²³I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.

Now, having laid a baseline for general behavior that should be encouraged in the newly planted churches, to better bring about the type of men to be trusted with keeping watch over the flock, Paul moves on to describe the basic qualities required for the two offices the Bible provides us; Bishop and Deacon. Note these aren't priests, or a honorific for high priests, the way the false denominations use the term "bishop," as we know all saints are part of the royal priesthood of believers. Rather, this is specifically about pastors, leading the flock and deacons who help him minister. If you recall, deacon was the position created by the Apostles at the churches in Jerusalem back in Acts 6: Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them, and said, It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables. Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business. But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word. And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch: whom they set before the apostles: and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them. And the word of God increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; We see in this that the churches are to be led by those ministering the Gospel, and the day to day management left to the deacons who work for them. Many modern churches are deacon-led, and this has caused innumerable problems, politicizing a church. They should be Christ-led, pastor in charge, deacons serving the pastor, as the Bible lays out. And here we come to the qualifications for each office, and see they are basically the same. Married, to one wife. With orderly children and household. In all gravity, meaning he takes this first role as husband and father seriously. Many churches have failed because their pastor, who may be a godly man, with a good wife and seemingly orderly house, allowed sin and disorder into their homes, which in turn affected the church, bringing many to ruin. Not this isn't saying he, his wife or kids must be perfect, but that the pastors and deacons be in control at home. This could mean a child act up, and being sufficiently punished, or even put out. Rather than their sins covered up and allowed due to the pastor or deacon's position. Many such cases. Sober men. Not given to wine, but full of hospitality for others. Not greedy. Not a striker, not a brawler. Not greedy for filthy lucre, money earned by dishonest means, and selling of favor from his position. Not covetous. Not a novice, who may be filled with pride at his newfound position of power. These are men who are established in the faith. We have already seen in the previous chapter that these offices cannot be for women, who aren't to be suffered to teach in the church. Female pastors are not biblical, and with reason. But of the men, they should be Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience...And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached unto the Gentiles, believed on in the world, received up into glory. We see what that mystery of faith is, the Gospel. Some have taken the first verse out of context to bring in gnostic heresy regarding some sort of oral tradition known only to those chosen to lead, but Paul gives the answer to the mystery. Their faith in Jesus as the redeemer, giving them a good conscience. They must also have wives who are grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things, because in truth and practice, though the wife isn't holding the office, they find themselves with duties and responsibilities within the church. These ideas regarding the two biblical offices of the local independent NT churches are further developed in the remaining pastoral epistles, but sufficient groundwork has been laid here to see what churches aren't using the scriptural standard, and so, reject them. In the next chapter, we will see further, Paul writing in the Spirit tells Timothy some warning signs of false teachers to watch out for. And God said, Let there be light: and there was light... This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all... Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life... That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world... And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God... Then Jesus said unto them, Yet a little while is the light with you. Walk while ye have the light, lest darkness come upon you: for he that walketh in darkness knoweth not whither he goeth. While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them... But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin... But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light... For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ... The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy rereward. And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light: and they shall reign for ever and ever.

Paul, expressly speaking in the Spirit, warns that in the latter times, the period post-ascension and before the day of the Lord's return, that some will depart from the faith, to teach doctrines of devils. The Holy Spirit describes these false prophets as having their conscience seared, because they are reprobates, and so they speak lies and hypocrisy. Again, this isn't Paul's spiritual discernment leading to his writing a prophetic dark saying, he says this is directly spoken by the Spirit, by God. And these are the examples of what those devilish doctrines of lies will teach; Forbidding to marry and abstaining from meats, insinuating that they will deceive those giving heed to seducing spirits, with the appearance of holiness. It shouldn't have to be said that this is directed at the same heresies the RCC would eventually take up. Their doctrines of devils. This is one of many admonitions against specific practices that the Catholic Church and many of its harlot daughters teach. Warnings against Idolatry, building ornate temples, vain repetitive prayers, having other mediators with God the Father than the man Christ Jesus, calling men "Father," taking heed to Jewish fables, adding works and "sacraments" to the Gospel, disregarding God's word as the only source for doctrine, persecution of believers, and here, forbidding to marry and abstaining from meats. As if that were not enough, there is Scripture recording Jesus saying to those seeking to worship Mary, "Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it." and "Who is my mother, or my brethren?...Behold my mother and my brethren! For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother." The word of God, spoken before the foundation of the world, and published in these latter times, expressly addresses the false teachers and their doctrines of what Jesus' revelation to John calls "the whore of Babylon." More than 200 years before the Roman empire created the Catholic Church. And still today some take heed of its seducing spirits and are led astray. Now to edify Timothy in his role as evangelist to the Ephesians, Paul gives yet more advice as to the doctrines he should be certain to instruct the churches. That every creature is good to eat, For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer, just as God told Adam and again to Noah. The dietary laws and carnal ordinances given to Moses for a season, done away with in Christ. This understanding will help the men of the church "be a good minister of Jesus Christ," not because of the food they eat, but rather the understanding of prayer and God's blessing. That, as Jesus said, the flesh profits nothing, rather they will be nourished up in the words of faith and of good doctrine. And so, avoid old wives tales, similarly, Jewish fables, and be about exercising godliness, their spirit, not the flesh. For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come. We the saved, having, present tense, the promise of the life that now is and the eternal life that awaits, must exercise and grow, spiritually. Godliness is our gainz, for our eternal life will be built upon that, not our PRs at the gym. This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation. And therefore, because of this doctrine of faith, living Godly, in the spiritual rather than the flesh, the faithful sayings Paul writes unto Timothy, he warns they will both labor to teach others, and be rebuked by those of this world, because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe. (Note to calvinists, God is the savior of all men, specially those who believe. Christ died for everyone, especially to those who believe and are saved) The chapter wraps up with more encouragement for Timothy from Paul, to give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine. To not let his youth be a hindrance to his ordained role, but to meditate and study these doctrines and live an example that, being blameless, will inspire others to see past his being young, because he is strong in the faith. Reminding him he has the Holy Ghost upon him, and to rely on that to bring the newly formed churches around.

Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world. ... Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow. ... He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment. There are two groups of people God has a special place for, and asks us to be protectors and caretakers of; widows and orphans. This biblical appeal actually became a means by which many fraternal orders, Masonic lodges and other less than godly organizations worked a grift. Collecting donations for the "widows and orphans fund" became a euphemism for this kind of shakedown charity by the 20th Century. The idea itself synonymous with corruption. A punchline euphemism for illegal activities hidden under the guise of charity. But in more recent decades, the concept, both Biblical and corrupt has all but disappeared, as the state welfare and entitlements has supplanted it. Now hardly any one, and sadly, few churches, give heed to the "pure religion" God commands us towards. Here, in chapter 5 of first Timothy, Paul instructs the young evangelist on the proper church role and management for care of widows indeed. Before getting to that, and continuing the thought of chapter 4 regarding Timothy's youth, and how to minimize those who look down on being told what to do by a younger man, Paul gives instruction. Don't rebuke an elder. Treat them as fathers, younger men as brothers, young girls as sisters (with a purity), and elderly women as mothers. This applies to us all, and our fellow congregants. We are family for Christ's sake, and as such have obligation for respect, and at times, honor. Honor in the Bible has a financial aspect to it, that we give honor, payment, support, to our parents, is one of the main meanings behind the commandment. Giving honor to whom it is due is a point repeatedly made by God throughout the Bible, and this is the context of Paul's instructions here. A widow indeed is one who, having lost her husband and not having sons or nephews (which means not only her siblings' children but grandchildren, and other younger relations), that these family members must honor her with support, that she not be a burden to the church. He warns; But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. This is similar language to those facing church discipline laid out by Jesus, that they be put out from the congregation and treated as if they are unsaved. Heathens. Infidels.
