As a side note, that may help with understanding these passages; just as "saved" in scripture isn't always referring to justification by faith, but often physical salvation from danger, "faith" isn't always referring to the saving faith that we need to be redeemed. Often, especially in the epistles (which are written to believers), "faith" can refer to the deeper trust in God, or being faithful to His commands and expectations, or our own responsibility to others. And in the same manner, "condemnation," "damnation," "justified," or even "infidel" may be being applied in the present sense, regarding how one is looked at by others, not their spiritual condition in regards to eternal life. These are important distinctions, and understanding the context of the terms when they are used will save you when some try to cherry pick verses to come to a different meaning regarding salvation. Continuing, Paul lists more qualifiers for a widow "indeed," that she be desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day. Poor, no means of support and giving her life to the faith, essentially. Further, he goes on to say she must be over 60, blameless and devoted to ministry of the church, and the wife of one man; ..having been the wife of one man. Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints' feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work. This makes her a true widow. A widow indeed. Paul contrasts this with the exceptions. One who lives for pleasure rather than service is excluded, for example. And age is a factor; The younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry; Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith. And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not. Young women, who could still remarry, shouldn't be given the honor by the church. Even if they swear they will be devoted to the ministry, and continuing in prayer, etc, Paul says they eventually will become wonton, that is, spoiled and pampered, having financial support with little to do all day but gossip and carry on, it will corrupt them, and eventually they will seek out a man to remarry, and make them abandon their first faith, that is that God will provide for them through the church that they are swearing devotion to, and leave for a husband. Damnation in this context means condemned by others for her behavior, not losing her salvation or going to Hell. This is all true, we witness it ourselves today, especially with welfare taking the place of charity or family support. And frequently you may see at church a godly woman, coming from divorce or a husband's death, will put herself all in to helping out to keep herself busy, and eventually get married, often to an unsaved man, or worse, a man of the church she led to adultery and divorce, and her testimony becomes an open shame. Many such cases. We see though out 1 Timothy, and other epistles but especially here, that the testimony to the unsaved by living blamelessly so that they may reach the lost with soul winning, is a top priority. That they give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully. Shifting gears, Paul gets back to how to handle elders of the church; Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine. For the scripture saith, thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward. Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses. Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear. So elders that serve the congregation faithfully should receive double honor, double payment for their efforts. Rewarded financially for their time. And accusations against them should be handled with respect, the same manner of which Jesus laid out, requiring witnesses and reproached privately, but publicly shamed and cast out if they don't repent. Far too many churches only do the first half, and then often will defer to the elder and their profession of innocence. It is sadly rare that they be openly shamed and cast out for their indiscretions and sin. Especially sexual immorality. The topic can be embarrassing for all involved, and the older man's excuses taken with more veracity than the younger girls (or boys) accusations. There is often fear of the entire congregation being smeared, and excuses and rationalizations made. This is the downfall to many churches, especially those that have drifted from biblical fundamentalism, and grown lukewarm. By not being respecters of persons in these matters, and worrying less about our own appearances, and more about doing what's right, an active lively church can avoid these pitfalls. If your church has an elder or any member, for that matter, who engages in sinful activities, especially fornication, adultery, and taking advantage of their position against young ones, they need to be put out, and put out publicly, and police involved if necessary. There is no excuse. Jesus will remove the candlestick of a church that does this. The hedge of protection will be gone. Paul charges these things to Timothy before God. This is a command as to how he should behave and what he must teach to the churches he is planting. It's a sacred duty. We have the same duty to our own churches, to maintain these standards and practices. To exercise pure religion, undefiled. He orders Timothy to not lay hands suddenly on no man. This may be an admonition against brawling, but more likely in this context, he means ordination with the Holy Ghost. Not to partake in another man's sin, which is great advice to us all. He says before you judge remember that while some good works or wrong doings may seem obvious, others come out later so basically don't make snap judgments. The kindly medical advice, to drink wine, (obviously meaning juice here as booze isn't good for the stomach), seems a non sequitur in the midst of being instructed not to show favoritism and be patient and reserved in judgment, but it seems apropos given the stress of the position and the weight of what's been charged to the young church planter.

The final chapter in 1st Timothy, and it is building on the theme of being able to give a good testimony for Christ to others by living like you have the gift of eternal life, not stuck in the cares of this world but growing in spirit. The admonition to obey earthly authority, to please God and make His glory seen of man that you may give a good witness is repeated throughout the New Testament, from Jesus rendering unto Caesar, to Romans 13 and 1 Peter 2, and elsewhere. This is one of the hardest doctrines for most American Christians today, spoiled by the supposed promises of "Liberty" from the Constitution, and missing the liberty we have in Christ. We bristle with pride at the idea of being good servants at work, living agreeably with all men as much as possible, paying taxes, tribute to whom tribute is due, custom to whom custom. Honor to parents and elders. This doctrine is seen as being a "Christ cuck." Seen as weak by those lacking understanding. Missing that while we defer to authority, we have roles of authority in God's hierarchy ourselves, and that we are instructed to always place God and His word as our final authority. Often those who cry loudest about supposed persecution and calls for riot and seditions, have abandoned their own roles, or are derelict in their own responsibilities. They care more for their comfort than for their testimony. They live in fear rather than faith. They see wrath as theirs, not God's. They, not being satisfied with what God has given them, and impatient with His longsuffering, are unable to bring others to believe and so, shoot themselves in the foot and worsen their own condition. We have one means to lead a nation back from wickedness, and that is the Gospel. Soul winning. Revival. And that requires our being good witnesses to the power of the Spirit and faith that God, who is holy and just, and will keep His promise and restore us. Paul is writing to Timothy who, living in Macedonia, a slave/caste society, will have gotten both masters and slaves saved, and in the same congregation. We are blessed not to be living in a society that openly enslaves people. But the same admonition applies to us as wage-slaves. Be the best employee at your job. Even if your boss is terrible. Your employer, even if he despises religion and doesn't know Christ should still be forced by your witness to see Christians as good employees. The best, because we work for God not them. Those of us under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed. We represent Christ to the world. We are to be a light that draws men near. And again, this isn't to say if a manager calls on you to do something that is contrary to God's word that you have to submit. We defer to the higher authority and there is none higher than God. But we do it peaceably, and with humility and meekness, trusting in God to save us should it lead to persecution. We don't obey to avoid being persecuted, but to please God, and with the full expectation that we might face tribulation when we defer to God's will over earthly authority. Paul uses Jesus' own example before Pilate, which by His meek silence led to Pilate confessing He was blameless, and leading to the Glory of God in the crucifixion. But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content. Opposition to this doctrine often amounts to the same general notion as a black shooting another black for "dissing" them by stepping on they Jordans. It's the same foolish pride, wrathful anger, and covetous materialism. Not a witness of someone who has the power of the Holy Spirit indwelling them. And if a false teacher says otherwise? If they teach rebellion, wrath and riot? He is proud, knowing nothing, but doting about questions and strifes of words, whereof cometh envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings, Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, and destitute of the truth, supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself. Christianity is not a sovereign citizen movement. The liberty we have in Christ is true liberty, from sin and Hell and death. Made heirs to the Kingdom. We have eternal life in Him and the life we have on this world is short. The rewards we seek for eternity have a short time to be earned. The more we waste on petty, temporal things, the more we shortchange God and ourselves. Paul continues, spinning off the warning about staying away from those who see earthly gain as proof of godliness, seeking after riches, we are given the adage "the love of money is the root of all evil." Storing up treasure on earth leads to temptations and snares, traps of our own making. Seeking after wealth while neglecting our stores in Heaven. O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness. Be satisfied with what God blessed you with, even if it is subsistence, knowing that if you win souls, your riches in Heaven will be greater. Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses. This is our calling, as those who have laid hold on eternal life; to live as though we believe it. That our hope isn't in vain, but on the promises of God, faithful and true. The promise that as we live blamelessly, unrebukable, that when Christ returns for the Day of the Lord, everyone will get as they gave, and justice will be served. God's wrath upon those who have troubled us. Vengeance being His. Which in his times he shall shew, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords; Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen. Finishing up, Paul advises that Timothy lay charge to those who are converted to the faith and already rich in wealth to be ready to hand it out to those in need. To do good works with that they've been blessed. To despise their riches here and store up rewards for Heaven. As Jesus told His disciples, it is harder for a rich man to enter the Kingdom than for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle. And because to whom much is given, much more is expected, they should be encouraged to do as much as possible for the brethren, edifying the church and giving glory to God. Finally, Paul warns young Timothy, his son in Christ, a ward of the Gospel, to Keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. We are entrusted with the Gospel of reconciliation. The doctrines of how to live, discipleship, prudence, fidelity to God's law and hope in His promise. To preach and to teach this to every creature. Saving who we can, by mercy or by warning of the fire. We should give good witness to this faith that we have been entrusted, the surety of which is our now quickened spirit, and the indwelling of the Holy Spirit inside us. A ready and meek answer for our hope to all who we give witness. We are to avoid the vain, that is unprofitable babblings of those seeking to debate us, to engender strife and disputations of the faith. Not to give answer to fools. Not to get into arguments with gnostics, and their science, falsely so-called. This includes debating atheists on creation, for example. We are warned repeatedly against answering a fool in their folly. Proverbs 9 7 He that reproveth a scorner getteth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh a wicked man getteth himself a blot. 8 Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee: rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee. 9 Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning. It is a bad witness to get caught up in disputations with a heretic. (Of this, I am chief) Titus 3:10-11 A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself. (This is primarily the reason for my pinned rules for the channel. To keep myself from sinning, being drawn into debates with fools. It's also why Twitter is such a snare.) The meat of the word, giving us instruction on how we should carry ourselves as saved Christians, to be a good witness, to live faith to faith, growing in the spirit, studying to be approved unto God, understanding the liberty we have in Christ, what the implications are for those of us possessing eternal life, what to expect at Jesus' coming, God's plan and promise, His justice and wrath...all this is impossible to understand without first understanding salvation in Christ. Without which you cannot receive even the milk of the word, as born again babes. The light of the Lord shines on us for a brief time, the Spirit convicts and draws the unbelieving to the light for a limited time, and then if a person remains unreceptive, is hid away. God gives every opportunity to you to repent and believe on Jesus Christ for salvation, but it isn't limitless. To day if ye will hear his voice, Harden not your heart...behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation...Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near! Just as God was longsuffering to the unbelieving as Noah built his ark, and then shut the door, too late to be saved, so to is His offer of grace. While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them. If you have not believed on Jesus Christ as the ONLY means of forgiveness and righteousness, if you have not accepted God's free gift of salvation, if you have been being called to the wedding feast, but have made excuse not to accept, or are trying to work your way in, repent. Tomorrow is not promised. You are being called today. Don't wait until it is too late. Don't harden your heart.

The introduction to this letter to Timothy, which Paul is writing from Rome, under house arrest, chained to a centurion day and night. We learn that Timothy got saved following his grandmother and mother to Christ, and was given the gifts of the Holy Ghost by the laying on of hands by Paul, an Apostle indeed. In his bonds, Paul shares that it is memories of things like Timothy's accepting of the Gospel that bring joy to him while in his predicament, and to encourage Timothy and others who may read this epistle to be of good cheer, hopeful in Christ and not ashamed of Paul's status. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind. He goes on to embolden Timothy, not to be ashamed of the Gospel, to lean on the power of the Holy Ghost upon him. To be a partaker of the persecution Paul suffers, willingly, because it is to the glory of God and the furtherance of the Gospel. Paul says to Timothy that God has called them, called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began, But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ. Note it is the predestination of Jesus Christ, not of the believer, that brings us to be used by God for His purpose, now that Christ was made manifest in Jesus, who abolished death and revealed immortality through the good news. The Gospel. This is how predestination works. Foreknowledge by God, predestinated in Christ, fulfilled in our belief, conformed to His use. For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day. Blessed assurance. We hold the ernest of His promise in our quickened spirit, the Holy Ghost indwelling within. Even in his persecution and humiliation, Paul knows the victory already won. He will not be ashamed for having placed his faith in the living God. Romans 10:11 For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed. Paul needs to write this encouraging word because of the betrayal of some in the faith, who having regarded his predicament, abandoned Paul. Not speaking out for him, and in fact turned away from the Apostle. Phygellus and Hermogenes are named in scripture, to their everlasting shame. But, not being a downer, Paul also gives praise to Onesiphorus for seeking him out and refreshing him in Paul's afflictions. Mercy and honor from God for being unashamed of the faith during tribulation. We should pray we can be like Paul, or at the very least Onesiphorus, when tribulations come.

2 Timothy 2 14 Of these things put them in remembrance, charging them before the Lord that they strive not about words to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers. 15 Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. 16 But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness. 17 And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus; 18 Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some. 19 Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity. It's funny how people who put these things in remembrance, who study to show themselves approved unto by God, generally agree on major doctrines and slight variation rather than difference on others, while people who read books and Wikipedia and YouTube and listen to strivings about words to no profit, debates and rantings, subverting the hearers believe the most outlandish things, and confidently, in a way that's both incredibly cringe and yet evidence of God blinding people who are more invested in their pride and status here in the world than their immortal soul. Paul continues his impassioned appeal to his young charge Timothy, written near the end of his life, from chains. Under house arrest in Rome. Unsure of his future but confident in his fate, Paul seeks to put his son in Christ firmly on the rock of the gospel, and in chapter 1 had recounted that many in Macedonia that he'd won to Christ had turned their backs on him in his tribulation, and turned from the truth of the gospel. Paul charges Timothy to be stedfast in the faith that won him, unashamed of Christ and the promise of God. Holding fast to the scriptures. He begs Timothy to be strong in the faith that Paul had won him by, with many witnesses, that is others who believed and were born again, those saved by the word, so as to be able to teach it to others. To endure hardness like a solider, as he's been called by God to be. Not entangled with any other cause or cares, but the one he's been drafted to. To strive for mastery, like an athlete. Earning crowns for his victories, without cheating, but with excellence. A husbandman, enjoying the fruits of his labor, souls won to Christ. He then impresses upon Timothy these doctrines that he feels are most important, beginning with the truth; Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead. For preaching this is what brought Paul to be in bonds. Scourged and stoned. Now facing the end of his race, he says he's endured all these things for the elects' sake. For the souls won by the same Gospel he's been persecuted for. That it was worth it all for their sake, that they may obtain salvation in Jesus Christ. (Note that he is saying they believed the preaching to be elect, and that he endured that they may have believed. Not that they were going to no matter what. Not that they were picked to believe, but having believed, become elected to the promise. This is not calvinism, but how the truth of the good news and the light of the Holy Spirit works in men to bring them to repentance and towards faith in God. That we must endure tribulation to share, that all men might be saved.) Paul continues. This is a faithful saying, that he charges Timothy to teach others; For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him: If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us: If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself. He writes that the vain babblings and striving, arguments about the law and doctrines not of scripture serve no other purpose but to subvert those who hear them. To keep people from the faith and salvation. It continues the theme of his previous letter to Timothy, about instructing church leaders at Ephesus to be first and foremost good witnesses to the word that men might be saved. Here too, he is seeking to reinforce this idea, especially where there are those like Hymenaeus and Philetus, teaching false doctrines and damnable heresies such as the resurrection having already been past. (Hymenaeus is the same heretic who Paul said he had given over to Satan for his blasphemy in 1 Timothy 1:20) Like Phygellus and Hermogenes, who ashamed of Paul's bonds, abandoned him and the calling, weakening the power of the Gospel for those who witnessed their shame and fear. These false teachers and weak leaders, subverting and deserting, are like cankers. Their striving and arguments like sores that fester and eat away at the word, leading men to damnation. Instead he charges Timothy to study to be approved by God rightly dividing the word that he may be able to stablish the faith of many, where these heretics overthrow the faith of some. Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity. Again, God knows who are His, but he lets, allows, every one that calls upon the name of Christ be saved. And being His, we are as vessels in His great house. Some earthen and wood. Carnal Christians. Who, while believing and part of the Kingdom, in the great house so to speak, but not being sanctified, are less suited to His purpose. He says not to be like they are, but to sanctify yourself that you become as the vessels made of gold and silver, meet for His use. For His good works. This dispels the false doctrine and damnable heresy of Lordship/perseverance of the saints. We are all saved who believe. And some will sanctify themselves to honor, becoming more useful to God. Others won't be more than earthen pots, and dishonored. But all are saved. We should strive for gold and silver. For crowns. For mastery. To be a soldier for God. Enduring hardship for the sake of those who may believe and be saved. And how does one sanctify themselves? How can we as believers be more than a wooden or clay pot, but become tools for God's glory? Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes. And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth; And that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will. We study His word. We know the answers to good questions that we may give meek and ready reason for the hope we have. Being patient. Charitable, loving people with the same grace shown us by God. Not striving, or argumentive, but gentle that those who are in sin come to the truth, and be saved. This is the meat of the word. It is next level stuff, not easily obtained, but that we must seek to be further transformed for the master's use. Praying for the wisdom and faith to grow in discipleship. Letting go of the cares of this world, that we may live in honor and glory in the next. Kings 2 18:4 He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brazen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan Isaiah 31:7 For in that day every man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you for a sin. Romans 1:21-25 Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. Psalms 115:4-8 Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not: They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not: They have hands, but they handle not: feet have they, but they walk not: neither speak they through their throat. They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them. Jeremiah 10:3-5 For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe. They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not. They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good." Isaiah 48:3-8 I have declared the former things from the beginning; and they went forth out of my mouth, and I shewed them; I did them suddenly, and they came to pass. Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass; I have even from the beginning declared it to thee; before it came to pass I shewed it thee: lest thou shouldest say, Mine idol hath done them, and my graven image, and my molten image, hath commanded them. Thou hast heard, see all this; and will not ye declare it? I have shewed thee new things from this time, even hidden things, and thou didst not know them. They are created now, and not from the beginning; even before the day when thou heardest them not; lest thou shouldest say, Behold, I knew them. Yea, thou heardest not; yea, thou knewest not; yea, from that time that thine ear was not opened: for I knew that thou wouldest deal very treacherously, and wast called a transgressor from the womb.

Paul, again in his final days, knowing he won't see Asia Minor and the churches he planted there or the evangelists like Timothy he's laid hands on and sent out, again, and having several of them turn from him in fear of persecution and shame of Paul's bonds, and several false teachers creep in to the churches to lead men shipwreck, is laying out the foundational doctrines for Timothy to remember and pass on. There's an urgency that allows Paul, in the Spirit to be as concise and precise as possible. It makes second Timothy one of the densest and deep books, despite it's brevity. Here we see, in order, the Reprobate Doctrine, the names of Pharaoh's court wizards (Jannes and Jambres), how reprobates will grow worse and worse over time, infiltrating houses, leading people astray, especially women. That God will give them what they deserve in the end. We learn the sound doctrines taught of Paul, purpose, faith, longsuffering, charity, patience, and the assurance that ALL who live Godly in Christ will see persecution. Tribulations and trouble for His name's sake. That faith comes from hearing and hearing by the Word of God. That scriptures make us wise unto salvation by faith in Jesus Christ. Faith alone, in Christ alone. Further, that All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works. We get out doctrine from scripture. No other source, but the word of God. It is perfect, meaning complete. It is inspired. It is preserved. If it weren't preserved, how could it thoroughly furnish a man of God unto salvation through faith? Unto good works? These doctrines are either denied or added to by denominations today. They deny reprobation. They deny salvation by faith alone. They deny scripture is preserved, inspired or even necessary for doctrine. Even prot denominations that claim Sola Fide and Sola Scriptura will add works to salvation and writings of "reformers" and church fathers to their faithless theology. Biblical Fundamentalism is the only way. New Testament churches, independent, pastor led, engaged in preaching the Gospel to every creature, a believer's baptism, a congregation of believers studying the scriptures to be approved by God, charitable to the brethren, judge to the fatherless, honoring elders and widows indeed. Eating communal suppers, in Jesus name. Tithing that those who work to the edification of the assembly are given their due. Awaiting the return of Jesus to save us out of great tribulation, and bring the wrath of God upon the wicked and profane. The rapture and resurrection of the saints. The millennial reign. The marriage feast of the lamb. Giving glory to God forever and ever. Amen. Everything else is doctrines of devils, having the appearance of righteousness, a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof. From these, the Bible says, flee.

This final instalment of a study on Reprobate Doctrine contains yet another list of their attributes by Paul (Romans 1:18-32 is another). We see the nature of our enemy, and how they will grow worse and worse as time goes by. Many false teachers seek to subvert the doctrine as they themselves are examples of it, having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof. "Ever learning but never coming to the knowledge of the truth" reminds me of the Ortho Gnome creature I posted about this morning. They will pridefully tell you all the books and "church fathers" they've read that reinforce their error, while mocking those who rely on the Bible alone for doctrine. From these, flee, because we know "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness."

I'm not crying you are crying. Paul, having come close to the end of his life, having written to Timothy, his son in Christ whom he led to salvation, grew in the faith, laid hands on for the gifts of the Holy Ghost and sent out into Asia Minor to evangelize and spread the gospel, planting churches, charging his protege with teaching the fundamentalist doctrines of God, reaches his summation. A poignant and inspiring end. Paul charges Timothy on God, in the name of Jesus, who will judge the quick and the dead, the living and the damned at His coming, to please be faithful to the doctrines he's left him. Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all long suffering and doctrine. The word of God must be preached, we must be ready with scripture, when it's popular and when it isn't, especially. For we must be, as Timothy, ready to use all scripture to teach, strengthen and correct those seeking truth. To whom God has called to us in the Holy Spirit. And this cause is great because, as Paul warns, people will wax cold to the truth, and turn towards fables and false doctrines that satisfy their itching ears, that justify and rationalize their sin, rather than lead them to the truth. So, as a stalwart in the faith, armed with the word, we, like Timothy must endure, for the sake of the elect that they may know the grace of God and His salvation. And we understand Paul's plea, that he facing uncertainty, and his impending death in this life, seeks to ensure the tradition of the Gospel lives on in his "son." For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing. This is the crown we should all strive for, the reward of those who work towards His coming. The Bible says; Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth. and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven. For Jesus will judge the quick, as well as the dead. We who believe and are given the gift of eternal life will see our works judged; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire. As Paul says, Every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible. And in Paul's striving for mastery, his running a good race, having fought the good fight, he knows with certainty as his end approaches, with that blessed assurance of the Spirit testifying within him, by the word that he has his hope in, that he will be rewarded by God as promised. For God is not slack regarding His promises. He is faithful in all things. Amen In the final verses, we see Paul is with Luke, author of that Gospel and Acts. He asks Timothy to make haste to come see him in Rome, asking him to bring Mark, who also wrote one of the four canonical Gospels. (it's interesting that he states Mark is useful for it was Mark ducking out of the first missionary trip with Paul and his uncle Barnabas, that caused the split between them later. Mark has redeemed himself in Paul's eyes, clearly) Prisca and Aquila, still doing great works for the Lord. Others, like Alexander the coppersmith, not so much. Paul lays it out there, good and bad, of those Timothy should salute, and those he cannot trust, having been shown what manner of men they are. Paul's warnings and salutations, his unwavering faith in God, and his personal requests for his cloak, his books, his parchments (possibly sources for Luke and Mark to draw on as they wrote their Gospels), are all touching in the context of his plight. Paul never stopped trusting God; the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

Paul, opens as he often does, professing he is a servant of God, and an Apostle, as evidenced by those who have believed his preaching unto salvation. His bona fides being those who believe. They having hope of eternal life, which God who cannot lie, promised before the world began, made manifest by the preaching of believers called to ministry of the Gospel. The preaching of this good news, which was commanded of Paul by Jesus Himself. The faith of those who received it of him bearing record. The fruit he has produced. This comes up often in Acts, and in most of his letters, and it's important to understand why God chose to repeatedly make this point, that Paul was His Apostle, born out of due time. There is heresy out there calling in to question Paul's authority, and casting doubt on his writings and doctrines, which make up a bulk of the NT books. Doubt that wicked men seek to cast to keep those ignorant of the truth from ever considering the epistles as scripture, not understanding that there is a perfect consistency between the inspired words of the prophets, patriarchs, Christ Jesus and His Apostles. Let alone considering the need of the clarity of doctrine regarding the implications of the common faith, of eternal life, by Grace. The mystery being revealed by the manifestation of Jesus in the flesh, His death, burial and His resurrection. Of how we are to partake in the promise, and having been adopted by God into His Kingdom, what then? What's next, having been saved? And so, thank God, He sought to give us the epistles, that we may be more perfect in our understanding. Just as He gave us the prophets, that we could be made meet for repentance, and the Gospels so we may know what we are to turn towards, we are given the Acts and letters of the apostles so we may know what we should do once we have turned toward God. And Revelation of Jesus Christ, that we may know what is to come. It is all one word, one testimony, one book made up of 66 smaller books, written over thousands of years, but with one voice, the inspiration of God, through the Spirit, testifying of the Son. Sometimes people lose sight of this. People who having believed the word, and should know better, as they have the same Spirit testifying to its power, within them. It is never so important to keep this in mind as when reading the Pastoral Epistles, 1st and 2nd Timothy, which we covered this past few weeks, and Titus today. At issue is the original organization of local churches. Of the offices and expectations, and the doctrines that should be preserved and taught among the congregations. Even supposed Christian denominations, especially those that claim an "Apostolic Tradition," will cast doubt on the epistles, denying Paul's authority by countermanding his doctrines, ignoring them, or claiming there were oral tradition that differs significantly from the whole body of scripture that contradicts their own edicts. There's a saying in studying scripture, that nothing in God's word is coincidental, incidental or accidental. And a maxim that if God repeats something, it is for emphasis and our edification. That it's important for us to get it. Much of scripture is terse, and brief and pithy. Giving exactly enough to convey the message intended. So, when God repeats the same lesson, we should listen. The Pastoral Epistles are an excellent example of this. One cannot say "Well, Paul was just telling Timothy this, we can't claim it's in all cases..." when he repeats the same doctrines to Titus. Just as Jude and Peter wrote nearly identical messages to the churches, just as we have four Gospel accounts. God's perfect judgement calls for multiple witness to establish truth, and He provides the same for us that we may believe Him, and those He sent. This epistle, written to Titus, Paul's son in the faith, who the Apostle had left in Crete to evangelize, just as he had Timothy in Ephesus. And just as he did in his letters to Timothy, Paul lays the foundation for the office of bishop, or pastor in today's parlance, a shepherd of the flock, and deacons or elders, those who work in a church ministering, serving the flock and aiding their shepherd. Commanding Titus to ordain elders in every city, the criteria being; blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly. Because, as the steward of God, the man handling the affairs and overseeing His sheep, must have these qualities; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre; But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate. Not given to wine and sober not being repetitive notions, but sober in scripture meaning not only clear-headed but serious as well. Matured in their attitudes. Not angry and wrathful and violent. Not a lover of money, corrupt, chasing after filthy lucre. A lover of hospitality and good men. Just, holy and temperate. This is the model for all seeking the offices of pastor or deacon, and should be what is given as an example for all young men of the faith to strive towards. Not only those who "feel a calling," but those who in humility and meekness seek to be right with God, that they may be blameless and able to win souls to the Lord. Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers. This should be the goal of all those who know Christ. Studying to be approved by God, and able to have a ready answer to those who seek truth, or who having hardened their hearts, seek to subvert it. And why is this so important to establish, especially with elders in the churches? Paul tells us, again warning as he has repeatedly, of those reprobate concerning the faith. For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake. Even in Paul's day, even in that first century, not far removed from Jesus' resurrection and ascension, even as Apostles and disciples blessed with the gifts of the Holy Ghost spread the word, preaching to every creature throughout the world, there were many false prophets. Vain talkers. Especially of the circumcision. Jews who being reprobate by God sought to subvert the nascent Christian communities with deceit, just as they do today. Paul gives an example of one such viper, who insulting the Cretians sought to keep them from the faith, and exhorts Titus to openly rebuke. To teach sound doctrines that the Cretan believers not be led astray, giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth. Judaizers who attacked the word of God and His churches then, never gave up, even forming their own religions based on Jewish fables, the apocryphal books and forgeries prevalent at the time. Doing it for filthy lucre's sake. For money, power, prestige. Control of others. Leaning on their own understanding, denying the power of scripture. Following after vain traditions and the commandments of men. Dead works, denying the power of the Gospel and faith unto salvation. This is the origin of the Roman Catholic Church, and the source of her harlot daughters, subverting whole houses. Who compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves, as Jesus said of the same Judaizers who murdered Him. Who could do such things? What kind of man could be so contrary to all other men, that they'd seek to subvert and damn others, as they are? Just as their father, the devil seeks to? Reprobates. Conscience seared, defiled, twice-dead. Deserving death. Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled. They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate. Every ordained Catholic priest, cardinal and 'pope.' Every Orthodox monk and Anglican bishop. Every works-based false salvationist. Every cult leader of LDS or JW. Calvinist lordshiper 'reformed' viper, with their corrupt modern translations. All of them. They are rejected of God and given over to their own unrighteousness. And over and over again scripture teaches us to be Biblical Fundamentalists, to cling to God's word, and to reject those who seek to turn others from the truth. Others who, with itching ears and mired in their own sins, can be turned from the truth by these vain talkers. Their mouths must be stopped, and it is by the word of God that we shut them up.

Paul is again writing of the reprobate, the rejected of God, and those abominable and disobedient deceivers going after the elect, or chosen. When Paul frequently writes of the Jewish persecution of the faithful, he frames it in terms of the reprobate vs the elect, because he is trying to show the Gentiles that THEY are the chosen people of God now, and the Jews the rejected: "Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them." Jeremiah 6:30 This deliberate use is misinterpreted by Calvinists who miss the point being made; that Saved Christians, "Greek and Jew" are now God's chosen, His elect, not the unbelieving Jew. And that they in their jealousy and envy, have further become filled with all unrighteousness. To be a Jew of the flesh after the coming of Christ is to reject God. To not retain Him in their knowledge. Jews whole identity is that rejection, and God's reprobation of them in return. This is why Jewish antichrists are so wicked. They are turned over to a reprobate mind.

Chapter 2 is a direct continuation of the same thought in chapter 1 (reminder that these divisions we're not in scripture and often seem clunky and forced). The "But" sets in contrast the reprobates being talked about at the end of chapter 1, to provide counterpoint to what Titus should teach and preach instead. Sound doctrines. That Christian men be sober and grave, clear minded and serious. Temperate, not given to wrath or over emotional, but instead being calm and measured. Sound in faith, trusting God, and in charity and patience, reflecting the love, mercy, longsuffering and grace God gave them, on to others. That women do likewise, behaving in holiness, not false accusers, drunken, but teachers of good things. Women being the teachers at home of the children, especially young women, so they may know how they ought to behave and that the young men learn to be sober minded as well. And that they all are given to doing good works out of the abundance of their heart, because of the sound doctrine they have been taught. This is all to serve the glory of God, to make us blameless that we may share His Gospel. That the word of God be not blasphemed. We are at Liberty in Christ. We aren't going to be judged by our works for justification before God, but we are judged of man. We are to be good witnesses to others, for the unbelieving's sake. That they may be called by the light of truth we magnify. To become the vessels of gold and silver, meet for the master's use. To be more perfect in our faith. To earn glory in the Kingdom which we are joint heirs. The Bible says everything else is vanity. But the occasion to blaspheme God by being a bad witness should also motivate us. That the devil is an accuser of the brethren. A ravenous lion seeking whom he may devour. By our sin as believers, we give him cause to blaspheme God. When Nathan reproaches David in his sin with Uriah the Hittite and Bathsheba, he says that David's sins of murder and adultery are already forgiven, as David was saved by faith. But because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme, God punishes David with the death of his newborn son. We too face reproach and punishment by God for being a bad witness to His power. He scourges His children for giving His enemies reason to blaspheme. For bringing dishonor to His house. In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity, Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you. This ties in with the much-abused James 2, and the exhortation of believers to do good works, that their faith be profitable to others, knowing that a man may judge their faith by their works. And again it's in furtherance of spreading the Gospel. We obey the commandments out of love and do good works out of love, that we being honor to the house of our Lord, and build His congregation with new believers. Edifying the church. This is our calling. All else is vanity. Paul continues, again as he has in other epistles, instructing that servants, indentured or employed, be honest and diligent. That they may show through their behavior the glory of the grace of God, who is not a respecter of persons. God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble. The lowly and the high status are all judged the same. When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom. Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up. This is a difficult saying, but it is found all through scripture. We are to be satisfied with our station, and be joyous in our salvation. Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: to be laid in the balance, they are altogether lighter than vanity. Knowing this, and knowing it is God's grace that sets us free, we shouldn't resent our station, and instead be thankful for what we have, blameless that we may win even those who we serve to Christ. And so, living uprightly and blamelessly, having Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you, we humble ourselves, esteeming others better than ourselves. If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee. And again, as Jesus taught us; And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away. Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust. For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same? And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the publicans so? Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect. The faith required to give up pride, knowing that God will reward you in the next life for wrongs suffered in this one, is one of the hardest hurdles we face in our Christian walk. And for what cause do we humble ourselves, living soberly and with all gravity? Giving good witness? Blameless that we may not be accused? Rendering good works and a meek answer for our hope, given with a clear conscience? For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world; Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ; Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works. These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee. We who are saved by faith, who have that blessed hope, an assurance given us by the Spirit, testifying within us. The new man, quickened, warning against the flesh, we have the grace of God teaching us that these things are so, and good, and right, and so me must exhort other believers to this cause, and rebuke those who oppose it, with all authority as His peculiar people. His priesthood of believers. To His glory, forever and ever. Amen

Finishing Titus, Paul continues his exhortation to teach sound and profitable doctrine to the Cretians. Letting no man despise Titus for the truth, encouraging him and those who he sets up as pastors and elders in the churches he plants as evangelist to make certain they have the the same doctrines of faith. This instruction has given us as men, women, girls and boys, servants and slaves, leaders and pastors the blueprint for Christian living. Continuing the theme, Paul writes, again, that we must subject ourselves to higher powers, even as we keep God as the highest. If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men, as he writes in Romans. And again, this is to make us blameless that we may win people who are in error, bringing them to repentance towards God and common salvation. Being a good witness. This is a hard saying, and pride, fear and wrath lead many to stumble at it. We are warned to speak evil of no man, because after all, the sins and flaws that they may be engaged in are sins common to man, and such were we at times. But with the kindness and mercy God showed us, so too we are to extend grace towards others that they may be drawn to the light. As Jesus taught, Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. And this is the purpose of good works, to be profitable to other men in showing them the light of God. Not to justify us before God, but that others may step into the light by our example. That works are not how we are saved is the clearest, most repeated doctrine in scripture, and yet it continues to be the stumbling block that keeps so many perishing, damned to Hell because they trust in their self righteousness to save them. It couldn't be any clearer than in Titus 3: ...That the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared, Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. There is no doubt we are saved from our sins and Hell by faith alone, by grace alone, in Christ alone. That God's grace extends to all men. That the renewing of our spirit comes from the Holy Ghost, and He through our faith in Jesus Christ, and God's promise that we be His heirs to the Kingdom of Heaven in the assurance of eternal life. This is the Gospel. There is nothing more to it. There can be nothing less. And to put works firmly in the place where they belong, to be encouraged in the life of those who are already saved, that we may be in service to those who have yet to be. (And no, they aren't automatic, as some false prophets preach, for if they were then we wouldn't need so much encouragement to commit ourselves to them) This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men. This is the Biblical Doctrine of good works. That they which have believed, past tense, in the Gospel that was just laid out, might do them and be profitable to others. We are justified by His grace. And so we should be reminded of that and do good works that others may benefit from our salvation. If your theology is anything else, repent. You're perishing. As wise and as knowledgeable to the doctrines of man as you might be, don't let your pride mislead you from the clear truth presented here, and throughout scripture. And, once again, God repeats for emphasis that we should avoid foolish questions, Jewish fables, endless genealogies, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain. Debates and silly theological questions and talmudic arguments about the law help no one. They can lead to heresy and blasphemy. They can be a snare and a stumbling block to those seeking truth. Be determined to know nothing but Christ and Him crucified. As far as those who endlessly strive about these things? They are heretics. A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject. If you've shown them clear scripture, two times, and they still insist they are right, then shake the dust. It's not worth it to answer a fool in his folly. It's why I have the pinned rules in my chat. Sincerely asked questions, met with polite consideration when answered is one thing, but demands to go back and forth with their natural man idea of scripture is vanity. Useless. Helping no one, and may give you cause to sin and them to accuse. Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself be satisfied, instead of having to prove them wrong. That's your pride, and it helps no one. (I have fallen in to this trap. It's so tempting) Grace be with you all. Amen. For those keeping track at home, together we have read every book in the New Testament except for Mark and Luke, 1st and 2nd Peter, revelation and Philemon.(although we've done studies out of all of them). And in all of these verse by verse breakdowns, we have yet to find any hint of salvation with works, lordship, calvinism, sacraments, man-made Church denominations, the authority of man to add to the word, or any other popular heresy. Clear verses, in context, and all of these doctrines remain unmentioned, while the clear teaching of salvation by faith alone through grace alone in Christ alone is given. Over and over again. Really makes you think... A common argument made by heretics who haven't taken correction after one or two admonishments with scripture is that "only God can judge if I am wrong." And while that's true, we are blessed to know His judgment as God has laid out precisely what the correct doctrine of salvation is in a way that's clear and understandable. Don't assume one's relationship with God by their works or sins. It's hypocritical and you don't know the full story, nor can you know where the Spirit may lead them. But you can absolutely judge by their doctrine. And if they tell you they don't believe the Gospel and are trusting in something other than it to be justified, you can safely consider them unsaved. What makes all these staged acts of vandalism doubly galling is that they involve wasting food at a time of growing fears of famine and inflation. Our instinct at times like this is to be shocked at deliberately wasting food. It's why they aren't using paint or anything else.

An epistle to Philemon, the host of a Colossian church, Paul writes from his bonds in support of Philemon's escaped slave Onesimus (or unfaithful servant, it has been debated), is an instruction on forgiveness. How we as Christians may settle scores between brothers in Christ, if not equals in station. Being peacemakers. Onesimus apparently fled Philemon, and wound up in Paul's camp, converted to the faith by the Apostle. Philemon, his master, already a prominent Christian in the early church. Paul's delicate appeal to take back the servant, not only as a servant, but forgiven as a brother in Christ is a model for us to follow. He reminds the elder Christian of his debt to those ministering the Gospel which he's saved by, and asks he see it right to extend the same grace to Onesimus, who is seeking forgiveness. Paul even offers to pay whatever debt is owed, though he gets in a not-so-subtle reminder that Philemon owes even more so, having eternal life by the word preached by Paul and his fellow laborers. We should also make overtures to bring brethren together, to help broker peace and forgiveness. And we should use reminders of what love Jesus Christ has for us that He gave Himself for us as sacrifice, that we may suffer a little worldly loss out of love for one another. Onesimus brought this letter and the general epistle to the Colossians from Paul in Rome, and the preservation of Philemon and the promulgation of Colossians suggests that Philemon found it in his heart to forgive him, and welcome him as a brother in Christ. Due to the current Kanye events, people are noticing that the Jew will take on whatever form or appearance necessary to avoid accountability. This was the original 'Big Lie' that (((history))) attributes to Nazis, when it was the Nazis description of Jewish behavior

If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men: 15 But my mercy shall not depart away from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before thee. 16 And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever. Deuteronomy 32:43 Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people: for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, and to his people. Psalm 104:4 Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire Psalm 45 2 Thou art fairer than the children of men: grace is poured into thy lips: therefore God hath blessed thee for ever. 3 Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O most mighty, with thy glory and thy majesty. 4 And in thy majesty ride prosperously because of truth and meekness and righteousness; and thy right hand shall teach thee terrible things. 5 Thine arrows are sharp in the heart of the king's enemies; whereby the people fall under thee. 6 Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre. 7 Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows. Psalm 102 25 Of old hast thou laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens are the work of thy hands. 26 They shall perish, but thou shalt endure: yea, all of them shall wax old like a garment; as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: 27 But thou art the same, and thy years shall have no end. Psalm 110:1 The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool. Acts 13:33 God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee. God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son... In the letter to the Hebrews, Paul seeks to create a definitive case for Jesus Christ as the fulfilment of scripture, the Son spoken of to the fathers by the prophets and the other diverse manners of God's revelation. He is writing to the saved, but greater is his appeal to those among the Hebrews, who, like him had rejected the truth of Jesus until coming to the truth at Damascus. Paul uses his mastery of scripture and the inspired word of God to show that at all times, in all ways, God told them of His promise. And that now, His promise has come. Continuing his thesis, and having established Jesus is the Son, by whom all things were done, and now sat at the right hand of the Father, Paul begins to break down what this means, from scripture. Using angels, who are considered holy and close to God, Paul writes that at no time have they been called sons of God. That they have not the glory or the power or the inheritance that Christ Jesus has by His very nature. The angels are created, ministering spirits, but the Lord Jesus is through whom all things were created. They are not the same. Some dispute the authorship of this epistle, claiming that it was not Paul who wrote it. And in a way they're correct. I firmly believe Paul is the human author of the book of Hebrews, a shout out to Timothy later on essentially removes any doubt. But of all the books and epistles, Hebrews to me reads as the most inspired, the closest to straight dictation from the Holy Spirit. That's of course my subjective opinion, but the beauty of the prose in the text and the doctrine found in Hebrews is so elegant and yet simple that regardless of the human author, once again, God is speaking to us. And it is beautiful. One of the establishing doctrines in the first three verses of Hebrews chapter 1 is the understanding that while there is one God, the Father and the Son are distinct persons within the godhead, That makes up the Trinity, along with the Holy Spirit. The Bible says that jesus is a separate being but the express likeness of God the Father's person, They are the same and yet different persons. Throughout the Bible we are told that Jesus is God. But having His own will, and obeying the will of He who sent Him, The basis and understanding of the Trinity is confirmed here, once again.

Having established Jesus as Christ, the redeemer, higher than the angels, Creator and the Son of God, our salvation to whom all the prophets gave witness, Paul builds upon this truth with the implications of our faith. Since Jesus is, therefore we should give greater heed, pay closer attention to the things spoken of by God, in diverse manners by the prophets to the fathers and by Lord Jesus Himself. That every transgression of the law (for sin is the transgression of the law) shall receive a "just recompense." Death and Hell. Just as the angels who rebelled will be all brought in subjection and cast into that lake of fire promised in Revelation, so too will man be if they neglect the good news of salvation, spoken of by the Lord and confirmed by those who witnessed Jesus ministry, and by signs and wonders of God, and through the gifts of the Holy Ghost given the disciples and Apostles. He's saying, "Look, we know who Jesus is not only by reputation but by scripture, the prophets, His followers who got it directly from Him, and we know about the fate of those angels who rebelled, Whom Jesus is greater than as He has them under subjection, so we need to listen and believe." But Jesus was also a man. Citing scripture, Paul notes how God made Jesus a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, that He may taste death for all men. That the Creator became as the created that he may bring us to glory. That He, as the captain of our salvation was made perfect, complete, by the suffering of the cross and death as a sin offering. For in Christ, we believers are His brethren, His brothers. Sanctified in Jesus we become as one with Him, sons adopted into the promise of His glory by the Father. Who Jesus is not ashamed to call brethren. Again and again, citing scripture that his audience would know, primarily the Psalms of David which teach so much doctrine, he lays out the case for his argument. By taking heed we are the children of God by the partaking of Jesus flesh and blood through His death. And by His resurrection, steal the power of death from the devil. Satan was a murderer from the beginning. His goal is to ensure every man faces death and Hell like him. To sin, and in sin, be condemned. This is the power of death the devil possesses. But Christ's triumph granting salvation to all who believe, and eternal life to never taste death, delivered us. Set free from the bondage of the law, which by fear of death we try and fail to save ourselves. But in Christ, liberated from that fear knowing we won't die for our sins, as they are forgiven in Him. And so, to provide this salvation Jesus took on the form of man. And in all things He was like us, tempted of the flesh that He may know our struggles and understand our pain, that He may serve as the propitiation for our sin and succour, comfort us, in our temptations and afflictions. This is so important to understand. That God so loved us, that He so regarded man, that He allowed the express image of His person, His only begotten Son, through Whom all things were made and under Whom all things will be brought under subjection, to be made lower than the angels, to be made flesh and blood, to be tempted and suffer and made sin for all, that we may have eternal life. Liberated from the fear of death found in transgression of the law by our redemption in His perfect work. Just as the prophets and scriptures promised. Just as those who came before believed on for salvation. This is the good news. This is the Gospel. Psalm 8 1 O LORD, our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens. 2 Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger. 3 When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; 4 What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? 5 For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour. 6 Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all things under his feet: 7 All sheep and oxen, yea, and the beasts of the field; 8 The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea, and whatsoever passeth through the paths of the seas. 9 O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! Psalm 22:22 I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee. Psalm 18 I will love thee, O LORD, my strength. 2 The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower. 3 I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised: so shall I be saved from mine enemies. 4 The sorrows of death compassed me, and the floods of ungodly men made me afraid. 5 The sorrows of hell compassed me about: the snares of death prevented me. 6 In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried unto my God: he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, even into his ears. Isaiah 8 13 Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread. 14 And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. 15 And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken. 16 Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples. 17 And I will wait upon the LORD, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.

Building the case laid out in the previous chapters, Paul makes an appeal to the faithfulness of Christ Jesus to God the Father, likening Him to Moses, and through this, linking the faith they share to enter into rest, and brought out of sin to the promised land to the Hebrews fleeing Egypt towards Canaan. He reminds them to be steadfast in the faith, to genuinely believe their salvation is as assured as the Hebrews was, least they like that first generation, be left in the wilderness for their sin and disbelief. Again, Paul uses the Psalms, credited to the true author, the Holy Spirit, rather than the man, David. And so too, like the Hebrews, if you hear His voice, heed it. Harden not your hearts with sin and doubt, but have full confidence in the promise made by the living God. Psalm 95 6 O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the LORD our maker. 7 For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice, 8 Harden not your heart, as in the provocation, and as in the day of temptation in the wilderness: 9 When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my work. 10 Forty years long was I grieved with this generation, and said, It is a people that do err in their heart, and they have not known my ways: 11 Unto whom I sware in my wrath that they should not enter into my rest.

Chapter 4 again builds on the previous; Hebrews 3 For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses. But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness? And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief. Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it. Therefore, because, their unbelief in the desert prevented them from entering the promised land, so too fear your unbelief keeping you from entering into the promised land, the rest in Jesus, the better country; the Kingdom of Heaven. By drawing the comparison to the Hebrews fleeing Egypt with those called coming out of bondage of the law and sin, Paul shows God's grace and His judgment parallels with Exodus spiritually. That it was a picture of Christ that so many Hebrews failed to believe and so died in the wilderness. For we which have believed do enter into rest. Note the tense. Salvation comes by belief at the moment we call upon His name. At that time we are freed of bondage and given rest, and it is done by the work God finished from the foundation of the world. Genesis 2:2 And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. Paul argues that if God says (again quoting Psalm 95) If they shall enter into my rest, that we can reckon that this is a possible thing, offered by God, and those whom it was first preached didn't enter their promised land due to unbelief, then we can know we will enter into His rest by faith, and be kept out without it. And further, as the Spirit moved Paul to write in Psalm 95; Today if ye will hear His voice, the offer is limited. We have but a short life to believe.
