Acts 17 God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen....But without faith it is impossible to please him. So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Faith is trusting someone or something promised. Relying on the hope of an offer or covenant. Of belief in the unseen based on faithfulness of the one making the promise. The testimony given. Their word. Faith in God relies on His word being true, His promises being kept. His end of the covenant being as a rock. God, who cannot lie tells us His word, and by hearing, we believe the report. That is faith. And the just live by faith. It isn't a mystical force. It isn't will-to-power sorcery. If faith moves mountains, it is by the promise of God to move it, not our will but His. The Hall of Faith saints written about here, the recitation of those people who the scriptures tell us believed God when He made promises to them, who were made righteous by their faith and did the will of God for a reward not seen. A promise to be kept. Blessings bestowed on future generations. But their faith held on His word allowed them the opportunity to do great things for the Lord. Because one of the many promises God makes unto us is that He is a rewarder of them that diligently seek Him. Beginning with salvation. For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God. That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. This is the first promise. Faith in this is the rock upon which Christ built His church. The Kingdom of promise that we trust in. The better country; that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city...a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God. We are dead in sin. But made righteous by faith, our spirit quickened. Given eternal life. For the just lives by faith. Literally. But more, once justified, we live by faith diligently seeking Him in His word. Rightly dividing His promises, and being told His will. And by faith we are blessed and rewarded. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth. These are some of the promises made by the word of God that we may know are true: Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel's, But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life. Or, These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world. Or, He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son. Just as Abraham was made a covenant, a son to Sarah delivered, and a blessing to Isaac promised. Just as Moses and David and the prophets were made promises they trusted, and were delivered by the Lord. Just as Jesus fulfilled so many of the promises made by God. So too, God has made promises to we who believe. Who please the Lord by our faith in His word. How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! One of the promises of blessings, rewards in Heaven and on earth, comes from our command, the Great Commission, to spread the word of God, and live blameless that we may be living witness to the unseen promises, that others may find faith by hearing, see evidence of the hope we have. That they may come to call upon the name of the Lord and be partakers in the same promise. To live by faith. But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias saith, Lord, who hath believed our report? Not all who hear believe. Not all who are told the word of God and see the promise of the hope we share, choose to believe. For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead. Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools. But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. The just live by faith but those without faith, who harden their hearts and stiffen their necks and refuse to believe God's word, die because they are faithless. He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son. Now, the expression of faith is found by obeying the will of God. By this a man's faith is justified before men. Just as the OT saints listed in Hebrews 11 believed and their faith was counted for righteousness, and by faith their works showed to others the power of God's promises. So too, we are to live our faith. For faith without works is dead, being alone. We may be justified by the blood of Christ before God, but if we hide that faith under a bushel, or we bury that which we've been trusted rather than gain an increase for the Lord, our faith is fruitless. Dead. The exhortation of James 2 to live out our faith and in doing so, help those in need, sharing that faith that they may come to the same and live, is a beautiful reminder of our calling. Those that twist it to make works their means of justification before God, damn themselves and put Christ to an open shame, for their dead works are without faith. Disobedient to the Gospel. Perishing. And so, a simple exercise for those of us seeking to grow in faith and understanding, by trusting in God's word and obeying His will as revealed by the same word; 1 Thessalonians 5:18 In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you Are you thankful in all things? Do you know how to be abased, and how to abound? To trust that you can do all things through Christ, who strengthens you? Do you have faith to know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose? Are you thankful for all things, good or bad, that the will of the Father for you in Christ Jesus is kept, and in so doing, regardless of what it is, good or bad, you give thanks? This one exercise of being thankful to the Lord and trusting His will regardless of our own will, having faith that by seeking Him and following His will for us we will be blessed and rewarded, even if it isn't something we can see as yet... Even if it remains hope on His promise...This one thing will change your life as profoundly as anything short of salvation. I testify to it, God is my witness. He is not slack concerning His promises. His will be done. In all things give thanks.

Amen! The pure hard preaching of Hebrews is building to a crescendo. The case made for faith in Christ Jesus, without the works of the law or traditions of man, against the temptations to backslide the way of Judaizers, but towards full faith in a better testament, nearly complete. The Spirit through the author, telling us the will of God and reminding the hearers of His word the excellency of His faithfulness in keeping the promises and bestowing the blessings on those who came before us. Those just who lived by faith. The saints named from the patriarchs and prophets, and the unnamed Christians who for their faith in the promise of Christ suffered mockery, pain and death: ...others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection: And others had trial of cruel mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment: They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented; (Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth. Many who endured in faith towards God's word, not seeing the promises but in hope knowing they would be delivered by the Lord, faithful and true. And so we, who carry burdens, the weight of guilt, of bitterness at correction, of the distractions and cares of this world, which can lead to envying of the unsaved and impatience with God, to sin, to the fornication of putting the pleasures of the flesh before the promise of our inheritance and the blessings to come, Paul encourages us to standfast in the faith. We have a race to run. A crown incorruptible to receive. The yoke of dead works and guilt for sins forgiven slowing us in our course. We must shed these things, striving for the mark set before us. And where we slip, where we stumble, know it is God's correction, rebuking those sons whom He loves. Bringing us reproach that we may turn from the sin or shed the burdens that slow us down. For our edification we must not despise the rod of correction given us by our Father, but take joy in that He loves us. Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God. For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds. Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin. If we consider Jesus, who literally authored the word that our faith hangs on, and finished it by the work He did, the first fruits of the resurrection assuring us of His faithfulness, if we keep in mind the shame of the cross which He endured for our sin and to do the will of He who sent Him. Our struggles with sin and the weight we carry in this world is nothing. Cast it off least we be castaway. So understanding this, that we need separation from this world, not to despise our promised blessings for a bowl of pottage, that we not satisfy the flesh in our short time here rather than see our hope for eternity. But, as Moses, Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season. Don't be down or angry with God for His chastening, which as it happens may seem grievous, but understand it builds righteousness so that we may better serve the living God, and bring forth fruit as an example to others. Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed. As scripture says: I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in right paths. I have taught you in the way of wisdom. I have led you in straight paths. And again, In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the LORD, and depart from evil. Following God's word, the hope that we believe on, we are given wisdom, our paths made straight. Not only for us but for those without, who are lame, who are perishing. That they may see God's glory reflecting from us like Moses come down from the mountain. Be peaceable with all men, showing holiness, the separation we are called for, that our faith obtains a good report, as it did the elders before us. Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled; Don't allow your burdens and sin, or bitterness at correction or anything to give a bad report of the faith, that others may not be defiled and not accept the grace of God. We are a holy priesthood. We are heirs to a kingdom. We have hope everlasting. Act like it that others may attain the same. It is the least we can do considering what Christ did for us. For when it is too late for those we turned away by our bitterness and strife, our bad report and our sin, our despising our inheritance, our lack of faith, they are rejected. And there will be no place for repentance. Therefore, we are again reminded that we aren't under the covenant of Sinai, but of Zion. We aren't like the Hebrews in the wilderness who, hearing God's voice and His commandments could not endure it and asked that God not speak directly to them any more (as much of fear of His commandments which establish death, as fear of the thunderings of God). We are of the new covenant of a Heavenly Zion, which established life, in the continued presence of the Lord. But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect, And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel. So we shouldn't be as those in the wilderness who turned from the voice of God, but instead glory in it, that He will not only shake the earth but the heavens as well. And so we serve God with grace, and reverence. God-fearing, where our faith brings good report. That we might bear fruit of those led to the straight paths we walk by His light that shines from us. Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear: For our God is a consuming fire. One of the key points throughout the book of Hebrews is that if we who are saved fall back again to the old ways, to the sin offerings and dead works, to bitterness at reproach, to neglecting our Christian walk, we bring others down with us, who have not received salvation. Who haven't yet come to the saving faith. Who may be pricked by the Spirit and hear the power of God's Word, and so taste of the heavenly calling and fall short by our example. And thereby many be defiled. Especially knowing that there comes a point where their rejection of the truth and refusal to find faith in the hope we have can leave them reprobate. Either in death, or by being turned over to a reprobate mind by God. We give them cause to harden their hearts. To be dull of hearing. To not believe our report. Our faith alone cannot bring another to the knowledge of the truth. But our lack of faith can lead the lame to stumble, as we bring them to uneven paths, leaning on our own understanding. Many of us harp on the Reprobate Doctrine because it is an extremely important Biblical truth that far too many are ignorant of, or reject to lean on their own understanding or follow the wisdom of men. There is a point where it is too late for some. And once they are given up and given over, they are twice-dead. Children of Hell, fit for burning. But this isn't simply for the cursing of those who have been rejected by way of their hardened heart, but a grave warning to those of us who have been blessed by the faith in God's promise and redeemed in the blood of Christ. Faith comes by hearing the word of God. So does reprobation. The Bible says they have the knowledge of the truth but don't wish to retain God in their knowledge. That they turn the truth of God into a lie. If they will harden their hearts and turn away from the truth, don't let it be that we, like David, despised the commandment of the LORD, and give great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme. Don't let it be by our bad report. Rather, if they reject the truth of God and His offer of grace and mercy, let it be because by our righteous conversation. Our behavior. That they see our faith and that we walk the straight paths, and if it offends them so be it. If our separation from the things of this world and the peace we have because of the blessed hope we've attained offends them, then it's their own dull hearing and seared conscience to blame. This is a great responsibility. Exodus 20:18-22 18 And all the people saw the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the noise of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking: and when the people saw it, they removed, and stood afar off. 19 And they said unto Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us, lest we die. 20 And Moses said unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before your faces, that ye sin not. 21 And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was. 22 And the Lord said unto Moses, Thus thou shalt say unto the children of Israel, Ye have seen that I have talked with you from heaven. Proverbs 3:11-12 My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of his correction. For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth. 1 Corinthians 9:24-27 Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain. And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible. I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air: but I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.

Thursday: After being placed in the tomb before 6pm on the start of the High Holy Sabbath for Passover (Wednesday night), Jesus spirit descend into Hell for 3 days and 3 nights to be the burnt sacrifice for our atonement... Matthew 12:40 40 For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. John 19:31-42 31 The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away. 32 Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him. 33 But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: 34 But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water. 35 And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe. 36 For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken. 37 And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced. 38 And after this Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus 39 And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight. 40 Then took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury. 41 Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new sepulchre, wherein was never man yet laid. Many who lack understanding, try to paint the idea of a believer being guided in truth and understanding of scripture by the Holy Spirit and their own quickened inner-man, as some form of gnostic heresy. This is incorrect. Gnosticism requires steps of "enlightenment" to be completed at the end of a long process, achieved by works. For the newly saved, the "babes in Christ," this understanding comes with the gift of the Holy Spirit, a gift given in the same grace of God as salvation, without works: John 16:13 Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come. 1 Corinthians 2:9-14 9 But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. 10 But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God. 11 For what man knoweth the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God. 12 Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God. 13 Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual. 14 But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned. Christianity is anti-gnostic

Paul's letter to the Hebrews ends with exhortation to pure doctrine, of love to our brethren and grace, and gratitude towards God. Remember in prayer and in well doing those of our brothers in bonds and persecution, adversity and tribulation. Verse 4 is a reminder that the intimacy of a married couple is blessed by God. Some, especially Catholics, believe all acts of sex are dirty and wicked. But God tells us the marriage bed is undefiled. Avoid covetousness in your behavior, don't want for things but instead be grateful for that which God provides knowing we have eternal life through Him. In that peace, of gratitude when you are abased or abound, in bad times or good, knowing God is with you, you will have nothing to fear. Not even death. And so nothing can be held over you by those who hate God. Obey and respect elders in the faith, paying attention to the fruits of their behavior. The results of their living by faith. Think on it as encouragement and walk in their paths that are straight. Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever. Amen! The warning against strange doctrine here refers to going back to the sacrifices, establishing a clean conscience by the offerings rather than by the grace of God, but it should apply to any doctrine of works or rituals that takes us from relying on our faith on Christ Jesus. Paul reminds us we have an altar, the Spirit inside us, by the stone cut without hands that is Christ, that none of these Judaizers are able to partake. That Jesus is the only sacrifice. Let the Judaizers and Pharisees and those that cling to dead works mock us. Let them put us without the camp. To the wilderness outside the earthly city. Bearing their reproach. For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come And so, in Jesus' name we give thanks and praise continually towards God. This is the only sacrifice we need, given of our lips and believed on in our hearts, given through the offering of Christ for us. And ending in a prayer, full of doctrine of the hope we who are saved share; Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant, Make you perfect in every good work to do his will, working in you that which is wellpleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. Signing off, we see why we believe Paul was the human author of this epistle, in bonds in Italy, sending Timothy who has been freed back out to his mission. The doubt cast on the author of Hebrews seeking to undermine what is one of the greatest books of NT doctrine. But we who are His sheep hear His voice, and the voice of God is clear here. Like a homily given directly from Heaven. Grace be with you all. Amen.

As we begin the epistle of James, written to saved, believing Christians of the Jews, in the various churches throughout Asia Minor, scattered abroad. In our reading of Acts 15, that James determined from Paul and in agreement with Peter, to write concerning edification of the churches forming, and to denounce the works-based salvation that was creeping back in from "certain Jews," specifically of circumcision. And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe. And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith. Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear? But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.Then all the multitude kept silence, and gave audience to Barnabas and Paul, declaring what miracles and wonders God had wrought among the Gentiles by them. And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying, Men and brethren, hearken unto me: Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name. And to this agree... So, at the outset we understand the context, the reason for the epistles and the dispensation of doctrine which they agreed upon; salvation by faith. After his greeting James wastes no time. He praises them for keeping faith through troubles and testing, that this grows patience in the believer. We see this in our own lives, that where we are tried, and maintain our trust in God, our spirit grows stronger and we become more complete as Christians. "Perfect" in the Bible means complete, or whole. Not sinless, or without any flaw, but as spiritually complete as one can be while still in the flesh. A more perfect Christian life is the theme James hammers throughout. James teaches the lesson that in faith, we may ask God for knowledge and understanding. That all wisdom comes from God is established in Proverbs 2:6 For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding. He cautions that we ask in faith, unwavering. Not half in, half out as some Christians are, believing the truth of the Gospel, but hedging their bets in the world. That a double minded man is unstable in all his ways. To be perfect and gain understanding we must commit to building up, faith on faith, while remaining humble, to not thinking you deserve God to just hand it to you. That lesson in humility carries on, that the poor should rejoice in gratitude for their salvation in God's grace, while the rich, in understanding that they are but dust, and with the same meekness and humility. He says again that the temptations and tests of this life are a blessing, that we are rewarded with the crown of life for our efforts. As Paul says in Romans 4, when we do His work, it is reckoned of debt, and we are paid for it by God, as His laborers. We rejoice in the free gift given by Him in grace, but receive rewards for our patience in temptation. He warns against blaming God for our affliction, even as God blesses, He tempts no man with evil. James tells us that it is our lusts that lead to sin, and sin to death and tribulations come from this cycle. But the gifts that come from God are blessings, given in His grace. That we have the word of Truth, that is Christ Jesus, was beget of God's own will, that we may be His first fruits of the harvest. Amen And so, we should avoid wrath and be patient. Avoid temptation of lust for the things of this world, and receive the word, "engrafted" in our hearts, which is able to save your souls. This is not just the Gospel and spiritual righteousness, but living in the word, obeying His law written in our hearts, saves us in the physical sense from the temptations and trials James is warning against. Salvation, or being saved, is not always referring to the righteousness imputed on us by Jesus' blood, through faith. It often means being saved in a literal sense, as we'd use it today. We are admonished to be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Many Christians go to church, sit through Bible study, and simply never grow because they are hearers only. They think they are complete Christians for their idle listening, while doing no soul winning, no charity, having no grace for others, being respecters of persons, esteeming those with power, wealth, credentials, etc, over the poor, the ignorant, those of low estate. This theme of not being a respecter of persons is another that James is hammering home in this epistle. We are blessed in our deeds, being doers of the word. We are called to not just be loudmouth Holy Rollers, judging everyone without grace, and puffing ourselves up for attending church, listening to preaching, and the other trappings of religion, without doing that which we are called to do. To visit the fatherless and the widow in their affliction and to keep ourselves unspotted from the world. To be a perfect, a more complete Christian, we should do the good works we are made for, as those justified by faith. So we have the themes of James' epistle; to edify the saved to do more than just accept the word, but to live it. To be humble in our own status, regardless of what it may be for we are all but grass that withers and dies. That by living in the word, we save ourselves from the temptations of the world. Avoiding wrath and lusts. That by practicing the pure religion, undefiled, we become more complete in our Christian life. And that we shouldn't hold any in higher esteem for worldly reasons, not being a respecter of persons. (That's the meaning of that, if you weren't sure) Now in the second chapter, James builds on this theme. That how we present ourselves in favoring one man over another for earthly things, we sin. In this favoritism and judgement based on the outward appearance and status the way the unsaved do, we begin to fool ourselves about our own temptations and sin in the same way. He reminds that the poor of this world are often the most faithful, and are joint heirs of the kingdom with us, and just as damned without faith and God's grace as we are. That it's the rich of this world who often are our oppressors and enemies of God. James then reasons with us, that those who keep the law for righteousness, if they offend in one point they are guilty of all. And that being a respecter of persons is sin, as it violates the "royal law," the golden rule, that we do unto others as we would do for ourselves. But we who are judged by the law of liberty, that is saved by faith in Jesus and so, our sins being covered, should not engage in this at all, but live the word that we have heard and believed. To judge with the same mercy and grace He has shown us. Now we come to the verses that are a snare to so many, where they justify works based righteousness, despite all of the mountain of scripture that assures us we are made righteous by faith alone, through grace alone, in the perfect work of Christ Jesus. But, comparing scripture with scripture, and the verses in context, it's not difficult to understand, unless you're a natural man seeking to force the Bible to fit your preconceived notion, rather than letting it tell you God's. First, what follows is a series of rhetorical questions and reasoning logic, designed to give example to what James has already preached. And again, it is written to the brethren, the author assumes it is to those already saved, to exhort and edify, not to get them to believe. Not to save them spiritually, but to those already saved, become more complete in their Christian life. We do not receive doctrine from rhetorical questions or "a man may say..." reasoning, stripped of context. We get them from clear statements that do not contradict others. For brevity sake I have already given argument above, with verses as to why this interpretation that we must do works to be able to go to heaven and have eternal life is damnable heresy. Scroll up. I may add to it as we study through this section, but if that's not sufficient for you, your argument is with God, the Gospel as given by Jesus and then shared by the Apostles, and clear, consistent verses, given again and again from Genesis to Revelation. If you are trusting in your own works to get righteous or to maintain the righteousness given by God in Christ, you are damning yourself and being made debtor to the whole of the law which no one can keep perfectly. For there are none righteous no not one. Repent, and obey the Gospel. What does it profit a man who says he has faith but doesn't do anything with it? Being a hearer of the word only, not a doer. James is continuing this theme, and as in the earlier verses, he is referring to being saved from the temptations and trials that arise from our lusts and sins. Remember, his goal is to educate believers into becoming more perfect, complete, Christians. Not to get people saved in the born again sense. Knowing the context answers the rhetorical question. Further, the example of this rhetorical question says he has faith. This is important. James is tying in the lesson that people generally are respecters of persons with the concept that we are to be doers of the word, as befits those who will be judged by the law of liberty. We aren't judged by our works and sin, as the debtors are. We are free in Christ. This is the context of the entire epistle. James has already told us that we earn crowns of life for our deeds. But salvation is a gift, unmerited. Grace-mixing isn't how any of it works. The next hypothetical in James reasoning, if someone is needy and you basically just say "thoughts and prayers!" it doesn't profit them anything. It's useless. Dead. It doesn't do anyone any good. Dead faith doesn't mean it doesn't exist, but that there's no life in it. Nothing to indicate it, outwardly. It's alone, profiting no one else. A dead body exists, but it just lays there. The same is the faith of a Christian who doesn't exercise it to help the fatherless and widows and the poor. See the theme? Understand the larger context? You'll have to forgive me, as I do this, I am preparing to leave for a weekend camping trip and getting everything in the garden, the chickens, and stuff we need to pack ready as I do this Bible study. I'm going to finish off the chapter in a minute, but I have to shower Getting back to it; next we see James continue to use rhetorical hypotheticals to reason with the believer, in this case, "a man may say..." Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble. But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead? A man may say this. What kind of man? Saved? Unsaved? A respecter of persons? Someone who could reasonably or unfairly doubt your profession of faith by your lack of visible works? You see that this is a device by which to show what someone could say, in order to get at the larger point. It is not directly stated doctrine. A man may say all manner of things. For example, we know devil's are not capable of coming to saving belief in Christ. Yet here it says, in this hypothetical man's argument, that they believe and tremble! It would take an extreme case of Nicodemus-level Asperger's to draw a doctrine that devils believe on God, as saved Christians do. And yet many draw doctrine from the very same verse! Amazing. James continues the argument: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar? Was Abraham justified by his works before God when he was prepared to sacrifice Isaac? Well, no. In fact we know that's not the case. A fact James makes clear in the summation following; Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God. James says, you see how Abraham's works shut up the hypothetical man, judging Abraham? That his faith was made complete by his works, in regards to being justified by men. We know this is true, because again in Romans 4, Paul cites the same scripture James does: 1 What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? 2 For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. 3 For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. 4 Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. 5 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. 6 Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, 7 Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. 8 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. 9 Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. 10 How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. 11 And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also: Abraham was saved spiritually, justified before God, by his faith alone. Decades before his circumcision. Decades before bringing Issac to the altar on the same mountain in Jerusalem where Jesus would later be crucified. But to be justified before man, that outward sign of his faith, made his faith more perfect. There was a visible tangible act of faith, works that a man may say that they've been shown his faith. Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way? Rahab was justified to Joshua and the Hebrews by her aid of the spies, but it was her faith in leaving out that crimson thread, representing the blood of Christ, that actually saved her and her household. Her deeds help others. They profited others. She very well could have said yeah yeah I believe you, and done nothing to help them, and her faith in them would be dead, profiting others nothing. I'll continue through the rest of James during this weekend if I have a chance, if not I will finish it up on Monday. I do these studies live, as we read I write. You can probably tell because they're not very polished all the time, but I do it off the dome for a reason. When you study the word of God, and stay in it reading it daily, you gain understanding and familiarity with the concepts of the totality of scripture. Any saved Christian can do this. All it takes is daily Bible reading, being in prayer, and turning towards God and away from the cares of this world as much as possible. As we see in James chapter 1, wisdom comes from God and all knowledge and understanding is His to give, but we can't just assume that he'll give it to us without our seeking it first, humbly and in prayer and in faith. By being doers of the word, and not hearers only. I hope this has helped some of you gain a deeper understanding. Don't be a respecter of persons and understand that the average man may judge your faith by your works, the use you actually have to others. Don't have dead faith, but be profitable for those in need and in service to God. Invariably, when someone doesn't accept Biblical reproach of their own lifestyle and choices, rejects the Word as complete and appeals to things like external writings, suggests that scripture is culturally grounded to when it was written, or contextually different based on audience, they also don't have faith in the simple Gospel of salvation in Christ alone. They nearly always have faith in their own works, the "repent of sin" misunderstanding, dispensationalism or other more damnable heresies, that has led to the lesser doctrinal error. And please don't get me wrong, James 2 is incredibly important lesson in how we as Christians should carry ourselves and use our faith to be effective for others through our works. It's also crucial when understanding how others perceive us and that they are respecters of persons even though God isn't, and we shouldn't be. It's also brilliant in how it's written, showing the Spirit of God in the words, framing the rhetorical question of what a man might say to a Christian to illustrate the points. But of course we know from scripture that Abraham was saved by faith alone, and wasn't justified or made righteous by his works decades later, willing to sacrifice Isaac, long after he accepted the Lord and called upon his name for salvation. We know this from reading the old testament, but more so we know it from the examples Paul uses regarding this in his Epistles. Quoting Genesis 15:6 "And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness." in Romans 4:3-5: 3 For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. 4 Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. 5 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. So, if these clear contradictions of the "faith without works is dead" interpretation can't be wrong, and if the snippet of out of context lines from James 2 cannot be wrong, then the interpretation, that James is saying Abraham wasn't saved until he was justified before God by his works instead of before man, must be wrong. This is made evident in simply reading the full James 2 epistle and understand what's being talked about, and comparing scripture with scripture, the litany of verses explaining the Gospel is by faith alone in Christ to to justify us, and accept God's forgiveness and eternal life, given in Grace, in return for that faith. Even he who worketh not... Because it is a gift. “Not of works, lest any man should boast.” Listen to me when I tell you that if your preacher priest or pastor is teaching you that you need to do works in order to be saved, they are lying to you to control you and to keep you from the knowledge of the Gospel of the Lord. Only Jesus saves, and he doesn't need our help for that. He does need our help in winning souls to Christ that can only be done by those who are redeemed in his blood and who have accepted him as their only means of salvation without works. His work alone perfect. Complete. If he is adding to that salvation with extra steps? Run. Then fall to your knees and call upon Christ alone to redeem you. "But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed."

Watch what you say. Get control of your own tongue. Speak meekly, in God's given wisdom, and show the world through your good conversation that new man that lives inside you. Don't be full of envy, coveting, wrath and strife. O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh And A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh. We can bring others to righteousness by our own display in our words, not just our works. Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives. As Jesus tells the disciples; Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.

James breathing fire. Condemning the wicked who are rich by deceit and who afflict the faithful. There is a false doctrine, invented by Catholics (among dozens of others), called the "Harrowing of Hell." Instead they claim Jesus went to Hell on a Saturday to give the Gospel to Old Testament saints and various heathens who "lived a righteous life," or were "seekers of truth" like Virgil and Plato and other pagans, so they could go with Him to Heaven. It is an incredibly natural man thing to believe, and it's no wonder that its origin comes from the false "Gospel of Nicodemus," supposedly written by the unsaved Pharisee in the Gospel of John who couldn't understand salvation and being born again, despite being a leader of the people, as Jesus pointed out. Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things? But to give it some anchor in scripture, they pull 1 Peter 4:6 to claim it. The verse states "For for this cause was the gospel preached also to them that are dead..." Which relates back to the previous chapter: 1 Peter 3 8 Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous: 9 Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing. 10 For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile: 11 Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it. 12 For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil. 13 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? 14 But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; 15 But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: 16 Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ. 17 For it is better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing. 18 For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: 19 By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; 20 Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water. 21 The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ: 22 Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him. Jesus triumph over death and Hell and the eternal destruction of those in prison, Hell, is a like image to the people destroyed in the flood, the dead in sin, and the quick are those with eternal life in Christ, by the resurrection of Jesus, like Noah and the other 7, saved by water, (which is also a figure of baptism, which is an answer of a good conscience toward God, not how we are saved, but that we are saved). The people in Hell were shown their disobedience by the resurrection of Jesus, just as they mocked Noah and were destroyed by the flood, they mocked God and were thrown into Hell to witness Jesus triumph.

Jude 24-25 Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen. Eternal security in Jude Another thing that becomes very clear as you go through the epistles in this quick fashion, is how the focus changes from opposition to Judaizers in the beginning of the earliest churches to the problem with apostates that came as those churches became more established. Judaizers sought to bring believers under the bondage of the law, as taught by Pharisees, and were primarily Jews. Apostates used the cloak of Christianity to bring in idolatry and fornication. Eating meats sacrificed to idols and fornication and adultery as part of religious practice. Nicolaitanes, Jezebel, those who introduced the way of Balaam, creeping into houses unawares, and leading captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts. As we recently read in Numbers, Balaam taught the Israelites to join in with the orgies and whoredoms of the Moabites and Midianites. For they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian...and God sent a plague among the Hebrews as punishment. The teaching of reprobation is directly tied to this apostasy. Paul, Peter, Jude and John all wrote about it. It is part of Jesus message to the seven churches in Revelation. Apostasy and reprobation go hand in hand, and we can understand that those who have an intellectual knowledge of the gospel but who go out from it, who taste the gift of the Spirit, but reject the truth and seek to pervert others, these false teachers, all become reprobates. Unable to come to the knowledge of the truth. Ever learning. That it is impossible for those who were once enlightened to be renewed again unto repentance. It really stands out how this threat evolved almost immediately when the pagan Gentiles began to come to salvation in Christ, surrounded by the degeneracy and vile affections of the heathen. Vexed by their filthy conversation as just Lot was in Sodom. Zechariah 3 presents the prophet with a vision of the high priest Joshua, in the time of Zerubbabel and the restoration of the Temple in Jerusalem. And the angel of the Lord stood before him, and Satan at his right hand to resist him. To accuse him and tempt him. The Lord rebukes Satan, the adversary, just as in Jude, where angels, even archangels, who all are mightier than man, don't bring railing accusations or curses against the Devil, but say "the Lord rebukes thee." There are many who have built an entire ministry on the basis of "rebuking Satan," railing against the devil. Not resisting him, that he flees, but they themselves speaking evil of dignities, railing against things they don't understand. They often come with a false gospel, adding works or strange doctrines. Charismatics and charlatans. But the Lord rebukes Satan here, saying that Joshua was an iron plucked from the fire. His instrument. Even as the Lord set His name on Jerusalem, so He had chosen Joshua to be His high priest. In the vision, Joshua is arrayed in filthy garments. And those that stood before him are ordered to take them away, that the Lord would clothe him in a change of raiment. Making him clean. Just as Jude writes of saving some by fear, pulling them from the fire, hating even the garments spotted by the flesh. Just as Jesus promises to clothe those who believe on His name in white. For the priests of the Old Testament must be cleansed and sanctified, made holy by diverse washings and sacrifices, but Joshua, without the temple and without the purification rituals was made clean by grace through faith by the living God. Joshua is given a fair mitre, a head covering for the office, and fine garments, as the angel of the Lord stood by. And again, we are given a conditional promise to the high priest, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; If thou wilt walk in my ways, and if thou wilt keep my charge, then thou shalt also judge my house, and shalt also keep my courts, and I will give thee places to walk among these that stand by. The angels around him. Then he is told through the prophet, that the Lord will bring forth His servant, the Branch, a promise of Christ Jesus. He says He will lay before Joshua a stone, that rock of salvation as Christ is called; Isaiah 28:16 Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste. As in 1 Peter 2:6-9 Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded. Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed. But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light The image of Christ as the foundation, the corner stone, perfect and square, and the sanctification in Him of the royal priesthood, carrying over from the Old Testament, done away with, and given to a new priesthood of believers, washed clean in the blood. The Lord of hosts says, I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree. That blessed day, at the coming of the Lord of hosts. Amen.

The revelation of Jesus Christ as told to John, signified by His angel, written to Jesus' servants, and directly to the 7 churches which were in Asia, to tell us the things which John had seen, which are and things which shall be hereafter. The book of Jesus Christ's Revelation is not written to obscure. Its intent is literally the title. To reveal. Those of us saved by Christ are blessed by reading it. Hearing it. Keeping the prophecy of those things written therein, for the time is at hand. Written in the late first century, likely around 93AD, by the Apostle John, who served Jesus in His earthly ministry with his brother James, who was martyred shortly after Christ's ascent. Called by Jesus "Boanerges," or the "sons of thunder," their mother asked Jesus for favor for her sons in Matthew 20:20-28. John was the apostle Jesus loved, who wrote the Gospel and epistles. Now, exiled to Patmos by Domitian, emperor of Rome from 81 to 96AD, for, as John writes here; "for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ." We know the timing and details from John's disciple, Polycarp, and early texts by historians Clement of Alexandria, Victorinus, Eusebius and Jerome. The timing of its writing doesn't much matter for us, blessed readers. The earthly things are incidental to spiritual. But the heresy of preterism requires the authorship to be pre-70AD, because it relies on the early writing to make the desolation of Judah by Rome, the destruction of the temple and murder and scattering of the Jews, serve as fulfilment of the prophecy. Other modern "scholars" cast doubt on the author's identity, deny John wrote Revelation, often claiming different people wrote the Gospel, epistles and Revelation attributed to John, however the style and description of spiritual things by the Apostle, as well as the clearly inspired truth contained put that heresy to bed sufficiently for believers. That John's peers and ancient historians testify that it was his bolsters that, but a careful reading of scripture is all we really need. Now as to the contents; there are many, many commentaries on end times Bible prophecy, and a multitude of heresies and blasphemy surrounding it. The most employed tactic by vipers seeking to sow doubtful disputations and confusion is painting Revelation as an obscure and difficult book to understand, and focusing on the earthly signs, fitting the timing to a predetermined schedule, convenient for these false teachers to generate the most fear and confusion possible. Keeping Christians from simply reading it themselves, and instead relying on others interpretations. We see here in chapter one that, like the rest of scripture, the focus is on Christ Jesus and the spiritual things of God. When we read any of the Bible, we should keep this our focus. Comparing spiritual things with spiritual. It greatly helps with rightly dividing the word of God. John writes that it comes "from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, and the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth. Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father; to him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen. Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen." This is what it's all about. It isn't about geopolitics. It's not about which earthly nation or events we want it to be. It's not a warning to those "left behind." It is written to be a blessing to the saved that we may know God's will in the last days, the honor and glory of Jesus and His triumph of the resurrection, His reign, wrath, judgement and victory. We are called simply witness to His glory, amen. Lord Jesus, who we are repeatedly told is "Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end," He which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty. John describes the vision of Jesus He has: the Son of man, clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle. His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire; And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace; and his voice as the sound of many waters. And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength. He is radiant, fitted with a golden girdle, hair white, feet bronzed, and from His mouth comes the Word, a two-edged sword. Hebrews 4:12 For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. Some heretical blacks use this passage to claim Jesus is black. It's foolishness. His feet are like brass as if they'd been burned in a furnace, not natural pigmentation. Again, it is applying natural man things to what is spiritual that leads people to nonsense doctrine. John says as he turned to witness Christ he sees seven stars and seven golden candlesticks. This is one of the many symbolic illustrations we will see as we go through Revelation. And these are the kinds of things that false prophets seize upon to claim that the book is too mysterious to understand directly. That one needs some gnostic process to understand. Yet, as we read on we see that each mystery is explained. Jesus says to John regarding the 7 stars/golden candlesticks; The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches. We aren't left to wonder about much. There are some hard passages and dark sayings contained in Revelation, but more often than not, they are explained in the narrative. God is not the author of confusion. Trust in the Spirit. So much of this is incredibly straightforward, it is a shame Satan has made people afraid to read Revelation. That confusion the devil has sown in the world keeps Christians from the blessing that is found in it. So, now heading into chapter 2, recall that the 7 stars are the angels of the 7 churches, and the 7 candlesticks are the churches themselves. Note, churches, plural. The idea of a single universal church is not biblical. They were independent and Christ led, New Testament churches from the beginning. Many interpreters of Revelation will claim the 7 churches are either different "ages" of "the church," which again presupposes a single universal church, or that the following descriptions of each actually applies to individual Christians. In some sense, they do but only in so far as these churches are models, a picture of what can befall any assembly, and so as church members, we have responsibility to avoid their pitfalls. But it is important to let God's word tell us what it means, and it plainly does when you read it in context and in full. Finally, reflect back on these verses, where John, writing to saved Christians, reminds us of the Gospel of reconciliation, the common faith we share: Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, and the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth. Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood,, And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father. If you are not 100% certain of this, if you don't know for sure that you're going to Heaven if you died today, unsure if you will be counted among the saints, at the resurrection when Jesus returns in the clouds, washed clean of all sin by His blood alone. Not of your own works or anything else, then please take a moment to listen to this presentation of the Gospel. For faith comes by hearing and hearing by the word of God. Did you read the Bible today?

Revelation 1:18-20 I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death. Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter; The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches. This week, we are going to look at the messages to the churches in Asia Minor that are addressed by Jesus in His revelation to John. I want to focus on a very specific aspect to these churches; even the worst had members who were right with God. There are some strange doctrines around these, the most common of which is that the churches represent some "church age," and that they describe a period of time, rather than the types of behaviors described. Others make these verses to be about individual people, and personal salvation when, as we see in the above passages, Christ is talking about groups of people and the candle is the assembly, not individuals. But these are literal places and people, real actual churches, and the lessons given are to serve as a model for our churches today. And a lesson for those who think they are too righteous for church, and so they forsake the assembly. Revelation 2:1-6 Unto the angel of the church of Ephesus write; These things saith he that holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks; I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted. Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love. Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent. But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitanes, which I also hate. The Ephesians, a well known church in the NT, has been around at this point for about 40 years. We know it was established during Paul's evangelizing around AD 60, and John is writing in mid-90 AD. They are given a mostly positive review by Christ. They are right on doctrine. They are right on preaching against false doctrines Christ hates. They rejected false Apostles, labor for God and are faithful, yet they have been lacking in their first love. Most see this as meaning soul-winning. Evangelizing to others, as we are called to do. While we as individuals can certainly serve as a witness to Christ and give the gospel to the lost, winning them to Jesus, the assembly of believers is called to do this in an organized way, and to provide a place for discipleship once someone is saved. A place for baptism and service. Edifying, that is building-up, the congregation. Training others to go out into the world, preaching to every creature. As good as Ephesians are, their lack of this is sufficient for Christ to rebuke them. But what does this mean for us today? It means that we need to encourage the brethren to do all those positive things mentioned that the church at Ephesus does, while not forgetting that first love. I will cover a church a day, but I will take this time to establish some definitions and doctrines. Church is a called out assembly of believers. Jabeshgilead was wiped out: Go and smite the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, with the women and the children. And this is the thing that ye shall do, Ye shall utterly destroy every male, and every woman that hath lain by man. There are consequences for not assembling when called. Preferably a place with a roof and protection from the elements. Maybe with chairs, since you'll be there a while. Lights and heat and AC would be great. Hey, why not a building dedicated to that purpose? You see the sophistry of saying it's not a place, when you actually stop and consider what that means. Well what about when Jesus says "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them" Yes! Wonderful promise of the Lord, that He blesses us with His presence when we gather together in His name! This presupposes you are actually gathering. It's not an excuse to not. "But it's getting bad out there, Satan is everywhere! So many false churches with bad doctrine!" All the more reason to get plugged into a local church: Hebrews 10:24-25 And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching. This appeal is explicitly about what we should do because things are getting worse, not an excuse not to. Colossians 3:16 Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. Can't do that from your sofa. Revelation 2:8-11 And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive; I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. But what does it mean to live godly in Christ? Well, for one it means to be in church. The saints at Smyrna were gathered together, and doing works that despite their poverty made them rich in the eyes of the Lord. And that brought persecution of the Jews against them. You will not be persecuted for the faith if you are practicing it in private, online, as a shut in. You are not doing works God sees and knows. You are not drawing attention of the enemies of Christ. You certainly aren't going to earn rewards in heaven for persecution that never happened. You won't be put in jail for Christ, not even 1 day. Being banned from social media or a chatroom isn't persecution. It takes being an open member of a congregation doing works for the Lord to stand out and be set upon by Satan. Romans 5:1-5 Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God. Genesis 28:10-22 And Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran. Revelation 2:12-16 And to the angel of the church in Pergamos write; These things saith he which hath the sharp sword with two edges; I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satan's seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth. The church at Pergamos was located in a city of committed idolatry. Pergamon was a wealthy city of trade and a center for the worship of Greek gods like Zeus and Dionysus. Jesus repeats that He hates this false doctrine. "The churches near me are full of hypocrites! They have some tertiary doctrines I don't agree with!" Are they offering meat unto idols? Still a candlestick was lit for that church. Still Jesus gave them encouragement and praise with His criticism. Go to church, even if you have minor disagreement with others there. Deuteronomy 24:19-20 When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the LORD thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands. When thou beatest thine olive tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow. As a reminder that God has provided a system to feed the poor, called gleaning, where the owner of a vineyard or orchard does not go back over the field after harvest to get every last morsel of fruit left in the vine, but instead leaves it for the poor to gather.
