Revelation chapters 2 and 3 deal with "what is," in the prophetic sayings of Christ Jesus, to the angels or messengers of the churches in Asia Minor, through John the Apostle. The letters He bids John write are addressed to the individual churches, from an aspect of description representing Jesus, have compliments and criticism and warning and rebuke for the church, followed by an encouragement for those with an ear, of what it means to be saved. This pattern can be split up, to better see the doctrine being given. First, we recall from chapter 1 that the 7 stars are the angels of the 7 churches. The 7 candlesticks, the churches themselves. Taking away their candle in this context means the church would fail. No longer having the blessing of God. And, they all eventually did as none remains. This is a lesson to churches today. Some or all of what these 7 model churches are engaged in can be found in even the best churches today. The Lord Jesus is warning each and warning us. The message of overcoming, as I posted a study on yesterday, is the promises of Christ to the saved who stay faithful, who repent to do the things He instructs. A reminder of what awaits us as saved sons of God that we may be true. Jesus singles out three groups whom He hates and will judge; those who say they are Jews but are not, who are the synagogue of Satan. The Nicolaitanes. Jezebel and those she's seduced. So, let's break it down, missive by missive to each church. Unto the angel of the church of Ephesus write; These things saith he that holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks; Jesus begins using a descriptor of Himself, from the description given by John from His vision in chapter 1. Jesus is holding the angels of the 7 churches in His hand. He is walking in this midst of their candlesticks. His message is to the Ephesians, the church founded 30 odd years before the writing of Revelation, by Paul and the other evangelists. That had fornication in their midst back in Ephesians 1. Jesus goes on to praise their good qualities; I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted. All good things. Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love. Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent. The Ephesians have left their first love. This is generally accepted as the spreading of the Gospel. They are working and laboring and being persecuted in Christ's name, trying false prophets who crept in unawares and rejecting them. But the first love of any church is the winning of souls to Christ. The joy of our salvation when fresh leads to our telling everyone about the good news. Churches grow from giving the Gospel. But many successful churches plateau and settle in with who they have, and get wrapped up in feasts of charity, laboring in their own community of believers while neglecting this command of Christ to preach the word to every creature. Without that, Jesus says, He will remove their candlestick. The church will die. But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitanes, which I also hate. Another compliment, that the church at Ephesus hates the deeds of the Nicolaitanes. We have to discern from this limited information that they were a group either led by or claiming to be followers of someone named Nicolas. Many speculate that it refers to Nicolas the proselyte from Antioch, who was elevated to deacon along with Stephen and Philip back in Acts. The doctrines referred to here, according to early writings and histories is that Nicolas, a pagan convert to the faith of the Jews, then accepting Jesus as the promised Christ, had the doctrine of despising the flesh, hating the material world, that he could better focus on the spiritual. The idea is given he was a just believer, but those who came after him took his views and drifted heavily into gnosticism. We can't know directly from scripture, but this seems very likely. It's also possible that gnostics took the name as a way of gaining legitimacy in the early churches, that they may creep in unawares, with damnable heresy. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God. The first promise to those who overcome, who believe on the Lord Jesus Christ for salvation, is the gift of eternal life. The eating of the fruit of the tree of life, in the midst of the paradise of God. The location is going to come up later in Revelation, but the important thing is the knowledge that we who believe in He that has overcome will be given of it to eat. Recall in Genesis 3 that God banishes Adam and Eve from the Garden to prevent their eating of this tree themselves, having already eaten of the tree of knowledge of good and evil. Having sinned. And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive; Again, addressing the church of Smyrna, as the first and the last, which was dead and is alive. This is Jesus. Alpha and Omega. The risen Christ. I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. The church at Smyrna is poor, but rich in spirit. They are working for Christ and being persecuted for it by the Jews, so-called. The synagogue of Satan. The absolute failure of those churches that teach Zionism and dispensationalism, Hebrew roots and other Judaizing heresies to recognize precisely who Jesus is talking about here - HINT: they call themselves Jews and meet in synagogues - that failing is the work of Satan in them. They are enemies of God, contrary to all men, and they kill and persecute the saints, liars and antichrists. The tribulation they gave the early churches has never stopped. Here, Christ encourages them that despite the tribulation of being jailed, it will be for ten days, and even if they die for His name they will be rewarded with crowns in heaven for their patience and eternal life for their faith. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death. Another promise to the saved; we shall not be hurt of the second death, which we will see later in Revelation refers to Hell and the lake of fire. The eternal damnation that those who have not overcome will suffer. And to the angel of the church in Pergamos write; These things saith he which hath the sharp sword with two edges; And so, to the church at Pergamum, from Jesus, the twoedged sword that proceeds out of His mouth, the word of God. I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satan's seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth. Pergamum was host to the main temple of Zeus, the altar to this false god was his "throne." Because of how strong the pagan religion was in the city, the Christians who professed the truth of the living God were subject to tribulation, harsh persecution even the martyrdom of one of their own, Antipas. These believers held fast, to declare the name of Jesus among the pagans. It is common to think of paganism as the religion of the wild barbarian. But the worship of dead idols in glorious temples made of marble and gold, their graven images and fancy altars, in the Hellenistic world (and today), is often the religion of the civilized. The superstitious nature of natural man leaves them wide open to attack by Satan, and his throne can be found in many advanced cultures as much as it is in the woods and huts of the savage. But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication. The doctrine of Balaam refers to the soothsaying false prophet from the OT, who appears in Deuteronomy, Joshua and Numbers, the son of Beor, a Mesopotamian false prophet who is seemingly familiar with the true God of Israel. He is sent for by Balak, the king of Moab to curse the Israelites who were warring against him in return for treasure. God prevents this in various ways, despite Balaam's best efforts to, he ends up blessing the Israelites. Balaam suggests finally that the Moabites could get Israel to sin, and that would bring God's disfavor on them. Specifically, he tells them to lead them to fornication with their daughters offered as whores, and then have the women lead them in their concupiscence to eating offerings to idols. We see the success of this in Numbers 25: And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods. And Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel. And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel. And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baalpeor. We see an admonition against chasing after the error of Balaam in 2 Peter 2: Spots they are and blemishes, sporting themselves with their own deceivings while they feast with you; Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children: Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; But was rebuked for his iniquity. Just as Balaam then, the church at Pergamos had those chasing after fornication, whores and eating the sacrifice made to idols. So hast thou also them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitanes, which thing I hate. Repent; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will fight against them with the sword of my mouth. And again the Nicolaitanes appear, but unlike the Ephesians, these Pergamites have allowed these heretics in their congregation. Jesus warns that he will destroy them if they don't repent of these errors. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it. Another promise to the saved; we will eat the hidden manna, the bread of Heaven, and receive a new name written on a white stone, a name which no man may know except he that received it. The Lord throughout the Bible has given new names unto those who have believed on Him. Jesus did it in His earthly ministry with his disciples, and this trait of God will continue, extended to the saint, we who have overcome. And unto the angel of the church in Thyatira write; These things saith the Son of God, who hath his eyes like unto a flame of fire, and his feet are like fine brass; Again, writing now to Thyatira, Jesus as described in John's vision. I know thy works, and charity, and service, and faith, and thy patience, and thy works; and the last to be more than the first. The church at Thyatira is doing well, their works growing, the last more than the first. Patient, charitable, serving others, faithful. Notwithstanding I have a few things against thee, because thou sufferest that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed unto idols. But the Thyatirians have multiple problems, that all stem from allowing, suffering, a woman to teach. 1 Timothy 2:12: But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. We see here exactly why this is a problem. Jezebel is joy only teaching, but in the authority she's gained over the men, has seduced them into fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols. The error of Balaam compounded by her role in their church. And I gave her space to repent of her fornication; and she repented not. Behold, I will cast her into a bed, and them that commit adultery with her into great tribulation, except they repent of their deeds. And I will kill her children with death; and all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works. That the sin she is in and leading others too comes from their disobeying God's word, and compounding the error, when given chance to repent and turn back towards God, she refused. Backslidden and defiant, Jesus says He will punish her and those who are with her. He chasteneth who He loves. These aren't some sort of reprobates like the Nicolaitanes, these are His servants gone astray. And the punishment is severe. Casting her into bed, stricken sick. Likely of STDs. And those she misled into great tribulation, until they repent. But unto you I say, and unto the rest in Thyatira, as many as have not this doctrine, and which have not known the depths of Satan, as they speak; I will put upon you none other burden. But that which ye have already hold fast till I come. Jesus says to the rest of the congregation that haven't fallen into this wickedness to holdfast. Encouraging them that He will honor His promises to us at His return. And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father. And I will give him the morning star. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches. We who are saved and keep to His commands, doing the works He has asked of us, we will be rewarded by ruling and reigning over the Earth with Him in the millennial Kingdom. Ruling with a rod of iron, the perfect law of God. And we will receive the morning star, the glory that is Christ Jesus. Amen. Thinking about it, at this rate. We will have finished every book in the New Testament by the end of spring, God willing. And likely the other 4 books of the Pentateuch by end of year for sure. Stick with it! And make sure to be reading and studying on your own and at What are the Seven Spirits of God Jesus talks about in Revelation? Isaiah 11 And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: 2 And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord; 3 And shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord: and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears: 4 But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth: with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked. 5 And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins Jesus of Revelation is the Christ promised of scripture. The Word of God.

Revelation 3:1-6 And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars; I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead. Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God. Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee. Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. One of the most common push-backs against going to church is that churches are "dead." That all the congregations in the area are filled with elderly women, senior saints, and a pastor managing the decline, whose ministry is deathbeds and funerals. It is not an indictment of churches, but younger generations not replenishing the pews. Sardis, which apparently had a reputation thought the region of being a great church doing great things for the Lord, is becoming dead. Jesus warns them to strengthen that which they have left, before He snuffs out the candlestick of their assembly. Young blood revitalizes an old church. Even in Sardis, there were believers who kept the faith and remembered that word which they had heard. Who are saved. Even if the rest were lifeless, and dead. Just going to go and not believing unto salvation. What a blessing it would be for those hanging on for that glorious day, and who would strengthen the works that remained, by having young red hot Christians to help them. What great things young people could do for the Lord by being a blessing to them. And for a pastor to be reinvigorated by the new sheep added to the flock. To look out at what was a dying church and see new life again. To plan baptisms and weddings instead of funerals. Go to church. Even if you are 40yrs younger than the youngest member. Even if it is uncomfortable at first. Learn from them. Help. Be used by God. Go to church. Romans 10:8-9 But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach; that if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. Born-again Christians are familiar with this beautiful verse, proclaiming the gospel by which we stand. What follows is equally important, and applies to those of us who have already called upon the name of the Lord. Romans 10:13-15 For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! How shall they hear without a preacher, how shall they preach without being sent. This is the first love of a church, and the great commission we have been given by Jesus as Christians. To be sent into the world, preaching the good news to every creature. To be sent requires a sender. To be skilled in preaching requires a tutor. An instructor in the faith. We are given the model of soul-winning by how Christ Himself sent out the apostles. Luke 10:1-3 After these things the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come. Therefore said he unto them, The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest. Go your ways: behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves. And traveling out to compel people to come to the Lord wasn't a new concept in the New Testament. Above, Paul was quoting Isaiah: Isaiah 52:7 How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth! As it is said; Proverbs 11:30 The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise. If you are not in a church, who is sending you out, two by two? Who is organizing it? Go to church. Revelation 3:7-11 And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth; I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth. Behold, I come quickly: hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown. The church at Philadelphia gets off the easiest from Christ's letters to the various independent churches of Asia Minor. They have kept the faith with patience and done great works, deserving crowns. They have everlasting life and the promise of Jesus that the Jews who persecuted them will be made to know He loves them. This promise extends to all who have overcome in Christ Jesus. Believe it or not, despite what charlatans online say, there are churches like this today. You can likely find a church full of salt of the earth believers in every county in the US, or within driving distance of one. Churches with the right gospel, the right mindset, filled with people who love the Lord with patience and faith, doing great works for the Lord, building each other up in persecution and edifying themselves in the word. And the crowns they earn for themselves in the Kingdom do not rust or mold. They last forever. But that is not something available to you at home, alone, consuming Rumble videos and listening to weirdos spout nonsense. True discipleship comes from joining the local church to be a worker for the Lord. Revelation 3:14-19 And unto the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write; These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God; I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth. Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see. As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent. The church at Laodicea is probably the most talked about in these seven letters to the seven churches. Many have some mistaken idea that the 7 churches represent 7 "church ages," and that we are in the "Laodicean age." That churches are generally lukewarm now, and it's just how it is. This is foolish. But this foolish idea has led many to abandon church altogether. "If Jesus is disgusted by their lukewarm Christianity, then I don't want to even bother!" Of course there are churches who are like all of these seven, and the model of each is given by Christ to John as a warning to us not to veer towards the negative things that any of them do. When faced with a lukewarm church, not facing much persecution, comfortable in their lot in life, just doing the bare minimum, lukewarm, the answer isn't to become cold to church and drop out, it is to become red hot for the Lord and heat things up. Be zealous! Add fire to your local assembly. Zeal is contagious. Humbly seek to serve God in the called out assembly, and watch it get red hot for the Lord. Go to church! Wrapping up this pre-Christmas series encouraging saved believers to join their local called out assembly, I want to add one last benefit to regular church attendance and membership in the local body; Every saved believer has a difficult time preaching to their loved ones, and getting friends and relatives saved. Matthew 13:54-58 And when he was come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this wisdom, and these mighty works? Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas? And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then hath this man all these things? And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house. And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief. Mark 6:4 But Jesus, said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. If the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God in the flesh had a hard time reaching those who knew Him best, it is natural that we do too. We all have shame at not being able to broach it with people who know us, especially if they knew us before we were saved. And while we may bring up salvation, and try to give them the gospel, they either don't want to hear it from you, or your own feelings get in the way. You might try winning them by your chaste conversation, by your behavior, but that is not as powerful as the meek and ready answer for the hope we have within us. Faith cometh by hearing the word of God after all. Homebound Christians have no remedy for this. But church-goers? Where the word is preached? There is a solution: Inviting them to services. Christmas, Easter, potluck, perhaps your own baptism, or just because. Most Baptist churches end with some form of gospel presentation, and even the few who don't end in an altar call preach enough of the word to prick the hearts of men. "Every head down, eyes closed, if you aren't sure today that you are saved, please raise your hand...I'd be happy to pray with you and talk with you about God's plan for salvation." It is an offer made by a man of God, preaching the word before a congregation of saved brethren all praying in that moment to open the hearts of those there who need it. It is a powerful thing.

And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars; Again, Jesus is addressing a church, this in Sardis, and He uses descriptors of Himself from scripture to sign the message. I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead. Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God. Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee. The church at Sardis has a reputation for being an active and lively congregation, but Jesus says He knows that's not the case. He warns them to return to what was preached unto them, that they won't die out completely. That His coming won't be a surprise to them, like a thief in the night overtaking them as He will the world of non-believers. Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy. His appeal then are to the genuinely saved among them in Sardis, encouraging them in their walk, and their reward in His return. And then, again another message to the saved, who have overcome the world by their faith in Him: He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches. The white raiment of the wedding feast, the garment we receive having been called by grace and accepting the invitation by faith. Whose names are not blotted out of the book of life. Note, we are born into the book of life, we are blotted out by death as unbelievers, or reprobation, or unpardonable sin such as blasphemy of the Holy Ghost, knowingly adding to or taking away from the word of God or, as we will see, taking the mark of the beast. No one in the Bible is added to the book of life, only blotted out and removed having already been there. Understanding of this helps when faced with a few false doctrines. Jesus promise to us who are saved is that He will confess our names before our Father, our counsel, the sole mediator we need. And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth; Jesus addresses the church at Philadelphia. Jesus is holy and true. He has the key of David, mentioned in Isaiah 22:22: And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open. To Him gave all the prophets witness. Also, don't miss this, Jesus opens the door of salvation to us as individual believers, and none may shut it. We have eternal life. It can't be lost or taken. But Christ Jesus also has the ability to shut the door, that none may open. This is reprobation, and it's a doctrine found throughout the Bible. Many find it difficult to accept or believe, but it is taught throughout scripture, clearly and with examples. Sadly today, many are offended at the concept. Jesus continues, praising them for their faith. Promising He's opened the door for them. Man has little strength. We cannot open that door ourselves, only His may. I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. The church in Philadelphia is being persecuted, like some of the others, and again it is the Jews. Jesus says they say they are Jews but are not. That they are liars. There are theories and interpretations as to what this means. Edomites? The Ashkenazi? Khazarians? These are earthly interpretations, with physical/genetic/ethnic implications. And they may very well be a marker that has some application. But what we know for certain, spiritually, that they who say they are Jews but are not, are spiritually Edom indeed. They are Esau, who sold their birthright, which has been taken by the Gentiles who are spiritually Jacob. Romans 2:28-29 For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God. For us, it is sufficient to understand that those who reject the Son have not the Father. That those who deny Jesus is the Christ are liars, and antichrists. By focusing on the spiritual application, it becomes inarguable that they who say they are Jews are not, but are liars. Without going down rabbi holes arguing about their origins and debates about genealogies. The word of God is sharper than any arguments of man, and discerns quickly exactly why they are not Jews; for if they kept the law of Moses and believed the prophets, they would believe Jesus is who He says He is. That He is the Christ. But we who are spiritually His, who are inwardly circumcised of the heart, we can take solace in our tribulations caused by the wicked Jew antichrists, that they are a synagogue of Satan and Jesus will make them worship at His feet and know that He loves us, His brothers and sisters who believed on His name. Who trusted God's word. Every knee shall bow and every tongue confess. Amen! Continuing to the Philadelphians; Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth. Behold, I come quickly: hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown. Jesus encourages them. They are doing well. Holdfast. Faint not. And as the temptation, the test of the deceiver, comes upon the world, they who remain patient and true will be protected from the deception. Note that Jesus encourages them to maintain their works and faith that they not lose crowns. Crowns are rewards in Heaven given to believers based on our works. They can be earned or lost. We are to be judged, every one of us, not of Heaven and Hell, but our works. Be they precious stones or wood, hay and stubble to be burned. 1 Corinthians 3:11-15 For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire. Pay close attention to this; he himself shall be saved, even if his works are burned up as not valuable to the Lord. But to each that has something that remains, to them is there a reckoning of reward. And again, more promises to the saved who have overcome in Christ: Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches. Amen. Amen. Amen! And unto the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write; These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God; The Amen! Jesus is the Amen, the 'let it be' of God. Verily. True. Through whom all things were created and through whom all things are fulfilled. Unto the Laodiceans. I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth. They are neither hot nor cold. They aren't doing much of anything for the Lord. A church that's lukewarm, does the bare minimum without any enthusiasm. Who haven't gone the way of dying off, apostasy, just grown cold to the truth of the word and aren't really living it. Comfortable. But this offense the Lord more than if they had just grown cold. Mailing it in is more offensive to God, and that's understandable. Many churches are this way. That is why the false doctrine of these churches representing ages claim we are living in the "Laodicean age." It's an easy comparison that allows a pastor to "rah rah" some life out of their members, but it being a false doctrine can lock congregations into complacency. "Sure the church isn't doing much, but it is the age we love in. Oh well." Meanwhile there are churches who are on fire for the Lord. There's always a remnant. 7000 who haven't bent the knee to Baal. And a dead or dying church can always be revived, this is the point of these messages from Christ Jesus Himself, to encourage and edify. Warn and chastise. But complacency is often found in comfort. Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see. Jesus is attacking that comfort. Saying they have physical wealth and are doing well, as many congregations are today, but they need to recognize they are poor; wretched and miserable. Blind to the word and naked in their sin. He says to buy Him gold tried in the fire, ala 1 Corinthians 3. Spiritual wealth, that comes from good works; spreading the Gospel, winning souls, caring for the least of us. Having the white raiment that comes from believing unto salvation and that covers our nakedness before God. Anointing their eyes with the word, being doers not just hearers, that they may see. And Jesus' harsh criticism is leveled against these churches out of love. As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent. Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me. Whom God loves, He chasteneth. Scourging every son. But the promise of His fellowship is such that any who open themself up towards Him, He shall come in unto. And His final message to the saved; To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches. Again, the promise to rule and reign with Him. Just as God has established Jesus Christ's throne, so too are we made heirs to the Kingdom, serving in the house of the Lord. Amen. We will study on Revelation 4 tomorrow, where the narrative shifts gears and John's visions take him before the throne in Heaven, setting the stage for the next section of the prophecy which runs through chapter 11. It gets pretty wild.

Daniel 7:9-14 I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire. A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened. I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld even till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame. As concerning the rest of the beasts, they had their dominion taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and time. I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him. And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed. The glory and Majesty of the Lord God, by Whom all things were made for His pleasure, and before whom we are not worthy. Who in His magnificent power and wisdom, is perfect and holy. And it is this same God, to whom only the hinder parts could be seen by mortal eyes, Who when He passed Moses could not bear to witness, and the flow of Moses face from being in His presence made the children of Israel turn away in shame. God who is worthy of praise and service. Serving with fear and trembling at His perfect will set before us in His word. So much so, our submission unto earthly hierarchy is done in submission to Him that set all things in the heavens and upon the earth, to please Him. As Christ, who thought it not blasphemy to declare Himself equal to God, submitted Himself to the will of the Father. So we must submit ourselves to doing what we are created for; giving pleasure to God. For Jesus is the equal of God, but submitted unto God, and there by was given glory and is exalted above everything: Philippians 2:6-11 Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. John 6:38-40 For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day. Ephesians 6:6-9 Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;With good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men: Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free. And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him. Submission to God is to do His will. His will is knowable in His word, and through His Spirit. In all things giving glory to God, knowing He is holy, and true. That we are created to give Him pleasure in all that we do. To honor Him as He is honored in Heaven. Hallowed be His name. For who are we? Where we there when He placed the stars in the heavens and made the leviathan? When the lightning was formed and the thunder of His wrath was made? God, appearing in a whirlwind to Job asks similar questions of righteous Job. He asks these things of the created who is questioning his Creator. And Job, having been subject to this glory of God and His Majesty, replies; Job 42:1-6 Then Job answered the Lord, and said, I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee. Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not. Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes. Husbands submit to Christ. Pastors submit to Christ. Wives submitting to husbands are submitting to Christ. Children honoring parents are submitting to Christ. Servants working diligently are submitting to Christ. Masters, or bosses, who rule justly are submitting to Christ, members of a nation submitting to authority do so, as they are serving Christ. And in all things Christ submitted to God the Father, that He may be given the world as His footstool, and exalted above all of creation. We Christians often approach the Bible with a "what is in it for me" attitude. From our salvation to our sanctification, to our separation. And mostly to our sin and compromise and rationalizing. Of doing the bare minimum in every thing, because we have to. Not with joy in service of the Lord God. We dread work, family obligations, being hospitable and neighborly. Avoiding commitments and shirking responsibilities, and rationalize it with our "works," we pray, we go to church, we read the Bible, we share the Gospel. We do that which is expected to varying degrees and with minimal enthusiasm, not to please God but to be seen of men, to justify being slack in other areas of life. Instead we should submit to serving God in everything. Who is holy and Whose glory we cannot see without falling down in repentance and fear and trembling, worshiping Him. As the angels in Heaven do without ceasing, we should serve God upon His throne, as glad servants to Him. In everything we do. For He is Holy, so we should be holy. Because it is pleasing to God.

Revelation 4 begins the shift in focus from the things that are, the then current day churches in Asia Minor, to the things which must be hereafter. Setting the scene, John, who is taken in the spirit and shown a throne in Heaven, and the radiant glory of the Lord upon His throne, and 4 creatures whose role is to give Him thanks and praise, as well as 24 elders, in seats surrounding the throne, given crowns themselves which they throw at the Lord's feet, saying "Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honor and power" for being creator of all things, and the reminder that it is for His pleasure that all things exist. Amen. This is a picture of Heaven. This is the throne before which we who are saved will bow and worship. Where the crowns we receive for the works worthy of reward will be cast before Jesus, the king of kings. As to the beasts, each stationed at the 4 points of the throne, their description is similar to the vision given Ezekiel: Ezekiel 1 5 Also out of the midst thereof came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance; they had the likeness of a man. 6 And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings. 7 And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass. 8 And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and they four had their faces and their wings. 9 Their wings were joined one to another; they turned not when they went; they went every one straight forward. 10 As for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face of a man, and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle. 11 Thus were their faces: and their wings were stretched upward; two wings of every one were joined one to another, and two covered their bodies. 12 And they went every one straight forward: whither the spirit was to go, they went; and they turned not when they went. 13 As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of lamps: it went up and down among the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went forth lightning. 14 And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning. These beasts had six wings. In Isaiah 6:, we are told that two wings cover their face, two wings cover their feet, and two wings were used to fly. Also, in Isaiah 6:1-4, that they praise the Lord continually: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly. And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory. Ezekiel 10 10 And as for their appearances, they four had one likeness, as if a wheel had been in the midst of a wheel. 11 When they went, they went upon their four sides; they turned not as they went, but to the place whither the head looked they followed it; they turned not as they went. 12 And their whole body, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes round about, even the wheels that they four had. 13 As for the wheels, it was cried unto them in my hearing, O wheel. 14 And every one had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle. 15 And the cherubims were lifted up. This is the living creature that I saw by the river of Chebar. 16 And when the cherubims went, the wheels went by them: and when the cherubims lifted up their wings to mount up from the earth, the same wheels also turned not from beside them. 17 When they stood, these stood; and when they were lifted up, these lifted up themselves also: for the spirit of the living creature was in them. These cherubims are consistent with John's own vision. The praise of the cherubim, saying Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, note that the three holy's, signifying that the Lord God is separate and unique of all things, special, is repeated three times, not just for emphasis in my opinion. But the very nature of God being the Father, Son and Spirit. He which was, and is, and is to come. Was, before creation, is now, and is to come in the eternal Kingdom of the Lord. And the praise of those in white raiment, with crowns, the elders before the throne who worship Him, saying Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power. This is without question the undeniable glory He deserves which we, in our flesh often neglect and find ourselves distracted by the cares of this world. But in the next, unrestrained by sin and fear, we will be able to give proper praise and understanding of creation; that it was always for Him, and His pleasure. We have the gift of fellowship with Him, to enjoy the wonders of it all. That's a heady thing to consider in the eternal life to come. Some additional Revelation 4 notes, particularly on heresy. Pre-trib rapture dispensationalists will use the taking up of John to Heaven to claim this is the secret rapture, that not only John but all the saved, are gathered at verse 1. They have to point to this event, because the following chapter, Revelation 5, begins the opening of the seals and the tribulation that follows. But Revelation 4:1-2 says nothing about the gathering of the elect (we will see that it is immediately after the tribulation, when the sun and moon are darkened). After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven: and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet talking with me; which said, Come up hither, and I will shew thee things which must be hereafter. And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. This is not the bodily resurrection of the saved, glorified unto God and gathered on the day of redemption. It is John, alone and in the spirit. Pre-trib rapture is a foolish doctrine. Another heresy justified out of Revelation 4, the vain and repetitive prayers offered by Catholics. Jesus tells us in Matthew 6:7; But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. Many Catholics will point to the praise given "without ceasing" by the 4 seraphim, the creatures before the throne of the Lord as a nullifying text that contradicts Jesus' instruction to us on prayer, and so repetitive speed-muttering "Hail Mary's" and the occasional "Our Father" until they become a mush of words used as an incantation to their idols they worship kneeling before them, is ok. It's preposterous. We shall praise the Lord without ceasing but that's not vain repetitions, but giving honor and glory to Christ. In prayer here, in this life, we should follow the model of conversational praise, gratitude and petition laid out by Jesus, in the manner described. Another heresy is the idea that when we die bodily, that our soul sleeps or something, rather than being in the presence of the Lord as the Bible says in 2 Corinthians 5 that to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord, and we see that there are men, in Heaven, the 24 Elders for example. (They are not the only souls in Heaven as we will see moving forward in Revelation) We can also dismiss the wicked heresy of gnosticism, that "matter is all evil," because we see, again, scripture has a different idea of creation, that God looked upon what He made and it was good. Here in Revelation 4 we see it in the praise given by the elders; for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created. The Lord God does not take pleasure in the wicked. Isaiah 6 In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple. 2 Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly. 3 And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory. 4 And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke. 5 Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts. Ezekiel 1 22 And the likeness of the firmament upon the heads of the living creature was as the colour of the terrible crystal, stretched forth over their heads above. 23 And under the firmament were their wings straight, the one toward the other: every one had two, which covered on this side, and every one had two, which covered on that side, their bodies. 24 And when they went, I heard the noise of their wings, like the noise of great waters, as the voice of the Almighty, the voice of speech, as the noise of an host: when they stood, they let down their wings. 25 And there was a voice from the firmament that was over their heads, when they stood, and had let down their wings. 26 And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it. 27 And I saw as the colour of amber, as the appearance of fire round about within it, from the appearance of his loins even upward, and from the appearance of his loins even downward, I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and it had brightness round about. 28 As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spake. Exodus 33 17 And the Lord said unto Moses, I will do this thing also that thou hast spoken: for thou hast found grace in my sight, and I know thee by name. 18 And he said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory. 19 And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before thee; and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy. 20 And he said, Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.

1 Peter 2 9 But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; 10 Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy. Psalms 56:8 Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book? Psalm 141:1-2 Lord, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee. Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice. Proverbs 15:8 The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the upright is his delight. Revelation 8:4 And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angel's hand. Our prayers are like incense, sweet smelling to the Lord. Our tears, He collects in vials. We will see the significance of that soon. The beasts and elders teach us a new song, the glory and praise of Jesus Christ at the moment that the book telling the final act, is to be opened. Each seal revealing more. The book cannot be opened by any man; on the earth, in Heaven above or in Hell beneath. Only the Lion of Judah, the root of David. We recently saw this promise of there being the savior out of Judah, compared to a lion, in the blessings given out by Israel to his sons in Genesis 49. The only other mention of this descriptor of Jesus. He is called the "root of David," which is a sign of His being before David was. The beginning and end. Alpha and Omega. Jesus is worthy. And we shall fall down and worship Him forever. The new song they sang; Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation; And hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign on the earth. We see the promise made to us as a holy nation, a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, as mentioned in 1 Peter 2, is part of that song. The promise that we be made heirs to the kingdom. Kings of God fit to rule the earth with Him. Amen. But only He is worthy. Our redemption made by His blood. Out of every kindred, tongue, people and nation. Elect to the promise made by God, through Christ before the foundation of the world.

And so the seven seals of the Great Tribulation are unsealed by the Lord Christ Jesus, and at each a portion of the book is opened to reveal to John what is to come. And he beheld a white horse, and a man, given a crown and carrying a bow who went forth conquering and to conquer. This is the Antichrist. A leader given power and taking more, riding on a white horse, an imitation of Christ. The Antichrist, and the many antichrists we are to expect in these, the last days, are not only opposed to the true Christ, but come in His place, using messianic claims and imagery. Here it's given that he will be riding a white horse, symbolic of the coming of Christ, so as to fool everyone who is not saved. His weapon, a bow, showing he is a man of war. His goal will be a one world government, a return to the sin of Babel. In Talmudic Judaism, especially the eschatology of Chabad Lubavitch, their moshiach or "Messiah" will come as a man who is made a king of war who conquers the world, establishing a throne in Jerusalem. Because they literally worship the Beast of the Antichrist. Satan who gives him power. The second seal is opened and the red horse of war is loosed upon the earth, Jesus breaks the third seal, and John sees revealed in the book a black horse; and he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand. This is famine. The voice John hears is like a snippet out of time saying "A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny; and see thou hurt not the oil and the wine." This is usually interpreted to mean that common commodities, flours of wheat and barley, would be very expensive, a measure, which is a small amount enough to make a single load would cost a penny, which in the Bible usually refers to a days wage for labor. Taking care not to hurt, or spill or waste, the even-more expensive oil and wine. The fourth seal is opened, and John is shown a pale horse; and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. This is often called pestilence, but it isn't only disease, but all manner of death, flowing from the first 3 horsemen, the Conqueror, the war and the famine. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth. This is the Great Tribulation preached on by Jesus. From Matthew 24, we see the same order of things: 3 And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world? 4 And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. 5 For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many. The white horse, the conqueror, the false Christ, deceiving many. This is the first seal. 6 And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. 7 For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places. The second seal, the red horse of war. The third seal, famine, and the fourth seal, death. The sword and hunger and pestilence and earthquakes, all causing mass death. And Jesus says "this is the beginning of sorrows." And then, back in Revelation, we see the 5th seal opened, and John is shown an altar in Heaven, and under the altar, standing before the Lord, are the souls of the martyrs who were slain for the Word of God. For their testimony that Jesus is Christ, that God's promise is true. Again, in Matthew 24: 9 Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. 10 And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. The events revealed in the seals tracking what Jesus gave as signs that the Apostles be not deceived. 15 When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:) 16 Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains Jerusalem is conquered, Jesus shifts from the "thees" and "ye's" of believers to "they" and "them" of the Jews in Jerusalem fleeing to the mountains. The abomination of desolation set up before them. (These are the days of vengeance, and we will talk about that more in the second half of Revelation) But continuing the narrative from Revelation 6, the 6th seal is opened and we are shown there is a great earthquake and the sun and moon are darkened. The stars falling from the heavens. Matthew 24: 29 Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: 30 And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. 31 And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other. Immediately AFTER THE TRIBULATION the sun and moon are darkened and the elect are gathered unto Jesus, returning in the clouds. The rapture. The timing of it is plain and we see it reflected here (and in Revelation 7) but back to the narrative of chapter 6: And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand? So we see that in Matthew 24, (also Luke 21 and Mark 13 for parallel passages) that the timeline for tribulation and the Great Tribulation line up with Revelation. It's interesting that the only Gospel that does not have the Olivet discourse, Jesus preaching end times prophecy, is the Gospel of John. Instead he is given an entire book of revelations from Christ. The day of the Lord, Christ's return to gather the elect and the beginning of the wrath to come, poured out on the earth has begun. I don't have time now to go over the significance of the day of the Lord. How it is mentioned throughout scripture and always is accompanied by the sun and moon darkening, and a great shout heard by all. A return visible to the whole world. And the wrath that follows. But suffice to say that the secret pre-trib rapture, that Jesus sneaks in and quietly disappears the saved so that they don't experience the wars, famine, pestilence, earthquakes and Great Tribulation of being persecuted for His sake, is a wicked heresy out of the pits of Hell. In the next chapter we will see from John's vantage in Heaven that the raptured saints appear by the multitudes before the throne. After the first six seals are opened. After the tribulation of those days. The 7th seal has yet to be opened....

After the sealing of the 144,000, we see the raptured souls of the saint appear in Heaven before the throne of the Lord. After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands; And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb. This is the day of redemption. The gathering of the elect on the great and terrible day of the Lord. Again note the order. They arrive after the tribulation, after the 6 seals, on the day of the Lord. Before the wrath, which only comes after the 7th seal is opened. It is a post-trib, pre-wrath rapture. Some false doctrine states that this chapter is out of sequence with 6 and 8. That it happens at a different time, or that it's some kind of separate vision. They have to to make their false doctrine of pre-trib or post-wrath rapture fit the narrative's timeline. But chapter 7 opens with "And after these things.." which places it firmly in sequential order to chapter 6. Verse 9 continues the timeline with "After this .." all one narrative. But finally, who are the mixed multitudes, of every kindred and tongue, who suddenly appear before the throne in white linen, praising and worshiping the Savior? Of this there is no question, for John is told: And one of the elders answered, saying unto me, What are these which are arrayed in white robes? and whence came they? And I said unto him, Sir, thou knowest. And he said to me, These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.Therefore are they before the throne of God, and serve him day and night in his temple: and he that sitteth on the throne shall dwell among them. They are the saints, the believers who came out of the great tribulation, saved by the return of Jesus, gathering His elect. There is no doubt that can be had that this should put the pre-trib (and post-wrath, preterist, amillennial, post millennial, "rapture isn't in the Bible!" "It's symbolic!") nonsense heresies to bed. And we are given the greatest of encouragements, the blessed hope we can count on as saved, born again believers; They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat. For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes. Amen!

So, to catch up, in chapter 6 the first 6 seals were opened, and the great tribulation came upon the earth with the rise of a great conqueror, wars and famine and mass death. The persecution of the saints was great, and they cried out in Heaven, having been killed for Jesus name, that God's wrath be poured out. They were told by the Lord to wait a little season, a short while longer. Finally, in the midst of the great tribulation, the sun and moon are darkened and the great and terrible day of the Lord has come. In chapter 7, from John's vantage point in Heaven he hears God stay the hand of the angels who are holding back the four winds. There are 144,000 made up of the tribes of Israel sent to Earth, sealed in their foreheads as protection from the wrath, and a mixed multitude of millions of saints, from every nation and tongue, appear before the throne, gathered by the angels at Jesus Christ's coming in the clouds. They honor and worship their savior. And now, in chapter 8 the 7th seal is finally opened, and the 7 trumpet judgments begin; the wrath of God pouring out on the inhabitants left on Earth. Jeremiah 16 16 Behold, I will send for many fishers, saith the LORD, and they shall fish them; and after will I send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of the holes of the rocks. 17 For mine eyes are upon all their ways: they are not hid from my face, neither is their iniquity hid from mine eyes. 18 And first I will recompense their iniquity and their sin double; because they have defiled my land, they have filled mine inheritance with the carcases of their detestable and abominable things. There is recompense for sin. God demands payment.

The 5th and 6th trumpet sound, bringing the first two woes; Locust-creatures from Hell and the horsemen from Hell led by angels, to torment and slay mankind for its wicked ways. And mankind repented not. As the 5th trumpet sounds, we are told of a star, an angel, that falls from the Heavens to earth, who has the key to Hell, and opens the fiery abyss to free the locust-like creatures to torment mankind. He is identified by John in the Hebrew as "Abaddon," in the Greek, "Apollyon," which means "Destroyer." But who is Abaddon? Many interpreters say this is Satan, fallen to earth and loosening the beasts of Hell to destroy the unbelieving, but the context given in Revelation creates some issues with this, primarily Revelation 20:1-3: And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season. See the problem? Also, we know that at the Resurrection, Jesus Himself had the keys to Hell and Death. Would He give them over to that old serpent? Seems unlikely. And, again, we are witnessing God's wrath with the 7 trumpet judgments, these woes poured upon the earth, and so in all things here, these plagues and the angels who are ministering them, are doing so as servants of God. This is why, in my opinion, Abaddon is the angel of death. An angel of destruction, working in service to God, and not Satan. And maybe we have seen the "destroyer" doing God's bidding before; 1 Chronicles 21:15 And God sent an angel unto Jerusalem to destroy it: and as he was destroying, the LORD beheld, and he repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed, It is enough, stay now thine hand. And the angel of the LORD stood by the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite. And, perhaps most famously in Exodus 12:23: For the Lord will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you. This is the destroyer. The angel of death. And to him was given the key to Hell, unleashing the nightmarish beasts, with the power to torment men a span of 5 months, was given unto him. Note the sealed 144,000 are spared the wrath and the woes. And the remaining trees and vegetation, the earth itself is spared. These woes are against man. And the 6th trumpet sounds and there appears the four angels which are bound in the great river Euphrates. These 4 angels are followed by two hundred million cavalrymen, riding horses with heads of fire-breathing lions and tails like snakes. And they proceed to kill a third of mankind, making war with the armies of man under control of the beast and the false prophet. Again, many will say that this is the army of Satan, loosed out of Hell, and that the 4 angels bound are devils, fallen and kept in Hell. But there are problems with this. Joel 2 contains a prophecy that pictures these end times events, and clearly the army is God's: Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of the Lord cometh, for it is nigh at hand; 2 A day of darkness and of gloominess, a day of clouds and of thick darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it, even to the years of many generations. 3 A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them. 4 The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so shall they run. 5 Like the noise of chariots on the tops of mountains shall they leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devoureth the stubble, as a strong people set in battle array. 6 Before their face the people shall be much pained: all faces shall gather blackness. 7 They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks: 8 Neither shall one thrust another; they shall walk every one in his path: and when they fall upon the sword, they shall not be wounded. 9 They shall run to and fro in the city; they shall run upon the wall, they shall climb up upon the houses; they shall enter in at the windows like a thief. 10 The earth shall quake before them; the heavens shall tremble: the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining: 11 And the Lord shall utter his voice before his army: for his camp is very great: for he is strong that executeth his word: for the day of the Lord is great and very terrible; and who can abide it? In the remaining verses of the chapter, God calls on the people facing His wrath, the unbelieving, those worshipping false gods and idols, to turn towards Him and repent. To be saved and given respite from His terrible wrath. These angels are servants of God. The army is His. Satan never has control over Hell. He never reigns there in scripture. The Bible says those tormented in Hell do so in the presence of the Lord. Judgment is His. These may be dark sayings and difficult to hear, and the interpretation of the symbolism and literal events being shown the prophets and John may have multiple meanings, short and long term implications, dual fulfilment, etc...But there can be no doubt that this is entirely of God. Not Satan, whose power is only through the men he may deceive, and the temptations and snares of sin he can convince us of in this world. Not of Heaven, not of Hell. The Bible says Satan is the prince of this world, not the prince of Hell. The rest of chapter 2 of Joel is heavy in end times Bible prophecy, and worth looking at here; 12 Therefore also now, saith the Lord, turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning: 13 And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil. 14 Who knoweth if he will return and repent, and leave a blessing behind him; even a meat offering and a drink offering unto the Lord your God? 15 Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly: 16 Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts: let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet. 17 Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God? 18 Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people. 19 Yea, the Lord will answer and say unto his people, Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and ye shall be satisfied therewith: and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: 20 But I will remove far off from you the northern army, and will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, and his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things. 21 Fear not, O land; be glad and rejoice: for the Lord will do great things. 22 Be not afraid, ye beasts of the field: for the pastures of the wilderness do spring, for the tree beareth her fruit, the fig tree and the vine do yield their strength. 23 Be glad then, ye children of Zion, and rejoice in the Lord your God: for he hath given you the former rain moderately, and he will cause to come down for you the rain, the former rain, and the latter rain in the first month. 24 And the floors shall be full of wheat, and the vats shall overflow with wine and oil. 25 And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you. 26 And ye shall eat in plenty, and be satisfied, and praise the name of the Lord your God, that hath dealt wondrously with you: and my people shall never be ashamed. 27 And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed. 28 And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions: 29 And also upon the servants and upon the handmaids in those days will I pour out my spirit. 30 And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke. 31 The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord come. 32 And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call. The Bible tells us that The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance. Even in His wrath and judgment upon the Earth, He seeks repentance of those being afflicted for their wicked hearts. And as we see in Revelation 9, despite the supernatural destruction, the signs and wonders in Heaven, the resurrection of the dead and gathering in the clouds of the elect, the woes and all, the men of the earth will still refuse.
