Wise as serpents, harmless as doves

Matthew 10:16 Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. Many Christians often fall into the trap of being harmless as doves, while failing to be wise as serpents. We tend to feel the need to show Grace and to try to bridge peace and avoid conflict in every situation. To be as sheep in both mind and spirit. But the wolves take advantage of this. Jesus says to be as wise as serpents. To understand the context and nature of those who come into our lives and exert a negative influence. Part of the problem is that we don't attempt to discern the intents of the heart of the person who we are dealing with. Sometimes they'll say something that has a grain of truth, and in the interest of fairness and to seem reasonable, we will validate their premise. But their premise may be in bad faith. They may not be seeking a dialogue and to come to an understanding. Their intent is to throw bombs. Sow discord. To validate slander in the interest of promoting their own agenda. Even those who come in, in error, weak in the faith, maybe confused or wrong on some doctrinal point, or turned around by something they've heard that you know is wrong, we are warned against giving them space to stay in error and to spread it. Romans 14:1 Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations. Yes we should cater to those who are ignorant, or convicted about something that isn't explicitly taught in the Bible, and we should attempt to correct them in love. But when they come in with doubtful disputations, that is creating turmoil and breaking the unity of the brotherhood of saints? Him we should not receive. Part of the problem often stems from the fact that we can't imagine how evil people might behave. We cut them slack. We give them grace based on our own conscience's sake, and show them kindness and mercy that only encourages and emboldens them. If they're simply in error, and too prideful or ignorant to accept rebuke, after you've admonished them kindly, shake the dust. Titus 3:10 A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; This is especially true at the door when you are out soul winning. It does no one any good to get bogged down in the doubtful disputation. Defending yourself against a false accusation built on bad faith premises does nothing but legitimize the other person's point. If someone accused you of being incestuous with your mother, your reaction should not be "I am not!" it should be "You're wicked!" You don't defend yourself from slander by reasoning with the slanderer. You identify them for what they're doing, and rebuke them. But the issue becomes entertaining these sowers of division in a house of God or in a space of fellowship. Not throwing them out at the first sign of their behavior. What that does is allow their contention to grow, and to draw others in to deal with it. Further you encourage those sheep who aren't as wise as serpents, to compromise with the truth in order to bring peace to the situation. To try to smooth things over. To debate the slander as a point with merit. This only encourages wolves and keeps the confused and weak-in-the-faith brother, in error. God hates those who sow division. Proverbs 6:14–19 Frowardness is in his heart, he deviseth mischief continually; he soweth discord. Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; suddenly shall he be broken without remedy. These six things doth the LORD hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren. We as Christians have absolutely no obligation to give them a platform to do the things that God hates, but rather to expel them and turn them over to Satan. If they are saved believers, God will deal with it. But the Bible says we are to treat them as heathen. Matthew 18:16–17 But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established. And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican. You should not allow someone free rein to spew lies and indignities, to overthrow the faith of some. Grace without discernment isn't biblical peace; it is a vulnerability that wolves exploit. 2 Timothy 2:16–18 But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness. And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus; Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some. It doesn't matter if the vain babblings are denying the future resurrection of saints, slandering men of God and their works, discouraging the first love of the faith, soul-winning, or teaching a false gospel that says men are made elect by their genealogy. It increases ungodliness among the brethren and overthrows the faith of some.

Proverbs 7:18–20 Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves. For the goodman is not at home, he is gone a long journey: He hath taken a bag of money with him, and will come home at the day appointed. Matthew 24:42–44 Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come. But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up. Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh. Christians are called to watch for the return of Christ, being good and faithful servants, and not letting the delay of His return lull us into sin. Matthew 24:46–51 Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing. Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods. But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; And shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of, And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. This is why we preach separation unto the Gospel, being a holy people and working to do the will of the Lord, so that when we are found approved in that day. But the evil servant is like the foolish woman, calling others to sin. Mark 13:33–37 Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is. For the Son of man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch. Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping. And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.
Tradition against the commandment of God

Matthew 15:3–8 But he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition. Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. If you're against the death penalty for murders while Jesus was for it for those that curse their parents, you ain't right.
The peace of God keeps the heart

Colossians 3:15–17 And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him. Philippians 4:6–7 Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. Isaiah 26:2–3 Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in. Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee. The Lord keeps those whose mind stays on Him, Whom they have trusted. God keeps your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. No matter what you call this, it is a promise of God. Let God be true and every man a liar!

Side note. When we don't sin and we follow the law to the best of our human ability and we love our neighbors and our brothers and sisters in Christ, and we forgive others, we are doing the bare minimum. It's our reasonable service. Luke 17:7–10 But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat? And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink? Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not. So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do. Of course we're going to receive rewards that have been promised to us for doing great works for Christ. And while I don't know exactly, I would imagine some of the things that we were commanded to do will produce rewards. Crowns in the next life. But the things that we're commanded to do are the bare minimum. I suppose it's the heart behind the things that we do, rather than the simple obedience that God looks at and rewards. I think God gives credit for effort, context and the spirit it was done in. I think Paul's warning about the wood, wood and stubble getting burnt up and suffering loss, is because there will be things that we absolutely expect to receive a reward for that ultimately were just our reasonable service. And we are going to receive crowns of Glory for acts that we didn't even consider were reward-worthy at the time. Things that Jesus looks at and says this was precious stones, silver or gold. Things where He will say well done my good and faithful servant, that we don't remember doing. Matthew 25:35–40 For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. While we are promised rewards, and it's often discussed the nature of them and how they are earned and what qualifies as precious stone or silver or gold, it's the little acts of love where Christ's light shines through us and others glorify God, where his mercy and his grace is magnified through the acts that we do simply because we are children of God, without any thought for ourselves. In fact, it's very likely that the things we expect a reward for will be burned and we will suffer loss, but it will be the times we unknowingly entertained angels, offered comfort and gave hospitality to the hopeless that will be judged worthy, on that day.
The Bema seat and wood, hay and stubble

At the Bema Seat, "bad" or wood, hay and stubble, does not mean God pulls out a list of your confessed or covered sins to punish you for them. It means he evaluates the things you did that were worthless for the Kingdom. Things like time wasted (arguing online👀), fleshly ambitions (popularity), or religious works done for the praise of men. Those works are burned up, resulting in a loss of reward, not a infliction of punishment.
The angel of the LORD and Sennacherib

2 Kings 19:35–36 And it came to pass that night, that the angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses. So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh. When Jerusalem was surrounded and under siege, is likely when Psalm 44 was written and sung. 2 Kings 19:32–34 Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it. By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD. For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake. It is always interesting to see that it was the preservation of Jerusalem itself and the promise made to David that motivated God to act. King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah tore their clothes, humbled themselves, and cried out to God in intense prayer for deliverance. The sons of Korah wrote and sang Psalms. The people lamented and prayed. But, what seems to have motivated Him wasn't necessarily His people. God considered His pleasure, promises and plans, and relented, confounding and destroying the army before the gates. It pleased Him to defend the city, to save it, for His own sake, and the promise He had made. Many times, our effectual and fervent prayers are answered, and God delivers us out of mercy and grace. But sometimes, it is His pleasure, promises and plans that He responds to. It is something to keep in mind as we look to do His will and take joy in it being done.

TL:DR - Believers cannot apostasize and apostates cannot believe Hebrews 6:7–9 For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned. Here, the Bible gives us the parable to explain the apostasy verses that came before it. The same rains and earth are given to both the dressed fields that bring forth herbs also brings forth thorns and briers, rejected and cast into the fire. This directly applies to those that tasted of the truth, but did not consume, who see the power of the Spirit but never trusted the truth. They are the thorns and briers. The saved are the herbs meet for the dresser (the fruit of those who won them to Christ). The ground that bears thorns isn't good soil that "lost" its status; it is bad ground whose true nature was finally exposed by the rain. The parable explains the concept beautifully. It does not say the herbs become thorns, let alone that briers eventually are turned to fruit. And so Paul, having explained this concept, reassures the believers he is writing to. Hebrews 6:9 But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak. And worse, when presented with context of their proofs, that show that the cherry-picked eisegesis is wrong, and why, they just dig in their heels and act like fools. Clowns.

Romans 1:18–23 For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. That which may be known of God is made manifest by His wrath revealed from Heaven. Man has no excuse. Many have this understanding, the law written in their hearts and the conviction of the Spirit, and the wonder of creation and even the example of mercy towards the saved believer...and still don't repent towards the gospel, perishing in their sins. But these people being described know the truth of God and hold it in unrighteousness. They do not wish to retain God in their knowledge. They reject the truth for a lie. They worship themselves and the created over the Creator. And God gives them up to a reprobate (rejected) mind. For those that not only had the manifest truth of God, but a clear articulation of the gospel of grace and reconciliation through faith in Christ Jesus, understand it, and even profess to assent to it, and then reject it? They are worse off than those that simply never hear or consider it. These have forsaken the right way; 2 Peter 2:17 These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. The apostates are reprobate, twice-dead. Not only dead and hellbound in the next world, but conscience seared and accursed in this one. 2 Peter 2:21 For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. But we who have trusted the truth in our hearts have a more sure hope. We have the Spirit of truth to defend us from the spirit of error. Jesus said it is impossible to fool the elect. But for the fallen away, God gives them strong delusions as punishment for their rejection of the truth. 2 Thessalonians 2:10–12 And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness. But praise God this is not possible for a believer. We are kept from falling by the power of God. By the witness of the Spirit. By the perfect work of Christ, knowing we have not believed in vain. Jude 1:24–25 Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen. Regarding the lie that those who are saved CAN fall away, can believe a strong delusion, can be fooled, the Bible teaches this is not possible. 1 John 2:18–27 Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time. They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us. But ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things. I have not written unto you because ye know not the truth, but because ye know it, and that no lie is of the truth. Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son. Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also. Let that therefore abide in you, which ye have heard from the beginning. If that which ye have heard from the beginning shall remain in you, ye also shall continue in the Son, and in the Father. And this is the promise that he hath promised us, even eternal life. These things have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you. But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him. John continues; 1 John 4:1–6 Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world. Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world. Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world. They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and the world heareth them. We are of God: he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us. Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error. This is the unction of the holy Spirit. This Spirit of truth. That we hear those of God and reject those heard of the world by their false teaching. John 10:1–5 Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber. But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep. To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out. And when he putteth forth his own sheep, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice. And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers. We who are saved WILL NOT FOLLOW the stranger. We hear Jesus' voice. This is the promise of God. John 10:26–30 But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father’s hand. I and my Father are one. It is impossible for a saved child of God to fall away into apostasy. The trust in a false way, after knowing and assenting to the truth in their hearts. And it is impossible for an apostate to ever be saved once they've rejected the truth. Hebrews 6:4–6 For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. Anyone teaching that saved believers can reject the truth, believe a lie, have strong delusion, and apostasize, is wrong. It's heresy. It is not possible. Just as it is not possible for one who went out from us, who held the truth in unrighteousness and didn't wish to retain God in their knowledge, to ever come to the knowledge of the truth. The Bible warns repeatedly against false prophets, false teachers who try to lead away people with itching ears by their vain jangling. Creeping unawares in order to spy out our liberty, and to make merchandise of us. Just like Satan, they try to make you doubt God's word in order to get you to sin. Or to believe foolishness. A saved believer can be led away into believing some heresies that are couched in the truth. These heresies are not necessarily apostasy. In order for it to be apostasy, it has to change the truth of God into a lie. Not all heresies are damnable. Not all heresies force someone to become apostates by their adopting them as a school of thought or a systematic that they apply to or over their existing faith. Nor does a heart that is no longer perfect towards God, but has added other elements of worship into their true faith, make someone an apostate. Yes they are not right and yes they are backslidden and yes they will face the chastening of God, but they have not lost their salvation. Theologians call adding falsehoods or heresies to true faith syncretism. Solomon was guilty of this. He never rejected the Lord God or the temple he was given to build or the covenant and sacrifices that represented the Christ to come. But his heart was turned away to other gods by the love of his wives, partaking in their idolatry in addition to the truth he held in his heart. This applies to saved believers who use terms like repent of your sins, or who believe in some of the elements of Calvinism and predestination. Or who get caught up in other false doctrines, or never fully abandon the religion that they were won out of. It may apply to someone who trusted in Christ at the door when a soul winner came and presented the gospel to them, but out of habit and loyalty and family ties they continue on going to a Catholic Church for example. Naaman was a Syrian general who asked the Lord for forgiveness for entering an idol's temple with his king, after believing on the truth of God. 2 Kings 5:18 In this thing the LORD pardon thy servant, that when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaneth on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow down myself in the house of Rimmon, the LORD pardon thy servant in this thing. He had full knowledge of what he was doing and understood that it was wrong. I would assume Solomon did too, knowing the punishment he received through his son and the divided Kingdom for his spiritual adultery. But there are thousands and thousands of saved believers who after trusting in God, and the blood of Christ, neglect to walk in the Spirit, and read the Bible and learn God's ways. Those who simply went back to their Catholic church or their Mormon church or whatever apostate cult they were in, and while it may prick them in the heart they might not recognize why. But what they'll never do is trust in the false gospel of that church. Just as Naaman never trusted in the false gods of his people ever again. And I think it's curious that this current heresy - that a saved believer could apostasize and could believe a false gospel in their heart, or reject the truth of God utterly, has been creeping up over the past few years. It's a twist on Arianism, which holds that a saved believer can become apostate and lose salvation. By adding the assurance of salvation to it, it allows them to lead away babes in Christ or people who aren't fully trusting the truth, and give them cover to chase after delusions. A believer they lead away with this vein jangling won't lose their salvation obviously. They also won't come to believe a lie ultimately because they can't. But they'll introduce doubt and they'll give a bad testimony and when the false teacher can get baby Christians to slander men of God, soul-winning efforts, the teaching of Truth, they ultimately hurt the cause of Christ. But a nominal Christian, someone who has not fully believed unto salvation, it allows them to continue in whatever lie they are holding on to to avoid repentance. And it softens them up to be led away by whatever other strange doctrine the false teacher decides to impart upon their proselytes. He makes them twofold more the child of Hell than themselves. These false teachers are attempting to have it both ways. They use the comforting banner of "Once Saved, Always Saved" as a Trojan horse to smuggle in a license for total apostasy, claiming a person can completely deny Christ, turn to paganism, or become an atheist, and that God will simply override their will and force them to believe in the end. This teaching collapses under the weight of Scripture for several critical reasons. It redefines Faith as a meaningless past transaction, that purchased salvation, Rather than treating belief as a state of being. It becomes a transient action in their minds, rather than the reality their heart would live in if they believe the truth. Of course we reject Calvinism, so there is no forcing of faith or salvation onto someone who has utterly rejected it. The Bible says they're ever learning and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. Jesus says depart for me I never knew you. It invents a class of people that the Bible doesn't say exists. There is a binary of those who believe and those who are condemned already because they have not believed. There is no third option. They purposefully overlook the power of the Holy Spirit and His purpose, to seal the believer, guide us to all truth and show the spirit of error. While that doesn't rise to the level of blaspheming the Holy Spirit, in my opinion, it sure does come close.

When a Catholic tells you you don't understand what "worship means" they are actually changing the meaning of the word to obfuscate their idolatry. The Hebrew term (שָׁחָה / shachah) is used 172 times in the Old Testament - translated as “worship” 99 times, “bow” 31, “bow down” 18, “obeisance” 9, “reverence” 5, “fall down” 3. Defined as to depress/prostrate oneself (especially in homage to a superior, royalty, or God) i.e., to bow, kneel, or fall down in respect and deference. The primary Greek term (proskuneō) accounts for the great majority of NT occurrences of “worship” (60 times) and is defined as "to fall upon the knees, touch the ground with the forehead/kneel or prostrate oneself" in homage or obeisance (whether to express respect or make supplication). Exodus 20:4–5 Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me The term is explicitly rendered as "bow" in the 2nd Commandment, and carries with it no qualifiers or anything indicating that the "level of honor" given when bowing and making supplication to an image or idol has any bearing when considering the commandment. There is no question that bowing before an image or idol, regardless of what it is meant to represent, is strictly forbidden. Deuteronomy 5:7–10 Thou shalt have none other gods before me. Thou shalt not make thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the waters beneath the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself unto them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me, And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments. There is no mention of special religious worship for images of God, versus images of men, where it is allowed. Jeroboam created a new religion for Israel, with images of golden calves that were meant to represent the Lord God of Israel, and God destroyed them for it: 1 Kings 12:28–32 Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. And he set the one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan. And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan. And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi. And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Bethel, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made. And because of this false religion of idolatry, God judged Israel 1 Kings 15:30 Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the LORD God of Israel to anger. It is no wonder that every nation that becomes majority Catholic is judged by God, and is either wiped out with famine, war, disease or invasion and ethnic replacement.

Augustine, Pelagius and the persecution of separated Christians

God's gospel is simple: grace through faith in Christ's finished work, which not only saves us from Hell and gives us eternal life in Jesus, the Spirit indwelling us, quickening our spirit, sealing us unto redemption, but God also graciously empowers us to choose obedience, His paths, His commandments, allowing us to strive for maturity in Him, and live separated lives as the New Testament demands. But over the centuries, and even today, that simplicity has been complicated, twisted, and poisoned by human systems that shift blame from personal choice to inherited inability or divine decree, and make grace no more grace. Leading men to destruction, and to pridefully destroy those that remind them of their error. Augustine's doctrines of Manichaean gnostic determinism, which he championed (including his novel theory of "original sin" as inherited corruption, "prevenient/irresistible grace" as the sole cause of good, and redefining predestination as preordainment) were advanced by redefining orthodoxy against a constructed "Pelagian" strawman opposite, and attributing to Pelagius heresies which were not held by the ascetic monk in Britain. This approach functioned as a Hegelian dialectic: Augustine pitted his views against an exaggerated opposite to legitimize them as the necessary middle ground. By securing Pelagius's condemnation through imperial and ecclesiastical pressure, Augustine's theology gained dominance in the emerging Roman Catholic Church, influenced by political patrons in the late Empire. This pressure of being made anathema and labeled a heretic served to make others who held the Eastern, Greek traditions of New Testament Christianity and understanding fearful of being similarly labeled. The writings of Pelagius and others who held his actual beliefs were either destroyed or allowed to fall into obscurity due to this fear, and so the lack of an extensive record lends even more credibility to Augustine's false doctrines. Regarding original sin, Augustine's formulation—where Adam's sin transmits inherited guilt and an inevitable inclination to evil from birth—was not a settled orthodox doctrine in the earlier churches. Pre-Augustinian Christian asceticism generally viewed human nature as inclined toward goodness, if incapable of being good outside of grace entered into by faith. That man is capable of moral progress in Christ, with sin arising from personal choices, habits, or imitation of bad examples rather than a deterministic corruption inherited biologically or legally. Despite the smears, Pelagius explicitly affirmed God's grace and the Spirit's work as essential: grace opens the heart, reveals truth, exposes snares, enlightens with heavenly gifts, and forgives sins gratuitously. In his Letter to Demetrias and other texts, he described virtue as resulting from cooperation—human consent and effort partnering with divine aid to battle sin and imitate Christ's example of holy living. This was not sinless perfection by fleshly will alone (he acknowledged ongoing weakness and the need for maturity, or perfection in Christ), nor salvation by Old Testament law-keeping (which he recognized all fall short of), but pursuit of Christ's new commandment: loving God fully, with all your heart and loving your neighbor as yourself, all enabled by grace in the regenerated life of the believer. Pelagius wasn't claiming sinless perfection or denying God's grace and human weakness/sin, we see a view of grace-enabled free agency and moral responsibility that was orthodox into the late 4th/early 5th-century Christian theology, particularly in the ascetic context—before Augustine's influence shifted the boundaries, and changed the conversation to say men are beyond responsibility, and can only be as "good" as God predetermined they be. In the predominantly Greek, Antioch tradition, they had grown to see the natural end result of following the New Testament was living simply, loving others, being charitable, not given to drink, gluttony, fornication, adultery, coveting, etc. To put others' profit above your own. This contrasted with late empire libertine culture in Rome, and the gnostic influence from Alexandria, which saw excess, and to the ascetic mind, sinful living being supported by the religious leaders there. Augustine, from North Africa with roots in Alexandrian thought, a deep Manichaean past, and limited Greek proficiency, which introduced interpretive errors and conclusions, because he lacked the ability to understand the Greek texts. So Augustine diverged from earlier traditions, and his heresies have over time become foundational for many supposed Christians. Pelagius's outspoken criticism of Roman hedonism and clerical hypocrisy made him unpopular among those Augustine later influenced to support his theology and anathematize his critic. This reevaluation of the false charges of "Pelagianism," isn't meant to idealize Pelagius but recognize that the traditional "heretic" label stems more from polemical and political wrangling by Augustine and others, than from his actual teachings. In that context, we should reconsider how Augustine's legacy shaped Western Christianity—often at the expense of biblical exegesis and understanding of choice, responsibility, and grace-empowered obedience. That the simplicity of the Gospel and simplicity of life we should strive for, has been complicated by systematics of men. That the separated life and sanctification believers should strive for has been abandoned by many professing Christians. And that the teachings on lack of responsibility, or "inability to respond," has allowed those influenced by Augustine to fall well short of the potential given us by grace through faith, and the example of Christ we should actually be striving for. The pattern is clear once you see it. Groups that actually try to live the separated, simple, holy life the New Testament calls for—loving God with all the heart, loving neighbor as self, putting others first, avoiding the flesh’s excesses—have always drawn persecution from the powers that be. Look at the Cathars (the "pure ones"): extreme ascetics who rejected Roman wealth, hierarchy, sacraments, and papal authority in favor of purity and spiritual living. Rome branded them dualist heretics with false charges and launched a full crusade to wipe them out, massacring thousands in genocidal campaigns like the siege of Béziers in 1209, where "Kill them all, God will know His own" became the motto. Their crime? Living too separated from the corruption they saw in the Church, exposing the hypocrisy just like Pelagius did. The Waldensians ("poor men of Lyon") did the same in a more biblical way: lay preaching, poverty, charity, vernacular Scripture (KJV-like emphasis on the Word for all), no oaths or excess, and rejection of papal authority and indulgences. They wanted apostolic simplicity. Rome excommunicated them, hunted them with crusades and Inquisition, burning them at stakes, drowning families, and slaughtering villages in the Alps—murderous false witness calling them heretics for rejecting infant baptism, purgatory, and clerical pomp. Why? Because their separated life exposed clerical hypocrisy, echoing the smears Augustine used on Pelagius. This false witness—strawmanning true believers as heretics to justify murder—didn't stop with Augustine and Rome. It continued through the Reformers: Luther labeled Anabaptists "fanatics" and supported their execution; Calvin had Servetus burned and drowned Anabaptists in Geneva for rebaptism; Zwingli oversaw the drowning of believers in Zurich rivers; Anglicans imprisoned and executed Puritans and early Baptists for nonconformity. Even "Bloody Mary" (Queen Mary I of England) burned hundreds of Protestants at the stake during her reign (1553–1558), including men, women, and children who rejected papal authority and held to Scripture alone—false witness and torture to enforce high-church conformity. Add in the Paulicians: 7th-century ascetics rejecting icons, hierarchy, sacraments, and papal-like authority, emphasizing Scripture and simple faith—they were massacred by Byzantine emperors and labeled Manichaean heretics (ironic, given Augustine's past). The Bogomils followed, dualistic but ascetic, persecuted by Orthodox and Catholic alike with burnings and exiles. Petrobrusians and Henricians (12th century) preached against infant baptism and corruption, only to be burned alive. Arnoldists rejected clerical wealth—hunted down. And the Lollards, followers of Wycliffe, pushed Bible in English, poverty, holy living, and rejection of papal authority—branded heretics, burned at stakes under English law, their bones dug up and scattered. Even quasi-Augustinian sects like the Puritans and Plymouth Brethren, who pursued disciplined, world-denying holiness—plain living, strict Sabbath, moral rigor—faced hostility. Puritans fled England under Anglican pressure, facing starvation and native attacks; Brethren separated from established bodies and were often mocked or marginalized, even as they carried some Calvinist errors. Rome and high-church Protestant systems alike use political power to silence those who live too close to Christ’s example. The simple gospel—grace through faith enabling obedience, choice, and separated living—threatens any institution that has grown fat on compromise. When believers start striving for the real thing, the powers that profit from laxity always push back with false witness and murder. History proves it: purity draws fire, leaving a trail of blood from NT martyrs through these groups to the burnings under Bloody Mary and beyond. Augustine’s legacy perverted the gospel and weakened responsibility which excused the excess and rationalized the evil done to separated Christians with standards; the faithful who keep trying to live Biblical lives and are persecuted for it. The pattern hasn’t changed. The Bible says, Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution. Jesus warns again and again that Christians will be hated for His name. That we will suffer persecution. Paul, Peter, John and Jude all write about scoffers, mockers, persecution for the faith, and the patience of the saints who endure it. We count ourselves blessed that in America, today, we aren't facing any real persecution. That we are free to worship, pray, read and own the Bible, go soul-winning...all without facing the same challenges our spiritual forefathers faced. Partly because our system of government was influenced by those fleeing persecution and sectarian violence. This gave us some protection against politically connected apostates coming against us for Godly living. But, another reason why Bible believing Christians today, including you and I, aren't facing the same level of persecution those 1st century NT Churches faced, or the various Christians throughout the last 2,000 years have faced, is because of our own lack of separation. Because we compromise. Because we shirk standards and give in to the flesh, and aren't as perfect, or mature, as we could be. Worldly. Carnal. Maybe we would have the crowns of glory given martyrs if we chose to live more like Christ and followed His example, the way these earlier Christians did. Luke 22:62 And Peter went out, and wept bitterly. There are times in every Christian's life where the story of Peter's betrayal of Christ hits hard. New Christians, who have just accepted the gospel and been saved, turn to their unsaved family and friends, and at the slightest pushback and mocking, get embarrassed and deny Jesus. Older, more mature Christians even, will keep their faith hidden in social settings or in the workplace. We may miss opportunities to go soul winning with our brothers and sisters, in part because of the fear of judgment. That you will be accused by scoffers as Peter was, and so preemptively decline to go. We all have a regret of not sharing the gospel in a time and place where we are given the opportunity by God to proclaim the faith that saved us. We may weep bitterly by the hospital bed of someone close to us, incapable of knowing the truth because we never shared it. The Apostle Peter's story in the gospels is very real and relatable. But it doesn't end at the crowing of the cock that morning. The risen Christ appears to Peter again during the 40 days between Easter and the Ascension. Peter, unsure of his calling and, I think, ashamed of his betrayal before the Son of God, decided to go fishing. John 21:1-4 After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself. There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples. Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. And as Jesus prepares them food, and eats with them, He gives Peter, who denied Him 3 times, the opportunity to affirm his love of Jesus 3 times. John 21:14-17 This is now the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen from the dead. So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs. He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep. He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep. Peter always loved Jesus, and trusted Him, but his shame for the denial of his Lord in His hour of death made him feel distant and alone. Jesus gave him the opportunity to work through that shame and realize his love for Christ is greater than his shame at letting Jesus down. And Jesus says at each affirmation, feed My sheep. Serve others. Win souls. Care for the flock. The answer to the shame we feel when we deny Christ or the opportunity to share Him with others, isn't to go fishing. To return to the world. But to return to the work of the ministry of reconciliation we all have. Soul-winning when you are down bad, and ashamed, when prayer feels a little empty, when Bible reading is falling off, when you know you gotta get right, even if you aren't backsliding, per se, is the way to show yourself the love of Jesus you have. It is restorative sharing with others the love He has for you, and them. Peter's story doesn't end there, either. In Acts we see him boldly proclaiming Christ, calling Jews to repentance and faith towards God. Enduring beatings and imprisonment to preach the gospel. Of going to the Gentiles with the truth when called by God. And even then, Peter isn't perfect. Even as an elder of the faith, he still occasionally felt the pressure to conform to the world. Here, he is called out by Paul. Galatians 2:11-14 But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? It is something we can all fall into, even as older more mature Christians. That's why, when Peter writes his epistles, his encouraging message to believers to holdfast their faith, even when facing scoffers, mockers, false teachers, etc...to be like Christ when we are reviled for His sake - is so powerful. Like most good preaching, he is talking about his own struggles, to edify others. 1 Peter 2:21-23 For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously Being ready to testify of the hope we have even as men falsely accused us, mocking and scoffing our faith, to have the mind of Christ: 1 Peter 3:13-16 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ. Even as Noah suffered the scoffers and blasphemers of the pre-flood world, as he prepared the ark, those spirits in Hell that Jesus went and preached to, showing those that trust the Lord shall not be ashamed; Those spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water. Peter says the flood that destroyed those wicked people is a like figure to the baptism of the believer, showing the same faith and confidence Noah had to build the ark, saving his family. The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ... Our obedience in baptism, to publicly proclaim our faith, similarly shuts the mouths of those scoffers, that our conscience is clean in Christ. 2 Peter 2:1-3 But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction. And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not. Verse 7-8, how God delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;) Speaking of a believer who didn't share his faith, just Lot still was delivered from their filthy conversation, just as God promises to deliver us from the same mockers and unrighteous people. cursed children: Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet. 2 Peter 3:3 Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts... And so let's learn from Peter's slip ups and mistakes, and take heart in the grace and knowledge of Christ. 2 Peter 3:18-19 Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness. But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. I think many of us like to think of ourselves as Paul, but if we are honest, we are a lot more like Peter.

Jeremiah 10 Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel: 2 Thus saith the Lord, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them. 3 For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe. 4 They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not. 5 They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Romans on the Jew and the elect

Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God...Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God? For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written. For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God. What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God. For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect? God forbid... What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles, that they are all under sin; As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God. Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin. But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus: Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus. Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith. Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law. Is he the God of the Jews only? is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also: Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith. Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law. What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression. Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham; who is the father of us all Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead; Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification. Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. 9 Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement. There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit....So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God. For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost, That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh: Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen. Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated. What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid. Belief as a state of being

"Believe" is often misunderstood as an action, but it's generally a state of being. Like other "be" verbs (is, am, are), it reflects an internal condition—holding something as true in your mind. For example, "I believe in kindness" describes a mental stance, not an act you perform. While it can seem active in some contexts, at its core, believing is a state of conviction. A state of being. "Believe" and "be" verbs (like is, am, are, was, were) are typically classified as stative verbs when describing a state of being. Stative verbs express a condition, state, or situation that exists, rather than an action. They express things like mental states, emotions, senses, possession, or existence, and typically don’t involve physical activity or change. Unlike action (or dynamic) verbs, which show something happening (e.g., "run," "write"), stative verbs indicate a steady, ongoing state. Stative verbs are rarely used in continuous (progressive) tenses like "am believing" because states are seen as enduring, not temporary actions. Saying "I am knowing" sounds unnatural and stupid compared to "I know." Understanding stative verbs helps in using correct grammar, especially avoiding progressive forms with verbs that don’t typically take them. It also clarifies why "believe"is generally a state of being—an internal condition—rather than an action. Repentance, understood as a change of mind, is the pivotal means of transforming belief because it involves a deliberate shift in one’s perspective or conviction. Belief, as a stative verb, represents an enduring mental state, a settled acceptance of something as true. Without repentance—actively rethinking or rejecting a prior belief—this state persists, as beliefs tend to remain fixed unless consciously challenged. By engaging in repentance, one reorients their mind, replacing old convictions with new ones, thus enabling a fundamental change in belief. Are saved versus are being saved

In 1 Corinthians 1:18, the Greek present passive participle σῳζομένοις conveys salvation as a divinely assured state, rendered in the KJV as "are saved" to reflect a completed act with lasting certainty. This choice aligns with the Biblical emphasis on God's definitive work, presenting salvation as a settled reality for believers. We ARE saved. Now and future, because of the work of Christ. However, modern translations like the NASB, NKJV, and LSB often use "are being saved," introducing the English present progressive tense through the auxiliary "are." This shift in tense makes it an ongoing, potentially incomplete process, which introduces ambiguity for readers, making them see salvation as something that is not guaranteed, that it isn't a past and lasting state. For comparison, consider the translations 1 Corinthians 1:18 KJV: "For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God." NASB: "For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God." NKJV: "For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God." LSB: "For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God." Modern translations are grammatically defensible, by dishonestly claiming their choice isn't denying the present perfect passive voice, they are lying. They will truncate it to "being saved" to make that claim, completely ducking the point that it is the use of "are being" that creates the change and renders their corrupt text as heresy. The KJV’s "are saved" perfectly preserves the assured, completed state implied by the Greek, whereas "are being saved" in modern versions turns that blessed assurance into a continuous, unfinished process, sowing doubt and promoting the idea that you can't know you're saved, or that salvation can be lost. Stick with the King James!

Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him. And finally, that while our expectations for God's promised providence should be trusted, in the end our suffering may not be of our own cause, but for His glory. For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. The KJV, the received text and other languages

While the KJV is the inerrant and preserved word of God in English, it was translated from what was called the received texts, thousands of manuscripts that had been compiled by Erasmus, Beza, and Stephanus prior to 1611, as well as manuscripts that we no longer have access to, and earlier translations like the Bishop's Bible, which used these and other Antioch preserved scripts. Scrivener’s Greek New Testament (1881), usually referred to as the Textus Receptus, or received text, was a compendium of the previous Greek TRs, synthesized, using the KJV authorized version to bring all the Greek into alignment. If we were to attempt a translation into another language, such as Spanish, there are some who believe this must be done from the KJV English, as an intermediary. And while it could be possible, it wouldn't be as accurate to read in that language as a translation from the TR. Idioms, phrasing, and word choice would create problems. For example.... Example 1: John 1:1 KJV English: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." Translated from KJV to Spanish: "En el principio era la Palabra, y la Palabra estaba con Dios, y la Palabra era Dios." Translated directly from Textus Receptus (TR) Greek to Spanish: "En el principio era el Logos, y el Logos estaba con el Dios, y el Logos era Dios." Problem: Translating from the KJV to Spanish loses the nuance of the Greek term "Logos" (λόγος), which carries more philosophical and theological depth than "Palabra," missing this richness. Additionally, the TR Greek specifies "el Dios" (the God) with the definite article, emphasizing distinction, which the KJV-to-Spanish translation might obscure by following the English structure too closely. Direct translation from the TR preserves these subtleties, avoiding the loss of meaning inherent in translating a translation from Anglo-Germanic to a romantic language like Spanish, which has so many similarities to Greek. Example 2: Philippians 2:6 KJV English: "Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:" Translated from KJV to Spanish: "El cual, estando en forma de Dios, no consideró como robo el ser igual a Dios:" Translated directly from Textus Receptus (TR) Greek to Spanish: "El cual, existiendo en forma de Dios, no consideró el ser igual a Dios algo a que aferrarse:" Problem: The KJV phrase "thought it not robbery" translates the Greek "ἁρπαγμόν" (harpagmon), which implies something grasped or seized. Translating from the KJV to Spanish retains "robo" (robbery), which can suggest a negative act, potentially misrepresenting the intent. The direct TR-to-Spanish translation captures the nuanced meaning of "harpagmon" as something not clung to and exploited, rather than a sense of theft. Translating from the KJV introduces ambiguity by relying on an English idiom, which we understand, but may be lost on the Spanish reader. So rather than the original Greek’s theological precision, it introduces confusion in the finished Spanish product. Example 3: Matthew 5:18 KJV English: "For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled." Translated from KJV to Spanish: "Porque de cierto os digo que hasta que pasen el cielo y la tierra, ni una jota ni una tilde pasará de la ley, hasta que todo se cumpla." Translated directly from Textus Receptus (TR) Greek to Spanish: "Porque en verdad os digo que hasta que pasen el cielo y la tierra, ni una iota ni un ápice pasará de la ley, hasta que todo se realice." Problem: The KJV uses "jot or tittle," translating the Greek "ἰῶτα" (iota) and "κεραία" (keraia), referring to the smallest Hebrew letter and a serif-like mark, respectively. The KJV-to-Spanish version keeps "jota" and "tilde," which are familiar but may not convey the precise Hebrew scribal context. The direct TR-to-Spanish translation uses "iota" and "ápice," preserving the original terms’ specificity and cultural nuance. Translating from the KJV risks losing the exactness of the Greek terms by adhering to English equivalents that are less precise in a word-for-word English to Spanish translation. This example is less problematic than the others, because you'd still need to understand the Hebrew style being referenced, but it would be in a word choice that the Spanish reader could better understand. These are but a few examples. And if we got to the Masoretic Text, to English-to Spanish, instead of a direct translation, we would see even more problems, because Hebrew is far from a romantic language, let alone English, and a lot of the beauty and wordplay would be entirely lost. God's preserved word has been available, in its most complete and necessary form, from all time. We are blessed to have a finished and easily accessible Bible, in English. But it would deny preservation to say that the word of God was not preserved until 1611, as millions were saved from every nation and tongue long before it, by faith. Which comes from hearing the word of God. On Pentecost, the Apostles and disciples speaking in tongues, preached the word of God in more than a dozen languages. When the NT saints heard the gospel, it was in Greek and Hebrew, and likely Aramaic and other languages. The power is in the word itself, and the Spirit moving in those receiving it. Not in the languages. We can recognize the providential nature and power of God used to create our KJV, without denying the preservation and power that His word has always and will always have.

The Septuagint Myth: Debunking the 2nd Century BC Narrative The traditional narrative of the Septuagint (LXX), a supposed 2nd-century BC Greek translation of the Old Testament (OT), is a historical fraud that cannot withstand scrutiny. The claim—rooted in the pseudepigraphic Letter of Aristeas—that 72 Jewish translators from all 12 tribes, commissioned by Ptolemy II, produced a unified Greek OT is not only implausible but contradicted by manuscript evidence, textual analysis, and biblical context. As a defender of God’s preserved word in the Hebrew Masoretic Text (MT) and Byzantine Majority Text, I argue that the LXX, as known today in 4th-century AD manuscripts like Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus, is a Roman Catholic fabrication, revised to align with New Testament (NT) quotations and shaped by the apostate Catholic Church’s agenda to alter scripture. Below, I synthesize my case, grounded in the King James Bible (KJV), exposing the LXX myth and its unreliable minority text foundations. The Letter of Aristeas: A Forgery The Letter of Aristeas, dated to the 2nd century BC, claims Ptolemy II (285–246 BC) commissioned 72 translators—six from each of Israel’s 12 tribes—to translate the Torah into Greek for the Library of Alexandria. This story is a fabrication. No Egyptian records corroborate Ptolemy’s commission, and the letter’s miraculous account of identical translations reeks of legend, not history. The involvement of scribes from the 10 northern tribes, dispersed by Assyria in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:6), is anachronistic nonsense, as these tribes were effectively lost. Even non-Levite scribes translating sacred texts stretches credulity, given the Levites’ exclusive role in preserving scripture (Deuteronomy 31:25–26). The Letter is a pseudepigraphic attempt to legitimize Greek texts for Hellenistic Jews, not a historical record. Scant Manuscript Evidence Manuscript evidence demolishes the idea of a 2nd-century BC Septuagint. Only 1.7–2.6% of the OT survives in Greek from BC sources, per fragments like 4Q120 (Leviticus, 1st century BC) and Papyrus Fouad 266 (Deuteronomy, 2nd–1st century BC). These scraps, covering parts of the Torah and Minor Prophets, are far from a complete OT. No unified Greek OT manuscript exists from the 1st century AD, when the NT was written. The earliest complete LXX texts—Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus—date to the 4th century AD, over 500 years after the supposed translation. These minority texts, riddled with thousands of variants (e.g., 6,000–7,000 NT differences), lack the reliability of the harmonious MT, which aligns closely with the Dead Sea Scrolls (DSS, 250 BC–70 AD). The DSS, with over 200 Hebrew manuscripts, confirm the MT’s stability, while Greek fragments show textual diversity, suggesting ad hoc translations, not a standardized Septuagint. Hebrew Primacy in the NT Era The NT assumes a Hebrew textual context, not a Greek one. In Matthew 5:18 (KJV), Jesus declares, “Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law.” “Jot” (Hebrew yod, smallest letter) and “tittle” (scribal stroke) refer to Hebrew script, meaningless in Greek. This underscores that Hebrew scrolls, not a Greek LXX, were read in 1st-century Judean synagogues (Luke 4:16–20). The DSS, overwhelmingly Hebrew, and rabbinic practices (e.g., Mishnah, Megillah 4:4) confirm Hebrew’s primacy. While Greek was spoken, NT writers like Paul, fluent in Hebrew, likely translated Hebrew texts into Greek for their audience, not quoted a non-existent Septuagint. Similarities between NT quotations (e.g., Isaiah 7:14, “virgin” in Matthew 1:23) and later LXX texts (e.g., parthenos) result from natural translation of Hebrew terms like almah (virgin or young maiden), not reliance on a unified Greek OT. Almah and Translation Integrity The claim that NT writers quoted an LXX misreading of almah in Isaiah 7:14 (KJV: “a virgin shall conceive”) is baseless. Almah, used seven times in the OT (e.g., Genesis 24:43, Rebekah as virgin), denotes a young, unmarried woman, often implying virginity in context (Song of Solomon 6:8). The NT’s parthenos (Matthew 1:23) accurately renders almah’s meaning, reflecting the miraculous sign of a virgin birth. Similarities with 4th-century LXX texts are due to shared translation choices, not NT dependence on a 2nd-century BC Septuagint. Like KJV translators, who used English terms (e.g., “charity” for agape) to convey meaning, NT writers rendered Hebrew into Greek, preserving sense over literalism. This explains overlaps without requiring a mythical LXX. 4th-Century Revision The LXX, as preserved in Vaticanus and Sinaiticus, is a 4th-century AD Roman Catholic product, revised to align with NT quotations. These minority texts, produced in Christian scriptoria, show deliberate harmonization. For example, Isaiah 7:14’s parthenos in Vaticanus matches Matthew 1:23, supporting the virgin birth, while the MT’s almah is ambiguous. Origen’s Hexapla (240 AD) and the Lucianic recension (300 AD) demonstrate Catholic scribes editing Greek OT texts, often to reflect NT theology. The Catholic Church, an apostate institution of the 4th century, sponsored this revisionism, as seen in Jerome’s Vulgate (382–405 AD), which included the Apocrypha despite early fathers like Melito and Jerome questioning their canonicity. The Apocrypha’s inclusion, absent from the Jewish MT and warned against by Athanasius, reflects Catholic tampering, not divine preservation. Unreliable Minority Texts Vaticanus and Sinaiticus, the backbone of the LXX, are unreliable. Their 4th-century dating, largely affirmed by Catholic-controlled scholarship (e.g., Vatican Library for Vaticanus), faces providential questions. Sinaiticus’ authenticity is further doubted due to 19th-century forgery claims by Constantine Simonides, who alleged creating it in 1839–1840. While paleography supports their antiquity, their 6,000–7,000 NT variants contrast with the Byzantine Majority Text’s harmony, which underpins the KJV. Westcott and Hort, 19th-century heretics with liberal biases, championed these texts to undermine the Textus Receptus, driven by profit and unorthodox agendas. Their work, like Catholic dating, cannot be trusted against the MT’s fidelity, confirmed by the DSS. Objections Answered Objection: BC Greek fragments (e.g., 4Q120) prove a 2nd-century BC Septuagint. Response: These fragments, covering only 1.7–2.6% of the OT, are disparate, not a unified text. They reflect localized translations, not a Ptolemaic commission. Objection: NT quotations (50–80% LXX-like) suggest a pre-Christian Septuagint. Response: Similarities stem from NT writers translating Hebrew texts, like almah to parthenos. Vaticanus/Sinaiticus were later harmonized to match NT, not quoted in the 1st century. Objection: Jewish use (e.g., Philo) and early papyri show an early LXX. Response: Philo cited individual Greek translations, not a standardized Septuagint. Papyri (e.g., Chester Beatty, 2nd–3rd century AD) are Christian, postdating the NT and reflecting revision, not a 2nd-century BC text. Objection: Catholic scholarship is ecumenical, not controlling dating. Response: The Catholic Church’s history of altering scripture (Vulgate, Apocrypha) and control of Vaticanus taint its credibility. Its apostate status by the 4th century undermines its role as a neutral arbiter. Conclusion The 2nd-century BC Septuagint is a myth, unsupported by manuscripts, contradicted by Hebrew primacy in the NT (Matthew 5:18), and exposed as a 4th-century AD revision in unreliable minority texts like Vaticanus and Sinaiticus. The Letter of Aristeas is a forgery, BC fragments are negligible, and NT-LXX similarities reflect translation, not a unified Greek OT. The Catholic Church’s apostate influence, from the Vulgate to Apocrypha inclusion, and the dubious scholarship of Westcott and Hort, confirm the LXX’s corruption. God’s preserved word lies in the MT and the Byzantine Majority Text, faithfully rendered in the KJV. Let us reject the LXX myth and uphold the true scriptures.
