Genesis 3 – The Fall Young Adult Sunday School · Genesis Series Genesis Chapter 3 The Fall • The Curse • The First Promise ✦ ✦ ✦ Use the arrow keys or swipe to move through the lesson. Tap any gold reference to read the verse. v. 1 · The Serpent’s Opening Move “Yea, Hath God Said?” Planting Doubt in God’s Word Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden? Genesis 3:1 The serpent does not begin with a lie; he begins with a question. He does not deny God’s word; he causes Eve to doubt it. The first weapon of the enemy is not atheism but uncertainty about what God has said. 2 Corinthians 11:3 vv. 2–5 · The Appeal, Become Like God The Lie: “Ye Shall Not Surely Die” And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die. And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die: For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil. Genesis 3:2-5 The serpent’s appeal: you are being held back. God is withholding something good from you. You can be as God. Pride was the first sin in heaven ( Isa. 14:13–14 ); the same bait is set for man. v. 6 · The Lust of the Eyes, Eve’s Choice, Then Adam’s She Saw • She Took • She Gave: He Did Eat And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her ; and he did eat. Genesis 3:6 Eve was deceived: she convinced herself through three appeals. Good for food (lust of the flesh), pleasant to the eyes (lust of the eyes), desired to make wise (pride of life): 1 John 2:16 . Adam was NOT deceived: 1 Tim. 2:14 . He received God’s command directly before Eve was created: Gen. 2:16–17 . Adam chose sin with open eyes. Cross References · Romans 5 Adam’s Choice: Death Through One Man, Life Through One Man Romans 5:12 Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned: Romans 5:12 Sin entered through Adam’s wilful choice. He was the federal head of the human race. His act condemned all who come from him. Romans 5:14 Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come. Romans 5:14 Adam is called a “figure,” a type, of Christ. The first Adam plunged the race into death; the Last Adam would lift it back to life. The “much more” of grace Romans 5:17 For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.) Romans 5:17 The “much more” of grace: what Adam lost, Christ restores in abundance. Death reigned through Adam; the redeemed shall reign in life through Christ. Romans 5:18–19 Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life. For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. Romans 5:18-19 The remedy is perfectly shaped to match the wound. One act of disobedience: condemnation. One act of obedience at the cross: justification. In Adam, or in Christ 1 Corinthians 15:21–22 For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. 1 Corinthians 15:21-22 Every human being stands in one of two federal heads: in Adam (dead), or in Christ (alive). There is no neutral ground. 1 Timothy 2:14 And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression. 1 Timothy 2:14 Eve was deceived. Adam was not. Adam chose to follow his wife into sin with full knowledge of God’s command. His representative role is therefore the greater. One man representing many Adam received the command directly from God before Eve existed. He was not deceived; he sinned deliberately. This is why Scripture assigns the Fall to Adam, not Eve. But the glory of the gospel is that the same principle that condemned us, one man representing many, is the very mechanism God uses to save us. In Adam, all die. In Christ, all who believe are made alive. v. 7 · Their Own Works, Insufficient Before a Holy God Fig Leaves: Man’s Attempt to Cover His Own Sin And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons. Genesis 3:7 Man’s first religious instinct after sin: cover yourself by your own works. Fig leaves could not atone. No human effort, religion, or righteousness can cover the guilt of sin before a holy God. Isa. 64:6 vv. 8–10 · The Lord God Walking, They Hid “Where Art Thou?” God Comes Seeking the Sinner And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day : and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God amongst the trees of the garden. And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou? And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself. Genesis 3:8-10 God knew exactly where Adam was. The question is not for God’s information; it is for Adam’s conviction. God is the one who comes seeking the sinner. This is the gospel pattern from the very beginning. Luke 19:10 vv. 11–13 · The Blame Game, No One Takes Responsibility Adam Blames God. Eve Blames the Serpent. All Are Guilty. And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat? And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat. And the Lord God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat. Genesis 3:11-13 Adam blames the woman, and subtly blames God who gave her. Eve blames the serpent. But God holds each accountable in turn. We are each guilty of our own choices. Rom. 14:12 • Ezek. 18:20 vv. 14–15 · The Serpent Cursed, The First Prophecy of Christ The Proto-Evangelium: The Seed of the Woman Shall Bruise His Head And the Lord God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field ; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. Genesis 3:14-15 The very first word of gospel The very first word of gospel in all Scripture. Before one curse falls on man, God announces the remedy. The seed of the woman, not of a man, points to the virgin birth. Gal. 4:4 He shall bruise thy head: the fatal, final blow at the cross and resurrection. Col. 2:15 • Rom. 16:20 Thou shalt bruise his heel: the suffering of Christ. Final end of the serpent: Rev. 20:10 v. 16 · Eve Cursed, and All Women Sorrow in Childbirth • Desire and Rule Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception ; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children ; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee. Genesis 3:16 The curse falls on the role God designed: childbearing becomes sorrow. The creation order of male headship is now complicated by the effects of sin. Every woman who has ever suffered in childbirth bears the mark of the Fall. Hope: 1 Tim. 2:15 vv. 17–19 · Adam Cursed, and All Men Thorns and Thistles • Sweat • Dust to Dust And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake ; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee ; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground ; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return. Genesis 3:17-19 Physical death enters here; every grave is the direct consequence of this moment. Every man who has ever broken his back for daily bread bears the mark of the Fall. The thorns Adam now cultivates foreshadow the crown of thorns on the Last Adam: Christ bore the curse in full. Gal. 3:13 • Rom. 5:12 v. 21 · The Lord Makes Coats of Skins Blood Must Be Shed: God Clothes the Sinner Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them. Genesis 3:21 Man covered himself with leaves: his own works. God replaced those leaves with skins. An animal had to die. Blood had to be shed. This is the first sacrifice in Scripture, and it is God who performs it. God himself provides the covering for sin at the cost of innocent life. Heb. 9:22 • John 1:29 • Isa. 61:10 vv. 22–24 · Driven Out • The Flaming Sword • The Tree of Life Guarded Expelled: Separated from God’s Presence And the Lord God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever: Therefore the Lord God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken. So he drove out the man ; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life. Genesis 3:22-24 Spiritual death: separation from the presence of God where He walked with man. The way to the tree of life is now barred. It will not be opened again until the cross tears the veil ( Matt. 27:51 ), and the last chapter of Scripture restores what was lost: Rev. 22:14 Genesis 3 in One Frame What the Fall Cost, What Christ Restores Man doubted God’s word. Man desired to be God. Man chose sin. Man tried to cover himself. Man hid from God. Man blamed others. Man was cursed. Man was driven out. But before the first curse was pronounced, God announced a Deliverer. Before the first animal died, God showed that blood would cover sin. Before the gate closed, God was already planning to open it again. For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. Genesis 4: Cain and Abel Looks at the two offerings, God's warning to Cain, the first murder, and the line that began to call on the LORD. Genesis 4 – Cain and Abel Young Adult Sunday School • Genesis Series Genesis 4: Cain and Abel The First Murder • Calling on the Lord Genesis 4:1-26 ✦ ✦ ✦ Use the arrow keys or swipe to move. Tap any reference to read the verse. vv. 1–2 Two Sons Born Cain and Abel And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord . And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground. Genesis 4:1-2 Eve’s declaration shows her faith that the promised seed of Genesis 3:15 would come from the Lord . Two brothers, two vocations, and two very different hearts before God. vv. 3–5 Two Offerings: One Accepted, One Rejected Abel’s Offering Accepted, Cain’s Rejected And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord . And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. Genesis 4:3-5 Abel brought blood, the firstlings of the flock. Cain brought the fruit of his own labor from the cursed ground. God had already shown in Genesis 3:21 that a blood covering was required. Heb. 9:22 The difference was not the quality of the gift but the nature of it, and the faith behind it. vv. 6–7 God Warns Cain “Sin Lieth at the Door”: Grace Before Judgment And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him. Genesis 4:6-7 God gives Cain a direct warning before he acts. Sin is pictured as a crouching beast at the threshold, desiring to master him, but he can still rule over it. Cain chose not to. God never sends judgment without first sending warning. 1 Pet. 5:8 v. 8 Cain Rises Against Abel The World’s First Murder: Brother Against Brother And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. Genesis 4:8 The first death in human history is not natural. It is murder. And the victim is a righteous man killed by a religious man whose worship was rejected. Matt. 23:35 : Jesus names Abel as the first of a long line of righteous martyrs. vv. 9–12 God’s Judgment: The Blood Cries Out “Am I My Brother’s Keeper?” The Voice of Blood And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper? And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground. And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand; When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth. Genesis 4:9-12 Cain lies to God as Adam hid from God. But the blood itself is a witness. Heb. 12:24 : the blood of Jesus speaketh better things than that of Abel. Abel’s blood cried for vengeance; Christ’s blood speaks peace. Cross references • Genesis 4:10 Hebrews 11:4: He Being Dead Yet Speaketh Hebrews 11:4 By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh. Hebrews 11:4 The difference between the two offerings was faith. Abel’s sacrifice was accepted not because it was larger or costlier, but because it was offered in faith, faith that required blood, pointing to the coming atonement. Though murdered, Abel still speaks through his faith recorded in Scripture. Hebrews 12:24 And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel. Hebrews 12:24 Abel’s blood cried out from the ground for justice and vengeance. The blood of Jesus speaks better things: it cries for mercy, for peace, for forgiveness. Both bloods speak; only one silences the accusation of the Law. Cross references • Genesis 4:10 Hebrews 11:4: He Being Dead Yet Speaketh (continued) Romans 3:25 Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; Romans 3:25 Every Old Testament blood sacrifice pointed forward to the propitiation Christ would make. Abel’s faith looked forward to the same cross we look back on. Abel did not earn God’s favor by working harder than Cain. He came God’s way, by faith, with blood. The entire book of Hebrews is built on this pattern: the old sacrifices were shadows; Christ is the substance. Abel understood by faith what the Law would later codify and the cross would finally fulfill. vv. 13–16 Cain’s Punishment: Departure from God’s Presence Cain Went Out from the Presence of the Lord And Cain said unto the Lord , My punishment is greater than I can bear. Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth; and it shall come to pass, that every one that findeth me shall slay me. And the Lord said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him. And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord , and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden. Genesis 4:13-16 Cain’s complaint is about his suffering, not about what he has done. He does not repent; he grieves his consequences. Note that even in judgment God shows restraint, setting a mark of protection on Cain. Yet the defining sentence of verse 16 is the saddest in the chapter: he went out from the presence of the Lord . Cross references • Genesis 4:16 1 John 3:12: Not as Cain 1 John 3:11-12 For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another. Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous. 1 John 3:11-12 John names the root of Cain’s murder: his works were evil and his brother’s righteous. Righteousness in another does not produce love in a corrupt heart; it produces hatred. This is the spirit that has always killed the prophets. 1 John 3:15 Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him. 1 John 3:15 John draws the line from Cain to the heart. Murder did not begin in the field; it began with the hatred before it. Cross references • Genesis 4:16 1 John 3:12: Not as Cain (continued) John 8:44 Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it. John 8:44 The spirit behind Cain’s act is identified: the devil was a murderer from the beginning. Cain, John says in 1 John 3:12 , “was of that wicked one.” Cain went out from the presence of the Lord , the saddest verse of the chapter. His legacy is not only the first murder but a pattern John warns the church against: religious performance without genuine faith, and hatred of the righteous because their righteousness is a rebuke to our own evil works. vv. 17–22 Civilization Without God Cain’s Descendants: City, Culture, Craft. Progress Without God: Building, Music, Metalwork And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch. And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech. And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah. And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle. And his brother’s name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ. And Zillah, she also bare Tubalcain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubalcain was Naamah. Genesis 4:17-22 The line of Cain builds civilization: cities, livestock, music, metalwork. None of it is evil in itself. But all of it is constructed apart from God. Man can fill the earth with art and industry and still be walking away from the presence of the Lord . vv. 23–24 Lamech’s Boast: Violence Escalates Lamech: The Way of Cain Goes Further And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. Genesis 4:23-24 Lamech takes God’s promise of protection over Cain and twists it into a boast of personal vengeance. He has murdered and glories in it. This is sin unchecked, from Cain’s silent deed in a field to Lamech’s proud song. Rom. 1:32 Cross references • Genesis 4:24 Jude 11: The Way of Cain Jude 10-11 But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves. Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. Jude 10-11 Jude uses “the way of Cain” as a defined category of apostasy: approaching God on your own terms, rejecting the blood, hating the righteous, and ultimately being driven from God’s presence. Lamech’s boast in verse 24 is the fruit of what Cain’s way produces across generations. Compare: Matthew 18:21-22 Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven. Matthew 18:21-22 Jesus directly inverts Lamech’s boast. Lamech: avenge seventy and sevenfold. Christ: forgive seventy times seven. The way of Cain multiplies vengeance; the way of Christ multiplies forgiveness. The way of Cain is the pattern of all religion that approaches God on its own terms, scorns the blood, hates the righteousness of others, and is driven further from God’s presence. Jude warns the church that this spirit appears among false teachers in every age. vv. 25–26 Seth Appointed: Men Call on the Lord “Then Began Men to Call upon the Name of the Lord ” And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord . Genesis 4:25-26 Against the backdrop of Cain’s city and Lamech’s boast, God quietly raises up another seed. Seth, appointed in Abel’s place, begins the godly line through which the promised Redeemer will come. And the mark of that line is this: they call upon the name of the Lord . Cross references • Genesis 4:26 Romans 10:13: Whosoever Shall Call Romans 10:13 For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. Romans 10:13 What began at Seth’s generation, calling upon the name of the Lord, is still the only way of salvation. The promise in Genesis 4:26 finds its fullest declaration here in Paul’s letter to Rome. Romans 10:9-10 That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. Romans 10:9-10 Calling upon the name of the Lord flows from a heart that believes and a mouth that confesses. The same faith Abel had, Seth’s generation expressed publicly in calling on the Lord . Cross references • Genesis 4:26 Joel 2:32 and Acts 2:21 Joel 2:32 And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call. Joel 2:32 This promise spans both Testaments: Joel, Romans 10:13, and Acts 2:21 all repeat it. What Seth’s generation began, the Church continues. Acts 2:21 And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved. Acts 2:21 Peter quotes Joel on the Day of Pentecost. The same promise first glimpsed in Genesis 4:26 is now proclaimed to all nations. The door has always been the same: call upon the Lord . Call upon the Lord Genesis 4 ends not with Lamech’s boast but with a quiet, eternal answer: men began to call upon the name of the Lord . Against every city Cain built and every song Lamech sang of blood, God was raising up a people who would simply call on Him. That calling, by faith, upon His name, is still the only way of salvation today. ‹ Prev Contents Next › Scripture Close Contents Close

Genesis 5: The Generations of Adam Reads the genealogy from Adam to Noah as literal history, noting that Adam's own likeness was passed to Seth. Genesis 5 – The Generations of Adam Young Adult Sunday School • Genesis Series Genesis 5: The Generations of Adam From Creation to Noah • A Testimony in Years Genesis 5:1-32 ✦ ✦ ✦ Use the arrow keys or swipe to move. Tap any reference to read the verse. vv. 1–2 The Book of the Generations In the Likeness of God This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him; Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created. Genesis 5:1-2 Moses opens this chapter the same way he opens a genealogy anywhere in Scripture, with a “book,” a formal, deliberate record. This is not legend passed down loosely around a fire. It is a document, a toledoth, meant to be taken as literal history, the same way we take the record of names, dates, and reigns anywhere else in the Old Testament. vv. 3–5 Adam: The First Entry In His Own Likeness, After His Image And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth: And the days of Adam after he had begotten Seth were eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters: And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died. Genesis 5:3-5 Verse 1 said Adam was made in God’s likeness. Verse 3 says Seth was born in Adam’s likeness: fallen, mortal, sinful. That is the whole doctrine of the fall in one verse: what is passed down is not innocence but Adam’s own broken image. And then the refrain begins: and he died. God’s word to Adam in the garden was not a bluff. vv. 6–8 Seth Nine Hundred Twelve Years, and He Died And Seth lived an hundred and five years, and begat Enos: And Seth lived after he begat Enos eight hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years: and he died. Genesis 5:6-8 vv. 9–11 Enos Then Began Men to Call Upon the Lord And Enos lived ninety years, and begat Cainan: And Enos lived after he begat Cainan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years: and he died. Genesis 5:9-11 Enos’s own birth was the moment Gen. 4:26 marks. With the third generation from Adam, public, corporate calling on the name of the Lord begins, a confession made with the mouth, standing alongside the blood faith of Abel. vv. 12–14 Cainan Nine Hundred Ten Years, and He Died And Cainan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalaleel: And Cainan lived after he begat Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years: and he died. Genesis 5:12-14 vv. 15–17 Mahalaleel Eight Hundred Ninety-Five Years, and He Died And Mahalaleel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared: And Mahalaleel lived after he begat Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Mahalaleel were eight hundred ninety and five years: and he died. Genesis 5:15-17 vv. 18–20 Jared Nine Hundred Sixty-Two Years, and He Died And Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch: And Jared lived after he begat Enoch eight hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Jared were nine hundred sixty and two years: and he died. Genesis 5:18-20 Jared lived longer than all but Methuselah, and he is the father of the one man in this chapter for whom the refrain never comes. Watch what happens in the very next entry. vv. 21–24 Enoch, the Seventh from Adam And Enoch Walked With God: And He Was Not; For God Took Him And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: And Enoch walked with God : and he was not; for God took him. Genesis 5:21-24 Every other name in this chapter closes the same way: and he died. Enoch’s does not. He is the seventh from Adam, not to be confused with Cain’s son Enoch, third from Adam in the other line ( Gen. 4:17 ), and Scripture is careful to tell us this was no ordinary death. Heb. 11:5 calls it a translation, by faith, and testifies that before it happened, he pleased God. Cross references • Genesis 5:24 Hebrews 11 and Jude: Enoch’s Testimony Hebrews 11:5 By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God. Hebrews 11:5 Two things are named here: the mechanism (faith) and the reward (translation, so that he never faced death at all). Before it happened, his testimony was already recorded: he pleased God. Jude 14-15 And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him. Jude 14-15 Jude, writing near the end of the New Testament, quotes a sermon preached before the flood. Enoch’s prophecy of the Lord’s coming in judgment is the same hope every believer since has held: Christ’s return with His saints. Cross references • Genesis 5:24 Hebrews 11 and Jude: Enoch’s Testimony (continued) John 8:51 Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death. John 8:51 What happened to Enoch bodily is the promise held spiritually for every believer in Christ: those who keep His word will never see death in the sense that matters, separation from God forever. Enoch is not a strange exception tucked into a genealogy. He is proof, planted in the earliest pages of Scripture, that walking with God by faith is a life death cannot ultimately touch. vv. 25–27 Methuselah The Oldest Man Who Ever Lived And Methuselah lived an hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech: And Methuselah lived after he begat Lamech seven hundred eighty and two years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died. Genesis 5:25-27 Nine hundred sixty-nine years: no man in Scripture, before or since, lived longer. Even the longest life this side of Eden still ends the same way every other life in this chapter ends. The refrain catches up to everyone but one. vv. 28–31 Lamech This Same Shall Comfort Us And Lamech lived an hundred eighty and two years, and begat a son: And he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed. And Lamech lived after he begat Noah five hundred ninety and five years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Lamech were seven hundred seventy and seven years: and he died. Genesis 5:28-31 This is a different Lamech than Cain’s descendant of Genesis 4 who boasted of vengeance seventy and sevenfold. This Lamech, of the line of Seth, names his son in hope, looking for relief from the curse on the ground pronounced back in Genesis 3:17 . He could not have known how, but Noah’s name proved prophetic the day the flood lifted and a new world began. v. 32 Noah Shem, Ham, and Japheth And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Genesis 5:32 Ten generations, one continuous line, from the dust of Eden to the three sons who would repopulate the whole earth after the flood. The chapter that opened “in the likeness of God” closes by naming the men through whom every nation on earth descends. The Ten Names, In Order Hidden in the Hebrew: The Names Themselves A Sentence Written Into the Genealogy Name Root Meaning Adam Man Seth Appointed Enosh (Enos) Mortal Kenan (Cainan) Sorrow Mahalalel The Blessed God Jared Shall come down Enoch Teaching Methuselah His death shall bring Lamech The despairing Noah Rest The Gospel, Hidden in the Meaning of the Names Man is appointed mortal sorrow, but the Blessed God shall come down teaching that His death shall bring the despairing rest. Read straight down the ten names Read straight down the family tree, in Hebrew, the ten names carrying us from Adam to Noah string together into that sentence: the gospel itself, laid into a genealogy centuries before Christ came down, taught among us, died, and gave rest to the despairing. Whether every root is pressed with equal precision or not, the pattern is hard to miss: the God who inspired this list wastes nothing, not even the names. Eight Times Repeated And He Died: The Refrain of the Chapter The Wages of Sin, Written in a Genealogy 8 times: and he died They Lived, They Had Children, and They Died Long-lived though they were, every man in this chapter but one lived, had sons and daughters, and died. Sons of God calling on the name of the Lord and sons of men who did not: all of them sinned, and all of them, in due time, died. This is not poetry or picture; it is the plain, literal accounting of years from creation to Noah. Taking the figurative as figurative and the literal as literal, these ages are given to us as literal history, the same rule of interpretation that lets us call Christ’s parables parables without turning His genealogies into parables too. Rom. 5:12 Cross references • Genesis 5, “and he died” Romans 6:23: The Wages of Sin Is Death Romans 6:23 For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. Romans 6:23 Genesis 5 is Romans 6:23 written out in eight literal case studies. Every long life in the chapter still ends exactly where Paul says sin’s wages lead. Romans 5:12 Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned: Romans 5:12 Adam’s sin did not stay Adam’s problem. It passed to every name on this genealogy, sons of God and sons of men alike, whether they called upon the name of the Lord or rejected His salvation. The refrain “and he died” is not filler between the numbers. It is the whole doctrine of sin and death, stated eight times over, so that the ninth time, when it doesn’t come, we notice. Genesis 5 and 11 • A Literal Chronology Counting the Years: From Creation to Christ About 2,008 Years, Adam to Abraham Patriarch Age at Next Birth Adam 130 Seth 105 Enos 90 Cainan 70 Mahalaleel 65 Jared 162 Enoch 65 Methuselah 187 Lamech 182 Noah (to Shem) ~500 Adam to Shem 1,556 yrs Adam to Abraham Following the given years of Genesis 5 forward, and then adding the generations of Genesis 11:10–32 from Shem down to Terah, father of Abraham, we arrive at roughly 2,008 years from Adam to Abraham. This isn’t a modern estimate imposed on the text; it’s simple addition of the years the text itself gives us. Matthew 1:17 Abraham to Christ Fourteen Generations, Three Times Over So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations. Matthew 1:17 Matthew closes the loop Genesis 5 opens. Between the literal years of Genesis and the counted generations of Matthew 1:17, Scripture hands us the recorded span from creation to Christ, inspired and preserved. Add the roughly two thousand years since, and the commonly accepted span places the earth at just slightly more than six thousand years old, give or take a century or two. Adam → Abel → Seth and Enos → Enoch A Pattern of Salvation in the Early Patriarchs Knowledge, Blood, Confession, and a Walk With God Reading these early chapters together, a pattern for salvation emerges in the lives of these men: Adam Knows God his Creator, and knows his own sin. Abel Brings the blood of atonement, offered in faith for redemption. Seth and Enos Show that with the mouth, confession is made: calling upon the name of the Lord . Enoch Gives the testimony that he walked with God, that he lived separated, pleasing God. Each of us passes through these same steps when we come to Christ and live for Him, an illustration God gave in His word, through the lives of these men, long before the cross. Hebrews 11:5 • John 8:51 Translated That He Should Not See Death A Prophet Who Preached, and a Promise to Every Believer Enoch was more than a name in a list. He was a prophet. Jude 1:14–15 preserves his preaching, a witness in the Spirit to Christ’s coming victory in the day of the Lord, given ages before the flood, let alone the cross. And what happened to him is the promise held out to every believer since: John 8:51 , “if a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.” A question worth sitting with • Genesis 5:24 What Does “Translated” Mean? John 3:13 And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven. John 3:13 Jesus says plainly that no man has ascended to heaven except Himself. So what are we to make of Enoch being taken, and of Elijah’s whirlwind ascent in [[2 Kings 2:11 What we can say plainly: Enoch walked with God, prophesied of Christ, and was pleasing to God, and he did not see death. Beyond that, Genesis leaves the mechanics a mystery, and we do well to leave them there too, drawing our application from what is written rather than from what isn’t. A caution Not Every Old Book Is Scripture The “Book of Enoch” Is Not Scripture There are rabbit trails worth naming and leaving alone. Ancient Jewish fables and the pseudepigraphal “Book of Enoch” claim to fill in what Genesis leaves silent, but the book contradicts itself and contains plain fabrications. It is not Scripture, whatever curiosity it satisfies. What we can know, and should hold to, is simply this: Enoch walked with God, prophesied of Christ, and pleased God, and by faith, we’re meant to draw the same inspiration to live pleasing to God ourselves, in the Spirit, however our own days end. ‹ Prev Contents Next › Scripture Close Contents Close

Genesis 6: Sons of God Who were the sons of God who took the daughters of men? Both views stated fairly, the believers of Seth's line and fallen angels, then compared text by text from the King James Bible: the two lines of Cain and Seth, the giants, and whether God would call fallen angels His sons. Genesis 6 – Sons of God A study in Genesis 6 Sons of God Who took the daughters of men to wife, and why it matters that God judged man . Genesis 6:1-2 ✦ ✦ ✦ Use the arrow keys or swipe to move. Tap any reference to read the verse. A disagreement among brethren Who the sons of God were in Genesis 6 is a tertiary doctrine. It does not touch salvation, and faithful believers who love the King James Bible hold both of these views: Sons are believers The sons of God were men of Seth’s believing line who married unbelieving women of the world. Sons are angels The sons of God were fallen angels who took human women as wives. We will show our work from the King James Bible alone, state each view as its holders would, and let the text decide. Romans 14:5 Ephesians 4:3 Two lines Cain’s family and Seth’s family, from Genesis 4 and 5 The case for Sons are believers The case for Sons are angels Stated fairly, then compared text by text After the Flood Giants, possession, and where Scripture puts the blame The deciding question Would God call fallen angels His sons? The line of Cain And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord , and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden. Genesis 4:16 Cain builds a city and names it after his son Enoch. Gen 4:17 Lamech takes two wives, the first man recorded to do so. Genesis 4:19 Lamech boasts to his wives that he has slain a man, and claims a vengeance greater than Cain’s. Gen 4:23–24 A line that walks away from the presence of the Lord and grows in cities, crafts, and violence. Not once in Genesis 4 does anyone in this line call upon God. The line of Seth And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord . Genesis 4:26 God appoints “another seed instead of Abel,” and from that seed men begin to call on the Lord . Genesis 5 then traces that line by name, ten generations from Adam to Noah. Gen 4:25–26 1 Adam 2 Seth 3 Enos 4 Cainan 5 Mahalaleel 6 Jared 7 Enoch 8 Methuselah 9 Lamech 10 Noah Two families now live side by side on the earth: one that went out from the Lord ’s presence, and one that calls on His name. Two Enochs, two Lamechs Moses gives both lines a man named Enoch and a man named Lamech, as if to set them side by side so we cannot miss the contrast. Cain’s line Seth’s line Enoch. A city is named for him. Genesis 4:17 Enoch. “Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.” Genesis 5:24 Lamech. Takes two wives and boasts of slaying a man. Genesis 4:23-24 Lamech. Names his son Noah, hoping for comfort from the ground the Lord cursed. Genesis 5:29 Same names, opposite hearts. When Genesis 6 speaks of “sons of God” and “daughters of men,” these two families are the ones the reader has just met. Noah, the last son before the Flood But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord . These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God. Genesis 6:8-9 Ten generations after Adam, the line that called on the Lord comes down to one man and his house. The sons of God had married into the world around them; Noah walked with God. “Perfect in his generations” means that among the men of his own time, Noah was a believer, mature in his faith. God calls Job “perfect” in the same way, and asks it of Abram. The verse explains itself: “Noah walked with God.” Job 1:1 Genesis 17:1 How anyone becomes a son of God But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name: John 1:12 For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God. Romans 8:14 For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. Galatians 3:26 Scripture never makes sonship a matter of nature, rank, or power. It is received by faith in the Son. Sons before the cross Christ is “the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” His work stands outside of time, and Old Testament saints believed God’s promise of Him. They looked to Christ The Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. Revelation 13:8 Abraham rejoiced to see Christ’s day. John 8:56 Moses esteemed the reproach of Christ. Hebrews 11:26 Seth’s line called on the name of the Lord . Gen 4:26 God called them His own “Ye are the children of the Lord your God.” Deuteronomy 14:1 “Bring my sons from far, and my daughters.” Isaiah 43:6 “Ye are the sons of the living God.” Hosea 1:10 The Old Testament already uses the language of sons for God’s believing people. Genesis 6 does not need a new definition. Read it slowly And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them, That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose. And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years. There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown. And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. And it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart. And the Lord said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them. Genesis 6:1-7 10 times the passage says man or men 0 times it says angel God’s Spirit strives with man, “for that he also is flesh.” The flesh in view is man’s. The wickedness God sees is man’s. The creature God repents of making is man. The order of events The giants are already there “There were giants in the earth in those days.” They are present before the text describes any union. Genesis 6:4 The sons of God take wives They choose by sight, “of all which they chose,” not by faith. Gen 6:2 Their children become famous men “Mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” Famous men . The text never calls the children giants, angels, or anything but men. Genesis 6:4 God sees the wickedness of man Every imagination of man’s heart was only evil continually. Genesis 6:5 God repents that He made man, and will destroy man Gen 6:6–7 But Noah found grace Gen 6:8 The judgment falls on the godly line’s compromise and the world’s wickedness alike. Nowhere does God name a hybrid race as the cause. Job 1 and 2: the sons of God in heaven Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord , and Satan came also among them. Job 1:6 Who stands before God The heavenly assembly includes “the spirits of just men made perfect.” Redeemed men stand in God’s presence. Heb 12:22–23 Among them, not of them Satan comes “among them” as the accuser, there to charge Job. He is never counted as one of the sons. Job 1:9–11 Job 2:1 Repeating the scene in chapter 2 adds nothing new: the same sons, and the same accuser in their midst. Job 2:1 Job 38:7: who is the corner stone? The strongest text for Sons are angels, and the answer rests on one question. Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth ? declare, if thou hast understanding. Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it? Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy? Job 38:4-7 Who are the morning stars? Angels. Scripture pictures angels as stars: Lucifer is the “son of the morning,” and the dragon’s tail drew “the third part of the stars of heaven.” The plural morning stars are not to be confused with Christ, who alone is “the bright and morning star.” Isaiah 14:12 Revelation 12:4 Revelation 22:16 So verse 7 names two companies, angels singing and the sons of God shouting. And God names two works: the foundations of the earth, and the corner stone. The sons of God shout when the corner stone is laid. So when was Christ laid as the corner stone? Before the foundation of the world The Lamb was foreordained before the foundation of the world, and is the Lamb slain from its foundation. 1 Pet 1:19–20 Revelation 13:8 At creation, He is the Creator “In the beginning was the Word… and the Word was God. All things were made by him.” At creation Christ is the Builder, not a stone laid in His own building. If the corner stone were laid at creation, the Creator would become part of the creation. John 1:1–3 Colossians 1:16 In time, God lays the corner stone God promised to lay it “in Zion” ( Isaiah 28:16 ). It was laid when He came in the flesh, was crucified and set at nought by the builders, and was raised from the dead. At the resurrection God fulfilled “Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.” Acts 4:10–11 Acts 13:33 Ephesians 2:20 The question: is laying the corner stone the same event as founding the earth? Sons are angels reads verses 4–7 as one creation scene, and on a first reading that is natural. Sons are believers sees two works, linked but separate: the earth founded by Christ the Creator, and Christ Himself laid as the corner stone in His triumph over death. At that, the morning stars (the angels) sing, and the sons of God, the redeemed, shout for joy, as Abraham rejoiced to see His day. John 8:56 Angels are not sons, and do not marry For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son? Hebrews 1:5 Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation? Hebrews 1:14 For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven. Matthew 22:30 For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as the angels which are in heaven. Mark 12:25 Hebrews 1:13-14 Angels serve the heirs of salvation; they are not the heirs. And the Lord Jesus uses angels as the very picture of beings who do not marry. Sons are angels, stated fairly Many faithful believers hold that the sons of God were fallen angels who took human wives. Most reject the Book of Enoch and build the case from the King James Bible. Stated as its holders would state it: In Job, the sons of God stand before the Lord in heaven, so Genesis 6 should be read the same way. Job 1:6 Job 2:1 Job 38:7 places the sons of God at the founding of the earth, before man was made. Job 38:4–7 Setting “sons of God” against “daughters of men” marks two different kinds of being. Gen 6:2 Angels have taken bodies, eaten, and been taken for men. Genesis 18:8 Genesis 19:1 Hebrews 13:2 Matthew 22:30 describes holy angels in heaven, not the ones who “left their own habitation.” Matthew 22:30 Jude 6 Jude, 2 Peter, and 1 Peter tie angelic sin to “strange flesh” and to the days of Noah. Jude 4–8 2 Pet 2:4–9 1 Pet 3:18–20 The children became “mighty men… of renown,” something beyond the ordinary. Genesis 6:4 We grant that this is a real case for angels, built from Scripture by people who love the Book. Notice, though, which angels it needs: not holy ones, but angels who had fallen or were falling in that very act. We will come back to that. The proof texts, side by side Sons are angels Sons are believers Job 38:4-7 (strongest text) The sons of God shout for joy when the earth’s foundations are laid, before Adam existed, so they must be angels. God names two works: the earth’s foundations, and the corner stone. At creation Christ is the Creator ( John 1:1–3 ), not a stone laid in His own building. The corner stone is laid in time: Christ made head of the corner when God raised Him from the dead ( Acts 4:10–11 , Ephesians 2:20 ). The sons rejoice in His triumph; the morning stars are angels, named apart from them ( Isaiah 14:12 , Revelation 12:4 ). Job 1:6 , Job 2:1 An assembly before God in heaven is an assembly of angels. Redeemed men stand in heaven ( Hebrews 12:23 ). Satan comes “among them” as accuser, not as a son. Genesis 6:2 “Sons of God” against “daughters of men” marks two kinds of being. It marks two kinds of people, as Scripture sets “the children of this world” against “the children of light” ( Luke 16:8 ). Both are men. Genesis 6:4 The unions produced the giants, or at least the extraordinary mighty men. The giants were already “in the earth in those days.” The children became “men of renown,” famous men, never called giants or hybrids. Genesis 18:8 , Genesis 19:1 , Hebrews 13:2 (strongest text) Angels can take bodies, eat, and be handled as men. An angel is a messenger, appearing as a man or as a winged creature as God sends him ( Isaiah 6:2 ). Angels are ministering spirits for the heirs of salvation ( Hebrews 1:14 ), never physically mankind. None weds or begets. Matthew 22:30 , Mark 12:25 These speak of holy angels “in heaven,” not angels who left their estate. Jesus states what angels are, not only where they are. Leaving a habitation does not grant a new nature. Jude 6-7 “In like manner… going after strange flesh” ties the angels’ sin to Sodom’s. Jude is warning about “certain men crept in unawares” (v. 4). He lists the judged: Israel destroyed in the wilderness, angels reserved in chains, Sodom and Gomorrha. Then: “Likewise also these filthy dreamers” (v. 8). It is a list of rebels destroyed, not a link between angels and strange flesh. Hell itself was prepared “for the devil and his angels” ( Matthew 25:41 ). 2 Peter 2:4-5 The angels that sinned are named right beside the Flood. Peter makes the same comparison as Jude, against false teachers (v. 1): angels, the old world, Sodom, then Lot delivered. The point is that “the Lord knoweth how… to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment” (v. 9), not that one judgment caused the next. 1 Peter 3:19-20 The spirits in prison were disobedient in the days of Noah. The spirits in prison are the disobedient of Noah’s day: scorners who heard Noah, “a preacher of righteousness” ( 2 Peter 2:5 ), while the ark was preparing, and were killed in the Flood. Genesis 6:9 “Perfect in his generations” means Noah’s line was untouched by the unions. Among the men of his time, Noah was a believer, mature in his faith. God calls Job “perfect” too ( Job 1:1 , Genesis 17:1 ). “Noah walked with God.” Jude 6, honestly And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. Jude 6 Jude 4-8 What it says Some angels did not keep their first estate. They left their own habitation. They are held in chains for the judgment. What it does not say When they left. Anything about women, marriage, or children. Anything about the Flood. The Sons are believers reading, held with an open hand: unclean spirits seek a habitation in men. The wickedness of Noah’s day may well have included spirits possessing men, as they still do, with no bodies, wives, or children of their own. Where Scripture is not plain, we should not build a doctrine. Matt 12:43–45 Angels in the form of men What Sons are angels rightly sees: angels have appeared as men, eaten a meal, and taken men by the hand. Some have entertained angels unawares. Genesis 18:8 Genesis 19:1 Hebrews 13:2 What Scripture also shows An angel is a messenger sent from God, and appears in whatever form God sends him: as men at Abraham’s tent, as six-winged seraphims in Isaiah’s vision. Isaiah 6:2 Hebrews calls them “ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation.” They are spirits who serve the sons of God, not mankind in the flesh. Heb 1:14 At Sodom, the angels are the ones defended, not the ones defiled. The lust belongs to the men of the city, and the angels strike them blind. Gen 19:10–11 No angel who appears as a man ever weds a woman or fathers a child. Appearing as a man for a message is not becoming a man for a marriage. The Flood settled it either way Whatever those unions were, God destroyed them. “Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.” Genesis 7:23 How Jesus told it In Noah’s days they were eating, drinking, marrying, and giving in marriage. Ordinary marriages of ordinary men. Matt 24:37–39 Luke 17:26–27 Never again After the Flood, Scripture never records another union of angels and women. If it happened once, it left no trace in the rest of the Book. Still today Possession by unclean spirits appears again and again, and missionaries still meet it. Mark 5 Acts 16:16 One explanation fits what Scripture keeps showing us. The other requires an event Scripture never shows again. Giants are men Genesis 6:4 says there were giants “also after that.” The rest of the Bible shows exactly that: tall men, after the Flood, with no angels involved. The sons of Anak, “which come of the giants.” Numbers 13:33 The Emims, “a people great, and many, and tall.” Deut 2:10–11 Og of Bashan, whose iron bed was nine cubits long, about thirteen and a half feet. Deuteronomy 3:11 Goliath of Gath, six cubits and a span, nearly ten feet. 1 Samuel 17:4 A man of great stature with six fingers and six toes, “born to the giant,” slain by David’s men. 2 Sam 21:20–22 In living memory, Robert Wadlow (1918–1940) stood 8 feet 11 inches tall. Great stature is a human trait, then and now. It needs no angelic father. Do not shift the blame And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat. And the Lord God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat. Genesis 3:12-13 Since the garden, man has pointed somewhere else. God answered each one for his own sin. But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed. James 1:14 In Genesis 6, God names one guilty party: man. Even if spirits were at work in that day, His verdict is “the wickedness of man.” A teaching that moves the weight of Genesis 6 onto a demonic host moves it where God did not put it, under either view. Genesis 6:5 Grant that they were angels Suppose the case for angels is right. Then they were not holy angels, who keep their estate. They were fallen angels, rebels against God in the very act of Genesis 6. So the question becomes: would God call those His sons? What Scripture says of fallen angels They share the devil’s final destination: hell, “prepared for the devil and his angels.” Matthew 25:41 Even wicked men are called “children of the devil” and “children of disobedience.” 1 John 3:10 Eph 2:2 John 8:44 God never calls an angel His son, holy or fallen. Hebrews 1:5 What Scripture says of sons who sin They are still sons. Just Lot was a righteous man while he vexed his soul in Sodom. 2 Pet 2:7–8 God’s sons are warned to come out and be separate, not yoked with unbelievers. 2 Cor 6:14 2 Cor 6:17–18 Israel was not to marry the nations, “for they will turn away thy son from following me.” Deut 7:3–4 Sons are made in His image So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. Genesis 1:27 Genesis 1:26-27 Man Made in the image and likeness of God. Christ took on Him the seed of Abraham, so that men might become sons by faith. Hebrews 2:16 John 1:12 Angels Spirits, created by Him and for His purpose, not made in His likeness. Colossians 1:16 Hebrews 1:14 Salvation is never offered to them: “he took not on him the nature of angels.” Hebrews 2:16 James, answering what “a man may say,” notes that “the devils also believe, and tremble.” Even so, that is not belief unto salvation, because saving grace was never extended to them. Sonship by faith is offered only to the creature made in God’s image. Jas 2:18–19 A note on the fringe The Book of Enoch, the “Watchers,” and giants thousands of feet tall are not found in the Bible, and they have no place in this study. Most who hold Sons are angels reject them as well. Jude’s quoting one prophecy of Enoch no more makes that book Scripture than Paul’s quoting pagan poets makes their writings Scripture. Jude 14 Acts 17:28 Titus 1:12 Proverbs 30:6 Romans 14:5 Be fully persuaded One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind. Romans 14:5 ✦ ✦ ✦ We have laid out both views and shown our work. Now search the Scriptures for yourself, as the Bereans did, and weigh these questions: Acts 17:11 Who does Scripture call the sons of God? Who is the corner stone of Job 38? Whose wickedness did God judge in Genesis 6? Would God call fallen angels His sons? Whichever way you land, Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord , by faith. Genesis 6: The Days of Noah How short the time was from the garden to the Flood, and how far man fell: wickedness only evil continually, God's grief and judgment, and Noah finding grace and walking with God by faith. As the days of Noah were, so shall the coming of the Son of man be. Genesis 6 – The Days of Noah A study in Genesis 6 The Days of Noah Man’s wickedness, God’s judgment, and grace found by faith. Genesis 6:1-9 ✦ ✦ ✦ Use the arrow keys or swipe to move. Tap any reference to read the verse. Only a short while after creation Genesis 6 is not far removed from the garden. Adding the ages given in Genesis 5, the whole world before the Flood fits inside a few overlapping lifetimes. 930 Adam dies. Noah’s father Lamech is already 56. 1056 Noah is born. 1656 Methuselah dies, at 969. 1656 The Flood, in Noah’s 600th year. Years counted from creation by the ages in Genesis 5 and 7. Genesis 5:27 Genesis 7:6 Men who had heard of Eden from Adam’s own mouth were alive when Noah’s father was born. And still, within ten generations, mankind had fallen so utterly that it corrupted the earth itself. The pattern of salvation The story of the patriarchs from Adam to Noah is a pattern of salvation given to us by God. Man has always been saved by grace through faith. By faith Noah, being warned of God of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith. Hebrews 11:7 Noah walked as Enoch walked “Enoch walked with God.” “Noah walked with God.” A just man, perfect in his generations, who found grace in the eyes of the Lord . Genesis 5:22 Genesis 6:8–9 Grace, then and now “For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.” Eph 2:8–9 When men began to multiply And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them, That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose. And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years. Genesis 6:1-3 The sons of God chose wives by sight: “that they were fair.” Not by faith, but by what pleased the eye. The Lord said His Spirit would not always strive with man, “for that he also is flesh.” To limit the wickedness of man, God set his days at an hundred and twenty years, and man’s natural life began to shorten. Who are the sons of God? This study reads them as believers, those who “call upon the name of the Lord .” Faithful believers differ here, and we cover both views in depth in Genesis 6 – Sons of God ↗ . Gen 4:26 John 1:12 Giants in the earth There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old , men of renown . Genesis 6:4 Giants were already there “In those days,” before the text describes the unions. And “also after that.” The children were men Mighty men of renown. Of great stature, no doubt, as we see in Goliath and his people, and even occasionally today. 1 Samuel 17:4 Numbers 13:33 The genetic potential of man is what it is, divinely made. Only evil continually And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. Romans: A Logical Argument - Understanding the Form and Format Romans: A Logical Argument Understanding the Form and Format of the Epistle In the epistle, or letter, to the Romans, Paul is using a dialectical format called a Diatribe . Dialectic: Discovering Truth Through Logical Exchange In an argument presentation, dialectic is a method of reasoning that seeks to discover truth through the exchange and logical reconciliation of opposing ideas. It is a process of critical analysis and dialogue (or even a single structured presentation) that aims for a higher, more comprehensive understanding rather than simply "winning" a debate. Diatribe: A Vigorous, Conversational Moral Discourse A diatribe (Greek diatribē, meaning "pastime" or "discourse") was a form of popular moral discourse or lecture among Greek and Roman philosophers. It is an oral or written presentation that uses a vigorous, conversational style to explore ethical questions and find truth. Dialogical Approach: It often employed a dialogue format with an imaginary or hypothetical opponent ( interlocutor ). It used a question-and-answer structure, rhetorical questions, and responses to anticipated objections. This was an extension of the Socratic method, designed to guide students or listeners to a better understanding of a philosophical point. Moral Exhortation: The primary goal was not simply debate, but moral instruction and persuasion. It aimed to expose contradictions in the audience's presuppositions and help them overcome false and biased ideas they held. Accessible Style: The language used is often colloquial, direct, and sometimes informal. It utilized colorful, everyday imagery, anecdotes, and historical examples to make complex philosophical ideas accessible to a general audience. Focus on a Single Theme: These discourses typically centered on a single ethical or philosophical theme. Paul’s overall theme is the election of grace , the understanding that the Gentile believers in Christ were as much God’s chosen people and equal part of the Kingdom as Jewish believers, and the implications of salvation by grace through faith for the believer’s life. The Connective Tissue: Inferential and Explanatory Words Words like "For," "Because," "Wherefore," and "Therefore" are not prepositions; they are logical connectors or inferential markers. They are essential transitional phrases that structure the debate, allowing the reader to trace Paul's logic from premises to conclusions. 1. Explanatory (Causal) Markers: "For" & "Because" These introduce the reason or cause behind a previous statement. They tell the reader, "Here is the evidence that supports what I just said." 2. Inferential (Conclusive) Markers: "Wherefore" & "Therefore" These introduce the consequence or conclusion drawn from the preceding facts. They tell the reader, "Based on everything I just proved, this is the logical outcome." Marker Type Key Words Function in Argument Explanatory (Premise) For (gar), Because Introduces the reason, evidence, or bedrock doctrine that justifies the preceding claim. Inferential (Conclusion) Therefore (dio, oun, ara), Wherefore Introduces the logical outcome or major implication of the premises just established. Paul’s Logical, “If/Then” Structure Paul’s diatribe uses a logical, “if/then” structure. He teaches the bedrock doctrines of faith as the building blocks for the main argument. IF Everyone (Jew & Gentile) is under sin. THEN Salvation is by grace through faith. THEREFORE Gentile believers are equal in the Kingdom. HOW THEN Should believers live?

Romans 2: The Inescapable Judgment Romans 2:1-11 on the judgment of God that no man escapes, Jew or Gentile, by judging others. Romans 2:1-11 - The Inescapable Judgment WEEK 3: ROMANS 2:1-11 The Inescapable Judgment 1. The Inexcusable Judge ( Romans 2:1-4 ) Paul is shifting his diatribe (a logical argument to persuade) from the Reprobate (Rom 1) to the person who would judge them, using the hypothetical Interlocutor ("O man"). The Condemnation of the Judge: "Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest". You Condemn Yourself: "for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself". The Judge Commits the Same Sins: "for thou that judgest doest the same things". The Concept of Wrath for Sin: Paul used the extreme case of Reprobates to establish the concept of wrath for sin. Recognizing the wrath of God against the reprobates means we who do any of the same are just as guilty. All are Accountable: Paul established that even heathens know enough about God to be held accountable. God is Just: "We are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things". 2. The Treasury of Wrath ( Romans 2:5-6 ) Paul is introducing a concept of judgment similar to accounting or bookkeeping. The sinner who persists in sin is actively building a record with God, not escaping. You Cannot Escape: "If you think you aren’t subject to the same wrath as the worst reprobate, you are wrong. None shall escape the judgment of God". The Sinner Builds an Account: The sinner "builds up an account with God". Storing Up Wrath: "Thou... treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God". The Final Standard: God will judge all men: "He will render to every man according to his deeds". 3. Judgment by Deeds and Recompense ( Romans 2:6-9 ) Just as the Reprobate receives the appropriate recompense for their error, so too does every man. CONDUCT (The Deeds) RECOMPENSE (The Judgment) Patient Continuance in Well Doing (Seeking for glory and honour and immortality) Eternal Life Contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness Indignation and Wrath, Tribulation and Anguish 4. No Respect of Persons ( Romans 2:9-11 ) Paul introduces another key theme of the Epistle to the Romans: Jews and Gentiles are all treated the same by God. Wrath or Peace for All: Wrath or peace is given "to the Jew first, and also of the Gentile (Greek)". The Final Rule: "For there is no respect of persons with God".
