Salvation: A Finished Work by Grace Through Faith Salvation: A Finished Work By Grace Through Faith I. The Drawing to Christ – Distinct Roles in the Godhead John 6:44 No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day. (The Father draws men to Jesus before the crucifixion.) John 12:32 And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me. (Jesus draws all men to Himself after the crucifixion.) John 16:8-11 And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged. Note: The Holy Spirit is never said to "draw" men to Christ; His role is conviction of the world concerning sin (unbelief), righteousness (now in Christ), and judgment (already executed on Satan, unbelievers in the time to come), alongside regeneration and sealing. II. How Faith Comes, Justification, and Imputation of Righteousness Romans 10:17 So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Romans 4:5-8 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. Romans 5:1-2 Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand... Romans 5:9 Much more then, being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him. 2 Corinthians 5:21 For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. At the moment of faith, God declares the believer righteous – justification – by imputing Christ’s perfect righteousness to us and our sin to Him. This is the Father’s judicial act based on the Son’s work at the cross. III. The Full Scope of Salvation – Reconciled by His Death, Saved by His Life John 19:30 When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost. Romans 5:10 For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. Romans 5:11 And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement. Romans 4:25 Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification. The redemptive price and atonement were fully paid and finished at the cross – “It is finished.” Christ still has future acts to do, the rapture/resurrection, the rewards of the faithful, the wrath on the unbelieving, Millennial rule- But reconciliation was finished by His death on the cross. Reconciliation is by His death alone. But the ongoing and ultimate salvation – deliverance from sin’s power, wrath, and presence – is by His resurrection, by His life, the living union with the risen Christ who ever lives. IV. Regeneration, Renewing, and Baptism by the Holy Spirit at the Moment of Faith (This is the Spirit’s baptizing us into Christ – placing us into the body of Christ – and the new birth.) Titus 3:5 Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost. John 3:5-6 Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. 1 Corinthians 12:13 For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit. Ephesians 1:13 In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise. All this happens the instant we believe: the Holy Spirit regenerates us (new birth), renews us, baptizes us into vital union with the living Christ, and seals us forever as God’s possession as the ernest towards the purchased possession. Electing us to be predestinated to be conformed to His image and glorified, adopted as children and made join-heirs with Christ to the Kingdom. V. Adoption and the Future Consummation – The Day of Redemption (Our Blessed Hope) Titus 2:13 Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ; Romans 8:23 And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. Ephesians 1:14 Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory. Ephesians 4:30 And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption. 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17 For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord. The payment was finished at the cross, but the full possession of the purchased inheritance – including the redemption of our body at the rapture – is the blessed hope we eagerly await. This is when the living Christ personally takes His church to Himself. VI. The Cosmic Reconciliation, Restitution of All Things, and Revelation of Christ’s Kingdom Colossians 1:20 And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven. Revelation 11:15 And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever. Revelation 12:10 And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night. Philippians 2:10-11 That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. The price was paid in full at the cross; the full cosmic reconciliation and open manifestation of Christ’s kingdom – Satan cast down forever, every knee bowing – awaits future enforcement when the living Christ returns in glory to subdue all things. VII. The Three Forms of Sanctification and Present Position (All believers are set apart unto God, elected unto obedience and service now, and made joint-heirs with Christ to reign in the coming kingdom.) Positional Sanctification (Past, completed at salvation) 1 Corinthians 6:11 And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God. Hebrews 10:10 By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. 1 Peter 1:2 Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ... Practical/Progressive Sanctification (Present, ongoing growth) 1 Thessalonians 5:23 And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. 2 Corinthians 3:18 But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory... Ephesians 2:10 For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them. Ultimate Sanctification (Future, complete conformity) 1 John 3:2 Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is. Philippians 3:21 Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body... Romans 8:17 And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. 2 Timothy 2:12 If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us. VIII. Intercession – The Present High Priestly Ministry of the Living Christ Hebrews 7:25 Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them. Romans 8:34 Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us. The living Christ continually intercedes for us, applying the benefits of the cross until He comes again to fully possess what He has purchased in the reconciliation. Conclusion: Eternal Security Reconciled by His Death, Saved by His Life, Awaiting the Blessed Hope John 10:28-29 And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand. Romans 8:38-39 For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. 1 Peter 1:3-5 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you, Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. The payment and legal basis were perfectly finished at the cross (“It is finished”), reconciling all of creation to God, giving us access to His grace the moment we believe. But the Scripture plainly teaches the “much more” salvation – eternal life, deliverance, and final redemption – is by the life of the risen Christ who ever lives. We have eternal life now because He lives, we are kept by His life now, that we shall be openly glorified when He appears – that blessed hope wherein the full victory purchased at the cross is manifested for all to see, raised up incorruptable, and we reign with Him as joint-heirs forever.

Romans 4: Abraham Believed God Abraham believed God and it was counted for righteousness, with the lineage from Adam to the twelve tribes. Romans 4: Faith and Righteousness Romans Chapter 4 The Foundation of Righteousness by Faith 1-8 What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt. But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works , Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. 9-12 Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness . How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also: And the father of circumcision to them who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised. 13-17 For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness of faith . For if they which are of the law be heirs, faith is made void, and the promise made of none effect: Because the law worketh wrath: for where no law is, there is no transgression. Therefore it is of faith, that it might be by grace ; to the end the promise might be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham ; who is the father of us all, ( As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations, ) before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were. 18-22 Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations, according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be. And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sarah's womb: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God; And being fully persuaded that, what he had promised, he was able also to perform. And therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness. 23-25 Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; But for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead; Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification . Romans 5: Peace and Grace Peace with God through justification by faith, atonement and reconciliation, the fall in Genesis 3 as its background, and the key verses on justification. Romans 5: Peace and Grace Romans Chapter 5 Peace with God and the Gift of Grace 1-5 Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God. And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us. 6-11 For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly. For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: yet peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die. But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Much more then, being now justified by his blood , we shall be saved from wrath through him. For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life. And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement. 12-17 Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned: (For until the law sin was in the world: but sin is not imputed when there is no law. Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come. But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many . And not as it was by one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment was by one to condemnation, but the free gift is of many offences unto justification. For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.) 18-21 Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification of life . For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord. A dramatic visual reference for Sunday School • Based on the King James Bible Atonement & Reconciliation in Romans Atonement & Reconciliation in Romans The Word “Atonement” Appears 70 times in the KJV 69 times in the Old Testament Once in the New Testament 70 — God’s number of divine completion and perfection Romans 5:11 (KJV) “And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement .” This “atonement” translates the Greek katallagē (καταλλαγή) , meaning reconciliation — the restoration of a broken relationship, bringing sinful humanity back into favor and peace with a holy God. Modern translations miss the mark. Key Verses Romans 5:10 “For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” Romans 5:11 “...by whom we have now received the atonement [ reconciliation ].” Atonement and Reconciliation are synonymous: God’s purchase of the sins of the world by the blood of Christ This brings the offer of peace with God through the gift of salvation — a gift that must be received by faith Genesis 3: The Fall of Man Genesis Chapter 3 The Fall of Man and the First Promise 1-5 Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said , Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden? And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die. And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die : For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil. 6-8 And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat . And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons. And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God amongst the trees of the garden. 9-13 And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou? And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself. And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat? And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat. And the Lord God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat. 14-19 And the Lord God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. For when ye were the servants of sin, ye were free from righteousness. What fruit had ye then in those things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death . For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. • Based on the King James Bible Romans 6: Baptism into Christ Baptism in Romans 6 "Baptized into Christ" • Spiritual Union vs. Water Baptism The Greek word baptisma means to immerse or become part of by immersion. In the New Testament it does not always refer to water baptism. In Romans 6, Paul describes believers being baptized into Jesus Christ and into his death (vv. 3-4)—a spiritual reality accomplished by the Holy Spirit at the moment of faith, placing us in union with Christ's death, burial, and resurrection. This is the baptism of regeneration (the baptism with fire). It is not referring to water baptism, which is only an outward symbol. Spiritual Baptism into Christ (By the Holy Spirit • Real Union • Regeneration) Water Baptism (Outward Symbol • Ordinance • Testimony) Romans 6:3-4 Baptized into Jesus Christ... baptized into his death... buried with him by baptism into death... raised to newness of life. An outward act in water, picturing the spiritual reality already accomplished. 1 Corinthians 12:13 For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body... Performed by men (e.g., Philip baptizing the eunuch in water – Acts 8:36-38 ). Galatians 3:27 For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Follows faith; a public testimony ( Acts 8:36-38 – “If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest”). Places believer in Christ instantly upon faith; the real identification that makes us dead to sin and alive to God. A like figure (symbol) of salvation, not the cause ( 1 Peter 3:21 – “The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us... the answer of a good conscience toward God”). Happens to all true believers the moment they believe; no delay possible. Can be separated from receiving the Spirit ( Acts 8:12-16 – Samaritans baptized in water but later received the Spirit; Acts 10:44-48 – Cornelius’ household received Spirit first, then water baptized). The baptism with the Holy Ghost and fire that John said Christ would bring (Matt. 3:11); regeneration itself. John preached “the baptism of repentance” (change of mind) to prepare for Christ ( Mark 1:4 ; Acts 19:4 ). Paul’s primary mission: the spiritual baptism that unites us to Christ ( 1 Cor. 1:17 – “Christ sent me not to baptize [in water], but to preach the gospel”). Important ordinance, but secondary to the gospel; Paul distinguished it from his main calling. Key Insight: Water baptism and the Spirit’s baptism are sometimes separate in Acts, proving they are distinct . The baptism in Romans 6 is the spiritual placement into Christ —the real union that makes us dead to sin and alive to God through the baptism of regeneration by the Holy Spirit. • Based on the King James Bible Romans Key Verses: Justification & Grace Romans Key Verses Justification by Faith & the Gift of Grace • Selected Passages from Romans 1–5 Romans 1:16-17 For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ : for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. Romans 7: The Struggle with Sin The law, the age of accountability, and the old man against the new: O wretched man that I am. Romans 7: The Struggle with Sin Romans Chapter 7 The Believer's Struggle • The Law, Sin, and the Flesh 1-6 Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,) how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth? For the woman which hath an husband is bound by the law to her husband so long as he liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband... Wherefore, my brethren, ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ ; that ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God . For when we were in the flesh, the motions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members to bring forth fruit unto death. But now we are delivered from the law , that being dead wherein we were held; that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter . 7-13 What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet. But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence . For without the law sin was dead. For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died. And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death. For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me . Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good . Was then that which is good made death unto me? God forbid. But sin, that it might appear sin, working death in me by that which is good; that sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful. 14-20 For we know that the law is spiritual : but I am carnal, sold under sin . For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I. If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good. Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me . For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not. For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do. Now if I do that I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me . 21-25 I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me. For I delight in the law of God after the inward man : But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind , and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members. O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin. A dramatic visual reference for Young Adult Sunday School • Based on the King James Bible Romans 7:7-13 • The Age of Accountability Romans 7:7-13 The Age of Accountability • The Holy Law Reveals Sin 7-13 What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law : for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet. But sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. For without the law sin was dead . For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died. And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death. For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me. Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good . Key Principle from Romans: Where there is no law, sin is not imputed (Romans 4:15; 5:13). Without knowledge of God's commandment, there is no conscious transgression — and therefore no imputation of sin. The Age of Accountability Young children and the mentally challenged who lack the capacity to understand God's moral law are not condemned for sin in the same way as those who knowingly rebel. God judges according to the light received — and where moral understanding is absent, He does not impute guilt. After the death of the infant son born to David and Bathsheba, David declared with confidence: “I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me” (2 Samuel 12:23) —expressing his assurance that he would one day be reunited with his child in heaven. Matthew 18:3 And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. Jesus holds up the humble, trusting nature of little children as the pattern for entering the kingdom — affirming their innocence and safe standing before God. Romans Chapter 8 • No Condemnation • Life in the Spirit Romans Chapter 8 No Condemnation • Life & Victory in the Spirit 1-4 There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus , who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death . For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh: That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. 5-11 For they that are after the flesh do mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit. For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace . Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be. So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God. But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit , if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his. And if Christ be in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the Spirit is life because of righteousness. But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you . 12-17 Therefore, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh. For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die: but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live. For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God . For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together. 18-23 For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us . For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope, Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God . For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body . 24-27 For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for? But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it. Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered . And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God. 28-30 And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God , to them who are the called according to his purpose. For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren. Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified. 31-39 What shall we then say to these things? If God be for us, who can be against us? He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things? Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God's elect? It is God that justifieth. Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us. Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us . For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh: Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed . For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sara shall have a son. 10-13 And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac; (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;) It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated . 14-18 What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid. A dramatic visual reference for Young Adult Sunday School • Based on the King James Bible Malachi 1 & Romans 9 • Jacob Loved, Esau Hated Malachi 1 & Romans 9 Jacob Loved, Esau Hated • Nations, Not Individuals Malachi 1:1-3 The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi. I have loved you , saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau , and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness. Romans 9:13 As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated . Genesis 25:21-23 • The Prophecy And Isaac intreated the LORD for his wife, because she was barren: and the LORD was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived. And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to enquire of the LORD. And the LORD said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger . The Meaning of "Loved" and "Hated" In Scripture, "loved" and "hated" often mean preferred over or chosen above the other, not absolute personal hatred or despising as we use the words today. Jesus said: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:26). This does not mean literal hatred or despising of family, but to love and prefer Christ more than all others — to place Him first. In the same way, "I loved Jacob, but Esau have I hated" means God preferred/chose Jacob's line over Esau's — not that He personally despised Esau as an individual. The Context: Nations, Not Individuals • The reference is not to the individual twins at birth in Genesis 25. • It is not about God hating and condemning Esau personally in the womb. • Esau was reconciled with Jacob, received his own blessing from Isaac, and lived prosperously (Genesis 33; 36). • The statement concerns the nations that came from them: Israel (Jacob) vs. Edom (Esau). • Edom (the nation) fell away, refused to help Israel in the wilderness, rejoiced in Judah’s captivity, and was ultimately destroyed ~1400 years later (Obadiah; Malachi 1:4). • Paul uses this to show: God’s choice of one nation/line over another (by grace, not works) is consistent — just as Gentiles are now grafted in while partial hardness came to unbelieving Jews (Romans 11). God Judges Individuals by Faith • Nations by Works • God judges individuals according to faith — whether they believe and call upon the Lord (Romans 10:13; Genesis 4:26). • Nations are judged here on earth according to their works and collective actions — obedience or rebellion, mercy or enmity (e.g., Edom’s treatment of Israel led to national judgment). Esau personally was blessed and reconciled; Edom as a nation was judged for its unbelief and hostility. The same principle applies in Romans: believing Jews and Gentiles are saved by faith; the unbelieving nation faced hardening and partial blindness. The phrase "Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated" refers to God’s preference of one nation over another — not personal hatred of Esau as an individual. "Loved" and "hated" here mean preferred/chosen above, just as Jesus taught to "hate" family in comparison to loving Him supremely. Individuals are judged by faith; nations are judged here on earth by their works. Paul’s point: God’s choice of lines/nations by grace is biblical — consistent with the gospel to the Gentiles and the pattern throughout Scripture. A dramatic visual reference for Young Adult Sunday School • Based on the King James Bible One People of God • From Adam to Christ One People of God From Adam to Christ • The Called-Out by Faith Beginning with Seth • Calling on the Name of the Lord And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD (Genesis 4:26). For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved (Romans 10:13). The line of faith — those who call on the Lord — begins early, with Seth’s generation, not limited to physical descent from Abraham. The Sons of God • Believers in the Coming Redeemer For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God (Romans 8:14). The “sons of God” throughout Scripture have always been believers looking to the Redeemer who liveth — from Adam’s faithful line through the patriarchs, prophets, and now all who are in Christ by faith. The Inward Jew & Circumcision of the Heart For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh: But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God (Romans 2:28–29). Not All Israel Which Are of Israel For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel : Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed (Romans 9:6–8). Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise (Galatians 4:28). Gentiles Once Strangers • Now Fellowcitizens Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh... That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world : But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ... Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God (Ephesians 2:11–13, 19). One in Christ • No Distinction There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus . And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise (Galatians 3:28–29). For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus (Galatians 3:26). All Israel Shall Be Saved • The Israel of God And so all Israel shall be saved : as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob (Romans 11:26). And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God (Galatians 6:16). The New & Better Covenant In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away (Hebrews 8:13). But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises (Hebrews 8:6). Scripture reveals one continuous called-out assembly — the sons of God: all believers in the Redeemer which liveth, from Adam and Seth’s line calling on the Lord, through Abraham, Isaac, and the remnant, to all who are in Christ. Gentiles, once aliens and strangers, are now fellowcitizens with the saints — made one body, the true Israel of God by faith. The only change: the Old Covenant (with its shadows and types) is done away — fulfilled and replaced by the New and better Covenant with better promises in Christ. No separate peoples: Jew and Gentile together form the Israel of God — defined by faith from beginning to end. A dramatic visual reference for Young Adult Sunday School • Based on the King James Bible Dispensation • Biblical Stewardship of the Gospel Dispensation Biblical Stewardship • Household Management of the Gospel The Greek Word Oikonomia The word "Dispensation" in the Greek, Oikonomia literally comes from οἶκος (oikos = "house") + νόμος (nomos = "law" or "management/rule"), so it fundamentally means "household management," "administration," or "stewardship." A steward or house manager is entrusted to oversee, protect, and faithfully distribute what belongs to the master — in this case, Paul compares his role to being entrusted with the gospel to faithfully preach and deliver it to others. 1 Corinthians 9:17 For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me. Ephesians 3:2 If ye have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me to you-ward. Colossians 1:25 Whereof I am made a minister, according to the dispensation of God which is given to me for you, to fulfil the word of God. Ephesians 1:10 That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him. Paul's Use of the Term In the three passages where Paul applies "dispensation" to himself (1 Cor 9:17, Eph 3:2, Col 1:25), he is saying he has been entrusted/stewarded with the gospel and the grace of God to faithfully preach and administer it to others. In Ephesians 1:10, the term refers to God's own stewardship/dispensation over the entire fullness of times, gathering all things together in Christ at the end. We all have a dispensation of the gospel — to keep the faith. One continuous gospel in Christ from Adam through today. God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son... (Hebrews 1:1-2). The difference over time was revelation of mysteries, given by the word of God through the prophets, the preaching of Christ, and the inspired New Testament authors, which gives us full revelation. The Old Testament replaced by the New — a physical nation with a spiritual one. The Bible does not say anywhere that there is a "Church age," or various "church ages" (Revelation 1-3). The "Church" is the called-out assembly of believers at the resurrection or individual independent congregations gathering at their local NT church. A dramatic visual reference for Young Adult Sunday School • Based on the King James Bible Comparative Theologies • Romans 11 Spectrum A Theological Spectrum Dispensationalism, Replacement and Covenant Theology, and other viewpoints in light of the Bible Introduction "I have no problem with the word 'dispensation.' It is a Bible word, but I do have a problem with dispensationalism which says that salvation comes in different ways in different dispensations." — Bro. Jack Hyles We'll start with views many of us have heard, move through the spectrum, hit the biblical center, then see how far some drift into error. Next: Mild Dispensationalism → Mild Dispensationalism Teaches Dispensations as stewardships or "administrations" (from the Greek oikonomia) — different ways God interacts with and tests humanity in various eras of history. Salvation is always by grace through faith alone in the promised Christ (Eph 2:8–9), looking forward to the cross (though some teach the understanding of a Messiah wasn't always clear — "through a glass darkly"). Common eras taught include: Innocence (Garden of Eden), Conscience (after fall to flood), Human Government (Noah onward), Promise (Abraham to Moses), Law (Moses to Christ), Grace/Church Age (Pentecost to rapture), Kingdom/Millennium (future 1,000-year reign). Emphasizes end-times prophecy and charts laying out the timing of events according to their theology. Holds to a future 7-year Tribulation, pre-tribulation rapture, and eventual Millennial kingdom; rejects post-millennial, amillennial, and preterist views. Sees future restoration of the physical nation of Israel during the Tribulation, where many (if not all) Jews will see the signs and wonders and turn to Christ. Uses Romans 11:26 as support. Who Generally Holds This View? Most Independent Fundamental Baptists (IFB), many conservative evangelicals, Bible churches, teachers like Jack Hyles, John R. Rice. Strength Strongly affirms one way of salvation—grace through faith in Christ—in every era, whether OT saints looking forward to the promised Savior or NT believers looking back to the cross. Provides room for disagreement on exact timing of end-times events (e.g., pre-, mid-, or post-tribulation rapture details) to avoid division among believers, and acts as a practical compromise with the prevailing theology in modern evangelical circles. Issue Uses "dispensation" to refer to distinct ages/eras with different tests/rules of responsibility, which the Bible does not explicitly define this way. May unintentionally suggest that the "church" is separate from Israel, with corporate Israel receiving promises and inheritance that are promised to all believers as a whole (see Gal 3:28–29; Eph 2:14–19—one body, one faith, no distinction in Christ). Next: Traditional Dispensationalism / Zionism → Traditional Dispensationalism / Zionism Teaches God works in distinct dispensations/ages with different tests/rules of responsibility (e.g., innocence, law, grace). The Church is seen as a "parenthesis" in God's primary plan for Israel — an ultimate failure or incomplete entity necessitating the future restoration of physical/national Israel. Uses the 7 churches in Revelation 1–3 as prophetic of distinct "church ages" (e.g., Ephesus = apostolic, Laodicea = apostate modern Church). Holds to a future literal 7-year Tribulation, pre-tribulation rapture of the Church, second coming, and restored national Israel in a literal millennial kingdom (with temple sacrifices as memorials). Ethnic Israel is still God's chosen people today, despite apostasy, with unconditional future promises to the nation as a whole. Pays lip-service to salvation always being by grace through faith, but often drifts into implying the OT dispensation required obedience to the law/works for blessing or acceptance. Who Generally Holds This View? Traditional dispensationalists, many Southern Baptists, Calvary Chapel, popular prophecy teachers (e.g., Tim LaHaye, John Walvoord, Hal Lindsey), and organizations like those associated with Scofield Bible notes. Strength Takes OT prophecies literally and emphasizes God's faithfulness to His promises. Strongly promotes evangelism and end-times awareness. Issue Pays lip-service to salvation always being by grace through faith, but often drifts into implying the OT dispensation required works of the law for acceptance/blessing. Treats the "Church" as an ultimate failure necessitating the restoration of physical Israel. Uses the 7 churches in Revelation as distinct ages of the "Church" (not stated in text). Sees ethnic Israel currently as still God's chosen people despite apostasy, potentially downplaying the NT emphasis on faith alone and one body in Christ (Gal 3:28–29; Eph 2:14–19). Next: Replacement Theology → Replacement Theology Teaches The Church directly replaces Israel because of Israel's rejection of Christ. Israel has forfeited its promises and role as God's chosen nation; the Church inherits them spiritually. The New Covenant replaces the Old (Heb 8:13). OT promises (land, kingdom, blessings) are transferred to or fulfilled in the Church. No future distinct restoration or role for ethnic/national Israel as a nation. Any salvation for Jews is individual entry into the Church. Strongly affirms the biblical pattern of God choosing the lesser over the greater, the younger over the older, the new over the old (e.g., Seth over Cain, Isaac over Ishmael, Jacob over Esau, Judah over Reuben, David over Saul, Esther over Vashti, publicans/harlots over Pharisees, etc.). Who Generally Holds This View? Many Independent Fundamental Baptists (especially NIFB and some who embrace the "replacement" label), conservative evangelicals who reject Zionism, post-trib/pre-wrath teachers, and others who emphasize the NT's fulfillment language while rejecting dispensational future-national-Israel programs. Note on Historic Premillennialism Some who hold a similar view of replacement/fulfillment and a future literal kingdom for all believers (Jew and Gentile together) call it "historic premillennialism" — future millennium after Christ's return, no pre-trib rapture, no separate Israel program. Strength Faithfully highlights the biblical pattern of replacement/fulfillment (lesser over greater, new over old) seen throughout Scripture. Rejects Zionism and any separate future program for national Israel. Holds to post-trib/pre-wrath timing and a millennial kingdom for all believers (Jew and Gentile together). Emphasizes faith in Christ alone and warns against relying on physical descent or works. Issue Can create too sharp a break with OT believers (while still acknowledging them as part of the Church), and in defending against critics sometimes over-emphasizes discontinuity and misses the full continuity of one vine/assembly by faith from Adam to now (Rom 11:16–24; Heb 11:39–40). Next: Biblical Fundamentalism → Biblical Fundamentalism Teaches One continuous vine/root in Christ (Rom 11:16–24): natural (Jewish) and wild (Gentile) branches one congregation/assembly in resurrection. All saved by calling on the Lord (Rom 10:13; Gen 4:26), knowing Redeemer liveth (Job 19:25), esteeming Christ's riches. Gospel preached, witnessed by Moses/prophets (Heb 4:2; 1 Pet 1:10–12), testified by apostles (1 Tim 2:6), unbroken to believers today. Various covenants/revelations, but salvation always grace through faith — no different gospels. New Covenant ends Old (Heb 8:13); physical nation to spiritual (1 Pet 2:9). No separate peoples/programs — unbelief cuts off, faith grafts in, mercy to whosoever believes. Who Generally Holds This View? Bible-believing Christians rejecting covenant over-spiritualization and dispensational insertions, prioritizing plain text (many IFB, independent Baptists). Key Scriptures Rom 11:16–24 (one olive tree); Gal 3:28–29 (one in Christ); Eph 4:4–6 (one body); Heb 11:39–40 (OT perfected with us); Rev 7:9–17 (all nations redeemed). Strength Lets Scripture speak plainly — one gospel by grace through faith from Genesis to Revelation, one people (Israel of God by faith), no inserted programs or multiple gospels. Issue None — aligns with NT teaching and avoids extremes. Next: Supersessionism → Supersessionism Teaches Church supersedes/replaces Israel in God's plan due to unbelief. OT promises fulfilled spiritually in Church. No distinct future for ethnic Israel; salvation for Jews is individual conversion into Church. Often amillennial; no literal future kingdom. Who Generally Holds This View? Roman Catholic Church, Eastern Orthodox, many mainline Protestants (Methodist, Episcopal), some early Church Fathers. Strength Affirms fulfillment in Christ and unity by faith. Issue May imply God abandoned Israel (contrary to Rom 11:1–2). Over-spiritualizes NT eschatology, potentially downplaying literal future resurrection/reign for all believers (Rev 20:4–6). Next: Mid-Acts Dispensationalism → Mid-Acts Dispensationalism Teaches Church begins mid-Acts (Acts 9/13) with Paul, not Pentecost. Early Acts under "Kingdom gospel" for Jews (baptism, signs). Paul's gospel distinct for Gentiles. Twists "rightly dividing" (2 Tim 2:15) to claim two gospels. Adds works subtly to both. False notion Paul's gospel different from Abraham's (Gal 3:8), Jesus'/Apostles' (Acts 10:43; 13:38–39). Rejects baptism/Lord's Supper for Church today. Who Generally Holds This View? Mid-Acts "grace movement," Berean Bible Society, teachers like Cornelius Stam, Charles Baker. Less common in mainstream IFB. Strength Emphasizes grace alone and Paul's apostleship. Issue Multiple gospels accursed (Gal 1:8–9). Adds works subtly. Creates unbiblical divisions, diminishing unity from Pentecost (Eph 4:4–6). Next: Hyper-Dispensationalism → Hyper-Dispensationalism Teaches Extreme Mid-Acts: Church begins post-Acts 28 or Paul's prison epistles. Rejects most NT for Church (Gospels, early Acts for Israel). Multiple gospels (Peter's, Paul's, others). Rejects baptism/Lord's Supper today. Some claim KJV advanced revelation corrects originals (Ruckman). Outlandish claims (millennium for physical Jews only, temple sacrifices necessary, OT saved by works+faith, Antichrist giant black alien in spaceship, believers transformed into 33-yo males, new Adams/Eves for alien planets). Who Generally Holds This View? Extreme KJV-only/hyper groups, Ruckman followers, Gene Kim/Bibleline Ministries, fringe online "grace" circles. Rejected by mainstream IFB/evangelicals. Strength Attempts to emphasize Paul's ministry (severely distorted). Issue Multiple gospels accursed (Gal 1:8–9). False distinctions from Abraham/Jesus/Apostles. Adds works/extreme divisions. Even further off rails: cultic/racial views (Christian Identity, Black Hebrew Israelites, etc.) contradict gospel to all nations (Matt 28:19; Rev 7:9). No flesh justified by works of the law (Rom 3:20). Righteousness by faith, apart from the law (Rom 3:21–22, 28). The true Jew is inward, circumcision of the heart (Rom 2:28–29). Not all Israel is Israel; children of promise are the seed (Rom 9:6–8). Israel sought righteousness by works and stumbled (Rom 9:30–33; 10:3). Zeal without knowledge; not submitted to God's righteousness (Rom 10:1–4). God stretched out hands all day to disobedient people (Rom 10:21). Has God cast away His people? God forbid — remnant by grace exists now (Rom 11:1–5). The rest blinded/hardened (Rom 11:7–10). Branches broken off for unbelief; wild branches grafted in by faith (Rom 11:17–22). IF they continue not in unbelief, they may be grafted in (Rom 11:23 — conditional, individual). IF Gentiles do not continue in His goodness, they too will be cut off — no boasting (Rom 11:22). Blindness in part until fulness of the Gentiles (Rom 11:25). And so all Israel shall be saved — the full redeemed people of God by faith (Rom 11:26; Gal 6:16). No Boasting — Not of Works, Tribe, or Law: Abraham had whereof to glory — but not before God (Rom 4:2). By grace through faith — not of works, lest any man should boast (Eph 2:8–9). Not by tribe, not by flesh, not by law-keeping — only humble belief (Rom 3:27; 4:16; Gal 3:11). God’s grace alone — no quality or condition besides faith in Christ. Jesus' Warnings of Cutting Off: Kingdom taken and given to a nation bringing forth fruit (Matt 21:43). Vineyard let to other husbandmen (Matt 21:41; Mark 12:9). Children of the kingdom cast into outer darkness (Matt 8:12). House left desolate (Matt 23:38). Fig tree cursed and withered — fruitless Israel (Mark 11:14, 20–21). Axe at the root; unfruitful trees hewn down (Matt 3:10; Luke 13:6–9). The future promise: resurrection and glorification for all who believe — from every nation, kindred, tongue, and people (Rev 7:9–17; 1 Cor 15:51–54; Phil 3:20–21). One unified story: promise → fulfillment in Christ → one people by faith → new covenant → old done away. No postponed kingdom or separate national program inserted — only mercy to whosoever believes , with no boasting in flesh, works, tribe, or law. Romans 13: Subject to the Higher Powers Submitting to God-given authority, Daniel's faithful refusal of the king's meat as its limit, and love as the fulfilling of the law. Romans Chapter 13 • Submit to Authorities • Love Fulfills the Law Romans Chapter 13 Submit to Authorities • Owe No Man Anything but Love 1-7 Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God : and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same : For he is the minister of God to thee for good. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake. For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing. Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour. 8-10 Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law . For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Thou shalt not covet; and if there be any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended in this saying, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself . Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law . 11-14 And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed. The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and envying . But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof . (Daniel 2:21) 1 Timothy 2:1-3 I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour. Example: David Spares Saul – “Touch Not the Lord’s Anointed” And David said to his men, The LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD’S anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the LORD. (1 Samuel 24:6) David refused to kill King Saul even when he had the opportunity, because Saul was God’s anointed king. He would not lay a hand on him, choosing instead to honor the position God had given, even while Saul pursued him unjustly. This illustrates respectful submission to authority while trusting God to deal with the leader. Civil Disobedience – When It Is Wrong The Bible warns against rebellious or self-willed resistance to authority. Examples of bad civil disobedience include: • Resisting lawful authority out of pride or rebellion — “Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.” (Romans 13:2) • Korah’s rebellion against Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16) — God judged the rebels severely. • The people’s demand for a king like the nations, rejecting God’s direct rule (1 Samuel 8) — led to later troubles. General principle: Civil disobedience is never justified when it stems from personal rebellion, selfishness, or refusal to submit to God-ordained order. We are called to submit for the Lord’s sake and for conscience, unless a clear command of God is violated. Romans 16: Greetings, Warnings and the Doxology The saints Paul greets by name and what history tells of them, the warning to mark and avoid them which cause divisions, and the closing doxology. Romans Chapter 16 • Greetings, Warnings & Final Doxology Romans Chapter 16 Greetings • Commendations • Warnings • Final Doxology 1-2 I commend unto you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea: That ye receive her in the Lord, as becometh saints, and that ye assist her in whatsoever business she hath need of you: for she hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also. 3-16 Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus: Who have for my life laid down their own necks: unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles. Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epaenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ. Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us. Salute Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen, and my fellowprisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me. Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord. Salute Urbane, our helper in Christ, and Stachys my beloved. Salute Apelles approved in Christ. Salute them which are of Aristobulus' household. Salute Herodion my kinsman. Greet them that be of the household of Narcissus, which are in the Lord. Salute Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord. Salute the beloved Persis, which laboured much in the Lord. Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine. Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren which are with them. Salute Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints which are with them. Salute one another with an holy kiss. The churches of Christ salute you. 17-20 Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them. For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple. For your obedience is come abroad unto all men. I am glad therefore on your behalf: but yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil. And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen. 21-24 Timotheus my workfellow, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen, salute you. I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord. Gaius mine host, and of the whole church, saluteth you. Erastus the chamberlain of the city saluteth you, and Quartus a brother. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen. 25-27 • Final Doxology Now to him that is of power to stablish you according to my gospel, and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began, But now is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the everlasting God, made known to all nations for the obedience of faith: To God only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen. A dramatic visual reference for Young Adult Sunday School • Based on the King James Bible Romans Chapter 16 • Historical Context of the Named Saints Romans Chapter 16 Historical Context of the Named Saints • Real People • Real Faith • Real Ministry Phoebe (vv. 1-2) A prominent Christian woman from Cenchrea (port of Corinth). Paul calls her a servant/deacon (diakonos) of the church and a succourer/patron (prostatis) of many, including himself. She likely carried this letter to Rome and was a woman of means who supported traveling ministers. Prisca (Priscilla) & Aquila (vv. 3-5) A married Jewish couple, tentmakers by trade. Expelled from Rome by Emperor Claudius (A.D. 49) along with other Jews. They hosted Paul in Corinth, traveled with him to Ephesus, and hosted a house church in both Ephesus and Rome. They risked their lives for Paul and instructed Apollos more accurately in the faith. Priscilla is often named first, showing her prominent role. Other Key Individuals Epaenetus — Paul’s beloved; the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia (Achaia). Mary — Worked very hard for the Roman believers. Andronicus & Junia — Paul’s Jewish relatives (likely a couple); fellow prisoners with Paul; became Christians before him and were well-known among the apostles. Ampliatus, Urbanus, Stachys, Apelles — Beloved in the Lord and fellow workers. Household of Aristobulus & Herodion — Likely connected to prominent households; Herodion was Paul’s relative. Tryphena & Tryphosa, Persis — Women who “laboured much in the Lord.” Rufus & his mother — Rufus “chosen in the Lord”; his mother had been like a mother to Paul. Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, Philologus, Julia, Nereus & his sister, Olympas — Groups of believers meeting in house churches; many were slaves or freedpeople. Overall Context (vv. 17-20) Paul warns the church to mark and avoid those who cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine they had learned. Many in this list had endured persecution (expulsion under Claudius) yet remained faithful. The Roman church was diverse — Jews and Gentiles, men and women, slaves and free — all united in Christ through house churches. Galatians 3:28 There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.
