We do not get all of what we truly deserve, because God is merciful and His grace abounds. We are blessed regardless of these troubles. Whatever temptation or troubles we do have, that tribulation builds our faith, and our patience, so we should glory in it: Romans 5:3-4 : " ...but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope ." Romans 8:28: " And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose. " And so, man’s suffering can simply be a means for God to work in us, to make us conform to His will for us and is ultimately going to work for good. Troubles in our life may also be a means of glorifying God to His purpose: John 9:1-3; And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth. And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind? Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him . When Jesus heals him it sets off a chain of events that both give glory to God among the people, and stirs up hatred among those who opposed Christ. How many poor, lame, blind, mute, crippled, even the possessed and the dead! - were healed by the mercy of Christ and their faith or the faith of others, such as parents? How much hope has that given Christians over the millenia? Were those healed by Christ from their afflictions sinners more than others in Jerusalem? Or were they suffering that the glory of God could be made manifest as a sign? As hope to us today? Another point to consider, as the bumper sticker says - Stuff Happens Ecclesiastes 8:14 " There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous " Sometimes the righteous suffer as if they were wicked, and vice versa - Stuff happens Ecclesiastes 9:11 " I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all . " Outcomes are not always tied to merit; chance affects everyone - Stuff happens Matthew 5:45 " ...He maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust. " God’s blessings and trials fall on all, regardless of righteousness. - Because Stuff happens Psalm 73:3, 12-13 " For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked… Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches... " The psalmist Asaph is bothered by the fact that the wicked may prosper while the righteous suffer but learns to see it as God sees it, and Asaph realizes - Stuff happens So, in review, the Bible clearly teaches.. That we are to judge with righteous judgment Not according to appearances We shouldn’t assume the afflicted are sinners or under divine judgment God doesn’t want us to be a respecter of persons - assuming wealthy and fortunate are good and the poor of the afflicted are bad That some suffering is for God’s purpose. Giving us strength for hard battles. To grow in faith. OR that He be glorified by it. To heal us or humble us. That He may use us better. And some suffering is just chance, bad luck... because Stuff Happens. All of this is an introduction to my message tonight, things to keep in mind and consider... The title of my presentation : Brother Mark and his lies! - Defending my brother Lazurus from the scurrilous railing and slanderous allegations made behind this very podium just a few weeks ago!! While making admittedly valid points on walking in the Spirit, expecting chastisement rather than blessings if you're backsliding, engaging in self-evaluation and fixing those things where we are lacking, conforming ourselves to the will of God in our lives - Brother Mark made an INTERESTING choice to use the story of Lazarus and the rich man from Luke 16 to justify his base calumny, slanderously reporting that poor sweet Lazarus was “clearly backslidden” and being “punished by God for his sin.” That despite being saved, Lazarus was the bad guy while the rich man was the good guy, that he must have lived a good and righteous life to be so well off, despite his eternal damnation.That Brother Lazurus was a sinner above all others in Jerusalem. That my dear brother in Christ…That stalwart Lazarus’s wickedness was great and his iniquity infinite. He even suggested that Lazarus was ashamed to hear the story of his triumph of faith. Clearly Saint Lazarus truly was a believer, yet he was a filthy beggar of crumbs, covered with sores, licked by dogs, having misery in all his life, BUT was he backslidden and unresponsive to God's chastening? Or, rather, was my dear, sweet brother in Christ, afflicted that God may glory? That Jesus could USE his tale as a warning to the wicked, gluttonous, cruel rich men of this world?! That they should heed the words of the prophets! That they were called to mercy and right judgment! The rich man was a wicked unregenerate SCOUNDREL who had been blessed by having the opportunity to feed and clothe and shelter faithful Lazarus, and had he, perhaps he would have been exposed to the gospel of truth by the beggar …But he blew it and so condemning himself to eternal torment in Hell. Imagine, being Lazarus, I would say walk a mile in his shoes, but he probably didn't even have any!…Despite his poverty, despite his health problems, despite his hunger, he trusted God. Like Job, Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him! What an example of faith. Lowly Lazarus is comfort to all who find themselves - through chance, through God’s purpose, through testing and temptation, stuck in a terrible spot and knowing that in the end it would all be for good, because they loved God.. Just like Lazarus. And so you see, the slander against this great and faithful servant by the filthy lies of brother Mark had to be answered. The honor and reputation of my beloved brother Lazarus, defended! Last point All kidding aside - Just as I don’t think we should judge Lazarus by his suffering, status and situation, we shouldn’t judge other Christians based on that, OR over good faith disagreements about secondary topics where opinions can differ, like Mark and myself. Because Mark and I agree on Christ’s atonement, the blood and eternal life, we can differ on Lazarus with love. In Romans 14 Paul writes Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand. When we are dealing with other believers, our brothers and sisters in Christ, we should be careful to judge them over minor disagreements on opinion. We should remember that all of us will stand or fall by the judgment of God. Of course the primary doctrines of the faith are undebatable. The reality of a holy God, and sin of man, the Trinity, Christ’s eternal Sonship and the resurrection, the gift of eternal life, sealed by the Spirit…death and hell for those that reject the gospel. Differences here shouldn’t be respected. We should reject doubtful disputations on primary doctrines and hate every false way. But there is room in much of scripture for reasonable men to come to different conclusions and have differing opinions on what God is showing us. The entire Bible is there to teach us discernment, and often things people do in scripture is there for us to practice judgment. Some churches and friendships have split over minor disagreements. Over semantics and differences of opinion on timings of prophecy, the meaning of terms, etc. We should remember Romans 14 THAT whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: Whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord's. Brothers and sisters should be able to respectfully disagree on things that aren’t explicitly taught in scripture. There should be room for grace regarding opinions and tertiary doctrine. I love Mark as a brother (despite his lies!) and we don’t all have to agree on how Lazarus got to the point he was in the story, because we DO agree on how he came to be held in the bosom of Abraham, being comforted by the patriarch’s embrace in paradise, in Heaven – because of his faith in the Lord. Let us be of this mind when you may hear an opinion from a saved brother or sister that you aren’t sure you agree with. Seek understanding. Search the scriptures to see if it’s so. But don’t be personally offended- love one another. Even when they are obviously wrong like Mark is.

Embracing Hope Follows Simeon, who embraced the child Jesus, as an Old Testament saint who waited in hope. It points to the faith of Hebrews 11 and the blessed hope of the resurrection and the rapture. Luke 2:25-33 And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel : and the Holy Ghost was upon him. And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ. Simeon was there when Mary and Joseph brought in the baby Jesus to be circumcised 8th day as was custom, and he took the child up in his arms , AND embraced Him , blessing God , saying , Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people ; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel. The title of my sermon tonight is Embracing Hope . Simeon is an example of an OT saint, faithful and waiting patiently for the coming of Christ and was rewarded to see his faith fulfilled. Literally Embracing the hope he had watched for. And Simeon wasn’t alone. Looking down to verse 36; we meet Anna, of the tribe of Asher, a prophetess of great age, long widowed, who the Bible says departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day. And there, seeing the Christ child, she gave thanks to the Lord, and spake of Him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem. I remember being a boy, around 8 and watching Charlie Brown Christmas and hearing Linus recite Luke 2 , detailing the miraculous birth of Jesus in the city of David to a virgin in a manger, angels announcing Him to shepherds, saying “That’s what Christmas is about Charlie Brown” - a cartoon kid Preaching from the King James Bible on national TV. LIKE MANY This was my first exposure to scripture. It moved me. I remember as a boy seeking it out and reading this chapter for the first time and realizing then that there were always people who had the hope of Christ, of being saved by faith in the promises of the Lord. This blew my young mind. And later, accepting Jesus, getting saved, reading the Bible and learning that, as the Bible says, to Him all of the prophets gave witness . Jesus telling the Pharisees If ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me; for he wrote of me. That God, in sundry times and diverse manners spoke to the fathers by the prophets..That throughout time God spoke in various ways to them. That they have faith on the hope set before them. So when Simeon saw Jesus and called him: A light to lighten the Gentiles , he was quoting the old testament prophet, Isaiah written 700yrs before . 🤯 Throughout the OT God made promises to man - and they believed God and it was counted for righteousness…And some they saw fulfilled immediately, as well as prophetic warnings relevant then and came to pass, and those they saw through a glass darkly, that carried promises for the far future. Of the coming of Christ, the Messiah - and of His death on the cross. And of His resurrection, and the eventual resurrection of believers unto eternal life, redemption..End times prophecy that has yet to be fulfilled. The Bible tells us to look at our forerunners in faith, and be like them: The OT was written for our admission, to learn how to live by faith. To show the same diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end: To be followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises . God made promises to Abraham, nearly 4,000 years before Christ… Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee. That in his seed Which is Christ , all nations would be blessed. The Bible says after he had patiently endured , Abraham obtained the promise from God Who cannot lie . He gives us His word, the Bible, to give us faith, to strengthen it. By seeing His promises kept again and again in supernatural ways, unfolding over thousands of years. We like Abraham should have a strong consolation , to know for sure His promise is true… AND lay hold upon the hope set before us , Like Simeon, who got to literally embrace his hope. Which hope The Bible Says we have as an anchor of the soul Hebrews 11:1 Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. Hope is a tangible thing, though we have not seen it or touched it, we know that it IS. As solid as this pulpit. As real as the pineapple pizza downstairs. We haven’t seen it, but we know that it’s there. Hall of faith is filled with the stories of the people who believed God and had the hope of salvation, esteeming the reproach of Christ, They had respect for the recompense of that reward : Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Issac, Jacob, Moses, Rahab,…ALL Looking forward to the cross and their salvation. Just as we look back. Hebrew 11:13 These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them , and embraced them …. What really fascinates me is the idea of being alive to see your hope fulfilled. Like Simeon and Anna. Or consider the apostles, many who had been waiting for the Messiah, and found Him in Christ Jesus. They were blessed to witness first hand His ministry, hearing the preaching and witnessing the miracles, and seeing the death, burial and resurrection of Christ, according to scriptures they had heard and believed. The gospel on which we now stand (1 Cor 15). That all who trust on Jesus have the hope of salvation, resurrection, eternal life. And so Just as the apostles watched as Jesus ascend into Heaven on Pentecost, 50 days after the resurrection, and were told by angels - to watch , for He shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go - We are called to likewise WATCH & WAIT on that HOPE To have this hope you must accept that free gift, given by the grace of the Father, paid for by the precious blood of our Saviour. Sealed by the Spirit unto that glorious day of redemption…. that holy Spirit of promise …the earnest of our inheritance… The Bible says We are bought with a price . And so we have a downpayment towards that day. A token of that hope, the Spirit testifying within us that we ARE children of God. So we watch for the Day of Redemption. The resurrection. Many think it may be in our lifetime. That like Simeon, Anna,and the Apostles who were alive and saw their hope, we may be blessed to be alive for the rapture, the gathering of the elect, those saved in Christ. Having the promise of eternal life in glorified bodies: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump… When our corruptible and broken flesh becomes incorruptible and we put on immortality ( 1 Corinthians 15:52 ) The dead in Christ rising first then, we who are alive and remain 🤞 To be caught up together in the clouds, The Rapture - to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord . (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17) My hope is built on nothing less than Jesus' blood and righteousness; I dare not trust the sweetest frame, but wholly lean on Jesus' name. STORY On Christ the solid rock I stand All other ground is sinking sand Perhaps we will be alive to witness our hope firsthand. But either way we embrace that hope within us. As the apostle John wrote, Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is. And every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as He is pure . ( 1 John 3:2-3) That’s the hope we embrace. Whether we are alive and remain or, like our forefathers, we die in faith, not having received it, but seeing our hope afar off. And so let us embrace it with full confidence. Let it be the anchor to our soul. Let it be on Jesus, on the solid rock we stand. Embracing Him, embracing that blessed hope. Amen

Faith Over Fear Encourages believers to put faith in the Lord over the fears of the world, while keeping a right fear of the LORD. Draws on the author's own nerves about preaching and soul winning, and on God's promise to be with His people. The title of my sermon tonight is Faith over fear . To have faith in God over the fears of the world. Nowadays we live in a society that loves to throw fear in our face and make us afraid, whether it’s the news or social media. And If you've spent any time on Facebook or Instagram doomscrolling, you may have seen the posts claiming that the Bible says “there are 365 verses from God telling us to not be afraid.” Very inspirational. But, like most internet theology it turns out it isn’t true, it is more like 110. Still, the idea of believers not having fear is a powerful message found throughout scripture. And tonight I'd like to encourage us as believers to put our faith in the Lord to have Faith over fear. The Bible says in 2 Timothy 1:7 … God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind That spirit of fear being mentioned is not in reference to god, it's the spirit of fear towards the world, and worldly things As it says in Proverbs 1:7 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge Now of course I'm preaching on having faith over fear, but first it needs to be understood that It’s good to fear the Lord, that’s how we gain knowledge, and grow us christians and it’s also how many gain faith. Fearing the Lord and His wraith, fear of Hell, brings many people to believe on Christ. As Jude writes And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire . We should fear god, have faith in the lord, but not fear the world Having a healthy fear of the Lord can build us as obedient followers and bring us closer to God. But fear of the world is irrational, and god doesnt want us to fear of things out of our control, in fact those things should bring us to just put our faith in the Lord. Trusting Him to handle it. That in Christ, we have nothing to fear. As Jesus says in Matthew 10:28 Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear Him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell Don't threaten me with a good time Being unafraid is a commandment of God: Joshua 1:9 Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest. Revelation 21:8 But the fearful, and unbelieving, ..and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone It is a powerful thing to know that God is with us at all times. In my last sermon I preached on eternal life and how once we are saved we are in God's hand and He will never let go of us. Like he says “No man can pluck them from my hand”. This understanding that God’s got me really helped me to actually deliver that sermon. Boy, was I nervous. Fear of public speaking, also known as glossophobia , is frequently cited as the most common phobia people have. It can be terrifying to get up before a room of people and speak. Let alone to try and preach the word of God! But the actual content of what I was preaching, reading verses in preparation about how God is always with us, actually helped me get past that. Especially when I have faith that what I’m preaching is the truth We have the most high God watching over us, we are his children so what is there to fear? When we started to go soul winning, you would have thought that we would be nervous or scared - Afraid about what people might think or how they’d react, and there’s definitely crazy people in this world! Also not to mention some large dogs, but for that I let brother Ron know he’s got that one. But I found I have no fear knowing I have the Lord watching over me. As the Bible says Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit…that utterance may be given unto me, that I may open my mouth boldly, to make known the mystery of the gospel. It became easier than I ever thought possible. The Spirit helping you to overcome fear, the power of God in our lives protecting us, showing us there is no need to fear, increases our faith. And the more faith we are given, the less fear we have. Isaiah 41:10 Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness. Fear thou not! We have the power of God with us and there’s nothing more powerful than God. Our faith in Him should trump any fears we may have. No matter what trouble or temptations come into our lives. As it says in Psalm 46:1-3 God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore will not we fear , though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea; Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof. In life we are all going to have storms come through and trouble us, Therefore will not we fear, im sure theres multiple things in each of our lives we are currently scared of or afraid of the results of certain things, but when you put all your faith in God and lean on Christ, no matter what happens He will strengthen you, and through the Spirit give you the strength to conquer all fears that come your way. Knowing I can do all things through Christ which strengthens me . Without the spirit of fear. But in faith. Amen

Haggai the Prophet Walks through Haggai's short ministry to the returned exiles, calling them to rebuild the temple. Notes that Zerubbabel is in the line of David that leads to Christ, and encourages believers to build up the local church. Haggai 1 In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, saying, Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, This people say, The time is not come, the time that the Lord's house should be built. Then came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet, saying, Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste? Haggai is considered one of the minor prophets, contrasted with the Major prophets by the length of their work, Haggai only consisting of 2 brief chapters. His ministry here is equally short, and takes place over just a 3 and a half month period at the end of the Babylonian exile and resulting in what we will cover tonight. He was a contemporary of Zecharaiah, and preached about a century before Malachi, the last of the OT prophets. The pre-exile prophets, including Isaiah and Jeremiah, were given the word of the Lord to warn of the impending destruction of the Northern Kingdom of Israel, and the eventual invasion of the Southern Kingdom of Judah by Babylon. The prophet Jeremiah had foretold that the Babylonian captivity would last 70 years, while Daniel, during the captivity recognized and reinforced this timeline, that God would eventually allow a remnant to return to Jerusalem, to keep His promise to David that a King would come from his lineage, the Messiah, and that the city where He chose to place His name, Jerusalem, would stand, setting the stage for Jesus. Haggai the prophet brings the word of the Lord of hosts to Zerubbabel, the governor of the province, Zerubbabel, a direct descendant of David, the grandson of King Jehoiachin, the next-to-last King of Judah before him, and Joshua son of Josedak, A Levite from the line of Zadok, Solomon’s high priest. The first message is given in the second year of the Persian King, Darius, on the first day of the sixth month. This was roughly 520 BC, again in the final year of the Babylonian captivity. During this time, Haggai and his peer, Zechariah, were given the word of the Lord to encourage the returned Jews, getting the nation to begin the work of rebuilding the Temple that had been destroyed during Nebbuchedezer’s conquest decades earlier. Over in Ezra 1:1-4 , we would find Cyrus the Great's proclamation, declaring that the Lord God of heaven had given him all the kingdoms of the earth and that God had instructed Cyrus to rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem. Cyrus called for the Jews to go up to Jerusalem and encouraged those Jews remaining behind throughout the diaspora to support the cause financially. However after Cyrus's death, few had returned, most Jews remained scattered, and the work on the Second Temple did not progress. Only a foundation had been laid. Then, after the passing of Cyrus the Great, and a brief period of political instability, his predecessor Darius came to power. He also supported the Jews return to Jerusalem and the rebuilding of the temple, but even with the support of these kings, the work had stalled. Jerusalem itself had begun being rebuilt and the people there lived in “ ceiled houses ,” that is paneled and permanent structures. But the Temple reconstruction languished, only a foundation had been laid. and the people said, “ The time is not come, the time that the Lord's house should be built ” And so the prophet preached: 5 Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways. Ye have sown much, and bring in little; ye eat, but ye have not enough; ye drink, but ye are not filled with drink; ye clothe you, but there is none warm; and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes. The Lord tells them through the prophet, in the Spirit, that they are in famine and their efforts amount to nothing because they have not prioritized God and His Temple. They sow much and bring in little. They eat and drink, but aren’t full, they have clothing, but not enough to warm themselves. They make money and it's gone faster than they can earn it. This can seem pretty relatable to many of us today. A nation's economy and our financial well-being can be a judgment of God and our walk with Him. And so God says to the people, Consider your ways. Verse 7 Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways. Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith the Lord. As God says in Isaiah 1:18 , Come now, and let us reason together. He tells the people their efforts come to naught because of their lack of work building His house, and their not taking advantage of the mercy He has shown them. The grace of bringing them back to Judah and Zion, to serve Him after all the tribulation, trials and travails that Judah's past sins brought on them. He calls on the people to build up His house, that He will take pleasure in it, and be glorified. An application in the Christian life can be seen here, where many after hearing the gospel and believing on Christ, laying that foundation that only He can, and then they languish spiritually. They see little growth, maintain living in the world, continuing under the sins they’ve been forgiven of, not taking advantage of the mercy God has shown them. He tells us to consider our ways. That we sow much and bring in little, but if we go forth and build up the temple, our spiritual lives, It will please the Lord. 9 Ye looked for much, and, lo it came to little; and when ye brought it home, I did blow upon it. Why? saith the Lord of hosts. Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house. It isn't just our spiritual lives but the local New Testament, bible believing soul-winning church. How relevant this verse is for us today in America, among Christians, where there are empty churches with dying congregations, with few coming behind them. Too many churches like the church at Ephesus in Revelation, who didn’t keep their first love, soul-winning. Or like the church at Leodacia, lukewarm, and languishing. Neglect of building up the house of God often isn't even due to the work of sowing fields and manual labor; earning a wage, working to survive, though sometimes a job may interfere with attending services. It seems mostly lost to pleasure and leisure, golf and cookouts and youth sports. Shopping. Dining out. Watching professional sports, gambling and drinking. We look for much and it comes to little and we wonder why. Because, the Lord says Because of my house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house …and turn on the 80" 4K, gorging themselves with pizza and wings and beer while betting a parlay on Draft Kings, forsaking the assembly and not worshipping the King of Kings. Americans chase riches and wants and lusts, and ignore the gathering of the called out assembly of God, and then wonder why our efforts often amount to nothing. Why even that little which they gather is blown away. The Lord says “ Consider your ways! ” I tell you I am standing here tonight because I was looking for much and bringing in little, and it was gone before I could do anything with what little I'd have. And the Lord said, “Consider your ways!” Believe me, after a lot of chastening and consideration, I saw it God's way. Verse 10 Therefore the heaven over you is stayed from dew, and the earth is stayed from her fruit. And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn, and upon the new wine, and upon the oil, and upon that which the ground bringeth forth, and upon men, and upon cattle, and upon all the labour of the hands. When Christians in a nation neglect God, and stop building His church, and spreading the gospel we shouldn’t be surprised when we suffer a drought upon the land, even upon the labor of our hands. Declining birth rates. Crumbling infrastructure. Livestock put down for disease. As God says in 2 Chronicles , If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. Look at verse 12 Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him, and the people did fear before the Lord. Then spake Haggai the Lord's messenger in the Lord's message unto the people, saying, I am with you, saith the Lord. And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they came and did work in the house of the Lord of hosts, their God, In the four and twentieth day of the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king. And so this preaching stirs the heart of Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest. And they began the work of rebuilding the 2nd Temple. We need this preaching just as much today. The local New Testament Church needs to be built up, that He take pleasure in us, and be glorified. But a few months later, they need another reminder Haggai 2 In the seventh month, in the one and twentieth day of the month, came the word of the Lord by the prophet Haggai… It is interesting to note that Haggai records four messages delivered over roughly 3.5 months in 520 BC, timestamped by God. The first message (1:1) came on the 1st of Elul (around August 29, coincidently enough), followed by another on the 24th of Elul (September 21), (1:15), a gap of 24 days. This third message in chapter 2 verse 1 comes on the 21st of Tishrei (October 17), about 27 days later. The final messages we will see were given on the 24th of Kislev (December 18) (2:10, 20), roughly 62 days after the third. From start to finish, these events span approximately 3 and a half months. And so the word of the Lord came to Haggai saying , Speak now to Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, and to the residue of the people, saying, Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing? While the people’s hearts were stirred, the work on the temple was still insufficient for the Lord, and here, God appeals to the older generation that had seen Solomon’s temple in its glory, and asking how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing? After 70 years of captivity and the destruction of the Temple, there would only be very elderly Jews who could remember the former glory of that Temple. Senior saints of the day. The work has begun, but clearly not enough was being done. He shames the elders among them, to get them to push the young to get it done. Again, how many churches in America today have a core of senior saints who remember the glory days of their congregation, and serve as an example, pushing the younger generation to help return their church to that glory? This church is blessed to have such active elders, prayer warriors and soul-winners, serving as examples to the young who come and stay due to the infectious faith and devotion by the elders in a church that has such a great history. He continues in verse 4 Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith the Lord; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Josedech, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts: According to the word that I covenanted with you when ye came out of Egypt, so my spirit remaineth among you: fear ye not. For thus saith the Lord of hosts; Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; And I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the Lord of hosts. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts. What an encouragement to be reminded of all those things God has done for us! He says to be strong, and know that He will deliver for us. Have faith, do as He commands, and He will provide in due time, increasing our faith. Many Christians stumble in their walk, establishing the foundation which is Christ, maybe even beginning to do what He has called them to, but then just trail off. Some worry about not having what they need to succeed in their minds, being discouraged and giving up. But it is God that began that work in you, and it is God Who will provide the materials and circumstances that we need to see it through. Be strong, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord, and work: for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts. He says in verse 9 The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the Lord of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the Lord of hosts. A promise by God, Who cannot lie…applicable to our Christian lives, our nation and to the local New Testament Church. 10 In the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, came the word of the Lord by Haggai the prophet, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Ask now the priests concerning the law, saying, If one bear holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and with his skirt do touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat, shall it be holy? And the priests answered and said, No. Then said Haggai, If one that is unclean by a dead body touch any of these, shall it be unclean? And the priests answered and said, It shall be unclean. So we see, it is now a couple months later, Haggai in the Spirit inquires of the priests, does that which is holy touching that which is not holy, make it holy? The priests rightly answer, no. And does that which is unclean touch that which is hole, shall it be unclean? Yes. Of course. So then that which is holy doesn't make that which is not holy clean, and that which is unclean makes even that which is holy unclean. You can't get something clean and holy out of that which is unholy and unclean by contact. A little dirt in water makes all the water dirty. Haggai says this is the state of the people, they have no means of sanctification not having the Temple and the ordinances, to do for them what the Spirit does for believers today. And so all the work they offer is unclean. And due to this, the Lord has made their works less profitable than they expect, less oil pressed, their crops covered with mold and disease. But God promises that even as the foundation is built upon, He will bless their efforts again. This also has applications in the Christian life. When we are in sin, and under reproach, feeling like we are never getting ahead. We need to consider our ways. We need to cleanse ourselves, and make ourselves holy, separated unto His work. Then He will bless our efforts. Then answered Haggai, and said, So is this people, and so is this nation before me, saith the Lord; and so is every work of their hands; and that which they offer there is unclean. And now, I pray you, consider from this day and upward, from before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the Lord: Since those days were, when one came to an heap of twenty measures, there were but ten: when one came to the pressfat for to draw out fifty vessels out of the press, there were but twenty. I smote you with blasting and with mildew and with hail in all the labours of your hands; yet ye turned not to me, saith the Lord. If you’re a gardener like me, you know that this is the season where plants start getting the blasting and mildew, mold and rot. Hail destroyed many people’s gardens up around Weymouth a few weeks ago. These things are devastating after a season of work, let alone when your very people’s survival depends on a harvest. But God promises to bless their efforts going forward. Consider now from this day and upward, from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, even from the day that the foundation of the Lord's temple was laid, consider it. Is the seed yet in the barn? yea, as yet the vine, and the fig tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree, hath not brought forth: from this day will I bless you. God is a rewarder of those that diligently seek him. Finally, in verse 20 And again the word of the Lord came unto Haggai in the four and twentieth day of the month, saying, Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, I will shake the heavens and the earth; And I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, and I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the heathen; and I will overthrow the chariots, and those that ride in them; and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother. In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the Lord, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord of hosts. The final word comes to Haggai, letting Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, of the line of David know he is chosen, anointed to be king and of his line comes Christ Jesus. Matthew 1:12-16 And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel; And Zorobabel begat Abiud;....Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ. Also found in the lineage of Mary, in Luke 3:27 Which was the son of Joanna, which was the son of Rhesa, which was the son of Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel, which was the son of Neri… There is some controversy or confusion among "scholars" given slight variations in the genealogy given in Luke, surrounding both Zerubbable's father (given as Nari) and different sons named. But these aren't identical genealogies, they are giving us Mary and Joseph's lines, and there are resonable explanations offered by many for the so-called discrepancy. I think we shouldn't be worried about it. Titus 3:9 But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies- they are unprofitable and vain. It is enough to know that the promise made to David runs through Zerubbable, just as Haggai preached. Half a millenia before Christ. Build upon the foundation laid which is Christ and God will bless you. For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Lay up treasures in Heaven, not wood, hay and stubble to be burned. Even if your greatest work for the Lord only lasts 3 and a half months, it can have a major impact! Haggai’s preaching still resonates with us today. Build up your local church. Senior saints, continue to encourage the youth! Remember God’s promises are kept! Even centuries later. Young people, don’t neglect your spiritual walk and the importance of church. Church is what you make of it. Always be willing to help build it up. Consider your ways and do that which is pleasing to the Lord, that He may continue to bless us and help heal our nation.

Help Me, Help You Presents helping others as a gift of God, a commandment of God and a promise of God. Teaches that charity is love in action and gives practical ways to serve at home, church and work. Help me, help you. 1 Corinthians 12: 27-28 Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular. And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps , governments, diversities of tongues. The title of my sermon tonight; Help me, help you . Paul is writing to the church in Corinth concerning Spiritual gifts and the contentions among them over the distribution of those gifts where some envied and coveted the more attractive The church are all members of the same body, Jesus the head over all Least comely- being a ministering servant is just as important as the more flashy, miracles and healings Paul expounds on a more excellent way. He writes that even if you have the gift of speaking every language, see all prophecies, give away all our possessions, understand all mysteries and have all knowledge…if you don’t have charity , the gift and desire to help others out of love, it profits us nothing. As Paul writes, of all the talents we have as Christians, the greatest of these is charity. Charity is love in action, and being a help to others as the expression of the Love God has shown us. The Bible says we should Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, pray to be a better helper, and for the opportunity to be used by God Not just money, BUT Time and God given talent. Doing for others out of love for God AND To show our love, helping one another by exercising this gift of God But more than a gift, being a helper of others is also a commandment of God : We all know The Golden Rule: Matthew 7:12 Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them : for this is the law and the prophets. Matthew 26:36-37 Jesus says - Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself James 1:27 Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world. James 4:17 Therefore to him that knoweth to do good , and doeth it not, to him it is sin . Helping one another. Doing unto others. Knowing to do good, being doers of the law…visiting those in need, being a help to all… In the Gospels Jesus calls us again and again to be a helper, to do unto the least of our brothers , and that by doing so, we are doing it unto Him. His burden is truly light. It really is the least we can do, helping others is our reasonable service .. our duty as Christians, and WE SHOULD help others with meekness and humility: Luke 17:10 So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do. And so in lowliness of mind let each esteem others better than themselves. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others…Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus ( Philippians 2:3-5 ) The ability and opportunity to help others is a gift from God . Helping others is a commandment of God And being a helper is a blessing for you, the giver. This is a promise from God Helping others helps you: Receive blessings in this life: Proverbs 19:17 He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again. Proverbs 22:9 The liberal soul shall be made fat, and he that watereth shall be watered also himself Acts 20:35 In all things I have shewed you, that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive These are rewards promised of God, for all we do for others. It’s never in vain. Even if it isn’t appreciated by anyone else. God knows, and He promises us Rewards in the next life : Hebrews 6:10 God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, and how ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister Matthew 16:27 For the Son of man shall come…and he shall reward every man according to his works. Matthew 6:20-21 Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven… For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. Hebrews 13:16 And do not forget to do good and to share with others , for with such sacrifices God is pleased By helping others, you help yourself and please God. What a wonderful blessing it is to be used by the Lord Who has done so much for us! Helpers have a gift from God , are obeying a commandment from God , that contains a promise from God . Practical encouragement I tell you all this Because as Paul wrote to the Phlipians … I desire fruit that may abound to your account …( Philippians 4:17) Helping me, helps you. Helping others, with your love, time, wealth, talents, by teaching, preaching, giving the gospel, ministering to the brethren, the brokenhearted…helping at home - helping your spouse, children helping your parents, helping at church, helping at work, school, or helping total strangers you meet in the world …This is the more excellent way Paul writes about. Also, knowing that when we help a stranger, thereby some have entertained angels unawares. ( Hebrews 13:2) Pray for the ability and opportunity to be used by God, to be a blessing and a help to others …IT WILL CHANGE YOUR LIFE… And finally, by helping others, we GIVE GLORY TO GOD 1 Corinthians 10:31 Whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God. Matthew 5:16 Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven Let us help others, ministering them as the ability and opportunity that God gives us, a GIFT FROM GOD Let us obey the Lord in helping others, as servants, For His yoke is easy, and His burden is light…. following the COMMANDMENT FROM GOD Let us remember that God is faithful to reward us for our service to others, which is a PROMISE OF GOD Because, when we help others, when we exercise our gift of helps, we GIVE GLORY TO GOD 1 Peter 4:11 If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God; if any man minister, let him do it as of the ability which God giveth: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen

In Defense of Christmas Explains that Jeremiah 10 is about carved and gilded idols and is not a prohibition of the Christmas tree. It answers common objections about the date and name of Christmas, and calls on believers to be fully persuaded in their own minds and to celebrate the birth of Christ. Jeremiah 10 Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel: 2 Thus saith the Lord, Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them. 3 For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe. 4 They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not. 5 They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good. ..8 But they are altogether brutish and foolish: the stock is a doctrine of vanities. 9 Silver spread into plates is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the workman, and of the hands of the founder: blue and purple is their clothing: they are all the work of cunning men. 10 But the Lord is the true God, he is the living God, and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his indignation. 11 Thus shall ye say unto them, The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth, even they shall perish from the earth, and from under these heavens. 12 He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion. 13 When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures. 14 Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them. 15 They are vanity, and the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish. We are there in Jeremiah chapter 10, and the Lord, speaking through the prophet by the Spirit, is casting judgments upon Judah, the remaining children of Israel after the destruction of the Northern Kingdom, this time focusing on their adopting the heathen practices of idol worshiping of graven images. Wood carvings plated with molten metals, hammered into place and carried about for feasts, bowed and served, used for religious practices. He begins by warning them not to be caught up in the signs of the sky. Astrology and the movement of the lights in the firmament, given as we read in Genesis as a way to mark time, but celestial disturbances were being used by those who worship idols, to scare people into thinking catastrophe was nigh. Babylonians especially had a very advanced system of astrology for prophesying, and God says this is vanity. Just as the workman and the founder, cutting down trees to make idols to Baal or the Queen of Heaven are vain. 2 It is important to see things as God sees them. And as He is the creator of all things, His view of the superstitious nonsense men invent to explain His creation, including worship the things He created, is both insulting to a jealous God, and laughably foolish. Romans 1:21-25 Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. We worship the living God, through Whom all things were made. The heathen in their fear worshiped the sun, the moon, the stars. Idols made of wood and stone and molten metals formed into the image of man, birds and beasts. Psalm 115:5-8 They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not: They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not: They have hands, but they handle not: feet have they, but they walk not: neither speak they through their throat. They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them. Acts 17:22-31 Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, To The Unknown God. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; Neither is worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things…Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man's device. And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent The Lord is consistently pointing out the vanity, the utter uselessness of these false gods. How foolish it is to bow and serve dead things as gods, that cannot save anyone. They are an invention of man's own vain imagination. And yet the children of Judah, even those going to the Temple and continuing the Levitical ceremonial ordinances and laws, had adopted the same idols and gods as the heathen. They baked cakes to the "queen of heaven." (the only Biblical appearance of that term, sorry Catholics) They participated in feasts to these false gods. They were made to fear the heavens God created, rather than the God who created them. And for this cause God is bringing destruction upon Judah, and the graven images and idols decked with golden plates will be destroyed, along with the carvers and founders, (someone who works a foundry with molten metal), who made them… All this is an introduction to my main point this evening : In Defense of Christmas! 3 There are many false teachers, Internet theologians and sincere but misled believers, who have taken Jeremiah 10 out of context, and twisted it to make the claim that this chapter isn't about graven images, carved, fashioned and decked with plated gold and silver, idols that are being worshipped and feared as if they have power, BUT rather saying that this chapter is explicitly about the tradition of the Christmas tree, and linking it to paganism and idol worship. Jehovah's Witnesses, many 7 day adventists claim this, but there are even IFB churches and pastors who are preaching against any recognition of Christmas today, that use these verses in Jeremiah 10 to teach against decorating your house with a plant (fake or real) while celebrating the birth of Christ Jesus. That the practice of having Christmas trees is paganism. They are a part of a movement that hates Christmas, Easter too, and they try to use the Bible to justify their beliefs. But what does God say? Isaiah 60:13 The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious. (A box is a type of evergreen, like the pine and fir tree) God commands the choicest evergreens to be brought into His house for beauty. If trees in the house were inherently pagan, the Lord just ordered paganism into the temple! I believe the evergreen is a symbol of eternal life, that it doesn’t die in winter the way other trees seem to do. So it makes sense God would use them as a way to beautify His house. “ They deck it with silver and with gold; they fasten it with nails and with hammers, that it move not. ” This is a description of an idol made of wood and covered with silver and gold. Notice that God tells Israel not to be afraid of these idols because “ they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good ” They have to be carried around. They are dead and worthless. But these idols are not a tree. Nobody prays to the plastic spruce from Walmart. Nobody is afraid the balsam fir in the corner is going to curse them if they don’t leave cookies under it. We put it up because it’s pretty, it smells good, and it gives us something to gather around while we read Luke chapter 2 and belt out “Hark! the Herald Angels Sing.” No one bows and serves a decorative house plant, they beautify their homes with them. No one worships a pine tree except maybe "druid" LARPers. Even the most secular reprobate consumerist, who strips Christ from Christmas and makes it entirely about Frosty and Rudolph, buying and coveting things, racking up the Amazon charges… doesn't look at the plastic tree covered in lights and tinsel in the corner of their living room and think, "I shall worship this." They don't even "venerate" it. 4 But that hasn't stopped some from judging believers in respect to holy days, and teaching doctrine of men as commandments. There are plenty of reasons to not want to participate in some of the modern traditional Christmas trappings, to not partake in the Black Friday-consumerist world of greed. 5 The lie of Santa, the works-based system of the naughty list - that “you have to have good works or you don't get a present!" The profane and the blasphemous way our subverted culture has secularized it all. This is all unfortunate and should be pushed back on, but sincere Christians can tell the baby Jesus from the bathwater. Now, I do not believe in having a Santa Claus at Sunday school or singing about snowmen and reindeer during the Sunday service. Lying to little ones is a sin. In my opinion, no Christian ought to condone it. The truth is so much better than a lie. We should tell them how the dear Lord came into the world to save sinners. We should teach them what Christmas is all about: celebrating the miracle of the birth of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. 6 Those same Scrooges and Grinches will say that Christians are being tricked into worshiping pagan Gods because they choose to celebrate the birth of Christ on December 25th. I have heard some claim to know it was in the Spring, others around September, because of the shepherds being near Bethlehem. These are “educated guesses” and no more valid than late December. They will say that since the Bible doesn’t give us a day of Jesus’ birth, and because some pagan traditions held feasts during the first days of Winter, Christmas is pagan. The winter solstice (the shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere) usually falls on 21 December, and unsurprisingly, agrarian cultures would mark the time when days began to get longer again, the first promise of Spring, with a feast. It is true that before the birth of Christ, December 25 was often a pagan holiday. The Encyclopedia Britannica says this date was a “ Mithraic feast day ”. We also know several other ancient cultures had some recognition of the times and season. Evidently many new converts in pagan Europe during the first centuries of Christianity were tempted to keep the pagan feast celebrated on December 25. Possibly it was to counteract this pagan influence that Christian leaders decided to observe this day as “Christmas”, which means “Christ-sent,” hoping this would help new converts resist the temptation of partaking in the pagan feast. Celebration of the birth of Jesus during this time isn’t wicked, we celebrate the Spring feast of Passover, which for Christians begins with the death of Christ, and His glorious resurrection 3 days later. Even though the pagans marked the same time with Spring feasts, it doesn’t turn our celebration into paganism. Or “stolen from the pagans,” as some would have it. No one can be tricked into sin. And If the heart is blessing the day in Christ, then it is of Christ. Period. These same people who claim that Christmas is “paganism” use the "pagan" names for days of the week and months of the year, and think nothing of it. “Thor’s day?” - really? Yet they sit in judgment against believers who seek to honor the Lord, and dictate to us that we aren't "real Christians." 7 That objection seems a little foolish in this context. Nearly all the names we have, we inherited from the heathen. Many cities, towns, counties and rivers in America have Indian names. But when we drive through Monponsett, Titicut, Manomet, or see the Nemasket or Wankinco River, we are not thinking about the Indians. When you say “I’m going fishing on Monponsett Pond” or “Meet me at the lights in Manomet,” you are speaking the same Wampanoag and Massachusett words that were used around pagan campfires 400 years ago. But nobody thinks you’re conducting a pow-wow or offering tobacco to the spirits when you say those names. The word has lost every trace of its original meaning and simply names a place or a time. Sometimes Seventh-day Adventists make much of the fact that the name of our day of worship “Sunday” comes from the worship of the sun. But no one has reference to the sun…only the SON when he worships on Sunday; just as no one has any reference to the god Saturn when they go to church on Saturday, which is named after him. 8 Some say “Christmas Means ‘Christ’s Mass’—a Catholic Holiday” that it was instituted by Catholics and therefore Christians ought not to observe it. To every sensible person, Christmas means simply Christmas, not some kind of mass. Catholics may observe it with a mass, but we don’t. Most of us take the season to reflect on scripture, to give thanksgiving to God the Father for His Son, to sing Psalms and hymns praising Him. And decorating their homes, eating special meals with family, giving gifts in the spirit of grace, just as God has given to each of us. 9 Paul told us exactly how to handle these disputes: Colossians 2:16 “ Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday …” Romans 14:5–6 “ One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind. He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord… ” If your conscience says “No tree, no Christmas,” then don’t have one. 10 But don’t take Jeremiah 10 , rip it out of its context, and swing it like a club against brothers and sisters who want to string some lights, sing about the virgin birth, and give their kids a gift because the Father gave us such a precious gift, that “ God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son .” If the heart is thanking God for the Incarnation of Christ, then the day is holy, the tree is pretty, and the celebration glorifies Jesus. Yes, people often dishonor God at Christmas. I am sorry they do. I hope you will not grieve God by such a sin. But we should not turn Christmas over to Satan and wicked people because some misuse the Christmas season. Isaiah 9:6 For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace Jesus came to offer peace towards men from God the Father, goodwill and reconciliation, while we were yet sinners, Christ was born, that He may die for us. That’s what Christmas is all about Charlie Brown.

Increase Our Faith Shows from Luke 17 that when the apostles asked for more faith, the Lord pointed them to obedience first. Applies the point to forgiving, honoring parents, marriage, work, church attendance and soul winning, and ends with an invitation to take the first step of trusting Christ. Luke 17:3-10 Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him. And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him. And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith. Jesus is teaching the apostles that it is not enough to forgive a brother one time or even 3. But, He says, even if it’s 7 times in a day, forgive . And the command isn’t merely 7 times Matthew 18:21-22 : "Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven 490 times! Jesus is using 7, God's number of perfection or completion, to say “every single time! Forgive him!” It's easy to do once. We may even, out of the charity of our regenerate Christian heart, forgive ‘em twice. But the command is to forgive them every time! Jesus’ call to forgive shows radical expectation of God’s limitless grace, to forgive others completely, just as He forgave us. The Apostles react to this saying “We don't have the faith to do it! We hear you Lord. We get what you're saying but ..common! SEVEN times? We are gonna need more faith than we have to do what you command us to do!” And the Lord said , If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you. Jesus says even the tiniest amount of faith could defy physics! Warp reality!! Work Miracles! Forgiving each other is nothing compared to that. Jesus then explains that if you want to increase your faith, you must first obey His commands. Because Obedience comes before faith! To demonstrate it, Jesus then gives us this parable about a servant and a master . The servant works all day, plowing the field, feeding the cattle and comes in at the end of the day. Imagine how exhausted he'd be! And his master says, make me dinner. Serve me, and after that you can eat. The servant doesn't say “I would, but you gotta increase my faith first” he just does it. Jesus asks Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not! He says No, I don’t think so!. Because at the end of the day, when we do what we are commanded to do, we are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do. As the great modern theologian, Chris Rock said about doing what you're supposed to do, “What do ya want? A cookie?” Jesus isn't suggesting we forgive others. He is commanding it. He doesn't care that you're too faithless to understand why, or to discipline yourself into obeying. He says, like Nike “Just do it.” O bedience to His command comes before the faith to do it! AND The payoff for obeying will show you the truth behind the commands. The results of forgiving a brother or sister, demonstrating the mercy of God, develops the fruit of the Spirit in us, longsuffering, patience...Joy. Love. The mercy we show others is shown to us. And you will see the promise of God fulfilled, and that will increase your faith. Because Obedience comes before faith! Jesus says If you love Me, keep my commandments . “Lord, I hear you. But…” HE SAID If you love Me keep my commandments! They are not grievous. His burden is light! Pick up your cross. The word of God convicts us . It's why we need to walk in His word every day, to know what God thinks. To hear His commands and learn His ways, for His ways are not our ways. What makes sense to God might not make sense to us. But you do what God says and He will give you the faith to understand and continue doing it. EVERYTIME! But first you gotta know what He says, and then do it. Obedience comes before faith The Bible says His word is a light unto our feet. It directs us where to go. God's word is like the flashlight app on your phone . Comes in very handy when you're in a dark place and you don't know where to turn. We should reach for the Bible when we can’t see where He wants us to go. And when we step out in obedience on the path God directs us towards, without the faith to do it, when we do what we don't think we are able to, He increases our faith to continue. We learn that Obedience comes before faith. You may say “I don't know Lord… not sure I can do that, I don’t think I can bear this burden. I don’t have the faith.” But you take the step anyway. Because Obedience comes before faith Some examples - God says children honor your parents . Fear them, that is have a healthy respect for them. It's the first commandment with promise! That you'll live long upon the earth. “But they are mean! They aren't fair! They are the worst!” Note God doesn't say a thing about how good or bad they are, He just says to honor them. No matter how old you get BTW And it pays off! A good relationship with your parents is a blessing! You gain their trust. You grow in grace. You live long upon this earth. God blesses you. Showing you that Obedience comes before faith Husbands, love your wives the way Jesus loves the church! “But she doesn't always listen!! She nags me…” The Bible doesn't say “if she was perfect.” Jesus loves His church despite how imperfect we are, while we were yet sinners Christ died for us! If things aren't going the way you think they should at home, step out in obedience, LOVE YOUR WIVES!…and God will give you the faith to continue. Watch it work! Watch her love for you grow, and your appreciation to God for such a wonderful spouse. And you will see that your Obedience comes before faith Wives, the Bible says to submit to your husband. And just as a Parent or Wife doesn't need to be perfect first for us to obey God, neither does he. “But he doesn't remember the anniversary! He can’t get his dirty socks in the hamper! He leaves the seat up!” God didn't tell you to submit to a perfect husband, but to the one ya got. And by your chaste conversation, your godly behavior, he’ll come around. But Obedience comes before faith When we step out in obedience to God, and He will increase your faith to continue doing the thing you trusted Him to do. But we must obey first. Because Obedience comes before faith! The Bible says to serve your boss , Working for them or your company or teacher or whoever has God given authority over you, as though you're working directly for God. “But the boss is a jerk!” the Bible says servants obey your masters even if they are froward. Even if they're jerks! Christians are to obey the higher power. That includes the government God gives us. To render unto Caesar, so pay your taxes! Without complaining …“Oh Lord, increase my faith!” …but Obedience comes before faith! The Bible says to go to church, you're all here and God bless you for it, but even when you don't feel like it, don't forsake the assembly! You obey and you see the blessing it is in your life. You learn you can’t live without it. And so God increases your faith in Him and His word. Obedience comes before faith! This sermon isn’t a lecture on being more forgiving or more obedient to your parents or being more loving to your spouse, although those are good things…It’s about how to grow your faith. I am using examples of commandments we may struggle with for a reason. Like the Apostles struggled with the idea of forgiving someone an absurd amount of times. To show that Obedience comes first. Increased faith in God and trust in His word and His ways follows that obedience. Obedience comes before faith! Especially when it’s hard. Especially when God’s commands bring us outside our comfort zone. When they challenge us to do hard things….God commands us - Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature. Go soul winning! “But I'm afraid! I won’t know what to say!” Go ye! He didn't say “Go some of ya! Go everyone but the socially awkward!” We obey, and as Ethan will tell you, you knock that door, you ring that bell…and suddenly the Spirit will fill you with exactly the measure of confidence and love that you need. And it becomes easy to talk with others about how much Jesus loves them. Your faith will increase having seen the Spirit in action. But Obedience comes before faith! Sometimes it might feel like you're stepping out onto shaky ground .Jesus says whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them is established, as if standing upon a rock. You step out in obedience and you think to yourself this isn't so bad . I can do this. And God blesses you and God rewards you for your obedience and you see things start to happen in your life. The Spirit moves. You see that jerk of a boss start to come around. You see your husband put the toilet seat down once in a while! You see your mom and dad trust you to do that thing you wanted to do. You step out again and again. You obey. You grow in faith. Because Obedience comes before faith… Love God with all your heart, Love your neighbors as yourselves, go to church,… don't steal or kill…, don't lie… We obey more and out faith grows … with every step we take.… We forgive and put others’ profit above our own, and we pray and see results, and read our bible every day and develop wisdom, understanding…. We grow in faith…Growing to trust in the Lord as we go…This is your Christian walk… You hesitate less and less, you step out in obedience more confidently with each step…now you are running … This is the race we run that’s set before us. As Paul writes, This is our course, God’s given a race for each and every one of us, not a competition between one another but with ourselves, pressing for that mark set before us … Knowing It's a marathon not a sprint . The Christian life is measured in decades not years. With each step our faith grows comparable to our obedience. Knowing Obedience comes before faith Yes there are stumbling stones and snares in our way….Temptations. Things that trigger us: God says Love thy enemies.. woah .. AND Pray for them. WHAT? Lord increase my faith. It’s hard. God knows it. God's word gives us encouragement and so step out without the faith to do it and trust Him.. Obedience comes before faith! But why? Why should you want to do the hard things, to obey? Why should we seek to increase our faith? Because, when hardship come s, when the troubles of this life weigh you down, when God gives you burdens you don’t think you can bear…when your unshakable faith is shaken..When you read “ I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me .” AND “ we know that all things work together for good to them that love God ,” we have the faith to trust Him and know that it’s so. So you take that step , and realize it is a true saying, " God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble " You'll have the faith to trust Him, to know it's true. That it will work out in the end to His will and His glory and our salvation. And you receive that peace that passes all understanding. No matter how heavy the burden is…sickness, financial trouble, deaths of loved ones, disasters and tragedies, When we are hardly able to see the path God directs us towards through the tears …Then we will have the faith to trust the Lord. Even in our darkest hours we can know, like Job. Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him. Even in death, trusting that to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord. And once you start obeying and stepping out on your course, and your faith increases, don’t be surprised at the heights the Lord will take you to. Pressing on the upward way, New heights I'm gaining every day; Still praying as I onward bound - Lord, plant my feet on higher ground. That higher ground ultimately leads to Heaven . However, like all journeys, it starts with the first step. And that first step is accepting that free gift of eternal life. Jesus says that we are to obey the will of the Father. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day. Friends if you're here tonight and you haven't made that first step, if you're afraid you don't have enough faith to trust Jesus as your savior… the Bible says God gives to every man a measure of faith enough to not just hear the gospel, but to respond to it. To hear about that free gift of Salvation given by the grace of the Father paid for by the blood of the Son and sealed unto the day of redemption by the Spirit. If you haven't trusted in Christ as your savior if you haven't asked for and received that free gift calling upon the name of the Lord. Take that step. “Lord save me cuz I can't save myself.” Invitation Pastor close us in prayer.

New Year, New Man Looks at New Year's resolutions in light of the Bible. It warns against rash worldly vows and gives godly principles: forget the past, commit everything to the Lord, and make practical resolutions such as daily Bible reading, prayer, gratitude, witnessing and service. New Year's Resolutions in Light of the Bible Philippians 3:13-14 "Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus." Proverbs 16:3 "Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established." Introduction New Year's Day is seen as a clean break, a fresh start. People make many vows or plans and neglect the will of God while putting too much worry on themselves and the future. The Bible teaches us to say, "If the Lord wills..." James 4:13-15 : "Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away. For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that." Worry about today, one day at a time. Matthew 6:24 : "Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof." I. The Danger of Worldly Resolutions The worldly tradition of New Year's resolutions means many are made with good intentions, but most fail quickly Many resolutions are fleshly or rash. Ecclesiastes 5:4-5 : "When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it... Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay." Jesus warned against careless oaths. Matthew 5:34-37 : "But I say unto you, Swear not at all... But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil." Jesus taught to count the cost. Luke 14:28-30 : "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him, Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish." Secular resolutions often emphasize the physical. 1 Timothy 4:8 : "For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come." Jesus warned about doing acts for show, such as fasting or dieting. Matthew 6:16-18 : "Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast...
