But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face; That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly." They often fail because they ignore God's will for our own. Proverbs 19:21 : "There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand." II. Biblical Principles for Godly Resolutions A. Forget the Past and Press Forward (Philippians 3:13-14) Leave behind failures, sins (confessed and forgiven), and even past successes. 1 John 1:9 : "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness." Remember your standing in Christ: Your sins are gone, and you are righteous in Him. Psalm 103:12 : "As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us." Hebrews 8:12 : "For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more." 2 Corinthians 5:21 : "For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him." Reach forth unto the prize: Move from milk to strong meat—grow up spiritually into maturity - let us go unto perfection Hebrews 5:13-14 : "For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe. But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil." B. Commit Everything to the Lord Proverbs 16:3 ; Psalm 37:5 : "Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass." Proverbs 3:6 : "In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths." Pray over plans; seek God's will first. James 1:5 : "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him." C. Renew Your Mind and Spirit Romans 12:2 : "Be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind..." Psalm 51:10 : "Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me." Galatians 5:16 : "Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh." Daily Bible reading and separation from worldliness. D. Trust God's Plans and Strength Philippians 4:13 : "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me." Isaiah 40:31 : "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint." Romans 8:28 : "And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose." E. If You Fail, Try Again Proverbs 24:16 : "For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief." Lamentations 3:22-23 : "It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness." Don't quit; repent, get up, and keep pressing toward the mark. III. Practical Biblical Resolutions for the New Year Read the Bible Daily Joshua 1:8 : "This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth... then thou shalt have good success." Remember that we need Scripture to survive spiritually. Matthew 4:4 : "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God." Value the Word more than physical sustenance. Job 23:12 : "I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food." Our church is encouraging the challenge: A 31-day plan to read the entire New Testament in January by reading 9 chapters a day, and/or 1 chapter of Proverbs a day (31 chapters for the 31 days—repeat monthly for wisdom). Pray Without Ceasing 1 Thessalonians 5:17 : "Pray without ceasing." James 5:16 : "The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much." Make prayer an all-day conversation with God. Psalm 55:17 : "Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice." More fervent prayer for self, family, church, lost souls, and especially praying for others. Develop an Attitude of Gratitude Philippians 4:6 : "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God." 1 Thessalonians 5:18 : "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you." Avoid grumbling and murmuring. Philippians 2:14 : "Do all things without murmurings and disputings." Witness Boldly Matthew 28:19 : "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations..." Romans 1:16 : "For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek." Share the Gospel more; invite others to church. Grow in Holiness 2 Corinthians 7:1 : "Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God." Ephesians 4:22-24 : "That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts; And be renewed in the spirit of your mind; And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness." Put off sin (the old man—fleshly habits, worldly ways); be renewed in the spirit of your mind. Put on the new man (righteousness and true holiness). Serve in the Church Galatians 5:13 : "By love serve one another." Hebrews 10:25 : "Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching." 1 Thessalonians 5:11 : "Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do." 2 Corinthians 9:7 : "Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver." Conclusion Recap: True resolutions aren't about self, but surrendering to God—He directs, strengthens, and picks us up when we fall. Proverbs 24:16 For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief. Make it about Him. Live day to day. Walk in the Spirit. Build others up. Make this New Year about the new man born inside you by faith in Christ.
Peter Went Out, and Wept Bitterly

Peter Went Out, and Wept Bitterly Takes Peter's denial of Christ and his restoration at the sea of Tiberias as an encouragement for believers who regret missed chances to share the gospel. Shows Peter's later boldness and his epistles' counsel to stand against scoffers. Luke 22:61-62 And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And Peter went out, and wept bitterly. There are times in every Christian's life where the story of Peter's betrayal of Christ hits hard. New Christians, who have just accepted the gospel and been saved, turn to their unsaved family and friends, and at the slightest pushback and mocking, get embarrassed and deny Jesus. Older, more mature Christians even, will keep their faith hidden in social settings or in the workplace. We may miss opportunities to go soul winning with our brothers and sisters, in part because of the fear of judgment. That you will be accused by scoffers as Peter was, and so preemptively decline to go. We all have a regret of not sharing the gospel in a time and place where we are given the opportunity by God to proclaim the faith that saved us. We may weep bitterly by the hospital bed of someone close to us, incapable of knowing the truth because we never shared it. The Apostle Peter's story in the gospels is very real and relatable. But it doesn't end at the crowing of the cock that morning. The risen Christ appears to Peter again during the 40 days between Easter and the Ascension. Peter, unsure of his calling and, I think, ashamed of his betrayal before the Son of God, decided to go fishing. John 21:1-4 After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself. There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples. Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. And as Jesus prepares them food, and eats with them, He gives Peter, who denied Him 3 times, the opportunity to affirm his love of Jesus 3 times. John 21:14-17 This is now the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen from the dead. So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs. He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep. He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep. Peter always loved Jesus, and trusted Him, but his shame for the denial of his Lord in His hour of death made him feel distant and alone. Jesus gave him the opportunity to work through that shame and realize his love for Christ is greater than his shame at letting Jesus down. And Jesus says at each affirmation, feed My sheep. Serve others. Win souls. Care for the flock. The answer to the shame we feel when we deny Christ or the opportunity to share Him with others, isn't to go fishing. To return to the world. But to return to the work of the ministry of reconciliation we all have been given. Soul-winning when you are down bad, and ashamed, when prayer feels a little empty, when Bible reading is falling off, when you know you gotta get right, maybe if the joy of salvation is feeling distant - even if you aren't backsliding, per se, is the way to show yourself the love of Jesus, by showing it to others. It is restorative sharing the love He has for you, and them. Peter's story doesn't end there, either. In Acts we see him boldly proclaiming Christ, calling Jews to repentance towards faith in Jesus. Enduring beatings and imprisonment to preach the gospel. Being supernaturally freed. Having visions and going to the Gentiles with the truth of Christ when called by God. And even then, Peter isn't perfect. Even as an elder of the faith, he still occasionally felt the pressure to conform to the world. Here, he is called out by Paul. Galatians 2:11-14 But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? It is something we can all fall into, even as older, more mature Christians. We are all prone to be like Peter, seeking approval among men, when we should know better. When we should seek the Lord first. That's why, when Peter writes his epistles, his encouraging message to believers to hold fast their faith, even when facing scoffers, mockers, false teachers, etc...to be like Christ when we are reviled for His sake - is so powerful. Like most good preaching, he is talking about his own struggles, to edify others. 1 Peter 2:21-23 21 For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously Being ready to testify of the hope we have even as men falsely accuse us, mocking and scoffing our faith, to have the mind of Christ: Encouraging to not fear these mockers and scoffers as Peter once did, to be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled. To be ready to boldly proclaim your blessed hope; 1 Peter 3:13-16 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ. Even as Noah suffered the scoffers and blasphemers of the pre-flood world, as he prepared the ark, those spirits in Hell that Jesus went and preached to, showing those that trust the Lord shall not be ashamed; Those spirits in prison; By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water. Peter says the flood that destroyed those wicked people is a like figure to the baptism of the believer, showing the same faith and confidence Noah had to build the ark, saving his family. The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ... Our obedience in baptism, to publicly proclaim our faith, similarly shuts the mouths of those scoffers, that our conscience is clean in Christ. 2 Peter 2:1-3 1 But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction. And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not. Verse 7-8, how God delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;) Speaking of a believer who didn't share his faith, Lot still was delivered from their filthy behavior, just as God promises to deliver us from the same mockers and unrighteous people . Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet. 2 Peter 3:3 Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts... And so, if you, like Peter, have wept bitterly over your embarrassment at the cause of Christ, your own missed opportunities and even denials in the face of ridicule and peer pressure, let's learn from Peter's slip ups and mistakes, and take heart in the grace and knowledge of Christ. 2 Peter 3:17-18 Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness. But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen.
Proverbs: Instruction to the Heirs of the Kingdom

Proverbs: Instruction to the Heirs of the Kingdom An overview of the book of Proverbs as Solomon's instruction to his son. It covers raising children in the fear of the LORD, Lady Wisdom against the strange woman, the gospel promises in Proverbs, and its counsel for the princes of the Kingdom. Overview of the book of Proverbs - Instruction to the heirs of the Kingdom I - The book of Proverbs is a gift of God given to man, with a very specific purpose: Proverbs 1:2-6 To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding; To receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, and judgment, and equity; To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion. A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels: To understand a proverb, and the interpretation; the words of the wise, and their dark sayings. That’s the purpose, and this instruction is for everyone: the simple, the young, the wise and the mature person of understanding can all learn from these sayings The book of Proverbs are primarily the recorded sayings of Solomon, to whom God gave an abundance of wisdom; 2 Chronicles 1:7-12 In that night did God appear unto Solomon, and said unto him, Ask what I shall give thee. Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this thy people, that is so great? And God said to Solomon, Because this was in thine heart, and thou hast not asked riches, wealth, or honour, nor the life of thine enemies, neither yet hast asked long life;...: wisdom and knowledge is granted unto thee; and I will give thee riches, and wealth, and honour, such as none of the kings have had that have been before thee, neither shall there any after thee have the like. 1 Kings 4:29 For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan... And he spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five....And there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, which had heard of his wisdom. While as King, Solomon displayed wisdom in ruling, making Israel great again , but ruling in his personal life, not so much. In 1 Kings 11 we read that king Solomon loved many strange women...he had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines: For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father. The wisest man in history, fell prey to the very thing he counseled against. And Solomon used this wisdom to instruct his sole heir, his only recorded son, Rehoboham: Solomon may have written these admonitions to Rehoboam in repentance and regret. He even may have been in the midst of struggling with his sin as he gave them. Parents of teens will see their own bad habits creeping into their children’s behavior, and when we correct them, they often will level charges of hypocrisy to justify themselves, while we are simply looking to help them avoid our own mistakes. Imagine Solomon telling his son not to chase the strange woman of folly when he had entire palaces built to hold his concubines from every nation. The Bible tells us that his son, King Rehoboam had eighteen wives and threescore (60) concubines and that “ He desired many wives. ” but It also says “ he dealt wisely ” as king. (In contrast, Jeroboam, who ruled the split northern kingdom of Israel had but one wife, yet he ruled wickedly and brought in a false religion of idols representing God, with unqualified priests making offerings to them, invented holidays and feasts. Catholicism 1.0) We all fall short, and there are no perfect parents, role models or preachers, we are still called to give ear to the ways of the Lord, and in fear of Him, gain wisdom, and to instruct others in His way, despite our own shortcomings. II - All that to say: With great wisdom comes the great responsibility - to impart the Lord’s ways to our children, be they physical or spiritual; The record of Solomon’s sayings were directed to the instruction of his only son and heir, Rehoboam. Preparing him to rule one day. Solomon writes, My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother, these truths are from God, and it is every parent's responsibility to teach them to our children, that they be an ornament of grace upon their head, and chains about their necks. Fear of the Lord and the wisdom that comes from it - is the greatest inheritance we can give our children. 3 John 1:4 I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth. It is also a command, with promise; Proverbs 22:6 Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it. Raising godly children is a grave responsibility. They are not ours, but His, we are blessed to be stewards, and instruct them as heirs. Not only are we to instruct children in the wisdom of God, but we are to chasten them, correcting them corporally. Proverbs 13:24 - He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes. I guess My Mom REALLY Loved me Proverbs 23:13-14 - Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die. Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell. Proverbs 19:18 - Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying. Spanking your child when they are young, doing it “ betimes ” meaning early, while they are very young, isn’t justifying abuse. A wack on the backside when “No” wasn’t sufficient will often teach the lesson. The establishment of corporal punishment teaches consequences more than trying to reason with a child, as children are inherently foolish: Proverbs 22:15 - Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him. Modern “parenting” has abandoned the wisdom of God, and created a generation of spoiled monsters, afraid of nothing, acting out to the shame of their parents. Proverbs 17:25 - A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him. Proverbs 29:15 - The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame. Proverbs 10:1 - ... a foolish son is the heaviness of his mother . The admonition to chasten your children is tempered with the understanding it is to be done with love. As Ephesians 6:4 commands: And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. The fear of a parent is the first lesson a child receives in fearing the Lord. Fear in this sense is a healthy respect for the authority of the Lord, His terrible judgments and position of authority in our lives, that there are consequences for our actions. Instruction at home establishes this understanding, as parents are proxies for God. As Solomon’s father, David wrote, Psalm 34:11 - Come, ye children, hearken unto me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord. When you read through Proverbs you see that many of the lessons are repeated, again and again, rephrased but carrying the same meaning. It's like those sayings we remember from our parents, who told us a million times. The Father uses repetitions to help get it through our hard hearts and thick skulls, the same way our folks did. Proverbs 9:10 - The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding. Our stewardship over the children God may bless us with, is meant to reflect the Father’s love for His children in Christ. Hebrews 12:5-11 - My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. Understanding of what's right, isn't a guarantee of being righteous in adulthood, but it certainly is a great inoculation against the snares and stumbling stones most people get caught in. We may wander, as we are all prone to. But those guardrails, if established early, can help keep us from venturing too far. Early admonition, a scourging betimes, the willingness to both instruct a child in the way of righteousness and giving them the rod of correction early, will help them form the foundation for fear of the Lord. III - Lady Wisdom vs the strange woman, Folly Solomon’s instruction on chasing after Lady Wisdom, pursuing knowledge, prudence and discretion, and his warning of being misled by the strange woman of folly, serves as both a metaphor for obtaining wisdom and avoiding foolishness, as well as having a practical application against chasing after strange women in a literal sense, avoiding adultery, something the king with a thousand wives and concubines knows all about. Solomon says in Proverbs 7 that the strange woman speaks sweet sayings, and is seductive in her ways, but her end is bitter. Proverbs 7 : My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee. Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye. Bind them upon thy fingers, write them upon the table of thine heart. Say unto wisdom, Thou art my sister; and call understanding thy kinswoman: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, from the stranger which flattereth with her words. Solomon then gives a parable, about a simple young man, in the dark of night, heading to the house of Lady Wisdom (v10) And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart. (She is loud and stubborn; her feet abide not in her house: Now is she without, now in the streets, and lieth in wait at every corner.) …So she caught him, and kissed him, and with an impudent face - she says to him she has given peace offerings and paid her vows, lying, saying essentially that she is ritually clean. Enticing him. (v15) Therefore came I forth to meet thee, diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee. I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt. I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon. Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves. Folly, the fruit of foolishness, of doing the wrong thing when you know better, is incredibly seductive. She flatters - “I was diligently seeking you!” She entices “I decked my bed in preparation for you. Come let us take our fill of love!” it’s one night, only to the morning, right? Where’s the harm? As they say: Sin will take you further than you want to go, keep you longer than you want to stay, and cost you more than you want to pay. In an adulterous relationship, engaging in sin - in our chasing folly; What may start in impulsive lust and seen as temporary, leads to trouble, with long lasting repercussions and consequences. Deadly. Just as the wages of sin is death, the path of folly is death. It shifts suddenly, making it easy to get lost, and the Bible says it is full of snares and stumbling stones. When you think you know where you are and what lies ahead, but instead find yourself caught in the snare of sin. This strange woman will also use the allure of getting away with what you know is wrong to further entice you: For the goodman is not at home, he is gone a long journey: He hath taken a bag of money with him, and will come home at the day appointed. Nibbling at the bait of flattery, at the promise of quick pleasure, closing the trap with the idea of getting away with something you know is wrong, topped with the covetousness of indulging in the rich man’s wealthy lifestyle. It’s a trap. ( v21 ) With her much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him. He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks; Till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life. The dart is a dagger. The fool taken in by Folly, a young man taken in by a harlot, and robbed and murdered. A person led away into sin, and slain by it. (v24) Hearken unto me now therefore, O ye children, and attend to the words of my mouth. Let not thine heart decline to her ways, go not astray in her paths. For she hath cast down many wounded: yea, many strong men have been slain by her. Her house is the way to hell, going down to the chambers of death. In contrast, Lady Wisdom shows us God's paths, which are straight and knowable, a path of life. The Way is laid out and the light of that path is His word. Proverbs 9:1-5 - Wisdom hath builded her house, She hath hewn out her seven pillars: She hath killed her beasts; she hath mingled her wine; She hath also furnished her table. She hath sent forth her maidens: she crieth Upon the highest places of the city, Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: As for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him, Come , eat of my bread, And drink of the wine which I have mingled. The repeated urgent calls from Wisdom (her maidens sent out, crying aloud in public places, inviting the simple/foolish to turn and live) parallels the gospel invitation found throughout scripture, and its urgency. The wedding feast parable ( Matt 22 / Luke 14 ) where the Lord tells his servants to go out to the highways and hedges, bidding both bad and good to come to the supper He has prepared for His Son, is a direct echo of Proverbs 9 . Wisdom calling the simple to her feast, just as we compel others to come and eat the bread and drink of the cup of the New Testament in Christ. Jesus is Wisdom personified (eternal, always existing, present at creation, better than riches, calling all to the feast.) The imagery of bread/wine as the body/blood prefigures or is an archetype of Christ. Jesus is the Wisdom of God ( 1 Cor 1:24, 30; Col 2:3 ), the Bread of Life ( John 6 ), living water ( John 7:37–38 ), and the ultimate fulfillment of the “Way, truth, and life” ( John 14:6 ). The marriage supper of the Lamb that all believers are invited to ( Rev 19 ) is the same feast Lady Wisdom has prepared. This is in stark contrast with Folly (seductive, deceptive, offering sweet-but-deadly pleasures, leading to death and Hell) all echoing the warnings against sin’s allure. The wages of sin, DEATH. Fearing the Lord, and thus seeking wisdom, hearing His word and following His way is the process by which we learn the gospel and believe. IV - The gospel promise of being delivered by the Lord is found throughout Proverbs. Beginning in chapter 1, Solomon places first things first: Proverbs 1:7 The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction. The call to learn fear of the Lord also carries His promises: Proverbs 1:33 But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from fear of evil. Proverbs 3:5-6 Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths. Throughout Proverbs we are told that the end of sin is death and destruction. And as we read the warnings and advice, if we have the fear of the Lord, if we are wise, we are convicted. The sayings against lying, laziness, being a talebearer or a gossip, holding anger for our neighbor, drinking, gluttony, being froward, a scoffer…all show we have all fallen short of the glory of God. Proverbs 24:9 tells us that even the thoughts of foolishness are sin! We all have had foolish thoughts. - Some of you are having them right as we speak! It is impossible to study Proverbs and not come away with the understanding that we are all sinners. But God commendeth His love towards us, that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. Proverbs 8:17 I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me. Proverbs 8:35-36 For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the LORD. But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death. Proverbs 3:33 The curse of the LORD is in the house of the wicked: but he blesseth the habitation of the just. Proverbs 9:10-11 The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding. For by me thy days shall be multiplied, and the years of thy life shall be increased. Proverbs 10:3 The LORD will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish: but he casteth away the substance of the wicked. Proverbs 11:8 The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead. Proverbs 11:21 Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered. Proverbs 14:26 In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge. Proverbs 15:29 The LORD is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous. Proverbs 18:10-11 - The name of the LORD is a strong tower : The righteous runneth into it, and is safe. The rich man's wealth is his strong city, And as an high wall in his own conceit. Again and again, we find the promise of the Lord to all who harken to Him, and His wrath reserved to those who reject Him. This promise of deliverance is contrasted with the earthly things a man may put his trust in: the rich man's trust is in his wealth and the works he does. As Jesus said; It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. We must choose humility, seeking that strong tower of the Lord as our only strength, rather than the haughty pride of the man who places his trust in the walls he has built for himself. Proverbs 22:4 By humility and the fear of the LORD are riches, and honour, and life. Proverbs 29:25 The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe. As you can see, the promises of the Gospel are repeated again and again. Proverbs 30:4 Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell? V - Instruction for the prince (and princesses) of the Kingdom My opinion is that the wisdom for princes and kings is also intended for the saved. That as co-heirs with Christ, who will rule and reign with Him during the millennium, and during any stewardship He blesses us with in this life, we need to understand these principles. To study to be approved unto God. Proverbs 25:1 : These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out. Hezekiah, the righteous son of the wicked king Ahaz, a descendant of Solomon who came roughly 250 years and 13 generations later, brought revival to Judah. He repaired the Temple, removed idols, restored Passover, and called the people back to the Lord. In that zeal he commanded these proverbs to be written down and preserved by his scribes, as instruction of righteousness and to pass on to future kings, including us. Even the least in the Kingdom of Heaven is a prince, who will judge angels. Study the word like princes and princesses who are under tutors, waiting for the day of adoption. The resurrection, when we come into our power as glorified children of God. Galatians 4:1-2 Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father. The primary context Paul is writing here, is understanding that the OT law serves to bring a man to understand our need for a savior, but the application also mirrors the process of a prince coming into his own by instruction, until the determined time of the King. As Paul writes in Romans 8:23 . ..even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body. The day of redemption, the resurrection, is the day of our adoption; the time of the giving of the inheritance, to rule and reign with Jesus. The Greek word Paul uses for 'adoption,' huiothesia , carries a heavier legal meaning than our modern idea of adoption. In that context, it wasn't about bringing an outsider into a family; it was the formal ceremony, the "placing as a son," where an heir reached the age of maturity, the father publicly recognized them as a legal adult, granting them the full authority, a signet ring, and power to manage the estate, or the lands appointed them. We become children of God when we are born again, but notice the adoption is at the resurrection. On the day of redemption. So, when we see proverbs about kings or princes, about judgement and mercy, who to be influenced by, who to seek counsel from...it is all instructions from THE King, God our Father, to His children, who will inherit the Kingdom. Theme Verse(s) Key Point Seek wise counsel Prov 20:18 – “ Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war. ” Good rulers seek multiple wise counselors before major decisions. Rule with justice & mercy Prov 20:28 – “ Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy. ” Mercy and truth stabilize a throne. Establish throne in righteousness Prov 25:5 – “ Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness .” Remove wicked advisors; rule righteously. Judge righteously Prov 29:14 – “ The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever. ” Protect and judge the poor fairly. Delight in truth & justice Prov 16:12 – “ It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness: for the throne is established by righteousness. ” Righteousness, not wickedness, establishes rule. Listen to reproof Don’t drink/pervert judgment Prov 15:31 – “ The ear that heareth the reproof of life abideth among the wise. ” Proverbs 31:4-5 It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted . A wise ruler accepts correction. A wise ruler is sober, not given to lusts that will corrupt their discernment and judgement Listen to your parents/elders Proverbs 1:8-9 : "My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother: For they shall be an ornament of grace unto thy head, and chains about thy neck " A wise ruler will seek wisdom from the older, more experienced people. Starting with their parents and extending to the “hoary heads” Compare with the admonition of what NOT to do: Theme Verse(s) Key Point Oppress the poor Prov 22:16 – “ He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches… shall surely come to want. ” Exploiting the poor for gain brings ruin. Accept bribes Prov 17:23 – “A wicked man taketh a gift out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment.” Bribery perverts justice. Rule with pride & violence Prov 28:15–16 – “As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people. The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor…” Wicked rulers terrorize and oppress. Listen to wicked counsel Prov 29:12 – “If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants are wicked. ” Bad advisors corrupt the whole administration. Remove landmarks / justice Prov 23:10 – “ Remove not the old landmark… ” Moving boundaries to cheat the poor is wicked. So we learn how a prince or princess should act. To be fair in judgment, not being a respecter of persons. We should delight in truth and reject lies. We should reject bribes and not be oppressive to those in need. We should seek wise counsel in war, and the safety of a multitude of councillors. It isn't wise to leave things to a committee, but rather, as a leader, seek options and opinions from other wise men. VI - Closing The wisdom given to Solomon was and is the greatest wisdom possessed of man, before or since. And we have been blessed by God to have much of this inspired wisdom providentially preserved in God's word. Although Solomon is said to have composed 3,000 proverbs, only 800 bearing his name appear in the book of Proverbs, these are the inspired word of God and given for our admonition and instruction. We also were given the book of Ecclesiastes , or the wisdom of the prophet of God, in which Solomon set out to test the truth in all things of this world, only to find all is vanity, except in the worship of the Lord. True philosophy from the Spirit. We have only one song of the 1,005 King Solomon composed, the Song of Songs, and its deep meaning, and reflections on Christ and believers. We have the cream of the wisdom given to Solomon by God, at our fingertips. Able to study and know it. What a blessing. But of the other proverbs and hundreds of songs and all his deep knowledge of flora and fauna and things of this earth and this life, we have no record. Only those sayings which pertain to God. Let this be a lesson for us, who are the co-heirs with Christ. To apply the wisdom, and discernment that is found in God’s word. To learn His ways, which are not our ways. In all our ways acknowledge Him, and He will direct our paths.

Psalm 32: The Blessedness of Forgiveness A Wednesday night study of David's psalm on forgiveness, tied to Paul's use of it in Romans 4. Walks through confession and God's mercy to the forgiven believer, with a deeper study of the words transgression, sin and iniquity. Wednesday Night Service A Psalm of David · The blessedness of forgiveness Psalm 32 1 Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. 2 Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile. 3 When I kept silence, my bones waxed old through my roaring all the day long. 4 For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: my moisture is turned into the drought of summer. Selah. 5 I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid. I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the LORD; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin. Selah. 6 For this shall every one that is godly pray unto thee in a time when thou mayest be found: surely in the floods of great waters they shall not come nigh unto him. 7 Thou art my hiding place; thou shalt preserve me from trouble; thou shalt compass me about with songs of deliverance. Selah. 8 I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye. 9 Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding: whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle, lest they come near unto thee. 10 Many sorrows shall be to the wicked: but he that trusteth in the LORD, mercy shall compass him about. 11 Be glad in the LORD, and rejoice, ye righteous: and shout for joy, all ye that are upright in heart. The Blessedness of Forgiveness Psalm 32:1–2 Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile. Psalm 32 opens with a very familiar and important doctrine, the understanding of God’s forgiveness for sin in the saved believer’s life. This foundational fact is repeated by Paul in the letter to the Romans: Romans 4:6–8 Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin. The truth is that, in Christ, whether it was in David’s day, or Paul’s or our own, God forgives believer’s past transgressions, covers our current sin, and will not hold our future sins and iniquity against us. This positional standing of righteousness before God, despite our sins, through His imputed righteousness — the Righteousness of Christ, is made possible, through the atonement of Jesus’ blood, and by the Holy Spirit, by the renewal, the regeneration, the quickening of our spirit — the new man within us. Blessed is the man in whose spirit there is no guile. We are given the Spirit of truth, that we may acknowledge our sin, knowing that we are forgiven of all sin — first, not by works but by faith. The same good news today as in David’s day. And this Psalm serves as an evangelical appeal. The lack of guile, or cunning duplicity and dishonesty, is both a feature of having the Spirit of truth within us, but is also the understanding that not lying to God and ourselves about our own sin is necessary for the blessings that come from forgiveness. Confession is good for the soul. The Weight of Silence Psalm 32:3–5 When I kept silence, my bones waxed old through my roaring all the day long. For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: my moisture is turned into the drought of summer. Selah. I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid. I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the LORD; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin. Selah. David writes of a man who kept his silence, who hadn’t called upon the name of the Lord, who suffered in their sins — bones waxing old and dried up by their roaring in the daytime, the heaviness of their iniquity weighing on them at night. This of course applies to the lost, in that their conscience, if it has not been seared by reprobation, should eat at them. Convicting them, to bring them to make a decision about Christ. But it also applies to the saved, who are withholding confession to God and deceiving themselves about the wrong we may do. The honesty and humility of acknowledging sin, not hiding anything from God, not remaining silent, confessing our transgressions unto the Lord, and knowing we are forgiven, is a blessing. Sinning throughout the day and being kept up at night by their conscience, being convicted in the Spirit, gives way to the peace that passes understanding — through the forgiveness that is given to us by God’s mercy and grace. 1 John 1:6–9 If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. Seek the Lord While He May Be Found Psalm 32:6 For this shall every one that is godly pray unto thee in a time when thou mayest be found: surely in the floods of great waters they shall not come nigh unto him. David reminds us that there is a time where God may be sought, before it is too late. Isaiah 55:6 Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near. God’s Spirit will not always strive with man. There comes a time when those that put off or reject the truth, not acknowledging that they are sinners, lying to God and themselves, are no longer able to come to Him, where He no longer extends His hand, because they have hardened their hearts and will not seek Him, even as they face destruction. Hebrews 4:7 Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts. We have the example of those who, in the days of Noah, mocked him for his faith in preparing the ark, and whose disobedient spirits — to whom Christ preached to in Hell — were destroyed by the flood, never coming nigh unto God. Just as those left to God’s wrath in the time to come will not repent, despite the horrors of His judgment. Revelation 9:20–21 And the rest of the men which were not killed by these plagues yet repented not of the works of their hands, that they should not worship devils, and idols of gold, and silver, and brass, and stone, and of wood: which neither can see, nor hear, nor walk: Neither repented they of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts. For the lost, there is a time where God no longer extends His hand, where He gives them up and gives them over, to hold the truth in unrighteousness and believe lies, condemning themselves. But Christians can also put off acknowledging and turning from the sin in their lives as well. We can lie to ourselves, rationalize it, and ignore the chastening of God. Hebrews 10:26–31 For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries… It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. Now Is the Day of Salvation The Evangelical Appeal There is a time, it is today. There is a day, and it is the present. If you haven’t accepted the truth that we are sinners in need of salvation, and that it is offered as a free gift to all who believe, through the grace of Almighty God — now is the time. 2 Corinthians 6:2 (For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.) Those who have heard and responded to the truth, who in the appointed day prayed unto Him, can rest assured that we are saved. But understand that God will chasten us, and can even call us home if we continue in sin. The promises of God to His children who walk in His ways are a blessing. Getting right with God is its own reward. Thou Art My Hiding Place Psalm 32:7–9 Thou art my hiding place; thou shalt preserve me from trouble; thou shalt compass me about with songs of deliverance. Selah. I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye. Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding: whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle, lest they come near unto thee. This is the hope we have — the same hope the congregations of the children of Israel sang of in the temple of Solomon, with the songs of his father David echoing this blessed promise, centuries before the first coming of Christ Jesus. And God responds to His children, in this inspired Psalm, promising to teach and guide us in His ways. He asks we come willingly, that we have the understanding to walk with Him, and not be like the horse or mule, needing a bit and bridle to pull us along. His yoke is light. The burden is easy. Be Glad and Rejoice Psalm 32:10–11 Many sorrows shall be to the wicked: but he that trusteth in the LORD, mercy shall compass him about. Be glad in the LORD, and rejoice, ye righteous: and shout for joy, all ye that are upright in heart. The wicked may suffer their sorrows of their own making, but we who are forgiven by His mercy — because we trust in the Lord — are preserved. What an amazing relief to know we are already forgiven; that we may come boldly before God to sing His praises, glorifying Him for His mercies’ sake. Amen! Deeper Study Transgression, Sin & Iniquity While it isn’t entirely wrong to take the words transgression, sin and iniquity and use them interchangeably, they do carry subtle differences in their meaning. Transgression Transgression is the wilful rebellion against the truth of God and His commands. The transgression of Adam, for example, having one law to obey, and choosing of their own volition (even as Eve was deceived, Adam most assuredly knew better), deciding to be disobedient. Sin Sin, which the Bible says is the transgression of the Law, also carries with it the idea of missing the mark, falling short. Romans 3:23 For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God. We aren’t able, in the flesh, to hit the mark — the target being the perfect holiness of God. Only Jesus Christ did. 2 Corinthians 5:21 For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. Iniquity Iniquity comes from the Hebrew word Avon, meaning to twist, bend, or distort — the perverted and crooked nature of fallen man. The bent toward evil, the perverted character that drives the outward actions. It is the guile or deceit mentioned in verse 2 coupled with reflexive actions to do evil to others. The propensity to lie, to steal, to lust, to covet. Our natural tendencies toward willful rebellion, to sin, and to lie to ourselves and others — including God — about the evil that we do. Isaiah 53 · The Cleared Ledger Taken Together: The Blessed Assurance Taken together, the blessed assurance found in verse 1–2, that our transgressions, sins and iniquities are eternally forgiven demonstrates the mercy and grace of our Lord towards His children, through the suffering of Jesus. Isaiah 53:5–6 But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all. He suffered these things for our iniquity and transgressions, that we may be purged — that His righteousness be imputed on our ledger, even as His blood blots away our sins. 1 John 2:1–2 My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous: And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world. Propitiation is a big word that means a sacrifice that turns away God’s holy anger against sin. Jesus took the punishment that people deserved. The payment for the wages of sin we have accrued. Our transgressions are forgiven, our sin is covered, our iniquity will not be added to our account, because we are justified in Christ. This accounting is a spiritual gift, applied to the ledger — that in judgment, we are found not guilty by God. Justified, just as I’d never sinned. (Theologians call this Penal Substitutionary Atonement — the idea that Jesus paid the price of the debt we owe, so that we do not have to receive the wages of sin. Many professing Christian sects reject this idea, despite the clear teaching of scripture on the propitiation. But whatever you want to call it, it is undeniable that Christ suffered that those who trust on Him won’t.) On the cross, Jesus carried away our rebellion, covered our failures with His blood, and cleared the ledger of our crooked nature by imputing His own perfect righteousness to us — past, present and future — that we may be made the righteousness of God. Deeper Study The Day of Atonement The concept of atonement — by the sacrifice, the scapegoat, and the blood — is established in Leviticus 16. The Sin Offering Leviticus 16:3, 5 Thus shall Aaron come into the holy place: with a young bullock for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering… And he shall take of the congregation of the children of Israel two kids of the goats for a sin offering, and one ram for a burnt offering. Aaron first brought a sin offering for himself and his own household, then a sin offering on behalf of the whole congregation — no priest, however faithful, could stand before God apart from his own need for atonement first. The Scapegoat Leviticus 16:8, 10, 21–22 And Aaron shall cast lots upon the two goats; one lot for the LORD, and the other lot for the scapegoat… But the goat, on which the lot fell to be the scapegoat, shall be presented alive before the LORD, to make an atonement with him, and to let him go for a scapegoat into the wilderness… And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat… And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a land not inhabited. The confessed sins of the people were laid upon the living goat, which was sent away, carrying that guilt out of the camp and out of sight — a picture of sin actually removed, not merely covered over. The Blood at the Mercy Seat Leviticus 16:15, 18–19 Then shall he kill the goat of the sin offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood within the vail… and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat, and before the mercy seat… And he shall sprinkle of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and hallow it from the uncleanness of the children of Israel. Only the high priest, only once a year, only by blood, could come within the veil — and even then, the atonement had to be renewed again the following year. Leviticus 16:29–30 And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all… For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the LORD. Rather than the picture of the imperfect sacrifice, the blood of bulls and goats which could never take away our sin, we have the flawless Lamb, Who took away the sins of the world, and Who is both the ultimate High Priest, and the one blood sacrifice for all time. Hebrews 10:10–14 By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified. He had no sin of His own to sacrifice for. He did not enter a man-made temple, but Heaven itself. He did not offer the blood of animals, but His own flawless blood upon the Mercy Seat in Heaven. Because of what Jesus did as both the High Priest and the Sacrifice, the work is finished. The ledger is cleared permanently. God no longer imputes our iniquity, our sins are eternally covered, and our transgressions have been carried as far as the east is from the west. And God will remember them no more. The Priest Who Sat Down Hebrews 10:11 And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins. In the physical Tabernacle and the Temple of Solomon, there were no chairs. A priest could never sit down, because his job was never done. The blood of bulls and goats only provided a temporary cover for the remembrance of sins, made again every year — meaning the priest had to stay on his feet, continuously working, because he could never truly take away sins. But then we see Jesus, the author and, most importantly, the finisher of our faith, sit down, on the right hand of the Father. Hebrews 10:12–14 But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified. The contrast of those who stood, continually ministering, versus Jesus, Who sat down forever — having perfected them that are sanctified — is a subtle but crucial detail. An interesting side note to the study, that we shouldn’t overlook.

Spiritual Father A Father's Day message honoring the pastor who led the author to Christ. The author tells how he went from a Catholic upbringing with no assurance to hearing the Romans Road and trusting Christ. 1 Corinthians 4:15 For though ye have ten thousand instructers in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the gospel. Father’s day - We have our physical fathers. Loved my dad. Blessed to have wonderful children But Every Christian has a spiritual father - Those who led us to the truth of Christ Today I want to honor mine, Pastor Harry Fletcher. I was raised Catholic, twelve years of parochial school, full catechism, confirmed — I had all the head knowledge and none of the assurance. College, Navy, married with young children. - Playing the roll of “father” We were living with my MIL Nancy - who for sure was an instructor in Christ who was instrumental in leading my oldest children to Christ - She convinced me that we should attend church with her. Pastor Fletcher was a great and gifted preacher. Wonderful sermons, kind. Testimony - 6 months went by, hearing the invitation every Sunday - TUNED IT OUT One beautiful spring day, approaching Easter, 1994. I remember where I was sitting. End seat on the left hand side. Romans Road Pastor Fletcher, began the invitation, as he always did: “With all heads bowed and eyes closed, are there any here this morning who do not know for sure they have eternal life in Christ” - Something about it caught my attention this time.It struck me that I actually did not know for sure. I thought I did but I had to admit to myself I didn’t He said something like “First, we are all sinners. You’ve sinned, I’ve sinned..” Romans 3:10 As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one Romans 3:23 : For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God." I didn’t need any persuading on this. I was struggling with sin every day. “And sin has a price. Death and Hell” I was raised Catholic, of course I knew there was a Hell! The guilt trips convinced me of that. Romans 6:23 For the wages of sin is death… Hebrews 9:27 And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment: But Pastor Fletcher continued the verse … but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord. Again, this struck me. Salvation IS a gift. How often I had heard about a gift, and God’s grace… but I was taught my whole life that ultimately salvation was on me. How could it be a gift if I had to pay for it? That contradiction had always bothered and discouraged me. Romans 5:8 But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. I was struck by this truth. Something I had NEVER heard before. This was entirely new information. I was taught my whole life that we had to cleanse ourselves with baptism, penance and all these things we must do to be “worthy of grace” He continued: Romans 10:9 That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. He said “It is the promise of God Who cannot lie!” That Romans 10:13 said Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. I knew John 3:16 For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever belieth on Him should not perish, but HAVE everlasting life - I KNEW it but never fully understood it. Pastor Fletcher finished the invitation, stressing that once you are saved, born again in Christ, you can never lose that precious gift. John 10:28-29 And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my My Father's hand . I had been taught my whole life that it was a “sin of presumption” to claim to know you will make it to Heaven, but now I saw that’s not what the Bible says. Raised hand - “If you want me to pray for you, or to be shown from the Bible that you can know for sure you're saved, just slip your hand up” He recited the “Sinners prayer,” encouraging those who raised their hands to call upon the name of the Lord. And so I did After the service , as I stood kind of in shock, a man approached me. I knew he was an usher or a deacon, I don’t think I ever learned his name. “You raised your hand during the invitation…do you have questions?” Boy did I! He proceeded to go over it with me again, asking at each step if I believed what he was saying was true. He led me in a prayer, again (just to be sure!). I still remember the joy and relief I felt. So many contradictions in my head were cleared up. So many questions were suddenly answered. I felt like the Ethiopian eunuch -after hearing the gospel and believing, and being baptized by Philip, his father in faith - he went on his way rejoicing. I certainly did. I think about Pastor Fletcher as my “spiritual father.” One sows the seeds, another waters, another harvests - But God gets the increase. Blessed to be the spiritual father to many, some here tonight. And that they have been used by God to lead others - Spiritual Grandfather! Tonight I want to honor my spiritual father and encourage you to as well 3 John 1:4 I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.

Taming Your Tongue Gathers what the Bible says about the tongue, from James 3 and Proverbs. It warns against vulgarity, swearing, gossip and talebearing, and urges using the tongue to praise God, edify others and share the gospel. Taming your tongue James 3:2-5 For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body. Behold, we put bits in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body. Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth. Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth! Ship’s rudder. Antrim helm experience Proverbs 21:23 - Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles. Ecclesiastes 5: 2 Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few. Ephesians 4:29 - Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers. Psalms 141:3 - Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips. Psalms 34:13 - Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile. James 1:26 - If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion is vain. Proverbs 17:28 - Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding. 1 Peter 3:10 - For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile: Proverbs 10:19 - In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise. Psalms 52:2 - Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully. Matthew 12:34 - O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. -Loose lips sink ships Samson and Delilah -Vulgarity, Cussin and swearing -Froward mouth.perverse, disobedient, and obstinate, contrary, negative, Jerk Proverbs 4: 24 - Put away from thee a froward mouth, and perverse lips put far from thee. Don't be a jerk. Don't say offensive things. Proverbs 16:28 ,- A froward man soweth strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends. Swearing is a vow Ecclesiastes 5:4-5 When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay. Matthew 5:34-37 But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil. Ecclesiastes 5:6 Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands? A Whisperer - Gossip, backbiter, talebearer Talebearer: A person who spreads secrets or rumors, and things that happen to others. "He that goeth about as a talebearer revealeth secrets; Therefore meddle not with him that openeth wide his lips." Proverbs 20:19 "The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly." Proverbs 18:8 Gossip: A person who spreads rumors or secrets. Proverbs 11:13, the concept is present where a "gossip reveals a secret" and the KJV uses the phrase "revealing a secret". "He that goeth about as a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips." Proverbs 11:13 "A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip separates close friends." Proverbs 16:28 Paul lists "gossips" alongside other extreme sinful behaviors like "envy, murder, and malice". Backbiting: Slandering someone when they are not present. The term appears in the KJV along with "whisperers" in verses like Romans 1:30, being filled with all unrighteousness. Busybody: A person who interferes in the affairs of others. 1 Timothy 5:13, Paul warns against idleness that leads to "tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not". Positive uses of the tongue To praise God: "And my tongue shall speak of thy righteousness and of thy praise all the day long" (Psalm 35:28). Sing Psalms hymns Ephesians 5:18-21 And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit; Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ; Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. To speak healing and truth: "the tongue of the wise is health" (Proverbs 12:18), and "A wholesome tongue is a tree of life" (Proverbs 15:4). To edify - encourage and build up others: "Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers" (Ephesians 4:29). To speak peace and love: "For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile: Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it" (1 Peter 3:10-11). Peacemakers Comfort the broken hearted Advocate for the fatherless and widows. To preach God's word to the lost To pray for others. To share the gospel: Use your tongue to share the good news of Jesus Christ to bring salvation to the lost. Gospel presentation To call upon the name of the Lord Romans 10:8-11 But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach;That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation. For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.

The Gift of Helps Looks at 1 Corinthians 12 and the less showy gift of helps as equal in the body of Christ. Urges believers to seek that gift and to serve the church and others with charity. 1 Corinthians 12 Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant. Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led. Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit. And there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord. And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all. But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal. For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit; To another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit; To another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another discerning of spirits; to another divers kinds of tongues; to another the interpretation of tongues: But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will. For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ. At the church in Corinth, there were many disputes among the brethren that Paul needed to address for their edification, and for ours. One cause of contention among them was the distribution of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, with some envying the more flashy gifts and others lording over others for having more comely, or attractive talents given them by God. Verse 19 ; And if they were all one member, where were the body? But now are they many members, yet but one body. And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you. Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary: And those members of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness. For our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked... Paul's point; The importance of each gift being equal to another in the proper execution of the body as a whole. He goes on; Verse 27 Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular. And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues.... My sermon tonight is on the gift of helps. The gift of being a helper to the cause of Christ, and to the body of the local church, of which Christ is our head. Not as flashy as some of the others mentioned. Wouldn't we all like to be healers? To speak diverse languages with ease (or miraculously through the Spirit?) During the time of the New Testament churches, where some of the more extraordinary gifts were given for a sign, the natural human desire to be "special" must have weighed heavily on those not given to miraculous gifts. But even now, there can be envy at those that are prophets, preachers, who are the center of attention, teachers or those who have the gift of governments, overseeing some aspect of the church's leadership. But Paul tells us there's a more excellent way. That if we should desire and seek gifts of God, the first should be charity; to do all things for the profit of others, in love. A voluntary giving of help to others. 1 Corinthians 13:13-14:1,12 And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity....Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts..,Even so ye, forasmuch as ye are zealous of spiritual gifts, seek that ye may excel to the edifying of the church. There are many early Christians who are immortalized in Paul's Epistles for their ministry in the church. Here in 1 Corinthians 16 , the Apostle calls out Stephanas ( 1 Corinthians 1:16; 16:15-17 ) – whose household was baptized by Paul, and who had addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints. What a beautiful example for us. The list of helpers in Romans 16 is perhaps the most well known; Phebe, Priscilla, Aquila, Epaenetus, Mary, Andronicus, Junia, Amplias, Urbane, Stachys, Apelles, Tryphena, Tryphosa, Persis, Rufus . All given the gift of the Spirit of being helpers, ministering to all the saints. An example for us to follow. As Paul writes in Ephesians 4:11 , these gifts are “ For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ… ” Unlike some of the gifts given as signs in the first century, the gift of helps is still given by the Spirit today. We all have it in some measure, as saved believers. The ability to put others before ourselves, and ask "Who needs help? What can I do to pitch in?" To humble ourselves, and put others needs, especially the needs of the church as a whole, before our own. Our role model is Christ Jesus Himself. He made Himself of no reputation, and took upon Him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. ( Philippians 2:7-8 ) The ultimate servant, who without contradiction is the Lord of lords. When the Apostles disputed among themselves over who would be first in the Kingdom of God, Jesus told them If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all . ( Mark 9:35 ) Jesus gave himself as the perfect example, Mark 10:45 For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many. After washing the disciples' feet, Jesus says “If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you. ” ( John 13:14-14 ) Again and again, Jesus calls us to do unto the least of our brothers, and that by doing so, we are doing it unto Him. That when we help a stranger, thereby some have entertained angels unawares. ( Hebrews 13:2) Let no man seek his own, but every man another's wealth. ( 1 Corinthians 10:24 ) Charity, the edifying of others, caring for the poor, and the poor in spirit, serves the Lord, is pleasing to God and will be rewarded. Blessings now, and riches stored up in Heaven. Remembering this, we should desire the gift of helps, to pray that God gives us opportunities throughout our day to be a blessing to others. To guide us in our life to better serve the Lord. To go out of our way to bring His love to someone who needs it. To be ready always help out at church, that the pastor knows he can call on you to do something, and it will get done, cheerfully. Or that a brother or sister in need can know they can count on you in times of trouble. And not just at home, or at church, but in the world. To let our light so shine. To be a servant to others. The Bible says seek not our own profit, but the profit of others, that they may be saved. That we, by our example, may lead them to Christ. Acts 20:35 I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive. There is no greater blessing than to be a help others. So seek after the gift of helps.

Watch Uses Simeon and Anna and the Hebrews 11 saints as examples of those who watched for redemption. Calls believers to watch and wait for Christ's return, redeeming the time by warning and winning souls. Luke 2:25-33 And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him. And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord's Christ.
