Post-Tribulation, Pre-Wrath Timeline Sets out a post-tribulation, pre-wrath timeline in Daniel's seven-year week, with general tribulation, a 75-day great tribulation and then God's wrath. Reads Revelation as two parallel accounts and has the church present through the tribulation. Post-Tribulation, Pre-Wrath Eschatological Timeline Based on a 7-Year Framework with a 75-Day Climactic Great Tribulation This document synthesizes a post-tribulation, pre-wrath rapture view of end-times events, grounded in a plain reading of the King James Version (KJV) scriptures. The timeline spans a 7-year period (Daniel’s “one week”), divided into approximately 3.5 years of general tribulation, a 75-day climactic great tribulation, and a period of God’s wrath, culminating in Christ’s return with glorified saints to establish the millennial kingdom. The Book of Revelation is structured as two parallel accounts (chapters 4-11 and 12-22) of the same events, with tribulation in Revelation 6-7 and 13, and wrath in the trumpets (Revelation 8-9) and vials (Revelation 16). This view refutes pre-tribulationism’s conflation of tribulation and wrath and its invention of “tribulation saints,” affirming the church’s presence during tribulation. Overview of the Timeline 7-Year Framework: Derived from Daniel 9:27’s “one week,” split at the midpoint by the abomination of desolation and the beast’s deadly wound/healing . Key Periods: First 3.5 Years (~1260 days): General tribulation (natural and manmade trials, beast’s rise). 75 Days: Climactic great tribulation, post-abomination and beast’s wound/healing , marked by the beast’s head wound, dragon empowerment, and intense persecution, “cut short” for the elect (Daniel 12:11-12’s 1290-1335 days). Wrath Period: Post-rapture, God’s judgments (trumpets and vials) on the beast’s kingdom while the beast continues his full 42-month reign , followed by Christ’s return with saints. Rapture: Occurs post-tribulation at Christ’s visible second coming (Matthew 24:29-31), after the 75-day climax ( ~1290 days from the abomination ), before wrath . Revelation’s Structure: Chapters 4-11 (heavenly perspective) and 12-22 (cosmic/earthly perspective) overlap, with tribulation in Revelation 6-7 and 13, rapture in Revelation 6:12-17 and 15:2, and wrath in Revelation 8-9 and 16. Chronological Timeline with Key Events and Scriptural Support 1. First 3.5 Years: General Tribulation (~1260 Days) Description: The 7-year period begins with a covenant, likely involving Israel, initiating tribulation—natural and manmade trials including wars, famines, and persecution. The beast rises, setting the stage for its dominance. The church endures these trials, refuting pre-tribulationism’s early rapture. Key Events: Covenant confirmed, starting the 7 years. Wars, famines, and death afflict the world (Revelation’s early seals). Believers face persecution; the beast gains influence. Scriptures: Daniel 9:27 (KJV) — “And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease.” The covenant marks the 7-year start, with the midpoint (~1260 days) pivotal. Revelation 6:1-8 (KJV) — “And I saw… a white horse… and he went forth conquering… a red horse… to take peace from the earth… a black horse… famine… a pale horse… Death.” The first four seals depict tribulation’s trials (war, famine, death). Matthew 24:6-9 (KJV) — “And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars… famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes… Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” Believers endure tribulation. Why: The church’s presence (Matthew 24:9, “ye”) and seals’ trials (Revelation 6) define tribulation as distinct from wrath. Pre-tribulationism’s claim that the church is absent ignores these scriptures. 2. Midpoint: Abomination of Desolation and Beast’s Empowerment (~1260 Days) Description: At the 7-year midpoint, the beast breaks the covenant, halts sacrifices, and sets up the abomination of desolation, triggering the great tribulation. The beast suffers a deadly head wound, is healed (possibly empowered/possessed by the dragon), and begins its 42-month reign, intensifying persecution. Key Events: Abomination of desolation desecrates the temple. Beast’s head wound is healed, gaining global worship. Dragon empowers the beast, starting its 42-month authority. Scriptures: Daniel 9:27 (KJV) — “In the midst of the week… for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate.” The abomination marks the midpoint. Matthew 24:15, 21 (KJV) — “When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation… For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world.” The church (“ye”) faces great tribulation. Revelation 13:3-5 (KJV) — “And I saw one of his heads as it were wounded to death; and his deadly wound was healed: and all the world wondered after the beast… And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months.” The wound and dragon’s power (Revelation 13:2, “the dragon gave him his power”) initiate the beast’s reign. 2 Thessalonians 2:4 (KJV) — “Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God… so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.” This parallels the abomination. Why: The abomination (Daniel 9:27) and beast’s wound (Revelation 13:3) trigger great tribulation, with saints present (Matthew 24:15, Revelation 13:7). Pre-tribulationism’s early rapture contradicts this. 3. 75 Days: Climactic Great Tribulation (~1260 to ~1335 Days) Description: The great tribulation’s climax, a 75-day period post-abomination and beast’s wound, is the most intense phase of persecution, “cut short” for the elect. The beast enforces the mark and image worship, warring against saints, until cosmic signs herald Christ’s return and the rapture. The 75 days derive from Daniel 12:11-12’s 1290-1335 days. Key Events: Beast enforces mark and image worship, persecuting saints. Great tribulation “cut short” to preserve the elect. Cosmic signs (sun darkened, stars fall) signal tribulation’s end. Rapture at Christ’s visible second coming (~1290 days). Scriptures: Daniel 12:11-12 (KJV) — “And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days.” The 1290 days may mark the rapture; 1335 days, a later blessing (e.g., kingdom). Revelation 13:7, 15-17 (KJV) — “And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them… And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast… and as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed… and that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark.” The beast’s persecution peaks. Matthew 24:22, 24 (KJV) — “And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened… insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.” The tribulation is cut short, with the elect present. Revelation 6:12-17 (KJV) — “And the sun became black as sackcloth of hair… And the kings of the earth… said… hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb.” Cosmic signs match Matthew 24:29. Matthew 24:29-31 (KJV) — “Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened… And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven… and they shall see the Son of man coming… And he shall send his angels… and they shall gather together his elect.” The rapture occurs post-tribulation. Revelation 7:9-14 (KJV) — “A great multitude… These are they which came out of great tribulation.” The multitude is raptured post-tribulation. Revelation 15:2 (KJV) — “And I saw… them that had gotten the victory over the beast… stand on the sea of glass.” These saints, post-75 days, parallel Revelation 7’s multitude. Why: The 75-day climax (Daniel 12:11-12) aligns with the beast’s persecution (Revelation 13:7) and cosmic signs (Revelation 6:12), ending with the rapture (Matthew 24:31). The church’s presence refutes pre-tribulationism, as saints endure the mark and deception (Matthew 24:24). Revelation’s parallel accounts place this in both 6-7 and 13-15. The beast’s full 42-month reign continues through the subsequent wrath period. 4. Half Hour of Silence: Transition to Wrath (~1290 Days) Description: After the rapture, a brief pause in heaven marks the shift from tribulation to God’s wrath, as the seventh seal is opened. Key Event: Silence in heaven, preparing for judgments. Scripture: Revelation 8:1 (KJV) — “And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour.” Why: The silence follows the sixth seal’s rapture (Revelation 6:12-17), distinguishing tribulation from wrath. The church, now raptured, is spared wrath (1 Thessalonians 5:9). 5. Wrath: Trumpets and Vials (~1290 to ~1335 Days or Beyond) Description: God’s wrath, post-rapture, targets the beast’s kingdom via trumpets and vials, which are parallel judgments in Revelation’s two accounts (4-11 and 12-22). The beast and his followers endure these supernatural judgments. Key Events: Trumpets afflict the earth (third part affected). Vials intensify judgments (universal scope). Beast’s kingdom suffers, gathers for Armageddon. Scriptures: Revelation 8:7 (KJV) — “The first angel sounded… hail and fire mingled with blood… a third part of trees was burnt up.” Revelation 16:2 (KJV) — “The first… vial… a noisome and grievous sore upon the men which had the mark of the beast.” Revelation 16:10 (KJV) — “And the fifth angel poured out his vial… and his kingdom was full of darkness; and they gnawed their tongues for pain.” Revelation 16:13-14 (KJV) — “And I saw three unclean spirits… go forth unto the kings of the earth… to gather them to the battle of that great day of God Almighty.” 1 Thessalonians 5:9 (KJV) — “For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ.” Why: Trumpets and vials, as parallel wrath (Revelation 8-9, 16), follow the rapture, targeting the beast’s followers (Revelation 16:2). The church’s absence during wrath aligns with the tribulation/wrath distinction, refuting pre-tribulationism’s conflation. The beast continues his reign throughout this period. 6. Christ’s Return with Glorified Saints and Millennial Kingdom (~1335 Days or Later) Description: After wrath, Christ returns with glorified saints (raptured earlier) to defeat the beast and false prophet, bind Satan, and establish the 1,000-year kingdom. Key Events: Christ returns with saints, defeats the beast. Beast and false prophet cast into the lake of fire. Satan bound for 1,000 years. Millennial kingdom established. Scriptures: Revelation 19:11-14 (KJV) — “And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True… And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” Revelation 19:20 (KJV) — “And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet… These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.” Revelation 20:1-3 (KJV) — “And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years.” Revelation 20:4-6 (KJV) — “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them… and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” Daniel 7:27 (KJV) — “And the kingdom… shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.” Revelation 11:15 (KJV) — “The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ.” This parallels Revelation 19 in the 4-11 account. Why: Christ’s return with saints (Revelation 19) follows wrath, fulfilling the kingdom’s establishment (Revelation 11:15, 20:4). The church, raptured post-tribulation, returns glorified, aligning with this view. Refutation of Pre-Tribulationism This timeline counters pre-tribulationism’s errors: Church’s Presence: Saints endure tribulation (Revelation 13:7, Matthew 24:24), facing the beast’s mark and abomination, contradicting an early rapture. Visible Rapture: The rapture at Christ’s second coming (Matthew 24:29-31, Revelation 6:12-17) is visible (Revelation 1:7), not secret. Tribulation vs. Wrath: Tribulation (persecution, disasters) is distinct from wrath (God’s judgments), with the church enduring the former (Revelation 6-7, 13) but spared the latter (Revelation 8-9, 16). No Invented Doctrines: “Saints” (Revelation 7:14, 13:7) are the church, not a separate “tribulation saints” group, aligning with a plain reading. Conclusion This post-tribulation, pre-wrath timeline, rooted in Daniel’s 7-year framework and Revelation’s parallel accounts, places the church in tribulation (3.5 years, 75-day climax), raptured at Christ’s visible second coming (~1290 days), spared wrath (trumpets/vials), and returning with Christ to establish the millennium. The 75-day climactic great tribulation, post-abomination and beast’s wound, is a pivotal period of intense persecution, cut short for the elect. Timeline of Days in Daniel 8 and 12

Timeline of Days in Daniel 8 and 12 Lays out the 2,300, 1,290 and 1,335 days of Daniel 8 and 12 within the seven-year week of Daniel 9:27. Divides the period into its two halves. Timeline of Days in Daniel 8 and 12 I. Daniel 8:13-14 – Vision of the Sanctuary Cleansing Daniel 8:13-14 Then I heard one saint speaking, and another saint said unto that certain saint which spake, How long shall be the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, and the transgression of desolation, to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot? And he said unto me, Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed. II. Daniel 12:11-12 – Specific Time Periods Daniel 12:11-12 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. III. Timeframe Breakdown Total Period: 7 Years Daniel 9:27 And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease… The "week" equals 7 prophetic years, calculated as 2,520 days (7 x 360-day lunar year+a “leap month" of 30 days). First Half: 3.5 Years (Tribulation of the Saints, 1,260 Days) Daniel 7:25 And he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time. This period of 1,260 days (3.5 x 360) represents the tribulation where the saints face persecution. Midpoint: Abomination of Desolation Daniel 9:27 …and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate… Occurs at the 1,260-day mark, splitting the 7 years. Second Half: 3.5 Years (Great Tribulation, 1,260 Days + 30 Days) Daniel 7:25 …a time and times and the dividing of time. Extends to 1,290 days: Daniel 12:11 And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days. Extra 30 Days: The 1,290 days include the 1,260 days of the second half plus an additional 30 days, likely an intercalary month in the Jewish lunar calendar to align the 360-day prophetic years with the solar calendar, ensuring proper timing of events. Additional 45 Days (Great Tribulation Concludes) Daniel 12:12 Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days. The 1,335 days extend 45 days beyond the 1,290 days (1,335 - 1,290 = 45). Total 75 Days: The 30 days (1,290 - 1,260) plus 45 days (1,335 - 1,290) form a 75-day period of intensified great tribulation, overlapping the second half’s end, concluding key events. Wrath of God: 3.5 Years (Post-1,335 Days) The remaining time after the 1,335 days (approximately 1,260 days, calculated as 2,520 total days minus 1,260 tribulation days and 75 great tribulation days) aligns with the period of God’s wrath, following the conclusion of the great tribulation.
Dispensationalism, an Enemy of Soul Winning

Dispensationalism, an Enemy of Soul Winning An excerpt from Jack Hyles, Enemies of Soul Winning, chapter 2, on ultra-dispensationalism. Holds that salvation has always been by grace through faith and answers the Scofield footnote on legal obedience. From "Enemies of Soul Winning" (Chapter 2: Ultra-Dispensationalism - An Enemy of Soul Winning) "I have no problem with the word 'dispensation.' It is a Bible word, but I do have a problem with dispensationalism which says that salvation comes in different ways in different dispensations. For example, the Scofield Reference Bible , page 1115, in sub point (2) of footnote 1 on grace, notice the words, 'As a dispensation, grace begins with the death and resurrection of Christ (Rom. 3. 24-26; 4. 24, 25)'. The note continues as follows, 'The point of testing is no longer legal obedience as the condition of salvation, but acceptance or rejection of Christ....' Now it is certainly true that salvation in this age is by acceptance or rejection of Christ, but Mr. Scofield is wrong when he says that before the death and resurrection of Christ the condition of salvation was legal obedience! This is what I call 'hyper-Dispensationalism' . There are those who likewise erroneously believe that salvation will be other than grace through faith during the millennium. This is also heresy! Salvation has always been and will always be by grace through faith in Christ. From the first sin in the garden of Eden until the last person who is saved in the millennium, every person who goes to Heaven will go there by grace. I take even stronger issue with the hyper-Dispensationalism which says that the letters to the seven churches in Asia Minor in Revelation 2 and 3 represent seven ages of church history. This kind of heresy is no where to be found in the Word of God, and the danger of it is that these hyper-dispensationalists enjoy teaching that since this is the day of apostasy, God does not do any great works anymore and that this is the day where we just hold out faithful to the end. According to them, no great churches can be built, and no great revivals can be had. It is a wicked thing for dusty Bible teachers with their dusty theology to compartmentalize the Bible concerning salvation and soul winning. It doesn't bother me for someone to talk about dispensations, and it doesn't bother me for people to divide the Bible, as long as they do not divide it up concerning the plan of salvation, concerning the power of God, and concerning soul winning! People can be saved today like they were in the book of Acts! God's people can have revival just like they always could! I am not fighting Dispensationalism; I am attacking vigorously the heresy and false teaching that says it can't be done today. Whatever God could do, God can do! Whatever God can do, God will do, if His people meet His conditions!" From "Exploring Prayer" (Chapter 9: God Is Trying to Get It to You!) "One of the great enemies of prayer is the temptation to take a prayer promise and apply it to some other age or dispensation, invalidating most of the Bible and its promises to us in this age. To be sure, there is a dispensational teaching in the Bible (though I think much too much emphasis is placed on it). In most cases, however, God's attitude toward one era and toward one people is the same as His attitude toward another era and another people. I am not disputing dispensational truth; I am disputing that kind of ultra-dispensationalism that almost makes it necessary for God to give us an audible promise for today since all the others have been used up in other dispensations! This is especially dangerous when we leave the impression, for example, that the dispensation of grace started at Pentecost. The dispensation of grace started the minute Adam and Eve sinned in the Garden of Eden. Adam was saved by grace, Abraham was saved by grace, David was saved by grace, and though I am sure the theologian does not intend to teach that salvation was ever any other way but by grace, he nevertheless leaves the impression to the immature mind by the very nature of the term, 'dispensation of grace'. The fact that THE dispensation of grace is mentioned implies that there was a time when we were not under the dispensation of grace. Every soul that has been saved since Adam and that will be saved until the last one comes to Christ in the millennium will be saved by grace through faith in God's provision for our salvation through the finished work of His Son, Jesus, on Calvary! Much harm has been done to the cause of Christ by non-soulwinning theologians who take far too much Bible from us and leave far too little Bible for us. We are so busy relegating the promises of God to another era that we are nearly bereft of His promises for today." From "Exploring Prayer" (Chapter 6: Answered Prayer Depends on a Changeless God) "There is a great danger of ultra-dispensationalism. Some things in the Bible do change, but some things never change; some things outlive a dispensation and cross over the line between the dispensations."

John R. Rice on Election Gives background on Calvinism and Arminianism and then sets out John R. Rice's teaching on unlimited atonement, whosoever-will salvation and election. Closes with the biblical fundamentalist view of election as a call to service and holiness. Historical and Theological Context: Calvinism and Arminianism Calvinism, often summarized today by the acronym TULIP (Total Depravity, Unconditional Election, Limited Atonement, Irresistible Grace, and Perseverance of the Saints), refers to a system of soteriology emphasizing God's absolute sovereignty in salvation. Its roots trace back to Augustine of Hippo (354–430 AD), who, after spending nearly a decade as a follower of Manichaean Gnosticism—a dualistic sect teaching determinism, total human inability apart from divine intervention, and a form of predestined election—incorporated similar premises into his later theology. While Augustine rejected Manichaeism's dualism, he retained and adapted ideas of inevitable human evil, unilateral divine predetermination, and grace that overrides human will, framing them monistically under one God. These concepts marked a shift from earlier church fathers' views on free will and were seen by some contemporaries as a "Gnosticized" heresy infiltrating Christianity. John Calvin (1509–1564) drew heavily from Augustine but did not systematize the full TULIP framework himself; his theology was less rigidly extreme on issues like limited atonement or double predestination. The strict five-point TULIP formulation emerged later at the Synod of Dort (1618–1619) as a response to Arminian challenges, and it gained sharper definition and popularity in Reformed circles during the 19th and early 20th centuries, becoming widely held in modern American Protestantism, particularly among Reformed Baptists. Arminianism arose in the early 17th century as a direct response to high Calvinism's interpretations of election and predestination. Jacobus Arminius and his followers accepted many of the same foundational assumptions—such as total depravity requiring prevenient grace and election tied to individual salvation—but conditioned election on foreseen faith—that is, on God's foreknowledge of who would believe—and emphasized unlimited atonement, resistible grace, and the potential “loss” of salvation. It sought to preserve human responsibility and God's universal love but shared the over-systematized framework that prioritized philosophical coherence on sovereignty and will over the Bible's plain emphasis on whosoever-will evangelism. In the 20th Century, Fundamentalist Baptists came to prominence. Although there is an unbroken line of Bible-believing Christians—living faith to faith and rejecting both the theological systems of the Protestants and the vain traditions and dead works of the apostate Roman church—widespread prominence for such voices did not come until late 19th- and 20th-century America. Freedom from persecution, due to the religious liberty enshrined in our Constitution (which was added due to influence of early Colonial Baptists), allowed Biblical alternatives to these systems to be widely promulgated. Dr. John R. Rice on election Dr. John R. Rice (1895–1980) was a prominent Independent Fundamental Baptist evangelist, pastor, author, and founder/editor of The Sword of the Lord newspaper (started in 1934). He was a key figure in 20th-century American Fundamentalism, known for his emphasis on biblical inerrancy, soul-winning evangelism, premillennialism, separation from modernism/liberalism/worldliness/formalism, and the verbal inspiration and divine preservation of Scripture. His ministry focused heavily on revival meetings, soul-winning campaigns, and publishing materials that promoted New Testament evangelism and personal holiness. Rice's teachings on atonement, salvation, and election rejected both strict Calvinism (especially its "five points" or TULIP) and Arminianism as overly systematized extremes that distort the plain biblical emphasis on grace, human responsibility, and the universal gospel offer. Key Aspects of Rice's Teachings Atonement: Rice strongly advocated an unlimited/general atonement. Christ died as a substitute for the sins of the whole world, all of the fallen creation, providing a sufficient, propitiatory sacrifice (blood atonement) that objectively removes the barrier of sin for all humanity and makes salvation genuinely available to everyone. He viewed limited atonement (a core of Reformed/hyper-Calvinism) as limiting God's love, grace, and provision, essentially slandering God by implying Christ did not die for all. He cited verses like 1 Timothy 2:6 , 1 John 2:2 , Romans 5:20 , and 1 Timothy 4:10 to argue that Christ is the "Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe" —potential/intentional for all, personal/effective for believers. The cross achieves real reconciliation and propitiation universally, but its benefits apply personally through faith. Salvation: Salvation is by grace through faith alone, not of works, wholly on the merits of Christ's atoning blood. It is instant for penitent believers, involving regeneration (new birth), forgiveness, and eternal security once received. Rice emphasized personal faith in Christ's death, burial, and resurrection as the means of receiving eternal life. He rejected any notion of salvation by human merit, rites, or works, while stressing that believers walking in the Spirit, answering calls to election in service, will lead to changed lives, and soul-winning as the calling all believers have, bringing us unto perfection (that is, maturity in the faith, not sinlessness). He opposed both Calvinist irresistible grace (which he saw as removing free response) and Arminian loss of salvation (affirming perseverance/eternal security for true believers). Salvation is a free gift offered to whosoever believes, enabled by God's grace but requiring personal trust. Election and Foreknowledge: Rice rejected unconditional election to salvation (Calvinist view) and conditional election based on foreseen faith (classic Arminian view). He saw election as God's sovereign choosing for roles, service, calling, or purpose—not synonymous with individual predestination to eternal life. Foreknowledge in Romans 8:29 is not God previewing who would believe and then electing them (Arminian), nor sovereign decree apart from response (Calvinist/hyper-Calvinist). Instead, it involves relational intimacy and God's plan for believers (corporate/categorical), assuring NT believers of the same outcomes seen in OT saints (foreknown, predestined to conformity to Christ, called, justified, glorified). Election is purpose-oriented (e.g., to holiness, service, or blessing), not a predetermined selection for damnation or irresistible salvation. Overall Stance on Calvinism and Arminianism Rice explicitly opposed both systems as "two sides of the same coin" or extremes that over-systematize Scripture. He labeled strict five-point Calvinism (especially limited atonement and unconditional election to salvation) as "hyper-Calvinism"—a false doctrine that limits God's love/grace, hinders evangelism by implying some cannot be saved, and contradicts universal atonement texts. He was not Arminian either, rejecting salvation's dependence on human initiative apart from grace, loss of salvation, or any works element. Instead, he urged following the Bible plainly: free grace offered to all through Christ's sufficient atonement, received by personal faith, with God's sovereign purposes in calling believers to service and assurance. Rice's approach prioritized practical evangelism—urging sinners to repent and believe—while upholding substitutionary atonement, blood propitiation, and the necessity of faith in Christ's resurrection life. His writings (e.g., Hyper-Calvinism: A False Doctrine, Predestined for Hell? No! ) and The Sword of the Lord promoted this balanced, soul-winning Fundamentalist theology, influencing generations of IFB preachers and churches. Summary: This is the Fundamentalist view: objective/cosmic reconciliation through unlimited atonement by the death of Jesus on the cross, His blood on the Mercy Seat, and personal, individual salvation by faith in the risen Christ. Election is the calling to service or the predestined role, blessings, traits given to groups of people based on the criteria of God, often for all believers, rather than picking and choosing who is predestined to salvation. In essence, the biblical Fundamentalist view rests on a straightforward trust in the Scripture as written—taking passages in their plain context and allowing the whole counsel of God to interpret itself—yielding unlimited atonement that reconciles the world to God (removing the barrier of sin and making grace genuinely available to all), whosoever-will salvation received personally through faith, and election as God’s call to service and holiness for all who believe. In contrast, both Calvinism and Arminianism begin with false premises about depravity, will, and God’s rule—premises ultimately traceable to Augustine’s incorporation of Gnostic ideas—then force those errors back into the text through eisegesis, redefining election, atonement, and foreknowledge in ways the Bible never intends. The result is a false dichotomy that pits a philosophical, micromanaging “sovereignty” (a modern term and concept foreign to the King James Bible) against man’s responsibility, when Scripture presents no such conflict. True biblical understanding rejects this man-made either/or and simply believes and proclaims the plain gospel truth: Christ died for all, His blood has reconciled the world unto God, salvation is freely offered to whosoever believeth, and God graciously calls believers to holy service.
